skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one CpG is of interest — the method's value comes from joint modelling of all CpGs in a CGI/DMR, not 'one-at-a-time' CpG calibration An existing correction such as Moskalev's CPR is required for direct comparison only — that is a separate calibration/correction path, not the Bayesian M1-M4 model family No standard-control samples with known methylation percentages are available — calibration curves cannot be derived

skills.description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing reads from multiple samples of the same tumour must be decomposed into latent epialleles at a locus, and Q, methylation patterns, and noise must be inferred from data rather than fixed a priori.
skills.name: bayesian-latent-variable-model-fitting
skills.search_text: bayesian-latent-variable-model-fitting Use when bisulfite-sequencing reads from multiple samples of the same tumour must be decomposed into latent epialleles at a locus, and Q, methylation patterns, and noise must be inferred from data rather than fixed a priori. Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so do not use this to phase methylation patterns across separate loci — the model is locus-local. Do not apply when a locus fails the eligibility filters (fewer than six CpGs, median read depth below 100, or more than 25% missing data), as the model was validated only on filtered loci. Do not treat per-locus inference as evidence for multi-patient or multi-tumour generalisation: the case study is a single patient (one tumour, seven regions, one matched normal). http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fits a Bayesian epiallele detection (BED) latent-variable model to pooled RRBS read matrices, automatically inferring the number of epialleles Q, epiallele DNAm patterns X, read assignments w, and a noise hyperparameter epsilon. Implemented in the R package 'bed' and applied to multi-region lung tumour (CRUK0062) plus matched normal data. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Fits a Bayesian epiallele detection (BED) latent-variable model to pooled RRBS read matrices, automatically inferring the number of epialleles Q, epiallele DNAm patterns X, read assignments w, and a noise hyperparameter epsilon. Implemented in the R package 'bed' and applied to multi-region lung tumour (CRUK0062) plus matched normal data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so do not use this to phase methylation patterns across separate loci — the model is locus-local. Do not apply when a locus fails the eligibility filters (fewer than six CpGs, median read depth below 100, or more than 25% missing data), as the model was validated only on filtered loci. Do not treat per-locus inference as evidence for multi-patient or multi-tumour generalisation: the case study is a single patient (one tumour, seven regions, one matched normal).

skills.description: Use when an ANNOVAR-annotated variant feature table (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM scores) contains missing entries and a complete matrix is required before computing summary statistics, correlations, or training a deep learning model.
skills.name: bayesian-pca-missing-value-imputation
skills.search_text: bayesian-pca-missing-value-imputation Use when an ANNOVAR-annotated variant feature table (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM scores) contains missing entries and a complete matrix is required before computing summary statistics, correlations, or training a deep learning model. The input is already a complete feature table with no missing entries in the five predictor score columns Missingness affects metadata columns (gene names, coordinates) rather than the DANN/CADD/EIGEN/GWAVA/FATHMM score columns, since bPCA imputation is designed for the numeric score block The goal is gene-level scores (RVIS, GTEx, haploinsufficiency, Phenolyzer) rather than variant-level non-coding predictor scores http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Imputes missing variant feature scores (DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) in the iMEGES/ncDeepBrain training matrices using Bayesian Principal Component Analysis (bPCA), so the deep-learning variant-prioritization step receives a complete feature matrix without dropping variants. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7
skills.summary: Imputes missing variant feature scores (DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) in the iMEGES/ncDeepBrain training matrices using Bayesian Principal Component Analysis (bPCA), so the deep-learning variant-prioritization step receives a complete feature matrix without dropping variants.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a complete feature table with no missing entries in the five predictor score columns Missingness affects metadata columns (gene names, coordinates) rather than the DANN/CADD/EIGEN/GWAVA/FATHMM score columns, since bPCA imputation is designed for the numeric score block The goal is gene-level scores (RVIS, GTEx, haploinsufficiency, Phenolyzer) rather than variant-level non-coding predictor scores

skills.description: Use when you have fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models per assay (e.g. from BWS standard controls at 0/25/50/75/100% methylation) and must numerically convert observed apparent methylation levels into corrected methylation degrees.
skills.name: bayesian-posterior-postprocessing-inla
skills.search_text: bayesian-posterior-postprocessing-inla Use when you have fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models per assay (e.g. from BWS standard controls at 0/25/50/75/100% methylation) and must numerically convert observed apparent methylation levels into corrected methylation degrees. You need the analytic hyperbolic calibration/inversion of Warnecke et al. (1997) rather than MethylCal's spline-based numeric inversion You only need calibration-curve visualisation or goodness-of-fit comparison (use MethylCalCalibrationPlot / MoskalevCalibrationPlot) rather than correcting case/control methylation levels Calibration models have not yet been fitted with INLA — the interpolant requires posterior means of the AMP random effects from fitted models http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Post-process fitted INLA posterior distributions from MethylCal's Bayesian methylation calibration: build a cubic-spline interpolant of the posterior means of the AMP random effects and numerically invert it (via optimize() minimisation of objective function (10)) to recover PCR-bias-corrected methylation degrees that cannot be obtained analytically. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Post-process fitted INLA posterior distributions from MethylCal's Bayesian methylation calibration: build a cubic-spline interpolant of the posterior means of the AMP random effects and numerically invert it (via optimize() minimisation of objective function (10)) to recover PCR-bias-corrected methylation degrees that cannot be obtained analytically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need the analytic hyperbolic calibration/inversion of Warnecke et al. (1997) rather than MethylCal's spline-based numeric inversion You only need calibration-curve visualisation or goodness-of-fit comparison (use MethylCalCalibrationPlot / MoskalevCalibrationPlot) rather than correcting case/control methylation levels Calibration models have not yet been fitted with INLA — the interpolant requires posterior means of the AMP random effects from fitted models

skills.description: Use when you have a BED file of differential accessibility or binding peak regions from a TR knockout, CRISPR perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type comparison and need to identify/rank the perturbed or cell-type-specific TRs in silico with posterior uncertainty.
skills.name: bayesian-transcriptional-regulator-ranking
skills.search_text: bayesian-transcriptional-regulator-ranking Use when you have a BED file of differential accessibility or binding peak regions from a TR knockout, CRISPR perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type comparison and need to identify/rank the perturbed or cell-type-specific TRs in silico with posterior uncertainty. Input is a gene set or expression signature rather than genomic region coordinates — BIT requires epigenomic region sets; gene-set-based tools like BART are the alternative The query genome is not human or mouse — the pre-compiled reference libraries cover only human (hg) and mouse (mm10) TR ChIP-seq data You need motif-level inference rather than context-specific binding evidence — BIT deliberately bypasses computationally predicted motifs and needs actual peak regions Rank candidate transcriptional regulators (TRs) from a user-provided epigenomic query region set (e.g., ATAC-seq DARs called by MACS2/DiffBind) using BIT, a Bayesian hierarchical model that measures genome-wide consistency against >10,000 human and >5,000 mouse TR ChIP-seq datasets and quantifies uncertainty with 95% credible intervals. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Rank candidate transcriptional regulators (TRs) from a user-provided epigenomic query region set (e.g., ATAC-seq DARs called by MACS2/DiffBind) using BIT, a Bayesian hierarchical model that measures genome-wide consistency against >10,000 human and >5,000 mouse TR ChIP-seq datasets and quantifies uncertainty with 95% credible intervals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene set or expression signature rather than genomic region coordinates — BIT requires epigenomic region sets; gene-set-based tools like BART are the alternative The query genome is not human or mouse — the pre-compiled reference libraries cover only human (hg) and mouse (mm10) TR ChIP-seq data You need motif-level inference rather than context-specific binding evidence — BIT deliberately bypasses computationally predicted motifs and needs actual peak regions

skills.description: Use when reproducing the Fig. 4 TT-quantile deviation analysis and you need a matched B-DNA control set: motif positions are loaded from non-B DNA DB hg38 and you must exclude all motif-overlapping windows before computing per-window translocation-time quantiles.
skills.name: bdna-motif-free-control-region-selection
skills.search_text: bdna-motif-free-control-region-selection Use when reproducing the Fig. 4 TT-quantile deviation analysis and you need a matched B-DNA control set: motif positions are loaded from non-B DNA DB hg38 and you must exclude all motif-overlapping windows before computing per-window translocation-time quantiles. The genomic windows of interest already overlap annotated non-B motifs — these are the case windows, not controls. Input is already a per-window quantile table; the control regions must exist upstream before quantiles can be compared. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Selects B-DNA control windows from motif-free regions of the hg38 reference that overlap high-quality ONT reads, as in Step 5 of the paper's window-preparation pipeline, to provide the baseline translocation-time distribution against which non-B DNA motif windows (100 bp, centered on non-B DNA DB motifs) are compared. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220

skills.description: Use when running Skipper's GFF partitioning step on a GENCODE/Ensembl GFF3 (e.g. gencode.v49.basic.annotation.gff3.gz) to produce the fixed <=100-nt window BED used for CLIP-seq binding site detection.
skills.name: bed-coordinate-manipulation
skills.search_text: bed-coordinate-manipulation Use when running Skipper's GFF partitioning step on a GENCODE/Ensembl GFF3 (e.g. gencode.v49.basic.annotation.gff3.gz) to produce the fixed <=100-nt window BED used for CLIP-seq binding site detection. The analysis goal is de novo peak discovery without a genome/transcript annotation — Skipper's tiling depends on an annotated GFF and skips peak calling by design Windows must span exon-intron or gene boundaries (e.g. genomic-region-level analyses), since Skipper windows are explicitly split at these boundaries The GFF is raw and unfiltered (many alternative isoforms per gene); filter to one best transcript per gene first or window selection will not be interpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Generates Skipper's transcriptome partition by tiling the filtered GENCODE GFF into disjoint windows of at most 100 nt that never cross exon-intron junctions or gene boundaries, replacing peak calling with a fixed window framework for eCLIP binding site detection. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Generates Skipper's transcriptome partition by tiling the filtered GENCODE GFF into disjoint windows of at most 100 nt that never cross exon-intron junctions or gene boundaries, replacing peak calling with a fixed window framework for eCLIP binding site detection.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is de novo peak discovery without a genome/transcript annotation — Skipper's tiling depends on an annotated GFF and skips peak calling by design Windows must span exon-intron or gene boundaries (e.g. genomic-region-level analyses), since Skipper windows are explicitly split at these boundaries The GFF is raw and unfiltered (many alternative isoforms per gene); filter to one best transcript per gene first or window selection will not be interpretable

skills.description: Use when a BED file of genomic intervals (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation and strand signs must be inherited from an overlapping strand-annotated feature file such as MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences.
skills.name: bed-coordinate-processing
skills.search_text: bed-coordinate-processing Use when a BED file of genomic intervals (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation and strand signs must be inherited from an overlapping strand-annotated feature file such as MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences. Intervals already carry strand annotation — skip orientation and run Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns, contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries directly No strand-annotated reference feature overlaps the unannotated intervals, so no strand sign can be inherited and peaks would remain unassigned The goal is de novo motif discovery or scanning (FIMO with the minimum P-value <10−6 threshold) rather than strand inheritance from existing annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reconstructs Asymmetron's orientation function: unannotated genomic intervals (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) inherit the strand sign of the overlapping strand-annotated feature (e.g. MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) whose center is nearest, enabling downstream strand asymmetry analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Reconstructs Asymmetron's orientation function: unannotated genomic intervals (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) inherit the strand sign of the overlapping strand-annotated feature (e.g. MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) whose center is nearest, enabling downstream strand asymmetry analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Intervals already carry strand annotation — skip orientation and run Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns, contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries directly No strand-annotated reference feature overlaps the unannotated intervals, so no strand sign can be inherited and peaks would remain unassigned The goal is de novo motif discovery or scanning (FIMO with the minimum P-value <10−6 threshold) rather than strand inheritance from existing annotations

skills.description: Use when you have chromosomal coordinates of identified eccDNA elements and need to annotate overlapping genes, requiring BED interval conversion and overlap-fraction computation.

skills.search_text: bed-file-coordinate-handling Use when you have chromosomal coordinates of identified eccDNA elements and need to annotate overlapping genes, requiring BED interval conversion and overlap-fraction computation. You need to identify eccDNAs de novo from WGS data (e.g., running the AmpliconArchitect pipeline) rather than annotating genes on an existing eccDNA catalog Intervals cannot be converted to a common BED representation, e.g., one source is in 1-based GTF/GFF coordinates and no coordinate conversion is performed before intersect You only need visualization of eccDNA–gene relationships rather than quantitative overlap annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts genomic interval catalogs (e.g., eccDNA coordinates) and gene annotations (e.g., GENCODE GRCh37 release 38) into compatible BED files and uses BedTools intersect -wo to quantify eccDNA–gene overlaps via the Re and Rg overlap ratios. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x

skills.description: Use when a GRanges object of differential regions (e.g., a DiffBind dba.report result) must be written out as a BED file to feed region-set tools like BIT.
skills.name: bed-file-export-with-rtracklayer
skills.search_text: bed-file-export-with-rtracklayer Use when a GRanges object of differential regions (e.g., a DiffBind dba.report result) must be written out as a BED file to feed region-set tools like BIT. The query regions are already in BED/peak format (e.g., MACS2 narrowPeak output) — BIT can consume them directly without re-export. The analysis is single-cell or RNA-seq based and produces no genomic coordinate ranges to export. The genome assembly is not mm10/hg38-mappable — coordinates must match the TR ChIP-seq reference library. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Exports differentially accessible region (DAR) GRanges objects — e.g., the RUNX1 cKO-vs-WT DAR set produced by DiffBind — to BED format (mm10_RUNX1.bed) so they can serve as epigenomic query region sets for BIT. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Exports differentially accessible region (DAR) GRanges objects — e.g., the RUNX1 cKO-vs-WT DAR set produced by DiffBind — to BED format (mm10_RUNX1.bed) so they can serve as epigenomic query region sets for BIT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query regions are already in BED/peak format (e.g., MACS2 narrowPeak output) — BIT can consume them directly without re-export. The analysis is single-cell or RNA-seq based and produces no genomic coordinate ranges to export. The genome assembly is not mm10/hg38-mappable — coordinates must match the TR ChIP-seq reference library.

skills.description: Use when producing BED interval outputs from ChIA-PET loop data — e.g., calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loops as chromosome/start/end BED records after peak-support and PET-count filtering.
skills.name: bed-file-generation
skills.search_text: bed-file-generation Use when producing BED interval outputs from ChIA-PET loop data — e.g., calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loops as chromosome/start/end BED records after peak-support and PET-count filtering. Input is raw ChIA-PET reads or unprocessed PET clusters that have not yet gone through ChIA-PIPE's linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and loop calling stages The goal is annotating individual enhancer-promoter loops (PET count ≥3 with peak support) rather than merging loops into domain-scale BED intervals Loops lack both-anchor peak-support annotations, since the CCD workflow exclusively uses both-anchor-peak-supported loops http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Generation of BED-format interval files within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling workflow, where merged CTCF loop-coverage regions are written as chromosome, start, end records. This skill covers the filtering and merging logic that determines which genomic intervals are emitted to the BED file. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Generation of BED-format interval files within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling workflow, where merged CTCF loop-coverage regions are written as chromosome, start, end records. This skill covers the filtering and merging logic that determines which genomic intervals are emitted to the BED file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ChIA-PET reads or unprocessed PET clusters that have not yet gone through ChIA-PIPE's linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and loop calling stages The goal is annotating individual enhancer-promoter loops (PET count ≥3 with peak support) rather than merging loops into domain-scale BED intervals Loops lack both-anchor peak-support annotations, since the CCD workflow exclusively uses both-anchor-peak-supported loops

skills.description: Use when you have peak-supported ChIA-PET/HiChIP loop BED files (e.g., RNAPII ChIA-PET loops with PET count >= 3 and unique loop IDs) and need to split them into category-specific tracks (E-P vs P-P vs neither) for separate browser visualization.
skills.name: bed-file-subsetting-and-partitioning
skills.search_text: bed-file-subsetting-and-partitioning Use when you have peak-supported ChIA-PET/HiChIP loop BED files (e.g., RNAPII ChIA-PET loops with PET count >= 3 and unique loop IDs) and need to split them into category-specific tracks (E-P vs P-P vs neither) for separate browser visualization. Loop anchors come from a factor whose binding is not enhancer/promoter-informative (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET), where E-P/P-P classification from RNAPII ChIA-PET data is not biologically meaningful. Input loops have not passed ChIA-PIPE loop calling thresholds (PET count >= 3 with peak support), so anchor coordinates and unique loop IDs required for classification are absent. The goal is 2D contact-map visualization (.hic/.cool for Juicebox/HiGlass) rather than per-category loop annotation tracks. Partitions ChIA-PIPE-called chromatin interaction loops (PET count >= 3, peak-supported, each with a unique loop ID) into enhancer-promoter (E-P), promoter-promoter (P-P), and 'neither' BED subsets by testing coordinate overlap of each loop's left/right anchor BED files against enhancer and promoter BED references using bedtools intersect. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Partitions ChIA-PIPE-called chromatin interaction loops (PET count >= 3, peak-supported, each with a unique loop ID) into enhancer-promoter (E-P), promoter-promoter (P-P), and 'neither' BED subsets by testing coordinate overlap of each loop's left/right anchor BED files against enhancer and promoter BED references using bedtools intersect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loop anchors come from a factor whose binding is not enhancer/promoter-informative (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET), where E-P/P-P classification from RNAPII ChIA-PET data is not biologically meaningful. Input loops have not passed ChIA-PIPE loop calling thresholds (PET count >= 3 with peak support), so anchor coordinates and unique loop IDs required for classification are absent. The goal is 2D contact-map visualization (.hic/.cool for Juicebox/HiGlass) rather than per-category loop annotation tracks.

skills.description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must become fixed 1000 bp, non-redundant training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input window.
skills.name: bed-format-genomic-file-handling
skills.search_text: bed-format-genomic-file-handling Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must become fixed 1000 bp, non-redundant training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input window. The peak set is already a non-redundant compendium of fixed-length intervals (e.g. a pre-built Basset compendium), so re-extending and re-merging would distort centers The analysis requires quantitative epigenomic signal per region — DeepFun binarizes peaks and explicitly ignores quantitative information The task is variant-effect prediction from a VCF using the pre-trained model, which consumes SNPs rather than re-preprocessed peak BEDs http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Preprocess raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into fixed-length, non-redundant genomic training windows (1000 bp extension, greedy merge with a 200 bp overlap cutoff, weighted-midpoint centers) for Basset/DeepFun CNN training. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Preprocess raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into fixed-length, non-redundant genomic training windows (1000 bp extension, greedy merge with a 200 bp overlap cutoff, weighted-midpoint centers) for Basset/DeepFun CNN training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak set is already a non-redundant compendium of fixed-length intervals (e.g. a pre-built Basset compendium), so re-extending and re-merging would distort centers The analysis requires quantitative epigenomic signal per region — DeepFun binarizes peaks and explicitly ignores quantitative information The task is variant-effect prediction from a VCF using the pre-trained model, which consumes SNPs rather than re-preprocessed peak BEDs
