skills.name: bed-genomic-track-generation
skills.search_text: bed-genomic-track-generation Use when Hi-C contact maps (bulk or pseudo-bulk single-cell, resolutions up to 10 kb) must be converted into per-bin compartment score tracks in a BED-like output, with automated PC1/PC2 and sign orientation per chromosome. Single-cell Hi-C maps used directly without pseudo-bulk aggregation — sparsity of single-cell contact maps makes compartment identification unreliable even at coarse resolution The goal is differential compartment testing between conditions — that is the downstream Mahalanobis-distance significance step, not track generation Resolutions finer than the supported range (dcHiC compartment analysis is stated for resolutions up to 10 kb; the README claims up to 5 kb for the optimized PCA) http://edamontology.org/topic_3912 Generates per-bin genomic tracks of A/B compartment scores as a BED-like table (compartment_scores.bed.gz) by computing principal components of distance-normalized Hi-C correlation matrices with an automated PC and sign selection. The sign is oriented so that GC-rich, gene-dense (A-type) bins carry positive scores. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Generates per-bin genomic tracks of A/B compartment scores as a BED-like table (compartment_scores.bed.gz) by computing principal components of distance-normalized Hi-C correlation matrices with an automated PC and sign selection. The sign is oriented so that GC-rich, gene-dense (A-type) bins carry positive scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-cell Hi-C maps used directly without pseudo-bulk aggregation — sparsity of single-cell contact maps makes compartment identification unreliable even at coarse resolution The goal is differential compartment testing between conditions — that is the downstream Mahalanobis-distance significance step, not track generation Resolutions finer than the supported range (dcHiC compartment analysis is stated for resolutions up to 10 kb; the README claims up to 5 kb for the optimized PCA)

skills.description: Use when a spikChIP-style spike-in normalization needs every segmentation bin of the sample (and spike-in) genome labelled as ChIP-enriched or background, from user-supplied BED peak files.
skills.name: bed-interval-overlap-classification
skills.search_text: bed-interval-overlap-classification Use when a spikChIP-style spike-in normalization needs every segmentation bin of the sample (and spike-in) genome labelled as ChIP-enriched or background, from user-supplied BED peak files. When the BED peak files have not yet been generated — peaks must be called beforehand (e.g. MACS2 broad peaks on the Bowtie-mapped BAM); spikChIP only checks their existence in Step 0 When a genome-wide normalization without any pre-defined selection of loci is desired and no external peak set should bias the classification When bins must have variable or annotation-driven sizes rather than fixed-size bins following ChromInfo.txt http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Labels fixed-size genomic bins (e.g. 1,000-bp bins of the hg19 sample genome) as 'peak' or 'background' by computing the overlap between MACS2-called broad peaks in BED format and the segmentation bins using SeqCode's matchpeaks, the bin-classification step of the spikChIP spike-in normalization pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Labels fixed-size genomic bins (e.g. 1,000-bp bins of the hg19 sample genome) as 'peak' or 'background' by computing the overlap between MACS2-called broad peaks in BED format and the segmentation bins using SeqCode's matchpeaks, the bin-classification step of the spikChIP spike-in normalization pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the BED peak files have not yet been generated — peaks must be called beforehand (e.g. MACS2 broad peaks on the Bowtie-mapped BAM); spikChIP only checks their existence in Step 0 When a genome-wide normalization without any pre-defined selection of loci is desired and no external peak set should bias the classification When bins must have variable or annotation-driven sizes rather than fixed-size bins following ChromInfo.txt

skills.description: Use when preparing bisulfite sequencing methylation callsets (e.g. bismark_methylation_extractor .cov files) as input for DXM's dxm_solveMethylation, which requires a tab-delimited BED-like file with a unique regionName per region.
skills.name: bed-like-methylation-file-conversion
skills.search_text: bed-like-methylation-file-conversion Use when preparing bisulfite sequencing methylation callsets (e.g. bismark_methylation_extractor .cov files) as input for DXM's dxm_solveMethylation, which requires a tab-delimited BED-like file with a unique regionName per region. Your data is already in the DXM 6-column BED-like format with unique region names — reconversion or a second bedtools intersect would duplicate region-name assignment. You need methylation profiles solved genome-wide rather than over defined regions — DXM requires user-defined regions with unique names, and a whole-chromosome profile is impractical given assembly gaps and repetitive DNA. Fractional methylation values are on a 0–100 scale and would be passed unconverted — DXM requires values between 0 (fully unmethylated) and 1 (fully methylated). http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Convert aligner methylation-extractor output (e.g. Bismark .cov) into the tab-delimited BED-like 6-column format required by DXM (chr, position1, position2, regionName, fractionalMethylation, coverage), assigning unique region names via bedtools intersect with an annotation bed. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Convert aligner methylation-extractor output (e.g. Bismark .cov) into the tab-delimited BED-like 6-column format required by DXM (chr, position1, position2, regionName, fractionalMethylation, coverage), assigning unique region names via bedtools intersect with an annotation bed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data is already in the DXM 6-column BED-like format with unique region names — reconversion or a second bedtools intersect would duplicate region-name assignment. You need methylation profiles solved genome-wide rather than over defined regions — DXM requires user-defined regions with unique names, and a whole-chromosome profile is impractical given assembly gaps and repetitive DNA. Fractional methylation values are on a 0–100 scale and would be passed unconverted — DXM requires values between 0 (fully unmethylated) and 1 (fully methylated).

skills.description: Use when you must convert mapped ChIP-seq reads (BAM/SAM) into genome-wide signal profiles (BedGraph) for browser visualization, especially when comparing profiles across sequencing depths or histone marks (e.g. sharp H3K4me3 vs broad H3K36me3).
skills.name: bedgraph-custom-track-coordinate-conventions
skills.search_text: bedgraph-custom-track-coordinate-conventions Use when you must convert mapped ChIP-seq reads (BAM/SAM) into genome-wide signal profiles (BedGraph) for browser visualization, especially when comparing profiles across sequencing depths or histone marks (e.g. sharp H3K4me3 vs broad H3K36me3). The profiles are needed in bigWig format — SeqCode defers bigWig generation to future versions The input is already a processed BedGraph/peak file rather than mapped reads — use tools like processmacs or combineChIPprofiles instead of buildChIPprofile Spike-in-normalized signal is required without manual work — the spike-in normalization factor must be introduced manually by users http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate compressed BedGraph genome-browser custom tracks of ChIP-seq signal with SeqCode buildChIPprofile, following SeqCode's conventions: a chromosome-size file defines coordinates/bins, BAM depth drives normalization, and unaligned reads must first be removed so profiles load correctly in genome browsers. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Generate compressed BedGraph genome-browser custom tracks of ChIP-seq signal with SeqCode buildChIPprofile, following SeqCode's conventions: a chromosome-size file defines coordinates/bins, BAM depth drives normalization, and unaligned reads must first be removed so profiles load correctly in genome browsers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The profiles are needed in bigWig format — SeqCode defers bigWig generation to future versions The input is already a processed BedGraph/peak file rather than mapped reads — use tools like processmacs or combineChIPprofiles instead of buildChIPprofile Spike-in-normalized signal is required without manual work — the spike-in normalization factor must be introduced manually by users

skills.description: Use when you have raw per-pixel interaction probability scores (BEDPE) from Peakachu score_genome/score_chromosome and need to derive a final non-redundant loop set with a model-specific probability threshold.
skills.name: bedpe-loop-pooling-and-thresholding
skills.search_text: bedpe-loop-pooling-and-thresholding Use when you have raw per-pixel interaction probability scores (BEDPE) from Peakachu score_genome/score_chromosome and need to derive a final non-redundant loop set with a model-specific probability threshold. Per-pixel scores have not yet been generated by 'peakachu score_genome' or 'score_chromosome' — pool operates only on those outputs The goal is to score individual pixels rather than collapse them into non-redundant loops — use score_chromosome with --minimum-prob instead Working with non-Hi-C contact maps lacking a calibrated model-specific probability cutoff (cutoffs for other cell lines are in Supplementary Data 2, not the main text) http://edamontology.org/topic_3957 Converts genome-wide per-pixel random-forest probability scores from Peakachu into a non-redundant set of chromatin loops by pooling scored pixels and applying a model-specific probability cutoff (e.g., 0.92 for the H3K27ac HiChIP-trained GM12878 model), yielding a BEDPE loop list. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Converts genome-wide per-pixel random-forest probability scores from Peakachu into a non-redundant set of chromatin loops by pooling scored pixels and applying a model-specific probability cutoff (e.g., 0.92 for the H3K27ac HiChIP-trained GM12878 model), yielding a BEDPE loop list.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Per-pixel scores have not yet been generated by 'peakachu score_genome' or 'score_chromosome' — pool operates only on those outputs The goal is to score individual pixels rather than collapse them into non-redundant loops — use score_chromosome with --minimum-prob instead Working with non-Hi-C contact maps lacking a calibrated model-specific probability cutoff (cutoffs for other cell lines are in Supplementary Data 2, not the main text)

skills.description: Use when preparing per-cytosine bismark/bsmap/biscuit methylation output for DXM: each CpG needs a unique regionName from an overlapping feature BED (CGIs, promoters, imprinted DMRs) before dxm_solveMethylation can run.
skills.name: bedtools-genomic-interval-intersection
skills.search_text: bedtools-genomic-interval-intersection Use when preparing per-cytosine bismark/bsmap/biscuit methylation output for DXM: each CpG needs a unique regionName from an overlapping feature BED (CGIs, promoters, imprinted DMRs) before dxm_solveMethylation can run. The methylation file already carries unique region names per tested region and is in DXM's six-column format — re-intersecting would be redundant The goal is deconvolving methylation across a whole chromosome or an unannotated region with no feature BED, since DXM requires unique region names per region of interest and large regions with many CpGs need more CpGs with methylation change to be solved as distinct profiles The feature BED's genome build does not match the methylation data's build — intersect would mislabel coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Use bedtools intersect (-wo) to assign unique region names (e.g. CpG island or imprinted DMR identifiers) to per-CpG bisulfite methylation BED files, producing the DXM-compatible six-column input format required before subpopulation deconvolution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Use bedtools intersect (-wo) to assign unique region names (e.g. CpG island or imprinted DMR identifiers) to per-CpG bisulfite methylation BED files, producing the DXM-compatible six-column input format required before subpopulation deconvolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The methylation file already carries unique region names per tested region and is in DXM's six-column format — re-intersecting would be redundant The goal is deconvolving methylation across a whole chromosome or an unannotated region with no feature BED, since DXM requires unique region names per region of interest and large regions with many CpGs need more CpGs with methylation change to be solved as distinct profiles The feature BED's genome build does not match the methylation data's build — intersect would mislabel coordinates

skills.description: Use when per-species mapped read counts from BWA-mem-mapped RIMS-seq, DNA-seq, and bisulfite-seq libraries are available and the goal is to test whether a sequencing protocol biases species relative abundances in a defined synthetic community.
skills.name: benchmark-community-figure-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-community-figure-reproduction Use when per-species mapped read counts from BWA-mem-mapped RIMS-seq, DNA-seq, and bisulfite-seq libraries are available and the goal is to test whether a sequencing protocol biases species relative abundances in a defined synthetic community. Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than mapped per-species counts — map with BWA-mem first (e.g. mapping.pl) before abundance normalization The goal is methylase specificity/motif discovery (the RIMS-seq.pl / MosDi pipeline) rather than comparing species abundance bias across protocols The library preparation is tagmentation-based; RIMS-seq only works with adapter-ligation libraries, so abundance comparisons with RIMS-seq libraries are invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the Figure 5A benchmark comparing normalized species relative abundances across RIMS-seq, DNA-seq(+3H), and bisulfite-seq libraries from ATCC MSA-1005/1006 synthetic gut and skin microbiome communities, quantifying bisulfite bias on AT-rich species. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Reproduces the Figure 5A benchmark comparing normalized species relative abundances across RIMS-seq, DNA-seq(+3H), and bisulfite-seq libraries from ATCC MSA-1005/1006 synthetic gut and skin microbiome communities, quantifying bisulfite bias on AT-rich species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ reads rather than mapped per-species counts — map with BWA-mem first (e.g. mapping.pl) before abundance normalization The goal is methylase specificity/motif discovery (the RIMS-seq.pl / MosDi pipeline) rather than comparing species abundance bias across protocols The library preparation is tagmentation-based; RIMS-seq only works with adapter-ligation libraries, so abundance comparisons with RIMS-seq libraries are invalid

skills.description: Use when a new predictor must be benchmarked against an existing published tool under identical cross-validation on shared datasets (e.g. DNA 6mA site prediction) and the deliverable is a side-by-side metrics table.
skills.name: benchmark-method-comparison-reporting
skills.search_text: benchmark-method-comparison-reporting Use when a new predictor must be benchmarked against an existing published tool under identical cross-validation on shared datasets (e.g. DNA 6mA site prediction) and the deliverable is a side-by-side metrics table. The goal is independent-test or jackknife evaluation rather than the paper's 5-fold cross-validation comparison (e.g. i6mA-Pred's ACC of 0.831 was reported by jackknife and is not directly comparable here). Only one dataset is available — the skill requires the shared cross-species, rice, and M. musculus benchmarks for the side-by-side comparison. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduces the head-to-head 5-fold cross-validation comparison of csDMA (ExtraTrees, Motif+Kmer+Binary features) against the iDNA6mA-PseKNC baseline (SVM, C=0.336, gamma=0.02) on the cross-species, rice, and M. musculus DNA 6mA benchmarks, assembling the results into a Table-4-style CSV. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the head-to-head 5-fold cross-validation comparison of csDMA (ExtraTrees, Motif+Kmer+Binary features) against the iDNA6mA-PseKNC baseline (SVM, C=0.336, gamma=0.02) on the cross-species, rice, and M. musculus DNA 6mA benchmarks, assembling the results into a Table-4-style CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is independent-test or jackknife evaluation rather than the paper's 5-fold cross-validation comparison (e.g. i6mA-Pred's ACC of 0.831 was reported by jackknife and is not directly comparable here). Only one dataset is available — the skill requires the shared cross-species, rice, and M. musculus benchmarks for the side-by-side comparison.

skills.description: Use when two or more enhancer-prediction methods must be compared on a shared benchmark with independent test sets and per-cell-line metrics such as BACC, to verify a claimed improvement.
skills.name: benchmark-metric-comparison-across-methods
skills.search_text: benchmark-metric-comparison-across-methods Use when two or more enhancer-prediction methods must be compared on a shared benchmark with independent test sets and per-cell-line metrics such as BACC, to verify a claimed improvement. Input sequences are not already split into training and independent test sets for the Enhancer-IF benchmark — random resampling would not support the head-to-head comparison on independent test data The goal is generic enhancer identification or enhancer-strength classification (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L generic dataset) rather than cell-specific comparison across the eight cell lines Only one method is being evaluated with no published baseline metric values to compare against http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Reproduce a head-to-head benchmark in which a new predictor (Enhancer-MDLF) and a prior method (Enhancer-IF) are evaluated on the same independent test sets across eight human cell lines, tabulating five metrics to quantify performance differences (e.g. the 9.54% BACC gain on HMEC). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Reproduce a head-to-head benchmark in which a new predictor (Enhancer-MDLF) and a prior method (Enhancer-IF) are evaluated on the same independent test sets across eight human cell lines, tabulating five metrics to quantify performance differences (e.g. the 9.54% BACC gain on HMEC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input sequences are not already split into training and independent test sets for the Enhancer-IF benchmark — random resampling would not support the head-to-head comparison on independent test data The goal is generic enhancer identification or enhancer-strength classification (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L generic dataset) rather than cell-specific comparison across the eight cell lines Only one method is being evaluated with no published baseline metric values to compare against

skills.description: Use when comparing multiple model classes (CNN baseline, DNA foundation models, task-specific expert) on the same prediction task across several biological subsets (e.g., cell lines) and a per-subset plus averaged score table is required.
skills.name: benchmark-results-tabulation-across-cell-lines
skills.search_text: benchmark-results-tabulation-across-cell-lines Use when comparing multiple model classes (CNN baseline, DNA foundation models, task-specific expert) on the same prediction task across several biological subsets (e.g., cell lines) and a per-subset plus averaged score table is required. The task is a short-range DNA prediction task (e.g., classification with AUROC metric) rather than a 2D contact map regression evaluated with stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient Only one model or one cell line is being evaluated, so a cross-model, cross-cell-line comparison table is not applicable The inputs are raw .tfr files that have not yet been run through model inference; tabulation requires predicted maps first http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Tabulate stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient (SCC) scores for all evaluated models (expert model, CNN, HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) per cell line and as a cross-cell-line average, reproducing the contact map prediction benchmark table (Table 4) from DNALONGBENCH. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Tabulate stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient (SCC) scores for all evaluated models (expert model, CNN, HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) per cell line and as a cross-cell-line average, reproducing the contact map prediction benchmark table (Table 4) from DNALONGBENCH.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a short-range DNA prediction task (e.g., classification with AUROC metric) rather than a 2D contact map regression evaluated with stratum-adjusted correlation coefficient Only one model or one cell line is being evaluated, so a cross-model, cross-cell-line comparison table is not applicable The inputs are raw .tfr files that have not yet been run through model inference; tabulation requires predicted maps first

skills.description: Use when a new network/pathway-detection method must be validated against established clustering tools on a time-series dataset for which a curated set of known associated pathways exists.
skills.name: benchmark-sensitivity-evaluation
skills.search_text: benchmark-sensitivity-evaluation Use when a new network/pathway-detection method must be validated against established clustering tools on a time-series dataset for which a curated set of known associated pathways exists. No gold-standard set of known pathway associations exists for the tissue/process under study, so sensitivity cannot be scored The input is a static (single-time-point) expression dataset, not a time series — TSMiner and the time-specific-network comparison are not applicable The aim is exploratory pathway discovery rather than method benchmarking; a direct enrichment analysis suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark a time-series regulatory-network method (e.g. TSMiner) against comparison methods (DREM, hclust, k-means, STEM, WGCNA) by computing sensitivity and AUC for detecting known LR-associated KEGG/Reactome pathways at P-value thresholds sweeping 0–0.05. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Benchmark a time-series regulatory-network method (e.g. TSMiner) against comparison methods (DREM, hclust, k-means, STEM, WGCNA) by computing sensitivity and AUC for detecting known LR-associated KEGG/Reactome pathways at P-value thresholds sweeping 0–0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No gold-standard set of known pathway associations exists for the tissue/process under study, so sensitivity cannot be scored The input is a static (single-time-point) expression dataset, not a time series — TSMiner and the time-specific-network comparison are not applicable The aim is exploratory pathway discovery rather than method benchmarking; a direct enrichment analysis suffices

skills.description: Use when a study reports execution time and memory footprint of a tool on named datasets and the task is to reproduce or extend that performance table on a local machine.
skills.name: benchmark-table-compilation
skills.search_text: benchmark-table-compilation Use when a study reports execution time and memory footprint of a tool on named datasets and the task is to reproduce or extend that performance table on a local machine. The task is to evaluate motif discovery quality (e.g. nCC or JASPAR comparison) rather than runtime and memory tractability The hardware is not desktop-class or the comparison target values were measured on a different architecture, making direct runtime comparison meaningless without re-baselining http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce and assemble a performance benchmark table (like Table 3 of the DiNAMO paper) by instrumenting tool runs to record wall-clock execution time and peak resident memory per dataset, then validating measurements against the published values. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Reproduce and assemble a performance benchmark table (like Table 3 of the DiNAMO paper) by instrumenting tool runs to record wall-clock execution time and peak resident memory per dataset, then validating measurements against the published values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to evaluate motif discovery quality (e.g. nCC or JASPAR comparison) rather than runtime and memory tractability The hardware is not desktop-class or the comparison target values were measured on a different architecture, making direct runtime comparison meaningless without re-baselining

skills.description: Use when reproducing the paper's functional-validation benchmarks: measuring what fraction of base pairs and genes of a known functional gene set (e.g. X-inactivated genes) are covered by differential modification calls.
skills.name: benchmark-table-reproduction
skills.search_text: benchmark-table-reproduction Use when reproducing the paper's functional-validation benchmarks: measuring what fraction of base pairs and genes of a known functional gene set (e.g. X-inactivated genes) are covered by differential modification calls. The calls are peak-like transcription-factor ChIP-seq peaks rather than broad diffuse repressive marks such as H3K9me3 or H3K27me3 You need exon-level or promoter-level overlap rather than whole gene-body coverage, since the provided GFF annotation contains only gene bodies and no exon information http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduce the benchmark tables of the histoneHMM paper, notably Table 4's X-inactivation coverage evaluation of H3K9me3 differential calls, by intersecting differential region calls with the 250 known X-inactivated protein coding genes and comparing histoneHMM against Diffreps, Chipdiff, Pepr and Rseg. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Reproduce the benchmark tables of the histoneHMM paper, notably Table 4's X-inactivation coverage evaluation of H3K9me3 differential calls, by intersecting differential region calls with the 250 known X-inactivated protein coding genes and comparing histoneHMM against Diffreps, Chipdiff, Pepr and Rseg.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The calls are peak-like transcription-factor ChIP-seq peaks rather than broad diffuse repressive marks such as H3K9me3 or H3K27me3 You need exon-level or promoter-level overlap rather than whole gene-body coverage, since the provided GFF annotation contains only gene bodies and no exon information

skills.description: Use when novelty scores (reconstruction error, Mahalanobis distance, IF/LOF/SVM scores) have been converted to empirical P-values against a B-DNA null and a per-window significance decision is needed at a fixed FDR level.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when novelty scores (reconstruction error, Mahalanobis distance, IF/LOF/SVM scores) have been converted to empirical P-values against a B-DNA null and a per-window significance decision is needed at a fixed FDR level. When a family-wise error guarantee is required instead of FDR control (BH controls expected false discovery proportion, not family-wise error) When P-values are not calibrated against an empirical B-DNA null — BH applied to raw novelty scores is invalid For supervised classification tasks (SVC, random forest, nearest neighbors, logistic regression, gaussian process), which do not use FDR calling in this workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction at a configured FDR level (fdr_level=0.2 in the GoFAE-DND workflow) to convert empirical-null P-values of novelty statistics into significant non-B DNA calls, controlling the false discovery rate across windows. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg multiple-testing correction at a configured FDR level (fdr_level=0.2 in the GoFAE-DND workflow) to convert empirical-null P-values of novelty statistics into significant non-B DNA calls, controlling the false discovery rate across windows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a family-wise error guarantee is required instead of FDR control (BH controls expected false discovery proportion, not family-wise error) When P-values are not calibrated against an empirical B-DNA null — BH applied to raw novelty scores is invalid For supervised classification tasks (SVC, random forest, nearest neighbors, logistic regression, gaussian process), which do not use FDR calling in this workflow

skills.description: Use when testing thousands of phased heterozygous SNPs for allelic imbalance in ChIA-PET read coverage and needing multiple-testing-corrected significance calls before classifying allele-specific loops.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction Use when testing thousands of phased heterozygous SNPs for allelic imbalance in ChIA-PET read coverage and needing multiple-testing-corrected significance calls before classifying allele-specific loops. Testing a single pre-specified hypothesis where no multiple-testing correction is needed Input data lack phased heterozygous SNP annotations, so no per-SNP allelic binomial tests can be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to per-SNP binomial test P values when detecting allelic bias in ChIA-PET read coverage, retaining SNPs with FDR Q <= 0.1 as significantly biased for resolving allele-specific phased peaks and loops. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to per-SNP binomial test P values when detecting allelic bias in ChIA-PET read coverage, retaining SNPs with FDR Q <= 0.1 as significantly biased for resolving allele-specific phased peaks and loops.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Testing a single pre-specified hypothesis where no multiple-testing correction is needed Input data lack phased heterozygous SNP annotations, so no per-SNP allelic binomial tests can be computed

skills.description: Use when a family of hypothesis tests has been run per cluster (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon tests across regions, or hypergeometric tests across MSigDB v5 gene sets) and raw p-values must be adjusted before thresholding significant regions or pathways.
skills.name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction Use when a family of hypothesis tests has been run per cluster (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon tests across regions, or hypergeometric tests across MSigDB v5 gene sets) and raw p-values must be adjusted before thresholding significant regions or pathways. Only a single hypothesis test (or a tiny pre-specified set) is being run, so family-wise FDR control is unnecessary and would over-penalize The p-values are already adjusted (e.g. loaded from a prior differential_enrichment_results.tsv) — re-applying BH would double-correct and inflate p-values The goal is per-peak raw significance inspection or effect-size ranking rather than controlled selection of significant regions/gene sets http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to p-value families generated in the ChromSCape workflow — per-cluster Wilcoxon rank-sum tests over genomic regions and hypergeometric tests over MSigDB v5 gene sets — so that differentially enriched H3K27me3 regions and enriched pathways are called at controlled FDR. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to p-value families generated in the ChromSCape workflow — per-cluster Wilcoxon rank-sum tests over genomic regions and hypergeometric tests over MSigDB v5 gene sets — so that differentially enriched H3K27me3 regions and enriched pathways are called at controlled FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single hypothesis test (or a tiny pre-specified set) is being run, so family-wise FDR control is unnecessary and would over-penalize The p-values are already adjusted (e.g. loaded from a prior differential_enrichment_results.tsv) — re-applying BH would double-correct and inflate p-values The goal is per-peak raw significance inspection or effect-size ranking rather than controlled selection of significant regions/gene sets

skills.description: Use when a family of P-values is large and potentially dependent (e.g. MEPP positional correlations at adjacent sequence positions, or all motifs at all positions) and a dependency-robust FDR adjustment is required.
skills.name: benjamini-yekutieli-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: benjamini-yekutieli-fdr-correction Use when a family of P-values is large and potentially dependent (e.g. MEPP positional correlations at adjacent sequence positions, or all motifs at all positions) and a dependency-robust FDR adjustment is required. When the P-value family is known to be independent — Benjamini-Hochberg FDR is less conservative than Benjamini-Yekutieli, which pays a dependence penalty via the harmonic-series factor When the goal is de novo motif discovery rather than testing enrichment of known motifs — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library (e.g. the JASPAR-format matrices supplied via --motifs) When only a handful of P-values are being corrected, where the BY correction's conservatism can drive all adjusted P-values far above any usable alpha (e.g. the 0.01 default) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Yekutieli (fdr_by) false-discovery-rate correction to large, dependent families of P-values — as MEPP does for positional-correlation P-values computed at every heatmap position across motifs, controlling for dependence between neighboring positions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Yekutieli (fdr_by) false-discovery-rate correction to large, dependent families of P-values — as MEPP does for positional-correlation P-values computed at every heatmap position across motifs, controlling for dependence between neighboring positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the P-value family is known to be independent — Benjamini-Hochberg FDR is less conservative than Benjamini-Yekutieli, which pays a dependence penalty via the harmonic-series factor When the goal is de novo motif discovery rather than testing enrichment of known motifs — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library (e.g. the JASPAR-format matrices supplied via --motifs) When only a handful of P-values are being corrected, where the BY correction's conservatism can drive all adjusted P-values far above any usable alpha (e.g. the 0.01 default)

skills.description: Use when you have a clustered-region methylation counts table (combined.csv with chr, start, end, CpG, per-sample -N and -X columns) and need to identify DMRs between two or more sample groups from MethylC-seq data.
skills.name: beta-binomial-differential-methylation-testing
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-differential-methylation-testing Use when you have a clustered-region methylation counts table (combined.csv with chr, start, end, CpG, per-sample -N and -X columns) and need to identify DMRs between two or more sample groups from MethylC-seq data. The goal is to model sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder 'identifies individual regions that are differentially methylated but does not consider sets of regions or quantitative traits'. The data contain batch effects that must be accounted for — DMRfinder 'cannot account for batch effects'. The question concerns differential methylation at individual CpG sites rather than regions of multiple CpG sites; the paper argues a more biologically appropriate approach is to test regions of multiple CpG sites. http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tests clustered genomic regions for differential methylation between sample groups using DSS's beta-binomial hierarchical modeling and Wald tests, as implemented in DMRfinder's findDMRs.r. Because methylation counts are conglomerated within each cluster, the number of hypothesis tests is reduced and statistical power increases compared with testing individual CpG sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Tests clustered genomic regions for differential methylation between sample groups using DSS's beta-binomial hierarchical modeling and Wald tests, as implemented in DMRfinder's findDMRs.r. Because methylation counts are conglomerated within each cluster, the number of hypothesis tests is reduced and statistical power increases compared with testing individual CpG sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to model sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder 'identifies individual regions that are differentially methylated but does not consider sets of regions or quantitative traits'. The data contain batch effects that must be accounted for — DMRfinder 'cannot account for batch effects'. The question concerns differential methylation at individual CpG sites rather than regions of multiple CpG sites; the paper argues a more biologically appropriate approach is to test regions of multiple CpG sites.

skills.description: Use when an HMM-style methylation deconvolution (e.g. DXM's Viterbi decoding over user-defined regions) needs emission probabilities for observed fractional methylation plus read coverage at each CpG of a region.
skills.name: beta-binomial-emission-probability-computation
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-emission-probability-computation Use when an HMM-style methylation deconvolution (e.g. DXM's Viterbi decoding over user-defined regions) needs emission probabilities for observed fractional methylation plus read coverage at each CpG of a region. Input is raw bisulfite reads or aligner output rather than a processed BED-like fractional-methylation/coverage file — convert and collapse across strands first Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (e.g. neuronal cell types), since DXM does not consider 5hmC Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where care must be taken interpreting DXM results http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes per-CpG emission likelihoods for a hidden Markov model over bisulfite sequencing methylation data, using the beta-binomial distribution (DXM Equation 1) applied to each CpG's fractional methylation value and integer coverage so the decoder can recover per-subpopulation methylation states. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Computes per-CpG emission likelihoods for a hidden Markov model over bisulfite sequencing methylation data, using the beta-binomial distribution (DXM Equation 1) applied to each CpG's fractional methylation value and integer coverage so the decoder can recover per-subpopulation methylation states.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw bisulfite reads or aligner output rather than a processed BED-like fractional-methylation/coverage file — convert and collapse across strands first Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (e.g. neuronal cell types), since DXM does not consider 5hmC Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where care must be taken interpreting DXM results

skills.description: Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq FASTQs that have matched input controls and at least 2 CLIP replicates, and you need reproducible, annotated binding-site windows rather than peak calls.
skills.name: beta-binomial-enriched-window-testing
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-enriched-window-testing Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq FASTQs that have matched input controls and at least 2 CLIP replicates, and you need reproducible, annotated binding-site windows rather than peak calls. The CLIP experiment lacks a matched input sample — the beta-binomial model cannot be constructed, so the analysis cannot be run at all Only a single CLIP replicate is available, since reproducible enriched windows require replication across at least 2 CLIP replicates The goal is peak-style binding coordinates rather than tiled transcript-window enrichment statistics, or the signal is expected outside annotated transcript windows (peak calling approaches are what Skipper intentionally replaces) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Statistical framework in Skipper that tests read-start enrichment in fixed windows tiled over annotated transcripts against matched input controls using a beta-binomial model, skipping peak calling entirely and reporting reproducible enriched windows as candidate RBP binding sites in eCLIP data. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Statistical framework in Skipper that tests read-start enrichment in fixed windows tiled over annotated transcripts against matched input controls using a beta-binomial model, skipping peak calling entirely and reporting reproducible enriched windows as candidate RBP binding sites in eCLIP data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CLIP experiment lacks a matched input sample — the beta-binomial model cannot be constructed, so the analysis cannot be run at all Only a single CLIP replicate is available, since reproducible enriched windows require replication across at least 2 CLIP replicates The goal is peak-style binding coordinates rather than tiled transcript-window enrichment statistics, or the signal is expected outside annotated transcript windows (peak calling approaches are what Skipper intentionally replaces)

skills.description: Use when detecting significant RBP binding to annotated repetitive elements or transcriptomic windows from eCLIP data with matched inputs, especially multi-mapping/repeat targets that peak callers miss.
skills.name: beta-binomial-enrichment-testing-with-gc-overdispersion-correction
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-enrichment-testing-with-gc-overdispersion-correction Use when detecting significant RBP binding to annotated repetitive elements or transcriptomic windows from eCLIP data with matched inputs, especially multi-mapping/repeat targets that peak callers miss. CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample — Skipper requires matched input to construct the beta-binomial model and cannot analyze them Analyses where only peak-called binding sites are needed and multi-mapping repeat/multi-mapping sequences are not of interest Datasets not aligned with STAR or missing the RepeatMasker annotation files Skipper expects as REPEAT_TABLE/REPEAT_BED http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Skipper's beta-binomial statistical framework tests STAR-aligned eCLIP IP vs. matched input reads for enrichment at annotated features (windows and RepeatMasker repetitive elements), correcting for GC content and overdispersion so that multi-mapping repeat targets can be detected across 219 ENCODE eCLIP datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Skipper's beta-binomial statistical framework tests STAR-aligned eCLIP IP vs. matched input reads for enrichment at annotated features (windows and RepeatMasker repetitive elements), correcting for GC content and overdispersion so that multi-mapping repeat targets can be detected across 219 ENCODE eCLIP datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample — Skipper requires matched input to construct the beta-binomial model and cannot analyze them Analyses where only peak-called binding sites are needed and multi-mapping repeat/multi-mapping sequences are not of interest Datasets not aligned with STAR or missing the RepeatMasker annotation files Skipper expects as REPEAT_TABLE/REPEAT_BED

skills.description: Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq reads must be tested for region-level differential methylation between two sample groups (e.g., IMR90/H1 replicates) with strict false-positive control, such that self-replicate contrasts yield minimal DMRs.
skills.name: beta-binomial-hierarchical-dmr-testing
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-hierarchical-dmr-testing Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq reads must be tested for region-level differential methylation between two sample groups (e.g., IMR90/H1 replicates) with strict false-positive control, such that self-replicate contrasts yield minimal DMRs. You need to model sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder identifies individual differentially methylated regions only Batch effects must be adjusted for — DMRfinder cannot account for batch effects The goal is single-CpG-site differential testing rather than multi-CpG region DMRs — the pipeline deliberately tests regions of multiple CpG sites http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Region-level differential methylation testing for MethylC-seq data: cluster CpG sites with DMRfinder's combine_CpG_sites.py and test sample groups with findDMRs.r, which applies beta-binomial hierarchical modeling (the DSS statistical framework) with Wald tests. This design kept same-sample IMR90 replicate contrasts near zero DMRs where alternative software reported substantial false positives. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Region-level differential methylation testing for MethylC-seq data: cluster CpG sites with DMRfinder's combine_CpG_sites.py and test sample groups with findDMRs.r, which applies beta-binomial hierarchical modeling (the DSS statistical framework) with Wald tests. This design kept same-sample IMR90 replicate contrasts near zero DMRs where alternative software reported substantial false positives.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to model sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder identifies individual differentially methylated regions only Batch effects must be adjusted for — DMRfinder cannot account for batch effects The goal is single-CpG-site differential testing rather than multi-CpG region DMRs — the pipeline deliberately tests regions of multiple CpG sites

skills.description: Use when analyzing tiled transcriptomic (or repetitive-element) windows from eCLIP data with matched IP and input read-start counts, and you need GC-bias-aware enrichment p-values accounting for count overdispersion.
skills.name: beta-binomial-regression-modeling
skills.search_text: beta-binomial-regression-modeling Use when analyzing tiled transcriptomic (or repetitive-element) windows from eCLIP data with matched IP and input read-start counts, and you need GC-bias-aware enrichment p-values accounting for count overdispersion. No matched input sample is available — the beta-binomial model cannot be constructed and Skipper cannot be applied The goal is free-form peak discovery with variable-width peaks rather than fixed-window enrichment testing over annotated transcripts Read counts come from a single pooled replicate with no input replicates to estimate overdispersion rho http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistical skill from the Skipper CLIP-seq pipeline: fit a beta-binomial model per GC-content decile to model overdispersion in read-start counts, then compute IP-vs-input enrichment p-values for tiled windows to call RNA-binding sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Statistical skill from the Skipper CLIP-seq pipeline: fit a beta-binomial model per GC-content decile to model overdispersion in read-start counts, then compute IP-vs-input enrichment p-values for tiled windows to call RNA-binding sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched input sample is available — the beta-binomial model cannot be constructed and Skipper cannot be applied The goal is free-form peak discovery with variable-width peaks rather than fixed-window enrichment testing over annotated transcripts Read counts come from a single pooled replicate with no input replicates to estimate overdispersion rho

skills.description: Use when a RNA-Seq expression-estimation method has been run with and without fragment-bias correction and the improvement must be validated against an independent qRT-PCR truth set (e.g., 907 uniquely probed MAQC HBR transcripts).
skills.name: bias-correction-evaluation
skills.search_text: bias-correction-evaluation Use when a RNA-Seq expression-estimation method has been run with and without fragment-bias correction and the improvement must be validated against an independent qRT-PCR truth set (e.g., 907 uniquely probed MAQC HBR transcripts). When no independently measured qRT-PCR (or equivalent external truth set) is available — the R2-vs-qRT-PCR comparison cannot be computed When the goal is to estimate bias parameters themselves rather than evaluate whether an existing bias-corrected estimator improves accuracy When transcripts cannot be restricted to a uniquely probed subset, since multi-mapping probes inflate or deflate R2 spuriously http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 A benchmark-driven skill for quantifying whether RNA-Seq fragment-bias correction improves expression estimates, by computing squared Pearson correlations (R2) between corrected and uncorrected transcript abundance estimates and independently measured qRT-PCR reference values on the MAQC HBR dataset. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: A benchmark-driven skill for quantifying whether RNA-Seq fragment-bias correction improves expression estimates, by computing squared Pearson correlations (R2) between corrected and uncorrected transcript abundance estimates and independently measured qRT-PCR reference values on the MAQC HBR dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no independently measured qRT-PCR (or equivalent external truth set) is available — the R2-vs-qRT-PCR comparison cannot be computed When the goal is to estimate bias parameters themselves rather than evaluate whether an existing bias-corrected estimator improves accuracy When transcripts cannot be restricted to a uniquely probed subset, since multi-mapping probes inflate or deflate R2 spuriously

skills.description: Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split at candidate bifurcation time points and Baum-Welch training of a tree-structure model needs effective initial parameters, e.g., TSMiner runs on mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq time courses.
skills.name: bifurcation-pattern-comparison-vector-construction
skills.search_text: bifurcation-pattern-comparison-vector-construction Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split at candidate bifurcation time points and Baum-Welch training of a tree-structure model needs effective initial parameters, e.g., TSMiner runs on mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq time courses. The data are not a time course (no ordered time points with a preceding reference), so the fold-change-based up/down/unchanged classification and comparison vector nc cannot be computed. A trained TSMiner saved model already exists and the task is only Viterbi decoding or interactive network visualization - no new bifurcation patterns are needed. The goal is a static regulatory network or plain clustering of non-temporal expression data; this skill's branching logic is specific to time-series expression profiles plus TF-TG interaction files. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Constructs the bifurcation patterns TSMiner uses to divide each path of its tree-structure input-output hidden Markov model: at candidate bifurcation time points, genes are classified as up-regulated, down-regulated, or unchanged by expression fold change and summarized into a three-dimensional comparison vector nc. A likelihood ratio test then partitions the gene set G to define branch points and supply effective initial parameters for Baum-Welch training. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Constructs the bifurcation patterns TSMiner uses to divide each path of its tree-structure input-output hidden Markov model: at candidate bifurcation time points, genes are classified as up-regulated, down-regulated, or unchanged by expression fold change and summarized into a three-dimensional comparison vector nc. A likelihood ratio test then partitions the gene set G to define branch points and supply effective initial parameters for Baum-Welch training.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not a time course (no ordered time points with a preceding reference), so the fold-change-based up/down/unchanged classification and comparison vector nc cannot be computed. A trained TSMiner saved model already exists and the task is only Viterbi decoding or interactive network visualization - no new bifurcation patterns are needed. The goal is a static regulatory network or plain clustering of non-temporal expression data; this skill's branching logic is specific to time-series expression profiles plus TF-TG interaction files.

skills.description: Use when you have TCGA or ENCODE ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks and need to quantify or visualize chromatin accessibility over a specific locus (e.g., an eccDNA-containing region) in cancer samples.
skills.name: bigwig-genomic-coverage-extraction
skills.search_text: bigwig-genomic-coverage-extraction Use when you have TCGA or ENCODE ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks and need to quantify or visualize chromatin accessibility over a specific locus (e.g., an eccDNA-containing region) in cancer samples. You need eccDNA amplicon reconstruction rather than chromatin accessibility — use the AmpliconArchitect WGS pipeline instead Raw FASTQ or BAM ATAC-seq alignments are the only available data (no BigWig signal track exists), requiring peak calling/coverage computation upstream The goal is circular layout visualization of eccDNA relationships rather than linear locus-level coverage rendering http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Extract per-base ATAC-seq signal from BigWig coverage tracks over a defined genomic interval (e.g., chr7:54370001-55996000 at the EGFR locus) using pyBigWig, aggregate per-sample signal across TCGA GBM samples, and render the coverage profile with pyGenomeTracks or matplotlib to assess chromatin accessibility at eccDNA-containing regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Extract per-base ATAC-seq signal from BigWig coverage tracks over a defined genomic interval (e.g., chr7:54370001-55996000 at the EGFR locus) using pyBigWig, aggregate per-sample signal across TCGA GBM samples, and render the coverage profile with pyGenomeTracks or matplotlib to assess chromatin accessibility at eccDNA-containing regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need eccDNA amplicon reconstruction rather than chromatin accessibility — use the AmpliconArchitect WGS pipeline instead Raw FASTQ or BAM ATAC-seq alignments are the only available data (no BigWig signal track exists), requiring peak calling/coverage computation upstream The goal is circular layout visualization of eccDNA relationships rather than linear locus-level coverage rendering

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or adapting GILoop's dual-branch architecture: two single-view encoders (GCN and U-Net) must be combined per pixel into one fused representation that feeds loop vs. non-loop pixel classification.
skills.name: bilinear-feature-fusion-layer-design
skills.search_text: bilinear-feature-fusion-layer-design Use when reconstructing or adapting GILoop's dual-branch architecture: two single-view encoders (GCN and U-Net) must be combined per pixel into one fused representation that feeds loop vs. non-loop pixel classification. Data is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C): the article states GILoop 'is still not capable enough to deal with' scHi-C and only focuses on bulk Hi-C. Only one view is needed: prior image-only tools (SIP, Chromosight) or graph-only approaches apply when graph-image fusion is not the goal. The targeted cell line's sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository and no retraining/downsampling pipeline is available — the article flags this as 'weak usability'. http://edamontology.org/topic_0128 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Design and validate the bilinear pooling fusion layer that combines GILoop's separately pre-trained GCN (graph-view) and U-Net (image-view) branch outputs into a joint 16-dimensional per-pixel representation for CTCF-mediated chromatin loop calling on Hi-C contact maps. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Design and validate the bilinear pooling fusion layer that combines GILoop's separately pre-trained GCN (graph-view) and U-Net (image-view) branch outputs into a joint 16-dimensional per-pixel representation for CTCF-mediated chromatin loop calling on Hi-C contact maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C): the article states GILoop 'is still not capable enough to deal with' scHi-C and only focuses on bulk Hi-C. Only one view is needed: prior image-only tools (SIP, Chromosight) or graph-only approaches apply when graph-image fusion is not the goal. The targeted cell line's sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository and no retraining/downsampling pipeline is available — the article flags this as 'weak usability'.

skills.description: Use when duplicate-filtered cfMeDIP-seq BAM files must be converted into per-bin methylation estimates with correction for CpG density bias, or when relative vs. absolute (vs. strand-aware) methylation strategies must be compared per sample.
skills.name: bin-level-genomic-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: bin-level-genomic-matrix-generation Use when duplicate-filtered cfMeDIP-seq BAM files must be converted into per-bin methylation estimates with correction for CpG density bias, or when relative vs. absolute (vs. strand-aware) methylation strategies must be compared per sample. Input data is not enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq (e.g., whole-genome bisulfite sequencing), where CpG-density-bias correction via MeDIP-style sigmoid/linear models is not applicable Only raw FASTQ files are available and no alignment/QC has been performed, since this module expects the aligned, duplicate-filtered BAM outputs of the upstream MEDIPIPE module A single consensus methylation track is already provided and the goal is only sample aggregation rather than per-bin quantification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates bin-sample methylation quantification tables from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq alignments using three CpG-density-bias-correcting models in MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module: MEDIPS (linear regression, relative methylation), QSEA (sigmoidal model with empirical knowledge, absolute methylation), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model, strand-aware absolute methylation). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Generates bin-sample methylation quantification tables from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq alignments using three CpG-density-bias-correcting models in MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module: MEDIPS (linear regression, relative methylation), QSEA (sigmoidal model with empirical knowledge, absolute methylation), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model, strand-aware absolute methylation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq (e.g., whole-genome bisulfite sequencing), where CpG-density-bias correction via MeDIP-style sigmoid/linear models is not applicable Only raw FASTQ files are available and no alignment/QC has been performed, since this module expects the aligned, duplicate-filtered BAM outputs of the upstream MEDIPIPE module A single consensus methylation track is already provided and the goal is only sample aggregation rather than per-bin quantification

skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq nuclei need a peak-free similarity representation — SnapATAC's runNormJaccard requires a binarized cell-by-bin matrix (makeBinary + addBmatToSnap) because per-cell signals are too sparse for peak-based clustering.
skills.name: binarized-accessibility-bin-counting
skills.search_text: binarized-accessibility-bin-counting Use when scATAC-seq nuclei need a peak-free similarity representation — SnapATAC's runNormJaccard requires a binarized cell-by-bin matrix (makeBinary + addBmatToSnap) because per-cell signals are too sparse for peak-based clustering. Input is already a peak-by-cell feature matrix or count table from a peak-aware pipeline (e.g., CellRanger-ATAC) — binarization of genome-wide bins is redundant and the peak matrix can be used directly The analysis requires quantitative count depth (e.g., differential accessibility testing on counts) rather than binary accessibility similarity — binarization discards per-bin fragment counts The data are single-cell RNA-seq or other non-accessibility assays — the snap AM session and Jaccard framework are designed for ATAC-seq fragments http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Binarizes genome-wide scATAC-seq accessibility into cell-by-bin matrices (e.g., 5,000 and 10,000 bp bins stored in a snap AM session) and counts fragments per bin so that cell-to-cell Jaccard similarity can be computed directly on genome-wide accessibility, without population-level peak annotation prior to clustering. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Binarizes genome-wide scATAC-seq accessibility into cell-by-bin matrices (e.g., 5,000 and 10,000 bp bins stored in a snap AM session) and counts fragments per bin so that cell-to-cell Jaccard similarity can be computed directly on genome-wide accessibility, without population-level peak annotation prior to clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-by-cell feature matrix or count table from a peak-aware pipeline (e.g., CellRanger-ATAC) — binarization of genome-wide bins is redundant and the peak matrix can be used directly The analysis requires quantitative count depth (e.g., differential accessibility testing on counts) rather than binary accessibility similarity — binarization discards per-bin fragment counts The data are single-cell RNA-seq or other non-accessibility assays — the snap AM session and Jaccard framework are designed for ATAC-seq fragments

skills.description: Use when snATAC-seq-derived distal CRE BED files (chromosome, start, stop, condition) must be assigned to their cell type of origin using motif-count features rather than sequence-based deep learning.
skills.name: binary-and-multiclass-cell-type-classification
skills.search_text: binary-and-multiclass-cell-type-classification Use when snATAC-seq-derived distal CRE BED files (chromosome, start, stop, condition) must be assigned to their cell type of origin using motif-count features rather than sequence-based deep learning. The question requires regulatory information beyond the input sequence (e.g. open chromatin status or enhancer activity influenced by regions outside the CRE), since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence. The regulatory code depends on motif order, orientation, or spacing (motif grammar), which the unordered bag-of-motifs representation ignores. Sequences of interest contain TF binding patterns not captured by current motif annotations in the provided MEME file, since reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Trains XGBoost gradient-boosted tree models on bag-of-motifs (unordered motif counts) representations of distal CREs to classify cell-type-specific regulatory elements, both pairwise binary and multiclass, as implemented in the BOM R package. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Trains XGBoost gradient-boosted tree models on bag-of-motifs (unordered motif counts) representations of distal CREs to classify cell-type-specific regulatory elements, both pairwise binary and multiclass, as implemented in the BOM R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question requires regulatory information beyond the input sequence (e.g. open chromatin status or enhancer activity influenced by regions outside the CRE), since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence. The regulatory code depends on motif order, orientation, or spacing (motif grammar), which the unordered bag-of-motifs representation ignores. Sequences of interest contain TF binding patterns not captured by current motif annotations in the provided MEME file, since reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences.

skills.search_text: binary-classification-auroc-auprc-evaluation Use when comparing binary classification models on DNALONGBENCH tasks such as enhancer-target gene prediction, where AUROC and AUPRC on a held-out test split are the benchmark metrics. skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is not binary classification — contact map prediction, regulatory sequence activity, and transcription initiation signals use different output shapes and metrics than AUROC/AUPRC Evaluation on short-range DNA tasks (e.g., GenomicBenchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE) that the paper distinguishes from its long-range benchmark Comparing against transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — the paper explicitly excluded these since quadratic self-attention is infeasible for 450,000 bp inputs

skills.description: Use when converting mapped single-end short reads (BED/ELAND) into a binned genome-wide coverage profile for peak calling, especially when fragment sizes are only approximately known from size selection.
skills.name: binned-genome-coverage-construction
skills.search_text: binned-genome-coverage-construction Use when converting mapped single-end short reads (BED/ELAND) into a binned genome-wide coverage profile for peak calling, especially when fragment sizes are only approximately known from size selection. The input is already pair-end with confident insert sizes handled natively — HPeak's pair-end mode (-pe -isize) treats both ends as one fragment and does not need directional extension with uncertain ends The goal is histone-modification comparative analysis across conditions — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to comparative histone data, whereas HPeak targets TF binding-site enriched regions Coverage must distinguish read orientation within peaks — the article states the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs a genome-wide ChIP-Seq coverage profile by directionally extending each mapped short read into a hypothetical DNA fragment (HDF), counting HDFs per fixed 25 bp bin, and applying HPeak's unbalanced end-weighting so uncertain fragment ends contribute decaying coverage. This accounts for fragment-length uncertainty before HMM-based peak calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Reconstructs a genome-wide ChIP-Seq coverage profile by directionally extending each mapped short read into a hypothetical DNA fragment (HDF), counting HDFs per fixed 25 bp bin, and applying HPeak's unbalanced end-weighting so uncertain fragment ends contribute decaying coverage. This accounts for fragment-length uncertainty before HMM-based peak calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already pair-end with confident insert sizes handled natively — HPeak's pair-end mode (-pe -isize) treats both ends as one fragment and does not need directional extension with uncertain ends The goal is histone-modification comparative analysis across conditions — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to comparative histone data, whereas HPeak targets TF binding-site enriched regions Coverage must distinguish read orientation within peaks — the article states the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak

skills.name: binomial-hypothesis-testing
skills.search_text: binomial-hypothesis-testing Use when counting strand-annotated feature occurrences (same vs opposite orientation) yields success/failure counts and you need a P-value for deviation from p = 0.5, e.g., motif-in-region strand bias tests. The data are continuous measurements rather than discrete same/opposite strand counts, so a binomial success/failure model does not apply You need empirical P-values that account for genomic covariates (e.g., regional GC or mappability) rather than a fixed p = 0.5 null; consider Asymmetron's permutation simulations instead You are testing a single feature with no multiplicity, so Bonferroni correction would be unnecessarily conservative http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Two-tailed binomial test used within Asymmetron to assess whether observed same/opposite strand asymmetry ratios of genomic features (e.g., Alu repeats within protein-coding genes) deviate significantly from an unbiased expectation, with Bonferroni correction for multiple tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052

skills.description: Use when reproducing or extending DESSO's TFBS identification step, where motif instance candidates from a CNN motif detector must be statistically assessed with binomial P-values at varying signal cutoffs instead of a fixed subjective cutoff.
skills.name: binomial-significance-testing
skills.search_text: binomial-significance-testing Use when reproducing or extending DESSO's TFBS identification step, where motif instance candidates from a CNN motif detector must be statistically assessed with binomial P-values at varying signal cutoffs instead of a fixed subjective cutoff. The analysis goal is training the CNN or predicting motif patterns themselves — this skill only covers post-prediction statistical selection of motif instances (TFBSs), not model training or motif discovery via predict.py. Motif detectors come from tools other than DESSO (e.g. DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP) whose outputs are not motif-instance candidate sets at a cutoff grid compatible with Omega(M, lambda) construction. The question concerns DNA shape integration or GCNN binding specificity prediction, which are separate DESSO workflows in the README. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reconstruct DESSO's binomial-distribution statistical model, which replaces a subjective motif signal cutoff with the selection of TFBS candidate sets whose binomial P-value is minimal, enabling objective motif instance identification from CNN motif detectors. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Reconstruct DESSO's binomial-distribution statistical model, which replaces a subjective motif signal cutoff with the selection of TFBS candidate sets whose binomial P-value is minimal, enabling objective motif instance identification from CNN motif detectors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is training the CNN or predicting motif patterns themselves — this skill only covers post-prediction statistical selection of motif instances (TFBSs), not model training or motif discovery via predict.py. Motif detectors come from tools other than DESSO (e.g. DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP) whose outputs are not motif-instance candidate sets at a cutoff grid compatible with Omega(M, lambda) construction. The question concerns DNA shape integration or GCNN binding specificity prediction, which are separate DESSO workflows in the README.

skills.description: Use when you have BED files with '+'/'-' strand annotations for both motifs (e.g., TFBS occurrences) and regions (e.g., GENCODE transcribed regions) and need to quantify orientation bias per motif with statistical significance.
skills.name: binomial-strand-orientation-testing
skills.search_text: binomial-strand-orientation-testing Use when you have BED files with '+'/'-' strand annotations for both motifs (e.g., TFBS occurrences) and regions (e.g., GENCODE transcribed regions) and need to quantify orientation bias per motif with statistical significance. The motif is palindromic (e.g., some restriction-site-like motifs) since it cannot be meaningfully oriented relative to the region strand Features lack strand annotation and no overlapping strand-assigned feature is available for orientation assignment (use Asymmetron's separate 'orientation' function first) You need empirical rather than binomial P-values — in that case use Asymmetron's permutation simulations (default N = 1000 random '+'/'-' assignments) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Tests whether strand-annotated motifs (e.g., TFBSs) are non-randomly oriented relative to strand-annotated genomic regions (e.g., transcribed gene regions) using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries overlap classification followed by a two-tailed binomial test with Bonferroni correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Tests whether strand-annotated motifs (e.g., TFBSs) are non-randomly oriented relative to strand-annotated genomic regions (e.g., transcribed gene regions) using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries overlap classification followed by a two-tailed binomial test with Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The motif is palindromic (e.g., some restriction-site-like motifs) since it cannot be meaningfully oriented relative to the region strand Features lack strand annotation and no overlapping strand-assigned feature is available for orientation assignment (use Asymmetron's separate 'orientation' function first) You need empirical rather than binomial P-values — in that case use Asymmetron's permutation simulations (default N = 1000 random '+'/'-' assignments) instead

skills.description: Use when a strand-orientation count (e.g. template vs non-template or vs lagging occurrences of breakpoints or motifs) must be tested against a background orientation probability, with multiple element classes tested simultaneously.
skills.name: binomial-test-with-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: binomial-test-with-bonferroni-correction Use when a strand-orientation count (e.g. template vs non-template or vs lagging occurrences of breakpoints or motifs) must be tested against a background orientation probability, with multiple element classes tested simultaneously. Data are already strand-annotated and only orientation assignment is needed (use the Asymmetron orientation/Pybedtools step instead of this statistical test). The null hypothesis is a symmetric 0.5 probability but the feature class has a known intrinsic orientation preference — using the default binomial P without substituting the background probability would inflate significance. Permutation-based empirical P-values are required rather than a parametric binomial test (Asymmetron separately offers N=1000 permutation simulations). Two-tailed binomial significance testing of strand asymmetry ratios, using each element class's background asymmetry probability as the null probability instead of the default 0.5, followed by Bonferroni correction for multiple tests. This is the statistical core used by Asymmetron to call transcriptional and replicative strand biases (e.g. of germline SV breakpoints at LINE/SINE elements). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Two-tailed binomial significance testing of strand asymmetry ratios, using each element class's background asymmetry probability as the null probability instead of the default 0.5, followed by Bonferroni correction for multiple tests. This is the statistical core used by Asymmetron to call transcriptional and replicative strand biases (e.g. of germline SV breakpoints at LINE/SINE elements).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already strand-annotated and only orientation assignment is needed (use the Asymmetron orientation/Pybedtools step instead of this statistical test). The null hypothesis is a symmetric 0.5 probability but the feature class has a known intrinsic orientation preference — using the default binomial P without substituting the background probability would inflate significance. Permutation-based empirical P-values are required rather than a parametric binomial test (Asymmetron separately offers N=1000 permutation simulations).

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0-100% AMP series) and observed methylation levels need PCR-bias correction and calibration across multiple CpGs.
skills.name: bisulfite-amplicon-sequencing-methylation-data-processing
skills.search_text: bisulfite-amplicon-sequencing-methylation-data-processing Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0-100% AMP series) and observed methylation levels need PCR-bias correction and calibration across multiple CpGs.
