Input is raw .ab1 trace files and no individual sample analysis has been run yet — the Grouped analysis requires individually analyzed samples Only a single sample is available — group comparison statistics require at least two groups of samples You need genomic-coordinate visualization for a sequence not in a reference genome — use the arbitrary-genome FAQ workflow instead of expecting correct coordinates in grouped plots/tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Aggregate individually analyzed BSP samples into group comparisons with ABSP's Shiny 'Grouped analysis' tab, computing two-by-two Student's t-tests on per-CpG methylation and generating boxplots, lollipop plots, and significance-annotated methylation profile plots. It converts per-sample methylation tables into group-level statistics and publication-ready graphics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: Aggregate individually analyzed BSP samples into group comparisons with ABSP's Shiny 'Grouped analysis' tab, computing two-by-two Student's t-tests on per-CpG methylation and generating boxplots, lollipop plots, and significance-annotated methylation profile plots. It converts per-sample methylation tables into group-level statistics and publication-ready graphics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw .ab1 trace files and no individual sample analysis has been run yet — the Grouped analysis requires individually analyzed samples Only a single sample is available — group comparison statistics require at least two groups of samples You need genomic-coordinate visualization for a sequence not in a reference genome — use the arbitrary-genome FAQ workflow instead of expecting correct coordinates in grouped plots/tables

skills.description: Use when validating or benchmarking an epiallele inference method on RRBS-style data and you need synthetic reads at a single locus with known ground-truth epialleles, mixing proportions, and a specified noise probability.
skills.name: bisulfite-sequencing-read-simulation
skills.search_text: bisulfite-sequencing-read-simulation Use when validating or benchmarking an epiallele inference method on RRBS-style data and you need synthetic reads at a single locus with known ground-truth epialleles, mixing proportions, and a specified noise probability. The goal is analysis of real RRBS tumour data rather than controlled validation with known ground-truth epialleles The locus has fewer CpGs than the model's simulated setting (e.g. <6 CpGs) or the reads are already phased and error-free, so noise-corrupted simulation adds no benchmarking value http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Simulates binary bisulfite sequencing reads over a single locus to benchmark Bayesian epiallele detection: generating a read matrix from known underlying epialleles with controlled noise (e.g. ε=0.05) so that recovery of epiallele number, patterns, and noise level can be quantified. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Simulates binary bisulfite sequencing reads over a single locus to benchmark Bayesian epiallele detection: generating a read matrix from known underlying epialleles with controlled noise (e.g. ε=0.05) so that recovery of epiallele number, patterns, and noise level can be quantified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is analysis of real RRBS tumour data rather than controlled validation with known ground-truth epialleles The locus has fewer CpGs than the model's simulated setting (e.g. <6 CpGs) or the reads are already phased and error-free, so noise-corrupted simulation adds no benchmarking value

skills.description: Use when you have BIT rank tables from cancer-type-specific accessible regions and need to determine which top-ranked TRs are functionally essential via DepMap CRISPR Chronos knockout scores.
skills.name: bit-rank-table-parsing
skills.search_text: bit-rank-table-parsing Use when you have BIT rank tables from cancer-type-specific accessible regions and need to determine which top-ranked TRs are functionally essential via DepMap CRISPR Chronos knockout scores. When the query region set has not yet been scored by BIT — run the BIT Bayesian hierarchical model first to obtain TR, BIT_score, and Rank columns When assessing TR essentiality by gene expression or survival (e.g., Kaplan-Meier plotter correlation) rather than DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 knockout viability When working with scRNA-seq or perturbation-seq data where functional essentiality is not defined by Chronos gene effect scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Parses per-cancer-type BIT output rank tables (TR, BIT_score, Rank columns) and intersects top-ranked transcriptional regulators with DepMap Chronos gene-effect scores to classify functionally essential TRs using the Chronos < -0.4 threshold. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Parses per-cancer-type BIT output rank tables (TR, BIT_score, Rank columns) and intersects top-ranked transcriptional regulators with DepMap Chronos gene-effect scores to classify functionally essential TRs using the Chronos < -0.4 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query region set has not yet been scored by BIT — run the BIT Bayesian hierarchical model first to obtain TR, BIT_score, and Rank columns When assessing TR essentiality by gene expression or survival (e.g., Kaplan-Meier plotter correlation) rather than DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 knockout viability When working with scRNA-seq or perturbation-seq data where functional essentiality is not defined by Chronos gene effect scores

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq peak lists for two chromatin marks have been intersected (e.g. H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 MACS peaks in mESCs) and you must assign peaks to genes and biologically characterize bivalent targets.
skills.name: bivalent-chromatin-mark-interpretation
skills.search_text: bivalent-chromatin-mark-interpretation Use when ChIP-seq peak lists for two chromatin marks have been intersected (e.g. H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 MACS peaks in mESCs) and you must assign peaks to genes and biologically characterize bivalent targets. When peaks come from only a single histone mark rather than an overlap of activating and repressive marks — this skill's premise is co-marking (bivalency), not general ChIP-seq annotation When the goal is genome-wide signal visualization (meta-plots, heatmaps, boxplots) rather than peak-to-gene assignment and functional enrichment — SeqCode's produceTSSmaps/producePEAKplots tools are the appropriate choice instead When the genome assembly has no RefSeq annotation available, since matchpeaksgenes relies on RefSeq transcript annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Interprets genomic regions co-marked by activating and repressive histone marks (e.g. H3K4me3+H3K27me3 bivalent peaks in mESCs) by mapping overlapping MACS peaks to nearby genes with SeqCode and testing the resulting gene set for developmental GO enrichment via Enrichr. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Interprets genomic regions co-marked by activating and repressive histone marks (e.g. H3K4me3+H3K27me3 bivalent peaks in mESCs) by mapping overlapping MACS peaks to nearby genes with SeqCode and testing the resulting gene set for developmental GO enrichment via Enrichr.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peaks come from only a single histone mark rather than an overlap of activating and repressive marks — this skill's premise is co-marking (bivalency), not general ChIP-seq annotation When the goal is genome-wide signal visualization (meta-plots, heatmaps, boxplots) rather than peak-to-gene assignment and functional enrichment — SeqCode's produceTSSmaps/producePEAKplots tools are the appropriate choice instead When the genome assembly has no RefSeq annotation available, since matchpeaksgenes relies on RefSeq transcript annotations

skills.description: Use when two ChIP-seq peak lists (e.g. BED files of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 peaks from Beringer et al., GSM2098958 and GSM2098952) must be partitioned into mutually exclusive active, bivalent, and silent site classes via overlap.
skills.name: bivalent-chromatin-state-annotation
skills.search_text: bivalent-chromatin-state-annotation Use when two ChIP-seq peak lists (e.g. BED files of H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 peaks from Beringer et al., GSM2098958 and GSM2098952) must be partitioned into mutually exclusive active, bivalent, and silent site classes via overlap. Input consists of raw sequencing reads or BigWig signal tracks rather than already-called peak lists — peak calling (MACS) must be done first, and SeqCode defers BigWig generation to future versions. The two peak sets come from different genome assemblies (mm9 vs mm10) without prior coordinate liftover, since overlap comparison requires consistent coordinates. The goal is graphical visualization of signal around peaks (meta-plots, heatmaps) rather than set-overlap classification of peak coordinates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Classifies mESC H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peak sets into active (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3–), bivalent (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+), and silent (H3K4me3–/H3K27me3+) classes by computing genomic overlap between the two peak lists with SeqCode's matchpeaks command. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Classifies mESC H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peak sets into active (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3–), bivalent (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+), and silent (H3K4me3–/H3K27me3+) classes by computing genomic overlap between the two peak lists with SeqCode's matchpeaks command.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of raw sequencing reads or BigWig signal tracks rather than already-called peak lists — peak calling (MACS) must be done first, and SeqCode defers BigWig generation to future versions. The two peak sets come from different genome assemblies (mm9 vs mm10) without prior coordinate liftover, since overlap comparison requires consistent coordinates. The goal is graphical visualization of signal around peaks (meta-plots, heatmaps) rather than set-overlap classification of peak coordinates.

skills.description: Use when paired treated/control ChIP-Seq aligned reads must be classified into ChIP-enriched versus background bins via an HMM whose emissions model both channels simultaneously (GP for enriched, ZIP for background).
skills.name: bivariate-gp-zip-paired-sample-classification
skills.search_text: bivariate-gp-zip-paired-sample-classification Use when paired treated/control ChIP-Seq aligned reads must be classified into ChIP-enriched versus background bins via an HMM whose emissions model both channels simultaneously (GP for enriched, ZIP for background). Input is a single-sample ChIP-Seq experiment with no matched control reads — the univariate GP/ZIP HMM variant suffices; the bivariate extension requires both channels Data are comparative histone-modification tracks from a method like ChIPDiff rather than read-level ChIP-Seq alignment data The goal is quantifying a false detection rate — the paper notes its method is not well-suited for quantifying FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extend HPeak's two-state HMM to paired ChIP treatment/control data by classifying fixed-length 25 bp bins jointly from both read channels, using a bivariate Generalized Poisson emission for ChIP-enriched bins and a bivariate zero-inflated Poisson emission for background bins. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Extend HPeak's two-state HMM to paired ChIP treatment/control data by classifying fixed-length 25 bp bins jointly from both read channels, using a bivariate Generalized Poisson emission for ChIP-enriched bins and a bivariate zero-inflated Poisson emission for background bins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-sample ChIP-Seq experiment with no matched control reads — the univariate GP/ZIP HMM variant suffices; the bivariate extension requires both channels Data are comparative histone-modification tracks from a method like ChIPDiff rather than read-level ChIP-Seq alignment data The goal is quantifying a false detection rate — the paper notes its method is not well-suited for quantifying FDR

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples (e.g. SHR vs BN rat heart H3K27me3) for broad, diffuse histone marks where peak-style callers produce false positives/negatives, and per-bin probabilistic differential calls are needed.
skills.name: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-differential-calling
skills.search_text: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-differential-calling Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples (e.g. SHR vs BN rat heart H3K27me3) for broad, diffuse histone marks where peak-style callers produce false positives/negatives, and per-bin probabilistic differential calls are needed. The histone mark has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods searching for peak-like features are the article's stated contrast, and narrow-peak callers are more appropriate Input is already a binned read-count table with no need for re-binning or duplicate removal, and only the HMM fitting/calling step is required More than two samples must be compared simultaneously — the histoneHMM bivariate model is designed for a two-sample comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply histoneHMM, a bivariate Hidden Markov Model implemented in R/C++, to call differentially modified regions between two ChIP-seq samples for broad histone marks such as H3K27me3, by aggregating short reads into 1000 bp genomic bins and classifying each bin as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Apply histoneHMM, a bivariate Hidden Markov Model implemented in R/C++, to call differentially modified regions between two ChIP-seq samples for broad histone marks such as H3K27me3, by aggregating short reads into 1000 bp genomic bins and classifying each bin as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The histone mark has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods searching for peak-like features are the article's stated contrast, and narrow-peak callers are more appropriate Input is already a binned read-count table with no need for re-binning or duplicate removal, and only the HMM fitting/calling step is required More than two samples must be compared simultaneously — the histoneHMM bivariate model is designed for a two-sample comparison

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples for a broad, diffuse histone modification and you need genome-wide calls of differentially modified regions rather than peak-like enrichment calls.
skills.name: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-fitting
skills.search_text: bivariate-hidden-markov-model-fitting Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of two samples for a broad, diffuse histone modification and you need genome-wide calls of differentially modified regions rather than peak-like enrichment calls. The histone mark produces sharp peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods designed for peak-like features were noted by the authors to behave poorly on broad marks, and this skill's rationale is specific to broad footprints like H3K27me3 Only a single sample is available and no pairwise comparison is intended in a differential two-sample setting (a univariate mode exists via run.univariate.hmm, but this skill is the bivariate two-sample fitting) Input is already a feature/region table or peak set rather than aligned short-read data, since the model requires binned bivariate read counts as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Fit the histoneHMM bivariate Hidden Markov Model on binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts from two samples to probabilistically classify 1000 bp genomic bins as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified. Designed for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) where peak-calling methods perform poorly. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Fit the histoneHMM bivariate Hidden Markov Model on binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts from two samples to probabilistically classify 1000 bp genomic bins as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified. Designed for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) where peak-calling methods perform poorly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The histone mark produces sharp peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods designed for peak-like features were noted by the authors to behave poorly on broad marks, and this skill's rationale is specific to broad footprints like H3K27me3 Only a single sample is available and no pairwise comparison is intended in a differential two-sample setting (a univariate mode exists via run.univariate.hmm, but this skill is the bivariate two-sample fitting) Input is already a feature/region table or peak set rather than aligned short-read data, since the model requires binned bivariate read counts as input

skills.description: Use when input peak files (BED/GRanges, e.g. ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag peaks) must be cleaned of anomalous-signal regions before comparison/QC, and when a blacklist-overlap percentage metric is needed per sample.
skills.name: blacklisted-genomic-region-removal
skills.search_text: blacklisted-genomic-region-removal Use when input peak files (BED/GRanges, e.g. ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag peaks) must be cleaned of anomalous-signal regions before comparison/QC, and when a blacklist-overlap percentage metric is needed per sample. Input is already a blacklist-filtered/standard-chromosome-only peak file — re-running would double-report the blacklist percentage against an already-tidied file Analysis goal is not peak QC/benchmarking but, e.g., sequence-level variant filtering — the blacklist removal here applies only to epigenomic peak intervals Genome build is not hg19 or hg38 and no user-supplied blacklist equivalent is available http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Remove peak intervals overlapping ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions (hg19 or hg38) from epigenomic peak files as EpiCompare's first quality-control step, and report the percentage of peaks falling in blacklist regions in the General Metrics section of the HTML report. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Remove peak intervals overlapping ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions (hg19 or hg38) from epigenomic peak files as EpiCompare's first quality-control step, and report the percentage of peaks falling in blacklist regions in the General Metrics section of the HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a blacklist-filtered/standard-chromosome-only peak file — re-running would double-report the blacklist percentage against an already-tidied file Analysis goal is not peak QC/benchmarking but, e.g., sequence-level variant filtering — the blacklist removal here applies only to epigenomic peak intervals Genome build is not hg19 or hg38 and no user-supplied blacklist equivalent is available

skills.description: Use when testing overlap/enrichment between two genomic range sets (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks, caQTLs, CREs) and a null distribution is needed that preserves local genomic correlation structure rather than shuffling ranges.
skills.name: block-bootstrap-null-range-generation
skills.search_text: block-bootstrap-null-range-generation Use when testing overlap/enrichment between two genomic range sets (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks, caQTLs, CREs) and a null distribution is needed that preserves local genomic correlation structure rather than shuffling ranges. When the range sets have no local genomic correlation structure to preserve, so simple shuffling is an acceptable null When the downstream analysis is not range-overlap/enrichment hypothesis testing (e.g. DEG logFC threshold optimization via generalized splines, macrophage.R, or multiome mean correlation, multiomicsCor.R), where bootRanges is applied differently http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Generates null sets of genomic ranges via block bootstrapping with the bootRanges function from the R/Bioconductor nullranges package, preserving local genomic correlation structure for enrichment and hypothesis testing. Contrasts with conventional shuffling/permutation, which yields overly narrow null distributions and inflated false positive rates. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Generates null sets of genomic ranges via block bootstrapping with the bootRanges function from the R/Bioconductor nullranges package, preserving local genomic correlation structure for enrichment and hypothesis testing. Contrasts with conventional shuffling/permutation, which yields overly narrow null distributions and inflated false positive rates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the range sets have no local genomic correlation structure to preserve, so simple shuffling is an acceptable null When the downstream analysis is not range-overlap/enrichment hypothesis testing (e.g. DEG logFC threshold optimization via generalized splines, macrophage.R, or multiome mean correlation, multiomicsCor.R), where bootRanges is applied differently

skills.description: Use when training RoboCOP's multivariate HMM to compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy of nucleosomes and ~150 TFs from MNase-seq or ATAC-seq accessibility plus nucleotide sequence, and you must initialize the transition matrix before Baum-Welch learning.
skills.name: boltzmann-transition-probability-initialization
skills.search_text: boltzmann-transition-probability-initialization Use when training RoboCOP's multivariate HMM to compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy of nucleosomes and ~150 TFs from MNase-seq or ATAC-seq accessibility plus nucleotide sequence, and you must initialize the transition matrix before Baum-Welch learning. Do not use as a generic HMM initializer for unrelated models — the two-standard-deviation cap on TF transitions is specific to RoboCOP's multivariate chromatin occupancy HMM and its ~150-TF state space. Do not reach for this when the analysis goal is peak calling plus TF labeling (MACS2 + FIMO alternative) rather than joint probabilistic occupancy computation via a hidden Markov model. Do not expect prior/experimentally measured transition probabilities to be incorporated — the article explicitly defers incorporation of prior DBF transition information to future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Initializes the transition probabilities of RoboCOP's multivariate hidden Markov model with a Boltzmann distribution, providing the starting point for Baum-Welch EM learning of TF and nucleosome transition probabilities in the joint chromatin occupancy model. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Initializes the transition probabilities of RoboCOP's multivariate hidden Markov model with a Boltzmann distribution, providing the starting point for Baum-Welch EM learning of TF and nucleosome transition probabilities in the joint chromatin occupancy model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not use as a generic HMM initializer for unrelated models — the two-standard-deviation cap on TF transitions is specific to RoboCOP's multivariate chromatin occupancy HMM and its ~150-TF state space. Do not reach for this when the analysis goal is peak calling plus TF labeling (MACS2 + FIMO alternative) rather than joint probabilistic occupancy computation via a hidden Markov model. Do not expect prior/experimentally measured transition probabilities to be incorporated — the article explicitly defers incorporation of prior DBF transition information to future work.

skills.description: Use when many p-values are produced simultaneously (e.g., 48 K-S tests per lane pair on genome-partitioned read distributions) and per-combination significance calls must be corrected for multiple testing.
skills.name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when many p-values are produced simultaneously (e.g., 48 K-S tests per lane pair on genome-partitioned read distributions) and per-combination significance calls must be corrected for multiple testing. Only one hypothesis test is being run, so no family-wise correction is needed The p-values come from different, unrelated families of tests — pooling them into one Bonferroni correction would be overly conservative and not what the assessment prescribes (correction is applied within each lane pair) The goal is peak calling on ChIP-Seq read data itself (e.g., HPeak HMM-based enrichment), rather than calling significance on genome-partitioned test statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_3489 Applies Bonferroni correction to control the family-wise error rate when many statistical tests are run in parallel, e.g., two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests across 48 chromosome/strand combinations per ChIP-Seq lane pair, using a significance threshold of 0.001 to call significant discrepancies. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Applies Bonferroni correction to control the family-wise error rate when many statistical tests are run in parallel, e.g., two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests across 48 chromosome/strand combinations per ChIP-Seq lane pair, using a significance threshold of 0.001 to call significant discrepancies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one hypothesis test is being run, so no family-wise correction is needed The p-values come from different, unrelated families of tests — pooling them into one Bonferroni correction would be overly conservative and not what the assessment prescribes (correction is applied within each lane pair) The goal is peak calling on ChIP-Seq read data itself (e.g., HPeak HMM-based enrichment), rather than calling significance on genome-partitioned test statistics

skills.description: Use when a strand asymmetry analysis produces many P-values from repeated two-tailed binomial tests (p = 0.5 expected asymmetry) and you need Bonferroni-corrected significance for each feature (TF PWM, motif, repeat class, ChIP-seq peak set).
skills.name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction Use when a strand asymmetry analysis produces many P-values from repeated two-tailed binomial tests (p = 0.5 expected asymmetry) and you need Bonferroni-corrected significance for each feature (TF PWM, motif, repeat class, ChIP-seq peak set). Only a single asymmetry comparison is being run — Bonferroni is unnecessary and needlessly conservative (Asymmetron applies it 'in case of multiple tests') The analysis calls for an empirical/permutation-based null instead — Asymmetron separately supports N = 1000 random-strand simulations for empirical P-values, which is a distinct procedure P-values are already adjusted with a different multiple-testing method; re-correcting would double-penalize http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Bonferroni adjustment of two-tailed binomial test P-values across the many strand-asymmetry comparisons performed by Asymmetron (e.g., dozens of TF PWMs, ChIP-seq experiments, or repeat classes), so that reported orientation biases like the 45% of TFs with significant DNA strand bias survive multiple-testing correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Bonferroni adjustment of two-tailed binomial test P-values across the many strand-asymmetry comparisons performed by Asymmetron (e.g., dozens of TF PWMs, ChIP-seq experiments, or repeat classes), so that reported orientation biases like the 45% of TFs with significant DNA strand bias survive multiple-testing correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single asymmetry comparison is being run — Bonferroni is unnecessary and needlessly conservative (Asymmetron applies it 'in case of multiple tests') The analysis calls for an empirical/permutation-based null instead — Asymmetron separately supports N = 1000 random-strand simulations for empirical P-values, which is a distinct procedure P-values are already adjusted with a different multiple-testing method; re-correcting would double-penalize

skills.description: Use when reporting a point estimate of entropy decrease (or similar per-cluster statistic) after DGW warping and you need an uncertainty range, e.g. mean 1.72% TSS decrease with a 95% bootstrap CI of 0.83–2.81%.
skills.name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
skills.search_text: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation Use when reporting a point estimate of entropy decrease (or similar per-cluster statistic) after DGW warping and you need an uncertainty range, e.g. mean 1.72% TSS decrease with a 95% bootstrap CI of 0.83–2.81%. Data has not been clustered and warped by DGW yet — there are no warped vs raw distributions to compare entropies over The statistic of interest is not expressible as a per-cluster (or resamplable) quantity, e.g. a single global value with no sampling units to bootstrap http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Quantifies uncertainty in DGW alignment quality metrics by bootstrapping the entropy decrease of TSS and FSS location distributions over clusters, yielding 95% confidence intervals for mean percent entropy reduction. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Quantifies uncertainty in DGW alignment quality metrics by bootstrapping the entropy decrease of TSS and FSS location distributions over clusters, yielding 95% confidence intervals for mean percent entropy reduction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data has not been clustered and warped by DGW yet — there are no warped vs raw distributions to compare entropies over The statistic of interest is not expressible as a per-cluster (or resamplable) quantity, e.g. a single global value with no sampling units to bootstrap

skills.description: Use when a benchmark metric is a proportion derived from a finite set of significant peaks (e.g., motif-proximal peak fraction) and its sampling uncertainty must be reported as a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for method comparison.
skills.name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
skills.search_text: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation Use when a benchmark metric is a proportion derived from a finite set of significant peaks (e.g., motif-proximal peak fraction) and its sampling uncertainty must be reported as a 95% bootstrap confidence interval for method comparison. When the comparison target is a per-position quantity (fits, standard errors, log p-values) rather than a summary statistic over a finite peak set — use plotGenoGAM()/pval(result) inspection instead When no motif center annotations are available for the factor, since the 30 bp motif-proximity proportion cannot be defined When the goal is runtime or memory benchmarking of GenoGAM 2.0 rather than peak-summit positioning quality http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies uncertainty in derived ChIP-Seq peak statistics by resampling significant peaks and computing 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, as used in the GenoGAM 2.0 peak-summit positioning benchmark (Fig. 5c) to report, per transcription factor, the proportion of significant peaks within 30 bp of the motif center. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Quantifies uncertainty in derived ChIP-Seq peak statistics by resampling significant peaks and computing 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, as used in the GenoGAM 2.0 peak-summit positioning benchmark (Fig. 5c) to report, per transcription factor, the proportion of significant peaks within 30 bp of the motif center.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the comparison target is a per-position quantity (fits, standard errors, log p-values) rather than a summary statistic over a finite peak set — use plotGenoGAM()/pval(result) inspection instead When no motif center annotations are available for the factor, since the 30 bp motif-proximity proportion cannot be defined When the goal is runtime or memory benchmarking of GenoGAM 2.0 rather than peak-summit positioning quality

skills.description: Use when testing whether an observed overlap between genomic range sets (e.g., caQTL SNPs and peaks, or DEGs and differential accessibility peaks) is significant, and shuffling-based nulls may be too narrow.
skills.name: bootstrap-null-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: bootstrap-null-distribution-analysis Use when testing whether an observed overlap between genomic range sets (e.g., caQTL SNPs and peaks, or DEGs and differential accessibility peaks) is significant, and shuffling-based nulls may be too narrow. Shuffling or permutation nulls are acceptable because local genomic correlation structure is not a concern — the paper shows such schemes may yield overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance, which is exactly what this skill avoids. The analysis involves conventional genomic-feature shuffling workflows such as the bootstrap.R conventional-shuffling step rather than block-bootstrap nulls. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantify enrichment of overlapping genomic ranges by standardizing an observed statistic (e.g., overlap rate or spline-fitted overlap count) against a block-bootstrap null distribution generated with bootRanges, yielding a z-score instead of relying on shuffling or permutation p-values. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Quantify enrichment of overlapping genomic ranges by standardizing an observed statistic (e.g., overlap rate or spline-fitted overlap count) against a block-bootstrap null distribution generated with bootRanges, yielding a z-score instead of relying on shuffling or permutation p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Shuffling or permutation nulls are acceptable because local genomic correlation structure is not a concern — the paper shows such schemes may yield overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance, which is exactly what this skill avoids. The analysis involves conventional genomic-feature shuffling workflows such as the bootstrap.R conventional-shuffling step rather than block-bootstrap nulls.

skills.description: Use when short paired-end or single-end methylation sequencing reads (36-100 bp FASTQ, e.g., SHERMAN-simulated TAPS data) must be aligned to a reference genome such as hg19 as the core step of a bisulfite or bisulfite-free methylation analysis.
skills.name: bowtie2-based-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: bowtie2-based-short-read-alignment Use when short paired-end or single-end methylation sequencing reads (36-100 bp FASTQ, e.g., SHERMAN-simulated TAPS data) must be aligned to a reference genome such as hg19 as the core step of a bisulfite or bisulfite-free methylation analysis. Input reads are from a BS-seq (bisulfite) library: the README mandates 3-letter mode with `-m BS`, so running the 4-letter alignment would be incorrect. The library has substantial non-CpG methylation: 4-letter mode ONLY supports processing of TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low (e.g., most somatic tissues in human). The goal is to validate 4-letter accuracy at inconsistent CpG sites — the article explicitly lacks strong evidence that the 4-letter mode is more accurate there, so this skill cannot serve as that validation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Aligns methylation sequencing reads (BS-seq or TAPS) to a reference genome using bowtie2 as the underline aligner inside Msuite's 3-letter (C-to-T converted) or 4-letter alignment mode, producing the SAM/BAM alignments that feed methylation calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Aligns methylation sequencing reads (BS-seq or TAPS) to a reference genome using bowtie2 as the underline aligner inside Msuite's 3-letter (C-to-T converted) or 4-letter alignment mode, producing the SAM/BAM alignments that feed methylation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are from a BS-seq (bisulfite) library: the README mandates 3-letter mode with `-m BS`, so running the 4-letter alignment would be incorrect. The library has substantial non-CpG methylation: 4-letter mode ONLY supports processing of TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low (e.g., most somatic tissues in human). The goal is to validate 4-letter accuracy at inconsistent CpG sites — the article explicitly lacks strong evidence that the 4-letter mode is more accurate there, so this skill cannot serve as that validation.

skills.name: c-to-t-deamination-signature-detection
skills.search_text: c-to-t-deamination-signature-detection Use when RIMS-seq (alkaline-treated) Illumina paired-end fastq.gz reads from bacteria must be converted into a de novo m5C methylase motif with a significance P-value, e.g. recovering CCWGG from E. coli K12 MG1655 time-course data. The sequencing library was prepared by tagmentation or another non-adapter-ligation protocol, which RIMS-seq explicitly does not support The methylation of interest is not m5C (e.g. m6A or m4C), since the C-to-T deamination signal is specific to 5-methylcytosine Sites have too little read coverage — RIMS-seq signals require enough coverage to compensate for the scarcity of methylated motif sites http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Recover de novo m5C methylase specificity motifs from RIMS-seq data, in which heat-alkaline treatment deaminates methylated cytosines to produce C-to-T signatures detectable in standard Illumina paired-end reads. The skill chains genome assembly, BWA-mem mapping, mpileup read splitting, and MoSDi-based motif discovery. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Recover de novo m5C methylase specificity motifs from RIMS-seq data, in which heat-alkaline treatment deaminates methylated cytosines to produce C-to-T signatures detectable in standard Illumina paired-end reads. The skill chains genome assembly, BWA-mem mapping, mpileup read splitting, and MoSDi-based motif discovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing library was prepared by tagmentation or another non-adapter-ligation protocol, which RIMS-seq explicitly does not support The methylation of interest is not m5C (e.g. m6A or m4C), since the C-to-T deamination signal is specific to 5-methylcytosine Sites have too little read coverage — RIMS-seq signals require enough coverage to compensate for the scarcity of methylated motif sites

skills.description: Use when calling cancer driver candidates with DriverPower and you want to incorporate functional impact evidence (CADD scores) alongside mutational burden tests, on coding or non-coding element sets.
skills.name: cadd-functional-score-integration
skills.search_text: cadd-functional-score-integration Use when calling cancer driver candidates with DriverPower and you want to incorporate functional impact evidence (CADD scores) alongside mutational burden tests, on coding or non-coding element sets. You only need burden-test-only driver calls without functional adjustment — omit --funcScore and call candidates without functional information Input mutations lack hg19 coordinates or CADD-compatible variant identifiers, so per-mutation CADD scores cannot be retrieved or intersected with elements The functional score scheme is not CADD — functional impact score schemes are currently biased toward coding mutations, so non-coding integration may add little signal http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Integrates per-mutation CADD PHRED scores into DriverPower's burden test as a functional impact covariate, aggregating per-element mean CADD scores with bedtools and supplying them via --funcScore/--funcScoreCut to increase driver discovery accuracy. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Integrates per-mutation CADD PHRED scores into DriverPower's burden test as a functional impact covariate, aggregating per-element mean CADD scores with bedtools and supplying them via --funcScore/--funcScoreCut to increase driver discovery accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need burden-test-only driver calls without functional adjustment — omit --funcScore and call candidates without functional information Input mutations lack hg19 coordinates or CADD-compatible variant identifiers, so per-mutation CADD scores cannot be retrieved or intersected with elements The functional score scheme is not CADD — functional impact score schemes are currently biased toward coding mutations, so non-coding integration may add little signal

skills.description: Use when you have sgRNA genomic coordinates (e.g. from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screening tables) and FANTOM CAGE TSS positions, and need TSS-proximity/nucleosome-positioning features per sgRNA for a model or filter.
skills.name: cage-tss-distance-calculation
skills.search_text: cage-tss-distance-calculation Use when you have sgRNA genomic coordinates (e.g. from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screening tables) and FANTOM CAGE TSS positions, and need TSS-proximity/nucleosome-positioning features per sgRNA for a model or filter. You already have a feature matrix containing TSS-distance or nucleosome-positioning columns and only need downstream modeling or normalization. Your input lacks genomic coordinates for sgRNAs (sequence-only input); EpiCas-DL supports sequence-only prediction via CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq models. Cell type or gene is unknown, so primary/secondary CAGE TSS cannot be correctly matched to the target locus. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns each sgRNA target site its distance to FANTOM-derived primary and secondary CAGE transcription start sites (nucleosome positioning features) using pybedtools, as done in EpiCas-DL to enrich sgRNA activity prediction beyond sequence-only models. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Assigns each sgRNA target site its distance to FANTOM-derived primary and secondary CAGE transcription start sites (nucleosome positioning features) using pybedtools, as done in EpiCas-DL to enrich sgRNA activity prediction beyond sequence-only models.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You already have a feature matrix containing TSS-distance or nucleosome-positioning columns and only need downstream modeling or normalization. Your input lacks genomic coordinates for sgRNAs (sequence-only input); EpiCas-DL supports sequence-only prediction via CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq models. Cell type or gene is unknown, so primary/secondary CAGE TSS cannot be correctly matched to the target locus.

skills.description: Use when analyzing bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation data (e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 / H19/IGF2 DMR assays) where PCR bias must be corrected before gain/loss-of-methylation calls are made for patient samples.
skills.name: calibrated-methylation-data-analysis
skills.search_text: calibrated-methylation-data-analysis Use when analyzing bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation data (e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 / H19/IGF2 DMR assays) where PCR bias must be corrected before gain/loss-of-methylation calls are made for patient samples. Data are already corrected methylation levels or come from a platform without a PCR-bias problem (e.g. epigenome-wide arrays) — recalibration adds no value No standard controls with known methylation percentages (0/25/50/75/100%) are available, so calibration curves cannot be derived The goal is one-at-a-time CpG calibration or calibration of the average methylation level, which MethylCal is explicitly designed to avoid http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Applies the MethylCal Bayesian calibration method (R package, INLA-based) to correct PCR-biased methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing, then classifies case samples as hyper-, hypo-, or normally methylated against healthy-control reference intervals. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Applies the MethylCal Bayesian calibration method (R package, INLA-based) to correct PCR-biased methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing, then classifies case samples as hyper-, hypo-, or normally methylated against healthy-control reference intervals.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already corrected methylation levels or come from a platform without a PCR-bias problem (e.g. epigenome-wide arrays) — recalibration adds no value No standard controls with known methylation percentages (0/25/50/75/100%) are available, so calibration curves cannot be derived The goal is one-at-a-time CpG calibration or calibration of the average methylation level, which MethylCal is explicitly designed to avoid

skills.description: Use when pyrosequenced or MiSeq methylation data from standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP 0/25/50/75/100) are available and competing PCR-bias calibration models must be fitted and compared per assay.
skills.name: calibration-model-goodness-of-fit-comparison
skills.search_text: calibration-model-goodness-of-fit-comparison Use when pyrosequenced or MiSeq methylation data from standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP 0/25/50/75/100) are available and competing PCR-bias calibration models must be fitted and compared per assay. When the goal is correcting observed methylation levels of case/control samples with an already-fitted curve — use MoskalevCorrection or MethycalCorrection instead of refitting calibration curves. When data have not yet been reshaped or explored — run Formatting()/TableFormatting() and ExploratoryPlot first, since MethylCal calibration functions require the formatted analysis format. When only a single CpG is of interest and joint-CpG modelling is unnecessary — the skill's advantage comes from jointly modelling all CpGs within a CGI or DMR. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fits and compares candidate calibration curves (Warnecke hyperbolic, Moskalev cubic polynomial regression, and MethylCal's Bayesian mixed additive model) for bisulfite amplicon-sequencing standard controls, selecting the best model per assay by DIC and validating goodness of fit via mlik, DIC, and RSS. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Fits and compares candidate calibration curves (Warnecke hyperbolic, Moskalev cubic polynomial regression, and MethylCal's Bayesian mixed additive model) for bisulfite amplicon-sequencing standard controls, selecting the best model per assay by DIC and validating goodness of fit via mlik, DIC, and RSS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is correcting observed methylation levels of case/control samples with an already-fitted curve — use MoskalevCorrection or MethycalCorrection instead of refitting calibration curves. When data have not yet been reshaped or explored — run Formatting()/TableFormatting() and ExploratoryPlot first, since MethylCal calibration functions require the formatted analysis format. When only a single CpG is of interest and joint-CpG modelling is unnecessary — the skill's advantage comes from jointly modelling all CpGs within a CGI or DMR.

skills.description: Use when you have a defined gene set (e.g. genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) and expression matrices from tumor and matched normal samples, and need per-gene expression ranks and t-test p-values per cancer cohort.
skills.name: cancer-cohort-expression-profiling
skills.search_text: cancer-cohort-expression-profiling Use when you have a defined gene set (e.g. genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) and expression matrices from tumor and matched normal samples, and need per-gene expression ranks and t-test p-values per cancer cohort. The analysis goal is eccDNA identification from WGS data (eccDNAdb's AmpliconArchitect pipeline), not expression-level comparison of already-annotated eccDNA genes No normal/matched control samples exist for the cohort, making a tumor-vs-normal t-test uninterpretable The input is already a differential expression results table rather than a raw per-sample expression matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Profiles gene expression of eccDNA-derived genes across tumor and normal cohorts (TCGA, CCLE) and quantifies per-gene tumor-vs-normal differences with two-tailed Student's t-tests, mirroring the Tumor-vs-Normal box plots with p-values presented in eccDNAdb. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Profiles gene expression of eccDNA-derived genes across tumor and normal cohorts (TCGA, CCLE) and quantifies per-gene tumor-vs-normal differences with two-tailed Student's t-tests, mirroring the Tumor-vs-Normal box plots with p-values presented in eccDNAdb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is eccDNA identification from WGS data (eccDNAdb's AmpliconArchitect pipeline), not expression-level comparison of already-annotated eccDNA genes No normal/matched control samples exist for the cohort, making a tumor-vs-normal t-test uninterpretable The input is already a differential expression results table rather than a raw per-sample expression matrix

skills.search_text: cancer-driver-candidate-comparison-against-reference-catalogs Use when you have a tool-called driver candidate list (e.g. DriverPower [outDir]/[name].result.tsv) and need to benchmark its novelty and error rate against CGC or PCAWG-consensus catalogs. skills.description: Use when a ranked candidate driver gene list (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes per SCNA) needs in silico validation against curated oncogene/tumor suppressor compendia (COSMIC, TUSON, OMIM, UniProt) or DepMap dependency data via one-sided Fisher/hypergeometric enrichment.
skills.name: cancer-driver-gene-curation
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-gene-curation Use when a ranked candidate driver gene list (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes per SCNA) needs in silico validation against curated oncogene/tumor suppressor compendia (COSMIC, TUSON, OMIM, UniProt) or DepMap dependency data via one-sided Fisher/hypergeometric enrichment. Predicting drivers de novo from raw SCNA and gene expression matrices — run construct_iEDGE/run_iEDGE first; this skill only validates an already-ranked driver list. Pathway-level annotation of cis/trans signatures with MSigDB GMTs (h.all.v5.0.symbols.gmt, c2.cp.v5.0.symbols.gmt, c3.tft.v5.0.symbols.gmt) — that is pathway enrichment annotation, not driver-compendia validation. Reference compendia that cannot be direction-labeled as OG/TN, since the Fisher tests stratify Rank-1 overlap by amplified versus deleted alterations. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Curates reference cancer driver gene compendia (COSMIC CGC, TUSON, OMIM, UniProt) with direction-of-alteration labels (OG for amplified, TN for deleted) and in silico validates ranked candidate drivers (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes) by one-sided Fisher exact / hypergeometric enrichment, optionally extending to DepMap DEMETER2 RNAi dependencies versus CCLE copy number. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Curates reference cancer driver gene compendia (COSMIC CGC, TUSON, OMIM, UniProt) with direction-of-alteration labels (OG for amplified, TN for deleted) and in silico validates ranked candidate drivers (e.g., iEDGE Rank-1 cis genes) by one-sided Fisher exact / hypergeometric enrichment, optionally extending to DepMap DEMETER2 RNAi dependencies versus CCLE copy number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Predicting drivers de novo from raw SCNA and gene expression matrices — run construct_iEDGE/run_iEDGE first; this skill only validates an already-ranked driver list. Pathway-level annotation of cis/trans signatures with MSigDB GMTs (h.all.v5.0.symbols.gmt, c2.cp.v5.0.symbols.gmt, c3.tft.v5.0.symbols.gmt) — that is pathway enrichment annotation, not driver-compendia validation. Reference compendia that cannot be direction-labeled as OG/TN, since the Fisher tests stratify Rank-1 overlap by amplified versus deleted alterations.

skills.description: Use when you have processed somatic mutation response tables (nMut, nSample, effective length per element) for coding or non-coding test elements and a pre-trained BMR model, and need to call driver candidates at q < 0.1.
skills.name: cancer-driver-mutation-inference
skills.search_text: cancer-driver-mutation-inference Use when you have processed somatic mutation response tables (nMut, nSample, effective length per element) for coding or non-coding test elements and a pre-trained BMR model, and need to call driver candidates at q < 0.1. You need to train the background mutation model from scratch — use the 'driverpower model' sub-command workflow instead of 'infer'. Your somatic mutations are not in hg19 or are not processed per-element response tables (the example data and tutorial are hg19-based). You expect modelling of negatively selected sites or burden-only calls without functional scores — DriverPower's BMR is trained on predominantly neutral regions and does not model negative selection. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run DriverPower's 'infer' sub-command to identify coding and non-coding cancer driver elements by combining mutational burden tests (binomial/negative binomial) with functional impact scores (e.g. CADD), using a pre-trained background mutation rate (BMR) model. Applied to PCAWG whole-genome data it yields 217 coding and 95 non-coding driver candidates across 2583 genomes. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Run DriverPower's 'infer' sub-command to identify coding and non-coding cancer driver elements by combining mutational burden tests (binomial/negative binomial) with functional impact scores (e.g. CADD), using a pre-trained background mutation rate (BMR) model. Applied to PCAWG whole-genome data it yields 217 coding and 95 non-coding driver candidates across 2583 genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train the background mutation model from scratch — use the 'driverpower model' sub-command workflow instead of 'infer'. Your somatic mutations are not in hg19 or are not processed per-element response tables (the example data and tutorial are hg19-based). You expect modelling of negatively selected sites or burden-only calls without functional scores — DriverPower's BMR is trained on predominantly neutral regions and does not model negative selection.

skills.description: Use when a ranked list of candidate TRs (e.g., BIT scores from TCGA cancer-type-specific accessible regions) must be checked for knockout-validated essentiality using DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos scores per cancer lineage.
skills.name: cancer-lineage-specific-essentiality-thresholding
skills.search_text: cancer-lineage-specific-essentiality-thresholding Use when a ranked list of candidate TRs (e.g., BIT scores from TCGA cancer-type-specific accessible regions) must be checked for knockout-validated essentiality using DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos scores per cancer lineage. The query TRs come from a lineage or tissue not represented in the DepMap Chronos screening data — no lineage-level score exists to threshold. The input is a gene set rather than a ranked TR list; use enrichment-style tools (e.g., BART geneset mode) instead of dependency-score intersection. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates computationally ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) against functional dependency data by intersecting top-ranked BIT TRs with lineage-level DepMap Chronos gene effect scores and classifying a TR as functionally essential when its Chronos score falls below -0.4 in a given cancer lineage. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Validates computationally ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) against functional dependency data by intersecting top-ranked BIT TRs with lineage-level DepMap Chronos gene effect scores and classifying a TR as functionally essential when its Chronos score falls below -0.4 in a given cancer lineage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query TRs come from a lineage or tissue not represented in the DepMap Chronos screening data — no lineage-level score exists to threshold. The input is a gene set rather than a ranked TR list; use enrichment-style tools (e.g., BART geneset mode) instead of dependency-score intersection.

skills.name: capture-hic-significant-interaction-calling
skills.search_text: capture-hic-significant-interaction-calling Use when you have promoter-other (P-O) pcHi-C fragment-pair tables with coverage values, interaction frequencies and distances, and need reproducible significant cis-interaction calls within 15 kb–2 Mb. Input is already a normalized contact map or feature table with significance calls — the skill operates on raw fragment-pair frequency tables with per-fragment coverage values Analyzing inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions — the article explicitly filters inter-chromosomal interactions and focuses on cis only Non-promoter-capture Hi-C data without promoter annotation, since the P-O split and asymmetric coverage thresholds (promoter 200 vs 'other' 50) depend on labeling frag1 as the promoter site http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calls significant promoter-centered long-range interactions from pcHi-C data using covNorm's two-stage normalization (negative binomial coverage normalization followed by distance-dependent background removal) with Weibull-based significance scoring, benchmarkable against CHiCAGO as a baseline. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Calls significant promoter-centered long-range interactions from pcHi-C data using covNorm's two-stage normalization (negative binomial coverage normalization followed by distance-dependent background removal) with Weibull-based significance scoring, benchmarkable against CHiCAGO as a baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized contact map or feature table with significance calls — the skill operates on raw fragment-pair frequency tables with per-fragment coverage values Analyzing inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions — the article explicitly filters inter-chromosomal interactions and focuses on cis only Non-promoter-capture Hi-C data without promoter annotation, since the P-O split and asymmetric coverage thresholds (promoter 200 vs 'other' 50) depend on labeling frag1 as the promoter site

skills.description: Use when testing whether observed genomic range overlaps (e.g., liver caQTL peaks vs. trait-associated SNPs) are significant, and you need a block-bootstrap null instead of naive shuffling.
skills.name: caqtl-snp-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: caqtl-snp-overlap-analysis Use when testing whether observed genomic range overlaps (e.g., liver caQTL peaks vs. trait-associated SNPs) are significant, and you need a block-bootstrap null instead of naive shuffling. When the analysis goal is overlap counts of DEGs vs. differential accessibility peaks with spline-fitted logFC thresholds (use the macrophage.R workflow instead) When deriving mean correlation from Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression data (use multiomicsCor.R instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify enrichment of human liver caQTL ATAC-seq peaks near total-cholesterol GWAS SNPs by computing an overlap rate (proportion of SNPs with a peak within 10 kb), its variance across bootRanges block-bootstrap nulls, and a z-score separating the observed rate from the null. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Quantify enrichment of human liver caQTL ATAC-seq peaks near total-cholesterol GWAS SNPs by computing an overlap rate (proportion of SNPs with a peak within 10 kb), its variance across bootRanges block-bootstrap nulls, and a z-score separating the observed rate from the null.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is overlap counts of DEGs vs. differential accessibility peaks with spline-fitted logFC thresholds (use the macrophage.R workflow instead) When deriving mean correlation from Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression data (use multiomicsCor.R instead)

skills.description: Use when a scATAC-seq clustering lacks cell-type identities and a matched or same-tissue scRNA-seq reference with curated labels is available; triggered by the need to color scATAC clusters (e.g. on a t-SNE embedding) with RNA-derived cell types.
skills.name: cca-based-cross-modality-annotation
skills.search_text: cca-based-cross-modality-annotation Use when a scATAC-seq clustering lacks cell-type identities and a matched or same-tissue scRNA-seq reference with curated labels is available; triggered by the need to color scATAC clusters (e.g. on a t-SNE embedding) with RNA-derived cell types. No matched scRNA-seq reference with trusted cell-type labels exists for the tissue, leaving nothing for the CCA anchor transfer to align against The scATAC-seq data has not yet been dimensionality-reduced and clustered in SnapATAC — snapToSeurat expects the SnapATAC embedding and cluster structure to already exist Working in R >= 3.6.0, where the rhdf5 dependency breaks and SnapATAC (v1) cannot load snap files http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Transfers cell-type labels from a scRNA-seq reference onto a scATAC-seq dataset by exporting the SnapATAC embedding to Seurat and using CCA-based anchor integration, as demonstrated on the 4,792-cell PBMC scATAC subset annotated from the ~10k-cell PBMC scRNA-seq reference. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Transfers cell-type labels from a scRNA-seq reference onto a scATAC-seq dataset by exporting the SnapATAC embedding to Seurat and using CCA-based anchor integration, as demonstrated on the 4,792-cell PBMC scATAC subset annotated from the ~10k-cell PBMC scRNA-seq reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched scRNA-seq reference with trusted cell-type labels exists for the tissue, leaving nothing for the CCA anchor transfer to align against The scATAC-seq data has not yet been dimensionality-reduced and clustered in SnapATAC — snapToSeurat expects the SnapATAC embedding and cluster structure to already exist Working in R >= 3.6.0, where the rhdf5 dependency breaks and SnapATAC (v1) cannot load snap files

skills.description: Use when a task needs expression values for cancer cell lines (CCLE) or TCGA tumor/normal cohorts to quantify differential expression of genes located on specific eccDNAs, e.g. genes on hsa_Chr7_3S_1 in TCGA-GBM.
skills.name: ccle-expression-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: ccle-expression-data-retrieval Use when a task needs expression values for cancer cell lines (CCLE) or TCGA tumor/normal cohorts to quantify differential expression of genes located on specific eccDNAs, e.g. genes on hsa_Chr7_3S_1 in TCGA-GBM. The eccDNAs of interest are from non-human species or non-cancer diseases, since eccDNAdb currently covers human cancers only The task requires eccDNA detection from raw WGS data (use AmpliconArchitect) rather than retrieval/analysis of already-annotated eccDNA gene expression Only normal tissue expression is needed and no tumor-vs-normal comparison is planned http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Retrieve and quantify cancer gene expression profiles from the CCLE (and matched TCGA cohorts) so that eccDNA-derived genes can be compared between tumor and normal samples using Student's t-tests, mirroring the eccDNAdb approach for eccDNA gene expression annotation. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Retrieve and quantify cancer gene expression profiles from the CCLE (and matched TCGA cohorts) so that eccDNA-derived genes can be compared between tumor and normal samples using Student's t-tests, mirroring the eccDNAdb approach for eccDNA gene expression annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The eccDNAs of interest are from non-human species or non-cancer diseases, since eccDNAdb currently covers human cancers only The task requires eccDNA detection from raw WGS data (use AmpliconArchitect) rather than retrieval/analysis of already-annotated eccDNA gene expression Only normal tissue expression is needed and no tumor-vs-normal comparison is planned

skills.description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment/BAM data must be converted into a snap-format cell-by-bin count matrix (e.g., at 5-kb resolution) as the starting feature representation for clustering or dimensionality reduction without population-level peak calling.
skills.name: cell-by-bin-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: cell-by-bin-matrix-construction Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment/BAM data must be converted into a snap-format cell-by-bin count matrix (e.g., at 5-kb resolution) as the starting feature representation for clustering or dimensionality reduction without population-level peak calling. Input is already a cell-by-peak or cell-by-bin feature table produced by CellRanger-ATAC or another pipeline — proceed directly to binarization and Jaccard kernel computation. The analysis goal requires peak-level resolution (e.g., motif or gene-activity analysis) rather than genome-wide binned clustering features. Working in R >= 3.6.0, since rhdf5 fails on that version for the original SnapATAC package. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Construction of a cell-by-bin accessibility matrix from scATAC-seq fragments, where the genome is tiled into fixed-size bins (e.g., 5-kb) and each cell is represented by its fragment counts per bin, forming the raw feature space for SnapATAC's downstream Jaccard-kernel analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Construction of a cell-by-bin accessibility matrix from scATAC-seq fragments, where the genome is tiled into fixed-size bins (e.g., 5-kb) and each cell is represented by its fragment counts per bin, forming the raw feature space for SnapATAC's downstream Jaccard-kernel analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-by-peak or cell-by-bin feature table produced by CellRanger-ATAC or another pipeline — proceed directly to binarization and Jaccard kernel computation. The analysis goal requires peak-level resolution (e.g., motif or gene-activity analysis) rather than genome-wide binned clustering features. Working in R >= 3.6.0, since rhdf5 fails on that version for the original SnapATAC package.

skills.name: cell-by-peak-anndata-construction
skills.search_text: cell-by-peak-anndata-construction Use when single-cell calling cards qbed insertions and called peaks (e.g., 902 Brd4 peaks from mouse cortex GSE148448) must be converted into a cell-by-peak count matrix for integration with Scanpy gene-expression AnnData. Input is already a cell-by-feature count matrix (AnnData/h5ad) rather than raw qbed insertion records Analysis targets bulk calling cards data rather than single-cell qbed data with per-cell barcodes Peaks have not yet been called and annotated — call_peaks and annotation must precede matrix construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Constructs a cell-by-peak AnnData matrix from single-cell calling cards qbed insertions and called Brd4 peaks using pycallingcards.preprocessing.make_Anndata, enabling downstream integration with scRNA-seq expression data in a MuData object for differential peak and peak–gene pairing analyses. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Constructs a cell-by-peak AnnData matrix from single-cell calling cards qbed insertions and called Brd4 peaks using pycallingcards.preprocessing.make_Anndata, enabling downstream integration with scRNA-seq expression data in a MuData object for differential peak and peak–gene pairing analyses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-by-feature count matrix (AnnData/h5ad) rather than raw qbed insertion records Analysis targets bulk calling cards data rather than single-cell qbed data with per-cell barcodes Peaks have not yet been called and annotated — call_peaks and annotation must precede matrix construction

skills.description: Use when a raw single-cell ChIP-seq/scATAC-seq count matrix (cells x bins/peaks/TSS regions) contains low-quality or extreme-coverage cells that must be filtered before PCA, t-SNE/UMAP, or clustering.

skills.search_text: cell-coverage-outlier-filtering Use when a raw single-cell ChIP-seq/scATAC-seq count matrix (cells x bins/peaks/TSS regions) contains low-quality or extreme-coverage cells that must be filtered before PCA, t-SNE/UMAP, or clustering. Input is already a quality-filtered count matrix with cell QC previously applied — reapplying thresholds would discard additional valid cells The goal is to filter genomic regions/peaks (e.g. regions detected in at least 1% of cells) rather than filter cells Data are bulk ChIP-seq or other non-single-cell data where per-cell coverage thresholds do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 ChromSCape's quality-control step that removes low-coverage and coverage-outlier cells from a single-cell epigenomic count matrix by applying a minimum read-count threshold per cell (e.g. 1600 unique reads) and dropping cells in the top 5% of coverage before downstream normalization. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: ChromSCape's quality-control step that removes low-coverage and coverage-outlier cells from a single-cell epigenomic count matrix by applying a minimum read-count threshold per cell (e.g. 1600 unique reads) and dropping cells in the top 5% of coverage before downstream normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a quality-filtered count matrix with cell QC previously applied — reapplying thresholds would discard additional valid cells The goal is to filter genomic regions/peaks (e.g. regions detected in at least 1% of cells) rather than filter cells Data are bulk ChIP-seq or other non-single-cell data where per-cell coverage thresholds do not apply

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell Hi-C contact matrices resolved by cell-cycle stage and need to test whether nested TLD hierarchy (modularity, TLD-adjR2, weighted similarity WS) changes across stages such as G1 vs S phase vs G2.
skills.name: cell-cycle-stage-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-cycle-stage-comparison Use when you have single-cell Hi-C contact matrices resolved by cell-cycle stage and need to test whether nested TLD hierarchy (modularity, TLD-adjR2, weighted similarity WS) changes across stages such as G1 vs S phase vs G2. Cells with insufficient TLDs identified by deDoc2 (as with the '2n DNA' stage, which was excluded from subsequent analysis in the article) Input is bulk Hi-C or already-imputed/aggregated data rather than per-cell contact matrices — the skill targets cell-to-cell hierarchy dynamics, not population-level TADs The question is TLD boundary accuracy or binsize selection rather than cross-stage dynamics of TLD hierarchy Quantify and compare the hierarchical TAD-like domain (TLD) structure of single-cell Hi-C contact matrices across cell-cycle stages (G1, early/mid/late S, G2) using deDoc2-derived nested TLDs, per-cell modularity Q, weighted similarity WS, and TLD-adjR2. It reveals how nested TLD hierarchy weakens through S phase (Nagano mouse ES cell scHi-C). epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Quantify and compare the hierarchical TAD-like domain (TLD) structure of single-cell Hi-C contact matrices across cell-cycle stages (G1, early/mid/late S, G2) using deDoc2-derived nested TLDs, per-cell modularity Q, weighted similarity WS, and TLD-adjR2. It reveals how nested TLD hierarchy weakens through S phase (Nagano mouse ES cell scHi-C).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells with insufficient TLDs identified by deDoc2 (as with the '2n DNA' stage, which was excluded from subsequent analysis in the article) Input is bulk Hi-C or already-imputed/aggregated data rather than per-cell contact matrices — the skill targets cell-to-cell hierarchy dynamics, not population-level TADs The question is TLD boundary accuracy or binsize selection rather than cross-stage dynamics of TLD hierarchy

skills.description: Use when cells from a scATAC-seq or scChIP-seq dataset have known labels (cell line, replicate, sample) and clusters computed by ChromSCape must be scored for label concordance or compared between samples with Fisher's exact test.
skills.name: cell-line-cluster-assignment-scoring
skills.search_text: cell-line-cluster-assignment-scoring Use when cells from a scATAC-seq or scChIP-seq dataset have known labels (cell line, replicate, sample) and clusters computed by ChromSCape must be scored for label concordance or compared between samples with Fisher's exact test. Cells have no known label of origin (cell line, replicate, or sample) to validate clusters against — the scoring metric is undefined The goal is de novo sub-population discovery rather than benchmarking a clustering against ground-truth labels Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ/BAM) rather than a reads-in-peaks count matrix — the data-engineering pipeline to generate count matrices must be run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantifies how well unsupervised clusters from ChromSCape correspond to known cell lines of origin by computing per-cell-line replicate assignment scores (e.g. K562 99.7%, GM12878 98.3%) on the GSE99172 scATAC-seq dataset, plus Fisher's exact tests comparing cluster proportions between samples. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Quantifies how well unsupervised clusters from ChromSCape correspond to known cell lines of origin by computing per-cell-line replicate assignment scores (e.g. K562 99.7%, GM12878 98.3%) on the GSE99172 scATAC-seq dataset, plus Fisher's exact tests comparing cluster proportions between samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cells have no known label of origin (cell line, replicate, or sample) to validate clusters against — the scoring metric is undefined The goal is de novo sub-population discovery rather than benchmarking a clustering against ground-truth labels Input is raw sequencing reads (FASTQ/BAM) rather than a reads-in-peaks count matrix — the data-engineering pipeline to generate count matrices must be run first

The features are already extracted in the 'feature' directory and the goal is only to train/predict — run 'python main.py --cell_line ${cell_line}' directly instead The input is a different data type (e.g. enhancer-promoter EPdata labels or the generic Liu et al. dataset) whose naming/format conventions differ from the eight-cell-line enhancer layout described in the README The goal is interpreting which TFBS motifs are important in a trained model — use SHAP.py ('SHAP.py' is the code for exploring important motifs) rather than re-extracting sequence features http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Encodes cell-specific enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into dna2vec word-vector features and 401-dimensional HOCOMOCO Human v11 motif frequency features for input to the Enhancer-MDLF multi-input deep learning framework. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Encodes cell-specific enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into dna2vec word-vector features and 401-dimensional HOCOMOCO Human v11 motif frequency features for input to the Enhancer-MDLF multi-input deep learning framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The features are already extracted in the 'feature' directory and the goal is only to train/predict — run 'python main.py --cell_line ${cell_line}' directly instead The input is a different data type (e.g. enhancer-promoter EPdata labels or the generic Liu et al. dataset) whose naming/format conventions differ from the eight-cell-line enhancer layout described in the README The goal is interpreting which TFBS motifs are important in a trained model — use SHAP.py ('SHAP.py' is the code for exploring important motifs) rather than re-extracting sequence features

skills.search_text: cell-line-similarity-analysis Use when you need to quantify how well a cell-specific enhancer model trained on one human cell line transfers to the other seven cell lines' test sets, and to rank cell line similarity from cross-prediction BACC. When the goal is within-cell-line enhancer identification on each cell line's own independent test set rather than cross-cell line transferability When working on the generic enhancer dataset (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L, 'generic data' folder) or the enhancer-promoter task ('EPdata' folder) instead of the eight cell-line enhancer sets When only a single cell line's training and test data are available, since no source-target pairs can be formed http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Quantifies the transferability of cell-specific enhancer models by training Enhancer-MDLF on each of eight human cell lines and evaluating it on the other seven cell lines' independent test sets. skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is within-cell-line enhancer identification on each cell line's own independent test set rather than cross-cell line transferability When working on the generic enhancer dataset (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L, 'generic data' folder) or the enhancer-promoter task ('EPdata' folder) instead of the eight cell-line enhancer sets When only a single cell line's training and test data are available, since no source-target pairs can be formed
