skills.search_text: cell-line-specific-enhancer-model-interpretation Use when you have a trained Enhancer-MDLF model on one of the eight human cell lines and need to identify which TFBS motifs drive enhancer predictions via SHAP attribution over motif-module features. The goal is to interpret the dna2vec sequence-embedding branch of Enhancer-MDLF rather than the motif-module features extracted by motif_find.py Sequences are outside the scope of the HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWM library or the enhancer data on the eight cell lines shipped in the 'data' folder No trained or pre-trained Enhancer-MDLF model is available and training it via main.py is out of scope for this interpretation task http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Interprets the motif-module input features of the Enhancer-MDLF cell-specific enhancer predictor with the SHAP framework to rank TFBS motifs by importance within enhancer regions across eight human cell lines, producing per-cell-line motif rankings and SHAP force-plot diagrams. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Interprets the motif-module input features of the Enhancer-MDLF cell-specific enhancer predictor with the SHAP framework to rank TFBS motifs by importance within enhancer regions across eight human cell lines, producing per-cell-line motif rankings and SHAP force-plot diagrams.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to interpret the dna2vec sequence-embedding branch of Enhancer-MDLF rather than the motif-module features extracted by motif_find.py Sequences are outside the scope of the HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWM library or the enhancer data on the eight cell lines shipped in the 'data' folder No trained or pre-trained Enhancer-MDLF model is available and training it via main.py is out of scope for this interpretation task

skills.description: Use when you have fasta-formatted SE/TE sequences for one cell line (e.g. mESC) and want a cell-line-specific sequence-only classifier with user-set learning rate and epochs.
skills.name: cell-line-specific-model-training
skills.search_text: cell-line-specific-model-training Use when you have fasta-formatted SE/TE sequences for one cell line (e.g. mESC) and want a cell-line-specific sequence-only classifier with user-set learning rate and epochs. You need a generalizing model across multiple cell lines or species — use DeepSE-integrative (train_integrative1/2/3.py) instead of the cell-line-specific model. skills.summary: Trains a DeepSE-specific two-layer CNN (Keras) that distinguishes super-enhancers from typical enhancers in a single chosen cell line, using only dna2vec k-mer feature embeddings of the SE/TE DNA sequences — no ChIP-seq data required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a generalizing model across multiple cell lines or species — use DeepSE-integrative (train_integrative1/2/3.py) instead of the cell-line-specific model. skills.description: Use when evaluating how loop-calling performance scales with the number of single cells, e.g. comparing SnapHiC on per-cell subsamples of mES scHi-C data against HiCCUPS on pooled contacts.

skills.search_text: cell-number-subsampling-scaling-analysis Use when evaluating how loop-calling performance scales with the number of single cells, e.g. comparing SnapHiC on per-cell subsamples of mES scHi-C data against HiCCUPS on pooled contacts. skills.summary: Benchmark a single-cell Hi-C loop caller by running it independently on a series of subsampled cell numbers (e.g. the 10-742 mES cell series) and comparing loop counts against a pooled-data bulk method (Juicer HiCCUPS with default and optimal parameters) to quantify how few cells are needed for reliable loop detection.

skills.search_text: cell-type-agnostic-feature-computation Use when candidate enhancer-gene pairs (e.g. cCRE-ELS within 500 KB of target gene TSSs) have been formed with createPairs and the CENTRE workflow requires the non-cell-type-specific feature columns before calling centrePrediction. Pairs have not yet been generated — run createPairs() first to collect cCRE-ELS within the 500 KB window around target TSSs You need the cell-type-specific features (CRUP-EP/CRUP-PP probabilities, regulatory distance, TPM) — use computeCellTypeFeatures(metaData, replicate, input.free, cores, sequencing, tpmData, pairs) instead You intend to train a TargetFinder-style model requiring hundreds of cell-specific genomic datasets — this skill only computes CT-agnostic statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes cell-type-agnostic features for candidate enhancer-target (ET) pairs in the CENTRE pipeline via computeGenericFeatures(pairs): genomic distance between enhancer midpoint and TSS, the precomputed cor_CRUP correlation, and the Fisher-combined Wilcoxon P-value statistic, all derived from precomputed public datasets rather than the cell type of interest. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad687
skills.summary: Computes cell-type-agnostic features for candidate enhancer-target (ET) pairs in the CENTRE pipeline via computeGenericFeatures(pairs): genomic distance between enhancer midpoint and TSS, the precomputed cor_CRUP correlation, and the Fisher-combined Wilcoxon P-value statistic, all derived from precomputed public datasets rather than the cell type of interest.

skills.description: Use when you have trained cell-type CRE classifiers (e.g., BOM/XGBoost on motif counts) and need to quantify prediction accuracy, such as fraction of elements assigned to the correct cell type or cross-species transfer rates.
skills.name: cell-type-classification-performance-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-classification-performance-evaluation Use when you have trained cell-type CRE classifiers (e.g., BOM/XGBoost on motif counts) and need to quantify prediction accuracy, such as fraction of elements assigned to the correct cell type or cross-species transfer rates. Input is already a feature/model output table and no cell-type labels or classifier predictions are involved — evaluation of classification rates does not apply. The goal is motif importance interpretation or SHAP visualization rather than accuracy assessment — use save_shap_multi()/shapPlots_multi() instead. Elements are proximal promoters or the regulatory activity depends on chromatin context beyond the input sequence, since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Evaluates motif-based (Bag-of-Motifs/XGBoost) classifiers of cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements by computing correct-classification rates on held-out or cross-species CRE sets, quantifying how often BOM models assign each element to its true cell type. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Evaluates motif-based (Bag-of-Motifs/XGBoost) classifiers of cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements by computing correct-classification rates on held-out or cross-species CRE sets, quantifying how often BOM models assign each element to its true cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/model output table and no cell-type labels or classifier predictions are involved — evaluation of classification rates does not apply. The goal is motif importance interpretation or SHAP visualization rather than accuracy assessment — use save_shap_multi()/shapPlots_multi() instead. Elements are proximal promoters or the regulatory activity depends on chromatin context beyond the input sequence, since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence.

skills.description: Use when CpG-level methylation calls (e.g., Roadmap WGBS) must be summarized per interval set and compared across cell types to test differential methylation level/variation between HOT regions and control regions like non-HOT CpG islands.
skills.name: cell-type-comparative-epigenomics
skills.search_text: cell-type-comparative-epigenomics Use when CpG-level methylation calls (e.g., Roadmap WGBS) must be summarized per interval set and compared across cell types to test differential methylation level/variation between HOT regions and control regions like non-HOT CpG islands. The task is defining HOT regions from ChIP-seq peak data (TF occupancy thresholds) rather than comparing methylation over pre-defined region sets No WGBS/CpG-level methylation data are available for the cell types of interest, so methylation summaries cannot be computed The comparison is not cross-cell-type (a single cell type), since medians/IQRs across cell types per region set are the core statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compares CpG methylation dynamics across multiple human cell types between defined genomic interval sets (HOT regions, occupancy-binned non-HOT regions, non-HOT CpG islands) using Roadmap Epigenomics WGBS data, to test whether HOT regions are constitutively hypo-methylated while non-HOT CpG islands vary more. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Compares CpG methylation dynamics across multiple human cell types between defined genomic interval sets (HOT regions, occupancy-binned non-HOT regions, non-HOT CpG islands) using Roadmap Epigenomics WGBS data, to test whether HOT regions are constitutively hypo-methylated while non-HOT CpG islands vary more.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is defining HOT regions from ChIP-seq peak data (TF occupancy thresholds) rather than comparing methylation over pre-defined region sets No WGBS/CpG-level methylation data are available for the cell types of interest, so methylation summaries cannot be computed The comparison is not cross-cell-type (a single cell type), since medians/IQRs across cell types per region set are the core statistics

skills.description: Use when comparing cell type annotation accuracy of cluster-based vs cell-based methods on scRNA-seq datasets with known reference labels, or when quantifying how swapping the underlying reference database affects annotation consistency.
skills.name: cell-type-consistency-evaluation
skills.search_text: cell-type-consistency-evaluation Use when comparing cell type annotation accuracy of cluster-based vs cell-based methods on scRNA-seq datasets with known reference labels, or when quantifying how swapping the underlying reference database affects annotation consistency. Input scRNA-seq data has no clusters or no manually curated reference cell types to compare against — consistency rates cannot be computed Goal is de novo cell type discovery or annotation of tissues with no markers in the CellMatch database, rather than evaluating annotation accuracy against known labels Datasets are not human or mouse — CellMatch contains only human and mouse references http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark cell type annotation methods (scCATCH, CellAssign, Garnett, SingleR, scMap, CHETAH) by computing cluster-level consistent rates against manually curated reference cell types on benchmark scRNA-seq datasets, and test how reference databases (e.g., CellMatch) change accuracy. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Benchmark cell type annotation methods (scCATCH, CellAssign, Garnett, SingleR, scMap, CHETAH) by computing cluster-level consistent rates against manually curated reference cell types on benchmark scRNA-seq datasets, and test how reference databases (e.g., CellMatch) change accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input scRNA-seq data has no clusters or no manually curated reference cell types to compare against — consistency rates cannot be computed Goal is de novo cell type discovery or annotation of tissues with no markers in the CellMatch database, rather than evaluating annotation accuracy against known labels Datasets are not human or mouse — CellMatch contains only human and mouse references

skills.description: Use when comparing methylated-core/epiallele structures across purified cell populations (e.g., astrocytes, neurons, MOEs from cerebellum and cortex) to test for shared precursor cores during postnatal differentiation.
skills.name: cell-type-epiallele-trajectory-comparison
skills.search_text: cell-type-epiallele-trajectory-comparison Use when comparing methylated-core/epiallele structures across purified cell populations (e.g., astrocytes, neurons, MOEs from cerebellum and cortex) to test for shared precursor cores during postnatal differentiation. Input is raw bisulfite FASTQ: reads must first be merged with PEAR (≥40 nt overlap), quality-filtered (Phred >33, 400-500 nt) and converted to binary epihaplotype files with ampliMethProfiler before MethCoresProfiler can run. The goal is single-CpG methylation quantification or single-epiallele abundance rather than shared phased mCpG combinations — the paper positions existing tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) in that space. Samples lack cell-type metadata (Tissue/Group/Rep columns) or replicates, so cross-population heatmaps, PCA and index comparisons cannot be meaningfully interpreted. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Cell-type-resolved comparison of epiallele families: MethCoresProfiler (R) extracts significant phased mCpG cores from bisulfite amplicons of each purified cell population, then clusters and compares them (heatmaps, PCA, MethCores/Clonality/E indices) to reveal shared precursor cores versus divergence across cell types during postnatal differentiation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Cell-type-resolved comparison of epiallele families: MethCoresProfiler (R) extracts significant phased mCpG cores from bisulfite amplicons of each purified cell population, then clusters and compares them (heatmaps, PCA, MethCores/Clonality/E indices) to reveal shared precursor cores versus divergence across cell types during postnatal differentiation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw bisulfite FASTQ: reads must first be merged with PEAR (≥40 nt overlap), quality-filtered (Phred >33, 400-500 nt) and converted to binary epihaplotype files with ampliMethProfiler before MethCoresProfiler can run. The goal is single-CpG methylation quantification or single-epiallele abundance rather than shared phased mCpG combinations — the paper positions existing tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) in that space. Samples lack cell-type metadata (Tissue/Group/Rep columns) or replicates, so cross-population heatmaps, PCA and index comparisons cannot be meaningfully interpreted.

skills.description: Use when building a Cellcano reference for scATAC-seq celltyping: the reference gene score matrix (from ArchR) has annotated cell type labels and features must be reduced to cell-type-specific genes before MLP training.
skills.name: cell-type-label-supervised-feature-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-label-supervised-feature-ranking Use when building a Cellcano reference for scATAC-seq celltyping: the reference gene score matrix (from ArchR) has annotated cell type labels and features must be reduced to cell-type-specific genes before MLP training. Input is raw scATAC-seq data (fragment file or bam file) — gene scores must first be generated via the ArchR pipeline before F-test selection is possible Reference data lacks annotated cell type labels — the F-test is supervised and requires cell type labels to score genes Features are peaks or bin counts rather than gene scores — this selection step is defined on the reference gene score matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Selects cell-type-specific gene features for Cellcano's supervised scATAC-seq celltyping by ranking reference gene scores with an F-test and retaining the top 3000 genes as model input. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Selects cell-type-specific gene features for Cellcano's supervised scATAC-seq celltyping by ranking reference gene scores with an F-test and retaining the top 3000 genes as model input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw scATAC-seq data (fragment file or bam file) — gene scores must first be generated via the ArchR pipeline before F-test selection is possible Reference data lacks annotated cell type labels — the F-test is supervised and requires cell type labels to score genes Features are peaks or bin counts rather than gene scores — this selection step is defined on the reference gene score matrix

skills.description: Use when you have Cellcano (or similar supervised) predicted cell-type labels for a target scATAC-seq dataset plus ground-truth labels (e.g., FACS-sorted FACS labels embedded in cell identifiers) and need to quantify per-class prediction accuracy.
skills.name: cell-type-prediction-confusion-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-prediction-confusion-matrix-computation Use when you have Cellcano (or similar supervised) predicted cell-type labels for a target scATAC-seq dataset plus ground-truth labels (e.g., FACS-sorted FACS labels embedded in cell identifiers) and need to quantify per-class prediction accuracy. Target cells carry no ground-truth labels (labels are not embedded in identifiers and no FACS/reference annotation exists), so no true-vs-predicted cross-tabulation is possible Predictions come from unsupervised clustering rather than a supervised transfer, so predicted label names are not directly comparable to the reference label vocabulary (B, CD4 T, CD8 T, Mono, NK) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Computes a true-vs-predicted cross-tabulation (confusion matrix) of cell-type labels to quantify prediction accuracy of a supervised celltyping method such as Cellcano, using ground-truth labels embedded in target cell identifiers. In the Cellcano quick-start demo, diagonal counts against FACS ground truth serve as the validation statistic. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Computes a true-vs-predicted cross-tabulation (confusion matrix) of cell-type labels to quantify prediction accuracy of a supervised celltyping method such as Cellcano, using ground-truth labels embedded in target cell identifiers. In the Cellcano quick-start demo, diagonal counts against FACS ground truth serve as the validation statistic.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Target cells carry no ground-truth labels (labels are not embedded in identifiers and no FACS/reference annotation exists), so no true-vs-predicted cross-tabulation is possible Predictions come from unsupervised clustering rather than a supervised transfer, so predicted label names are not directly comparable to the reference label vocabulary (B, CD4 T, CD8 T, Mono, NK)

skills.description: Use when you have EpiRegio GeneQuery REM tables (regressionCoefficient, per-cell-type DNase1 signal) for a gene and need cell type-specific REM contributions to gene expression.
skills.name: cell-type-score-computation
skills.search_text: cell-type-score-computation Use when you have EpiRegio GeneQuery REM tables (regressionCoefficient, per-cell-type DNase1 signal) for a gene and need cell type-specific REM contributions to gene expression. Input is already a scored REM table (e.g. a downloaded CSV with Cell type score thresholds already applied) rather than raw regressionCoefficient and DNase1 signals The goal is TF motif enrichment or ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis rather than quantifying REM contributions to gene expression Computes EpiRegio's Cell type score, which normalizes the contribution of each REM to its target gene's expression in a specific cell type, as predicted by the STITCHIT linear model, and validates that scores fall in [-1, 1] and sum to 1 in absolute value per gene per cell type. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Computes EpiRegio's Cell type score, which normalizes the contribution of each REM to its target gene's expression in a specific cell type, as predicted by the STITCHIT linear model, and validates that scores fall in [-1, 1] and sum to 1 in absolute value per gene per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a scored REM table (e.g. a downloaded CSV with Cell type score thresholds already applied) rather than raw regressionCoefficient and DNase1 signals The goal is TF motif enrichment or ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis rather than quantifying REM contributions to gene expression

skills.description: Use when a set of REMs from an EpiRegio Gene Query must be prioritized by cell type/tissue specificity (e.g. 'heart') before downstream TF motif enrichment such as PASTAA.
skills.name: cell-type-score-ranking-of-rems
skills.search_text: cell-type-score-ranking-of-rems Use when a set of REMs from an EpiRegio Gene Query must be prioritized by cell type/tissue specificity (e.g. 'heart') before downstream TF motif enrichment such as PASTAA. The goal is finding a gene's REMs regardless of cell type specificity, with no downstream rank-aware enrichment tool — an unranked EpiRegio Gene Query suffices. The input is already ChIP-seq peak regions to intersect with REMs — use EpiRegio's Region Query with an Overlap percentage instead of Cell type score ranking. The downstream motif tool does not exploit sequence ranking (e.g. set-based tools like Clover or Homer accept unordered region sets). http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Ranks regulatory elements (REMs) retrieved from EpiRegio by their Cell type score — the STITCHIT-derived estimate of each REM's cell type-specific contribution to its target gene's expression — so that motif enrichment tools like PASTAA receive meaningfully ordered high- and low-ranked sequences. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Ranks regulatory elements (REMs) retrieved from EpiRegio by their Cell type score — the STITCHIT-derived estimate of each REM's cell type-specific contribution to its target gene's expression — so that motif enrichment tools like PASTAA receive meaningfully ordered high- and low-ranked sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is finding a gene's REMs regardless of cell type specificity, with no downstream rank-aware enrichment tool — an unranked EpiRegio Gene Query suffices. The input is already ChIP-seq peak regions to intersect with REMs — use EpiRegio's Region Query with an Overlap percentage instead of Cell type score ranking. The downstream motif tool does not exploit sequence ranking (e.g. set-based tools like Clover or Homer accept unordered region sets).

skills.name: cell-type-specific-differential-peak-analysis
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-differential-peak-analysis Use when single-cell CC/qbed insertion data (e.g., Brd4 mouse cortex, GSE148448) must be converted to a cell-by-peak AnnData and differential TF binding peaks per cell type must be linked to nearby gene expression. Input is already a cell-by-peak count matrix — cc.pp.call_peaks and cc.pp.make_Anndata operate on qbed insertion records, not feature tables The goal is bulk (non-single-cell) calling cards peak calling without cell-type stratification — a simpler CCcaller/MACCs bulk workflow suffices The task is motif discovery or ChIP-seq comparison only; use pycallingcards' Tools (tl) motif calling or plotting functions instead of the differential peak–gene pairing pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A Pycallingcards-based workflow for detecting cell-type-specific transcription factor binding peaks from single-cell calling cards (CC) data and pairing differential peaks with nearby gene expression to generate binding–expression hypotheses. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: A Pycallingcards-based workflow for detecting cell-type-specific transcription factor binding peaks from single-cell calling cards (CC) data and pairing differential peaks with nearby gene expression to generate binding–expression hypotheses.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a cell-by-peak count matrix — cc.pp.call_peaks and cc.pp.make_Anndata operate on qbed insertion records, not feature tables The goal is bulk (non-single-cell) calling cards peak calling without cell-type stratification — a simpler CCcaller/MACCs bulk workflow suffices The task is motif discovery or ChIP-seq comparison only; use pycallingcards' Tools (tl) motif calling or plotting functions instead of the differential peak–gene pairing pipeline

skills.description: Use when you have trained BOM/XGBoost classifiers on cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements (e.g. mouse E8.25 scATAC-derived CREs) and need per-motif SHAP importance rankings plus local explanations at a locus of interest.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-enhancer-motif-ranking
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-enhancer-motif-ranking Use when you have trained BOM/XGBoost classifiers on cell-type-specific distal regulatory elements (e.g. mouse E8.25 scATAC-derived CREs) and need per-motif SHAP importance rankings plus local explanations at a locus of interest. You need motif grammar (spacing/orientation/order) effects — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and grammar integration remains future work Regulatory activity depends on regions beyond the input sequence length or on open chromatin/histone marks — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence The relevant TFs lack known PWMs in the motif library — reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Ranks TF binding motifs by their contribution to cell-type-specific cis-regulatory element classification using SHAP values from BOM's gradient-boosted tree (XGBoost) models built on FIMO motif count matrices, and validates that the rankings correspond to known lineage-specific TFs (e.g. MEF2C/NKX2-5/GATA for cardiomyocytes, FLI1/JUN-FOS/SOX7-ETV6 for endothelial cells). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Ranks TF binding motifs by their contribution to cell-type-specific cis-regulatory element classification using SHAP values from BOM's gradient-boosted tree (XGBoost) models built on FIMO motif count matrices, and validates that the rankings correspond to known lineage-specific TFs (e.g. MEF2C/NKX2-5/GATA for cardiomyocytes, FLI1/JUN-FOS/SOX7-ETV6 for endothelial cells).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need motif grammar (spacing/orientation/order) effects — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and grammar integration remains future work Regulatory activity depends on regions beyond the input sequence length or on open chromatin/histone marks — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence The relevant TFs lack known PWMs in the motif library — reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif annotations

skills.description: Use when single-cell expression data for known cell types (e.g., Astro, MG, L2/3, Vip) and per-cell nested TLD boundary calls are available and you need to designate genes or boundaries as cell-type-specific.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-gene-expression-identification
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-gene-expression-identification Use when single-cell expression data for known cell types (e.g., Astro, MG, L2/3, Vip) and per-cell nested TLD boundary calls are available and you need to designate genes or boundaries as cell-type-specific. Input is bulk Hi-C or bulk RNA-seq data without per-cell labels — the frequency-based boundary specificity test requires single-cell boundary calls per cell type Cell types have not been pre-identified (e.g., the 14 Lee PFC labels) and no representative cell types such as L2/3, Vip, Astro, MG can be picked The goal is TLD boundary detection itself rather than associating existing TLD boundaries with cell identity http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identify cell-type-specific highly expressed genes and cell-type-specific nested TLD boundaries for representative cell types (L2/3, Vip, Astro, MG) from the human prefrontal cortex, linking TLD hierarchy to cellular identity. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Identify cell-type-specific highly expressed genes and cell-type-specific nested TLD boundaries for representative cell types (L2/3, Vip, Astro, MG) from the human prefrontal cortex, linking TLD hierarchy to cellular identity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Hi-C or bulk RNA-seq data without per-cell labels — the frequency-based boundary specificity test requires single-cell boundary calls per cell type Cell types have not been pre-identified (e.g., the 14 Lee PFC labels) and no representative cell types such as L2/3, Vip, Astro, MG can be picked The goal is TLD boundary detection itself rather than associating existing TLD boundaries with cell identity

skills.description: Use when scoring structural variants (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) with hg19 breakpoints against phenotypes like head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system or pituitary to identify causative genes and coding vs long-range.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-genomic-data-integration
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-genomic-data-integration Use when scoring structural variants (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) with hg19 breakpoints against phenotypes like head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system or pituitary to identify causative genes and coding vs long-range. The SV is suspected to cause a recessive disorder — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been evaluated The relevant cell type, developmental stage or differentiation time point lacks genomic data (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so the SHH duplication case fails) A single SV needs only a quick online check — the online version at postre-tool.csic.es supports only Single SV submissions, not Multiple SV submissions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Integrates cell type/tissue-specific enhancer, TAD and gene expression data to predict structural variant (SV) pathogenicity, causative genes, and long-range pathomechanisms (e.g. enhancer disconnection, enhancer adoption) as implemented in POSTRE. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Integrates cell type/tissue-specific enhancer, TAD and gene expression data to predict structural variant (SV) pathogenicity, causative genes, and long-range pathomechanisms (e.g. enhancer disconnection, enhancer adoption) as implemented in POSTRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV is suspected to cause a recessive disorder — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been evaluated The relevant cell type, developmental stage or differentiation time point lacks genomic data (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so the SHH duplication case fails) A single SV needs only a quick online check — the online version at postre-tool.csic.es supports only Single SV submissions, not Multiple SV submissions

skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-locus-annotation Use when DA peaks or age-related expression changes from PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq must be assigned to cell-type-specific loci to test whether aging signatures (e.g., B cell decline) are shared or sex-specific between men and women. When the analysis targets cell-composition differences measured by flow cytometry rather than chromatin accessibility at annotated loci When the input lacks cell-type-specific locus annotations (e.g., chromHMM B cell-specific labels), since over-representation testing requires them When studying aging changes within a single sex only — the key signal here is the opposite opening/closing pattern between men and women http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates differentially accessible ATAC-seq peaks and age-related gene expression changes by cell-type specificity (e.g., chromHMM B cell-specific loci) to detect sex-specific immune aging patterns, such as the male-specific decline in B-cell accessibility alongside BCL7A/PAX5/CD79A downregulation. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis targets cell-composition differences measured by flow cytometry rather than chromatin accessibility at annotated loci When the input lacks cell-type-specific locus annotations (e.g., chromHMM B cell-specific labels), since over-representation testing requires them When studying aging changes within a single sex only — the key signal here is the opposite opening/closing pattern between men and women

skills.description: Use when scHi-C-derived loops from matched cell type subsets (e.g. 261-cell astrocyte/microglia/ODC/L2/3 neuron SnapHiC runs) need epigenomic and expression validation against matched bulk references.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-loop-summit-annotation
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-loop-summit-annotation Use when scHi-C-derived loops from matched cell type subsets (e.g. 261-cell astrocyte/microglia/ODC/L2/3 neuron SnapHiC runs) need epigenomic and expression validation against matched bulk references. When loops come from pooled (non-cell-type-resolved) Hi-C and no matched cell type epigenomic/expression references exist — matched vs. unmatched contrast cannot be computed. When the goal is loop discovery itself rather than biological validation of already-called summits — use the SnapHiC pipeline steps ('bin', 'rwr', 'interaction', 'postprocess') instead. When references use a different genome build than the loops (hg19 vs. mm10/hg38) without liftover — anchors will not align to the reference signal tracks. http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Annotates SnapHiC-identified cell type-specific chromatin loops by testing whether loop anchors carry cell type-matched ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, and linked-gene RNA-seq enrichment (Nott et al. epigenomic and Zhang et al. expression references), validating loop calls biologically. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Annotates SnapHiC-identified cell type-specific chromatin loops by testing whether loop anchors carry cell type-matched ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, and linked-gene RNA-seq enrichment (Nott et al. epigenomic and Zhang et al. expression references), validating loop calls biologically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When loops come from pooled (non-cell-type-resolved) Hi-C and no matched cell type epigenomic/expression references exist — matched vs. unmatched contrast cannot be computed. When the goal is loop discovery itself rather than biological validation of already-called summits — use the SnapHiC pipeline steps ('bin', 'rwr', 'interaction', 'postprocess') instead. When references use a different genome build than the loops (hg19 vs. mm10/hg38) without liftover — anchors will not align to the reference signal tracks.

skills.name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-landscape-integration
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-regulatory-landscape-integration Use when interpreting patient structural variants (inversions, deletions, duplications, translocations) whose pathogenic effect is suspected to be non-coding/long-range, and cell type-specific enhancer and TAD data are needed to nominate disease genes. The SV is a coding variant or clearly disrupts the coding sequence of a known gene — POSTRE's long-range enhancer scoring is unnecessary and the intronic/truncating filter handles this differently The phenotype of interest falls outside the 7 supported contexts (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) or lacks genomic data for the appropriate developmental stage Regulatory landscapes are only available as bulk whole-tissue data that cannot resolve focal enhancers (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so the SHH duplication case is mispredicted) Integrates cell type/tissue-specific enhancer (H3K27ac) and TAD regulatory landscapes into structural variant interpretation via POSTRE, so that long-range (enhancer-driven) pathomechanisms such as enhancer disconnection or adoption can be predicted for congenital disorder SVs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Integrates cell type/tissue-specific enhancer (H3K27ac) and TAD regulatory landscapes into structural variant interpretation via POSTRE, so that long-range (enhancer-driven) pathomechanisms such as enhancer disconnection or adoption can be predicted for congenital disorder SVs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV is a coding variant or clearly disrupts the coding sequence of a known gene — POSTRE's long-range enhancer scoring is unnecessary and the intronic/truncating filter handles this differently The phenotype of interest falls outside the 7 supported contexts (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) or lacks genomic data for the appropriate developmental stage Regulatory landscapes are only available as bulk whole-tissue data that cannot resolve focal enhancers (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so the SHH duplication case is mispredicted)

skills.description: Use when mapping enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes via cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe), e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in human prefrontal cortex.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-regulatory-variant-mapping
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-regulatory-variant-mapping Use when mapping enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes via cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe), e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in human prefrontal cortex. Calling chromatin loops de novo from single-cell Hi-C contact files — run the SnapHiC steps (bin, rwr, hic, interaction, postprocess) instead; this skill consumes already-called loop summits. Variants are coding or already carry eQTL/colocalization-based gene assignments, so enhancer-promoter loop linkage adds no new information. Only bulk (non-cell-type-resolved) chromatin contact data is available — the cell type-specific linkage restriction cannot be honored. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps noncoding neuropsychiatric GWAS SNPs to putative target genes by intersecting enhancer-resident SNP coordinates with cell type-specific SnapHiC loop summits from single-nucleus methyl-3C-seq data of 2,869 human prefrontal cortical cells, yielding SNP-gene linkages each supported by a named brain cell type. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Maps noncoding neuropsychiatric GWAS SNPs to putative target genes by intersecting enhancer-resident SNP coordinates with cell type-specific SnapHiC loop summits from single-nucleus methyl-3C-seq data of 2,869 human prefrontal cortical cells, yielding SNP-gene linkages each supported by a named brain cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling chromatin loops de novo from single-cell Hi-C contact files — run the SnapHiC steps (bin, rwr, hic, interaction, postprocess) instead; this skill consumes already-called loop summits. Variants are coding or already carry eQTL/colocalization-based gene assignments, so enhancer-promoter loop linkage adds no new information. Only bulk (non-cell-type-resolved) chromatin contact data is available — the cell type-specific linkage restriction cannot be honored.

skills.description: Use when submitting a gene list to EpiRegio's Gene Query and you need REMs restricted to a relevant cell type or tissue context rather than genome-wide REMs.
skills.name: cell-type-specific-rem-filtering
skills.search_text: cell-type-specific-rem-filtering Use when submitting a gene list to EpiRegio's Gene Query and you need REMs restricted to a relevant cell type or tissue context rather than genome-wide REMs. Running a Region Query with TF ChIP-seq peaks (e.g. ENCODE BED files), where the relevant filter is the 'Overlap percentage' setting, not a cell-type/tissue filter You need all REMs linked to the genes regardless of cellular context, e.g. for genome-wide annotation rather than cell-type-specific interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Narrow EpiRegio Gene Query results to REMs active in a specific cell type or tissue (e.g. 'heart') by using the 'Filter for cell types/tissues' field, so retrieved REMs are biologically relevant to the cell context of the input gene set. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Narrow EpiRegio Gene Query results to REMs active in a specific cell type or tissue (e.g. 'heart') by using the 'Filter for cell types/tissues' field, so retrieved REMs are biologically relevant to the cell context of the input gene set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Running a Region Query with TF ChIP-seq peaks (e.g. ENCODE BED files), where the relevant filter is the 'Overlap percentage' setting, not a cell-type/tissue filter You need all REMs linked to the genes regardless of cellular context, e.g. for genome-wide annotation rather than cell-type-specific interpretation

skills.description: Use when clustered scRNA-seq data needs cell type annotation and one-against-all marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers) may contain pseudo markers upregulated in multiple clusters, or when a reproducible, reference-database-based annotation is required.
skills.name: cellmatch-reference-mapping
skills.search_text: cellmatch-reference-mapping Use when clustered scRNA-seq data needs cell type annotation and one-against-all marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers) may contain pseudo markers upregulated in multiple clusters, or when a reproducible, reference-database-based annotation is required. The CellMatch reference lacks the tissue or cell type of interest — the article notes the limited reference database potentially led to incorrect annotation, and users should supply a custom cellmatch in that case The goal is annotating individual cells against reference profiles rather than pre-defined clusters (cell-based methods such as SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH are the alternative category) Data are not yet clustered — cluster analysis must be performed first, since scCATCH annotates existing cluster identities rather than performing clustering http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Annotates pre-identified scRNA-seq clusters by matching paired-comparison marker genes against the CellMatch tissue-specific cell taxonomy reference database (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) using scCATCH's evidence-based scoring, thereby avoiding pseudo marker genes from one-against-all marker identification. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Annotates pre-identified scRNA-seq clusters by matching paired-comparison marker genes against the CellMatch tissue-specific cell taxonomy reference database (353 cell types, 686 subtypes, 184 tissues, 2,096 human/mouse references) using scCATCH's evidence-based scoring, thereby avoiding pseudo marker genes from one-against-all marker identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CellMatch reference lacks the tissue or cell type of interest — the article notes the limited reference database potentially led to incorrect annotation, and users should supply a custom cellmatch in that case The goal is annotating individual cells against reference profiles rather than pre-defined clusters (cell-based methods such as SingleR, CellAssign, Garnett, scMap, CHETAH are the alternative category) Data are not yet clustered — cluster analysis must be performed first, since scCATCH annotates existing cluster identities rather than performing clustering

skills.description: Use when a BED feature file (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation but an overlapping strand-assigned reference file (e.g. MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) exists, and downstream strand-asymmetry analysis requires oriented features.
skills.name: center-distance-feature-matching
skills.search_text: center-distance-feature-matching Use when a BED feature file (e.g. CTCF ChIP-seq peaks on hg38) lacks strand annotation but an overlapping strand-assigned reference file (e.g. MA0139.1 CTCF motif occurrences) exists, and downstream strand-asymmetry analysis requires oriented features. The features already carry strand annotation — apply Asymmetron's consecutive/contained/pairwise asymmetry functions directly instead of orienting. No overlapping strand-assigned reference feature exists for the input coordinates — the orientation function depends on overlap and cannot assign a strand by proximity alone. The reference motifs are palindromic or otherwise strand-symmetric — the transferred sign carries no directional information for asymmetry analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns a strand sign ('+' or '-') to an unannotated genomic feature (e.g. a CTCF ChIP-seq peak) using the strand sign of an overlapping annotated feature (e.g. a JASPAR/Unibind CTCF motif occurrence); when multiple annotated features overlap, the one whose center is closest to the unannotated feature's center wins. This is the Asymmetron 'orientation' function, implemented on BED files via Pybedtools. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Assigns a strand sign ('+' or '-') to an unannotated genomic feature (e.g. a CTCF ChIP-seq peak) using the strand sign of an overlapping annotated feature (e.g. a JASPAR/Unibind CTCF motif occurrence); when multiple annotated features overlap, the one whose center is closest to the unannotated feature's center wins. This is the Asymmetron 'orientation' function, implemented on BED files via Pybedtools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The features already carry strand annotation — apply Asymmetron's consecutive/contained/pairwise asymmetry functions directly instead of orienting. No overlapping strand-assigned reference feature exists for the input coordinates — the orientation function depends on overlap and cannot assign a strand by proximity alone. The reference motifs are palindromic or otherwise strand-symmetric — the transferred sign carries no directional information for asymmetry analysis.

skills.description: Use when estimating bin-level methylation from cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data and CpG-density bias must be corrected, e.g. choosing among linear-regression, sigmoidal, or strand-aware sigmoid normalization models.
skills.name: cfmedip-methylation-quantification
skills.search_text: cfmedip-methylation-quantification Use when estimating bin-level methylation from cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data and CpG-density bias must be corrected, e.g. choosing among linear-regression, sigmoidal, or strand-aware sigmoid normalization models. Input is raw FASTQ rather than aligned, duplicate-filtered BAM files — the upstream alignment/QC module must run first Data are not enrichment-based (cf)MeDIP-seq reads, e.g. bisulfite or nanopore methylation calls, which need different quantification methods MEDStrand is being used but the sample lacks sufficient read depth for the stranded sigmoid model fit http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module estimates relative and absolute methylation levels from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data by offering three CpG-density-bias-correcting normalization models: MEDIPS (linear regression), QSEA (sigmoidal with empirical knowledge), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module estimates relative and absolute methylation levels from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data by offering three CpG-density-bias-correcting normalization models: MEDIPS (linear regression), QSEA (sigmoidal with empirical knowledge), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ rather than aligned, duplicate-filtered BAM files — the upstream alignment/QC module must run first Data are not enrichment-based (cf)MeDIP-seq reads, e.g. bisulfite or nanopore methylation calls, which need different quantification methods MEDStrand is being used but the sample lacks sufficient read depth for the stranded sigmoid model fit

skills.description: Use when raw cfMeDIP-seq or (cf)MeDIP-seq FASTQ files (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-in/UMI sequences) need automated QC, alignment, methylation quantification, and multi-sample aggregation into tab-delimited bin-sample matrices.
skills.name: cfmedip-seq-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: cfmedip-seq-pipeline-execution Use when raw cfMeDIP-seq or (cf)MeDIP-seq FASTQ files (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-in/UMI sequences) need automated QC, alignment, methylation quantification, and multi-sample aggregation into tab-delimited bin-sample matrices. Input data is not MeDIP-seq/cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing or array methylation), since MEDIPIPE's QC and quantification models (MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand) assume MeDIP enrichment profiles Data is already aligned and QC'd (BAM-level inputs) and only downstream statistical modelling is needed — MEDIPIPE starts from raw FASTQ files Single-sample exploratory analysis where the aggregation and group/batch-level QC reporting machinery is unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Execute MEDIPIPE, a Snakemake-based end-to-end pipeline that takes cfMeDIP-seq raw FASTQ files through QC, alignment, methylation quantification, and aggregation, producing aggregated bin-sample methylation matrices and summarized QC reports. It automates per-tool environment deployment via Conda and scales across cluster engines such as SLURM. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Execute MEDIPIPE, a Snakemake-based end-to-end pipeline that takes cfMeDIP-seq raw FASTQ files through QC, alignment, methylation quantification, and aggregation, producing aggregated bin-sample methylation matrices and summarized QC reports. It automates per-tool environment deployment via Conda and scales across cluster engines such as SLURM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not MeDIP-seq/cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing or array methylation), since MEDIPIPE's QC and quantification models (MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand) assume MeDIP enrichment profiles Data is already aligned and QC'd (BAM-level inputs) and only downstream statistical modelling is needed — MEDIPIPE starts from raw FASTQ files Single-sample exploratory analysis where the aggregation and group/batch-level QC reporting machinery is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when starting from raw FASTQ files of cfMeDIP-seq (or (cf)MeDIP-seq) libraries and you need adapter trimming, conditional UMI barcode handling, and per-sample QC reports as the first module of an automated pipeline.
skills.name: cfmedip-seq-read-qc
skills.search_text: cfmedip-seq-read-qc Use when starting from raw FASTQ files of cfMeDIP-seq (or (cf)MeDIP-seq) libraries and you need adapter trimming, conditional UMI barcode handling, and per-sample QC reports as the first module of an automated pipeline. Input data has already been adapter-trimmed or UMI-processed and only needs alignment or methylation quantification (this skill covers only module i, read trimming and QC) The data type is not cfMeDIP-seq / (cf)MeDIP-seq FASTQ (e.g. bulk WGBS or RNA-seq reads), since MEDIPIPE is a framework specifically designed for cfMeDIP-seq data http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Read-level trimming and quality-control module (module i) of the MEDIPIPE cfMeDIP-seq pipeline: conditional UMI barcode extraction with UMI-tools, adapter/quality trimming with Trim Galore, and FastQC reporting on raw and trimmed reads, orchestrated as Snakemake rules with Conda-deployed environments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Read-level trimming and quality-control module (module i) of the MEDIPIPE cfMeDIP-seq pipeline: conditional UMI barcode extraction with UMI-tools, adapter/quality trimming with Trim Galore, and FastQC reporting on raw and trimmed reads, orchestrated as Snakemake rules with Conda-deployed environments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has already been adapter-trimmed or UMI-processed and only needs alignment or methylation quantification (this skill covers only module i, read trimming and QC) The data type is not cfMeDIP-seq / (cf)MeDIP-seq FASTQ (e.g. bulk WGBS or RNA-seq reads), since MEDIPIPE is a framework specifically designed for cfMeDIP-seq data

skills.description: Use when raw or Trim Galore-trimmed cfMeDIP-seq FASTQs (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-ins/UMIs) must be mapped, duplicate-processed, and QC-assessed to produce sorted BAMs and fragment-size metrics.
skills.name: cfmedip-seq-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: cfmedip-seq-short-read-alignment Use when raw or Trim Galore-trimmed cfMeDIP-seq FASTQs (single-end or paired-end, with or without spike-ins/UMIs) must be mapped, duplicate-processed, and QC-assessed to produce sorted BAMs and fragment-size metrics. Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been adapter/quality trimmed with Trim Galore — pre-processing must happen before BWA-MEM alignment Data type is not cfMeDIP-seq / (cf)MeDIP-seq methylome data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite or regular ChIP-seq) — MEDIPIPE is scoped to (cf)MeDIP-seq QC and analysis Alignment-only is needed without duplicate handling — the skill specifically dispatches between SAMtools markdup and UMI-tools dedup based on library UMI status http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align Trim Galore-processed cfMeDIP-seq reads with BWA-MEM to a primary genome reference (plus spike-in sequences when declared in the YAML config), then filter, deduplicate (SAMtools markdup vs UMI-tools dedup depending on UMI usage), and collect alignment QC with Picard insert-size metrics and SAMtools BAM statistics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Align Trim Galore-processed cfMeDIP-seq reads with BWA-MEM to a primary genome reference (plus spike-in sequences when declared in the YAML config), then filter, deduplicate (SAMtools markdup vs UMI-tools dedup depending on UMI usage), and collect alignment QC with Picard insert-size metrics and SAMtools BAM statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been adapter/quality trimmed with Trim Galore — pre-processing must happen before BWA-MEM alignment Data type is not cfMeDIP-seq / (cf)MeDIP-seq methylome data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite or regular ChIP-seq) — MEDIPIPE is scoped to (cf)MeDIP-seq QC and analysis Alignment-only is needed without duplicate handling — the skill specifically dispatches between SAMtools markdup and UMI-tools dedup based on library UMI status

skills.description: Use when query regions in one genome (e.g., hg38 SNP coordinates) must be mapped to another genome (e.g., mm10), especially when regulatory function of mapped loci matters and plain chain-based liftOver may multi-map or miss orthologous elements.
skills.name: chain-file-coordinate-conversion
skills.search_text: chain-file-coordinate-conversion Use when query regions in one genome (e.g., hg38 SNP coordinates) must be mapped to another genome (e.g., mm10), especially when regulatory function of mapped loci matters and plain chain-based liftOver may multi-map or miss orthologous elements. The input is a protein or transcript-level correspondence problem rather than genomic interval coordinate conversion Only syntactic coordinate transfer is needed and regulatory similarity is irrelevant, multi-mapping is acceptable, and the extra epigenomic/grammar scoring overhead is unnecessary No chain file or matched orthologous functional genomic datasets are available for the target species, so candidate regions cannot be extended or scored http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts genomic coordinates (e.g., fine-mapped GWAS SNPs or regulatory intervals) across species using UCSC reciprocal-best chain files, either via standard UCSC liftOver/rtracklayer or as the region-extension step that feeds AdaLiftOver's epigenomic and sequence grammar scoring. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Converts genomic coordinates (e.g., fine-mapped GWAS SNPs or regulatory intervals) across species using UCSC reciprocal-best chain files, either via standard UCSC liftOver/rtracklayer or as the region-extension step that feeds AdaLiftOver's epigenomic and sequence grammar scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a protein or transcript-level correspondence problem rather than genomic interval coordinate conversion Only syntactic coordinate transfer is needed and regulatory similarity is irrelevant, multi-mapping is acceptable, and the extra epigenomic/grammar scoring overhead is unnecessary No chain file or matched orthologous functional genomic datasets are available for the target species, so candidate regions cannot be extended or scored

skills.description: Use when you have a normalized, binned scATAC-seq accessibility matrix and need to call focal amplifications (e.g., double minutes) at single-cell resolution without a matched normal control.
skills.name: changepoint-segmentation-of-binned-coverage
skills.search_text: changepoint-segmentation-of-binned-coverage Use when you have a normalized, binned scATAC-seq accessibility matrix and need to call focal amplifications (e.g., double minutes) at single-cell resolution without a matched normal control. The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot be used in this setting The goal is chromosome arm-level gains and losses rather than focal amplifications, or the input is a raw fragment file rather than a normalized binned matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects focal amplifications in single cells by running mean-variance changepoint segmentation on per-cell, per-chromosome scaled scATAC-seq bin profiles (Copy-scAT), flagging segments whose scaled signal exceeds a z-score > 5 cutoff relative to the chromosome baseline, then pooling per-cell calls into consensus amplified regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Detects focal amplifications in single cells by running mean-variance changepoint segmentation on per-cell, per-chromosome scaled scATAC-seq bin profiles (Copy-scAT), flagging segments whose scaled signal exceeds a z-score > 5 cutoff relative to the chromosome baseline, then pooling per-cell calls into consensus amplified regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot be used in this setting The goal is chromosome arm-level gains and losses rather than focal amplifications, or the input is a raw fragment file rather than a normalized binned matrix

skills.description: Use when comparing categorical occurrence counts (e.g., motif families from Genomatix MatBase) between test and control sequence sets to quantify which category is most enriched, such as STAT motif enrichment in ChIP-Seq peaks versus ChIP-chip regions.
skills.name: chi-square-contingency-analysis
skills.search_text: chi-square-contingency-analysis Use when comparing categorical occurrence counts (e.g., motif families from Genomatix MatBase) between test and control sequence sets to quantify which category is most enriched, such as STAT motif enrichment in ChIP-Seq peaks versus ChIP-chip regions. Peak calling or read-enriched region definition is still needed — use HPeak (HMM with GP/ZIP emissions) first; chi-square analysis only evaluates the resulting sequences The motifs of interest are not represented in a motif matrix database (the authors note many stored motifs may be inaccurate and novel motifs may not exist in databases) http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 A family-level motif enrichment comparison that tabulates MatInspector motif family occurrence counts in test versus control sequences and applies chi-square statistics to test each motif family's enrichment, as used to show STAT family enrichment in STAT1 ChIP-Seq peaks exceeds that in ChIP-chip regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: A family-level motif enrichment comparison that tabulates MatInspector motif family occurrence counts in test versus control sequences and applies chi-square statistics to test each motif family's enrichment, as used to show STAT family enrichment in STAT1 ChIP-Seq peaks exceeds that in ChIP-chip regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peak calling or read-enriched region definition is still needed — use HPeak (HMM with GP/ZIP emissions) first; chi-square analysis only evaluates the resulting sequences The motifs of interest are not represented in a motif matrix database (the authors note many stored motifs may be inaccurate and novel motifs may not exist in databases)

skills.description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing epihaplotype matrices (binary mCpG per molecule) must be mined for statistically significant co-methylated CpG combinations underlying stable epiallele families.
skills.name: chi-square-independence-testing-of-mcpg-combinations
skills.search_text: chi-square-independence-testing-of-mcpg-combinations Use when bisulfite-sequencing epihaplotype matrices (binary mCpG per molecule) must be mined for statistically significant co-methylated CpG combinations underlying stable epiallele families. The goal is quantifying methylation of single CpGs or abundance of individual epialleles without testing phased co-occurrence — tools like ampliMethProfiler, methclone or EBA are designed for that, and MethCoresProfiler's independence testing is unnecessary. Input data are not single-molecule (phased) bisulfite reads; unphased bulk methylation levels cannot support co-occurrence testing of mCpG pairs within molecules. Randomized/shuffled epihaplotype controls are the input: by construction mCpGs are independent, so all combinations should be non-significant and the test would flag nothing meaningful. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Statistical core of MethCoresProfiler: identify which combinations of phased methylated CpGs (mCpGs) co-occur within single DNA molecules more frequently than expected under independence, using chi-square tests of independence at P ≤ 10−9, to define the 'methylated cores' shared by epiallele families. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Statistical core of MethCoresProfiler: identify which combinations of phased methylated CpGs (mCpGs) co-occur within single DNA molecules more frequently than expected under independence, using chi-square tests of independence at P ≤ 10−9, to define the 'methylated cores' shared by epiallele families.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is quantifying methylation of single CpGs or abundance of individual epialleles without testing phased co-occurrence — tools like ampliMethProfiler, methclone or EBA are designed for that, and MethCoresProfiler's independence testing is unnecessary. Input data are not single-molecule (phased) bisulfite reads; unphased bulk methylation levels cannot support co-occurrence testing of mCpG pairs within molecules. Randomized/shuffled epihaplotype controls are the input: by construction mCpGs are independent, so all combinations should be non-significant and the test would flag nothing meaningful.

skills.description: Use when a weighted, correlation-corrected per-gene p-value (e.g. from SMITE's scorePval/stoufferTest with MCM bootstrapping) must be converted into a single comparable score statistic and calibrated against a known null distribution for gene- or module-level significance.
skills.name: chi-square-score-transformation
skills.search_text: chi-square-score-transformation Use when a weighted, correlation-corrected per-gene p-value (e.g. from SMITE's scorePval/stoufferTest with MCM bootstrapping) must be converted into a single comparable score statistic and calibrated against a known null distribution for gene- or module-level significance. Component p-values are independent and correlation correction plus MCM bootstrapping is unnecessary — plain Fisher's method on raw p-values suffices without SMITE's resampling Input is a single omics layer with no weighted combination of expression and methylation component scores to integrate The task is module discovery/topology via spin-glass algorithms (igraph spinglass, FEM) rather than per-gene score calibration against a Chi-square null Transforms each gene's integrated SMITE significance into a single score via Fisher's method, G_i = −2ln(p_i), where p_i is the per-gene p-value from MCM bootstrapping of the correlation-aware Stouffer combination of expression and methylation component scores; G is approximately Chi-square distributed with 2 degrees of freedom. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Transforms each gene's integrated SMITE significance into a single score via Fisher's method, G_i = −2ln(p_i), where p_i is the per-gene p-value from MCM bootstrapping of the correlation-aware Stouffer combination of expression and methylation component scores; G is approximately Chi-square distributed with 2 degrees of freedom.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Component p-values are independent and correlation correction plus MCM bootstrapping is unnecessary — plain Fisher's method on raw p-values suffices without SMITE's resampling Input is a single omics layer with no weighted combination of expression and methylation component scores to integrate The task is module discovery/topology via spin-glass algorithms (igraph spinglass, FEM) rather than per-gene score calibration against a Chi-square null

skills.description: Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from two or more Hi-C contact maps are quantile-normalized and you must call per-bin significant compartment differences, including changes without a compartment flip.
skills.name: chi-square-significance-testing
skills.search_text: chi-square-significance-testing Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from two or more Hi-C contact maps are quantile-normalized and you must call per-bin significant compartment differences, including changes without a compartment flip. You only have a single Hi-C contact map with no second condition to compare — standard PCA per-map compartment calling is the right scope (standard PCA is limited to analyzing each contact map individually, which is why dcHiC's distance step exists) Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized across maps/replicates; applying the distance measure to non-comparable scores invalidates the covariance estimate You need differential interaction calls rather than compartment-level differences — Fit-Hi-C (which dcHiC integrates for loops anchored in significant differential compartments) is the relevant tool http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 dcHiC's step-2 differential compartment procedure: compute a per-bin Mahalanobis distance on quantile-normalized PC1/PC2 compartment scores, assign chi-square p-values to flag outlier bins, and correct for multiple testing with IHW or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: dcHiC's step-2 differential compartment procedure: compute a per-bin Mahalanobis distance on quantile-normalized PC1/PC2 compartment scores, assign chi-square p-values to flag outlier bins, and correct for multiple testing with IHW or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains spanning kb to Mb scales (e.g., H3K27me3 or H3K9me3) from mapped-read BED files, especially where whole-domain integrity (covering full gene bodies of repressed genes) matters more than sharp peak positions.

skills.search_text: chip-seq-broad-domain-calling Use when the goal is to identify broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains spanning kb to Mb scales (e.g., H3K27me3 or H3K9me3) from mapped-read BED files, especially where whole-domain integrity (covering full gene bodies of repressed genes) matters more than sharp peak positions. The target marks produce sharp, punctate peaks rather than diffuse kb-to-Mb domains (RECOGNICER is designed for broad signal detection, not narrow peak calling) You need to resolve two domains separated by fine-scale gaps — RECOGNICER can falsely merge them into one coarse-scale domain, requiring manual monitoring or masked/featured regions Multiple RECOGNICER instances must run in parallel from the same directory (hard-coded temporary filenames will interfere); use separate directories instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Call multi-scale broad enrichment domains (kb-to-Mb, e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3) from ChIP-seq mapped reads using RECOGNICER's recursive coarse-graining block transformation, followed by candidate domain retrieval with boundary determination and Poisson-model significance testing with FDR control. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Call multi-scale broad enrichment domains (kb-to-Mb, e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3) from ChIP-seq mapped reads using RECOGNICER's recursive coarse-graining block transformation, followed by candidate domain retrieval with boundary determination and Poisson-model significance testing with FDR control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target marks produce sharp, punctate peaks rather than diffuse kb-to-Mb domains (RECOGNICER is designed for broad signal detection, not narrow peak calling) You need to resolve two domains separated by fine-scale gaps — RECOGNICER can falsely merge them into one coarse-scale domain, requiring manual monitoring or masked/featured regions Multiple RECOGNICER instances must run in parallel from the same directory (hard-coded temporary filenames will interfere); use separate directories instead

skills.search_text: chip-seq-coverage-binning Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM files for one or more epigenomic marks (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3/H3K9ac) plus a MACS/MACS2 peak list must be turned into fixed-width binned coverage profiles for shape-based alignment or clustering. The coverage data are already binned into fixed windows or represented as a feature table, so re-binning is redundant. The analysis requires absolute-position or gene-anchored comparison (e.g. explicitly anchored on transcription start sites or gene annotation) rather than unsupervised shape alignment. Peak regions are shorter than 5 or longer than 1000 bins, or contain no bin with more than 10 reads, so they fall outside the analysed set by design. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Converts aligned-read ChIP-seq BAM signal for multiple epigenomic marks into fixed-length, per-peak coverage profiles by extending single-end reads to estimated fragment lengths and binning coverage into non-overlapping 50 bp windows, so each peak becomes a sequence of multidimensional vectors suitable for DTW-based shape comparison in DGW. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0

skills.when_to_use_negative: The coverage data are already binned into fixed windows or represented as a feature table, so re-binning is redundant. skills.description: Use when a differential ChIP-seq analysis needs its raw aligned reads (BAM) fetched from public repositories, specifically when reproducing the ENCODE H1-hESC vs K562 histone mark comparison via GEO sample accessions.
skills.name: chip-seq-data-retrieval-from-geo
skills.search_text: chip-seq-data-retrieval-from-geo Use when a differential ChIP-seq analysis needs its raw aligned reads (BAM) fetched from public repositories, specifically when reproducing the ENCODE H1-hESC vs K562 histone mark comparison via GEO sample accessions. The analysis requires unaligned FASTQ reads or a different genome assembly than hg19 — the article used only the aligned hg19 BAM files. The target samples are not covered by the article's listed GEO accessions (e.g. the Roadmap Epigenomics SRA runs SRR019561–SRR029349 or rat rn4 data use different accession routes). Peak-like (narrow) histone marks or transcription factor ChIP-seq are the target — histoneHMM is designed for broad genomic footprints like H3K27me3 and H3K9me3. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0607 Retrieves aligned ChIP-seq BAM files for histone marks H3K9me3, H3K79me2, H3K36me3 and H3K27me3 in H1-hESC and K562 from the ENCODE GEO sample accessions cited in the histoneHMM article (hg19 assembly), providing the raw input for downstream bivariate HMM differential analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Retrieves aligned ChIP-seq BAM files for histone marks H3K9me3, H3K79me2, H3K36me3 and H3K27me3 in H1-hESC and K562 from the ENCODE GEO sample accessions cited in the histoneHMM article (hg19 assembly), providing the raw input for downstream bivariate HMM differential analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires unaligned FASTQ reads or a different genome assembly than hg19 — the article used only the aligned hg19 BAM files. The target samples are not covered by the article's listed GEO accessions (e.g. the Roadmap Epigenomics SRA runs SRR019561–SRR029349 or rat rn4 data use different accession routes). skills.summary: Constructs a per-bin ChIP-Seq coverage signal by directionally extending short reads into hypothetical DNA fragments (HDFs) following Robertson et al., partitioning the genome into fixed-length 25 bp bins, and counting HDF coverage per bin with HPeak's unbalanced weighting scheme that down-weights fragment-end coverage. skills.search_text: chip-seq-motif-prediction Use when raw or processed human ChIP-seq peak calls (e.g. ENCODE BED with summits) are available and the goal is to discover TF-DNA binding motifs with significance scores and compare them to documented motifs. Input is already a curated motif or feature table rather than ChIP-seq peak coordinates; no motif discovery is needed. The organism/genome lacks a matched reference FASTA and GC-matched background sequences, so per-dataset CNN training cannot be grounded. Only DNA shape features (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) are of interest and no sequence-based model comparison is required — use the DNAShape branch specifically instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a CNN-based deep learning framework (DESSO) on 101-bp ChIP-seq peak sequences from ENCODE datasets and predict sequence/shape motifs with a binomial-distribution cutoff scan, benchmarked against DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP, KMAC and gkm-SVM using TOMTOM similarity to JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Train a CNN-based deep learning framework (DESSO) on 101-bp ChIP-seq peak sequences from ENCODE datasets and predict sequence/shape motifs with a binomial-distribution cutoff scan, benchmarked against DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP, KMAC and gkm-SVM using TOMTOM similarity to JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated motif or feature table rather than ChIP-seq peak coordinates; no motif discovery is needed. skills.description: Use when the input is raw ChIP-Seq short reads (BED or ELAND format, human or mouse) or BED files for transcription-factor or histone-mark datasets, and the goal is to identify read-enriched regions and compare peak callers.

skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-calling Use when the input is raw ChIP-Seq short reads (BED or ELAND format, human or mouse) or BED files for transcription-factor or histone-mark datasets, and the goal is to identify read-enriched regions and compare peak callers. The analysis goal is comparative histone modification (differential) data — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to that setting, not HPeak. A rigorous false detection rate estimate is required — the authors state 'our method is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', which may disadvantage HPeak in FDR-based comparisons. Peak summits require strand/orientation information — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Calls ChIP-enriched genomic regions from short-read ChIP-Seq data using HPeak, a two-state HMM that partitions the genome into 25 bp bins, extends reads directionally into hypothetical DNA fragments (HDFs), and models enriched-bin counts with a generalized Poisson (GP) emission and background counts with a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Calls ChIP-enriched genomic regions from short-read ChIP-Seq data using HPeak, a two-state HMM that partitions the genome into 25 bp bins, extends reads directionally into hypothetical DNA fragments (HDFs), and models enriched-bin counts with a generalized Poisson (GP) emission and background counts with a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is comparative histone modification (differential) data — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to that setting, not HPeak. A rigorous false detection rate estimate is required — the authors state 'our method is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', which may disadvantage HPeak in FDR-based comparisons. Peak summits require strand/orientation information — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak.

skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-calling-for-loop-anchors Use when processing ChIA-PET data where chromatin loops must be called between ChIP-Seq-like peak anchors, e.g. after bwa alignment and removeDup, before bedpe2Interaction/MICC loop calling. skills.summary: Converts deduplicated ChIA-PET bedpe files to tagAlign format with buildTagAlign and calls anchor peaks with MACS2 (q-value 0.05) so that chromatin interactions can be detected between peak-anchored PET pairs, as implemented in the ChIA-PET2 pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw paired-end FASTQ — linker trimming (trimLinker), bwa alignment and removeDup must precede tagAlign/peak calling Data are not from a peak-anchored assay (e.g. Hi-C contact maps) — ChIA-PET2 loop calling assumes anchors sit at ChIP-Seq-like peaks The bedpe already contains interactions restricted to known peak anchors and no new peak calling is needed
