skills.description: Use when starting from aligned-read BAM files of one or more ChIP-seq marks plus a matched input/control BAM, and you need enriched peak regions (e.g. as BED input for unsupervised alignment/clustering) rather than gene-anchored windows.
skills.name: chip-seq-peak-calling-with-control
skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-calling-with-control Use when starting from aligned-read BAM files of one or more ChIP-seq marks plus a matched input/control BAM, and you need enriched peak regions (e.g. as BED input for unsupervised alignment/clustering) rather than gene-anchored windows. When peaks are already available or the input is a pre-computed enrichment/feature table — only the subsequent DGW stages are needed, not peak calling. When the analysis is anchored to genomic landmarks such as transcription start sites or gene annotation, since this skill specifically derives peak regions from MACS2 calls rather than annotation-anchored windows. When no matched input/control sample exists for the ChIP-seq experiment, as MACS2 enrichment here is defined relative to the input control BAM. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Call ChIP-seq enriched regions with MACS2 against an input control sample (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 and H3K9ac Std AlnRep1 BAMs vs the K562 Control Std AlnRep1 BAM) and merge peak sets across marks to define regions of interest for downstream shape-based analysis such as DGW. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Call ChIP-seq enriched regions with MACS2 against an input control sample (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 and H3K9ac Std AlnRep1 BAMs vs the K562 Control Std AlnRep1 BAM) and merge peak sets across marks to define regions of interest for downstream shape-based analysis such as DGW.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peaks are already available or the input is a pre-computed enrichment/feature table — only the subsequent DGW stages are needed, not peak calling. When the analysis is anchored to genomic landmarks such as transcription start sites or gene annotation, since this skill specifically derives peak regions from MACS2 calls rather than annotation-anchored windows. When no matched input/control sample exists for the ChIP-seq experiment, as MACS2 enrichment here is defined relative to the input control BAM.

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs (e.g. the 100 TFs expressed in K562) have DESSO-predicted motifs and TFBSs, and you need to separate direct from indirect binding to infer tethering.
skills.name: chip-seq-peak-motif-classification
skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-motif-classification Use when ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs (e.g. the 100 TFs expressed in K562) have DESSO-predicted motifs and TFBSs, and you need to separate direct from indirect binding to infer tethering. Peaks lacking DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs for the TF panel, so no own-motif vs. other-motif discrimination is possible Studies aiming to discover de novo motifs rather than classify existing peaks — DESSO motif prediction (train.py/predict.py) should be run first Single-TF ChIP-seq analysis with no second TF's motifs available for cross-matching indirect peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Classifies each ChIP-seq peak of a TF into direct-binding (D), indirect-binding (I), or indecipherable (K) sets based on whether the peak contains the TF's own DESSO-predicted motif, another TF's motif, or neither, enabling downstream inference of protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Classifies each ChIP-seq peak of a TF into direct-binding (D), indirect-binding (I), or indecipherable (K) sets based on whether the peak contains the TF's own DESSO-predicted motif, another TF's motif, or neither, enabling downstream inference of protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks lacking DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs for the TF panel, so no own-motif vs. other-motif discrimination is possible Studies aiming to discover de novo motifs rather than classify existing peaks — DESSO motif prediction (train.py/predict.py) should be run first Single-TF ChIP-seq analysis with no second TF's motifs available for cross-matching indirect peaks

skills.description: Use when preparing summit-centered, score-annotated FASTA inputs for MEPP positional motif profiling from MACS2 narrowpeak calls (e.g. ENCODE K562 GATA1 ChIP-seq or mESC Nanog ChIP-seq/ChIP-nexus peaks).
skills.name: chip-seq-peak-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-sequence-extraction Use when preparing summit-centered, score-annotated FASTA inputs for MEPP positional motif profiling from MACS2 narrowpeak calls (e.g. ENCODE K562 GATA1 ChIP-seq or mESC Nanog ChIP-seq/ChIP-nexus peaks). Input is a whole peak interval or a BED file without summit (narrowPeak) coordinates — MEPP positional profiles require a well-defined anchor point such as the MACS2 summit, not arbitrary region boundaries Sequences lack a score and would have to be binarized — MEPP's design avoids arbitrary threshold selection and needs a score-based continuum of biological interest De novo motif discovery is the goal — MEPP 'currently functions with a fixed motif library' and its motif-learning module, not interval extraction, would be the wrong frame here http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Extracts ±200 bp genomic sequences centered on MACS2 peak summits from ChIP-seq or ChIP-nexus narrowpeak calls and attaches each peak's MACS2 log2 fold-change as a sequence-level score, producing the scored FASTA continuum that MEPP requires for positional motif enrichment profiling. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Extracts ±200 bp genomic sequences centered on MACS2 peak summits from ChIP-seq or ChIP-nexus narrowpeak calls and attaches each peak's MACS2 log2 fold-change as a sequence-level score, producing the scored FASTA continuum that MEPP requires for positional motif enrichment profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a whole peak interval or a BED file without summit (narrowPeak) coordinates — MEPP positional profiles require a well-defined anchor point such as the MACS2 summit, not arbitrary region boundaries Sequences lack a score and would have to be binarized — MEPP's design avoids arbitrary threshold selection and needs a score-based continuum of biological interest De novo motif discovery is the goal — MEPP 'currently functions with a fixed motif library' and its motif-learning module, not interval extraction, would be the wrong frame here

skills.description: Use when you have TR ChIP-seq peak bed files with signal enrichment values and gene TSS annotations and need quantitative TR-target scores (RP scores) rather than binary target lists.
skills.name: chip-seq-peak-signal-integration
skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-signal-integration Use when you have TR ChIP-seq peak bed files with signal enrichment values and gene TSS annotations and need quantitative TR-target scores (RP scores) rather than binary target lists. ChIP-seq data lacks reliable target information or contains too few targets — the paper notes such data 'would mislead the identification of TRs' You only need a binary TR-target list rather than quantitative, signal-weighted regulation strengths Peak files lack signal enrichment values (m), making the modified peak-strength weighting inapplicable http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Compute regulatory-potential (RP) scores from ENCODE TR ChIP-seq peaks using RePhine's modified model, which weights each peak-to-target distance contribution by the peak's ENCODE signal enrichment (m) in addition to peak count and distance, yielding a gene x TR RP-score matrix for downstream drug-response regulator identification. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Compute regulatory-potential (RP) scores from ENCODE TR ChIP-seq peaks using RePhine's modified model, which weights each peak-to-target distance contribution by the peak's ENCODE signal enrichment (m) in addition to peak count and distance, yielding a gene x TR RP-score matrix for downstream drug-response regulator identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ChIP-seq data lacks reliable target information or contains too few targets — the paper notes such data 'would mislead the identification of TRs' You only need a binary TR-target list rather than quantitative, signal-weighted regulation strengths Peak files lack signal enrichment values (m), making the modified peak-strength weighting inapplicable

skills.description: Use when strand-annotated ChIP-seq peak BED files and strand-assigned TFBS BED files are available and the goal is to test whether motif-level strand asymmetry (e.g. CTCF non-template strand preference) is recapitulated within peaks.
skills.name: chip-seq-peak-strand-orientation-analysis
skills.search_text: chip-seq-peak-strand-orientation-analysis Use when strand-annotated ChIP-seq peak BED files and strand-assigned TFBS BED files are available and the goal is to test whether motif-level strand asymmetry (e.g. CTCF non-template strand preference) is recapitulated within peaks. The peak or TFBS features are not strand-annotated and no independent orientation source exists — use Asymmetron's orientation function first or a different approach The question concerns consecutive occurrences of a single element or pairs of motifs, not motifs contained within regions — use consecutive_patterns or pairwise_asymmetries instead Motifs are palindromic, so +/− orientation is uninformative (e.g. some motif classes) and same/opposite classification is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A validation skill that tests whether transcription factor binding site (TFBS) orientation biases are corroborated by an independent analysis of TF orientation within strand-annotated ChIP-seq peaks, using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries function and two-tailed binomial tests with Bonferroni correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: A validation skill that tests whether transcription factor binding site (TFBS) orientation biases are corroborated by an independent analysis of TF orientation within strand-annotated ChIP-seq peaks, using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries function and two-tailed binomial tests with Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak or TFBS features are not strand-annotated and no independent orientation source exists — use Asymmetron's orientation function first or a different approach The question concerns consecutive occurrences of a single element or pairs of motifs, not motifs contained within regions — use consecutive_patterns or pairwise_asymmetries instead Motifs are palindromic, so +/− orientation is uninformative (e.g. some motif classes) and same/opposite classification is meaningless

skills.description: Use when compiling ChiLin QC outputs (e.g., id_frip FRiP JSON records) and you need to benchmark what proportion of ChIP versus input samples exceed a 1% FRiP threshold.
skills.name: chip-seq-quality-atlas-stratification
skills.search_text: chip-seq-quality-atlas-stratification Use when compiling ChiLin QC outputs (e.g., id_frip FRiP JSON records) and you need to benchmark what proportion of ChIP versus input samples exceed a 1% FRiP threshold. Input is raw FASTQ/BAM data rather than already-compiled FRiP QC records — run the ChiLin pipeline including step 7 (FRiP score calculation) first The goal is general QC of a single experiment (PBC, NSC/RSC, fragment size) rather than population-level FRiP threshold assessment across the quality atlas Samples cannot be reliably classified as ChIP treatment versus input control, since the stratified proportions depend on this distinction http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Stratifies samples from the compiled ChiLin quality atlas (23,677 public ChIP-seq and DNase-seq samples) into ChIP (treatment) versus input (control) classes and evaluates them against a 1% FRiP score cutoff to validate FRiP as a ChIP enrichment reference metric. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Stratifies samples from the compiled ChiLin quality atlas (23,677 public ChIP-seq and DNase-seq samples) into ChIP (treatment) versus input (control) classes and evaluates them against a 1% FRiP score cutoff to validate FRiP as a ChIP enrichment reference metric.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/BAM data rather than already-compiled FRiP QC records — run the ChiLin pipeline including step 7 (FRiP score calculation) first The goal is general QC of a single experiment (PBC, NSC/RSC, fragment size) rather than population-level FRiP threshold assessment across the quality atlas Samples cannot be reliably classified as ChIP treatment versus input control, since the stratified proportions depend on this distinction

skills.description: Use when raw ChIP-seq FASTQ libraries from a spike-in experiment (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 GSE60104 with fruit fly spike-in) must be mapped to a concatenated synthetic reference and filtered before genome segmentation and normalization.
skills.name: chip-seq-read-alignment-spike-in-genome
skills.search_text: chip-seq-read-alignment-spike-in-genome Use when raw ChIP-seq FASTQ libraries from a spike-in experiment (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 GSE60104 with fruit fly spike-in) must be mapped to a concatenated synthetic reference and filtered before genome segmentation and normalization. BAM files of each sample/spike genome have already been generated with a mapping tool — spikChIP consumes these directly and remapping would be redundant The experiment has no exogenous spike-in material, so a synthetic combined genome is unnecessary and mapping should target the single sample genome Peak calling or normalization stages are the goal — those use MACS2 BED peaks and the spikChIP normalization strategies (RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAG REMOVAL, SPIKCHIP), not the mapping step http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Maps raw ChIP-seq FASTQ reads against a combined sample+spike-in (e.g. hg19+dm3) reference genome with Bowtie, discarding multi-locus reads, and removes unmapped alignments with Samtools so downstream per-bin counting can separate human sample reads from fly spike-in reads. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Maps raw ChIP-seq FASTQ reads against a combined sample+spike-in (e.g. hg19+dm3) reference genome with Bowtie, discarding multi-locus reads, and removes unmapped alignments with Samtools so downstream per-bin counting can separate human sample reads from fly spike-in reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: BAM files of each sample/spike genome have already been generated with a mapping tool — spikChIP consumes these directly and remapping would be redundant The experiment has no exogenous spike-in material, so a synthetic combined genome is unnecessary and mapping should target the single sample genome Peak calling or normalization stages are the goal — those use MACS2 BED peaks and the spikChIP normalization strategies (RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAG REMOVAL, SPIKCHIP), not the mapping step

skills.description: Use when preparing raw ChIP-seq BAM files of broad-footprint histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3) for histoneHMM differential or single-sample calling, where per-bin bivariate read counts must be computed before HMM fitting.
skills.name: chip-seq-read-count-binning
skills.search_text: chip-seq-read-count-binning Use when preparing raw ChIP-seq BAM files of broad-footprint histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3) for histoneHMM differential or single-sample calling, where per-bin bivariate read counts must be computed before HMM fitting. The modification has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse marks — the article notes peak-searching methods are the wrong model for broad marks like H3K27me3, and conversely binning-based histoneHMM is aimed at broad footprints Input is already a binned read-count table (e.g. the distributed BN.txt/SHR.txt preprocessed data) — skip directly to HMM fitting A caller requiring per-base or peak-level resolution is needed, since aggregation into 1000 bp bins deliberately discards sub-bin resolution http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Partition a genome into equally sized 1000 bp bins and aggregate ChIP-seq short-read counts per bin per sample, producing the binned bivariate read-count table that histoneHMM requires as input for its unsupervised HMM classification of broad histone marks like H3K27me3. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Partition a genome into equally sized 1000 bp bins and aggregate ChIP-seq short-read counts per bin per sample, producing the binned bivariate read-count table that histoneHMM requires as input for its unsupervised HMM classification of broad histone marks like H3K27me3.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modification has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse marks — the article notes peak-searching methods are the wrong model for broad marks like H3K27me3, and conversely binning-based histoneHMM is aimed at broad footprints Input is already a binned read-count table (e.g. the distributed BN.txt/SHR.txt preprocessed data) — skip directly to HMM fitting A caller requiring per-base or peak-level resolution is needed, since aggregation into 1000 bp bins deliberately discards sub-bin resolution

skills.description: Use when raw Illumina ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g., TF immunoprecipitation samples from GEO accession GSE136050) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed prior to genome alignment and macs2 peak calling.
skills.name: chip-seq-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: chip-seq-read-quality-trimming Use when raw Illumina ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g., TF immunoprecipitation samples from GEO accession GSE136050) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed prior to genome alignment and macs2 peak calling. Input is already trimmed or provided as aligned BAM files — skip trimming and go directly to bwa mem mapping and macs2 peak calling. The goal is RNA-seq differential expression (GSE136191 in this study) rather than TF binding peak detection; the trimming rationale here targets ChIP-seq peak calling. Peak sets are already called and the task is only overlap/annotation analysis (e.g., findOverlaps.pl, getPeakAnno.pl on existing macs2 output). http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Trims adapters and low-quality bases from ChIP-seq FASTQ reads with Trimmomatic before aligning to the V. harveyi ATCC BAA-1116 genome (bwa) and calling TF binding peaks with macs2, the pipeline used to quantify LuxR and H-NS occupancy in GSE136050. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Trims adapters and low-quality bases from ChIP-seq FASTQ reads with Trimmomatic before aligning to the V. harveyi ATCC BAA-1116 genome (bwa) and calling TF binding peaks with macs2, the pipeline used to quantify LuxR and H-NS occupancy in GSE136050.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already trimmed or provided as aligned BAM files — skip trimming and go directly to bwa mem mapping and macs2 peak calling. The goal is RNA-seq differential expression (GSE136191 in this study) rather than TF binding peak detection; the trimming rationale here targets ChIP-seq peak calling. Peak sets are already called and the task is only overlap/annotation analysis (e.g., findOverlaps.pl, getPeakAnno.pl on existing macs2 output).

skills.description: Use when preparing mapped ChIP-seq (or control) BED files for broad-domain calling with RECOGNICER, i.e. when the analysis requires converting raw read coordinates into nucleosome-resolution (default 200 bp) binary blocks before recursive block transformation.
skills.name: chip-seq-read-window-binning
skills.search_text: chip-seq-read-window-binning Use when preparing mapped ChIP-seq (or control) BED files for broad-domain calling with RECOGNICER, i.e. when the analysis requires converting raw read coordinates into nucleosome-resolution (default 200 bp) binary blocks before recursive block transformation. The task is peak calling for sharp, punctate transcription-factor signals rather than broad domains (kb-to-Mb H3K27me3/H3K9me3-style enrichment), where local-statistical peak callers are the article's stated contrast Input data are not mapped reads in BED format (e.g. alignment BAM files that have not been converted, or already-binned signal tracks), since RECOGNICER v1.0 expects two BED files Multiple RECOGNICER instances must run from the same directory, since temporary files have hard-coded names and parallel runs from one directory would produce absurd outcomes — use separate directories instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocessing step of RECOGNICER that converts mapped ChIP-seq reads in BED format into binary ('0'/'1') 200 bp genomic blocks by shifting single-end read 5' ends by half the DNA fragment size and thresholding window read counts against the random-placement average, providing the finest-scale input for downstream coarse-graining. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Preprocessing step of RECOGNICER that converts mapped ChIP-seq reads in BED format into binary ('0'/'1') 200 bp genomic blocks by shifting single-end read 5' ends by half the DNA fragment size and thresholding window read counts against the random-placement average, providing the finest-scale input for downstream coarse-graining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is peak calling for sharp, punctate transcription-factor signals rather than broad domains (kb-to-Mb H3K27me3/H3K9me3-style enrichment), where local-statistical peak callers are the article's stated contrast Input data are not mapped reads in BED format (e.g. alignment BAM files that have not been converted, or already-binned signal tracks), since RECOGNICER v1.0 expects two BED files Multiple RECOGNICER instances must run from the same directory, since temporary files have hard-coded names and parallel runs from one directory would produce absurd outcomes — use separate directories instead

skills.description: Use when predicting TF-DNA binding specificity from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks with long DNA sequences (1001 bp) and a gated CNN, or when comparing GCNN AUCs against the 101-bp one-layer CNN baseline.
skills.name: chip-seq-sequence-encoding-and-gc-matched-background-sampling
skills.search_text: chip-seq-sequence-encoding-and-gc-matched-background-sampling Use when predicting TF-DNA binding specificity from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks with long DNA sequences (1001 bp) and a gated CNN, or when comparing GCNN AUCs against the 101-bp one-layer CNN baseline. Goal is motif prediction with the one-layer CNN on 101-bp peaks (use --peak_flank 50 --network CNN instead of GCNN with peak_flank 500). Input is DNA shape features (DNAShape: HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than DNA sequences — use --feature_format DNAShape, not Seq. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Assemble GC-matched long-sequence ChIP-seq inputs (e.g., 1001-bp peak windows from data/encode_1001 plus GRCh37.p13.genome.fa) for training DESSO's gated-CNN (GCNN) to predict TF–DNA binding specificity, evaluating with test-set ROC AUC. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Assemble GC-matched long-sequence ChIP-seq inputs (e.g., 1001-bp peak windows from data/encode_1001 plus GRCh37.p13.genome.fa) for training DESSO's gated-CNN (GCNN) to predict TF–DNA binding specificity, evaluating with test-set ROC AUC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Goal is motif prediction with the one-layer CNN on 101-bp peaks (use --peak_flank 50 --network CNN instead of GCNN with peak_flank 500). Input is DNA shape features (DNAShape: HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than DNA sequences — use --feature_format DNAShape, not Seq.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking peak callers on qbed calling-cards data and you need orthogonal validation: average ChIP-seq (bigWig) signal under each caller's peaks plus pairwise peak-overlap concordance between callers.
skills.name: chip-seq-signal-aggregation-over-peaks
skills.search_text: chip-seq-signal-aggregation-over-peaks Use when benchmarking peak callers on qbed calling-cards data and you need orthogonal validation: average ChIP-seq (bigWig) signal under each caller's peaks plus pairwise peak-overlap concordance between callers. Input is already a differential peak or gene-expression result — this skill validates peak-caller output quality, not downstream differential analysis No matching ChIP-seq bigWig signal track exists for the cell type and factor of the calling-cards data, since signal aggregation would be uninterpretable Peaks have not yet been called and filtered (pp.filter_peaks); aggregating signal over raw insertions rather than peak intervals defeats the comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Aggregates ChIP-seq signal (e.g., H3K27ac, SP1 bigWig tracks) under called calling-cards peaks to quantify how well each peak caller's outputs are enriched for orthogonal TF-binding evidence, enabling quantitative comparison of CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, and ccf_tools. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Aggregates ChIP-seq signal (e.g., H3K27ac, SP1 bigWig tracks) under called calling-cards peaks to quantify how well each peak caller's outputs are enriched for orthogonal TF-binding evidence, enabling quantitative comparison of CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, and ccf_tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a differential peak or gene-expression result — this skill validates peak-caller output quality, not downstream differential analysis No matching ChIP-seq bigWig signal track exists for the cell type and factor of the calling-cards data, since signal aggregation would be uninterpretable Peaks have not yet been called and filtered (pp.filter_peaks); aggregating signal over raw insertions rather than peak intervals defeats the comparison

skills.description: Use when validating Hi-C-derived sub-compartment probabilities against independent enrichment tracks (TSA-seq, ChIP-seq, cTSA-seq) and comparing correlation performance against published compartment callers.
skills.name: chip-seq-signal-benchmarking
skills.search_text: chip-seq-signal-benchmarking Use when validating Hi-C-derived sub-compartment probabilities against independent enrichment tracks (TSA-seq, ChIP-seq, cTSA-seq) and comparing correlation performance against published compartment callers. Input Hi-C interactions are not in HOMER HiCsummary format — reformat or run runHiCpca.pl first, as the tool explicitly only accepts that format You need per-region visualization rather than benchmarking — use the XXX_cscore.bedgraph output instead of computing correlations http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark inferred 3D sub-compartment scores (A1, B1, B3) from CscoreTool-M against independent protein-DNA interaction datasets (SON TSA-seq for A1, H3K27me3 ChIP-seq for B1, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq for B3) by computing genome-wide correlation coefficients against competing methods (Rao's Gaussian-HMM, SNIPER, SCI, Calder). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Benchmark inferred 3D sub-compartment scores (A1, B1, B3) from CscoreTool-M against independent protein-DNA interaction datasets (SON TSA-seq for A1, H3K27me3 ChIP-seq for B1, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq for B3) by computing genome-wide correlation coefficients against competing methods (Rao's Gaussian-HMM, SNIPER, SCI, Calder).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C interactions are not in HOMER HiCsummary format — reformat or run runHiCpca.pl first, as the tool explicitly only accepts that format You need per-region visualization rather than benchmarking — use the XXX_cscore.bedgraph output instead of computing correlations

skills.description: Use when motif-centered genomic sequences need a continuous biological-activity score (e.g. mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal from GSE203135) so MEPP can profile partner-motif enrichment along a score continuum instead of arbitrary binding thresholds.
skills.name: chip-seq-signal-scoring-of-motif-sites
skills.search_text: chip-seq-signal-scoring-of-motif-sites Use when motif-centered genomic sequences need a continuous biological-activity score (e.g. mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal from GSE203135) so MEPP can profile partner-motif enrichment along a score continuum instead of arbitrary binding thresholds. No continuous activity track exists for the motif sites (no ChIP-seq signal for the factor) — there is nothing to rank sequences on and a score-based analysis cannot proceed The goal is de novo motif discovery: MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library, so scoring sequences will not reveal unmodeled partner motifs The design already bins sites into discrete classes or quartiles (CentriMo/TFEA-style analyses) rather than scoring each sequence on a continuum http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Attaches a continuous ChIP-seq activity score to each deduplicated, RepeatMasker-filtered motif-centered sequence (e.g. ±200 bp around mm10 Nanog motif sites, scored with mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal from GEO GSE203135) and writes MEPP's required '>sequence_name sequence_score' FASTA headers. The continuum scoring is what lets MEPP profile Sox2 motif enrichment positionally around central Nanog anchors without arbitrary binding thresholds. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Attaches a continuous ChIP-seq activity score to each deduplicated, RepeatMasker-filtered motif-centered sequence (e.g. ±200 bp around mm10 Nanog motif sites, scored with mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal from GEO GSE203135) and writes MEPP's required '>sequence_name sequence_score' FASTA headers. The continuum scoring is what lets MEPP profile Sox2 motif enrichment positionally around central Nanog anchors without arbitrary binding thresholds.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No continuous activity track exists for the motif sites (no ChIP-seq signal for the factor) — there is nothing to rank sequences on and a score-based analysis cannot proceed The goal is de novo motif discovery: MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library, so scoring sequences will not reveal unmodeled partner motifs The design already bins sites into discrete classes or quartiles (CentriMo/TFEA-style analyses) rather than scoring each sequence on a continuum

skills.description: Use when you have a BED file of TF ChIP-seq peaks and want to learn the biological function of the target genes linked to those binding regions via GO/KEGG enrichment.
skills.name: chip-seq-target-gene-set-analysis
skills.search_text: chip-seq-target-gene-set-analysis Use when you have a BED file of TF ChIP-seq peaks and want to learn the biological function of the target genes linked to those binding regions via GO/KEGG enrichment. The goal is to identify enriched TF motifs within the REM sequences rather than function of associated genes — use PASTAA motif enrichment instead You need REM–gene associations de novo from chromatin accessibility/expression data rather than linking existing ChIP-seq peaks to genes — use EpiRegio Gene Query/StitchIt workflow directly http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Functional enrichment analysis (g:Profiler, default parameters, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 0.05) of the gene set associated with a transcription factor's ChIP-seq binding regions, as demonstrated by mapping ARID3A peaks (ENCFF002CVL) to REMs with EpiRegio and recovering SLE/alcoholism KEGG pathways and chromatin-assembly GO terms. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Functional enrichment analysis (g:Profiler, default parameters, Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 0.05) of the gene set associated with a transcription factor's ChIP-seq binding regions, as demonstrated by mapping ARID3A peaks (ENCFF002CVL) to REMs with EpiRegio and recovering SLE/alcoholism KEGG pathways and chromatin-assembly GO terms.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify enriched TF motifs within the REM sequences rather than function of associated genes — use PASTAA motif enrichment instead You need REM–gene associations de novo from chromatin accessibility/expression data rather than linking existing ChIP-seq peaks to genes — use EpiRegio Gene Query/StitchIt workflow directly

skills.description: Use when you need to infer which genes a transcriptional regulator targets from ChIP-seq peak data (e.g., ENCODE), especially as input to regression-based drug response association such as RePhine on CCLE data.
skills.name: chip-seq-target-inference
skills.search_text: chip-seq-target-inference Use when you need to infer which genes a transcriptional regulator targets from ChIP-seq peak data (e.g., ENCODE), especially as input to regression-based drug response association such as RePhine on CCLE data. No ChIP-seq data exist for the TR of interest, or the available ChIP-seq data have too few targets — the article states this 'would mislead the identification of TRs' Reliable target information is unavailable for the TR — RePhine is restricted to cases where reliable target information exists The goal is to detect acquired (post-treatment) resistance mechanisms, e.g., acquired STAT3 activation for erlotinib, which RePhine could not detect from CCLE pre-treatment data http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Quantitative inference of transcriptional regulator (TR) targets from ENCODE ChIP-seq data by combining peak signal strength and the distances from peaks to targets, producing regulatory potential (RP) scores that RePhine uses to link TRs to drug response in CCLE pharmacogenomic data. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Quantitative inference of transcriptional regulator (TR) targets from ENCODE ChIP-seq data by combining peak signal strength and the distances from peaks to targets, producing regulatory potential (RP) scores that RePhine uses to link TRs to drug response in CCLE pharmacogenomic data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ChIP-seq data exist for the TR of interest, or the available ChIP-seq data have too few targets — the article states this 'would mislead the identification of TRs' Reliable target information is unavailable for the TR — RePhine is restricted to cases where reliable target information exists The goal is to detect acquired (post-treatment) resistance mechanisms, e.g., acquired STAT3 activation for erlotinib, which RePhine could not detect from CCLE pre-treatment data

skills.description: Use when filtered .bam/.bai ChIPseq alignments (e.g. post-samtools filter output) must be turned into genome-browser track files and GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis.
skills.name: chipseq-alignment-to-track-conversion
skills.search_text: chipseq-alignment-to-track-conversion Use when filtered .bam/.bai ChIPseq alignments (e.g. post-samtools filter output) must be turned into genome-browser track files and GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis. Input is still raw FASTQ or an unfiltered .bam that has not passed the NEAT 'filter' module (duplicate-read and fragment-size filtering) — run filtering and peakcalling first The goal is exploratory QC or metagene/DEG analysis rather than track-file generation (use the NEAT QC or 'Analyze project' modules instead) Converts NEAT's processed, filtered .bam/.bai ChIPseq alignments into visualization-ready genome-browser tracks — compressed small-size wiggle (.wig) files with bigwig counterparts — plus compact R/Bioconductor GRanges objects for downstream analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Converts NEAT's processed, filtered .bam/.bai ChIPseq alignments into visualization-ready genome-browser tracks — compressed small-size wiggle (.wig) files with bigwig counterparts — plus compact R/Bioconductor GRanges objects for downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ or an unfiltered .bam that has not passed the NEAT 'filter' module (duplicate-read and fragment-size filtering) — run filtering and peakcalling first The goal is exploratory QC or metagene/DEG analysis rather than track-file generation (use the NEAT QC or 'Analyze project' modules instead)

skills.description: Use when you have paired ChIP and control mapped-read BED files for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb domains) and need to call integral domains and compare their functional association across methods.
skills.name: chipseq-control-based-significance-testing
skills.search_text: chipseq-control-based-significance-testing Use when you have paired ChIP and control mapped-read BED files for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb domains) and need to call integral domains and compare their functional association across methods. Calling sharp, point-source transcription-factor peaks — the method is designed for broad domains (kb to Mb) and most existing peak callers handle local narrow enrichment The input is raw sequencing reads rather than mapped-read BED files, or no matched control BED sample is available for the control-based FDR significance testing You need a single-domain guarantee where two fine-scale domains separated by gaps must never be merged — coarse-graining can falsely merge such domains http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Calls broad H3K27me3 enrichment domains from ChIP-seq mapped reads using RECOGNICER's coarse-graining algorithm, with input-matched control-based significance (FDR) determination, and benchmarks the resulting domains against SICER, RSEG, and MUSIC on repressed-gene gene-body coverage. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Calls broad H3K27me3 enrichment domains from ChIP-seq mapped reads using RECOGNICER's coarse-graining algorithm, with input-matched control-based significance (FDR) determination, and benchmarks the resulting domains against SICER, RSEG, and MUSIC on repressed-gene gene-body coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling sharp, point-source transcription-factor peaks — the method is designed for broad domains (kb to Mb) and most existing peak callers handle local narrow enrichment The input is raw sequencing reads rather than mapped-read BED files, or no matched control BED sample is available for the control-based FDR significance testing You need a single-domain guarantee where two fine-scale domains separated by gaps must never be merged — coarse-graining can falsely merge such domains

skills.description: Use when you have region intervals stratified by TF occupancy (e.g. HOT >99th percentile, MILD 75th-99th, COLD <75th) plus IgG-control bigWig tracks, and need to quantify/plot class-wise control enrichment.
skills.name: chipseq-control-signal-profiling
skills.search_text: chipseq-control-signal-profiling Use when you have region intervals stratified by TF occupancy (e.g. HOT >99th percentile, MILD 75th-99th, COLD <75th) plus IgG-control bigWig tracks, and need to quantify/plot class-wise control enrichment. The goal is estimating what fraction of antibody-specific error comes from pull-down of non-target proteins vs. direct binding to polynucleotide epitopes — the paper states this is not possible with currently available data Input tracks are TF ChIP-seq samples rather than IgG/mock controls, so control ('hyper-ChIPable') enrichment cannot be assessed A KO ChIP-seq experiment shows no signal — lack of signal may reflect technical conditions (low read number, low library complexity, unsuccessful IP) rather than the artifact being probed here http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Profiles IgG mock-control ChIP-seq signal over HOT, MILD and COLD occupancy-region classes from ENCODE controls to test whether unspecific antibody binding ('hyper-ChIPable' behavior) contributes to the apparent high occupancy of HOT regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Profiles IgG mock-control ChIP-seq signal over HOT, MILD and COLD occupancy-region classes from ENCODE controls to test whether unspecific antibody binding ('hyper-ChIPable' behavior) contributes to the apparent high occupancy of HOT regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is estimating what fraction of antibody-specific error comes from pull-down of non-target proteins vs. direct binding to polynucleotide epitopes — the paper states this is not possible with currently available data Input tracks are TF ChIP-seq samples rather than IgG/mock controls, so control ('hyper-ChIPable') enrichment cannot be assessed A KO ChIP-seq experiment shows no signal — lack of signal may reflect technical conditions (low read number, low library complexity, unsuccessful IP) rather than the artifact being probed here

skills.description: Use when modeling ChIP-Seq read-count frequencies along chromosomes as smooth functions (e.g. factorial designs with genotype or treatment), or when genome-wide base-level and region-level significance testing with data-driven smoothing is required.
skills.name: chipseq-count-based-gam-fitting
skills.search_text: chipseq-count-based-gam-fitting Use when modeling ChIP-Seq read-count frequencies along chromosomes as smooth functions (e.g. factorial designs with genotype or treatment), or when genome-wide base-level and region-level significance testing with data-driven smoothing is required. When the analysis target is RNA-seq or non-genomic count data where the position-based GAM design (s(x) along chromosomes) does not apply When only ad-hoc window/bin statistics are acceptable and data-driven cross-validated smoothing is unnecessary (GenoGAM's advantage is eliminating ad-hoc binning) When interactive fitting on very large genomes without HDF5 out-of-core storage is attempted — full in-memory fitting will not scale to gigabase-scale genomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Fit a genome-wide generalized additive model (GenoGAM 2.0) to ChIP-Seq count data using a tiled overlapping-interval strategy with the fastGenoGAM R package, exploiting model sparsity (SuperLU solver) and HDF5 out-of-core storage to scale to gigabase-scale genomes. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Fit a genome-wide generalized additive model (GenoGAM 2.0) to ChIP-Seq count data using a tiled overlapping-interval strategy with the fastGenoGAM R package, exploiting model sparsity (SuperLU solver) and HDF5 out-of-core storage to scale to gigabase-scale genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis target is RNA-seq or non-genomic count data where the position-based GAM design (s(x) along chromosomes) does not apply When only ad-hoc window/bin statistics are acceptable and data-driven cross-validated smoothing is unnecessary (GenoGAM's advantage is eliminating ad-hoc binning) When interactive fitting on very large genomes without HDF5 out-of-core storage is attempted — full in-memory fitting will not scale to gigabase-scale genomes

skills.description: Use when standard errors or position-wise significance are needed for smooth (spline) terms fitted to ChIP-Seq count data with a sparse penalized Hessian, and forming the full matrix inverse is infeasible.
skills.name: chipseq-count-smoothing-model-statistics
skills.search_text: chipseq-count-smoothing-model-statistics Use when standard errors or position-wise significance are needed for smooth (spline) terms fitted to ChIP-Seq count data with a sparse penalized Hessian, and forming the full matrix inverse is infeasible. The model is small enough that the full Hessian can be inverted densely with no memory concern — direct inversion is simpler The analysis target is differential occupancy testing between conditions rather than pointwise uncertainty of the smooth fit itself The fit was produced by a non-sparse or non-penalized smoother (e.g. plain mgcv without sparsity exploitation), where the sparse inverse subset on NZ(H) does not apply as described http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes pointwise standard errors (and downstream log p-values) for smooth fits in GenoGAM-style genome-wide GAMs by extracting only the needed elements of the inverse penalized Hessian via the sparse inverse subset algorithm (sparseinv/SuiteSparse), avoiding explicit inversion of the full sparse Hessian. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Computes pointwise standard errors (and downstream log p-values) for smooth fits in GenoGAM-style genome-wide GAMs by extracting only the needed elements of the inverse penalized Hessian via the sparse inverse subset algorithm (sparseinv/SuiteSparse), avoiding explicit inversion of the full sparse Hessian.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is small enough that the full Hessian can be inverted densely with no memory concern — direct inversion is simpler The analysis target is differential occupancy testing between conditions rather than pointwise uncertainty of the smooth fit itself The fit was produced by a non-sparse or non-penalized smoother (e.g. plain mgcv without sparsity exploitation), where the sparse inverse subset on NZ(H) does not apply as described

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq differential modification calls (e.g., broad marks like H3K27me3/H3K9me3) must be intersected with a DESeq-derived DE gene list (FDR<0.01) and the overlap significance quantified and compared across peak-calling methods.
skills.name: chipseq-differential-modification-gene-mapping
skills.search_text: chipseq-differential-modification-gene-mapping Use when ChIP-seq differential modification calls (e.g., broad marks like H3K27me3/H3K9me3) must be intersected with a DESeq-derived DE gene list (FDR<0.01) and the overlap significance quantified and compared across peak-calling methods. The modification is a narrow/peak-like mark rather than a broad footprint (H3K27me3/H3K9me3-style); the article notes peak-searching methods generate false positives/negatives on broad marks and histoneHMM was designed for this regime. No matched gene expression data exist, so a DE gene list (DESeq FDR<0.01) cannot be constructed for the overlap test. Samples are from different strains/species without a common gene identifier mapping strategy via the GFF annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Tests whether histoneHMM's differentially modified ChIP-seq regions (e.g., rat SHR/BN H3K27me3, mouse H3K9me3) overlap differentially expressed genes more significantly than competing methods' calls, using Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables built via GFF gene annotation mapping. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Tests whether histoneHMM's differentially modified ChIP-seq regions (e.g., rat SHR/BN H3K27me3, mouse H3K9me3) overlap differentially expressed genes more significantly than competing methods' calls, using Fisher's exact tests on 2x2 contingency tables built via GFF gene annotation mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The modification is a narrow/peak-like mark rather than a broad footprint (H3K27me3/H3K9me3-style); the article notes peak-searching methods generate false positives/negatives on broad marks and histoneHMM was designed for this regime. No matched gene expression data exist, so a DE gene list (DESeq FDR<0.01) cannot be constructed for the overlap test. Samples are from different strains/species without a common gene identifier mapping strategy via the GFF annotation.

skills.description: Use when you have differential region calls from two or more ChIP-seq peak/broad-mark callers on the same genome assembly and an independent ground-truth coordinate set (qPCR-validated regions, X-inactivated gene bodies) to score sensitivity and false discovery per method.
skills.name: chipseq-differential-region-intersection
skills.search_text: chipseq-differential-region-intersection Use when you have differential region calls from two or more ChIP-seq peak/broad-mark callers on the same genome assembly and an independent ground-truth coordinate set (qPCR-validated regions, X-inactivated gene bodies) to score sensitivity and false discovery per method. Input is raw ChIP-seq reads or BAM files with no differential calls yet produced — run a caller such as histoneHMM first The ground truth is a continuous track or signal profile rather than a discrete coordinate set suitable for GenomicRanges overlap operations Region calls and reference coordinates are on different genome assemblies — intersecting without lifting over to a common assembly (e.g. rn4) will produce spurious labels http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark ChIP-seq differential modification calls by intersecting each method's called regions (histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff, Rseg, Pepr) with independent coordinate sets — qPCR-surveyed regions or annotated gene bodies — using GenomicRanges overlap operations, then labeling each overlap as Y, FP, or FN. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Benchmark ChIP-seq differential modification calls by intersecting each method's called regions (histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff, Rseg, Pepr) with independent coordinate sets — qPCR-surveyed regions or annotated gene bodies — using GenomicRanges overlap operations, then labeling each overlap as Y, FP, or FN.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ChIP-seq reads or BAM files with no differential calls yet produced — run a caller such as histoneHMM first The ground truth is a continuous track or signal profile rather than a discrete coordinate set suitable for GenomicRanges overlap operations Region calls and reference coordinates are on different genome assemblies — intersecting without lifting over to a common assembly (e.g. rn4) will produce spurious labels

skills.description: Use when processing mapped ChIPseq reads (BAM) downstream of the 'map' module and before peakcalling, and duplicate-read handling and fragment-size bounds must be applied reproducibly across a project.
skills.name: chipseq-duplicate-read-filtering
skills.search_text: chipseq-duplicate-read-filtering Use when processing mapped ChIPseq reads (BAM) downstream of the 'map' module and before peakcalling, and duplicate-read handling and fragment-size bounds must be applied reproducibly across a project. The input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been aligned — filtering runs after the 'map' module, not before it The project is RNAseq differential expression analysis (NEAT's QC/DEG track) rather than ChIPseq peak calling No duplicate-read or fragment-size handling is desired and default unfiltered alignments should be passed straight to peakcalling A ChIPseq pipeline step from NEAT that filters aligned reads using user-specified parameters — notably how to manage duplicate reads plus minimum and maximum fragment sizes — applied identically to standard and, when present, spike-in alignments before peakcalling. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: A ChIPseq pipeline step from NEAT that filters aligned reads using user-specified parameters — notably how to manage duplicate reads plus minimum and maximum fragment sizes — applied identically to standard and, when present, spike-in alignments before peakcalling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been aligned — filtering runs after the 'map' module, not before it The project is RNAseq differential expression analysis (NEAT's QC/DEG track) rather than ChIPseq peak calling No duplicate-read or fragment-size handling is desired and default unfiltered alignments should be passed straight to peakcalling

skills.description: Use when you need to benchmark DiNAMO's execution time and memory footprint on the article's ChIP-seq FASTA signal/control dataset pairs (e.g. GATA1) or compare its runtime with MEME-CHIP, HOMER and Discrover as in Table 3.
skills.name: chipseq-fasta-dataset-handling
skills.search_text: chipseq-fasta-dataset-handling Use when you need to benchmark DiNAMO's execution time and memory footprint on the article's ChIP-seq FASTA signal/control dataset pairs (e.g. GATA1) or compare its runtime with MEME-CHIP, HOMER and Discrover as in Table 3. When the goal is motif-discovery accuracy (nCC, JASPAR matrix comparison) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — use the synthetic implanted-motif evaluation instead When the input is not a paired signal/control FASTA dataset but, e.g., a sequencing-error coordinate set (the monocyte dataset with 3,272 Hg18 coordinates), which targets a different DiNAMO application When sequences lack a common fixed motif position — fixed-position mode (-p) is only appropriate when motifs occur at a specific offset relative to the sequence end http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Reproduce the DiNAMO benchmark of Table 3 by running the DiNAMO binary (github.com/bonsai-team/DiNAMO) on the ChIP-seq FASTA dataset pairs (GATA1 14,351 sequences; SOX2 4,526; OCT4 3,761; STAT3 2,546; KLF1 945) in both scanning and fixed-position modes, recording wall-clock time and peak resident memory. This validates the paper's claim that DiNAMO runs on a desktop machine with < 8 GB of RAM and quantifies its tractability versus MEME-CHIP, HOMER and Discrover. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Reproduce the DiNAMO benchmark of Table 3 by running the DiNAMO binary (github.com/bonsai-team/DiNAMO) on the ChIP-seq FASTA dataset pairs (GATA1 14,351 sequences; SOX2 4,526; OCT4 3,761; STAT3 2,546; KLF1 945) in both scanning and fixed-position modes, recording wall-clock time and peak resident memory. This validates the paper's claim that DiNAMO runs on a desktop machine with < 8 GB of RAM and quantifies its tractability versus MEME-CHIP, HOMER and Discrover.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is motif-discovery accuracy (nCC, JASPAR matrix comparison) rather than runtime/memory benchmarking — use the synthetic implanted-motif evaluation instead When the input is not a paired signal/control FASTA dataset but, e.g., a sequencing-error coordinate set (the monocyte dataset with 3,272 Hg18 coordinates), which targets a different DiNAMO application When sequences lack a common fixed motif position — fixed-position mode (-p) is only appropriate when motifs occur at a specific offset relative to the sequence end

skills.description: Use when assessing whether ChIP-seq signal at HOT regions is a technical artifact: you have KO transcription factor ChIP-seq IP/control FASTQ pairs and a HOT region interval set, and need per-experiment fold-enrichment over those regions.
skills.name: chipseq-fold-enrichment-over-hot-regions
skills.search_text: chipseq-fold-enrichment-over-hot-regions Use when assessing whether ChIP-seq signal at HOT regions is a technical artifact: you have KO transcription factor ChIP-seq IP/control FASTQ pairs and a HOT region interval set, and need per-experiment fold-enrichment over those regions. When the goal is to identify genuine, functional transcription factor binding sites or canonical motif occupancy — HOT regions are defined by ChIP-seq and are shown to lack canonical motifs for the TFs thought to be bound there. When you need to decompose artifact signal into antibody-specific pull-down of non-target proteins versus direct binding to polynucleotide epitopes — the article states this proportion cannot be estimated with currently available data. When the ChIP-ed protein is present in the cell (non-KO experiments) — this skill's rationale depends on the target TF being absent so any signal is necessarily false positive. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies false-positive ChIP-seq signal on HOT (high-occupancy target) regions by computing log2(IP/control) fold enrichment for ChIP-seq experiments performed on knocked-out transcription factors, where the ChIP-ed protein is absent from the cell, following the 'HOT or not' analysis (NAR, 2019). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Quantifies false-positive ChIP-seq signal on HOT (high-occupancy target) regions by computing log2(IP/control) fold enrichment for ChIP-seq experiments performed on knocked-out transcription factors, where the ChIP-ed protein is absent from the cell, following the 'HOT or not' analysis (NAR, 2019).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to identify genuine, functional transcription factor binding sites or canonical motif occupancy — HOT regions are defined by ChIP-seq and are shown to lack canonical motifs for the TFs thought to be bound there. When you need to decompose artifact signal into antibody-specific pull-down of non-target proteins versus direct binding to polynucleotide epitopes — the article states this proportion cannot be estimated with currently available data. When the ChIP-ed protein is present in the cell (non-KO experiments) — this skill's rationale depends on the target TF being absent so any signal is necessarily false positive.

skills.description: Use when narrowPeak/BED peak files from epigenomic assays (e.g. K562 ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq vs H3K27ac ChIP-seq) need biological interpretation — genomic state (ChromHMM), nearest-gene (ChIPseeker) and TSS-enrichment annotation — rather than just QC metrics.
skills.name: chipseq-functional-annotation-of-peak-features
skills.search_text: chipseq-functional-annotation-of-peak-features Use when narrowPeak/BED peak files from epigenomic assays (e.g. K562 ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq vs H3K27ac ChIP-seq) need biological interpretation — genomic state (ChromHMM), nearest-gene (ChIPseeker) and TSS-enrichment annotation — rather than just QC metrics. Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than already-called peak files — EpiCompare assumes post-peak-calling narrowPeak/BED inputs The goal is only QC metrics (peak counts, widths, blacklist fraction) — the General Metrics section, not functional annotation, covers this Peak sets are in an unsupported genome build or have not been checked against hg19/hg38 blacklisted regions, since blacklisted and non-standard-chromosome peaks are removed prior to analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotate epigenomic peak sets (ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, DNase-seq narrowPeak files) functionally using EpiCompare's built-in ChromHMM, ChIPseeker and enrichment analyses, including peak enrichment around Transcription Start Sites, as rendered in the third section of a single interactive HTML report. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Annotate epigenomic peak sets (ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq, DNase-seq narrowPeak files) functionally using EpiCompare's built-in ChromHMM, ChIPseeker and enrichment analyses, including peak enrichment around Transcription Start Sites, as rendered in the third section of a single interactive HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ/BAM) rather than already-called peak files — EpiCompare assumes post-peak-calling narrowPeak/BED inputs The goal is only QC metrics (peak counts, widths, blacklist fraction) — the General Metrics section, not functional annotation, covers this Peak sets are in an unsupported genome build or have not been checked against hg19/hg38 blacklisted regions, since blacklisted and non-standard-chromosome peaks are removed prior to analysis

skills.description: Use when you have mapped ChIP-seq BAM files plus RefSeq gene groups ranked by expression (e.g. highly/moderately/silent RNA-seq groups) and need per-group, sequencing-depth-normalized signal levels over gene bodies to build boxplot correlation panels.
skills.name: chipseq-gene-body-signal-quantification
skills.search_text: chipseq-gene-body-signal-quantification Use when you have mapped ChIP-seq BAM files plus RefSeq gene groups ranked by expression (e.g. highly/moderately/silent RNA-seq groups) and need per-group, sequencing-depth-normalized signal levels over gene bodies to build boxplot correlation panels. Input is still raw FASTQ — reads must first be mapped with Bowtie and unaligned reads removed from the BAM before any SeqCode command can process them You need genome-browser-ready tracks: bigWig profile generation is not supported and deferred to future SeqCode versions The experiment includes spike-in material and you need global scaling — SeqCode normalization is by sequencing depth and the spike-in factor must be manually introduced by the user http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Quantify normalized ChIP-seq signal (avg/max/total read counts) over gene bodies of selected gene groups using SeqCode's recoverChIPlevels, after Bowtie mapping to mm9, MACS peak calling, and exclusion of unaligned reads from the BAM. skills.description: Use when you have a positive multi-FASTA of ChIP-seq peak sequences (e.g. GATA1, SOX2, OCT4, STAT3, KLF1 peaks) plus a negative control FASTA, and need exhaustive IUPAC motif discovery to identify over-represented TF binding sites.
skills.name: chipseq-overrepresented-motif-discovery
skills.search_text: chipseq-overrepresented-motif-discovery Use when you have a positive multi-FASTA of ChIP-seq peak sequences (e.g. GATA1, SOX2, OCT4, STAT3, KLF1 peaks) plus a negative control FASTA, and need exhaustive IUPAC motif discovery to identify over-represented TF binding sites. There is no negative control dataset — DiNAMO is inherently discriminative and requires both a positive (signal.fa) and a negative (control.fa) dataset to compute contingency tables and Fisher's exact test P-values You need variable-length, gapped, or position-weight-matrix motifs rather than fixed-length IUPAC degenerate motifs of a single length L The question is motif occurrence at a known fixed offset relative to sequence ends (e.g. fixed-position sequencing-error motifs) — that requires DiNAMO's '-p' fixed-position mode rather than default scanning mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Discriminative discovery of over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs in ChIP-seq peak sequences using DiNAMO's exhaustive lattice algorithm, which compares a positive signal dataset against a negative control dataset and reports motifs passing a Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted Fisher's exact test. Applied in scanning (sliding-window) mode it recovers the expected transcription factor binding motif plus secondary co-factor motifs. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Discriminative discovery of over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs in ChIP-seq peak sequences using DiNAMO's exhaustive lattice algorithm, which compares a positive signal dataset against a negative control dataset and reports motifs passing a Holm–Bonferroni-adjusted Fisher's exact test. Applied in scanning (sliding-window) mode it recovers the expected transcription factor binding motif plus secondary co-factor motifs.

skills.description: Use when you have TAD boundary coordinates (e.g., from TOAST on GM12878 Hi-C) plus ENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq files or enhancer/promoter interval sets, and need to quantify the fraction of boundaries anchored by each regulatory signal.

skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-boundary-overlap-analysis Use when you have TAD boundary coordinates (e.g., from TOAST on GM12878 Hi-C) plus ENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq files or enhancer/promoter interval sets, and need to quantify the fraction of boundaries anchored by each regulatory signal. The goal is to identify TAD boundaries from Hi-C contact matrices rather than to validate existing boundaries — use the TOAST GAE+HDBSCAN pipeline itself instead Only raw ChIP-seq reads are available without called narrowPeak peaks or enhancer/promoter interval annotations — peak calling and E/P annotation must precede this skill The TAD caller output lacks genomic start/end locations (only bin indices and no resolution metadata), since the 20 Kb overlap window cannot be applied reliably http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes anchoring ratios of ChIP-seq peaks (transcription factors, histone marks, enhancers, promoters) at TAD boundaries by counting peaks overlapping a 20 Kb window centered on each boundary. Used in the TOAST paper to validate that algorithm-called TAD boundaries coincide with known regulatory landmarks such as CTCF, SMC3, and RAD21. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Computes anchoring ratios of ChIP-seq peaks (transcription factors, histone marks, enhancers, promoters) at TAD boundaries by counting peaks overlapping a 20 Kb window centered on each boundary. Used in the TOAST paper to validate that algorithm-called TAD boundaries coincide with known regulatory landmarks such as CTCF, SMC3, and RAD21.

skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-calling Use when base-level ChIP-seq peak calling is needed for factorial-design experiments (IP vs control/genotype), especially on gigabase-scale genomes where memory-efficient, out-of-core GAM fitting is required. Data are not ChIP-seq read counts from a factorial design (IP vs control/genotype) modeled by smooth functions along chromosomes A quick region-level-only caller is desired without base-resolution significance testing or GAM smoothing-parameter control Environment runs R < 3.4.1 or lacks correct Armadillo/RcppArmadillo 64-bit-word configuration needed for large sparse matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Call significant ChIP-seq peaks using GenoGAM 2.0, a genome-wide generalized additive model approach that fits smooth functions along chromosomes on HDF5-backed tiles and provides base- and region-level significance testing without ad-hoc binning or windowing. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Call significant ChIP-seq peaks using GenoGAM 2.0, a genome-wide generalized additive model approach that fits smooth functions along chromosomes on HDF5-backed tiles and provides base- and region-level significance testing without ad-hoc binning or windowing.

skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-calling-with-macs Use when mapped ChIP-seq reads (BAM/SAM, e.g. Bowtie-aligned to mm9/mm10) must be reduced to a peak set that serves as the region reference for meta-plots, heatmaps, or ChIP-level quantification in SeqCode-based workflows. skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-file-retrieval Use when you have a transcription factor of interest and need its ChIP-seq peak regions as a BED file to query against a REM database such as EpiRegio for target-gene association. skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-summit-density-windowing Use when you have many narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files for numerous TFs in a genome assembly and need to call HOT regions by peak-summit density rather than individual binding sites. skills.search_text: chipseq-peak-to-enclave-overlap-counting Use when BHi-Cect cluster output (named lists of loci per enclave) is available and you need to characterize each bottom enclave's regulatory content by quantifying ChIP-seq TF binding per enclave.
