skills.search_text: chipseq-read-alignment-and-unaligned-read-filtering Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. GEO accessions such as GSM2645501/GSM2645502) that must be mapped to a genome (mm9, mm10, hg38, dm3) and converted into clean BAM files for peak calling or SeqCode read-count/visualization commands. Input is already a mapped BAM/SAM file — only the unaligned-read exclusion applies, no Bowtie mapping is needed Data are RNA-seq or ATAC-seq expression/count matrices where sequencing data are already processed past the mapping stage and only visualization (SeqCode meta-plots, heatmaps, boxplots) is required A genome assembly not supported by Bowtie/RefSeq annotations is required, since SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations for every organism http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps ChIP-seq FASTQ reads to a reference genome with Bowtie (e.g. mouse mm9/mm10) and removes unaligned reads from the resulting BAM files so they are valid inputs for SeqCode commands and downstream peak calling. This preprocessing step underpins reproducible ChIP-level quantification and visualization in SeqCode workflows. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Maps ChIP-seq FASTQ reads to a reference genome with Bowtie (e.g. mouse mm9/mm10) and removes unaligned reads from the resulting BAM files so they are valid inputs for SeqCode commands and downstream peak calling. This preprocessing step underpins reproducible ChIP-level quantification and visualization in SeqCode workflows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a mapped BAM/SAM file — only the unaligned-read exclusion applies, no Bowtie mapping is needed Data are RNA-seq or ATAC-seq expression/count matrices where sequencing data are already processed past the mapping stage and only visualization (SeqCode meta-plots, heatmaps, boxplots) is required A genome assembly not supported by Bowtie/RefSeq annotations is required, since SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations for every organism

skills.description: Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM files from a factorial design experiment (e.g. two conditions × two replicates) must be converted into position-indexed read counts over overlapping genomic tiles as input to a GenoGAM model fit.
skills.name: chipseq-read-count-ingestion-genomic-intervals
skills.search_text: chipseq-read-count-ingestion-genomic-intervals Use when raw ChIP-seq BAM files from a factorial design experiment (e.g. two conditions × two replicates) must be converted into position-indexed read counts over overlapping genomic tiles as input to a GenoGAM model fit. The data are already a GenoGAMDataSet or pre-binned count matrix — re-ingestion would duplicate the tiling step The analysis requires ad-hoc fixed binning/windowing rather than data-driven smoothing over overlapping tiles Non-count genomic data (e.g. continuous tracks) that do not originate from BAM read alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Ingest ChIP-seq BAM files into tiled genomic read-count intervals with GenoGAMDataSet() using a factorial design (~ s(x) + s(x, by = genotype)), chunkSize = 50000 and overhangSize = 1000, choosing between in-memory (hdf5 = FALSE) and HDF5-backed storage before fitting a genome-wide GAM. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Ingest ChIP-seq BAM files into tiled genomic read-count intervals with GenoGAMDataSet() using a factorial design (~ s(x) + s(x, by = genotype)), chunkSize = 50000 and overhangSize = 1000, choosing between in-memory (hdf5 = FALSE) and HDF5-backed storage before fitting a genome-wide GAM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already a GenoGAMDataSet or pre-binned count matrix — re-ingestion would duplicate the tiling step The analysis requires ad-hoc fixed binning/windowing rather than data-driven smoothing over overlapping tiles Non-count genomic data (e.g. continuous tracks) that do not originate from BAM read alignments

skills.description: Use when two or more sequencing lanes from the same ChIP-Seq sample group (e.g., stimulated or unstimulated STAT1) must be checked for consistent genome-wide read distributions across chromosome/strand combinations, or when within-group vs cross-group reproducibility must be contrasted.
skills.name: chipseq-read-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: chipseq-read-distribution-analysis Use when two or more sequencing lanes from the same ChIP-Seq sample group (e.g., stimulated or unstimulated STAT1) must be checked for consistent genome-wide read distributions across chromosome/strand combinations, or when within-group vs cross-group reproducibility must be contrasted. Input is a called peak set or binding-site list rather than per-lane read count distributions over the genome — this skill assesses raw read distribution consistency, not peak overlap. Data are probe-based assays (e.g. ChIP-chip intensities) rather than genome-wide sequencing reads; the paper treats ChIP-chip as the lower-resolution comparator, not the target of this test. Lanes being compared belong to different biological conditions and the goal is reproducibility assessment — cross-group comparisons there will legitimately show 36–42/48 significant combinations and must not be read as assay failure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies ChIP-Seq assay reproducibility by applying two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests to genome-wide read count distributions over all 48 chromosome/strand combinations (24 chromosomes × 2 strands), comparing lanes within a sample group. Developed on the STAT1 ChIP-Seq dataset, where it showed near-identical read distributions within groups but strong divergence between stimulated and unstimulated lanes. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Quantifies ChIP-Seq assay reproducibility by applying two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests to genome-wide read count distributions over all 48 chromosome/strand combinations (24 chromosomes × 2 strands), comparing lanes within a sample group. Developed on the STAT1 ChIP-Seq dataset, where it showed near-identical read distributions within groups but strong divergence between stimulated and unstimulated lanes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a called peak set or binding-site list rather than per-lane read count distributions over the genome — this skill assesses raw read distribution consistency, not peak overlap. Data are probe-based assays (e.g. ChIP-chip intensities) rather than genome-wide sequencing reads; the paper treats ChIP-chip as the lower-resolution comparator, not the target of this test. Lanes being compared belong to different biological conditions and the goal is reproducibility assessment — cross-group comparisons there will legitimately show 36–42/48 significant combinations and must not be read as assay failure.

skills.description: Use when raw ChIPseq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome inside an automated pipeline, especially when standard and spike-in (exogenous epigenome) samples must be aligned with identical parameters for ChIP-rx normalization.
skills.name: chipseq-read-mapping
skills.search_text: chipseq-read-mapping Use when raw ChIPseq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a reference genome inside an automated pipeline, especially when standard and spike-in (exogenous epigenome) samples must be aligned with identical parameters for ChIP-rx normalization. Reads are already aligned (.bam available) — proceed directly to the 'filter', 'cleanfiles' or 'GRanges' modules instead of re-mapping The data are RNAseq rather than ChIPseq — although NEAT supports RNAseq, this skill is scoped to ChIPseq read mapping feeding peak calling and ChIP-rx normalization A non-NEAT, fully scripted workflow with custom aligner parameters is required — NEAT exposes alignment only through the centralized Targets.txt project file http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Align ChIPseq reads within the NEAT pipeline using the 'map' module, which maps reads with bwa or bowtie and feeds aligned reads into the filter, cleanfiles and peakcalling stages. Mapping parameters are centralized in the Targets.txt project file so every sample is aligned identically. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Align ChIPseq reads within the NEAT pipeline using the 'map' module, which maps reads with bwa or bowtie and feeds aligned reads into the filter, cleanfiles and peakcalling stages. Mapping parameters are centralized in the Targets.txt project file so every sample is aligned identically.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are already aligned (.bam available) — proceed directly to the 'filter', 'cleanfiles' or 'GRanges' modules instead of re-mapping The data are RNAseq rather than ChIPseq — although NEAT supports RNAseq, this skill is scoped to ChIPseq read mapping feeding peak calling and ChIP-rx normalization A non-NEAT, fully scripted workflow with custom aligner parameters is required — NEAT exposes alignment only through the centralized Targets.txt project file

skills.description: Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. ENA/ENCODE IP and control libraries) that must be cleaned prior to alignment with a short-read aligner such as Bowtie, especially when computing read coverage or IP/control enrichment over genomic intervals like HOT regions.
skills.name: chipseq-read-quality-trimming
skills.search_text: chipseq-read-quality-trimming Use when starting from raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (e.g. ENA/ENCODE IP and control libraries) that must be cleaned prior to alignment with a short-read aligner such as Bowtie, especially when computing read coverage or IP/control enrichment over genomic intervals like HOT regions. Input is already trimmed FASTQ or an alignment file (BAM/SAM) — trimming is redundant and the pipeline should continue at the alignment or coverage stage The goal is quantifying signal on ordinary (non-HOT) peak calls without artifact concerns — the trimming rationale here is tied to the false-positive/HOT-region enrichment analysis Reads are single-cell or long-read data — bbduk short-read adapter trimming as used in this workflow is not the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Preprocess ChIP-seq FASTQ reads (IP and matching control) by trimming adapters and low-quality bases with bbduk before genome alignment, so that downstream IP/control enrichment measurements (e.g. log2 fold enrichment over HOT regions) are not inflated by adapter contamination or poor-quality bases. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Preprocess ChIP-seq FASTQ reads (IP and matching control) by trimming adapters and low-quality bases with bbduk before genome alignment, so that downstream IP/control enrichment measurements (e.g. log2 fold enrichment over HOT regions) are not inflated by adapter contamination or poor-quality bases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already trimmed FASTQ or an alignment file (BAM/SAM) — trimming is redundant and the pipeline should continue at the alignment or coverage stage The goal is quantifying signal on ordinary (non-HOT) peak calls without artifact concerns — the trimming rationale here is tied to the false-positive/HOT-region enrichment analysis Reads are single-cell or long-read data — bbduk short-read adapter trimming as used in this workflow is not the appropriate choice

skills.description: Use when you have two genome-wide binding peak sets (e.g. MACS2 ChIP-seq peaks for two TFs) and RNA-seq differential expression results, and need to define promoters bound and co-regulated by both regulators.
skills.name: chipseq-rnaseq-regulatory-integration
skills.search_text: chipseq-rnaseq-regulatory-integration Use when you have two genome-wide binding peak sets (e.g. MACS2 ChIP-seq peaks for two TFs) and RNA-seq differential expression results, and need to define promoters bound and co-regulated by both regulators. You only have single-factor ChIP-seq peaks with no RNA-seq expression data — binding alone cannot establish co-regulation, only co-occupancy. Your peaks are not proximal to annotated ORFs (≤500 bp upstream rule here); promoter-level intersection requires gene-proximal assignments. The regulatory question is post-transcriptional (e.g. the unexplained luxCDABE translational control) — ChIP-seq/RNA-seq intersection addresses promoter occupancy and transcription only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Integrates ChIP-seq binding data (co-occupied LuxR/H-NS regions) with RNA-seq differential-expression data to identify promoters that are both co-occupied and co-regulated — here yielding 28 promoters controlling 63 genes in V. harveyi quorum sensing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Integrates ChIP-seq binding data (co-occupied LuxR/H-NS regions) with RNA-seq differential-expression data to identify promoters that are both co-occupied and co-regulated — here yielding 28 promoters controlling 63 genes in V. harveyi quorum sensing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have single-factor ChIP-seq peaks with no RNA-seq expression data — binding alone cannot establish co-regulation, only co-occupancy. Your peaks are not proximal to annotated ORFs (≤500 bp upstream rule here); promoter-level intersection requires gene-proximal assignments. The regulatory question is post-transcriptional (e.g. the unexplained luxCDABE translational control) — ChIP-seq/RNA-seq intersection addresses promoter occupancy and transcription only.

skills.description: Use when setting up a new NEAT ChIPseq project on an institution's cluster and raw compressed fastq files must be mapped to user-defined sample names, replicates, antibodies and pipeline blocks before execution.
skills.name: chipseq-sample-metadata-annotation
skills.search_text: chipseq-sample-metadata-annotation Use when setting up a new NEAT ChIPseq project on an institution's cluster and raw compressed fastq files must be mapped to user-defined sample names, replicates, antibodies and pipeline blocks before execution. The analysis will be run outside NEAT (e.g. on a Galaxy-style web platform) — Targets.txt is NEAT's own centralized project file and exact-word matching will not transfer Raw fastq files and sample-to-input/replicate relationships are unavailable or the data are already processed past the 'unzip' stage, so the metadata file cannot anchor the pipeline The working environment is not the institution's cluster under Mac OSx, the only operating system supported in the article's setup http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reconstructs and populates NEAT's centralized Targets.txt project file, which encodes sample names, replicates, sample-to-input relationships, H3K4me3 antibody specificities, and cluster-specific parameters as the single source of metadata for an automated ChIPseq pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Reconstructs and populates NEAT's centralized Targets.txt project file, which encodes sample names, replicates, sample-to-input relationships, H3K4me3 antibody specificities, and cluster-specific parameters as the single source of metadata for an automated ChIPseq pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis will be run outside NEAT (e.g. on a Galaxy-style web platform) — Targets.txt is NEAT's own centralized project file and exact-word matching will not transfer Raw fastq files and sample-to-input/replicate relationships are unavailable or the data are already processed past the 'unzip' stage, so the metadata file cannot anchor the pipeline The working environment is not the institution's cluster under Mac OSx, the only operating system supported in the article's setup

skills.description: Use when BHi-Cect tree output (nested cluster list) and ChIP-seq tracks must be combined to compute epigenomic signal prevalence per bottom enclave for gene ranking or enrichment analysis.
skills.name: chipseq-signal-aggregation-per-cluster
skills.search_text: chipseq-signal-aggregation-per-cluster Use when BHi-Cect tree output (nested cluster list) and ChIP-seq tracks must be combined to compute epigenomic signal prevalence per bottom enclave for gene ranking or enrichment analysis. The clustering structure is not yet available — raw Hi-C alone cannot assign loci to bottom enclaves The analysis targets top-level/TAD-like contiguous domains rather than BHi-Cect bottom enclaves, which are mostly non-contiguous and deeply interwoven The goal is TF-content profiling of bottom enclaves (correspondence analysis), not ChIP-seq signal aggregation for GSEA http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Aggregates mean ChIP-seq signal (e.g., RNAP2 in IMR90, H3K4me3 in K562) over BHi-Cect bottom-enclave loci to produce per-enclave prevalence values that are used to rank genes for downstream GO GSEA. It connects Hi-C-derived enclave structure with epigenomic activity of the underlying DNA. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Aggregates mean ChIP-seq signal (e.g., RNAP2 in IMR90, H3K4me3 in K562) over BHi-Cect bottom-enclave loci to produce per-enclave prevalence values that are used to rank genes for downstream GO GSEA. It connects Hi-C-derived enclave structure with epigenomic activity of the underlying DNA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering structure is not yet available — raw Hi-C alone cannot assign loci to bottom enclaves The analysis targets top-level/TAD-like contiguous domains rather than BHi-Cect bottom enclaves, which are mostly non-contiguous and deeply interwoven The goal is TF-content profiling of bottom enclaves (correspondence analysis), not ChIP-seq signal aggregation for GSEA

skills.description: Use when ChIPseq samples must be quantitatively compared genome-wide and an exogenous spike-in epigenome (ChIP-rx) control was sequenced, or when reconstructing/running the NEAT 'chiprx' module.
skills.name: chipseq-spike-in-normalization
skills.search_text: chipseq-spike-in-normalization Use when ChIPseq samples must be quantitatively compared genome-wide and an exogenous spike-in epigenome (ChIP-rx) control was sequenced, or when reconstructing/running the NEAT 'chiprx' module. No exogenous spike-in epigenome was sequenced — standard ChIPseq samples without ChIP-rx controls cannot be scaled by spike-in quantity The goal is RNAseq analysis (e.g., differentially expressed gene analysis) rather than ChIPseq signal normalization Only peak-level (binary) comparisons are needed rather than genome-wide quantitative ChIPseq signal comparisons http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Applies ChIP-rx, a genome-wide ChIPseq normalization method that scales signal by a defined quantity of an exogenous spike-in epigenome, enabling quantitative comparison of ChIPseq signal across samples. In NEAT this is packaged as the automated 'chiprx' module within its ChIPseq pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Applies ChIP-rx, a genome-wide ChIPseq normalization method that scales signal by a defined quantity of an exogenous spike-in epigenome, enabling quantitative comparison of ChIPseq signal across samples. In NEAT this is packaged as the automated 'chiprx' module within its ChIPseq pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No exogenous spike-in epigenome was sequenced — standard ChIPseq samples without ChIP-rx controls cannot be scaled by spike-in quantity The goal is RNAseq analysis (e.g., differentially expressed gene analysis) rather than ChIPseq signal normalization Only peak-level (binary) comparisons are needed rather than genome-wide quantitative ChIPseq signal comparisons

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across conditions (e.g. drug treatment series) using spike-in chromatin, and a genome-wide normalization that preserves background signal while correcting peak signal is needed.
skills.name: chipseq-spikein-normalization
skills.search_text: chipseq-spikein-normalization Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across conditions (e.g. drug treatment series) using spike-in chromatin, and a genome-wide normalization that preserves background signal while correcting peak signal is needed. There is no exogenous spike-in chromatin in the experiment (spikChIP requires sample/spike BAM pairs and spike-in peak BEDs) Only a subset of pre-selected loci needs normalizing and a uniform spike-in factor (ChIP-Rx or tag removal) is acceptable — spikChIP is designed for genome-wide, region-class-aware normalization The spike-in material has fewer than ~1 million reads or falls well below 2%-5% of the experimental genome, since normalization reliability depends on sufficient spike-in depth http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 spikChIP is a Perl pipeline that normalizes multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in chromatin (e.g. Drosophila DNA mixed into human samples) using a local regression (LOESS) strategy that applies the spike-in correction factor gradually from background to enriched regions, avoiding the background overcorrection seen in ChIP-Rx and tag removal. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: spikChIP is a Perl pipeline that normalizes multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in chromatin (e.g. Drosophila DNA mixed into human samples) using a local regression (LOESS) strategy that applies the spike-in correction factor gradually from background to enriched regions, avoiding the background overcorrection seen in ChIP-Rx and tag removal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: There is no exogenous spike-in chromatin in the experiment (spikChIP requires sample/spike BAM pairs and spike-in peak BEDs) Only a subset of pre-selected loci needs normalizing and a uniform spike-in factor (ChIP-Rx or tag removal) is acceptable — spikChIP is designed for genome-wide, region-class-aware normalization The spike-in material has fewer than ~1 million reads or falls well below 2%-5% of the experimental genome, since normalization reliability depends on sufficient spike-in depth

skills.description: Use when pharmacogenomic drug sensitivity data (e.g. CCLE) must be linked to ChIP-seq-defined TR target sets to infer drug-response-associated transcriptional regulators or to organize drugs into mechanism-of-action clusters.
skills.name: chipseq-target-set-integration
skills.search_text: chipseq-target-set-integration Use when pharmacogenomic drug sensitivity data (e.g. CCLE) must be linked to ChIP-seq-defined TR target sets to infer drug-response-associated transcriptional regulators or to organize drugs into mechanism-of-action clusters. ChIP-seq data are missing or target sets contain too few targets, which would mislead TR identification Post-treatment data are needed (e.g. detection of acquired resistance such as erlotinib/STAT3 activation) — CCLE lacks post-treatment data so these associations cannot be detected Reliable TR target information is unavailable; RePhine identifies response-related TRs through targets and is restricted to cases where such information exists http://edamontology.org/topic_3369 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Integrate ENCODE ChIP-seq regulatory potential (RP) scores for 160 transcriptional regulators with CCLE pharmacogenomic drug response data using the RePhine regression, then transform uniP statistics into −Log10(uniP) TR response signatures to cluster drugs by mechanism of action. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Integrate ENCODE ChIP-seq regulatory potential (RP) scores for 160 transcriptional regulators with CCLE pharmacogenomic drug response data using the RePhine regression, then transform uniP statistics into −Log10(uniP) TR response signatures to cluster drugs by mechanism of action.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ChIP-seq data are missing or target sets contain too few targets, which would mislead TR identification Post-treatment data are needed (e.g. detection of acquired resistance such as erlotinib/STAT3 activation) — CCLE lacks post-treatment data so these associations cannot be detected Reliable TR target information is unavailable; RePhine identifies response-related TRs through targets and is restricted to cases where such information exists

skills.search_text: chipseq-test-dataset-processing Use when a NEAT project must be exercised end-to-end on the bundled truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq test fastq files (Targets.txt registered), or when validating that NEAT's double-clickable pipeline modules run without programming experience. skills.name: chipseq-tss-meta-plot-generation
skills.search_text: chipseq-tss-meta-plot-generation Use when you have a mapped ChIP-seq BAM (e.g. H3K4me3 in mESC), RefSeq refGene and chromosome-size files for the assembly, and need standardized TSS-centered meta-plots or heatmaps to visualize enrichment around transcription start sites. Input BAM still contains unaligned reads — SeqCode requires these to be excluded first Analysis targets genome-wide bigwig profile export — generation of genome-wide profiles in bigwig format is not supported and deferred to future versions Goal is peak calling or read counting rather than TSS-centered signal visualization — use other SeqCode applications or tools like MACS http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate averaged TSS meta-plots and TSS heatmaps from ChIP-seq BAM files using SeqCode's produceTSSplots and produceTSSmaps, relying on RefSeq annotations and UCSC chromosome-size files, with the -w window option tuning graphical resolution without altering biological results. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Generate averaged TSS meta-plots and TSS heatmaps from ChIP-seq BAM files using SeqCode's produceTSSplots and produceTSSmaps, relying on RefSeq annotations and UCSC chromosome-size files, with the -w window option tuning graphical resolution without altering biological results.

skills.description: Use when combining two-sided p-values (e.g. methylation promoter/other-context p-values in a genomic interval) that are correlated, so Stouffer-style combination would otherwise be invalid.
skills.name: cholesky-factorization-whitening
skills.search_text: cholesky-factorization-whitening Use when combining two-sided p-values (e.g. methylation promoter/other-context p-values in a genomic interval) that are correlated, so Stouffer-style combination would otherwise be invalid. The p-values being combined are already independent — plain Stouffer combination suffices and whitening adds unnecessary error The correlation matrix Sigma is not symmetric positive-definite (e.g. pairwise-correlation estimates with missing values), so chol() will fail and the whitening transform is undefined The p-values are one-sided or you intend to combine untransformed p-values rather than normal-quantile-transformed Z scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Whitens correlated, two-sided p-values so they can be combined as independent experiments: transform p to Z via Phi^-1(1-p/2), then apply the inverse Cholesky factor of the correlation matrix Sigma = C^T C, as SMITE does in its Stouffer-based correlated p-value combination. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Whitens correlated, two-sided p-values so they can be combined as independent experiments: transform p to Z via Phi^-1(1-p/2), then apply the inverse Cholesky factor of the correlation matrix Sigma = C^T C, as SMITE does in its Stouffer-based correlated p-value combination.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values being combined are already independent — plain Stouffer combination suffices and whitening adds unnecessary error The correlation matrix Sigma is not symmetric positive-definite (e.g. pairwise-correlation estimates with missing values), so chol() will fail and the whitening transform is undefined The p-values are one-sided or you intend to combine untransformed p-values rather than normal-quantile-transformed Z scores

skills.search_text: chromatin-accessibility-data-processing Use when paired-end chromatin accessibility reads (BAM from MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) must be classified by fragment length and converted to per-base midpoint-count tracks for nucleosome/TF occupancy modeling. Input is single-end sequencing or a genome without paired-end fragment insert sizes, since fragment-length classification (127–187 bp vs <80 bp) cannot be computed The goal is peak calling or footprint labeling rather than building HMM observables — the article treats MACS2 + FIMO as an alternative comparison approach, not this preprocessing route Data are already processed midpoint-count tracks or bedGraph observables; re-running classification would double-apply the Tn5 correction or re-threshold fragments http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Transforms raw paired-end MNase-seq and ATAC-seq fragment alignments into the one-dimensional genomic midpoint-count signals (nucFrags and shortFrags tracks) that RoboCOP's multivariate HMM consumes as observables. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Transforms raw paired-end MNase-seq and ATAC-seq fragment alignments into the one-dimensional genomic midpoint-count signals (nucFrags and shortFrags tracks) that RoboCOP's multivariate HMM consumes as observables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end sequencing or a genome without paired-end fragment insert sizes, since fragment-length classification (127–187 bp vs <80 bp) cannot be computed The goal is peak calling or footprint labeling rather than building HMM observables — the article treats MACS2 + FIMO as an alternative comparison approach, not this preprocessing route Data are already processed midpoint-count tracks or bedGraph observables; re-running classification would double-apply the Tn5 correction or re-threshold fragments

skills.description: Use when analyzing sparse single-cell (or bulk) ATAC-seq fragment counts to identify motifs or genomic annotations associated with cell-to-cell variability in chromatin accessibility, or to derive per-cell deviation scores for downstream clustering/t-SNE.
skills.name: chromatin-accessibility-deviation-computation
skills.search_text: chromatin-accessibility-deviation-computation Use when analyzing sparse single-cell (or bulk) ATAC-seq fragment counts to identify motifs or genomic annotations associated with cell-to-cell variability in chromatin accessibility, or to derive per-cell deviation scores for downstream clustering/t-SNE. The goal is pure cell clustering or embedding rather than annotating TF motif usage — the chromVAR README notes that kmers + PCA is the best chromVAR variant for clustering and that SnapATAC outperforms chromVAR for the clustering tasks evaluated The input is already a matrix of per-cell deviation/deviation scores (e.g. feeding deviationsTsne) rather than raw fragment counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Compute chromVAR bias-corrected motif deviation scores and per-motif variability from sparse single-cell ATAC-seq counts: after GC-bias correction, sample/peak filtering, and motif matching with motifmatchr, computeDeviations yields per-cell 'deviations' and Z-score 'deviationScores' assays, and computeVariability ranks motifs by standard deviation of Z-scores. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/nmeth.4401
skills.summary: Compute chromVAR bias-corrected motif deviation scores and per-motif variability from sparse single-cell ATAC-seq counts: after GC-bias correction, sample/peak filtering, and motif matching with motifmatchr, computeDeviations yields per-cell 'deviations' and Z-score 'deviationScores' assays, and computeVariability ranks motifs by standard deviation of Z-scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is pure cell clustering or embedding rather than annotating TF motif usage — the chromVAR README notes that kmers + PCA is the best chromVAR variant for clustering and that SnapATAC outperforms chromVAR for the clustering tasks evaluated The input is already a matrix of per-cell deviation/deviation scores (e.g. feeding deviationsTsne) rather than raw fragment counts

skills.description: Use when lifted-over SNP or interval sets must be linked to cell-type-specific regulatory activity — e.g., testing whether mapped SCZ GWAS SNPs are enriched in chromatin accessible regions of mouse excitatory vs inhibitory neuron populations.
skills.name: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis Use when lifted-over SNP or interval sets must be linked to cell-type-specific regulatory activity — e.g., testing whether mapped SCZ GWAS SNPs are enriched in chromatin accessible regions of mouse excitatory vs inhibitory neuron populations. The input is already a feature/enrichment table — no interval intersection is needed. Query regions lack a defined target genome or the relevant cell-population accessibility data for the species of interest is unavailable. The goal is plain coordinate conversion (liftOver) without any downstream functional or cell-type interpretation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Intersects lifted-over GWAS SNPs (or query intervals) with chromatin accessible regions of specific cell populations (e.g., mouse excitatory and inhibitory neurons) using GenomicRanges, then computes enrichment statistics to identify cell-type-specific regulatory associations, as done in the AdaLiftOver SCZ GWAS case study. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Intersects lifted-over GWAS SNPs (or query intervals) with chromatin accessible regions of specific cell populations (e.g., mouse excitatory and inhibitory neurons) using GenomicRanges, then computes enrichment statistics to identify cell-type-specific regulatory associations, as done in the AdaLiftOver SCZ GWAS case study.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/enrichment table — no interval intersection is needed. Query regions lack a defined target genome or the relevant cell-population accessibility data for the species of interest is unavailable. The goal is plain coordinate conversion (liftOver) without any downstream functional or cell-type interpretation.

skills.description: Use when ATAC-seq DA peak sets (opening vs. closing with age) must be tested for enrichment of cell-type-specific chromatin annotations per sex, e.g. to verify male-specific B cell locus decline or female opening patterns.
skills.name: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatin-accessibility-enrichment-analysis Use when ATAC-seq DA peak sets (opening vs. closing with age) must be tested for enrichment of cell-type-specific chromatin annotations per sex, e.g. to verify male-specific B cell locus decline or female opening patterns. The question concerns shared (non-sex-stratified) aging signatures such as declining naive T cell or increasing monocyte/cytotoxic functions, where a single pooled enrichment test suffices Input is bulk gene expression without ATAC-seq DA peak direction labels — the Fisher test requires opening/closing peak contingency counts Analysis needs single-cell or sorted-cell resolution, which the authors explicitly flag as unestablished for these sex differences http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tests whether functionally annotated loci (e.g., chromHMM B cell-specific loci) are over-represented among age-related closing vs. opening differentially accessible ATAC-seq peaks, stratified by sex, to detect sex-specific epigenomic decline such as the male-specific B cell accessibility loss reported for PBMCs from 172 healthy adults aged 22–93. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Tests whether functionally annotated loci (e.g., chromHMM B cell-specific loci) are over-represented among age-related closing vs. opening differentially accessible ATAC-seq peaks, stratified by sex, to detect sex-specific epigenomic decline such as the male-specific B cell accessibility loss reported for PBMCs from 172 healthy adults aged 22–93.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns shared (non-sex-stratified) aging signatures such as declining naive T cell or increasing monocyte/cytotoxic functions, where a single pooled enrichment test suffices Input is bulk gene expression without ATAC-seq DA peak direction labels — the Fisher test requires opening/closing peak contingency counts Analysis needs single-cell or sorted-cell resolution, which the authors explicitly flag as unestablished for these sex differences

skills.description: Use when you have paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq samples across multiple cell types/tissues and need to link regulatory regions to genes whose expression variation they explain.
skills.name: chromatin-accessibility-expression-integration
skills.search_text: chromatin-accessibility-expression-integration Use when you have paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq samples across multiple cell types/tissues and need to link regulatory regions to genes whose expression variation they explain. You only have a user-provided set of DNA regions and want enriched TF motifs with no expression data — use motif enrichment tools such as PASTAA, Clover, MotifCounter or Homer instead. You need REMs identified de novo from chromatin data without any paired gene expression variation across samples — the STITCHIT linear model requires correlated accessibility/expression variation. You want a reverse mapping (starting from genomic regions to find associated genes) — EpiRegio/STITCHIT explicitly starts with a gene and looks for REMs, not vice versa. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Integrates paired DNase1-seq chromatin accessibility and RNA-seq gene expression data using the STITCHIT linear model (as implemented in EpiRegio) to identify Regulatory EleMents (REMs) whose accessibility variation is associated with changes in target gene expression across samples. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Integrates paired DNase1-seq chromatin accessibility and RNA-seq gene expression data using the STITCHIT linear model (as implemented in EpiRegio) to identify Regulatory EleMents (REMs) whose accessibility variation is associated with changes in target gene expression across samples.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a user-provided set of DNA regions and want enriched TF motifs with no expression data — use motif enrichment tools such as PASTAA, Clover, MotifCounter or Homer instead. You need REMs identified de novo from chromatin data without any paired gene expression variation across samples — the STITCHIT linear model requires correlated accessibility/expression variation. You want a reverse mapping (starting from genomic regions to find associated genes) — EpiRegio/STITCHIT explicitly starts with a gene and looks for REMs, not vice versa.

skills.description: Use when ChIA-PIPE loop-calling output (PET clusters with coordinates, PET counts, and anchor peak-support flags) from CTCF ChIA-PET data must be converted into chromatin contact domain (CCD) intervals.
skills.name: chromatin-contact-domain-calling
skills.search_text: chromatin-contact-domain-calling Use when ChIA-PIPE loop-calling output (PET clusters with coordinates, PET counts, and anchor peak-support flags) from CTCF ChIA-PET data must be converted into chromatin contact domain (CCD) intervals. Input is raw ChIA-PET reads — this skill operates downstream of linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and loop calling, not on FASTQ data The goal is enhancer-promoter loop annotation or allele-specific peak/loop resolution, which ChIA-PIPE implements as separate analyses with different criteria (e.g., PET count >=3 loops, phased SNPs) Loops lack anchor peak-support annotations, so the both-anchor-supported filter cannot be evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reconstructs the ChIA-PIPE CCD-calling algorithm, which defines chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET data by merging high-confidence, both-anchor-peak-supported loops into contiguous genomic intervals. This turns discrete loop calls into domain-scale annotations without additional sequencing input. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Reconstructs the ChIA-PIPE CCD-calling algorithm, which defines chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET data by merging high-confidence, both-anchor-peak-supported loops into contiguous genomic intervals. This turns discrete loop calls into domain-scale annotations without additional sequencing input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ChIA-PET reads — this skill operates downstream of linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and loop calling, not on FASTQ data The goal is enhancer-promoter loop annotation or allele-specific peak/loop resolution, which ChIA-PIPE implements as separate analyses with different criteria (e.g., PET count >=3 loops, phased SNPs) Loops lack anchor peak-support annotations, so the both-anchor-supported filter cannot be evaluated

skills.description: Use when you have an intra-chromosomal NxN Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., KR-normalized at 50/25/5 Kb from GM12878) and need unsupervised TAD boundary detection without complex parameter tuning.
skills.name: chromatin-contact-map-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatin-contact-map-analysis Use when you have an intra-chromosomal NxN Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., KR-normalized at 50/25/5 Kb from GM12878) and need unsupervised TAD boundary detection without complex parameter tuning. Input is raw sequencing reads or .hic files alone without first dumping a normalized NxN contact matrix — TOAST requires the matrix format as input The analysis goal is enhancer-promoter interaction prediction (e.g., EPIANN's GM12878 EPI dataset task), which is a different problem from TAD boundary identification You need supervised TAD calling against a labeled ground truth on simulated data with known boundaries at noise levels where FMS degrades substantially http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Identify topologically associated domains (TADs) from Hi-C contact matrices using TOAST, which encodes each genomic bin as a graph node, derives 16-dimensional embeddings with a 2-layer graph auto-encoder, clusters them with HDBSCAN, and calls contiguous same-label regions longer than 200 Kb as TADs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Identify topologically associated domains (TADs) from Hi-C contact matrices using TOAST, which encodes each genomic bin as a graph node, derives 16-dimensional embeddings with a 2-layer graph auto-encoder, clusters them with HDBSCAN, and calls contiguous same-label regions longer than 200 Kb as TADs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or .hic files alone without first dumping a normalized NxN contact matrix — TOAST requires the matrix format as input The analysis goal is enhancer-promoter interaction prediction (e.g., EPIANN's GM12878 EPI dataset task), which is a different problem from TAD boundary identification You need supervised TAD calling against a labeled ground truth on simulated data with known boundaries at noise levels where FMS degrades substantially

skills.name: chromatin-contact-significance-calling
skills.search_text: chromatin-contact-significance-calling Use when normalized Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair data are available and you need per-contact significance scores, reproducibility fractions between biological replicates, or a ROC AUC comparison against Fit-Hi-C. Input is raw FASTQ or unnormalized BAM files — coverage computation (BEDTools coverage) and normalization must precede significance calling Analysis targets promoter-centered pcHi-C interactions with different coverage thresholds (promoter 200, other 50) rather than symmetric Hi-C fragment coverages Contact maps are needed only for reproducibility scoring (HiC-spector) or compartment A/B correlation, not for per-contact significance calls http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 A workflow for calling significant long-range chromatin contacts from normalized Hi-C data using covNorm's Weibull background p-values with FDR correction, and benchmarking significance calls against Fit-Hi-C by replicate overlap and ROC AUC (~0.85). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041

Input is raw interaction data that has not yet passed the negative binomial coverage normalization (normCoverage) step — distance normalization assumes bias-removed residuals Rij Working with pcHi-C PO-interactions restricted to the 15 kb–2 Mb promoter-centered window without the modified normCoverage call (do_shuffle=FALSE, cov1_thresh=200, cov2_thresh=50) done first Only inter-chromosomal contacts are of interest — the covNorm workflow filters to cis-interactions and normalizes against a genomic-distance background that only applies intra-chromosomally http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Implements covNorm's genomic distance-dependent background normalization step: after coverage normalization, fit expected ligation frequencies as a function of genomic distance and remove that background from fragment-pair interaction frequencies using covNormRpkg's normDistance function. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate or rank TLD/TAD predictions from a Hi-C matrix (bulk or single-cell) by 2D structural entropy and modularity indices, e.g., to confirm a predictor's first-class performance beyond AMI/WS benchmarks.
skills.name: chromatin-domain-modularity-assessment
skills.search_text: chromatin-domain-modularity-assessment Use when you need to evaluate or rank TLD/TAD predictions from a Hi-C matrix (bulk or single-cell) by 2D structural entropy and modularity indices, e.g., to confirm a predictor's first-class performance beyond AMI/WS benchmarks. Input is already an imputed or normalized contact matrix — deDoc2 needs no normalization and modularity is computed on the raw matrix with zero diagonals replaced and log2-processing applied at assessment time Your goal is boundary-accuracy benchmarking only — AMI (sklearn.metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score) and weighted similarity WS are the appropriate metrics, not entropy/modularity indices The TLD partition contains unresolved single-bin 'TLD' lines — these must be removed as non-TAD regions before building the encoding tree, otherwise entropy is misestimated http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Assess the quality of predicted TAD-like domains (TLDs) by computing the 2D structural entropy of a height-2 encoding tree built from each predictor's TLDs, and the modularity of the Hi-C contact matrix after replacing zero diagonal elements and log2-processing the remaining entries. This provides entropy/modularity index values that complement boundary-accuracy metrics like AMI and WS when comparing TLD predictors. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Assess the quality of predicted TAD-like domains (TLDs) by computing the 2D structural entropy of a height-2 encoding tree built from each predictor's TLDs, and the modularity of the Hi-C contact matrix after replacing zero diagonal elements and log2-processing the remaining entries. This provides entropy/modularity index values that complement boundary-accuracy metrics like AMI and WS when comparing TLD predictors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an imputed or normalized contact matrix — deDoc2 needs no normalization and modularity is computed on the raw matrix with zero diagonals replaced and log2-processing applied at assessment time Your goal is boundary-accuracy benchmarking only — AMI (sklearn.metrics.adjusted_mutual_info_score) and weighted similarity WS are the appropriate metrics, not entropy/modularity indices The TLD partition contains unresolved single-bin 'TLD' lines — these must be removed as non-TAD regions before building the encoding tree, otherwise entropy is misestimated

skills.name: chromatin-interaction-data-processing
skills.search_text: chromatin-interaction-data-processing Use when raw paired-end FASTQ from ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq libraries must be processed end-to-end into peaks, loops, chromatin contact domains, and 2D contact maps viewable in Juicebox/HiGlass. skills.summary: Run ChIA-PIPE, a fully automated pipeline that performs linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, loop calling, and automated quality control on ChIA-PET data, and extend it via pseudolinker handling to related 3D genome assays (HiChIP, PLAC-seq), producing peak/loop calls plus browser-ready .hic and .cool contact maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already processed interaction data (e.g., existing peak/loop BED files or .hic/.cool maps) rather than raw paired-end FASTQ needing linker filtering and alignment. skills.description: Use when processing ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq read pairs (short 2×21 bp or long 2×150 bp) and you need to call chromatin interaction loops with peak-supported anchors from uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs.
skills.name: chromatin-interaction-loop-calling
skills.search_text: chromatin-interaction-loop-calling Use when processing ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq read pairs (short 2×21 bp or long 2×150 bp) and you need to call chromatin interaction loops with peak-supported anchors from uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs. Input is raw ChIA-PET FASTQ not yet processed for linker filtering and read mapping — loop calling requires uniquely aligned, deduplicated PETs (MAPQ ≥ 30). The data type is a plain chromatin contact map or Hi-C matrix rather than ligated PET reads with bridge linkers; ChIA-PIPE's linker-based loop detection is not appropriate. The dataset is too small to yield loops with PET count ≥ 3 and peak support, in which case loop calls would be unreliable. ChIA-PIPE's loop-calling stage identifies chromatin interaction loops (anchor-to-anchor PETs) from ChIA-PET/HiChIP data after linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and duplicate removal, then classifies PETs as self-ligation versus interligation and annotates loops as enhancer-promoter or promoter-promoter. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: ChIA-PIPE's loop-calling stage identifies chromatin interaction loops (anchor-to-anchor PETs) from ChIA-PET/HiChIP data after linker filtering, read mapping, peak calling, and duplicate removal, then classifies PETs as self-ligation versus interligation and annotates loops as enhancer-promoter or promoter-promoter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ChIA-PET FASTQ not yet processed for linker filtering and read mapping — loop calling requires uniquely aligned, deduplicated PETs (MAPQ ≥ 30). The data type is a plain chromatin contact map or Hi-C matrix rather than ligated PET reads with bridge linkers; ChIA-PIPE's linker-based loop detection is not appropriate. The dataset is too small to yield loops with PET count ≥ 3 and peak support, in which case loop calls would be unreliable.

skills.description: Use when assessing how well sequence-based 3D genome folding predictions (deepC) reproduce observed Hi-C contacts on holdout chromosomes, e.g. computing Pearson correlations for raw vs smoothed maps or low-depth training sets.

skills.search_text: chromatin-interaction-prediction-evaluation Use when assessing how well sequence-based 3D genome folding predictions (deepC) reproduce observed Hi-C contacts on holdout chromosomes, e.g. computing Pearson correlations for raw vs smoothed maps or low-depth training sets. The goal is functional interpretation of deletion effects (in silico deletion screen scoring) rather than prediction-accuracy evaluation against observed Hi-C. The task is training or fine-tuning a deepC model itself rather than evaluating an already-trained model on holdout data. Data are not chromatin contact maps (e.g. 1D ChIP-seq/DNase tracks), since the Pearson correlation benchmarks are defined on interaction matrices. http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantitative evaluation of deepC-predicted chromatin interaction maps against observed Hi-C on held-out chromosomes, using distance-stratified and mean Pearson correlations across raw and smoothed contact maps and across Hi-C sequencing depths. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Quantitative evaluation of deepC-predicted chromatin interaction maps against observed Hi-C on held-out chromosomes, using distance-stratified and mean Pearson correlations across raw and smoothed contact maps and across Hi-C sequencing depths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is functional interpretation of deletion effects (in silico deletion screen scoring) rather than prediction-accuracy evaluation against observed Hi-C. skills.description: Use when ChIA-PET reads must be resolved to allele-specific loops for a sample with genome-wide SNP phasing (e.g., NA12878), and you need statistically biased SNPs at loop anchors.
skills.name: chromatin-loop-anchor-resolution
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-anchor-resolution Use when ChIA-PET reads must be resolved to allele-specific loops for a sample with genome-wide SNP phasing (e.g., NA12878), and you need statistically biased SNPs at loop anchors. Input data lacks genome-wide SNP phasing information for the sample — allele-specific resolution cannot be performed Data type is not chromatin-mapping data (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq); the loop-calling and anchor-resolution logic is specific to these PET-based assays The goal is bulk loop calling without allele specificity — plain loop calling (PET count ≥ 3 with peak support) suffices and the SNP bias testing is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Resolves haplotype-specific (phased) chromatin interaction loops from ChIA-PET data by assigning haplotype labels to uniquely aligned reads overlapping phased SNPs, testing allelic coverage bias per SNP, and classifying loops as allele-specific phased interactions. This is how ChIA-PIPE derived the 636 phased CTCF loops from GM12878 (NA12878) data. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Resolves haplotype-specific (phased) chromatin interaction loops from ChIA-PET data by assigning haplotype labels to uniquely aligned reads overlapping phased SNPs, testing allelic coverage bias per SNP, and classifying loops as allele-specific phased interactions. This is how ChIA-PIPE derived the 636 phased CTCF loops from GM12878 (NA12878) data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks genome-wide SNP phasing information for the sample — allele-specific resolution cannot be performed Data type is not chromatin-mapping data (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or PLAC-seq); the loop-calling and anchor-resolution logic is specific to these PET-based assays The goal is bulk loop calling without allele specificity — plain loop calling (PET count ≥ 3 with peak support) suffices and the SNP bias testing is unnecessary

skills.name: chromatin-loop-calling-from-imaging-data
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-calling-from-imaging-data Use when the input is per-cell, per-allele 3D coordinates of genomic loci from multiplexed DNA FISH or DNA seqFISH+ (e.g., 25 Kb or 5 Kb bins) and the goal is de novo chromatin loop detection and benchmarking against HiCCUPS references. skills.summary: Identify de novo chromatin loops from multiplexed DNA FISH / chromatin tracing data using SnapFISH, which models continuous 3D Euclidean distances with a local-background two-sample T-test rather than count-based proximity-ligation statistics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is proximity-ligation assay data (Hi-C / Micro-C contact count matrices) — existing count-based loop callers such as HiCCUPS are the appropriate choice, not SnapFISH Only pairwise distances or heatmaps are needed without loop calling — use 'SnapFISH step1' instead of the full call-loops pipeline Multi-way (3+ locus) chromatin interactions are the target — SnapFISH only considers pairwise interactions in this work

skills.description: Use when you have per-cell (tab-separated, optionally gzipped) scHi-C contact files for mm10/hg19/hg38 and need cell-type-specific chromatin loop candidates and summits.
skills.name: chromatin-loop-calling-from-schic
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-calling-from-schic Use when you have per-cell (tab-separated, optionally gzipped) scHi-C contact files for mm10/hg19/hg38 and need cell-type-specific chromatin loop candidates and summits. Input is bulk Hi-C or already-aggregated contact matrices rather than per-cell contact files — SnapHiC's per-cell paired t-test requires single-cell contacts Genome assembly other than mm10, hg19, or hg38, since SnapHiC uses these to determine autosomal chromosome count and generate .hic files Goal is 3D haplotype-resolved genome reconstruction rather than loop identification (use Dip-C/hickit instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 SnapHiC-style loop calling from single-cell Hi-C: bin contacts at 10-kb, impute per-cell contact probabilities via random walk with restart (RWR), then test each bin pair against global and local background models to identify high-resolution chromatin loops. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: SnapHiC-style loop calling from single-cell Hi-C: bin contacts at 10-kb, impute per-cell contact probabilities via random walk with restart (RWR), then test each bin pair against global and local background models to identify high-resolution chromatin loops.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Hi-C or already-aggregated contact matrices rather than per-cell contact files — SnapHiC's per-cell paired t-test requires single-cell contacts Genome assembly other than mm10, hg19, or hg38, since SnapHiC uses these to determine autosomal chromosome count and generate .hic files Goal is 3D haplotype-resolved genome reconstruction rather than loop identification (use Dip-C/hickit instead)

skills.description: Use when input is per-cell scHi-C or sn-m3C-seq contact files (e.g. 2,869 human prefrontal cortex sn-m3C-seq cells or 742 mouse ESCs) and the goal is to call cell-type-specific chromatin loops at 10-kb resolution.
skills.name: chromatin-loop-calling-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-calling-statistical-testing Use when input is per-cell scHi-C or sn-m3C-seq contact files (e.g. 2,869 human prefrontal cortex sn-m3C-seq cells or 742 mouse ESCs) and the goal is to call cell-type-specific chromatin loops at 10-kb resolution. skills.summary: Identify chromatin loops at high resolution from single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data using SnapHiC's five-step pipeline—binning, random-walk-with-restart (RWR) imputation, .hic/.cool generation, global/local background loop-candidate testing, and postprocessing into loop summits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Hi-C or a pooled contact matrix without per-cell contact files — SnapHiC's RWR imputation and per-cell binning require one contact file per single cell Reference genome is not mm10, hg19, or hg38 — SnapHiC uses the genome name to determine the number of autosomal chromosomes and to generate .hic files Input is already a per-cell RNA-seq/ATAC-seq table or a Dip-C seg/3dg output — this skill only covers chromatin loop calling, not 3D genome reconstruction or preprocessing pipelines

skills.description: Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool/.hic contact map and a positive interaction set (ChIA-PET/HiChIP/Capture Hi-C bedpe) and need supervised, data-driven chromatin loop calls that are robust to low sequencing depth.
skills.name: chromatin-loop-prediction-from-contact-maps
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-prediction-from-contact-maps Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool/.hic contact map and a positive interaction set (ChIA-PET/HiChIP/Capture Hi-C bedpe) and need supervised, data-driven chromatin loop calls that are robust to low sequencing depth. The goal is an unsupervised/enrichment-based call (local Poisson background as in HiCCUPS or distance-dependent splines as in Fit-Hi-C) rather than supervised classification against orthogonal positives No positive interaction training set (ChIA-PET/HiChIP/Capture Hi-C bedpe) or suitable pre-trained model is available for the cell type/platform The contact map is not binned near 10 kb resolution or lacks an ICE weight column (and raw signals are not appropriate for the chosen model) http://edamontology.org/topic_3940 Predict chromatin loops from genome-wide contact maps (Hi-C, Micro-C, DNA SPRITE) using Peakachu, a Random Forest classifier trained on orthogonal positive interaction sets (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe files) rather than statistical enrichment of pixels. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Predict chromatin loops from genome-wide contact maps (Hi-C, Micro-C, DNA SPRITE) using Peakachu, a Random Forest classifier trained on orthogonal positive interaction sets (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe files) rather than statistical enrichment of pixels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is an unsupervised/enrichment-based call (local Poisson background as in HiCCUPS or distance-dependent splines as in Fit-Hi-C) rather than supervised classification against orthogonal positives No positive interaction training set (ChIA-PET/HiChIP/Capture Hi-C bedpe) or suitable pre-trained model is available for the cell type/platform The contact map is not binned near 10 kb resolution or lacks an ICE weight column (and raw signals are not appropriate for the chosen model)

skills.description: Use when a Hi-C contact map implies a transitive or redundant chromatin loop between loci and a ChIA-PET2 CTCF bedpe/contact matrix is available to confirm or refute the direct interaction.
skills.name: chromatin-loop-transitivity-and-redundancy-analysis
skills.search_text: chromatin-loop-transitivity-and-redundancy-analysis Use when a Hi-C contact map implies a transitive or redundant chromatin loop between loci and a ChIA-PET2 CTCF bedpe/contact matrix is available to confirm or refute the direct interaction. When starting from raw ChIA-PET FASTQ — this skill operates downstream of ChIA-PET2's trimLinker, buildBedpe, removeDup and loop-calling steps on deduplicated bedpe output When the goal is only significant loop calling (MICC/ChiaSig/Mango comparison) without cross-referencing an external Hi-C contact map The paper provides only a few illustrative examples of transitivity/redundancy/robustness, so this is not a validated genome-wide transitivity classifier http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Cross-checks ChIA-PET2-derived CTCF chromatin loops against a matched Hi-C contact map to test whether Hi-C-implied transitive loops (e.g., L1–L3a and L1–L4a implying L3a–L4a) exist as direct ChIA-PET loops, and to tabulate redundancy cases where one Hi-C loop resolves into multiple CTCF-mediated loops. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Cross-checks ChIA-PET2-derived CTCF chromatin loops against a matched Hi-C contact map to test whether Hi-C-implied transitive loops (e.g., L1–L3a and L1–L4a implying L3a–L4a) exist as direct ChIA-PET loops, and to tabulate redundancy cases where one Hi-C loop resolves into multiple CTCF-mediated loops.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When starting from raw ChIA-PET FASTQ — this skill operates downstream of ChIA-PET2's trimLinker, buildBedpe, removeDup and loop-calling steps on deduplicated bedpe output When the goal is only significant loop calling (MICC/ChiaSig/Mango comparison) without cross-referencing an external Hi-C contact map The paper provides only a few illustrative examples of transitivity/redundancy/robustness, so this is not a validated genome-wide transitivity classifier

skills.description: Use when comparing timepoint-specific nucleosome dyad positions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium MNase-seq) across promoter-aligned gene groups to detect +1 nucleosome shifts and nucleosome-depleted region remodeling.
skills.name: chromatin-ndr-dynamics-visualization
skills.search_text: chromatin-ndr-dynamics-visualization Use when comparing timepoint-specific nucleosome dyad positions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium MNase-seq) across promoter-aligned gene groups to detect +1 nucleosome shifts and nucleosome-depleted region remodeling. Input is ATAC-seq rather than MNase-seq and the goal is the cadmium-stress dyad-shift analysis — the paper reports markedly better RoboCOP performance with MNase-seq, so composite dyad shifts from ATAC-seq would be less reliable The question is single-locus nucleosome positioning rather than composite promoter-averaged +1 dyad behavior across gene groups http://edamontology.org/topic_3176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Visualizes cadmium-stress chromatin dynamics by computing composite +1 nucleosome dyad probability distributions across promoters for gene groups defined by RNA-seq response, using RoboCOP_MNase timepoint-specific occupancy profiles and DynaCOP figure notebooks to reveal NDR expansion or contraction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Visualizes cadmium-stress chromatin dynamics by computing composite +1 nucleosome dyad probability distributions across promoters for gene groups defined by RNA-seq response, using RoboCOP_MNase timepoint-specific occupancy profiles and DynaCOP figure notebooks to reveal NDR expansion or contraction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is ATAC-seq rather than MNase-seq and the goal is the cadmium-stress dyad-shift analysis — the paper reports markedly better RoboCOP performance with MNase-seq, so composite dyad shifts from ATAC-seq would be less reliable The question is single-locus nucleosome positioning rather than composite promoter-averaged +1 dyad behavior across gene groups

skills.description: Use when processing ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) libraries and protein-factor binding peaks must be called from self-ligation PETs to support loop calling, CCD calling, and enhancer-promoter annotation.
skills.name: chromatin-peak-calling
skills.search_text: chromatin-peak-calling Use when processing ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) libraries and protein-factor binding peaks must be called from self-ligation PETs to support loop calling, CCD calling, and enhancer-promoter annotation. The data are not chromatin-mapping reads (e.g., plain ChIP-seq or RNA-seq) with no PET linker structure, so self-ligation/interligation classification does not apply No input-control sample is available and false-positive peaks would invalidate the strict ChIA-PIPE peak-calling defaults The goal is alignment or linker filtering rather than peak detection — those are separate upstream ChIA-PIPE stages http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0607 Call protein-factor binding peaks from ChIA-PET self-ligation PETs as implemented in ChIA-PIPE, using uniquely aligned (MAPQ ≥ 30), nonredundant PETs and an input-control sample to suppress false positives, producing peak calls that anchor downstream loop and chromatin contact domain analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Call protein-factor binding peaks from ChIA-PET self-ligation PETs as implemented in ChIA-PIPE, using uniquely aligned (MAPQ ≥ 30), nonredundant PETs and an input-control sample to suppress false positives, producing peak calls that anchor downstream loop and chromatin contact domain analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not chromatin-mapping reads (e.g., plain ChIP-seq or RNA-seq) with no PET linker structure, so self-ligation/interligation classification does not apply No input-control sample is available and false-positive peaks would invalidate the strict ChIA-PIPE peak-calling defaults The goal is alignment or linker filtering rather than peak detection — those are separate upstream ChIA-PIPE stages

skills.description: Use when a set of query noncoding SNPs must be functionally screened for their impact on chromatin accessibility, histone marks, or TF binding across many ENCODE/Roadmap epigenomic profiles in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner.
skills.name: chromatin-profile-score-interpretation
skills.search_text: chromatin-profile-score-interpretation Use when a set of query noncoding SNPs must be functionally screened for their impact on chromatin accessibility, histone marks, or TF binding across many ENCODE/Roadmap epigenomic profiles in a tissue- or cell type-specific manner. The question concerns long-range effects such as 3D DNA contact — the DeepFun model has not considered long-range interactions Quantitative (continuous) epigenomic signal is required — DeepFun binarizes peaks during training and ignores the quantitative information The variant is already annotated in a feature table with functional scores, so no allele-level re-scoring is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Screens noncoding SNPs with DeepFun pre-trained CNN models (Basset framework, Torch7) to compute per-variant, per-profile SAD = P(alt) − P(ref) and log-odds differences across 7879 epigenomic profiles (1548 DNase I, 1536 histone mark, 4795 transcription factor binding; 225 tissues/cell types). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Screens noncoding SNPs with DeepFun pre-trained CNN models (Basset framework, Torch7) to compute per-variant, per-profile SAD = P(alt) − P(ref) and log-odds differences across 7879 epigenomic profiles (1548 DNase I, 1536 histone mark, 4795 transcription factor binding; 225 tissues/cell types).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns long-range effects such as 3D DNA contact — the DeepFun model has not considered long-range interactions Quantitative (continuous) epigenomic signal is required — DeepFun binarizes peaks during training and ignores the quantitative information The variant is already annotated in a feature table with functional scores, so no allele-level re-scoring is needed

skills.description: Use when you have genome-wide multi-track epigenomic signals (histone mark ChIP-seq tracks) for one or more Roadmap/ENCODE samples and need discrete chromatin state sequences as input to EpiAlign alignment or compression benchmarking.
skills.name: chromatin-state-annotation
skills.search_text: chromatin-state-annotation Use when you have genome-wide multi-track epigenomic signals (histone mark ChIP-seq tracks) for one or more Roadmap/ENCODE samples and need discrete chromatin state sequences as input to EpiAlign alignment or compression benchmarking. Input is already a single-track chromatin state sequence or a compressed state-label sequence — re-annotating with ChromHMM is unnecessary; proceed directly to EpiAlign alignment The goal is comparing raw multi-track signal matrices rather than chromatin state sequences — EpiAlign's premise is to reduce signal comparison to state sequence comparison, not to align signal matrices directly Regions of interest are dominated by the quiescent state 'o', which lacks a good biological interpretation and is excluded from motif analysis in the article http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Annotates genome-wide multi-track epigenomic signals (e.g. ChIP-seq histone marks from NIH Roadmap samples such as E071 brain) into single-track chromatin state sequences using a hidden Markov model method such as ChromHMM, producing the discrete state-label sequences that EpiAlign consumes for local alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Annotates genome-wide multi-track epigenomic signals (e.g. ChIP-seq histone marks from NIH Roadmap samples such as E071 brain) into single-track chromatin state sequences using a hidden Markov model method such as ChromHMM, producing the discrete state-label sequences that EpiAlign consumes for local alignment.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking an order-aware chromatin-state comparison method (e.g. EpiAlign) against a simple, order-agnostic baseline, or when only overall chromatin state composition — not sequence order — is needed to distinguish epigenomic samples.
skills.name: chromatin-state-frequency-vector-comparison
skills.search_text: chromatin-state-frequency-vector-comparison Use when benchmarking an order-aware chromatin-state comparison method (e.g. EpiAlign) against a simple, order-agnostic baseline, or when only overall chromatin state composition — not sequence order — is needed to distinguish epigenomic samples. The analysis goal is to retrieve genomic regions similar to a query region in terms of epigenomic signal order — the frequency baseline ignores sequential information, which the EpiAlign paper identifies as the gap in former epigenome comparative studies Chromatin state sequences have not yet been annotated and compressed (ChromHMM states + run-length compression); raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices are not the direct input A principled similarity measure is needed on its own, not a deliberately naive comparator: this skill exists to be the weak baseline that EpiAlign is shown to outperform http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 A naive baseline for comparing Roadmap epigenomes that represents each sample's chromatin state sequence as a vector of state frequency proportions and scores pairwise similarity from these vectors, deliberately ignoring sequential order. skills.search_text: chromatin-state-regulatory-element-classification Use when RNAPII ChIA-PET loop calls (PET count ≥3 with peak support) need to be annotated as enhancer-promoter or promoter-promoter interactions and exported as separate per-category loop files for visualization in BASIC Browser tracks. skills.summary: Classifies called ChIA-PET loops (PET count ≥3, peak-supported, each with a unique loop ID) into enhancer-promoter (E-P), promoter-promoter (P-P), or neither categories by intersecting loop anchor coordinates against enhancer and promoter BED annotations, producing per-category subset loop files for separate browser track display.

skills.name: chromatin-state-sequence-compression
skills.search_text: chromatin-state-sequence-compression Use when chromatin state sequences (e.g. from ChromHMM on Roadmap epigenomes) are about to be aligned with EpiAlign, or when uncompressed sequences contain long runs of a single state such as the quiescent state 'o'. Input is still raw multi-track epigenomic signal (ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq tracks) that has not yet been converted to discrete chromatin state labels — run chromatin state annotation (e.g. ChromHMM) first Analysis intentionally depends on state duration/run lengths, e.g. reproducing the uncompressed baseline that the paper shows fails to distinguish real from randomized epigenomes and takes ~20x longer http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Run-length compression of ChromHMM-style chromatin state sequences, collapsing consecutive occurrences of the same state into a single label (abbcc -> abc), so that long quiescent stretches do not dominate EpiAlign local alignments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Run-length compression of ChromHMM-style chromatin state sequences, collapsing consecutive occurrences of the same state into a single label (abbcc -> abc), so that long quiescent stretches do not dominate EpiAlign local alignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw multi-track epigenomic signal (ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq tracks) that has not yet been converted to discrete chromatin state labels — run chromatin state annotation (e.g. ChromHMM) first Analysis intentionally depends on state duration/run lengths, e.g. reproducing the uncompressed baseline that the paper shows fails to distinguish real from randomized epigenomes and takes ~20x longer

skills.description: Use when two genomic regions are represented as ChromHMM-derived chromatin state label sequences and you need a similarity score that accounts for varying state lengths, state frequencies, mismatches, and deletions (e.g. -match queries in 500 kb regions).
skills.name: chromatin-state-weight-scoring
skills.search_text: chromatin-state-weight-scoring Use when two genomic regions are represented as ChromHMM-derived chromatin state label sequences and you need a similarity score that accounts for varying state lengths, state frequencies, mismatches, and deletions (e.g. -match queries in 500 kb regions). Input is still raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than single-track chromatin state sequences produced by ChromHMM or a similar annotator The comparison requires aligning genomic regions whose sequences are dominated by long single-state stretches and cannot be meaningfully compressed first (e.g. quiescent stretches lacking biological interpretation, per Supplementary Figure S1) The task is clustering whole epigenomes by global genome-wide profiles rather than scoring local pairwise similarity of chromatin state sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3302 Weight-based scoring scheme from EpiAlign (NAR 2019) that quantifies similarity between two compressed chromatin state sequences using a weight function W(k,S) — equal or frequency-based — feeding match/mismatch (MF), mismatch (NF = -epsilon_N * (W+W)), and deletion (DF = -epsilon_D * W) score functions inside a local-alignment dynamic programming recurrence. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Weight-based scoring scheme from EpiAlign (NAR 2019) that quantifies similarity between two compressed chromatin state sequences using a weight function W(k,S) — equal or frequency-based — feeding match/mismatch (MF), mismatch (NF = -epsilon_N * (W+W)), and deletion (DF = -epsilon_D * W) score functions inside a local-alignment dynamic programming recurrence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than single-track chromatin state sequences produced by ChromHMM or a similar annotator The comparison requires aligning genomic regions whose sequences are dominated by long single-state stretches and cannot be meaningfully compressed first (e.g. quiescent stretches lacking biological interpretation, per Supplementary Figure S1) The task is clustering whole epigenomes by global genome-wide profiles rather than scoring local pairwise similarity of chromatin state sequences

skills.name: chromatogram-peak-height-quantification

skills.summary: Visualize and compare the chromatin-state distribution of epigenomic peak sets by intersecting each peak file with ChromHMM cell-line annotations and rendering the per-state overlap percentages as a heatmap, as implemented in EpiCompare's Functional Annotation report section.
