skills.description: Use when evaluating enhancer-target interaction prediction models on genomic coordinate data (e.g. BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio ET pairs) where random folds would leak spatially autocorrelated loci between train and test chromosomes.
skills.name: chromosome-based-cross-validation-design
skills.search_text: chromosome-based-cross-validation-design Use when evaluating enhancer-target interaction prediction models on genomic coordinate data (e.g. BENGI All-Pairs.Natural-Ratio ET pairs) where random folds would leak spatially autocorrelated loci between train and test chromosomes. The input is a single pre-computed feature table with no genomic coordinates, so chromosome-based splitting cannot be defined The goal is hyperparameter tuning on one cell line (e.g. the GM12878 consensus LCL training set) rather than an unbiased outer evaluation The question does not concern spatial generalization — e.g. evaluating feature importances on the full training set http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A validation design for enhancer-target interaction classifiers (e.g. CENTRE's XGBoost model) in which the 12 cross-validation groups are split by chromosome, so held-out test folds always lie in different genomic regions than the training folds. This prevents genomic-region leakage when evaluating ET pair prediction on BENGI datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad687
skills.summary: A validation design for enhancer-target interaction classifiers (e.g. CENTRE's XGBoost model) in which the 12 cross-validation groups are split by chromosome, so held-out test folds always lie in different genomic regions than the training folds. This prevents genomic-region leakage when evaluating ET pair prediction on BENGI datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a single pre-computed feature table with no genomic coordinates, so chromosome-based splitting cannot be defined The goal is hyperparameter tuning on one cell line (e.g. the GM12878 consensus LCL training set) rather than an unbiased outer evaluation The question does not concern spatial generalization — e.g. evaluating feature importances on the full training set

skills.description: Use when you have a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g. IMR90 at 50 kb or 5 kb resolution) and need a recursive, hierarchy-aware clustering of loci without imposing genomic contiguity.
skills.name: chromosome-cluster-nesting-analysis
skills.search_text: chromosome-cluster-nesting-analysis Use when you have a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g. IMR90 at 50 kb or 5 kb resolution) and need a recursive, hierarchy-aware clustering of loci without imposing genomic contiguity. When the goal is standard contiguous TAD calling, since TADs postulate clustering among neighboring loci contiguous along the genome coordinate and BHi-Cect instead allows non-contiguous, interwoven enclaves When the input is not a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix but an already-processed feature table or a non-Hi-C interaction dataset When mechanistic inference about loop extrusion vs phase separation is required — the analysis cannot infer these details http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Runs BHi-Cect, a top-down spectral clustering method that partitions Hi-C loci into nested, non-contiguous self-interacting clusters ('enclaves') and returns a binary partition tree plus per-cluster locus lists. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Runs BHi-Cect, a top-down spectral clustering method that partitions Hi-C loci into nested, non-contiguous self-interacting clusters ('enclaves') and returns a binary partition tree plus per-cluster locus lists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is standard contiguous TAD calling, since TADs postulate clustering among neighboring loci contiguous along the genome coordinate and BHi-Cect instead allows non-contiguous, interwoven enclaves When the input is not a 3-column sparse Hi-C contact matrix but an already-processed feature table or a non-Hi-C interaction dataset When mechanistic inference about loop extrusion vs phase separation is required — the analysis cannot infer these details

The analysis is single-genome ChIP-seq without spike-in — no exogenous chromosome renaming is needed and spikChIP's FLY/HUMAN/MOUSE/EXO distinction does not apply The BAM files already use the required exogenous genome identifier (e.g. FLY prefix) and a valid combined ChromInfo file exists Peak calling or downstream normalization steps (MACS2, spikChIP normalization) are being run on pre-existing correctly named files — this skill belongs to the pre-mapping setup stage http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs the combined sample+spike-in ChromInfo file required by spikChIP by renaming exogenous (dm3 fruit fly) chromosomes with the mandatory 'FLY' suffix and merging them with sample (hg19 human) chromosomes, so that a single synthetic genome index and bin segmentation can distinguish sample from spike-in reads. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064

skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis is single-genome ChIP-seq without spike-in — no exogenous chromosome renaming is needed and spikChIP's FLY/HUMAN/MOUSE/EXO distinction does not apply The BAM files already use the required exogenous genome identifier (e.g. FLY prefix) and a valid combined ChromInfo file exists Peak calling or downstream normalization steps (MACS2, spikChIP normalization) are being run on pre-existing correctly named files — this skill belongs to the pre-mapping setup stage

skills.description: Use when per-chromosome Hi-C contact maps (bulk or pseudo-bulk, resolutions up to 10 kb, or 5 kb with optimized PCA) need to be converted into A/B compartment score tracks for downstream differential analysis.
skills.name: chromosome-wise-hic-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: chromosome-wise-hic-matrix-processing Use when per-chromosome Hi-C contact maps (bulk or pseudo-bulk, resolutions up to 10 kb, or 5 kb with optimized PCA) need to be converted into A/B compartment score tracks for downstream differential analysis. The goal is differential compartment testing across samples — this skill only produces per-sample scores; the Mahalanobis-distance/chi-square differential step operates on its output afterwards. Input is single-cell Hi-C without pseudo-bulk aggregation — the paper notes genomic compartment identification from individual single-cell maps is still limited by sparsity, so first aggregate to pseudo-bulk (as few as ~100 cells per condition). Performs chromosome-wise Hi-C contact-map preprocessing — observed/expected distance normalization, transformation into a correlation matrix, and a memory-efficient parallelized partial SVD via a Filebacked Big Matrix — to yield A/B compartment scores, with automated selection of PC1 (or PC2) and sign orientation against GC content and gene density. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Performs chromosome-wise Hi-C contact-map preprocessing — observed/expected distance normalization, transformation into a correlation matrix, and a memory-efficient parallelized partial SVD via a Filebacked Big Matrix — to yield A/B compartment scores, with automated selection of PC1 (or PC2) and sign orientation against GC content and gene density.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential compartment testing across samples — this skill only produces per-sample scores; the Mahalanobis-distance/chi-square differential step operates on its output afterwards. Input is single-cell Hi-C without pseudo-bulk aggregation — the paper notes genomic compartment identification from individual single-cell maps is still limited by sparsity, so first aggregate to pseudo-bulk (as few as ~100 cells per condition).

skills.description: Use when assessing the reproducibility of iEDGE Rank-1 cis driver predictions across bootstrapped resamples of a TCGA-style SCNA/gene-expression cohort, or when a stability measure for mediation-ranked cis genes is required.
skills.name: cis-driver-gene-rank-derivation
skills.search_text: cis-driver-gene-rank-derivation Use when assessing the reproducibility of iEDGE Rank-1 cis driver predictions across bootstrapped resamples of a TCGA-style SCNA/gene-expression cohort, or when a stability measure for mediation-ranked cis genes is required. Cohort is too small or correlation effects too weak for the Sobel test's validity assumptions — the article notes these conditions were not met in all datasets. The goal is single-run discovery of novel cis drivers (with pathway enrichment via run_hyperEnrichment), not stability testing of already-derived Rank-1 calls. Data are unpaired or lack copy-number alteration and gene expression measured in the same samples, so the cis/trans mediation structure cannot be re-estimated per resample. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Quantifies bootstrap reproducibility of iEDGE's Rank-1 cis driver calls: 100 with-replacement resamples of a TCGA BRCA-style cohort are each rerun through the cis FDR 0.25 / trans FDR 0.01 differential-expression and Sobel mediation pipeline, and per-gene fraction-of-inclusion values test the reported stability (69.2% of Rank-1 genes above 0.75). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Quantifies bootstrap reproducibility of iEDGE's Rank-1 cis driver calls: 100 with-replacement resamples of a TCGA BRCA-style cohort are each rerun through the cis FDR 0.25 / trans FDR 0.01 differential-expression and Sobel mediation pipeline, and per-gene fraction-of-inclusion values test the reported stability (69.2% of Rank-1 genes above 0.75).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Cohort is too small or correlation effects too weak for the Sobel test's validity assumptions — the article notes these conditions were not met in all datasets. The goal is single-run discovery of novel cis drivers (with pathway enrichment via run_hyperEnrichment), not stability testing of already-derived Rank-1 calls. Data are unpaired or lack copy-number alteration and gene expression measured in the same samples, so the cis/trans mediation structure cannot be re-estimated per resample.

skills.summary: Benchmarks computational enhancer–gene linkage predictions against experimentally derived cis-eQTLs by ranking predicted gene-peak pairs and computing AUROC and AUPRC. Provides quantitative evidence that imputed expression–accessibility associations recover validated regulatory links (AUROC = 0.66, AUPRC = 0.68 in the SnapATAC PBMC analysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent cis-eQTL or functional validation set exists for the cell type/stimulus — AUROC/AUPRC against a mismatched positive set is not meaningful The goal is de novo enhancer–gene prediction rather than benchmarking an existing ranked prediction list Input data are bulk ATAC/RNA or lack single-cell barcode matching, since the linkage model depends on per-cell imputed expression–accessibility coupling

skills.description: Use when a cis/trans differential-expression signature table exists for SCNA events and candidate cis genes must be ranked by their trans mediation to designate the Rank-1 driver per alteration.
skills.name: cis-trans-mediation-ranking
skills.search_text: cis-trans-mediation-ranking Use when a cis/trans differential-expression signature table exists for SCNA events and candidate cis genes must be ranked by their trans mediation to designate the Rank-1 driver per alteration. Sample size is small or cis-trans correlation effects are weak — the Sobel test achieved high AUC only under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions, conditions not met in all datasets The goal is identifying altered regions or genes within the alteration only (a GISTIC2.0-style analysis) with no need to rank cis drivers by downstream trans mediation The assumption that the number of mediated trans genes proxies driver importance is not appropriate for the specific use case http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 The mediation/pruning module of iEDGE: for each (epi-)DNA alteration (SCNA), it applies Sobel tests of statistical mediation to determine which candidate cis genes predict trans gene expression, then aggregates per-pair results into a Weighted Fraction of Trans Mediation (WFTM) score to rank cis genes and flag the Rank-1 candidate driver. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: The mediation/pruning module of iEDGE: for each (epi-)DNA alteration (SCNA), it applies Sobel tests of statistical mediation to determine which candidate cis genes predict trans gene expression, then aggregates per-pair results into a Weighted Fraction of Trans Mediation (WFTM) score to rank cis genes and flag the Rank-1 candidate driver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sample size is small or cis-trans correlation effects are weak — the Sobel test achieved high AUC only under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions, conditions not met in all datasets The goal is identifying altered regions or genes within the alteration only (a GISTIC2.0-style analysis) with no need to rank cis drivers by downstream trans mediation The assumption that the number of mediated trans genes proxies driver importance is not appropriate for the specific use case

skills.description: Use when replicating POSTRE's dosage-sensitivity scoring for structural variant pathogenicity prediction, especially when genes on sex chromosomes lack triplosensitivity (TS) scores and a proxy must be substituted before thresholding.
skills.name: clingen-haploinsufficiency-score-integration
skills.search_text: clingen-haploinsufficiency-score-integration Use when replicating POSTRE's dosage-sensitivity scoring for structural variant pathogenicity prediction, especially when genes on sex chromosomes lack triplosensitivity (TS) scores and a proxy must be substituted before thresholding. The SVs or annotations are not on GRCh37/hg19 coordinates — POSTRE_multiSV() explicitly requires hg19 and remapping would invalidate the BED interval-to-gene mapping The goal is predicting SVs implicated in recessive phenotypes — the article states POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its recessive capacity has not been specifically evaluated A gene already has a published TS score — the HI-as-TS proxy substitution is only for genes on sex chromosomes lacking TS scores and must not override existing scores http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs POSTRE's per-gene dosageSensitivityScore module by integrating ClinGen haploinsufficiency (HI) and triplosensitivity (TS) scores with the ClinGen_haploinsufficiency_gene_GRCh37.bed interval annotations, applying a 0.85 threshold to derive binary LOF/GOF dosage-sensitivity calls. Sex-chromosome genes lacking published TS scores receive the HI score as a TS proxy (final_TS_score = final_HI_score). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Reconstructs POSTRE's per-gene dosageSensitivityScore module by integrating ClinGen haploinsufficiency (HI) and triplosensitivity (TS) scores with the ClinGen_haploinsufficiency_gene_GRCh37.bed interval annotations, applying a 0.85 threshold to derive binary LOF/GOF dosage-sensitivity calls. Sex-chromosome genes lacking published TS scores receive the HI score as a TS proxy (final_TS_score = final_HI_score).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SVs or annotations are not on GRCh37/hg19 coordinates — POSTRE_multiSV() explicitly requires hg19 and remapping would invalidate the BED interval-to-gene mapping The goal is predicting SVs implicated in recessive phenotypes — the article states POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its recessive capacity has not been specifically evaluated A gene already has a published TS score — the HI-as-TS proxy substitution is only for genes on sex chromosomes lacking TS scores and must not override existing scores

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon epihaplotype tables are available and you need to distinguish clonally expanded (dominant) epiallele families from stochastic methylation by scoring each methylated core with a clonality index and E index.
skills.name: clonality-index-computation
skills.search_text: clonality-index-computation Use when bisulfite amplicon epihaplotype tables are available and you need to distinguish clonally expanded (dominant) epiallele families from stochastic methylation by scoring each methylated core with a clonality index and E index. Input is raw FASTQ/FASTA or per-read methylation calls rather than Module-2-annotated epialleles/cores — run PEAR, PRINSEQ, ampliMethProfiler and Modules 1–2 first. Goal is quantifying methylation of single CpGs or abundance of single epialleles without assessing phased core clonality — single-nucleotide methods or tools like EBA/methclone cover that scope. The population contains rare amplified epialleles at ~10% frequency of the kind in Cond 3/Cond 4 — these escape detection by Modules 1 and 2, so clonality values derived from them would be misleading without Module 3-based identification. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Computes the clonality index — the frequency of methylated cores normalized to the average methylation of the population — alongside the MethCores Index and the entanglement (E) index, as implemented in MethCoresProfiler Module 3 (MethCores_Analyst) to quantify clonal dominance of epiallele families in complex DNA populations. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Computes the clonality index — the frequency of methylated cores normalized to the average methylation of the population — alongside the MethCores Index and the entanglement (E) index, as implemented in MethCoresProfiler Module 3 (MethCores_Analyst) to quantify clonal dominance of epiallele families in complex DNA populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/FASTA or per-read methylation calls rather than Module-2-annotated epialleles/cores — run PEAR, PRINSEQ, ampliMethProfiler and Modules 1–2 first. Goal is quantifying methylation of single CpGs or abundance of single epialleles without assessing phased core clonality — single-nucleotide methods or tools like EBA/methclone cover that scope. The population contains rare amplified epialleles at ~10% frequency of the kind in Cond 3/Cond 4 — these escape detection by Modules 1 and 2, so clonality values derived from them would be misleading without Module 3-based identification.

skills.search_text: coarse-graining-block-transformation Use when calling broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains (e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3 spanning kb to Mb) from mapped-read BED files, or when characterizing multi-scale structure via auto-correlation length under coarse-graining. skills.search_text: coefficient-table-interpretation Use when you have per-donor flow cytometry cell proportion data plus donor metadata (age, sex) and need to determine which individual-level factor is most strongly associated with each immune cell population's composition. Data are bulk genomic (ATAC-seq/RNA-seq) loci rather than per-donor flow cytometry proportions — use differential/trajectory/breakpoint analyses instead The analysis goal is differential expression or enrichment rather than attributing cell-composition variation to individual-level covariates Donor metadata lacks both age and sex, so the age × sex interaction design cannot be fitted http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits per-cell-population generalized linear models of PBMC flow cytometry proportions against age, sex, and age-by-sex interaction, then extracts coefficients, standard errors, and p-values into a single table (flow_glm_coefficients.csv) that is ranked to attribute composition variation to age vs. sex. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Fits per-cell-population generalized linear models of PBMC flow cytometry proportions against age, sex, and age-by-sex interaction, then extracts coefficients, standard errors, and p-values into a single table (flow_glm_coefficients.csv) that is ranked to attribute composition variation to age vs. sex.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are bulk genomic (ATAC-seq/RNA-seq) loci rather than per-donor flow cytometry proportions — use differential/trajectory/breakpoint analyses instead The analysis goal is differential expression or enrichment rather than attributing cell-composition variation to individual-level covariates Donor metadata lacks both age and sex, so the age × sex interaction design cannot be fitted

skills.description: Use when validating a supervised chromatin loop caller on a perturbation system where loops are expected to disappear, such as a cohesin (RAD21-AID) auxin-depletion Hi-C experiment, to estimate the model's false discovery rate.
skills.name: cohesin-depletion-loop-loss-quantification
skills.search_text: cohesin-depletion-loop-loss-quantification Use when validating a supervised chromatin loop caller on a perturbation system where loops are expected to disappear, such as a cohesin (RAD21-AID) auxin-depletion Hi-C experiment, to estimate the model's false discovery rate. The input maps are not a biological perturbation in which loops are expected to disappear (e.g. two untreated cell types) — residual loops then do not straightforwardly represent false positives. The pre-trained model was not trained on raw contact values (a normalized weight was used in training) — in that case --clr-weight-name must match the model's training normalization instead of 'raw'. The goal is de novo loop discovery rather than model validation; use peakachu train with a positive bedpe training set instead. Estimates the false discovery rate of the Peakachu chromatin loop detector by scoring matched auxin-treated (cohesin-depleted) and untreated HCT-116 RAD21-AID Hi-C maps with the same CTCF ChIA-PET-trained Random Forest model, using the near-total loss of loops upon cohesin depletion (19 vs 11,814 loops) to derive an FDR of ~0.2%. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Estimates the false discovery rate of the Peakachu chromatin loop detector by scoring matched auxin-treated (cohesin-depleted) and untreated HCT-116 RAD21-AID Hi-C maps with the same CTCF ChIA-PET-trained Random Forest model, using the near-total loss of loops upon cohesin depletion (19 vs 11,814 loops) to derive an FDR of ~0.2%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input maps are not a biological perturbation in which loops are expected to disappear (e.g. two untreated cell types) — residual loops then do not straightforwardly represent false positives. The pre-trained model was not trained on raw contact values (a normalized weight was used in training) — in that case --clr-weight-name must match the model's training normalization instead of 'raw'. The goal is de novo loop discovery rather than model validation; use peakachu train with a positive bedpe training set instead.

skills.description: Use when an existing NGS workflow's default tool (e.g. Bowtie2/TopHat2 alignment in systemPipeR) is too slow or unsuitable and you need to swap in an alternative command-line aligner by editing its parameter files and re-running the affected step.
skills.name: command-line-tool-parameterization
skills.search_text: command-line-tool-parameterization Use when an existing NGS workflow's default tool (e.g. Bowtie2/TopHat2 alignment in systemPipeR) is too slow or unsuitable and you need to swap in an alternative command-line aligner by editing its parameter files and re-running the affected step. The analysis goal is not tool substitution or benchmarking — e.g. the default Bowtie2/TopHat2 configuration already meets runtime and quality requirements The input is not FASTQ short-read data routed through a systemPipeR (or equivalent parameter-file-driven) workflow, since the parameter-editing approach depends on that configuration structure Only the downstream statistical steps (e.g. differential expression) need changes and the alignment step is untouched http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Rewire and parameterize external command-line tools (e.g. swapping the default Bowtie2/TopHat2 alignment step of a systemPipeR RNA-Seq workflow to HISAT2 or Rsubread) by editing the workflow's parameter/configuration files, then execute and benchmark the modified step to compare wall-clock runtime against the published baseline. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1241-0
skills.summary: Rewire and parameterize external command-line tools (e.g. swapping the default Bowtie2/TopHat2 alignment step of a systemPipeR RNA-Seq workflow to HISAT2 or Rsubread) by editing the workflow's parameter/configuration files, then execute and benchmark the modified step to compare wall-clock runtime against the published baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is not tool substitution or benchmarking — e.g. the default Bowtie2/TopHat2 configuration already meets runtime and quality requirements The input is not FASTQ short-read data routed through a systemPipeR (or equivalent parameter-file-driven) workflow, since the parameter-editing approach depends on that configuration structure Only the downstream statistical steps (e.g. differential expression) need changes and the alignment step is untouched

skills.description: Use when a pairwise Hi-C comparison (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb bins) yields dcHiC significance calls and each significant bin must be labeled as A->B flip, B->A flip, or within-compartment change, with flip fractions and HOMER concordance tallied.
skills.name: compartment-flip-annotation-genomic-bins
skills.search_text: compartment-flip-annotation-genomic-bins Use when a pairwise Hi-C comparison (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb bins) yields dcHiC significance calls and each significant bin must be labeled as A->B flip, B->A flip, or within-compartment change, with flip fractions and HOMER concordance tallied. Analysis of a single contact map with no comparative condition — no differential call or flip can be defined; use standard PCA-based compartment calling instead Pseudo-bulk single-cell Hi-C with far fewer than ~80–100 cells per condition, where compartment identification is unreliable due to map sparsity When the goal is significance of individual chromatin interactions rather than compartmentalization changes — that is Fit-Hi-C's differential interaction domain, not bin-level flip annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Annotates dcHiC's significant differential compartment bins (100 kb, FDR < 0.1) in a pairwise mouse ESC vs NPC Hi-C comparison as A->B flips, B->A flips, or within-compartment changes, then cross-checks them against HOMER's 3,042 differential bins (1,355 overlapping with ±1 bin slack). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Annotates dcHiC's significant differential compartment bins (100 kb, FDR < 0.1) in a pairwise mouse ESC vs NPC Hi-C comparison as A->B flips, B->A flips, or within-compartment changes, then cross-checks them against HOMER's 3,042 differential bins (1,355 overlapping with ±1 bin slack).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analysis of a single contact map with no comparative condition — no differential call or flip can be defined; use standard PCA-based compartment calling instead Pseudo-bulk single-cell Hi-C with far fewer than ~80–100 cells per condition, where compartment identification is unreliable due to map sparsity When the goal is significance of individual chromatin interactions rather than compartmentalization changes — that is Fit-Hi-C's differential interaction domain, not bin-level flip annotation

skills.description: Use when a Hi-C dataset (real or simulated from known models) has been deconvolved by CscoreTool-M and each inferred sub-compartment must be assigned to, or validated against, a reference cell-type or model parameter set.
skills.name: compartment-score-parameter-correlation
skills.search_text: compartment-score-parameter-correlation Use when a Hi-C dataset (real or simulated from known models) has been deconvolved by CscoreTool-M and each inferred sub-compartment must be assigned to, or validated against, a reference cell-type or model parameter set. Input is a single homogeneous cell-type Hi-C dataset with no reference model parameters to correlate against — the correlation step has nothing to validate against You need de novo sub-compartment inference itself rather than validation of already-inferred sub-compartments (run the CscoreTool-M executable first) The Hi-C interactions have not been processed by CscoreTool-M (no _cscore.txt output exists) http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Validates CscoreTool-M sub-compartment inference by correlating each inferred sub-compartment's Cscore profile (from XXX_cscore.txt) against the reference model parameters used to generate or characterize the data, e.g. separating GM12878-like from IMR90-like sub-compartments in a mixed-population simulation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Validates CscoreTool-M sub-compartment inference by correlating each inferred sub-compartment's Cscore profile (from XXX_cscore.txt) against the reference model parameters used to generate or characterize the data, e.g. separating GM12878-like from IMR90-like sub-compartments in a mixed-population simulation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single homogeneous cell-type Hi-C dataset with no reference model parameters to correlate against — the correlation step has nothing to validate against You need de novo sub-compartment inference itself rather than validation of already-inferred sub-compartments (run the CscoreTool-M executable first) The Hi-C interactions have not been processed by CscoreTool-M (no _cscore.txt output exists)

skills.description: Use when you have compartment (PCA) scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered time points or developmental stages and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare transitions one at a time.
skills.name: compartment-score-time-series-clustering
skills.search_text: compartment-score-time-series-clustering Use when you have compartment (PCA) scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered time points or developmental stages and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare transitions one at a time. You only have two Hi-C conditions/time points — use dcHiC's pairwise differential compartment testing (Mahalanobis distance with chi-square significance) instead of time-series clustering Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized across datasets, so score scales are not comparable and z-transformed trajectories would be confounded by batch/scale differences The goal is calling significant differential compartments or differential interactions rather than grouping bins by temporal trajectory http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Groups genomic bins by how their dcHiC-derived, quantile-normalized compartment scores evolve across a multi-point time course, using z-transformation followed by TCseq time-series clustering. This enables simultaneous analysis of compartmentalization dynamics across all stages rather than pairwise transition comparisons. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Groups genomic bins by how their dcHiC-derived, quantile-normalized compartment scores evolve across a multi-point time course, using z-transformation followed by TCseq time-series clustering. This enables simultaneous analysis of compartmentalization dynamics across all stages rather than pairwise transition comparisons.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have two Hi-C conditions/time points — use dcHiC's pairwise differential compartment testing (Mahalanobis distance with chi-square significance) instead of time-series clustering Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized across datasets, so score scales are not comparable and z-transformed trajectories would be confounded by batch/scale differences The goal is calling significant differential compartments or differential interactions rather than grouping bins by temporal trajectory

skills.description: Use when comparing nucleosome positioning around +1 dyads between two conditions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium) for gene groups defined by RNA-seq response, using RoboCOP_MNase dyad probabilities.
skills.name: composite-dyad-probability-plotting
skills.search_text: composite-dyad-probability-plotting Use when comparing nucleosome positioning around +1 dyads between two conditions (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium) for gene groups defined by RNA-seq response, using RoboCOP_MNase dyad probabilities. Only a single condition/timepoint is available, so no between-timepoint dyad shift can be computed The analysis goal is TF occupancy or DBF footprinting rather than nucleosome dyad positioning at promoters Input is ATAC-seq rather than MNase-seq when the goal is replicating this cadmium-stress nucleosome result (MNase-seq gave markedly better RoboCOP performance in the paper) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Generates composite +1 nucleosome dyad probability distributions aligned across promoter sets (e.g., top 100 up-, down-regulated, or constant genes under cadmium stress) from RoboCOP_MNase timepoint-specific occupancy profiles, to reveal NDR expansion or contraction between conditions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Generates composite +1 nucleosome dyad probability distributions aligned across promoter sets (e.g., top 100 up-, down-regulated, or constant genes under cadmium stress) from RoboCOP_MNase timepoint-specific occupancy profiles, to reveal NDR expansion or contraction between conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single condition/timepoint is available, so no between-timepoint dyad shift can be computed The analysis goal is TF occupancy or DBF footprinting rather than nucleosome dyad positioning at promoters Input is ATAC-seq rather than MNase-seq when the goal is replicating this cadmium-stress nucleosome result (MNase-seq gave markedly better RoboCOP performance in the paper)

skills.description: Use when you must quantify how compute cost scales with Hi-C matrix resolution for a TAD-calling method, and demonstrate that chromosome-parallel execution reduces total runtime for a fixed cell line and parameter set.
skills.name: computation-runtime-benchmarking
skills.search_text: computation-runtime-benchmarking Use when you must quantify how compute cost scales with Hi-C matrix resolution for a TAD-calling method, and demonstrate that chromosome-parallel execution reduces total runtime for a fixed cell line and parameter set. The goal is to benchmark TAD-calling accuracy (e.g., FMS or boundary anchoring ratios) rather than compute time — this skill measures runtime only. The input is a simulated or toy Hi-C matrix (e.g., Forcato et al. or Trussart et al. datasets) where the paper's resolution-scaling runtime claims do not apply. The matrix is a single small chromosome where sequential vs parallel timing differences are trivially small and uninformative. Benchmark the sequential versus parallel wall-clock runtime of the TOAST TAD-calling pipeline (GAE + HDBSCAN) on GM12878 Hi-C contact matrices at 50 Kb, 25 Kb, and 5 Kb resolutions, reproducing the reported 2 h / 4 h / 11 h sequential times and ~0.5 h parallel time. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Benchmark the sequential versus parallel wall-clock runtime of the TOAST TAD-calling pipeline (GAE + HDBSCAN) on GM12878 Hi-C contact matrices at 50 Kb, 25 Kb, and 5 Kb resolutions, reproducing the reported 2 h / 4 h / 11 h sequential times and ~0.5 h parallel time.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to benchmark TAD-calling accuracy (e.g., FMS or boundary anchoring ratios) rather than compute time — this skill measures runtime only. The input is a simulated or toy Hi-C matrix (e.g., Forcato et al. or Trussart et al. datasets) where the paper's resolution-scaling runtime claims do not apply. The matrix is a single small chromosome where sequential vs parallel timing differences are trivially small and uninformative.

skills.description: Use when quantifying how much time a workflow management system itself adds on top of the real task runtimes, e.g. when validating that adopting a WMS does not inflate analysis wall time.
skills.name: computational-performance-reporting
skills.search_text: computational-performance-reporting Use when quantifying how much time a workflow management system itself adds on top of the real task runtimes, e.g. when validating that adopting a WMS does not inflate analysis wall time. The goal is to profile the runtime of the individual analysis tasks themselves rather than the overhead added by the workflow management system The workflows under test cannot be expressed identically in both Watchdog XML and Snakemake rules, so wall-time comparisons would not be attributable to the WMS Only a single sample count is available, so the trend of negligible overhead across the sample-count range cannot be assessed http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark and report the computational overhead of a workflow management system (Watchdog or Snakemake) by comparing total wall-clock execution time against the summed runtime of the actual executed tasks, demonstrating that WMS overhead is negligible relative to task runtime. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2107-4
skills.summary: Benchmark and report the computational overhead of a workflow management system (Watchdog or Snakemake) by comparing total wall-clock execution time against the summed runtime of the actual executed tasks, demonstrating that WMS overhead is negligible relative to task runtime.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to profile the runtime of the individual analysis tasks themselves rather than the overhead added by the workflow management system The workflows under test cannot be expressed identically in both Watchdog XML and Snakemake rules, so wall-time comparisons would not be attributable to the WMS Only a single sample count is available, so the trend of negligible overhead across the sample-count range cannot be assessed

skills.description: Use when validating that a fast analytic estimator matches slower simulation-based alternatives and you must quantify the computational cost trade-off (wall-clock time and peak memory) alongside accuracy.
skills.name: computational-resource-benchmarking-runtime-memory
skills.search_text: computational-resource-benchmarking-runtime-memory Use when validating that a fast analytic estimator matches slower simulation-based alternatives and you must quantify the computational cost trade-off (wall-clock time and peak memory) alongside accuracy. When the analytic method and the simulation-based alternatives estimate fundamentally different quantities — benchmark agreement is only meaningful if the same outputs (expected expressed genes, DE power, overall power) are derivable from all tools When the target design exceeds the pilot data scale (e.g. hundreds of samples for eQTL studies) — the article notes such data sets 'will be very difficult to simulate', so the simulation arm of the benchmark is infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmarks competing computational methods not only on output agreement (here, power estimates from scPower vs simulation-based powsimR and muscat) but also on runtime and peak memory, exposing the orders-of-magnitude cost gap that motivates analytic approaches. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks competing computational methods not only on output agreement (here, power estimates from scPower vs simulation-based powsimR and muscat) but also on runtime and peak memory, exposing the orders-of-magnitude cost gap that motivates analytic approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analytic method and the simulation-based alternatives estimate fundamentally different quantities — benchmark agreement is only meaningful if the same outputs (expected expressed genes, DE power, overall power) are derivable from all tools When the target design exceeds the pilot data scale (e.g. hundreds of samples for eQTL studies) — the article notes such data sets 'will be very difficult to simulate', so the simulation arm of the benchmark is infeasible

skills.description: Use when comparing the speed, memory footprint, mapping efficiency, or accuracy of methylation read-alignment tools (e.g., Msuite vs. Bismark vs. BWA-meth) on a controlled read set.
skills.name: computational-resource-profiling
skills.search_text: computational-resource-profiling Use when comparing the speed, memory footprint, mapping efficiency, or accuracy of methylation read-alignment tools (e.g., Msuite vs. Bismark vs. BWA-meth) on a controlled read set. The goal is methylation calling or biological interpretation rather than comparing tool performance — this skill only profiles computational metrics and mapping statistics. Input is real clinical/experimental data where ground-truth mapping accuracy cannot be computed; simulated reads with known origins are needed for the accuracy column. The aligner is not methylation-aware (plain BWA/STAR): the TAPS/BS conversion modes (-3/-4, -m TAPS/BS) and the comparison framing do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Benchmarking skill for comparing alignment/tool performance on identical in-silico datasets: it measures mapping efficiency, mapping accuracy, total running time, and peak memory usage per tool/mode (e.g., Msuite 3- and 4-letter modes vs. Bismark v0.22.3 and BWA-meth v0.2.2 on simulated TAPS reads). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Benchmarking skill for comparing alignment/tool performance on identical in-silico datasets: it measures mapping efficiency, mapping accuracy, total running time, and peak memory usage per tool/mode (e.g., Msuite 3- and 4-letter modes vs. Bismark v0.22.3 and BWA-meth v0.2.2 on simulated TAPS reads).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is methylation calling or biological interpretation rather than comparing tool performance — this skill only profiles computational metrics and mapping statistics. Input is real clinical/experimental data where ground-truth mapping accuracy cannot be computed; simulated reads with known origins are needed for the accuracy column. The aligner is not methylation-aware (plain BWA/STAR): the TAPS/BS conversion modes (-3/-4, -m TAPS/BS) and the comparison framing do not apply.

skills.description: Use when building an automated ChIPseq/RNAseq mapping step where samples in a project must be routed to bwa, bowtie, or Tophat according to the experiment type recorded per sample.
skills.name: conditional-aligner-dispatch-by-experiment-type
skills.search_text: conditional-aligner-dispatch-by-experiment-type Use when building an automated ChIPseq/RNAseq mapping step where samples in a project must be routed to bwa, bowtie, or Tophat according to the experiment type recorded per sample. The data are single-cell or long-read reads for which bwa/bowtie/Tophat are not the intended aligners The sample is not a ChIPseq or RNAseq library, since the experiment-type dispatch is defined only for those two NEAT pipeline types Reads are already aligned (e.g. BAM input), as this skill maps raw fastq files listed in Targets.txt http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Implements NEAT's read-alignment logic in which the 'map' module dispatches each sample to a different aligner based on its experiment type: bwa or bowtie for ChIPseq FASTQ reads and the bowtie-based Tophat for RNAseq, reading all parameters from AdvancedSettings.txt and Targets.txt. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Implements NEAT's read-alignment logic in which the 'map' module dispatches each sample to a different aligner based on its experiment type: bwa or bowtie for ChIPseq FASTQ reads and the bowtie-based Tophat for RNAseq, reading all parameters from AdvancedSettings.txt and Targets.txt.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are single-cell or long-read reads for which bwa/bowtie/Tophat are not the intended aligners The sample is not a ChIPseq or RNAseq library, since the experiment-type dispatch is defined only for those two NEAT pipeline types Reads are already aligned (e.g. BAM input), as this skill maps raw fastq files listed in Targets.txt

skills.description: Use when inferring whether transcriptional regulators (TRs) are associated with drug response from pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, pharmacology profiles) plus ChIP-seq-derived target information, and naive mRNA-level correlation would be confounded by copy number or mutations.
skills.name: confounder-adjusted-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: confounder-adjusted-correlation-analysis Use when inferring whether transcriptional regulators (TRs) are associated with drug response from pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, pharmacology profiles) plus ChIP-seq-derived target information, and naive mRNA-level correlation would be confounded by copy number or mutations. No reliable ChIP-seq target information is available, or ChIP-seq data have too few targets — RePhine would mislead TR identification since it identifies TRs through their targets The goal is to detect secondary/acquired resistance arising from post-treatment events (e.g. acquired STAT3 activation under erlotinib), which RePhine cannot detect due to lack of post-treatment data in CCLE The question is causal mechanism rather than association — the detected TR–drug relationships may not be causal and require knockout/activation validation http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 RePhine's regression-based strategy for measuring gene–drug response correlations while removing confounding effects (CNVs, kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations, cancer type), used to identify transcriptional regulators associated with drug response from CCLE pharmacogenomic and ENCODE ChIP-seq data. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: RePhine's regression-based strategy for measuring gene–drug response correlations while removing confounding effects (CNVs, kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations, cancer type), used to identify transcriptional regulators associated with drug response from CCLE pharmacogenomic and ENCODE ChIP-seq data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable ChIP-seq target information is available, or ChIP-seq data have too few targets — RePhine would mislead TR identification since it identifies TRs through their targets The goal is to detect secondary/acquired resistance arising from post-treatment events (e.g. acquired STAT3 activation under erlotinib), which RePhine cannot detect due to lack of post-treatment data in CCLE The question is causal mechanism rather than association — the detected TR–drug relationships may not be causal and require knockout/activation validation

skills.description: Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. randomForest RFT for enhancer vs. non-enhancer elements) must be validated on held-out test classes and its accuracy quantified via a confusion matrix.
skills.name: confusion-matrix-model-evaluation
skills.search_text: confusion-matrix-model-evaluation Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. randomForest RFT for enhancer vs. non-enhancer elements) must be validated on held-out test classes and its accuracy quantified via a confusion matrix. You only have a single pooled dataset with no held-out class-balanced test split — accuracy on training data would be inflated and the 93% criterion does not apply. The classification task is multi-class or the goal is class-specific metrics (precision/recall per class) beyond the binary enhancer/non-enhancer accuracy reported here. Input is raw NGS signal (bedGraph/RPM tracks) that has not yet been converted into per-element average coverage features for the classifier. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Evaluates a trained binary classifier (e.g. CIPHER's random-forest enhancer predictor) by scoring it on a held-out test set and computing accuracy from a confusion matrix, accepting performance slightly above 93%. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1
skills.summary: Evaluates a trained binary classifier (e.g. CIPHER's random-forest enhancer predictor) by scoring it on a held-out test set and computing accuracy from a confusion matrix, accepting performance slightly above 93%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a single pooled dataset with no held-out class-balanced test split — accuracy on training data would be inflated and the 93% criterion does not apply. The classification task is multi-class or the goal is class-specific metrics (precision/recall per class) beyond the binary enhancer/non-enhancer accuracy reported here. Input is raw NGS signal (bedGraph/RPM tracks) that has not yet been converted into per-element average coverage features for the classifier.

skills.description: Use when peak-calling Calling Cards (CC) insertions from a qbed dataset and you need candidate TF binding regions formed by merging windows that are consecutively enriched in experimental over background insertions, as in the MACCs algorithm.
skills.name: consecutive-enriched-window-merging
skills.search_text: consecutive-enriched-window-merging Use when peak-calling Calling Cards (CC) insertions from a qbed dataset and you need candidate TF binding regions formed by merging windows that are consecutively enriched in experimental over background insertions, as in the MACCs algorithm. Input is already a called-peak BED/peak file rather than raw qbed insertions — use annotation or filter_peaks instead of re-calling Analysis goal is differential peak analysis or motif calling on existing peaks (Tools (tl) stage), not candidate-region discovery Data is gene-expression or ChIP-seq signal being compared against CC peaks rather than CC insertion data itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 The window-scan candidate-peak stage of the MACCs peak caller in Pycallingcards: scan a qbed insertion dataset with a fixed window and step size, mark windows enriched in experimental over background insertions, and merge consecutively enriched windows into candidate CC peak regions whose centers are then Poisson-tested with TTAA-site density correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: The window-scan candidate-peak stage of the MACCs peak caller in Pycallingcards: scan a qbed insertion dataset with a fixed window and step size, mark windows enriched in experimental over background insertions, and merge consecutively enriched windows into candidate CC peak regions whose centers are then Poisson-tested with TTAA-site density correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a called-peak BED/peak file rather than raw qbed insertions — use annotation or filter_peaks instead of re-calling Analysis goal is differential peak analysis or motif calling on existing peaks (Tools (tl) stage), not candidate-region discovery Data is gene-expression or ChIP-seq signal being compared against CC peaks rather than CC insertion data itself

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a novel clustering method against consensus clustering on the same gene expression matrix, or when you need to quantify cluster-solution agreement (e.g., Jaccard Pair Similarity per K) between two cluster assignments on shared samples.
skills.name: consensus-clustering-analysis
skills.search_text: consensus-clustering-analysis Use when benchmarking a novel clustering method against consensus clustering on the same gene expression matrix, or when you need to quantify cluster-solution agreement (e.g., Jaccard Pair Similarity per K) between two cluster assignments on shared samples. When the goal is subtype discovery without a predefined K — consensus/bootstrap clustering requires a predefined parameter, K, which is a stated limitation for subtype discovery When the reference method comparison is unnecessary and you only need cluster assignments — consensus clustering is a benchmarking comparator here, not the primary method being evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Runs consensus clustering on the log2-transformed, median-centered TCGA-LUAD expression matrix (434 samples, >25000 transcripts) using hierarchical clustering with ward's linkage on Pearson correlation distances, 2000 iterations, and 70% resampling of items and features, then scores similarity to a reference (SRIQ) solution via a Jaccard-based Pair Similarity score. This is the benchmarking standard against which SRIQ's K3 and K6 solutions were evaluated. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: Runs consensus clustering on the log2-transformed, median-centered TCGA-LUAD expression matrix (434 samples, >25000 transcripts) using hierarchical clustering with ward's linkage on Pearson correlation distances, 2000 iterations, and 70% resampling of items and features, then scores similarity to a reference (SRIQ) solution via a Jaccard-based Pair Similarity score. skills.search_text: contingency-table-probability-estimation Use when a set of candidate motifs (or features) has already been ranked by a score such as mutual information and each candidate has a 2x2 contingency table of counts in a positive and a negative dataset that must be tested for over-representation with multiple-comparison control. This is DiNAMO's final filtering step after mutual-information-based motif selection.

skills.search_text: count-matrix-read-count-normalization Reference for converting a raw single-cell genomic bin/peak count matrix into a filtered, normalized matrix prior to PCA/clustering, when cell coverage varies and sparse outlier cells or regions must be removed. skills.search_text: coverage-based-hic-normalization Use when Hi-C or capture Hi-C replicate contact maps must be bias-corrected before reproducibility assessment, or when comparing how normalization methods hold up as sequencing depth is downsampled to 15%-50%. Input is already normalized or is a matrix-format .hic contact map rather than a fragment-pair feature table with coverage columns The target is promoter-centered capture Hi-C PO-interaction normalization with distinct thresholds (promoter side 200, other side 50) and 15 kb-2 Mb interaction selection, which requires the pcHi-C variant of the workflow No replicate data exist to compute a reproducibility score against http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Normalize Hi-C contact maps for fragment-coverage biases using covNorm's negative binomial GLM (log(u) = beta0 + beta1*C_frag1 + beta2*C_frag2), then quantify reproducibility across biological replicates with the HiC-spector score, including robustness under downsampling to 15%-50% of sequencing depth. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Normalize Hi-C contact maps for fragment-coverage biases using covNorm's negative binomial GLM (log(u) = beta0 + beta1*C_frag1 + beta2*C_frag2), then quantify reproducibility across biological replicates with the HiC-spector score, including robustness under downsampling to 15%-50% of sequencing depth.

skills.description: Use when aligning reads from bisulfite-free methylation protocols (TAPS, 5hmC-CATCH, ATAC-me) where CpH methylation is very low, and full 3-letter C-to-T conversion would destroy strand-discriminating information.
skills.name: cpg-context-cytosine-conversion
skills.search_text: cpg-context-cytosine-conversion Use when aligning reads from bisulfite-free methylation protocols (TAPS, 5hmC-CATCH, ATAC-me) where CpH methylation is very low, and full 3-letter C-to-T conversion would destroy strand-discriminating information. Data generated with BS-seq (bisulfite) protocols — the README mandates 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode does not support it Samples with appreciable non-CpG methylation (e.g., plant or embryonic tissues) — 4-letter mode assumes non-CpG methylation is very low, as in most human somatic tissues General-purpose alignment where no cytosine-conversion semantics are needed — plain bowtie2 should be used instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Implements Msuite's 4-letter alignment-mode conversion, in which only CpG-context cytosines (not CpH) are converted to thymines in both the reference genome and sequencing reads, preserving enough sequence information to align bisulfite-free (e.g., TAPS) reads without the 3-letter all-C-to-T collapse. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Implements Msuite's 4-letter alignment-mode conversion, in which only CpG-context cytosines (not CpH) are converted to thymines in both the reference genome and sequencing reads, preserving enough sequence information to align bisulfite-free (e.g., TAPS) reads without the 3-letter all-C-to-T collapse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data generated with BS-seq (bisulfite) protocols — the README mandates 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode does not support it Samples with appreciable non-CpG methylation (e.g., plant or embryonic tissues) — 4-letter mode assumes non-CpG methylation is very low, as in most human somatic tissues General-purpose alignment where no cytosine-conversion semantics are needed — plain bowtie2 should be used instead

skills.description: Use when quantifying methylation from cfMeDIP-seq (MeDIP-seq) enrichment data — e.g. duplicate-filtered BAM files after alignment/QC — where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among relative, absolute, or strand-aware methylation estimates is needed.
skills.name: cpg-density-bias-correction
skills.search_text: cpg-density-bias-correction Use when quantifying methylation from cfMeDIP-seq (MeDIP-seq) enrichment data — e.g. duplicate-filtered BAM files after alignment/QC — where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among relative, absolute, or strand-aware methylation estimates is needed. Input is bisulfite or enzymatic methyl-seq (WGBS/EM-seq) data, where methylation is called directly from conversion rather than enrichment and no CpG-density-bias correction model is needed BAM files have not yet passed the upstream alignment and duplicate-filtering QC steps of the pipeline Read depth is insufficient for MEDStrand's sigmoid fit, leaving only MEDIPS and QSEA as viable normalization options http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 This skill reconstructs MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module, which corrects CpG-density bias in enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data using three alternative normalization models — MEDIPS (linear regression, relative methylation), QSEA (sigmoidal model with empirical knowledge, absolute methylation), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model, strand-aware absolute methylation). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: This skill reconstructs MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module, which corrects CpG-density bias in enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data using three alternative normalization models — MEDIPS (linear regression, relative methylation), QSEA (sigmoidal model with empirical knowledge, absolute methylation), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model, strand-aware absolute methylation).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bisulfite or enzymatic methyl-seq (WGBS/EM-seq) data, where methylation is called directly from conversion rather than enrichment and no CpG-density-bias correction model is needed BAM files have not yet passed the upstream alignment and duplicate-filtering QC steps of the pipeline Read depth is insufficient for MEDStrand's sigmoid fit, leaving only MEDIPS and QSEA as viable normalization options

skills.description: Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP trace files (.ab1) must have their cytosine/CpG positions converted to genomic coordinates from a reference .fasta template, as in ABSP individual sample methylation analysis.
skills.name: cpg-dinucleotide-coordinate-annotation
skills.search_text: cpg-dinucleotide-coordinate-annotation Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP trace files (.ab1) must have their cytosine/CpG positions converted to genomic coordinates from a reference .fasta template, as in ABSP individual sample methylation analysis. Input is high-throughput bisulfite sequencing (FASTQ/aligner-based) data rather than .ab1 trace files from BSP PCR products Only CpG-numbered or relative positions are needed and no genomic coordinate annotation is required (ABSP can label by 'CpG numbers' or 'None' in Grouped Analysis) The reference sequence has no real genomic location and arbitrary coordinates were assigned — then the computed coordinates must not be interpreted as genomic http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Annotates cytosines in bisulfite sequencing PCR reads with genomic CpG coordinates by local pair-wise alignment of each trimmed .ab1 read against the reference DNA template, using the alignment offset formula (read position = template position − Sstart + Pstart). This lets ABSP report methylation percentages at genomic coordinates rather than read-local positions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: Annotates cytosines in bisulfite sequencing PCR reads with genomic CpG coordinates by local pair-wise alignment of each trimmed .ab1 read against the reference DNA template, using the alignment offset formula (read position = template position − Sstart + Pstart). This lets ABSP report methylation percentages at genomic coordinates rather than read-local positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is high-throughput bisulfite sequencing (FASTQ/aligner-based) data rather than .ab1 trace files from BSP PCR products Only CpG-numbered or relative positions are needed and no genomic coordinate annotation is required (ABSP can label by 'CpG numbers' or 'None' in Grouped Analysis) The reference sequence has no real genomic location and arbitrary coordinates were assigned — then the computed coordinates must not be interpreted as genomic

skills.search_text: cpg-distance-binned-correlation-analysis Use when you need to characterize how correlation between adjacent DNA methylation p-values decays with genomic distance, e.g. to justify correlation-aware p-value combination in SMITE or reproduce its Figure 2 correlation analysis. The p-values are independent across sites, so a correlation correction is unnecessary The data are not methylation p-values assayed at genomic coordinates (no distance binning possible) You only need combined gene-level p-values without characterizing the underlying CpG correlation structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Estimates the distance-dependent correlation structure of CpG methylation p-values using SMITE's annotateModification with mod_corr=TRUE and Monte Carlo resampling of combined scores, then tabulates and plots average Pearson correlation across 500 genomic distance bins for the T. gondii HFF dataset. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Estimates the distance-dependent correlation structure of CpG methylation p-values using SMITE's annotateModification with mod_corr=TRUE and Monte Carlo resampling of combined scores, then tabulates and plots average Pearson correlation across 500 genomic distance bins for the T. gondii HFF dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values are independent across sites, so a correlation correction is unnecessary The data are not methylation p-values assayed at genomic coordinates (no distance binning possible) You only need combined gene-level p-values without characterizing the underlying CpG correlation structure

skills.search_text: cpg-island-annotation-enrichment-analysis Use when interpreting top-value-method-selected CpG probes from an Illumina 450K methylation matrix (e.g. cola SD vs ATC top probes) by CpG-island association category, to judge whether features capture local or global methylation patterns. The input is expression or single-cell RNA-Seq data (e.g. Golub leukemia, HSMM, recount2 datasets) where rows are genes rather than CpG probes — CpG-island categories do not apply Probes have not been filtered and preprocessed first (sex-chromosome/SNP-overlapping probes removed, low-variance rows dropped), since unfiltered probe sets confound the enrichment comparison You need subtype classification itself rather than interpretation of which features were selected — use cola's run_all_consensus_partitions() instead Annotates top-ranked CpG probes from methylation array feature selection (e.g. cola SD- vs ATC-selected probes on the Illumina 450K GBM dataset GSE36278) with CpG-island association categories and compares enrichment fractions to interpret whether selected features reflect local CpG-island structure or global methylation changes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146

skills.description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing FASTA reads (e.g. DDO1/DAO amplicons from PRJEB28662) must be quality-filtered prior to epiallele-frequency or methylated-core extraction with ampliMethProfiler or MethCoresProfiler.
skills.name: cpg-methylation-read-quality-filtering
skills.search_text: cpg-methylation-read-quality-filtering Use when bisulfite-sequencing FASTA reads (e.g. DDO1/DAO amplicons from PRJEB28662) must be quality-filtered prior to epiallele-frequency or methylated-core extraction with ampliMethProfiler or MethCoresProfiler. The input is already a table of epiallele configurations or MethCoresProfiler output (Tab_Epialleles / ComposCore) — filtering has already been applied upstream. The data are not bisulfite-sequencing reads of targeted CpG-containing amplicons (e.g. single-CpG methylation arrays), where per-molecule phased configurations are unavailable. skills.summary: Applies the ampliMethProfiler read-quality filter chain (length ±50% of reference, ≥80% primer similarity, ≥98% bisulfite efficiency, ≥60% base alignment, removal of ambiguous CpG calls) before extracting single-molecule mCpG configurations from bisulfite sequencing reads, so that downstream epiallele and methylated-core frequency estimates are not corrupted by low-confidence methylation calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a table of epiallele configurations or MethCoresProfiler output (Tab_Epialleles / ComposCore) — filtering has already been applied upstream.
