skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-platform peak set with no comparable alternative-assay region set — use standard peak-calling QC instead No expected motif or motif-family database is available for the assayed transcription factor, since the comparison relies on enriching the known TF motif family The goal is peak-coordinate overlap (Jaccard/intersection) rather than biological signal-quality comparison — a direct interval-overlap tool is more appropriate

skills.description: Use when multiple shotgun libraries of the same synthetic or mixed microbial community (e.g. RIMS-seq +3H, DNA-seq, bisulfite-seq) have been mapped to the same reference and you need to check whether protocol choice distorts species relative abundances.
skills.name: cross-protocol-abundance-ratio-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-protocol-abundance-ratio-analysis Use when multiple shotgun libraries of the same synthetic or mixed microbial community (e.g. RIMS-seq +3H, DNA-seq, bisulfite-seq) have been mapped to the same reference and you need to check whether protocol choice distorts species relative abundances. The goal is de novo methylase specificity/motif discovery from RIMS-seq reads (use the mapping.pl -> split_mapped_reads.pl -> get_motif_all.pl/MoSDi pipeline instead) Libraries are not mapped to the same reference genomes with BWA-mem, so per-species counts across protocols are not comparable and ratios would be meaningless Assessing sequencing quality (coverage, GC content, mapping rate) rather than abundance bias between protocols http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Quantifies per-species relative abundances from BWA-mem-mapped read counts of RIMS-seq, DNA-seq and bisulfite-seq libraries of the ATCC MSA-1005/1006 synthetic microbiomes, and computes pairwise protocol-to-DNA-seq abundance ratios to test whether a sequencing chemistry biases AT-rich species. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Quantifies per-species relative abundances from BWA-mem-mapped read counts of RIMS-seq, DNA-seq and bisulfite-seq libraries of the ATCC MSA-1005/1006 synthetic microbiomes, and computes pairwise protocol-to-DNA-seq abundance ratios to test whether a sequencing chemistry biases AT-rich species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo methylase specificity/motif discovery from RIMS-seq reads (use the mapping.pl -> split_mapped_reads.pl -> get_motif_all.pl/MoSDi pipeline instead) Libraries are not mapped to the same reference genomes with BWA-mem, so per-species counts across protocols are not comparable and ratios would be meaningless Assessing sequencing quality (coverage, GC content, mapping rate) rather than abundance bias between protocols

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across ≥2 conditions with spike-in chromatin (e.g. drug titration series), especially when total-read normalization would mask a global occupancy reduction, and peak/background classification (MACS2 broad-peak BEDs) is available.
skills.name: cross-sample-chip-signal-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: cross-sample-chip-signal-distribution-analysis Use when comparing ChIP-seq signal across ≥2 conditions with spike-in chromatin (e.g. drug titration series), especially when total-read normalization would mask a global occupancy reduction, and peak/background classification (MACS2 broad-peak BEDs) is available. ChIP-seq experiments lack exogenous spike-in chromatin — the correction factor cannot be computed from spike-in material The question concerns only a pre-selected subset of loci rather than genome-wide signal comparison — spikChIP normalizes over the complete genome, not just selected regions No peak files (e.g. MACS2 broad-peak BEDs) are available for the experimental or spike-in genomes, since bin classification into peaks/background is required for the local regression http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Genome-wide comparison of ChIP-seq signal distributions across multiple experimental conditions using spikChIP's local regression spike-in normalization, which increasingly applies the spike-in correction factor from background to peak regions so that global occupancy changes (e.g. gradual H3K79me2 reduction across 0%–100% EPZ5676 mixtures) become detectable. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Genome-wide comparison of ChIP-seq signal distributions across multiple experimental conditions using spikChIP's local regression spike-in normalization, which increasingly applies the spike-in correction factor from background to peak regions so that global occupancy changes (e.g. gradual H3K79me2 reduction across 0%–100% EPZ5676 mixtures) become detectable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ChIP-seq experiments lack exogenous spike-in chromatin — the correction factor cannot be computed from spike-in material The question concerns only a pre-selected subset of loci rather than genome-wide signal comparison — spikChIP normalizes over the complete genome, not just selected regions No peak files (e.g. MACS2 broad-peak BEDs) are available for the experimental or spike-in genomes, since bin classification into peaks/background is required for the local regression

skills.description: Use when you have cell-type-annotated CRE BED intervals from two species sharing homologous cell types (e.g. seven adult heart cell types in human and mouse) and need to classify cell-type-specific regulatory sequences or assign single cells across species using motif-based models.
skills.name: cross-species-cell-type-assignment-from-motif-importance
skills.search_text: cross-species-cell-type-assignment-from-motif-importance Use when you have cell-type-annotated CRE BED intervals from two species sharing homologous cell types (e.g. seven adult heart cell types in human and mouse) and need to classify cell-type-specific regulatory sequences or assign single cells across species using motif-based models. Input is already a motif count or feature matrix — BOM's pipeline starts from genomic intervals and a BSgenome, so pre-computed features skip generateAllFasta/runFIMO and need a different path The task requires motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) information — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and integration with motif grammar is described as an important future direction Cell types are not shared/homologous between the training and target species, since the cross-species transfer relies on seven shared adult heart cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Train multiclass Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) gradient-boosted-tree models on TF motif counts from distal cis-regulatory elements of shared cell types in one species, then use SHAP-aggregated feature attributions to assign single cells to cell types in another species' heart, checking generalization against reported auROCs (0.90 human, 0.85 mouse) and assignment rates (83% overall). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Train multiclass Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) gradient-boosted-tree models on TF motif counts from distal cis-regulatory elements of shared cell types in one species, then use SHAP-aggregated feature attributions to assign single cells to cell types in another species' heart, checking generalization against reported auROCs (0.90 human, 0.85 mouse) and assignment rates (83% overall).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a motif count or feature matrix — BOM's pipeline starts from genomic intervals and a BSgenome, so pre-computed features skip generateAllFasta/runFIMO and need a different path The task requires motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) information — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and integration with motif grammar is described as an important future direction Cell types are not shared/homologous between the training and target species, since the cross-species transfer relies on seven shared adult heart cell types

skills.description: Use when orthologous non-coding regulatory elements (e.g., TF ChIP-seq peaks) must be lifted between species and naive chain-file liftOver suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate.
skills.name: cross-species-chip-seq-peak-liftover
skills.search_text: cross-species-chip-seq-peak-liftover Use when orthologous non-coding regulatory elements (e.g., TF ChIP-seq peaks) must be lifted between species and naive chain-file liftOver suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate. The input regions are coding sequences or whole-genome alignments, not non-coding regulatory intervals whose orthology depends on regulatory signal No orthologous epigenomic datasets exist for the species pair, and no matched data is available to train the logistic parameters via training_module The task is simple synteny/gene orthology mapping rather than functional orthologous regulatory element identification http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Maps TF ChIP-seq peak sets across species (e.g., mouse mm10 to human hg38) using AdaLiftOver, which extends query regions via the UCSC liftOver framework and prioritizes candidate target regions by epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarity, outperforming UCSC liftOver in precision and true-positive recovery. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Maps TF ChIP-seq peak sets across species (e.g., mouse mm10 to human hg38) using AdaLiftOver, which extends query regions via the UCSC liftOver framework and prioritizes candidate target regions by epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarity, outperforming UCSC liftOver in precision and true-positive recovery.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input regions are coding sequences or whole-genome alignments, not non-coding regulatory intervals whose orthology depends on regulatory signal No orthologous epigenomic datasets exist for the species pair, and no matched data is available to train the logistic parameters via training_module The task is simple synteny/gene orthology mapping rather than functional orthologous regulatory element identification

skills.description: Use when raw labeled FASTA sequences (e.g., the cross-species DNA 6mA benchmark of 2,768 positive / 2,716 negative 41-nt samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric k-mer frequency features for machine-learning classification.
skills.name: cross-species-dna-6ma-dataset-handling
skills.search_text: cross-species-dna-6ma-dataset-handling Use when raw labeled FASTA sequences (e.g., the cross-species DNA 6mA benchmark of 2,768 positive / 2,716 negative 41-nt samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric k-mer frequency features for machine-learning classification. Input is already a numeric feature matrix (e.g., precomputed matrix_motif or matrix_binary files) rather than raw FASTA sequences Sequences are not fixed-length DNA segments around 6mA sites (the csDMA cross-species samples are 41-nt); variable-length or non-DNA input breaks the window-count normalization The goal is classifier training rather than feature encoding — use csDMA_training.py or classifier_selection.py with the already-encoded matrices instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3318 Implements the csDMA K-mer pattern frequency encoding that converts 41-nt DNA 6mA candidate sequences into numerical feature vectors by computing relative frequencies of dinucleotide, trinucleotide, and tetranucleotide patterns (k=2,3,4 → 4^2+4^3+4^4 = 336 features per sample). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4
skills.summary: Implements the csDMA K-mer pattern frequency encoding that converts 41-nt DNA 6mA candidate sequences into numerical feature vectors by computing relative frequencies of dinucleotide, trinucleotide, and tetranucleotide patterns (k=2,3,4 → 4^2+4^3+4^4 = 336 features per sample).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature matrix (e.g., precomputed matrix_motif or matrix_binary files) rather than raw FASTA sequences Sequences are not fixed-length DNA segments around 6mA sites (the csDMA cross-species samples are 41-nt); variable-length or non-DNA input breaks the window-count normalization The goal is classifier training rather than feature encoding — use csDMA_training.py or classifier_selection.py with the already-encoded matrices instead

skills.description: Use when you have cell-type-specific CRE models trained in one species (e.g., mouse cardiomyocyte/erythroid) and want to classify homologous CREs from another species, or to test whether predictions depend on sequence alignment.
skills.name: cross-species-enhancer-classification-transfer
skills.search_text: cross-species-enhancer-classification-transfer Use when you have cell-type-specific CRE models trained in one species (e.g., mouse cardiomyocyte/erythroid) and want to classify homologous CREs from another species, or to test whether predictions depend on sequence alignment. The goal is within-species enhancer discovery from scratch rather than transferring an already-trained cross-species model — use the standard BOM training workflow (binModel) instead Input is already a motif-count feature table rather than genomic coordinates needing sequence extraction (generateAllFasta) and FIMO scanning The elements of interest depend on regulatory information beyond the input sequence window, since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Applies mouse-trained Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) models to classify homologous CREs from another species (e.g., human fetal cardiomyocyte and erythroblast elements), demonstrating that motif-count-based prediction transfers across species even when no detectable sequence alignment exists. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Applies mouse-trained Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) models to classify homologous CREs from another species (e.g., human fetal cardiomyocyte and erythroblast elements), demonstrating that motif-count-based prediction transfers across species even when no detectable sequence alignment exists.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is within-species enhancer discovery from scratch rather than transferring an already-trained cross-species model — use the standard BOM training workflow (binModel) instead Input is already a motif-count feature table rather than genomic coordinates needing sequence extraction (generateAllFasta) and FIMO scanning The elements of interest depend on regulatory information beyond the input sequence window, since BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence

skills.description: Use when mapping regulatory peaks (ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone yields multi-mappers or low precision, and matched orthologous epigenomic datasets are available for both species.
skills.name: cross-species-epigenomic-region-mapping
skills.search_text: cross-species-epigenomic-region-mapping Use when mapping regulatory peaks (ChIP-seq, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone yields multi-mappers or low precision, and matched orthologous epigenomic datasets are available for both species. No matched orthologous epigenomic datasets (TF/DNA methylation ChIP-seq or DNase-seq) exist in both species — epigenomic signal similarity cannot be computed and default parameters may not transfer. No UCSC chain file or BSgenome object is available for the species pair and genome builds in question. The goal is coding-sequence or whole-genome syntenic alignment rather than prioritizing orthologous non-coding regulatory elements. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3452 Cross-species identification of orthologous non-coding regulatory elements: query peaks are extended via the UCSC liftOver framework and candidate target regions are prioritized by aggregating epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarities into logistic probability scores. It counters the multi-mapping, low precision, and low mapping rate of sequence-only conservation methods. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Cross-species identification of orthologous non-coding regulatory elements: query peaks are extended via the UCSC liftOver framework and candidate target regions are prioritized by aggregating epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarities into logistic probability scores. It counters the multi-mapping, low precision, and low mapping rate of sequence-only conservation methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No matched orthologous epigenomic datasets (TF/DNA methylation ChIP-seq or DNase-seq) exist in both species — epigenomic signal similarity cannot be computed and default parameters may not transfer. No UCSC chain file or BSgenome object is available for the species pair and genome builds in question. The goal is coding-sequence or whole-genome syntenic alignment rather than prioritizing orthologous non-coding regulatory elements.

skills.description: Use when DRIP-seq IP/control raw data (with RNaseH-treated or mock controls) are available for cell lines and C. elegans, and the goal is to test whether HOT regions are enriched for R-loops relative to occupancy-matched control regions.
skills.name: cross-species-hot-region-comparison
skills.search_text: cross-species-hot-region-comparison Use when DRIP-seq IP/control raw data (with RNaseH-treated or mock controls) are available for cell lines and C. elegans, and the goal is to test whether HOT regions are enriched for R-loops relative to occupancy-matched control regions. The goal is defining HOT regions from ChIP-seq TF occupancy itself (peak calling/occupancy thresholding) rather than testing R-loop enrichment on pre-existing HOT region coordinates. No DRIP-seq IP data and no RNaseH-treated or mock control exist for the species/cell line in question, making log2(IP/control) enrichment uncomputable. The analysis targets ChIP-seq artifact properties (e.g., false positive signals in knocked-out TF ChIP-seq) rather than R-loop/RNA-DNA hybrid enrichment. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Quantifies R-loop (RNA-DNA hybrid) enrichment on high-occupancy target (HOT) regions via DRIP-seq log2(IP/control) signal across multiple cell lines and C. elegans, comparing HOT regions against occupancy-binned control region sets on equal footing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Quantifies R-loop (RNA-DNA hybrid) enrichment on high-occupancy target (HOT) regions via DRIP-seq log2(IP/control) signal across multiple cell lines and C. elegans, comparing HOT regions against occupancy-binned control region sets on equal footing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is defining HOT regions from ChIP-seq TF occupancy itself (peak calling/occupancy thresholding) rather than testing R-loop enrichment on pre-existing HOT region coordinates. No DRIP-seq IP data and no RNaseH-treated or mock control exist for the species/cell line in question, making log2(IP/control) enrichment uncomputable. skills.description: Use when narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files for multiple genomes (hg19, mm9, dm3, ce10) must be converted into HOT region BED tracks and per-species counts checked against published HOT-region numbers.

skills.search_text: cross-species-hot-region-count-validation Use when narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files for multiple genomes (hg19, mm9, dm3, ce10) must be converted into HOT region BED tracks and per-species counts checked against published HOT-region numbers. skills.summary: Reproduce high-occupancy target (HOT) region calls from ENCODE/modENCODE ChIP-seq narrowPeak files across human, mouse, D. melanogaster and C. elegans using a peak-summit density method with a 99th-percentile occupancy threshold, and validate species-level counts against the HOT-or-not paper (4324 human, 2638 mouse, 422 C. elegans, 408 D. melanogaster).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is functional interpretation of already-called HOT regions (e.g. GC/CpG k-mer, R-loop or G-quadruplex enrichment) rather than de novo calling and count validation from peak files. skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a cell-line specific model or a within-species integrative model — use train_specific.py or train_integrative1.py/train_integrative2.py instead, since train_integrative3.py is specific to training on one species and testing on another. skills.description: Use when you have csRNA-seq TSS calls and need score-continuum sequences centered on each TSS for positional motif enrichment analysis (MEPP) of core promoter elements such as Inr, TATA-box, and DPE.
skills.name: csrna-seq-tss-sequence-scoring
skills.search_text: csrna-seq-tss-sequence-scoring Use when you have csRNA-seq TSS calls and need score-continuum sequences centered on each TSS for positional motif enrichment analysis (MEPP) of core promoter elements such as Inr, TATA-box, and DPE. You need de novo motif discovery from the scored sequences — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library (e.g. the Ohler or HOMER motif files), so novel motifs cannot be assembled with this skill. Your sequences are not centered on an anchor point (e.g. TSS or motif) — the method requires centered genomic sequences to produce a positional profile relative to an anchor. You only have a binary (thresholded) high/low activity grouping rather than a continuous score — MEPP exploits a score continuum and would lose its main advantage if scores are collapsed to two classes. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Preparation of ±200 bp DNA sequences centered on high-confidence csRNA-seq transcription start sites (44,877 Drosophila TSSs), each scored with log-transformed csRNA-seq coverage, so that MEPP can compute position-dependent motif enrichment profiles relative to the TSS anchor point. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Preparation of ±200 bp DNA sequences centered on high-confidence csRNA-seq transcription start sites (44,877 Drosophila TSSs), each scored with log-transformed csRNA-seq coverage, so that MEPP can compute position-dependent motif enrichment profiles relative to the TSS anchor point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo motif discovery from the scored sequences — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library (e.g. the Ohler or HOMER motif files), so novel motifs cannot be assembled with this skill. Your sequences are not centered on an anchor point (e.g. TSS or motif) — the method requires centered genomic sequences to produce a positional profile relative to an anchor. You only have a binary (thresholded) high/low activity grouping rather than a continuous score — MEPP exploits a score continuum and would lose its main advantage if scores are collapsed to two classes.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DNA methylation aligners on reads from CT/GA-rich regions, or when stratifying human genome bins by CT/GA proportion (≥70%/≥80%) to compare 4-letter vs 3-letter mapping efficiency and accuracy.
skills.name: ct-ga-rich-region-sequence-selection
skills.search_text: ct-ga-rich-region-sequence-selection Use when benchmarking DNA methylation aligners on reads from CT/GA-rich regions, or when stratifying human genome bins by CT/GA proportion (≥70%/≥80%) to compare 4-letter vs 3-letter mapping efficiency and accuracy. Data generated with a BS-seq protocol — the README states you MUST use the 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low Samples with high non-CpG methylation (e.g., not most human somatic tissues), where the 4-letter mode's assumption does not hold The goal is methylation calling or visualization on real data rather than benchmarking aligner mapping performance on CT/GA-enriched regions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A benchmarking skill that stratifies human-genome 500-bp bins by CT/GA proportion (≥70% and ≥80%) and uses in silico TAPS-converted paired-end 36-bp reads from those bins to demonstrate that Msuite's unique 4-letter alignment mode outperforms 3-letter mode (Msuite, Bismark, BWA-meth) in mapping efficiency and accuracy. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that stratifies human-genome 500-bp bins by CT/GA proportion (≥70% and ≥80%) and uses in silico TAPS-converted paired-end 36-bp reads from those bins to demonstrate that Msuite's unique 4-letter alignment mode outperforms 3-letter mode (Msuite, Bismark, BWA-meth) in mapping efficiency and accuracy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data generated with a BS-seq protocol — the README states you MUST use the 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low Samples with high non-CpG methylation (e.g., not most human somatic tissues), where the 4-letter mode's assumption does not hold The goal is methylation calling or visualization on real data rather than benchmarking aligner mapping performance on CT/GA-enriched regions

skills.description: Use when fine-mapping a locus to decide which of several non-coding SNPs overlapping CTCF binding sites is the likely causal variant driving altered chromatin architecture or gene expression.
skills.name: ctcf-binding-site-variant-prioritization
skills.search_text: ctcf-binding-site-variant-prioritization Use when fine-mapping a locus to decide which of several non-coding SNPs overlapping CTCF binding sites is the likely causal variant driving altered chromatin architecture or gene expression. The question concerns large structural variants or element deletions rather than single base-pair SNPs — deepC's SNP scoring workflow here targets single nucleotide changes No tissue-specific trained deepC model is available for the relevant cell type, since transfer-learned tissue-specific models are needed for accurate interaction predictions Candidate variants do not lie in regulatory elements (e.g. CTCF binding sites) relevant to genome folding, so interaction-map differences are unlikely to be informative http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Prioritize candidate regulatory SNPs by using deepC to predict the effect of single base-pair variants on 3D genome folding: each variant is scored by the mean absolute difference between reference and variant predicted chromatin interaction maps, then ranked against a background set of sampled CTCF-site SNPs to nominate the likely causal variant. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Prioritize candidate regulatory SNPs by using deepC to predict the effect of single base-pair variants on 3D genome folding: each variant is scored by the mean absolute difference between reference and variant predicted chromatin interaction maps, then ranked against a background set of sampled CTCF-site SNPs to nominate the likely causal variant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns large structural variants or element deletions rather than single base-pair SNPs — deepC's SNP scoring workflow here targets single nucleotide changes No tissue-specific trained deepC model is available for the relevant cell type, since transfer-learned tissue-specific models are needed for accurate interaction predictions Candidate variants do not lie in regulatory elements (e.g. CTCF binding sites) relevant to genome folding, so interaction-map differences are unlikely to be informative

skills.description: Use when you have BED-formatted genomic peaks or features lacking strand annotation and a second BED file of the same features with '+'/'-' strand labels, and you need every feature oriented before strand asymmetry analysis.
skills.name: ctcf-chipseq-peak-orientation
skills.search_text: ctcf-chipseq-peak-orientation Use when you have BED-formatted genomic peaks or features lacking strand annotation and a second BED file of the same features with '+'/'-' strand labels, and you need every feature oriented before strand asymmetry analysis. Input features already carry strand annotation — Asymmetron's orientation step is only needed for unassigned features Peaks do not overlap any strand-annotated motif, so no strand sign can be transferred; use a nearest-neighbor annotation strategy instead The goal is computing strand asymmetry P-values rather than assigning orientation — use the consecutive_patterns, contained_asymmetries, or pairwise_asymmetries functions instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Orients strand-unannotated CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (BED, hg38) by transferring the strand sign of overlapping strand-annotated CTCF motif occurrences (e.g. MA0139.1 JASPAR/Unibind maps), using Asymmetron's orientation function implemented with pybedtools interval overlap. This enables downstream strand asymmetry analysis of the peaks. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Orients strand-unannotated CTCF ChIP-seq peaks (BED, hg38) by transferring the strand sign of overlapping strand-annotated CTCF motif occurrences (e.g. MA0139.1 JASPAR/Unibind maps), using Asymmetron's orientation function implemented with pybedtools interval overlap. This enables downstream strand asymmetry analysis of the peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input features already carry strand annotation — Asymmetron's orientation step is only needed for unassigned features Peaks do not overlap any strand-annotated motif, so no strand sign can be transferred; use a nearest-neighbor annotation strategy instead The goal is computing strand asymmetry P-values rather than assigning orientation — use the consecutive_patterns, contained_asymmetries, or pairwise_asymmetries functions instead

skills.description: Use when you need to identify CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C data — especially at reduced sequencing depth or when transferring a loop-calling model trained on one cell line (e.g., GM12878) to another (K562, HeLa-S3) — rather than threshold-based callers like SIP or Chromosight.
skills.name: ctcf-mediated-loop-calling
skills.search_text: ctcf-mediated-loop-calling Use when you need to identify CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C data — especially at reduced sequencing depth or when transferring a loop-calling model trained on one cell line (e.g., GM12878) to another (K562, HeLa-S3) — rather than threshold-based callers like SIP or Chromosight. The input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data: GILoop focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with extremely sparse scHi-C. You need a single-view image-based caller on raw hic files without a trained model — SIP or Chromosight treat matrices as images and may be simpler, though less robust. The targeted cell line's sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository and you cannot retrain or downsample. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Call genome-wide CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C contact maps using GILoop, a dual-branch neural network that learns from both graph (GCN) and image views of the intra-chromosomal interaction matrix, including transfer of pre-trained models across cell lines. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Call genome-wide CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from Hi-C contact maps using GILoop, a dual-branch neural network that learns from both graph (GCN) and image views of the intra-chromosomal interaction matrix, including transfer of pre-trained models across cell lines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data: GILoop focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with extremely sparse scHi-C. You need a single-view image-based caller on raw hic files without a trained model — SIP or Chromosight treat matrices as images and may be simpler, though less robust. The targeted cell line's sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository and you cannot retrain or downsample.

skills.search_text: ctcf-motif-orientation-classification Use when you have SnapHiC loop calls (*.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) with CTCF binding on both anchors and need to quantify convergent vs tandem vs divergent CTCF motif orientation. Loops where CTCF does not bind both anchors — motif orientation is undefined without motifs on both anchors Loop calls in a format other than SnapHiC's postprocessed summits bedpe, or from a genome build other than mm10 (the JASPAR scan and reference sequences assume mm10 coordinates) Bulk Hi-C or other chromatin-interaction datasets where per-cell detection counts (outlier_count) needed for the >= 50 cell filter are not available http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Classifies each SnapHiC-identified chromatin loop as convergent, tandem, or divergent based on CTCF motif strands at its two anchors, testing the loop extrusion model's prediction that loops favor convergent orientation. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2

skills.search_text: ctga-rich-genomic-bin-mining Use when you need to extract CT/GA-rich regions from a reference genome (e.g., hg19) as in silico read-restriction sets for a bisulfite-free 4-letter alignment benchmark, or to test promoter enrichment of such regions against genomic background. Input is sequencing reads (FASTQ) to be aligned or methylation-called — use Msuite's 3-letter or 4-letter alignment mode instead of genome-wide bin mining The reference genome or species is not hg19/mm9/mm10/hg38 and no RefSeq annotation has been downloaded from the UCSC genome browser, since the TSS/promoter definition depends on RefSeq annotation files The goal is per-read 4-letter alignment accuracy measurement rather than characterizing where CT/GA-rich regions occur genome-wide http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 This skill mines the human hg19 genome for CT/GA-rich regions — 500-bp non-overlapping bins with CT proportion ≥80% or GA proportion ≥80% — the same restriction criterion used to build Msuite's in silico TAPS reads for the 4-letter alignment benchmark, and then tests whether these bins are enriched in promoters versus the genomic background. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127

skills.description: Use when fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models and observed apparent methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing are available, and the PCR-corrected methylation degree must be recovered numerically rather than analytically.
skills.name: cubic-spline-interpolation-of-random-effects
skills.search_text: cubic-spline-interpolation-of-random-effects Use when fitted MethylCal/INLA calibration models and observed apparent methylation levels from bisulfite amplicon sequencing are available, and the PCR-corrected methylation degree must be recovered numerically rather than analytically. When the calibration method is Warnecke's hyperbolic approach, whose inversion is analytic and does not require spline interpolation plus numerical optimization When only exploratory visualization of calibration curves is needed (use ExploratoryPlot or MethylCalCalibrationPlot instead of correction) When the data have not been through the Formatting() step and no fitted INLA calibration model exists for the assay Numerically inverts MethylCal's PCR-bias calibration by fitting a cubic spline through the posterior means of the AMP random effects (η_i) and minimizing objective function (10) with R's optimize(), yielding the corrected methylation degree per CpG-AMP combination. Unlike Warnecke's hyperbolic method, MethylCal's correction has no closed form, so this spline-plus-optimization procedure is required. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Numerically inverts MethylCal's PCR-bias calibration by fitting a cubic spline through the posterior means of the AMP random effects (η_i) and minimizing objective function (10) with R's optimize(), yielding the corrected methylation degree per CpG-AMP combination. Unlike Warnecke's hyperbolic method, MethylCal's correction has no closed form, so this spline-plus-optimization procedure is required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the calibration method is Warnecke's hyperbolic approach, whose inversion is analytic and does not require spline interpolation plus numerical optimization When only exploratory visualization of calibration curves is needed (use ExploratoryPlot or MethylCalCalibrationPlot instead of correction) When the data have not been through the Formatting() step and no fitted INLA calibration model exists for the assay

skills.description: Use when AmpliconArchitect has produced reconstructed cycles from WGS focal amplifications and you need tabular eccDNA coordinate records for a database or BED/TSV catalog.

skills.search_text: cycle-to-ecdna-coordinate-conversion Use when AmpliconArchitect has produced reconstructed cycles from WGS focal amplifications and you need tabular eccDNA coordinate records for a database or BED/TSV catalog. skills.search_text: differential-enrichment-analysis-scchipsq Use when scChIP-seq count matrices have been clustered into epigenomic subpopulations (e.g. via ConsensusClusterPlus in ChromSCape) and you need per-cluster differentially enriched regions and biological interpretation. Input is raw unfiltered count matrices — cells must first pass QC (min 1600 unique reads, top 5% coverage removal) and correlation-based filtering Data are bulk ChIP-seq with high coverage — ChromSCape is designed for sparse single-cell histone modification data Only one cluster/subpopulation exists — differential enrichment requires at least two subpopulations to compare http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Run per-cluster differential enrichment analysis in ChromSCape on H3K27me3 single-cell ChIP-seq data to identify genomic regions differentially enriched between epigenomic subpopulations, then interpret them via gene-set and pathway enrichment (MSigDB v5) using the Gencode_hg38_v26 transcriptome annotation. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Run per-cluster differential enrichment analysis in ChromSCape on H3K27me3 single-cell ChIP-seq data to identify genomic regions differentially enriched between epigenomic subpopulations, then interpret them via gene-set and pathway enrichment (MSigDB v5) using the Gencode_hg38_v26 transcriptome annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw unfiltered count matrices — cells must first pass QC (min 1600 unique reads, top 5% coverage removal) and correlation-based filtering Data are bulk ChIP-seq with high coverage — ChromSCape is designed for sparse single-cell histone modification data Only one cluster/subpopulation exists — differential enrichment requires at least two subpopulations to compare

skills.description: Use when a filtered, normalized single-cell epigenomic count matrix (H3K27me3 scChIP-seq or scATAC-seq) has per-cell cluster labels and you must find regions enriched or depleted per cluster versus all other cells, then interpret them via gene set enrichment.
skills.name: differential-enrichment-region-testing-cluster-vs-rest
skills.search_text: differential-enrichment-region-testing-cluster-vs-rest Use when a filtered, normalized single-cell epigenomic count matrix (H3K27me3 scChIP-seq or scATAC-seq) has per-cell cluster labels and you must find regions enriched or depleted per cluster versus all other cells, then interpret them via gene set enrichment. The input is bulk ChIP-seq data — ChromSCape is built for the low coverage and sparsity of single-cell histone modification datasets Clusters have not been defined yet (no per-cell labels) — run QC filtering, PCA (50 PCs), t-SNE/UMAP and clustering first The goal is only visualizing cell populations without needing cluster-specific chromatin features or pathway interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Per-cluster differential testing of genomic regions in single-cell epigenomic count matrices (e.g., H3K27me3 scChIP-seq from the tumor micro-environment), followed by linking significant regions to genes and running MSigDB v5 gene set enrichment. It turns ChromSCape's epigenomic clusters into interpretable, cluster-specific chromatin features. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Per-cluster differential testing of genomic regions in single-cell epigenomic count matrices (e.g., H3K27me3 scChIP-seq from the tumor micro-environment), followed by linking significant regions to genes and running MSigDB v5 gene set enrichment. It turns ChromSCape's epigenomic clusters into interpretable, cluster-specific chromatin features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk ChIP-seq data — ChromSCape is built for the low coverage and sparsity of single-cell histone modification datasets Clusters have not been defined yet (no per-cell labels) — run QC filtering, PCA (50 PCs), t-SNE/UMAP and clustering first The goal is only visualizing cell populations without needing cluster-specific chromatin features or pathway interpretation

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq gene expression data must be converted into a differentially expressed gene set and tested for significant overlap with differential histone modification calls (e.g. H3K27me3 or H3K9me3).
skills.name: differential-expression-gene-list-processing
skills.search_text: differential-expression-gene-list-processing Use when RNA-seq gene expression data must be converted into a differentially expressed gene set and tested for significant overlap with differential histone modification calls (e.g. H3K27me3 or H3K9me3). Input ChIP-seq data contains peak-like histone marks rather than broad diffuse modifications such as H3K27me3/H3K9me3, where peak-calling methods are adequate and histoneHMM's broad-footprint modeling is unnecessary The task is only to call modified/differentially modified regions from ChIP-seq read data without any matched gene expression data to overlap against http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Derive a differentially expressed gene list from RNA-seq expression data (DESeq FDR<0.01), map it and histoneHMM differential modification calls to a common gene identifier via GFF annotation, and test their overlap with Fisher's exact test plus GO enrichment to validate differential modification calls. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Derive a differentially expressed gene list from RNA-seq expression data (DESeq FDR<0.01), map it and histoneHMM differential modification calls to a common gene identifier via GFF annotation, and test their overlap with Fisher's exact test plus GO enrichment to validate differential modification calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input ChIP-seq data contains peak-like histone marks rather than broad diffuse modifications such as H3K27me3/H3K9me3, where peak-calling methods are adequate and histoneHMM's broad-footprint modeling is unnecessary The task is only to call modified/differentially modified regions from ChIP-seq read data without any matched gene expression data to overlap against

skills.description: Use when raw sequencing counts from paired control/condition anchored genomic regions must be converted to a continuous biological activity score for a score-based motif enrichment analysis such as MEPP.
skills.name: differential-expression-log2foldchange-scoring
skills.search_text: differential-expression-log2foldchange-scoring Use when raw sequencing counts from paired control/condition anchored genomic regions must be converted to a continuous biological activity score for a score-based motif enrichment analysis such as MEPP. Sequences are uncentered or not anchored to a defined coordinate (TSS/cleavage site), since MEPP profiles motif enrichment relative to a central anchor point The analysis goal is de novo motif discovery — MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library Regions lack a graded activity signal (e.g. only binary differential calls), since MEPP scores regions across a continuum of biological interest rather than presence/absence labels Computes DESeq2 log2 fold changes of LPS-stimulated vs resting macrophage anchored regions (csRNA-seq TSSs, ATAC-seq Tn5 cleavage sites, H3K27ac MNase-seq cleavage sites from GSE203135) and uses them as the biological activity score continuum that MEPP requires for positional motif enrichment profiling. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Computes DESeq2 log2 fold changes of LPS-stimulated vs resting macrophage anchored regions (csRNA-seq TSSs, ATAC-seq Tn5 cleavage sites, H3K27ac MNase-seq cleavage sites from GSE203135) and uses them as the biological activity score continuum that MEPP requires for positional motif enrichment profiling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are uncentered or not anchored to a defined coordinate (TSS/cleavage site), since MEPP profiles motif enrichment relative to a central anchor point The analysis goal is de novo motif discovery — MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library Regions lack a graded activity signal (e.g. only binary differential calls), since MEPP scores regions across a continuum of biological interest rather than presence/absence labels

skills.description: Use when overlap counts between differential expression genes and differential accessibility peaks (or SNP/gene statistics) are available and an objective, bootstrap-justified logFC or P-value cutoff is needed instead of an arbitrary threshold.
skills.name: differential-expression-threshold-estimation
skills.search_text: differential-expression-threshold-estimation Use when overlap counts between differential expression genes and differential accessibility peaks (or SNP/gene statistics) are available and an objective, bootstrap-justified logFC or P-value cutoff is needed instead of an arbitrary threshold. The analysis goal is a simple enrichment z score at a fixed, pre-specified cutoff rather than optimizing the threshold itself (use the standard bootRanges var.R overlap-rate/z-score workflow instead). The input consists of caQTL–SNP overlap rates in human liver tissue (the liver script uses splines for a conditional density plot, not DEG logFC threshold optimization). Null sets were generated by conventional shuffling or permutation, which may produce overly narrow test statistic null distributions and over-estimate significance. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 A bootRanges-based spline-fitting procedure that derives data-driven significance thresholds for differential analysis — e.g. SNPs with -log10(P-value) > 8 and genes with |logFC| > 2 in the Alasoo 2018 macrophage dataset — by locating where the observed penalized-spline fit over logFC separates from the block-bootstrap null envelope. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: A bootRanges-based spline-fitting procedure that derives data-driven significance thresholds for differential analysis — e.g. SNPs with -log10(P-value) > 8 and genes with |logFC| > 2 in the Alasoo 2018 macrophage dataset — by locating where the observed penalized-spline fit over logFC separates from the block-bootstrap null envelope.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a simple enrichment z score at a fixed, pre-specified cutoff rather than optimizing the threshold itself (use the standard bootRanges var.R overlap-rate/z-score workflow instead). The input consists of caQTL–SNP overlap rates in human liver tissue (the liver script uses splines for a conditional density plot, not DEG logFC threshold optimization). Null sets were generated by conventional shuffling or permutation, which may produce overly narrow test statistic null distributions and over-estimate significance.

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq differential expression results must be integrated with ChIP-seq peak-to-promoter annotations to identify loci where two regulators both bind and co-regulate the same genes.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when RNA-seq differential expression results must be integrated with ChIP-seq peak-to-promoter annotations to identify loci where two regulators both bind and co-regulate the same genes. Input is only raw RNA-seq counts without matching ChIP-seq occupancy data — this skill requires co-occupied promoter regions, not expression data alone The analysis targets a single promoter (e.g. luxCDABE only) rather than a genome-wide intersection of co-occupied peaks with co-regulated genes Regulators of interest do not have ChIP-seq peak sets that overlap; the 500 bp upstream peak-to-ORF filtering step is the core precondition http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Intersects ChIP-seq co-occupied LuxR/H-NS promoter regions with RNA-seq differential co-regulation data (GSE136050) to derive the set of promoters and downstream genes co-regulated by both regulators. In the V. harveyi quorum sensing study this yielded 28 promoters controlling 63 co-regulated genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Intersects ChIP-seq co-occupied LuxR/H-NS promoter regions with RNA-seq differential co-regulation data (GSE136050) to derive the set of promoters and downstream genes co-regulated by both regulators. In the V. harveyi quorum sensing study this yielded 28 promoters controlling 63 co-regulated genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is only raw RNA-seq counts without matching ChIP-seq occupancy data — this skill requires co-occupied promoter regions, not expression data alone The analysis targets a single promoter (e.g. luxCDABE only) rather than a genome-wide intersection of co-occupied peaks with co-regulated genes Regulators of interest do not have ChIP-seq peak sets that overlap; the 500 bp upstream peak-to-ORF filtering step is the core precondition

skills.description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files and sample metadata need end-to-end processing (QC, STAR/BBMap alignment, featureCounts quantification, RUVSeq normalization) followed by DEG testing, or when a two-factor CIPHER expInfo schema must be extended to multi-condition or time-series contrasts.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files and sample metadata need end-to-end processing (QC, STAR/BBMap alignment, featureCounts quantification, RUVSeq normalization) followed by DEG testing, or when a two-factor CIPHER expInfo schema must be extended to multi-condition or time-series contrasts. Do not mix single-ended and pair-ended data into the same CONFIG file — the README states CIPHER does not handle this use case yet Do not use when only a subset of tools is needed — CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, not subsets of tools Do not rely on CIPHER's default expInfo schema alone for designs with more than two factor levels or time-series contrasts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 CIPHER's RNA-seq workflow performs differential gene expression analysis as part of a Nextflow-based pipeline spanning raw sequence evaluation, read mapping, and QC. It is optimized for two-type experimental designs (e.g. WT versus KO), so multi-factor and time-series designs require constructing custom DESeq2/edgeR GLM design matrices outside CIPHER's default schema. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1
skills.summary: CIPHER's RNA-seq workflow performs differential gene expression analysis as part of a Nextflow-based pipeline spanning raw sequence evaluation, read mapping, and QC. It is optimized for two-type experimental designs (e.g. WT versus KO), so multi-factor and time-series designs require constructing custom DESeq2/edgeR GLM design matrices outside CIPHER's default schema.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Do not mix single-ended and pair-ended data into the same CONFIG file — the README states CIPHER does not handle this use case yet Do not use when only a subset of tools is needed — CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, not subsets of tools Do not rely on CIPHER's default expInfo schema alone for designs with more than two factor levels or time-series contrasts

skills.description: Use when you have paired copy-number/epi-DNA alteration calls (e.g. GISTIC2.0 focal SCNAs) and matched RSEM log2 expression for the same tumor samples, and need cis (in-peak) and trans (genome-wide) DE genes per alteration.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when you have paired copy-number/epi-DNA alteration calls (e.g. GISTIC2.0 focal SCNAs) and matched RSEM log2 expression for the same tumor samples, and need cis (in-peak) and trans (genome-wide) DE genes per alteration. When you only need genes prioritized as drivers by their mediation of trans effects — use the iEDGE mediation (calc_sobel) module instead of raw DE When alterations are broad arm-level events rather than focal peaks — iEDGE_DE is designed around focal peak cis gene lists; use make_GISTIC2 arm-level processing instead When expression and alteration data come from unpaired or mismatched samples — the design requires paired omics profiles from the same specimens http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 limma-based cis/trans differential expression analysis of gene expression between samples with and without a focal (epi-)DNA alteration, as implemented in the iEDGE R package's iEDGE_DE engine to identify alteration-associated cis and trans gene signatures. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: limma-based cis/trans differential expression analysis of gene expression between samples with and without a focal (epi-)DNA alteration, as implemented in the iEDGE R package's iEDGE_DE engine to identify alteration-associated cis and trans gene signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you only need genes prioritized as drivers by their mediation of trans effects — use the iEDGE mediation (calc_sobel) module instead of raw DE When alterations are broad arm-level events rather than focal peaks — iEDGE_DE is designed around focal peak cis gene lists; use make_GISTIC2 arm-level processing instead When expression and alteration data come from unpaired or mismatched samples — the design requires paired omics profiles from the same specimens

skills.description: Use when cluster assignments from an unsupervised expression clustering solution (e.g., SRIQ, 6 clusters at diameter 0.63) exist and per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists and GO terms are needed.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-analysis Use when cluster assignments from an unsupervised expression clustering solution (e.g., SRIQ, 6 clusters at diameter 0.63) exist and per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists and GO terms are needed. Expression data are not log2-transformed (and off-set by 0.1 or with values <1 set to 1), as required before SAM analysis No cluster solution exists yet — run SRIQ clustering and EXTRACT clusters first Goal is assigning samples into clusters rather than characterizing existing SRIQ clusters by DEG/enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Performs one-versus-rest differential gene expression per SRIQ core cluster using SAM permutation testing (SAMDEG), then maps genes to symbols and runs EnrichR GO enrichment to characterize transcriptional programs of tumor subgroups in TCGA LUAD. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: Performs one-versus-rest differential gene expression per SRIQ core cluster using SAM permutation testing (SAMDEG), then maps genes to symbols and runs EnrichR GO enrichment to characterize transcriptional programs of tumor subgroups in TCGA LUAD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Expression data are not log2-transformed (and off-set by 0.1 or with values <1 set to 1), as required before SAM analysis No cluster solution exists yet — run SRIQ clustering and EXTRACT clusters first Goal is assigning samples into clusters rather than characterizing existing SRIQ clusters by DEG/enrichment

skills.description: Use when RNA-seq expression changes across an environmental perturbation (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium in yeast, GSE153609) must be binned into ranked gene groups to subset downstream chromatin analyses such as +1 nucleosome dyad composites.
skills.name: differential-gene-expression-stratification
skills.search_text: differential-gene-expression-stratification Use when RNA-seq expression changes across an environmental perturbation (e.g., 0 min vs 60 min cadmium in yeast, GSE153609) must be binned into ranked gene groups to subset downstream chromatin analyses such as +1 nucleosome dyad composites. The analysis goal is a genome-wide continuous ranking or statistical differential-expression table rather than discrete top-100 gene groups for downstream stratified compositing Only one experimental condition/timepoint is available, so no expression change can be computed to rank genes into upmost/downmost/constant groups Genes are already stratified by a prior differential-expression step and only chromatin compositing remains http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Stratifies yeast genes into discrete transcriptional-response groups (upmost: top 100 most up-regulated, downmost: top 100 most down-regulated, constant: 100 unchanged) from RNA-seq expression changes under cadmium stress, so that chromatin dynamics can be composited per group from RoboCOP_MNase nucleosome occupancy profiles. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Stratifies yeast genes into discrete transcriptional-response groups (upmost: top 100 most up-regulated, downmost: top 100 most down-regulated, constant: 100 unchanged) from RNA-seq expression changes under cadmium stress, so that chromatin dynamics can be composited per group from RoboCOP_MNase nucleosome occupancy profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a genome-wide continuous ranking or statistical differential-expression table rather than discrete top-100 gene groups for downstream stratified compositing Only one experimental condition/timepoint is available, so no expression change can be computed to rank genes into upmost/downmost/constant groups Genes are already stratified by a prior differential-expression step and only chromatin compositing remains

skills.description: Use when PCR-bias-corrected (MethylCal or Moskalev's CPR) methylation levels for case/control pyrosequencing or bisulfite amplicon data must be called as gain/loss of methylation against a healthy-control ±3SD interval, e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 and H19/IGF2 calls.
skills.name: differential-methylation-classification
skills.search_text: differential-methylation-classification Use when PCR-bias-corrected (MethylCal or Moskalev's CPR) methylation levels for case/control pyrosequencing or bisulfite amplicon data must be called as gain/loss of methylation against a healthy-control ±3SD interval, e.g. BWS KCNQ1OT1 and H19/IGF2 calls. Input is raw observed (uncorrected) methylation data — calibration/correction with MethylCal must precede classification, since borderline cases are only resolved after PCR-bias correction Input is CpG island or DMR standard-control calibration data (five controls at 0/25/50/75/100%) — that calls for MethylCalCalibrationPlot/MethylCalCalibrationOutlierPlot, not the case/control differential test The analysis requires a genome-wide methylation profile rather than a small set of targeted bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing assays Classify case samples as hypermethylated, hypomethylated, or normal at a targeted DMR by comparing PCR-bias-corrected methylation levels against a healthy-control confidence interval, using the differential methylation test built into MethylCal's MethylCalCorrection (R package based on INLA). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Classify case samples as hypermethylated, hypomethylated, or normal at a targeted DMR by comparing PCR-bias-corrected methylation levels against a healthy-control confidence interval, using the differential methylation test built into MethylCal's MethylCalCorrection (R package based on INLA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw observed (uncorrected) methylation data — calibration/correction with MethylCal must precede classification, since borderline cases are only resolved after PCR-bias correction Input is CpG island or DMR standard-control calibration data (five controls at 0/25/50/75/100%) — that calls for MethylCalCalibrationPlot/MethylCalCalibrationOutlierPlot, not the case/control differential test The analysis requires a genome-wide methylation profile rather than a small set of targeted bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing assays

skills.description: Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq (bisulfite) data in SAM/BAM format needs post-alignment processing to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) between two or more sample groups, e.g., IMR90 vs H1.
skills.name: differential-methylation-region-testing
skills.search_text: differential-methylation-region-testing Use when Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq (bisulfite) data in SAM/BAM format needs post-alignment processing to identify differentially methylated regions (DMRs) between two or more sample groups, e.g., IMR90 vs H1. The analysis needs modeling of sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder only identifies individual differentially methylated regions The data contain batch effects that must be accounted for — DMRfinder cannot correct for batch effects Input is raw methylation calls from a non-Bismark aligner lacking 'XM' methylation strings and 'XG' genome designations in the SAM output http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A three-script DMRfinder pipeline that extracts per-CpG methylation counts from Bismark SAM/BAM alignments, clusters CpG sites into genomic regions via modified single-linkage clustering, and tests regions for differential methylation using DSS beta-binomial hierarchical modeling and Wald tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: A three-script DMRfinder pipeline that extracts per-CpG methylation counts from Bismark SAM/BAM alignments, clusters CpG sites into genomic regions via modified single-linkage clustering, and tests regions for differential methylation using DSS beta-binomial hierarchical modeling and Wald tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis needs modeling of sets of regions or quantitative traits — DMRfinder only identifies individual differentially methylated regions The data contain batch effects that must be accounted for — DMRfinder cannot correct for batch effects Input is raw methylation calls from a non-Bismark aligner lacking 'XM' methylation strings and 'XG' genome designations in the SAM output

skills.description: Use when two condition-specific differentially bound peak sets (e.g. female vs male GBM CC peaks) exist and the goal is to identify which TF motif families are enriched in one condition but not the other, reproducing published family-level enrichment patterns.
skills.name: differential-peak-motif-verification
skills.search_text: differential-peak-motif-verification Use when two condition-specific differentially bound peak sets (e.g. female vs male GBM CC peaks) exist and the goal is to identify which TF motif families are enriched in one condition but not the other, reproducing published family-level enrichment patterns. Input is a single undivided peak set with no condition/sex grouping — call motifs directly on the peaks instead of running a between-group comparison The question is differential peak binding itself (pp/tl differential analysis), not which motifs explain already-computed differential peaks Peaks are not TF-binding calling cards (qbed/ccf-derived) peaks; HOMER motif discovery on unrelated feature sets is out of scope for this workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Verifies sex-specific transcription factor motif enrichment by calling motifs on differentially bound Brd4 peaks from female vs male glioblastoma calling cards data with pycallingcards' HOMER-backed tools, then comparing enrichment between groups to confirm reported TF family patterns. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Verifies sex-specific transcription factor motif enrichment by calling motifs on differentially bound Brd4 peaks from female vs male glioblastoma calling cards data with pycallingcards' HOMER-backed tools, then comparing enrichment between groups to confirm reported TF family patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single undivided peak set with no condition/sex grouping — call motifs directly on the peaks instead of running a between-group comparison The question is differential peak binding itself (pp/tl differential analysis), not which motifs explain already-computed differential peaks Peaks are not TF-binding calling cards (qbed/ccf-derived) peaks; HOMER motif discovery on unrelated feature sets is out of scope for this workflow

When the raw and imputed matrices would be analyzed on different peak sets — the comparison of significant motif counts is only valid if both are subset to the same sites When the goal is SCALE clustering or UMAP embedding on all peaks rather than motif scoring on a differential peak set http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Subsets both the raw peak-count matrix and the SCALE-imputed matrix (adata.obsm['imputed']) to a defined set of differentially accessible sites so that downstream chromVAR motif deviation scoring operates on a shared, comparable peak set. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12630-7
skills.summary: Subsets both the raw peak-count matrix and the SCALE-imputed matrix (adata.obsm['imputed']) to a defined set of differentially accessible sites so that downstream chromVAR motif deviation scoring operates on a shared, comparable peak set.

skills.name: dimensionality-reduction-umap-visualization
skills.search_text: dimensionality-reduction-umap-visualization Use when analyzing gzipped single-cell BED files from sparse single-cell histone-modification assays (e.g. H3K27me3 scCUT&Tag K562/H1, H3K4me3 scChIC-seq) and you need a 2D embedding to assess whether known cell populations or expected clusters separate. Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or precomputed feature table — PCA/UMAP recomputation is redundant Data is bulk ChIP-seq; the article states existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are 'not fit for the low coverage and sparsity of these single-cell histone modifications datasets' and this pipeline targets sparse single-cell assays Cells fall below the 1600 unique reads per cell coverage threshold — the projection is unreliable on unfiltered, low-coverage cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Visualize single-cell epigenomic datasets (scCUT&Tag, scChIC-seq, scChIP-seq) as a 2D UMAP computed on a PCA embedding of filtered count matrices, optionally after FastMNN batch correction, to reveal sub-populations and verify that known cell types or clusters are recovered. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Visualize single-cell epigenomic datasets (scCUT&Tag, scChIC-seq, scChIP-seq) as a 2D UMAP computed on a PCA embedding of filtered count matrices, optionally after FastMNN batch correction, to reveal sub-populations and verify that known cell types or clusters are recovered.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-dimensional embedding or precomputed feature table — PCA/UMAP recomputation is redundant Data is bulk ChIP-seq; the article states existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are 'not fit for the low coverage and sparsity of these single-cell histone modifications datasets' and this pipeline targets sparse single-cell assays Cells fall below the 1600 unique reads per cell coverage threshold — the projection is unreliable on unfiltered, low-coverage cells

skills.description: Use when integrating expression with promoter/body methylation or histone-mark p-values in SMITE and you have prior knowledge of the expected direction of each modification–expression relationship, so opposite-direction evidence should be penalized rather than treated as concordant.
skills.name: directionality-penalty-specification
skills.search_text: directionality-penalty-specification Use when integrating expression with promoter/body methylation or histone-mark p-values in SMITE and you have prior knowledge of the expected direction of each modification–expression relationship, so opposite-direction evidence should be penalized rather than treated as concordant. When there is no defensible a priori expectation of direction for a modification–expression relationship — declaring 'decrease' or 'increase' without biological grounding will penalize true signals. When only a single data type is available, since directionality penalties apply to relationships between component scores, not to one isolated p-value layer. When the analysis goal is direction-agnostic aggregation of all significant loci rather than SMITE's directional composite scoring — the article positions SMITE against methods that prune to the most significant subset of loci. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Specifies a priori directionality coefficients for each epigenomic/expression component when SMITE combines per-gene p-values, penalizing modification–expression relationships that run opposite to the expected biology (e.g., promoter methylation 'decrease'). This ensures the Stouffer/Fisher composite gene score reflects mechanistic direction, not just statistical significance. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Specifies a priori directionality coefficients for each epigenomic/expression component when SMITE combines per-gene p-values, penalizing modification–expression relationships that run opposite to the expected biology (e.g., promoter methylation 'decrease'). This ensures the Stouffer/Fisher composite gene score reflects mechanistic direction, not just statistical significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When there is no defensible a priori expectation of direction for a modification–expression relationship — declaring 'decrease' or 'increase' without biological grounding will penalize true signals. When only a single data type is available, since directionality penalties apply to relationships between component scores, not to one isolated p-value layer. When the analysis goal is direction-agnostic aggregation of all significant loci rather than SMITE's directional composite scoring — the article positions SMITE against methods that prune to the most significant subset of loci.

skills.name: dirichlet-hyperparameter-configuration
skills.search_text: dirichlet-hyperparameter-configuration Use when a cisTopic object holds a binary accessibility matrix (e.g. ~97k regulatory regions over 5,335 PBMCs) and multiple LDA models across a topic-number grid must be fitted for downstream model selection. cisTopic is deprecated — for new analyses prefer pycisTopic, per the repository README The input is raw fragment/peak files rather than a binarized accessibility matrix already stored in a cisTopic object — first build the object with createcisTopicObjectFrom10X Configure and fit Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic models over a binary accessibility matrix in cisTopic, keeping the default Dirichlet hyperparameters (alpha=50/number of topics, beta=0.1) while sweeping a grid of topic numbers so that model complexity can be selected by log likelihood. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-019-0367-1
skills.summary: Configure and fit Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic models over a binary accessibility matrix in cisTopic, keeping the default Dirichlet hyperparameters (alpha=50/number of topics, beta=0.1) while sweeping a grid of topic numbers so that model complexity can be selected by log likelihood.
