skills.search_text: discriminative-positive-negative-dataset-construction Use when preparing inputs for discriminative motif discovery with DiNAMO: you have genomic coordinates or event positions (e.g., 3272 monocyte SSE coordinates on Hg18) and must build signal.fa and a matched control.fa pair. The analysis goal is positional motif enrichment with no discriminative comparison — a single-sequence-set motif finder would suffice without building a control dataset Input is already a motif frequency matrix or curated motif set rather than raw sequence coordinates — dataset construction is unnecessary Events are not sequence-localized (no genomic coordinates or positions to extract sequences around) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Constructs a matched pair of FASTA datasets — a positive (signal) dataset of sequences centered on the events of interest (e.g., systematic sequencing error positions) and a negative (control) dataset from non-event regions — so DiNAMO can perform exact discriminative IUPAC motif discovery against a background. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Constructs a matched pair of FASTA datasets — a positive (signal) dataset of sequences centered on the events of interest (e.g., systematic sequencing error positions) and a negative (control) dataset from non-event regions — so DiNAMO can perform exact discriminative IUPAC motif discovery against a background.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is positional motif enrichment with no discriminative comparison — a single-sequence-set motif finder would suffice without building a control dataset Input is already a motif frequency matrix or curated motif set rather than raw sequence coordinates — dataset construction is unnecessary Events are not sequence-localized (no genomic coordinates or positions to extract sequences around)

skills.description: Use when you have decontaminated epiallele (or analogous binary/continuous feature) profiles per tumour region and need a phylogenetic tree linking sample evolutionary relationships.
skills.name: distance-based-phylogenetic-tree-inference
skills.search_text: distance-based-phylogenetic-tree-inference Use when you have decontaminated epiallele (or analogous binary/continuous feature) profiles per tumour region and need a phylogenetic tree linking sample evolutionary relationships. Input is raw read-level methylation data rather than decontaminated epiallele profiles — the Bayesian detection and purity/decontamination steps must run first Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so the approach is unsuitable when phased multi-locus haplotypes are required Only a single bulk sample is available — the method relies on tracing epialleles across multiple tumour regions (the study used seven regions of CRUK0062 plus one matched normal) http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reconstructs the evolutionary history of multi-region tumour samples by computing pairwise Euclidean distances between decontaminated epiallele profiles, averaging per-locus distance matrices, and fitting a tree with the balanced minimum evolution method (fastme.bal from the ape R package), output in Newick format. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Reconstructs the evolutionary history of multi-region tumour samples by computing pairwise Euclidean distances between decontaminated epiallele profiles, averaging per-locus distance matrices, and fitting a tree with the balanced minimum evolution method (fastme.bal from the ape R package), output in Newick format.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw read-level methylation data rather than decontaminated epiallele profiles — the Bayesian detection and purity/decontamination steps must run first Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so the approach is unsuitable when phased multi-locus haplotypes are required Only a single bulk sample is available — the method relies on tracing epialleles across multiple tumour regions (the study used seven regions of CRUK0062 plus one matched normal)

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed 40 kb-resolution cis-interaction Hi-C or capture Hi-C contact map still shows distance-decay-dominated ligation frequencies after coverage-bias removal and you need background-corrected contact frequencies.
skills.name: distance-dependent-background-removal
skills.search_text: distance-dependent-background-removal Use when a preprocessed 40 kb-resolution cis-interaction Hi-C or capture Hi-C contact map still shows distance-decay-dominated ligation frequencies after coverage-bias removal and you need background-corrected contact frequencies. The input is raw inter-chromosomal (trans) interaction data — covNorm focuses on cis-interactions, and inter-chromosomal interactions were filtered in the article's pipeline. Only coverage bias (unequal fragment coverage) is present and the distance-decay signal itself is the quantity of interest, e.g. building expected-vs-distance curves for compartment analysis. The contact map has not been processed by the coverage-bias-removing step, since the background removal is applied sequentially after it in the covNorm workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 A covNorm normalization step that removes the genomic distance-dependent background signal from Hi-C contact maps after negative binomial coverage-bias removal, applied sequentially to improve contact map reproducibility. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: A covNorm normalization step that removes the genomic distance-dependent background signal from Hi-C contact maps after negative binomial coverage-bias removal, applied sequentially to improve contact map reproducibility.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw inter-chromosomal (trans) interaction data — covNorm focuses on cis-interactions, and inter-chromosomal interactions were filtered in the article's pipeline. Only coverage bias (unequal fragment coverage) is present and the distance-decay signal itself is the quantity of interest, e.g. building expected-vs-distance curves for compartment analysis. The contact map has not been processed by the coverage-bias-removing step, since the background removal is applied sequentially after it in the covNorm workflow.

skills.description: Use when stress-testing TLD/TAD prediction robustness on sparse (single-cell-like) Hi-C matrices: noise must respect distance-dependent decay, so each secondary diagonal is sampled independently rather than uniformly across the whole matrix.
skills.name: distance-dependent-noise-sampling-per-secondary-diagonal
skills.search_text: distance-dependent-noise-sampling-per-secondary-diagonal Use when stress-testing TLD/TAD prediction robustness on sparse (single-cell-like) Hi-C matrices: noise must respect distance-dependent decay, so each secondary diagonal is sampled independently rather than uniformly across the whole matrix. The goal is TLD prediction on a single clean matrix rather than noise-robustness benchmarking across a perturbation series Input is experimental single-cell Hi-C whose sparsity is intrinsic; the perturbation would confound natural sparsity with synthetic noise The noise model must be uniform over the matrix rather than distance-dependent, since this scheme samples each secondary diagonal separately by its contact probability http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 A controlled perturbation scheme that adds arbitrary noise to downsampled bulk Hi-C contact matrices (0.025% sampling rate, 40 kb binsize) by sampling 10%, 20%, or 40% of contact entries separately within each secondary diagonal according to its distance-dependent contact probability, used to benchmark robustness of TLD predictors such as deDoc2. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: A controlled perturbation scheme that adds arbitrary noise to downsampled bulk Hi-C contact matrices (0.025% sampling rate, 40 kb binsize) by sampling 10%, 20%, or 40% of contact entries separately within each secondary diagonal according to its distance-dependent contact probability, used to benchmark robustness of TLD predictors such as deDoc2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is TLD prediction on a single clean matrix rather than noise-robustness benchmarking across a perturbation series Input is experimental single-cell Hi-C whose sparsity is intrinsic; the perturbation would confound natural sparsity with synthetic noise The noise model must be uniform over the matrix rather than distance-dependent, since this scheme samples each secondary diagonal separately by its contact probability

skills.description: Use when a KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact map must be converted to an O/E matrix before tiling into 64x64 kb patches for dual-branch (image + graph) loop-calling model training or prediction.
skills.name: distance-normalization-oe-matrix-computation
skills.search_text: distance-normalization-oe-matrix-computation Use when a KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact map must be converted to an O/E matrix before tiling into 64x64 kb patches for dual-branch (image + graph) loop-calling model training or prediction. Input is already a KR-normalized O/E matrix from Juicer dump output — GILoop's demo_from_processed.py path applies patching/training only, so re-normalization would be redundant Data are extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the paper states GILoop is 'not capable enough' to deal with scHi-C despite robustness on low-depth bulk Hi-C Only raw (unnormalized) contact counts are available and no expected-vector calculation or normalization step (e.g., KR, sequencing-depth alignment) will be run — O/E computation on unnormalized counts is out of scope here http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Converts KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrices into distance-normalized observed/expected (O/E) matrices by dividing each observed contact count by the expected contact frequency at the corresponding genomic distance, yielding inputs suitable for paired image and graph sampling in GILoop. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Converts KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrices into distance-normalized observed/expected (O/E) matrices by dividing each observed contact count by the expected contact frequency at the corresponding genomic distance, yielding inputs suitable for paired image and graph sampling in GILoop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a KR-normalized O/E matrix from Juicer dump output — GILoop's demo_from_processed.py path applies patching/training only, so re-normalization would be redundant Data are extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the paper states GILoop is 'not capable enough' to deal with scHi-C despite robustness on low-depth bulk Hi-C Only raw (unnormalized) contact counts are available and no expected-vector calculation or normalization step (e.g., KR, sequencing-depth alignment) will be run — O/E computation on unnormalized counts is out of scope here

skills.description: Use when converting raw KR-normalized Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. Rao et al. GSE63525 at 5 kb bins) into categorical skeleton annotations to train or run predictions with deepC.
skills.name: distance-stratified-contact-decile-binning
skills.search_text: distance-stratified-contact-decile-binning Use when converting raw KR-normalized Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. Rao et al. GSE63525 at 5 kb bins) into categorical skeleton annotations to train or run predictions with deepC. Input is already a normalized or categorical skeleton file — re-binning would destroy the original percentile classes Working with plaid/other binning schemes or raw unnormalized contact maps without KR normalization, where the percentile classes will not match the deepC-trained targets http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 DeepC skeleton preprocessing that percentile-normalizes raw Hi-C contact frequencies by genomic interaction distance, converting continuous contact values into 10 discrete percentile tags (1-10) using an uneven pyramid binning scheme. This reveals longer-range interactions and enhances contrast at domain boundaries for training and prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: DeepC skeleton preprocessing that percentile-normalizes raw Hi-C contact frequencies by genomic interaction distance, converting continuous contact values into 10 discrete percentile tags (1-10) using an uneven pyramid binning scheme. This reveals longer-range interactions and enhances contrast at domain boundaries for training and prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized or categorical skeleton file — re-binning would destroy the original percentile classes Working with plaid/other binning schemes or raw unnormalized contact maps without KR normalization, where the percentile classes will not match the deepC-trained targets

skills.description: Use when a sequence-derived chromatin contact prediction (e.g. from deepC) needs quantitative validation against observed Hi-C on held-out chromosomes, requiring distance-stratified Pearson correlations for raw and smoothed maps.
skills.name: distance-stratified-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: distance-stratified-correlation-analysis Use when a sequence-derived chromatin contact prediction (e.g. from deepC) needs quantitative validation against observed Hi-C on held-out chromosomes, requiring distance-stratified Pearson correlations for raw and smoothed maps. The goal is a direct comparative benchmark of deepC against alternative models such as Akita — the article explicitly defers such comparison to future work Validation target is locus-specific 3C-style data (NG Capture-C, Tiled-C) rather than genome-wide distance-stratified Hi-C agreement Predictions must be run on CPU only — chromosome-scale prediction is prohibitively slow without GPU support http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Validates sequence-based chromatin contact predictions (deepC) against observed Hi-C by computing Pearson correlation coefficients within genomic distance bins on holdout chromosomes, separately for raw and smoothed contact maps. Quantifies prediction accuracy in a cross-validation scheme across cell lines (GM12878 and K562). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Validates sequence-based chromatin contact predictions (deepC) against observed Hi-C by computing Pearson correlation coefficients within genomic distance bins on holdout chromosomes, separately for raw and smoothed contact maps. Quantifies prediction accuracy in a cross-validation scheme across cell lines (GM12878 and K562).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a direct comparative benchmark of deepC against alternative models such as Akita — the article explicitly defers such comparison to future work Validation target is locus-specific 3C-style data (NG Capture-C, Tiled-C) rather than genome-wide distance-stratified Hi-C agreement Predictions must be run on CPU only — chromosome-scale prediction is prohibitively slow without GPU support

skills.description: Use when a SMITE PvalueAnnotation has been built from methylation/expression/ChIP-seq p-values and you must decide whether to weight interval contributions by distance from the TSS, or must verify that weighted and unweighted aggregated scores agree.
skills.name: distance-weighted-genomic-scoring
skills.search_text: distance-weighted-genomic-scoring Use when a SMITE PvalueAnnotation has been built from methylation/expression/ChIP-seq p-values and you must decide whether to weight interval contributions by distance from the TSS, or must verify that weighted and unweighted aggregated scores agree. When the goal is to compare SMITE against FEM or evaluate module identification on a network, rather than to test sensitivity of interval scores to the weight scheme When input p-values have not been pre-filtered (zero p-values and NA p-values must first be replaced with the minimum non-zero p-value and removed, respectively) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A robustness-check skill for SMITE that re-scores genomic intervals using Stouffer-combined p-values with optional distance-based weights (e.g., distance from transcription start site) and demonstrates, via regression against an unweighted run, that final gene scores are essentially unchanged (R^2 ≈ 0.99). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: A robustness-check skill for SMITE that re-scores genomic intervals using Stouffer-combined p-values with optional distance-based weights (e.g., distance from transcription start site) and demonstrates, via regression against an unweighted run, that final gene scores are essentially unchanged (R^2 ≈ 0.99).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to compare SMITE against FEM or evaluate module identification on a network, rather than to test sensitivity of interval scores to the weight scheme When input p-values have not been pre-filtered (zero p-values and NA p-values must first be replaced with the minimum non-zero p-value and removed, respectively)

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a Spark/HDFS-based distributed aligner's scalability: you need per-cluster-size throughput for two algorithmic variants (e.g. --testmode plain vs balancing) on the same dataset.
skills.name: distributed-cluster-throughput-measurement
skills.search_text: distributed-cluster-throughput-measurement Use when benchmarking a Spark/HDFS-based distributed aligner's scalability: you need per-cluster-size throughput for two algorithmic variants (e.g. --testmode plain vs balancing) on the same dataset. Benchmarking mappability, sensitivity, or alignment accuracy rather than speed/scalability — this skill times alignment only and does not compare mapping outputs against truth sets Single-node or scale-up performance testing — the skill requires a multi-node scale-out cluster (10/20/40 slave nodes) served by HDFS End-to-end pipeline timing where index building and input distribution must be included — those stages are deliberately excluded from the measured elapsed time here Measures alignment throughput (reads per second) of a distributed aligner across increasing cluster sizes (10, 20, 40 slave nodes) under two execution variants (plain vs load-balanced) to quantify the scalability gradient and the load-balancing versus shuffling trade-off. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2498-2
skills.summary: Measures alignment throughput (reads per second) of a distributed aligner across increasing cluster sizes (10, 20, 40 slave nodes) under two execution variants (plain vs load-balanced) to quantify the scalability gradient and the load-balancing versus shuffling trade-off.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Benchmarking mappability, sensitivity, or alignment accuracy rather than speed/scalability — this skill times alignment only and does not compare mapping outputs against truth sets Single-node or scale-up performance testing — the skill requires a multi-node scale-out cluster (10/20/40 slave nodes) served by HDFS End-to-end pipeline timing where index building and input distribution must be included — those stages are deliberately excluded from the measured elapsed time here

skills.description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated sequencing reads (e.g., WGBS FASTQ from simulated Sherman data or GEO accessions) is computationally bottlenecked on a single node and a scale-out Spark/HDFS cluster is available.
skills.name: distributed-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: distributed-short-read-alignment Use when aligning bisulfite-treated sequencing reads (e.g., WGBS FASTQ from simulated Sherman data or GEO accessions) is computationally bottlenecked on a single node and a scale-out Spark/HDFS cluster is available. When the task is methylation array interrogation (Illumina 27K/450K/850K BeadChip) rather than bisulfite sequencing read alignment When no Spark/HDFS cluster or Spark >= 1.6 / HDFS 2.6 environment is available and the dataset fits single-node tools like Bismark When reads are not bisulfite-treated; a general-purpose aligner without three-letter/wildcard conversion is appropriate instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A scale-out short-read alignment skill that parallelizes bisulfite 'three-letter' read mapping across an Apache Spark cluster (BiSpark), addressing the up-to-4x data expansion that makes bisulfite alignment a bottleneck of methylome analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2498-2
skills.summary: A scale-out short-read alignment skill that parallelizes bisulfite 'three-letter' read mapping across an Apache Spark cluster (BiSpark), addressing the up-to-4x data expansion that makes bisulfite alignment a bottleneck of methylome analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the task is methylation array interrogation (Illumina 27K/450K/850K BeadChip) rather than bisulfite sequencing read alignment When no Spark/HDFS cluster or Spark >= 1.6 / HDFS 2.6 environment is available and the dataset fits single-node tools like Bismark When reads are not bisulfite-treated; a general-purpose aligner without three-letter/wildcard conversion is appropriate instead

skills.name: dmr-caller-concordance-benchmarking
skills.search_text: dmr-caller-concordance-benchmarking Use when you have simulated or known-composition heterogeneous bisulfite sequencing mixtures plus methylation calls from the sorted underlying cell types, and need to quantify how many independently called DMRs a deconvolution method recovers as i-DMRs. The input is a single homogeneous sample with no sorted comparator cell types available to call reference DMRs against You want to evaluate subpopulation prevalence/fraction estimation accuracy rather than DMR-level concordance The regions of interest contain allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where DXM results require special care and would confound concordance interpretation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Benchmarks DXM intrasample DMR (i-DMR) calls against DMRs called by an independent caller (DSS) on sorted cell types, quantifying overlap with bedtools. skills.summary: Benchmarks DXM intrasample DMR (i-DMR) calls against DMRs called by an independent caller (DSS) on sorted cell types, quantifying overlap with bedtools. skills.description: Use when comparing DXM i-DMRs from heterogeneous bisulfite data against an independently called DMR set between sorted reference cell types, or when a DMR caller with explicit count-based statistics is needed on sorted methylation counts.

skills.search_text: dmr-statistical-calling-from-bisulfite-methylation-counts Use when comparing DXM i-DMRs from heterogeneous bisulfite data against an independently called DMR set between sorted reference cell types, or when a DMR caller with explicit count-based statistics is needed on sorted methylation counts. skills.search_text: dmr-threshold-filtering Use when beta-binomial-tested clustered regions from MethylC-seq data must be filtered into a final DMR table using CpG-count, methylation-difference, and p/q-value cutoffs. Input is raw per-CpG methylation counts that have not yet been clustered into regions by combine_CpG_sites.py The analysis requires modeling sets of regions, quantitative traits, or batch effects, which DMRfinder explicitly does not support The goal is single-CpG-site differential testing rather than whole-region testing http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filters clustered genomic regions for differential methylation by applying DMRfinder's reporting thresholds — minimum CpG count, minimum methylation difference, and maximum p-/q-value cutoffs — after beta-binomial testing with DSS, so that only biologically meaningful DMRs are reported. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Filters clustered genomic regions for differential methylation by applying DMRfinder's reporting thresholds — minimum CpG count, minimum methylation difference, and maximum p-/q-value cutoffs — after beta-binomial testing with DSS, so that only biologically meaningful DMRs are reported.

skills.description: Use when you have a GenBank genome and a set of genomic positions (e.g., ChIP-chip/ChIP-seq peak centers or transcription start sites) and need to discover or reproduce a DNA binding motif as a sequence logo and PWM.
skills.name: dna-binding-motif-information-content-alignment
skills.search_text: dna-binding-motif-information-content-alignment Use when you have a GenBank genome and a set of genomic positions (e.g., ChIP-chip/ChIP-seq peak centers or transcription start sites) and need to discover or reproduce a DNA binding motif as a sequence logo and PWM. You lack both a GenBank genome file and a coordinate-anchored sites file — Delila-PY requires exactly these two inputs and cannot work from raw reads or an unanchored sequence set. Your goal is de novo motif discovery from sequences with no genomic coordinates or strand information; the sites file format (chromosome, name, strand, base pair position) is mandatory. You need an interactive, hand-tuned motif analysis — Delila-PY uses standard (often default) Delila parameter values for quick, reproducible runs, sacrificing the full flexibility of running the Delila programs individually. http://edamontology.org/topic_3125 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A Delila-PY–based three-cycle information-theory workflow that aligns genomic binding-site sequences to maximize information content and produces a DNA sequence logo and PWM. It was validated by reproducing the R. sphaeroides FnrL binding motif from ChIP-chip-derived genomic locations. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: A Delila-PY–based three-cycle information-theory workflow that aligns genomic binding-site sequences to maximize information content and produces a DNA sequence logo and PWM. It was validated by reproducing the R. sphaeroides FnrL binding motif from ChIP-chip-derived genomic locations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack both a GenBank genome file and a coordinate-anchored sites file — Delila-PY requires exactly these two inputs and cannot work from raw reads or an unanchored sequence set. Your goal is de novo motif discovery from sequences with no genomic coordinates or strand information; the sites file format (chromosome, name, strand, base pair position) is mandatory. You need an interactive, hand-tuned motif analysis — Delila-PY uses standard (often default) Delila parameter values for quick, reproducible runs, sacrificing the full flexibility of running the Delila programs individually.

skills.description: Use when running Delila-PY's second cycle and per-sequence information content (bits) values are available, and poorly matching sequences (≤0 bits) must be removed before regenerating the book with delila.
skills.name: dna-binding-motif-sequence-curation
skills.search_text: dna-binding-motif-sequence-curation Use when running Delila-PY's second cycle and per-sequence information content (bits) values are available, and poorly matching sequences (≤0 bits) must be removed before regenerating the book with delila. The pipeline is in cycle 1, where malign and malin select the highest-information alignment and no ≤0-bit cutoff is applied Per-sequence information content values have not yet been computed (alist/encode/cmp/rseq have not run) Generating the final motif in cycle 3, which uses alist, encode, cmp, rseq, dalvec, and makelogo rather than ri-based filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Removes poorly matching sequences from the Delila-PY cycle-2 book by applying the ri program's deterministic cutoff: any sequence with ≤0 bits of information content (computed via alist/encode/cmp/rseq) is dropped, and the retained sequences are fed back to delila to regenerate an updated book file before motif generation. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: Removes poorly matching sequences from the Delila-PY cycle-2 book by applying the ri program's deterministic cutoff: any sequence with ≤0 bits of information content (computed via alist/encode/cmp/rseq) is dropped, and the retained sequences are fed back to delila to regenerate an updated book file before motif generation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The pipeline is in cycle 1, where malign and malin select the highest-information alignment and no ≤0-bit cutoff is applied Per-sequence information content values have not yet been computed (alist/encode/cmp/rseq have not run) Generating the final motif in cycle 3, which uses alist, encode, cmp, rseq, dalvec, and makelogo rather than ri-based filtering

skills.description: Use when building DNAffinity feature matrices from DNA sequences and the direct-readout electrostatic block must be derived per tetramer, or when validating the encoding against the AACT worked example.
skills.name: dna-electrostatic-direct-readout-encoding
skills.search_text: dna-electrostatic-direct-readout-encoding Use when building DNAffinity feature matrices from DNA sequences and the direct-readout electrostatic block must be derived per tetramer, or when validating the encoding against the AACT worked example. Input is already a DNAffinity feature matrix or a precomputed tetramer feature table — the encoding step is already done The analysis targets indirect-readout geometry/flexibility (AVG equilibrium and DIAG stiffness values from MD tetramer tables) rather than chemical-group electrostatics Sequences contain non-standard or modified nucleobases outside the four canonical bases covered by the integer acceptor/donor/hydrophobic coding scheme http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Encodes the direct-readout (chemical-group) component of DNAffinity features by assigning, per base-pair step, an integer electrostatic scheme coding acceptor, donor, and hydrophobic chemical groups, then column-summing base codes over each tetramer to yield five values per tetramer. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Encodes the direct-readout (chemical-group) component of DNAffinity features by assigning, per base-pair step, an integer electrostatic scheme coding acceptor, donor, and hydrophobic chemical groups, then column-summing base codes over each tetramer to yield five values per tetramer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a DNAffinity feature matrix or a precomputed tetramer feature table — the encoding step is already done The analysis targets indirect-readout geometry/flexibility (AVG equilibrium and DIAG stiffness values from MD tetramer tables) rather than chemical-group electrostatics Sequences contain non-standard or modified nucleobases outside the four canonical bases covered by the integer acceptor/donor/hydrophobic coding scheme

The task input is short-range (well below the 1 million bp context DNALONGBENCH targets) — benchmarks limited to short-range tasks are explicitly out of scope for this suite The goal is to evaluate an expert/task-specific model (e.g. Enformer, Akita, Puffin, ABC) rather than fine-tune a foundation model You intend to use a quadratic self-attention transformer (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) on ultra-long inputs — the article notes this quadratic cost renders such tasks infeasible for these models http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fine-tunes pretrained DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) on the five DNALONGBENCH long-range genomics tasks (ETGP, eQTL, CMP, RSAP, TISP) so their performance can be compared against task-specific expert models and a CNN baseline. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Fine-tunes pretrained DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) on the five DNALONGBENCH long-range genomics tasks (ETGP, eQTL, CMP, RSAP, TISP) so their performance can be compared against task-specific expert models and a CNN baseline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task input is short-range (well below the 1 million bp context DNALONGBENCH targets) — benchmarks limited to short-range tasks are explicitly out of scope for this suite The goal is to evaluate an expert/task-specific model (e.g. Enformer, Akita, Puffin, ABC) rather than fine-tune a foundation model You intend to use a quadratic self-attention transformer (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) on ultra-long inputs — the article notes this quadratic cost renders such tasks infeasible for these models

skills.search_text: dna-kmer-sequence-embedding Use when raw enhancer DNA sequences (FASTA) must be converted into fixed feature vectors/matrices before feeding a CNN classifier such as DeepSE, and pre-trained k-mer embeddings exist for the genome. skills.search_text: dna-mechanical-property-feature-classification Use when random-forest models have been trained on multiple experimental binding datasets (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) and you need to compare which DNA-property feature classes drive predictive power in each run. skills.summary: Aggregates individual random-forest feature importances from DNAffinity regressors into three feature classes — sequence composition, indirect readout, and direct readout — to determine whether class importance depends on the experimental training dataset (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX).

skills.description: Use when analyzing reads generated by bisulfite-free methylation assays such as TAPS or 5hmC-CATCH, where non-CpG methylation is low and the default 3-letter BS alignment wastes read complexity.
skills.name: dna-methylation-call-from-bisulfite-free-reads
skills.search_text: dna-methylation-call-from-bisulfite-free-reads Use when analyzing reads generated by bisulfite-free methylation assays such as TAPS or 5hmC-CATCH, where non-CpG methylation is low and the default 3-letter BS alignment wastes read complexity. Data generated by BS-seq protocols: 3-letter mode with -m BS is mandatory; 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low Tissues with high non-CpG methylation (e.g., ESCs), which violate the low-CpH assumption of 4-letter analysis Input is already aligned BAM or an existing methylation call table — this skill performs alignment and calling jointly via Msuite http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Calls DNA methylation from bisulfite-free protocol reads (e.g., TAPS) using Msuite's unique 4-letter alignment mode, which preserves cytosines to exploit higher nucleotide complexity, then deduces CpG/CpH methylation densities for accuracy evaluation. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Calls DNA methylation from bisulfite-free protocol reads (e.g., TAPS) using Msuite's unique 4-letter alignment mode, which preserves cytosines to exploit higher nucleotide complexity, then deduces CpG/CpH methylation densities for accuracy evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data generated by BS-seq protocols: 3-letter mode with -m BS is mandatory; 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data where non-CpG methylation is very low Tissues with high non-CpG methylation (e.g., ESCs), which violate the low-CpH assumption of 4-letter analysis Input is already aligned BAM or an existing methylation call table — this skill performs alignment and calling jointly via Msuite

skills.description: Use when methylation calls from a bisulfite (BS) or bisulfite-free (TAPS) library have been produced by Msuite and you need per-CpG methylation densities, or mode-to-mode (4-letter vs 3-letter) call agreement statistics.
skills.name: dna-methylation-call-parsing
skills.search_text: dna-methylation-call-parsing Use when methylation calls from a bisulfite (BS) or bisulfite-free (TAPS) library have been produced by Msuite and you need per-CpG methylation densities, or mode-to-mode (4-letter vs 3-letter) call agreement statistics. Data are plain (non-methylation) sequencing reads or already-processed feature tables such as bedGraph methylation tracks BS-seq data would be run through 4-letter mode — the README states 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data with very low non-CpG methylation; BS data MUST use '-3 -m BS' Input reads are from ATAC-me or similar protocols requiring '-k nextera' rather than standard methylation calling http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parse and compare per-CpG methylation call files (e.g., Msuite.CpG.meth.call) produced by Msuite's 3-letter or 4-letter alignment modes, quantifying agreement between modes via Pearson correlation of methylation densities and the fraction of discordant CpG sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127

skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are plain (non-methylation) sequencing reads or already-processed feature tables such as bedGraph methylation tracks BS-seq data would be run through 4-letter mode — the README states 4-letter mode ONLY supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data with very low non-CpG methylation; BS data MUST use '-3 -m BS' Input reads are from ATAC-me or similar protocols requiring '-k nextera' rather than standard methylation calling

skills.search_text: dna-methylation-pcr-bias-calibration Use when pyrosequenced or MiSeq-amplified methylation levels in a targeted CGI/DMR need PCR-bias correction, and standard controls with known methylation percentages (AMPs) are available alongside case and control samples. Input is epigenome-wide array data or whole-genome methylation rather than targeted bisulfite amplicon sequencing of a CGI/DMR No standard controls with known methylation percentages (AMPs) exist, so calibration curves cannot be derived Only average methylation per region is available, since the method explicitly avoids 'one-at-a-time' CpG calibration but requires CpG-resolved levels Bayesian PCR-bias calibration of bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation levels using MethylCal, which fits joint calibration curves across all CpGs of a CGI or DMR via INLA and corrects observed methylation degrees in case/control samples. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Bayesian PCR-bias calibration of bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation levels using MethylCal, which fits joint calibration curves across all CpGs of a CGI or DMR via INLA and corrects observed methylation degrees in case/control samples.

skills.description: Use when you need to enumerate all degenerate IUPAC motifs of length L whose exact instances all occur in a positive DNA dataset, or to reimplement/validate lattice-based motif generalization from counted L-mers.
skills.name: dna-motif-generalization
skills.search_text: dna-motif-generalization Use when you need to enumerate all degenerate IUPAC motifs of length L whose exact instances all occur in a positive DNA dataset, or to reimplement/validate lattice-based motif generalization from counted L-mers. When a heuristic or restricted search space is acceptable and exhaustiveness is not required — this skill's value is exactly that no motif is excluded a priori When motifs are variable-length or gapped (DiNAMO builds fixed-length IUPAC motifs of length L in scanning or fixed-position mode) When input is protein sequence or already-degenerate consensus strings rather than raw DNA from which exact L-mers must be counted http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reconstructs DiNAMO's exhaustive construction of degenerate IUPAC motifs by generalizing exact DNA L-mers position-by-position along the 4-level IUPAC character lattice (A,C,G,T → K,M,R,S,W,Y → B,D,H,V → N), keeping only motifs whose every exact instance is present in the hashtable of counted L-mers, so the motif space is never restricted a priori. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Reconstructs DiNAMO's exhaustive construction of degenerate IUPAC motifs by generalizing exact DNA L-mers position-by-position along the 4-level IUPAC character lattice (A,C,G,T → K,M,R,S,W,Y → B,D,H,V → N), keeping only motifs whose every exact instance is present in the hashtable of counted L-mers, so the motif space is never restricted a priori.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a heuristic or restricted search space is acceptable and exhaustiveness is not required — this skill's value is exactly that no motif is excluded a priori When motifs are variable-length or gapped (DiNAMO builds fixed-length IUPAC motifs of length L in scanning or fixed-position mode) When input is protein sequence or already-degenerate consensus strings rather than raw DNA from which exact L-mers must be counted

skills.description: Use when searching a large signal (e.g. ChIP-seq peak) FASTA against a control FASTA for over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs of a fixed length, without any prior restriction on the motif.
skills.name: dna-motif-overrepresentation-analysis
skills.search_text: dna-motif-overrepresentation-analysis Use when searching a large signal (e.g. ChIP-seq peak) FASTA against a control FASTA for over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs of a fixed length, without any prior restriction on the motif. When motifs must be exact strings rather than degenerate IUPAC models — tools like RSAT handle exact strings instead When a position-specific frequency-matrix (EM-based) search is required, e.g. the MEME algorithm, rather than exact IUPAC motif enumeration When only a single sequence set is available with no control/negative dataset, since scoring relies on a 2x2 contingency table over positive vs negative datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 An exact, exhaustive method for discovering over-represented degenerate IUPAC DNA motifs in a positive sequence dataset compared to a negative control, implemented in the DiNAMO software. skills.search_text: dna-sequence-binary-encoding Use when raw 41-nt DNA sequences (A/C/G/T FASTA records) must be converted into fixed-length binary features before classifier training, e.g. reproducing csDMA's Binary feature block alongside Motif and Kmer subsets. Input sequences are already encoded as a numeric feature table (e.g. Motif score matrix or 336-dim Kmer vectors) rather than raw FASTA nucleotide strings Samples are not fixed-length 41-nt DNA reads, or contain characters outside A/C/G/T (e.g. RNA or ambiguous IUPAC codes), since the three dichotomies assume exactly A, C, G, T http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes each nucleotide of a 41-nt DNA sample into three binary physico-chemical indicator rules (purine/pyrimidine x, A/T-vs-C/G y, A/C-vs-G/T z), producing a 3 × 41 = 123-element feature vector per sequence for csDMA's 6mA prediction model. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4

skills.description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking multi-task DNA regression on DNALONGBENCH RSAP (TensorFlow-record train/valid/test splits) and per-sample PCC on human vs mouse tracks is the target metric.
skills.name: dna-sequence-multitask-regression
skills.search_text: dna-sequence-multitask-regression Use when reproducing or benchmarking multi-task DNA regression on DNALONGBENCH RSAP (TensorFlow-record train/valid/test splits) and per-sample PCC on human vs mouse tracks is the target metric. skills.name: drosophila-core-promoter-motif-analysis
skills.search_text: drosophila-core-promoter-motif-analysis Use when you have scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor point (e.g. csRNA-seq TSSs) and need to determine whether motif presence correlates with biological activity at specific positions relative to that anchor, such as core promoter element positioning. MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library, so this skill is the wrong choice if the goal is de novo motif discovery/assembly (left to future work per the discussion) The input is a single unscored sequence or sequences lacking a meaningful continuous biological score — MEPP's positional profiles require sequences scored across a continuum reflecting two extremes of biological interest Sequences are dominated by degenerate/repeat bases beyond the accepted threshold (--dgt, default 100) or contain no anchor point to center the positional profile on http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Applies MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) to ±200 bp sequences centered on high-confidence Drosophila csRNA-seq TSSs scored by log-transformed coverage, using the fixed Ohler Drosophila core promoter motif library to compute position-dependent enrichment profiles for motifs such as Inr, TATA-box, and DPE relative to the TSS anchor point. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Applies MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) to ±200 bp sequences centered on high-confidence Drosophila csRNA-seq TSSs scored by log-transformed coverage, using the fixed Ohler Drosophila core promoter motif library to compute position-dependent enrichment profiles for motifs such as Inr, TATA-box, and DPE relative to the TSS anchor point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library, so this skill is the wrong choice if the goal is de novo motif discovery/assembly (left to future work per the discussion) The input is a single unscored sequence or sequences lacking a meaningful continuous biological score — MEPP's positional profiles require sequences scored across a continuum reflecting two extremes of biological interest Sequences are dominated by degenerate/repeat bases beyond the accepted threshold (--dgt, default 100) or contain no anchor point to center the positional profile on

skills.description: Use when you need to identify transcriptional regulators independently associated with pharmacological drug response from cell line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation) plus ChIP-seq target information, as with CCLE/ENCODE and PLX4720.
skills.name: drug-response-biomarker-identification
skills.search_text: drug-response-biomarker-identification Use when you need to identify transcriptional regulators independently associated with pharmacological drug response from cell line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation) plus ChIP-seq target information, as with CCLE/ENCODE and PLX4720. No ChIP-seq data are available for a TR, or the ChIP-seq data have too few targets, which would mislead target-based identification The question is secondary/acquired resistance arising post-treatment (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation in erlotinib resistance) — RePhine uses pre-treatment CCLE data and cannot detect it Reliable target information is unavailable for the TRs of interest, since RePhine identifies drug response-related TRs only through their targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Regression-based identification of drug response-related transcriptional regulators (TRs) by integrating CCLE pharmacogenomic data with ENCODE ChIP-seq-derived regulation potential (RP) scores, as implemented in the RePhine R package. It recovers resistance- and sensitivity-associated TRs (e.g., for BRAF inhibitor PLX4720) while adjusting confounders such as CNVs and kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Regression-based identification of drug response-related transcriptional regulators (TRs) by integrating CCLE pharmacogenomic data with ENCODE ChIP-seq-derived regulation potential (RP) scores, as implemented in the RePhine R package. It recovers resistance- and sensitivity-associated TRs (e.g., for BRAF inhibitor PLX4720) while adjusting confounders such as CNVs and kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ChIP-seq data are available for a TR, or the ChIP-seq data have too few targets, which would mislead target-based identification The question is secondary/acquired resistance arising post-treatment (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation in erlotinib resistance) — RePhine uses pre-treatment CCLE data and cannot detect it Reliable target information is unavailable for the TRs of interest, since RePhine identifies drug response-related TRs only through their targets

skills.description: Use when comparing methods for identifying drug response-related TRs on synthetic pharmacogenomic data (gene expression + drug response + ChIP-seq targets), especially under injected noise or spurious-correlation confounders.
skills.name: drug-response-tr-benchmarking
skills.search_text: drug-response-tr-benchmarking Use when comparing methods for identifying drug response-related TRs on synthetic pharmacogenomic data (gene expression + drug response + ChIP-seq targets), especially under injected noise or spurious-correlation confounders. No reliable target information (ChIP-seq data missing or with too few targets) exists — RePhine identification would be misled The goal is detecting acquired/secondary resistance from post-treatment data — CCLE lacks post-treatment data so secondary resistance (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation for erlotinib) cannot be detected The task is establishing causal TR-drug relationships rather than association-based benchmarking — TR knockout/activation experiments with drug response examination are required for causal validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Benchmark RePhine, a regression-based pharmacogenomic and ChIP-seq data integration method, against Pearson correlation analysis, logistic regression, and GSEA on simulated pharmacogenomic data with added noises or confounders to quantify its superiority in identifying drug response-related transcriptional regulators (TRs). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Benchmark RePhine, a regression-based pharmacogenomic and ChIP-seq data integration method, against Pearson correlation analysis, logistic regression, and GSEA on simulated pharmacogenomic data with added noises or confounders to quantify its superiority in identifying drug response-related transcriptional regulators (TRs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No reliable target information (ChIP-seq data missing or with too few targets) exists — RePhine identification would be misled The goal is detecting acquired/secondary resistance from post-treatment data — CCLE lacks post-treatment data so secondary resistance (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation for erlotinib) cannot be detected The task is establishing causal TR-drug relationships rather than association-based benchmarking — TR knockout/activation experiments with drug response examination are required for causal validation

skills.description: Use when a drug-sensitivity table (e.g. CCLE pharmacological profiles) can be split into mutation-defined groups — such as BRAF+H3K27me3/PRC2 double mutants versus BRAF-only — and the goal is a two-sample test of response difference.
skills.name: drug-sensitivity-group-comparison
skills.search_text: drug-sensitivity-group-comparison Use when a drug-sensitivity table (e.g. CCLE pharmacological profiles) can be split into mutation-defined groups — such as BRAF+H3K27me3/PRC2 double mutants versus BRAF-only — and the goal is a two-sample test of response difference. You only have mRNA expression levels of a transcriptional regulator and no per-cell-line drug-sensitivity values — use the RePhine association workflow instead of a group t-test. Groups are defined by a continuous covariate rather than discrete mutation categories (e.g. copy-number-adjusted expression) — regression-based association is more appropriate. No mutation annotations are available to form the BRAF+PRC2 and BRAF-only groups, so the two-sample comparison cannot be constructed. http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Statistically compares pharmacological sensitivity measurements (e.g. CCLE PLX4720 response values) between mutation-defined cell-line groups, testing whether an alteration such as loss-of-function of EZH2/PRC2 changes drug response. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Statistically compares pharmacological sensitivity measurements (e.g. CCLE PLX4720 response values) between mutation-defined cell-line groups, testing whether an alteration such as loss-of-function of EZH2/PRC2 changes drug response.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have mRNA expression levels of a transcriptional regulator and no per-cell-line drug-sensitivity values — use the RePhine association workflow instead of a group t-test. Groups are defined by a continuous covariate rather than discrete mutation categories (e.g. copy-number-adjusted expression) — regression-based association is more appropriate. No mutation annotations are available to form the BRAF+PRC2 and BRAF-only groups, so the two-sample comparison cannot be constructed.

skills.description: Use when MethylC-seq methylation counts have already been clustered into genomic regions (combined.csv) and you need to test regions for differential methylation between two or more sample groups.
skills.name: dss-wald-test-workflow
skills.search_text: dss-wald-test-workflow Use when MethylC-seq methylation counts have already been clustered into genomic regions (combined.csv) and you need to test regions for differential methylation between two or more sample groups. Input is per-CpG-site methylation counts rather than clustered-region counts — cluster the CpGs first with combine_CpG_sites.py You need to model sets of regions or quantitative traits, or account for batch effects — DMRfinder explicitly does not support these The comparison goal is finding per-site differential methylation rather than DMRs over multiple CpG sites http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Tests clustered genomic regions for differential methylation between sample groups using the DSS beta-binomial hierarchical model and Wald tests, as implemented in DMRfinder's findDMRs.r, which tests whole regions (methylation counts conglomerated within clusters) rather than individual CpG sites to reduce hypothesis count and increase power. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Tests clustered genomic regions for differential methylation between sample groups using the DSS beta-binomial hierarchical model and Wald tests, as implemented in DMRfinder's findDMRs.r, which tests whole regions (methylation counts conglomerated within clusters) rather than individual CpG sites to reduce hypothesis count and increase power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is per-CpG-site methylation counts rather than clustered-region counts — cluster the CpGs first with combine_CpG_sites.py You need to model sets of regions or quantitative traits, or account for batch effects — DMRfinder explicitly does not support these The comparison goal is finding per-site differential methylation rather than DMRs over multiple CpG sites

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq enrichment measurements within peak regions (e.g. MACS2-called peaks) must be aligned and clustered by shape similarity in a completely unsupervised way, without transcription start sites or gene annotation.
skills.name: dtw-alignment-of-epigenomic-peak-shapes
skills.search_text: dtw-alignment-of-epigenomic-peak-shapes Use when ChIP-seq enrichment measurements within peak regions (e.g. MACS2-called peaks) must be aligned and clustered by shape similarity in a completely unsupervised way, without transcription start sites or gene annotation. When gene annotation, TSS anchors, or supervised labels are available and preferred for alignment When peaks are shorter than 5 bins, longer than 1000 bins, or have fewer than 10 counts — these are filtered out before DGW When standard hierarchical clustering on raw (unaligned) profiles suffices — it only succeeds for small noise/modifications (v<0.15, p<0.15) http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Unsupervised simultaneous alignment and clustering of epigenomic ChIP-seq peak shapes using Dynamic Genome Warping (DGW), which applies Dynamic Time Warping to adaptively rescale and align genomic distances across multiple marks, grouping regions of interest with similar shapes without TSS or gene annotation anchors. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Unsupervised simultaneous alignment and clustering of epigenomic ChIP-seq peak shapes using Dynamic Genome Warping (DGW), which applies Dynamic Time Warping to adaptively rescale and align genomic distances across multiple marks, grouping regions of interest with similar shapes without TSS or gene annotation anchors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When gene annotation, TSS anchors, or supervised labels are available and preferred for alignment When peaks are shorter than 5 bins, longer than 1000 bins, or have fewer than 10 counts — these are filtered out before DGW When standard hierarchical clustering on raw (unaligned) profiles suffices — it only succeeds for small noise/modifications (v<0.15, p<0.15)

skills.description: Use when clustering multiple epigenomic marks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage vectors per 50 bp bin) by shape and you need a warping-invariant pairwise distance plus per-cluster prototype sequences.
skills.name: dtw-prototype-shape-averaging
skills.search_text: dtw-prototype-shape-averaging Use when clustering multiple epigenomic marks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage vectors per 50 bp bin) by shape and you need a warping-invariant pairwise distance plus per-cluster prototype sequences. Peaks shorter than 5 or longer than 1000 bins, or with fewer than 10 counts — these were filtered out before alignment in the DGW workflow Unexpressed regions lacking any bin with more than 10 reads (the --min-pileup constraint) — such regions are ignored upstream When accurate alignment requires external landmarks such as transcription start sites or gene annotation — DGW is designed to align without such information http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Multidimensional DTW alignment of epigenomic coverage tracks (binned 50 bp per peak) constrained by a Sakoe-Chiba band of width 12, followed by scaled prioritised shape averaging to derive a prototype sequence per dendrogram node in DGW. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Multidimensional DTW alignment of epigenomic coverage tracks (binned 50 bp per peak) constrained by a Sakoe-Chiba band of width 12, followed by scaled prioritised shape averaging to derive a prototype sequence per dendrogram node in DGW.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks shorter than 5 or longer than 1000 bins, or with fewer than 10 counts — these were filtered out before alignment in the DGW workflow Unexpressed regions lacking any bin with more than 10 reads (the --min-pileup constraint) — such regions are ignored upstream When accurate alignment requires external landmarks such as transcription start sites or gene annotation — DGW is designed to align without such information

skills.description: Use when epigenomic ChIP-Seq peak regions (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3/H3K9ac K562) have already been DGW-aligned and clustered and you need to visually inspect DTW-warped heat-maps, cluster prototypes, and validate alignment against TSS/FSS points of interest.
skills.name: dtw-warped-profile-visualization
skills.search_text: dtw-warped-profile-visualization Use when epigenomic ChIP-Seq peak regions (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3/H3K9ac K562) have already been DGW-aligned and clustered and you need to visually inspect DTW-warped heat-maps, cluster prototypes, and validate alignment against TSS/FSS points of interest. Raw BAM/ChIP-Seq data that has not yet been peak-called (MACS2), binned into 50 bp windows, and clustered — run the DGW worker first to produce the .dgw artefacts Data lacking points of interest — regions without any entry in fss.poi should be dropped with --ignore-no-poi-regions, so POI entropy validation is impossible without annotation Datasets where standard feature tables or pre-computed profiles suffice and shape-based alignment adds no value http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reconstruct the DGW dgw-explorer aligned-cluster heatmap visualisation: launch the interactive explorer on a {prefix}_config.dgw run, cut the dendrogram into shape-based clusters, and render four-panel per-cluster views (prototype, average DTW projection, original and warped coverage heat-maps) with points-of-interest overlays and POI entropy validation. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Reconstruct the DGW dgw-explorer aligned-cluster heatmap visualisation: launch the interactive explorer on a {prefix}_config.dgw run, cut the dendrogram into shape-based clusters, and render four-panel per-cluster views (prototype, average DTW projection, original and warped coverage heat-maps) with points-of-interest overlays and POI entropy validation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Raw BAM/ChIP-Seq data that has not yet been peak-called (MACS2), binned into 50 bp windows, and clustered — run the DGW worker first to produce the .dgw artefacts Data lacking points of interest — regions without any entry in fss.poi should be dropped with --ignore-no-poi-regions, so POI entropy validation is impossible without annotation Datasets where standard feature tables or pre-computed profiles suffice and shape-based alignment adds no value

skills.description: Use when you have a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode matrix and need a close-to-binary accessibility matrix; scATAC-seq open-chromatin data is inherently close-to-binary and binarization removes replicate-specific imputation artifacts.
skills.name: dual-mean-threshold-imputation-filtering
skills.search_text: dual-mean-threshold-imputation-filtering Use when you have a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode matrix and need a close-to-binary accessibility matrix; scATAC-seq open-chromatin data is inherently close-to-binary and binarization removes replicate-specific imputation artifacts. The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data — the article notes direct application of scRNA-seq methods is unsuitable for scATAC-seq precisely because of its close-to-binary nature, and this rule is calibrated for scATAC-seq peak data The input matrix is already binary — re-thresholding would destroy the values You need continuous imputed values for downstream quantitative analysis rather than binary accessibility calls http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Binarizes a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq accessibility matrix (peaks x barcodes) by keeping an entry as 1 only where the imputed value exceeds both the row (peak) mean of the raw matrix and the column (cell) mean of the raw matrix, reproducing SCALE's --binary behavior. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12630-7
skills.summary: Binarizes a SCALE-imputed scATAC-seq accessibility matrix (peaks x barcodes) by keeping an entry as 1 only where the imputed value exceeds both the row (peak) mean of the raw matrix and the column (cell) mean of the raw matrix, reproducing SCALE's --binary behavior.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw scRNA-seq expression data — the article notes direct application of scRNA-seq methods is unsuitable for scATAC-seq precisely because of its close-to-binary nature, and this rule is calibrated for scATAC-seq peak data The input matrix is already binary — re-thresholding would destroy the values You need continuous imputed values for downstream quantitative analysis rather than binary accessibility calls

skills.description: Use when scanning centered, scored DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA with score headers) for transcription factor motif occurrences where motif strand is unknown, and positional enrichment profiles must reflect matches on either orientation.
skills.name: dual-orientation-motif-scoring
skills.search_text: dual-orientation-motif-scoring Use when scanning centered, scored DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA with score headers) for transcription factor motif occurrences where motif strand is unknown, and positional enrichment profiles must reflect matches on either orientation. The assay resolves motif strand (e.g. ChIP-nexus) and only the forward orientation should be counted — use --orientations '+' instead of the dual-orientation max rule The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than scanning a fixed motif library, since MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library Sequences are not centered on a common anchor point (TSS, peak summit, or motif), so positional enrichment relative to an anchor is not meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Scores every JASPAR PWM against both the forward and reverse-complement strands of one-hot encoded sequences and collapses the two scans with a max rule, so each positional heatmap cell carries the strongest strand-agnostic motif match excess (score − MOODS threshold). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Scores every JASPAR PWM against both the forward and reverse-complement strands of one-hot encoded sequences and collapses the two scans with a max rule, so each positional heatmap cell carries the strongest strand-agnostic motif match excess (score − MOODS threshold).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The assay resolves motif strand (e.g. ChIP-nexus) and only the forward orientation should be counted — use --orientations '+' instead of the dual-orientation max rule The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than scanning a fixed motif library, since MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library Sequences are not centered on a common anchor point (TSS, peak summit, or motif), so positional enrichment relative to an anchor is not meaningful

skills.description: Use when a mapped-read BAM from a NEAT ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline step must be deduplicated according to user-defined duplicate-management settings in AdvancedSettings.txt.
skills.name: duplicate-read-removal
skills.search_text: duplicate-read-removal Use when a mapped-read BAM from a NEAT ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline step must be deduplicated according to user-defined duplicate-management settings in AdvancedSettings.txt. Input is raw FASTQ rather than an aligned BAM — alignment (NEAT 'map') must happen first The library protocol requires retaining duplicates (e.g. ultra-low-input where amplification is expected) and the AdvancedSettings.txt policy explicitly keeps them Peak calling has already been performed; filtering precedes peakcalling in NEAT's pipeline order http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Removes or manages PCR/optical duplicate reads from aligned BAM files using samtools rmdup, as implemented in NEAT's 'filter' module within its ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Removes or manages PCR/optical duplicate reads from aligned BAM files using samtools rmdup, as implemented in NEAT's 'filter' module within its ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ rather than an aligned BAM — alignment (NEAT 'map') must happen first The library protocol requires retaining duplicates (e.g. ultra-low-input where amplification is expected) and the AdvancedSettings.txt policy explicitly keeps them Peak calling has already been performed; filtering precedes peakcalling in NEAT's pipeline order

skills.description: Use when two or more genomic regions must be compared by their single-track chromatin state sequences (e.g. ChromHMM output) rather than raw multi-track signal matrices, and ordered state patterns—not just state frequencies—must drive the similarity score.
skills.name: dynamic-programming-alignment-scoring
skills.search_text: dynamic-programming-alignment-scoring Use when two or more genomic regions must be compared by their single-track chromatin state sequences (e.g. ChromHMM output) rather than raw multi-track signal matrices, and ordered state patterns—not just state frequencies—must drive the similarity score. The analysis only needs overall state composition—comparing state frequency vectors without sequential order is the naive baseline, and the alignment machinery is unnecessary overhead Input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices of differing dimensions rather than discrete chromatin state label sequences; annotation (e.g. ChromHMM) must be applied first Motifs or regions dominated by the quiescent state 'o', which lacks good biological interpretation and was excluded in the paper's motif analyses http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 EpiAlign-style local alignment of chromatin state sequences via a modified Smith–Waterman dynamic programming recurrence with state-weight-based match (MF = W(k,S1)+W(l,S2)), mismatch (NF = -1.5*(W(k,S1)+W(l,S2))) and deletion (DF = -1*W(k,S)) score functions, applied after run-length compression of ChromHMM state labels. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: EpiAlign-style local alignment of chromatin state sequences via a modified Smith–Waterman dynamic programming recurrence with state-weight-based match (MF = W(k,S1)+W(l,S2)), mismatch (NF = -1.5*(W(k,S1)+W(l,S2))) and deletion (DF = -1*W(k,S)) score functions, applied after run-length compression of ChromHMM state labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs overall state composition—comparing state frequency vectors without sequential order is the naive baseline, and the alignment machinery is unnecessary overhead Input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices of differing dimensions rather than discrete chromatin state label sequences; annotation (e.g. ChromHMM) must be applied first Motifs or regions dominated by the quiescent state 'o', which lacks good biological interpretation and was excluded in the paper's motif analyses

skills.description: Use when epigenomic enrichment peaks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage in 50 bp bins) must be aligned by shape and clustered despite variable lengths, strand orientation, or local rescaling of genomic features like TSSs and FSSs.
skills.name: dynamic-time-warping-peak-alignment
skills.search_text: dynamic-time-warping-peak-alignment Use when epigenomic enrichment peaks (e.g. ChIP-Seq H3K4me3/H3K9ac coverage in 50 bp bins) must be aligned by shape and clustered despite variable lengths, strand orientation, or local rescaling of genomic features like TSSs and FSSs. Peaks are already fixed-length and positionally aligned, so plain hierarchical clustering without warping suffices (the article's no-DTW baseline only succeeds when noise v and modifications p are small, e.g. v<0.15, p<0.15) The analysis goal is visualisation of individual enrichment peaks rather than shape-based clustering, where the UCSC genome browser is the article's recommended tool Input data are raw BAM alignments rather than binned peak coverage; MACS2 peak calling and binning must precede DTW alignment http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Constrained multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping (Sakoe-Chiba band, width 12) for aligning binned epigenomic peak coverage profiles so that marks can be matched by shape rather than strict positional correspondence, as implemented in the DGW Python package. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Constrained multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping (Sakoe-Chiba band, width 12) for aligning binned epigenomic peak coverage profiles so that marks can be matched by shape rather than strict positional correspondence, as implemented in the DGW Python package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peaks are already fixed-length and positionally aligned, so plain hierarchical clustering without warping suffices (the article's no-DTW baseline only succeeds when noise v and modifications p are small, e.g. v<0.15, p<0.15) The analysis goal is visualisation of individual enrichment peaks rather than shape-based clustering, where the UCSC genome browser is the article's recommended tool Input data are raw BAM alignments rather than binned peak coverage; MACS2 peak calling and binning must precede DTW alignment

skills.description: Use when reproducing eccDNAdb summary statistics or summarizing a merged eccDNA catalog into a stats table (counts, size distribution, segment counts, copy numbers) with exact reference values.
skills.name: eccdna-catalog-aggregation
skills.search_text: eccdna-catalog-aggregation Use when reproducing eccDNAdb summary statistics or summarizing a merged eccDNA catalog into a stats table (counts, size distribution, segment counts, copy numbers) with exact reference values. The input is raw WGS data and the goal is eccDNA detection — run AmpliconArchitect first rather than aggregating statistics The eccDNAs come from only one provenance (e.g. only literature curation) and you cannot reconstruct the 754/516 WGS/curated split The goal is integration of gene expression, clinical, or ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility data rather than catalog-level summary statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aggregate the WGS-derived eccDNA catalog (AmpliconArchitect on tumor WGS data) with the manually curated literature set into a single eccDNAdb catalog and compute its summary statistics — total count, provenance split, gene count, size, segment-number, and copy-number distributions. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Aggregate the WGS-derived eccDNA catalog (AmpliconArchitect on tumor WGS data) with the manually curated literature set into a single eccDNAdb catalog and compute its summary statistics — total count, provenance split, gene count, size, segment-number, and copy-number distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw WGS data and the goal is eccDNA detection — run AmpliconArchitect first rather than aggregating statistics The eccDNAs come from only one provenance (e.g. only literature curation) and you cannot reconstruct the 754/516 WGS/curated split The goal is integration of gene expression, clinical, or ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility data rather than catalog-level summary statistics

skills.description: Use when a catalog of eccDNA genomic coordinates (BED-style intervals) must be mapped to overlapping genes from a reference annotation (e.g., GENCODE GRCh37) to build an eccDNA gene table with Re/Rg overlap fractions.
skills.name: eccdna-gene-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: eccdna-gene-annotation-mapping Use when a catalog of eccDNA genomic coordinates (BED-style intervals) must be mapped to overlapping genes from a reference annotation (e.g., GENCODE GRCh37) to build an eccDNA gene table with Re/Rg overlap fractions. Input is an eccDNA identifier/gene list without chromosomal coordinates — interval intersection requires genomic start/end positions. The goal is expression or clinical comparison of already-annotated eccDNA genes (e.g., TCGA vs. CCLE t-tests) — use the downstream expression-analysis skill instead of re-running annotation. http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotate identified eccDNA elements with genes by interval intersection of the eccDNA catalog against comprehensive gene annotation, computing per-pair overlap ratios Re (fraction of the eccDNA covered by the gene) and Rg (fraction of the gene covered by the eccDNA), yielding the eccDNA-derived gene set for downstream functional annotation as in eccDNAdb. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Annotate identified eccDNA elements with genes by interval intersection of the eccDNA catalog against comprehensive gene annotation, computing per-pair overlap ratios Re (fraction of the eccDNA covered by the gene) and Rg (fraction of the gene covered by the eccDNA), yielding the eccDNA-derived gene set for downstream functional annotation as in eccDNAdb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is an eccDNA identifier/gene list without chromosomal coordinates — interval intersection requires genomic start/end positions. The goal is expression or clinical comparison of already-annotated eccDNA genes (e.g., TCGA vs. CCLE t-tests) — use the downstream expression-analysis skill instead of re-running annotation.

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether chromatin is highly accessible at an eccDNA-containing region by extracting per-base ATAC-seq signal from BigWig tracks over a fixed coordinate interval and aggregating per-sample coverage.
skills.name: eccdna-region-signal-aggregation
skills.search_text: eccdna-region-signal-aggregation Use when you need to test whether chromatin is highly accessible at an eccDNA-containing region by extracting per-base ATAC-seq signal from BigWig tracks over a fixed coordinate interval and aggregating per-sample coverage. You need to detect eccDNAs de novo from WGS data — use AmpliconArchitect (the eccDNAdb pipeline) rather than region signal aggregation The region of interest lacks a matching ATAC-seq signal track (e.g. no TCGA ATAC-seq coverage for the cancer type), so no accessibility comparison is possible The goal is gene expression or clinical association rather than chromatin accessibility — use the eccDNAdb TCGA/CCLE expression integration instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates chromatin accessibility signal (e.g. TCGA ATAC-seq BigWig tracks) over a defined eccDNA-containing genomic region, such as the EGFR locus chr7:54370001-55996000 in glioblastoma, to quantify and visually confirm that eccDNA-mapped loci are highly accessible, as in eccDNAdb's integration of TCGA ATAC-seq. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Aggregates chromatin accessibility signal (e.g. TCGA ATAC-seq BigWig tracks) over a defined eccDNA-containing genomic region, such as the EGFR locus chr7:54370001-55996000 in glioblastoma, to quantify and visually confirm that eccDNA-mapped loci are highly accessible, as in eccDNAdb's integration of TCGA ATAC-seq.

Input is not WGS-derived copy-number data — the paper's pipeline identified eccDNAs only via AmpliconArchitect on WGS, not from CIRCLE-seq or CIDER-Seq data You need to capture small eccDNAs below the 100 kb size cutoff, since the filtering thresholds will exclude them Candidate regions have already been filtered and reconstructed by AmpliconArchitect http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Filters copy-number alteration calls from low-coverage WGS to retain candidate regions (copy number >5, size >100 kb) as AmpliconArchitect input for eccDNA reconstruction, removing blacklist regions derived from normal-sample analyses. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Filters copy-number alteration calls from low-coverage WGS to retain candidate regions (copy number >5, size >100 kb) as AmpliconArchitect input for eccDNA reconstruction, removing blacklist regions derived from normal-sample analyses.
