skills.description: Use when candidate eCLIP binding sites must be evaluated against orthogonally ascertained true binding sites (e.g., chrM for FASTKD2, splice sites for PRPF8, GURUG motif for TARDBP) to compare peak callers.
skills.name: eclip-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: eclip-benchmark-evaluation Use when candidate eCLIP binding sites must be evaluated against orthogonally ascertained true binding sites (e.g., chrM for FASTKD2, splice sites for PRPF8, GURUG motif for TARDBP) to compare peak callers. The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, so Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and reproducible_enriched_windows cannot be produced for benchmarking No orthogonal, RBP-specific truth set exists for the RBP of interest — overlap-based precision/recall would be uninterpretable The goal is to quantify binding-site count differences rather than benchmark accuracy (use the 210%-320% more-sites analysis instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Benchmark CLIP-seq analysis methods (Skipper vs. CLIPper, Piranha, etc.) by scoring called binding sites against RBP-specific orthogonal truth sets and computing precision, relative recall, and F1 per method-RBP pair across six example eCLIPs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Benchmark CLIP-seq analysis methods (Skipper vs. CLIPper, Piranha, etc.) by scoring called binding sites against RBP-specific orthogonal truth sets and computing precision, relative recall, and F1 per method-RBP pair across six example eCLIPs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, so Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and reproducible_enriched_windows cannot be produced for benchmarking No orthogonal, RBP-specific truth set exists for the RBP of interest — overlap-based precision/recall would be uninterpretable The goal is to quantify binding-site count differences rather than benchmark accuracy (use the 210%-320% more-sites analysis instead)

skills.description: Use when Skipper has produced reproducible_enriched_windows tables for two or more eCLIP conditions (e.g., wild-type vs missense-mutant RBP constructs) and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding sites per transcript region or per annotated locus class such as tRNA.
skills.name: eclip-enriched-window-feature-quantification
skills.search_text: eclip-enriched-window-feature-quantification Use when Skipper has produced reproducible_enriched_windows tables for two or more eCLIP conditions (e.g., wild-type vs missense-mutant RBP constructs) and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding sites per transcript region or per annotated locus class such as tRNA. CLIP datasets lack matched input controls — Skipper requires a matched input sample to construct the beta-binomial model, so enriched-window tables cannot be generated in the first place The question is mechanism-level (complex formation vs localization vs binding preference) — eCLIP window proportions alone cannot resolve this The input is raw CLIP reads rather than Skipper output — the end-to-end Skipper pipeline (preprocessing, alignment, GFF partitioning, enriched window identification) must run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies the distribution of Skipper's reproducible enriched windows across transcript feature classes (CDS, UTRs, deep introns, tRNA loci) and tests WT-vs-mutant shifts, as done for RPS19 eCLIP (R62W, R101H) where CDS binding rose 33%→45% and deep intronic binding fell 20%→7% (p < 2.2e−16). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Quantifies the distribution of Skipper's reproducible enriched windows across transcript feature classes (CDS, UTRs, deep introns, tRNA loci) and tests WT-vs-mutant shifts, as done for RPS19 eCLIP (R62W, R101H) where CDS binding rose 33%→45% and deep intronic binding fell 20%→7% (p < 2.2e−16).
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lack matched input controls — Skipper requires a matched input sample to construct the beta-binomial model, so enriched-window tables cannot be generated in the first place The question is mechanism-level (complex formation vs localization vs binding preference) — eCLIP window proportions alone cannot resolve this The input is raw CLIP reads rather than Skipper output — the end-to-end Skipper pipeline (preprocessing, alignment, GFF partitioning, enriched window identification) must run first

skills.description: Use when comparing the number of enriched CLIP-seq/eCLIP binding sites called by a new caller against established methods (Piranha, CLIPper) on shared ENCODE eCLIP datasets.
skills.name: eclip-peak-calling-benchmarking
skills.search_text: eclip-peak-calling-benchmarking Use when comparing the number of enriched CLIP-seq/eCLIP binding sites called by a new caller against established methods (Piranha, CLIPper) on shared ENCODE eCLIP datasets. CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample — Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and cannot be analyzed The goal is per-read or motif-level characterization rather than comparing counts of enriched binding sites across peak-calling methods Analysis targets non-transcriptomic genomic regions outside the tiled windows over annotated transcripts http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Benchmark the Skipper end-to-end eCLIP workflow against legacy peak callers (Piranha, CLIPper) by counting reproducible enriched binding-site windows per RBP across matched IP/input ENCODE eCLIP replicates, quantifying how many more transcriptomic binding sites Skipper detects. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Benchmark the Skipper end-to-end eCLIP workflow against legacy peak callers (Piranha, CLIPper) by counting reproducible enriched binding-site windows per RBP across matched IP/input ENCODE eCLIP replicates, quantifying how many more transcriptomic binding sites Skipper detects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample — Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and cannot be analyzed The goal is per-read or motif-level characterization rather than comparing counts of enriched binding sites across peak-calling methods Analysis targets non-transcriptomic genomic regions outside the tiled windows over annotated transcripts

skills.description: Use when eCLIP/eCLIP-seq IP and matched input samples must be tested for significant binding to annotated repetitive elements (e.g., GU-rich simple repeats, LINE1) rather than annotated transcripts.
skills.name: eclip-repeat-read-aggregation
skills.search_text: eclip-repeat-read-aggregation Use when eCLIP/eCLIP-seq IP and matched input samples must be tested for significant binding to annotated repetitive elements (e.g., GU-rich simple repeats, LINE1) rather than annotated transcripts. The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, since Skipper requires one to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing The goal is peak calling on annotated transcripts rather than testing pre-annotated multi-mapping repetitive elements The alignment has not been done or the repeat annotation file has overlapping intervals, since REPEAT_BED must be sorted, non-overlapping, and gzip-compressed http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregate eCLIP reads per RepeatMasker-annotated repetitive element and test each element for enrichment using Skipper's beta-binomial framework with GC-content and overdispersion modeling, enabling detection of RBP binding to multi-mapping repeat sequences that peak callers miss. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Aggregate eCLIP reads per RepeatMasker-annotated repetitive element and test each element for enrichment using Skipper's beta-binomial framework with GC-content and overdispersion modeling, enabling detection of RBP binding to multi-mapping repeat sequences that peak callers miss.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, since Skipper requires one to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing The goal is peak calling on annotated transcripts rather than testing pre-annotated multi-mapping repetitive elements The alignment has not been done or the repeat annotation file has overlapping intervals, since REPEAT_BED must be sorted, non-overlapping, and gzip-compressed

skills.description: Use when you have per-window IP and input read-start counts from tiled CLIP/eCLIP windows plus matched input replicates, and need genome-wide enrichment p-values to call reproducible RBP binding windows.
skills.name: eclip-significant-window-filtering
skills.search_text: eclip-significant-window-filtering Use when you have per-window IP and input read-start counts from tiled CLIP/eCLIP windows plus matched input replicates, and need genome-wide enrichment p-values to call reproducible RBP binding windows. CLIP datasets lacking matched input samples — Skipper requires them to construct the beta-binomial model and cannot analyze such data Analyses needing continuous peak calling with flexible fragment-level boundaries — Skipper deliberately skips peak calling and uses fixed tiled windows, so it is the wrong fit for peak-style outputs Windows with fewer total reads than THRESHOLD_MIN across IP and input fractions, or skyscraper windows failing GINI_CUTOFF — these are excluded by design rather than tested http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Statistically tests tiled transcriptomic and repetitive-element windows for enrichment of IP read-start signal over matched input in eCLIP data by fitting GC-stratified beta-binomial models and computing per-window p-values, as implemented in Skipper's enriched window identification stage. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Statistically tests tiled transcriptomic and repetitive-element windows for enrichment of IP read-start signal over matched input in eCLIP data by fitting GC-stratified beta-binomial models and computing per-window p-values, as implemented in Skipper's enriched window identification stage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking matched input samples — Skipper requires them to construct the beta-binomial model and cannot analyze such data Analyses needing continuous peak calling with flexible fragment-level boundaries — Skipper deliberately skips peak calling and uses fixed tiled windows, so it is the wrong fit for peak-style outputs Windows with fewer total reads than THRESHOLD_MIN across IP and input fractions, or skyscraper windows failing GINI_CUTOFF — these are excluded by design rather than tested

skills.description: Use when you have paired bias-corrected and uncorrected Cufflinks/eXpress output per transcript and need to quantify how much fragment bias correction shifted effective lengths, or to test if GC content predicts the bias signal.
skills.name: effective-length-fold-change-computation
skills.search_text: effective-length-fold-change-computation Use when you have paired bias-corrected and uncorrected Cufflinks/eXpress output per transcript and need to quantify how much fragment bias correction shifted effective lengths, or to test if GC content predicts the bias signal. Input is a single expression matrix with no paired corrected/uncorrected effective-length estimates, since the log fold change cannot be computed Analysis goal is direct expression-level accuracy assessment against qRT-PCR rather than characterizing the nature of the bias signal itself The library was already processed with a bias-correction method so both sides of the fold change are corrected and the quantity is trivially zero http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies per-transcript fragment bias in RNA-Seq as the log fold change in effective length between bias-corrected (eXpress/eXpress-D) and uncorrected expression estimates, then correlates this sequence-specific bias signal with transcript GC content to test whether GC normalization proxies bias correction (strong in human SRA012427, weak in yeast SRA020818_RH). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Quantifies per-transcript fragment bias in RNA-Seq as the log fold change in effective length between bias-corrected (eXpress/eXpress-D) and uncorrected expression estimates, then correlates this sequence-specific bias signal with transcript GC content to test whether GC normalization proxies bias correction (strong in human SRA012427, weak in yeast SRA020818_RH).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single expression matrix with no paired corrected/uncorrected effective-length estimates, since the log fold change cannot be computed Analysis goal is direct expression-level accuracy assessment against qRT-PCR rather than characterizing the nature of the bias signal itself The library was already processed with a bias-correction method so both sides of the fold change are corrected and the quantity is trivially zero

skills.description: Use when you need compartment scores (A/B calls) from one or more Hi-C contact maps, especially at high resolution (up to 5-10 kb) or across multiple maps/replicates needing comparable scores.
skills.name: eigenvector-principal-component-analysis
skills.search_text: eigenvector-principal-component-analysis Use when you need compartment scores (A/B calls) from one or more Hi-C contact maps, especially at high resolution (up to 5-10 kb) or across multiple maps/replicates needing comparable scores. The goal is detecting significant compartment differences between maps rather than calling compartments per map — use dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance differential step instead of plain PCA Input is single-cell Hi-C individual cells, where sparsity makes compartment identification unreliable — dcHiC recommends pseudo-bulk aggregation first (down to ~80-100 cells per condition) You only need significant chromatin interactions rather than compartmentalization — Fit-Hi-C, not eigenvector PCA, is the appropriate tool http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Computes A/B compartments from a Hi-C contact map by distance normalization, conversion to a correlation matrix, and eigenvector decomposition, retaining PC1/PC2 as compartment scores. dcHiC implements this as a parallelized partial SVD on a memory-efficient Filebacked Big Matrix followed by quantile normalization, enabling analysis up to 5 kb resolution. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Computes A/B compartments from a Hi-C contact map by distance normalization, conversion to a correlation matrix, and eigenvector decomposition, retaining PC1/PC2 as compartment scores. dcHiC implements this as a parallelized partial SVD on a memory-efficient Filebacked Big Matrix followed by quantile normalization, enabling analysis up to 5 kb resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is detecting significant compartment differences between maps rather than calling compartments per map — use dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance differential step instead of plain PCA Input is single-cell Hi-C individual cells, where sparsity makes compartment identification unreliable — dcHiC recommends pseudo-bulk aggregation first (down to ~80-100 cells per condition) You only need significant chromatin interactions rather than compartmentalization — Fit-Hi-C, not eigenvector PCA, is the appropriate tool

skills.description: Use when a labeled set of genomic intervals (e.g. HOT vs COLD regions) must be classified from sequence-derived features such as k-mer frequencies, GC content, and CpG observed/expected ratio, with feature importance ranking.
skills.name: elastic-net-classification
skills.search_text: elastic-net-classification Use when a labeled set of genomic intervals (e.g. HOT vs COLD regions) must be classified from sequence-derived features such as k-mer frequencies, GC content, and CpG observed/expected ratio, with feature importance ranking. When the goal is to assess whether HOT region signal reflects true TF binding vs ChIP-seq artifact (e.g. KO TF ChIP-seq controls) — sequence classification alone cannot resolve that When regions lack paired class labels or the input is already a curated feature table rather than raw interval sets plus sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Trains species-specific elastic net classifiers (glmnet, binomial family, 10-fold CV) to discriminate HOT from COLD genomic regions using sequence-derived features (k-mer frequencies for k=2–4, GC content, GC skew, CpG O/E ratio), yielding cross-validation AUCs and ranked feature importances. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Trains species-specific elastic net classifiers (glmnet, binomial family, 10-fold CV) to discriminate HOT from COLD genomic regions using sequence-derived features (k-mer frequencies for k=2–4, GC content, GC skew, CpG O/E ratio), yielding cross-validation AUCs and ranked feature importances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to assess whether HOT region signal reflects true TF binding vs ChIP-seq artifact (e.g. KO TF ChIP-seq controls) — sequence classification alone cannot resolve that When regions lack paired class labels or the input is already a curated feature table rather than raw interval sets plus sequences

skills.description: Use when fitting a bivariate Hidden Markov Model to binned ChIP-seq read counts (e.g. histoneHMM on 1000 bp bins of broad marks like H3K9me3/H3K27me3) to classify bins as modified or differentially modified.
skills.name: em-baum-welch-hmm-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: em-baum-welch-hmm-parameter-estimation Use when fitting a bivariate Hidden Markov Model to binned ChIP-seq read counts (e.g. histoneHMM on 1000 bp bins of broad marks like H3K9me3/H3K27me3) to classify bins as modified or differentially modified. The mark produces sharp peak-like features rather than broad diffuse footprints (e.g. typical transcription factor ChIP-seq), where peak-calling methods are appropriate Input is already a list of called regions or a feature table rather than per-bin bivariate read counts Only one sample/condition is available and no two-sample comparison is intended — use the univariate HMM (run.univariate.hmm) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Estimate bivariate HMM parameters for histoneHMM ChIP-seq differential analysis: emission mixture parameters via the EM algorithm, state transition probabilities via Baum-Welch, and per-bin enrichment posteriors via the forward-backward algorithm on 1000 bp binned read counts. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Estimate bivariate HMM parameters for histoneHMM ChIP-seq differential analysis: emission mixture parameters via the EM algorithm, state transition probabilities via Baum-Welch, and per-bin enrichment posteriors via the forward-backward algorithm on 1000 bp binned read counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mark produces sharp peak-like features rather than broad diffuse footprints (e.g. typical transcription factor ChIP-seq), where peak-calling methods are appropriate Input is already a list of called regions or a feature table rather than per-bin bivariate read counts Only one sample/condition is available and no two-sample comparison is intended — use the univariate HMM (run.univariate.hmm) instead

skills.description: Use when you already have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output per 400x400 Hi-C submatrix) and need density-based, parameter-light unsupervised clustering to label every bin.
skills.name: embedding-clustering-annotation
skills.search_text: embedding-clustering-annotation Use when you already have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output per 400x400 Hi-C submatrix) and need density-based, parameter-light unsupervised clustering to label every bin. Input is still a raw NxN Hi-C contact matrix — embeddings must be generated by the GAE module first (train with hidden_dim=64, output_dim=16 on non-overlapping 400x400 submatrices) You need multiscale or parameter-tunable TAD boundaries — HDBSCAN runs unsupervised with no user-set metric parameters, unlike Armatus/TopDom-style callers Embedding dimension differs substantially from the validated 16-dim (or 128-dim single-layer) setting, where the paper's TAD identification quality was established http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 Assigns a cluster label to each genomic bin by running the unsupervised HDBSCAN algorithm on 16-dimensional GAE embeddings derived from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices, as done in TOAST; contiguous regions sharing a label become TADs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Assigns a cluster label to each genomic bin by running the unsupervised HDBSCAN algorithm on 16-dimensional GAE embeddings derived from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices, as done in TOAST; contiguous regions sharing a label become TADs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still a raw NxN Hi-C contact matrix — embeddings must be generated by the GAE module first (train with hidden_dim=64, output_dim=16 on non-overlapping 400x400 submatrices) You need multiscale or parameter-tunable TAD boundaries — HDBSCAN runs unsupervised with no user-set metric parameters, unlike Armatus/TopDom-style callers Embedding dimension differs substantially from the validated 16-dim (or 128-dim single-layer) setting, where the paper's TAD identification quality was established

skills.description: Use when you have per-SNP saliency (or other continuous variant) scores for a candidate SNP set plus a matched background set and need to test whether the two distributions differ, as in fine-mapping GTEx v7 eQTLs.
skills.name: empirical-cdf-comparison
skills.search_text: empirical-cdf-comparison Use when you have per-SNP saliency (or other continuous variant) scores for a candidate SNP set plus a matched background set and need to test whether the two distributions differ, as in fine-mapping GTEx v7 eQTLs. You only have raw deepC Hi-C interaction predictions and have not yet computed per-SNP saliency scores (this skill expects already-scored variants) You need to identify TADs or chromatin domains from Hi-C contact matrices — use a domain caller such as TopDom instead of a distributional test on saliency scores The candidate and background SNP sets are not matched for chromatin context (e.g. both should be drawn from DNase/CTCF peak regions), which would confound the KS comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Builds empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs) of deepC saliency scores for a cell-type-specific eQTL set versus a matched, re-sampled background SNP set and compares them with a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to judge whether variant saliency is enriched. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Builds empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs) of deepC saliency scores for a cell-type-specific eQTL set versus a matched, re-sampled background SNP set and compares them with a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to judge whether variant saliency is enriched.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have raw deepC Hi-C interaction predictions and have not yet computed per-SNP saliency scores (this skill expects already-scored variants) You need to identify TADs or chromatin domains from Hi-C contact matrices — use a domain caller such as TopDom instead of a distributional test on saliency scores The candidate and background SNP sets are not matched for chromatin context (e.g. both should be drawn from DNase/CTCF peak regions), which would confound the KS comparison

skills.description: Use when a high-dimensional genomic matrix (e.g., gene expression or CpG methylation) needs feature scoring before partitioning and variance-based top-value methods (SD, MAD, CV) are insufficient because the global correlation structure matters.
skills.name: empirical-cdf-feature-scoring
skills.search_text: empirical-cdf-feature-scoring Use when a high-dimensional genomic matrix (e.g., gene expression or CpG methylation) needs feature scoring before partitioning and variance-based top-value methods (SD, MAD, CV) are insufficient because the global correlation structure matters. The matrix already contains a small curated feature set and no feature selection step is needed before partitioning Features are independent or the goal is purely per-feature variance ranking where correlation to other rows is irrelevant (SD/MAD/CV top-value methods suffice) The input is single-cell RNA-Seq with several thousands of cells, where cola's runtime and memory usage may be unacceptable per the article's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Computes per-row feature scores from the empirical CDF of a row's absolute correlation coefficients to all other rows (the ATC method in cola), so rows strongly correlated with many other rows receive high scores and can be selected as top features for consensus partitioning. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: Computes per-row feature scores from the empirical CDF of a row's absolute correlation coefficients to all other rows (the ATC method in cola), so rows strongly correlated with many other rows receive high scores and can be selected as top features for consensus partitioning.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix already contains a small curated feature set and no feature selection step is needed before partitioning Features are independent or the goal is purely per-feature variance ranking where correlation to other rows is irrelevant (SD/MAD/CV top-value methods suffice) The input is single-cell RNA-Seq with several thousands of cells, where cola's runtime and memory usage may be unacceptable per the article's discussion

skills.description: Use when tumour RRBS samples contain normal tissue contamination and per-locus epiallele distributions are available for tumour regions and matched normal tissue, so that purity can be estimated from the empirical density of xi.
skills.name: empirical-density-estimation
skills.search_text: empirical-density-estimation Use when tumour RRBS samples contain normal tissue contamination and per-locus epiallele distributions are available for tumour regions and matched normal tissue, so that purity can be estimated from the empirical density of xi. Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so do not apply this to infer purity or heterogeneity across phasing assumptions between separate loci Do not use on loci failing the study filters (median read depth < 100, fewer than six CpGs, > 25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y) The model was validated on a single patient (one tumour with seven regions plus one matched normal); do not assume multi-patient generalisation without re-estimating rho per sample Estimate tumour sample purity from Bayesian epiallele detections by computing the per-locus epiallele divergence xi = 0.5 * sum_q |phi_q - n_q| and reading the rightmost maximum of the empirical density of xi as the purity rho (rho = 0.535 for CRUK0062 tumour region 2). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Estimate tumour sample purity from Bayesian epiallele detections by computing the per-locus epiallele divergence xi = 0.5 * sum_q |phi_q - n_q| and reading the rightmost maximum of the empirical density of xi as the purity rho (rho = 0.535 for CRUK0062 tumour region 2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads cannot be phased between disjoint loci, so do not apply this to infer purity or heterogeneity across phasing assumptions between separate loci Do not use on loci failing the study filters (median read depth < 100, fewer than six CpGs, > 25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y) The model was validated on a single patient (one tumour with seven regions plus one matched normal); do not assume multi-patient generalisation without re-estimating rho per sample

skills.description: Use when you need an empirical P-value for a clustering-agreement metric (VI) between a hierarchical partition and benchmark annotations, and a parametric null is unavailable.
skills.name: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-by-random-bisection
skills.search_text: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-by-random-bisection Use when you need an empirical P-value for a clustering-agreement metric (VI) between a hierarchical partition and benchmark annotations, and a parametric null is unavailable. When a parametric or analytic null distribution for the agreement metric is available and appropriate When the alternative clustering does not assume a nested hierarchy — the null model specifically mimics BHi-Cect's recursive bisection structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Assesses whether an observed clustering agreement statistic (e.g. variation of information between BHi-Cect enclaves and TAD/compartment calls) is significant by building an empirical null distribution from 500 random recursive bisection partitions that preserve the nested-hierarchy assumption of BHi-Cect. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Assesses whether an observed clustering agreement statistic (e.g. variation of information between BHi-Cect enclaves and TAD/compartment calls) is significant by building an empirical null distribution from 500 random recursive bisection partitions that preserve the nested-hierarchy assumption of BHi-Cect.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a parametric or analytic null distribution for the agreement metric is available and appropriate When the alternative clustering does not assume a nested hierarchy — the null model specifically mimics BHi-Cect's recursive bisection structure

skills.description: Use when testing whether a strand asymmetry ratio (e.g. same vs opposite orientation of consecutive motif pairs) is statistically significant and a closed-form binomial test needs empirical confirmation via strand-label permutations.
skills.name: empirical-permutation-pvalue-calculation
skills.search_text: empirical-permutation-pvalue-calculation Use when testing whether a strand asymmetry ratio (e.g. same vs opposite orientation of consecutive motif pairs) is statistically significant and a closed-form binomial test needs empirical confirmation via strand-label permutations. When features are palindromic or strand cannot be assigned — no orientation information exists to permute When the question concerns compositional or mutational strand bias already covered by the binomial test rather than orientation of consecutive/paired features When a very small N (e.g. 100) is used but fine-grained P-values below ~0.01 are required, since resolution is bounded by 1/N http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Asymmetron's permutation-based approach for computing empirical two-tailed P-values of strand asymmetry: N simulations (default 1000, task card used 100) randomly permute '+'/'-' strand labels while keeping the +/− counts fixed, and the observed asymmetry ratio is compared against this null distribution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Asymmetron's permutation-based approach for computing empirical two-tailed P-values of strand asymmetry: N simulations (default 1000, task card used 100) randomly permute '+'/'-' strand labels while keeping the +/− counts fixed, and the observed asymmetry ratio is compared against this null distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When features are palindromic or strand cannot be assigned — no orientation information exists to permute When the question concerns compositional or mutational strand bias already covered by the binomial test rather than orientation of consecutive/paired features When a very small N (e.g. 100) is used but fine-grained P-values below ~0.01 are required, since resolution is bounded by 1/N

skills.description: Use when novelty/outlier scores (reconstruction or model-based) must be turned into calibrated per-window P-values and FDR-controlled non-B DNA calls on ONT translocation-time windows.
skills.name: empirical-pvalue-computation
skills.search_text: empirical-pvalue-computation Use when novelty/outlier scores (reconstruction or model-based) must be turned into calibrated per-window P-values and FDR-controlled non-B DNA calls on ONT translocation-time windows. Input data is simulated rather than experimental translocation-time windows, where the specific B-DNA empirical background calibration for NA12878 ONT data does not apply The goal is supervised classification (SVC, random forest, etc.) on labeled non-B windows rather than FDR-controlled novelty calling without labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Converts per-window novelty scores (from GoFAE-DND Gaussian goodness-of-fit optimization, isolation forest, LOF, or one-class SVM) into empirical P-values against a motif-free B-DNA background distribution, then applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at fdr_level=0.2 to call non-B DNA novelties. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Converts per-window novelty scores (from GoFAE-DND Gaussian goodness-of-fit optimization, isolation forest, LOF, or one-class SVM) into empirical P-values against a motif-free B-DNA background distribution, then applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at fdr_level=0.2 to call non-B DNA novelties.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is simulated rather than experimental translocation-time windows, where the specific B-DNA empirical background calibration for NA12878 ONT data does not apply The goal is supervised classification (SVC, random forest, etc.) on labeled non-B windows rather than FDR-controlled novelty calling without labels

skills.description: Use when a pipeline needs raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (paired IP and matching control) for a defined list of ENA accessions — e.g., the 25 knocked-out transcription factor experiments listed in Supplementary Table S1 of the HOT-or-not study.
skills.name: ena-accession-based-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: ena-accession-based-data-retrieval Use when a pipeline needs raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files (paired IP and matching control) for a defined list of ENA accessions — e.g., the 25 knocked-out transcription factor experiments listed in Supplementary Table S1 of the HOT-or-not study. The required data are already available locally as FASTQ or BAM files, so re-querying ENA would duplicate retrieval The analysis only needs deposited processed files (e.g., ENCODE peak calls or coverage tracks) rather than raw reads for IP/control reprocessing The accession list is not a matched IP/control set (e.g., single-end ChIP-seq without controls), since the downstream log2(IP/control) fold-enrichment computation on HOT regions requires both http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Resolves ENA run accession numbers for IP and matching control samples into raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files, enabling reproducible re-analysis (here, KO transcription factor ChIP-seq to detect false-positive signal on HOT regions) from primary reads rather than preprocessed peaks. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Resolves ENA run accession numbers for IP and matching control samples into raw ChIP-seq FASTQ files, enabling reproducible re-analysis (here, KO transcription factor ChIP-seq to detect false-positive signal on HOT regions) from primary reads rather than preprocessed peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The required data are already available locally as FASTQ or BAM files, so re-querying ENA would duplicate retrieval The analysis only needs deposited processed files (e.g., ENCODE peak calls or coverage tracks) rather than raw reads for IP/control reprocessing The accession list is not a matched IP/control set (e.g., single-end ChIP-seq without controls), since the downstream log2(IP/control) fold-enrichment computation on HOT regions requires both

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq RPM-normalized bedGraph signals are available and genomic regions must be classified as enhancers versus promoters, e.g. enhancer discovery in a human cell line.
skills.name: encode-enhancer-region-annotation
skills.search_text: encode-enhancer-region-annotation Use when ChIP-seq (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq RPM-normalized bedGraph signals are available and genomic regions must be classified as enhancers versus promoters, e.g. enhancer discovery in a human cell line. Input is already a curated enhancer list or feature table rather than raw/processed NGS signal from which bedGraph coverage features must be computed The analysis goal is RNA-seq differential expression or read-mapping QC rather than genomic regulatory element classification Only DNase-seq data is available without the required H3K4me1/H3K4me3/H3K27ac ChIP-seq signatures http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Trains and validates CIPHER's random-forest-based enhancer prediction model, which classifies genomic elements as enhancers versus promoters using chromatin signatures (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq DNase hypersensitive site signal, achieving accuracy slightly above 93%. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1
skills.summary: Trains and validates CIPHER's random-forest-based enhancer prediction model, which classifies genomic elements as enhancers versus promoters using chromatin signatures (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq DNase hypersensitive site signal, achieving accuracy slightly above 93%.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a curated enhancer list or feature table rather than raw/processed NGS signal from which bedGraph coverage features must be computed The analysis goal is RNA-seq differential expression or read-mapping QC rather than genomic regulatory element classification Only DNase-seq data is available without the required H3K4me1/H3K4me3/H3K27ac ChIP-seq signatures

skills.description: Use when raw fastq files from RNA:DNA pulldown high-throughput experiments (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) must be uniformly peak-called and replicate-harmonised to build a binding-site benchmark.
skills.name: encode-pipeline-execution
skills.search_text: encode-pipeline-execution Use when raw fastq files from RNA:DNA pulldown high-throughput experiments (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) must be uniformly peak-called and replicate-harmonised to build a binding-site benchmark. The experiment lacks downloadable raw data or has unclear replicate annotation — these were explicitly excluded from the benchmark The goal is de novo triplex prediction rather than building an experimental binding-site benchmark (use 3plex directly on FASTA inputs instead) The dataset is Xist (X-chromosome-limited data), which was excluded from the collection http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Uniformly re-analyse published experimentally determined lncRNA:DNA binding datasets (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) by processing raw fastq files with the ENCODE ChIP-seq pipeline (v1.6.1) and deriving replicate-consistent peak sets via defined peak filtering methods, yielding a benchmark of validated TPX binding sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Uniformly re-analyse published experimentally determined lncRNA:DNA binding datasets (ChIRP-seq, ChOP-seq, CHART-seq, RAP-seq) by processing raw fastq files with the ENCODE ChIP-seq pipeline (v1.6.1) and deriving replicate-consistent peak sets via defined peak filtering methods, yielding a benchmark of validated TPX binding sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experiment lacks downloadable raw data or has unclear replicate annotation — these were explicitly excluded from the benchmark The goal is de novo triplex prediction rather than building an experimental binding-site benchmark (use 3plex directly on FASTA inputs instead) The dataset is Xist (X-chromosome-limited data), which was excluded from the collection

skills.description: Use when a set of differentially expressed genes (e.g. during EndoMT) must be linked to regulatory elements and screened for enriched TF binding motifs in a cell type-specific manner.
skills.name: endothelial-mesenchymal-transition-gene-set-analysis
skills.search_text: endothelial-mesenchymal-transition-gene-set-analysis Use when a set of differentially expressed genes (e.g. during EndoMT) must be linked to regulatory elements and screened for enriched TF binding motifs in a cell type-specific manner. The goal is to identify a TF's target genes from ChIP-seq peaks rather than to find TFs enriched in REMs of a gene set — use EpiRegio's Region Query workflow instead. The input is already a set of REM sequences with a ranking, so no gene-to-REM association step is needed — run PASTAA directly rather than via the Gene Query pipeline. The task requires mapping TF binding sites within REMs of a single gene of interest — use the identifyTFBindingSites scenario from the ApplicationScenarioExamples repository instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3179 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies transcription factors whose binding motifs are enriched in REMs of genes differentially expressed during TGF-β-induced EndoMT in HUVECs, by running EpiRegio's Gene Query (filtered for 'heart'), ranking REMs by Cell type score, and applying PASTAA motif enrichment with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR ≤ 0.05. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Identifies transcription factors whose binding motifs are enriched in REMs of genes differentially expressed during TGF-β-induced EndoMT in HUVECs, by running EpiRegio's Gene Query (filtered for 'heart'), ranking REMs by Cell type score, and applying PASTAA motif enrichment with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR ≤ 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to identify a TF's target genes from ChIP-seq peaks rather than to find TFs enriched in REMs of a gene set — use EpiRegio's Region Query workflow instead. The input is already a set of REM sequences with a ranking, so no gene-to-REM association step is needed — run PASTAA directly rather than via the Gene Query pipeline. The task requires mapping TF binding sites within REMs of a single gene of interest — use the identifyTFBindingSites scenario from the ApplicationScenarioExamples repository instead.

skills.description: Use when an hg19 structural variant (deletion, inversion, translocation or duplication) lies outside a gene's coding sequence and a long-range, enhancer-driven pathomechanism is suspected for a congenital phenotype (limb, craniofacial, cardiac, neurodevelopmental, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system.
skills.name: enhancer-disconnection-analysis
skills.search_text: enhancer-disconnection-analysis Use when an hg19 structural variant (deletion, inversion, translocation or duplication) lies outside a gene's coding sequence and a long-range, enhancer-driven pathomechanism is suspected for a congenital phenotype (limb, craniofacial, cardiac, neurodevelopmental, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system. The SV's suspected mechanism is coding (truncation/deletion of the coding sequence) rather than long-range enhancer regulation — although POSTRE reports coding events, enhancer-disconnection interpretation applies only when breakpoints spare the gene body. The disease-relevant cell type or developmental stage is not represented in POSTRE's genomic data (e.g. the SHH/ZRS case fails because POSTRE uses bulk whole limb bud data in which the ZRS enhancer cannot be identified). The phenotype is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Predicts SV-driven enhancer disconnection — loss of gene expression caused by breakpoints separating a gene from its cell-type-specific enhancers — using POSTRE's cell-type-specific enhancer, TAD and expression data (hg19). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Predicts SV-driven enhancer disconnection — loss of gene expression caused by breakpoints separating a gene from its cell-type-specific enhancers — using POSTRE's cell-type-specific enhancer, TAD and expression data (hg19).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV's suspected mechanism is coding (truncation/deletion of the coding sequence) rather than long-range enhancer regulation — although POSTRE reports coding events, enhancer-disconnection interpretation applies only when breakpoints spare the gene body. The disease-relevant cell type or developmental stage is not represented in POSTRE's genomic data (e.g. the SHH/ZRS case fails because POSTRE uses bulk whole limb bud data in which the ZRS enhancer cannot be identified). The phenotype is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated.

skills.description: Use when a structural variant has been mapped to a cell-type-specific rearranged enhancer-gene domain and per-gene direction of enhancer activity change (loss vs gain) must be assigned from control vs patient H3K27ac bigWig signals.
skills.name: enhancer-disconnection-gof-lof-gene-scoring
skills.search_text: enhancer-disconnection-gof-lof-gene-scoring Use when a structural variant has been mapped to a cell-type-specific rearranged enhancer-gene domain and per-gene direction of enhancer activity change (loss vs gain) must be assigned from control vs patient H3K27ac bigWig signals. The SV effect is purely coding (gene deletion/truncation) rather than long-range enhancer-driven — use POSTRE's coding pathomechanism predictions instead The disease-relevant cell type lacks genomic data in POSTRE (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so SHH duplication cases fail) The phenotype of interest is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Aggregates cell-type-specific H3K27ac enhancer activity changes across POSTRE-rearranged regulatory domains onto candidate genes, assigning each gene a binary geneEnhancerScore_LOF or geneEnhancerScore_GOF label that flags enhancer disconnection (loss) or enhancer adoption (gain). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Aggregates cell-type-specific H3K27ac enhancer activity changes across POSTRE-rearranged regulatory domains onto candidate genes, assigning each gene a binary geneEnhancerScore_LOF or geneEnhancerScore_GOF label that flags enhancer disconnection (loss) or enhancer adoption (gain).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV effect is purely coding (gene deletion/truncation) rather than long-range enhancer-driven — use POSTRE's coding pathomechanism predictions instead The disease-relevant cell type lacks genomic data in POSTRE (e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so SHH duplication cases fail) The phenotype of interest is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated

skills.description: Use when a set of predicted open-chromatin regions or candidate CREs needs functional benchmarking against an external enhancer catalog with per-region assay outcomes, and you must report an enrichment rate versus a defined background rate.
skills.name: enhancer-enrichment-background-comparison
skills.search_text: enhancer-enrichment-background-comparison Use when a set of predicted open-chromatin regions or candidate CREs needs functional benchmarking against an external enhancer catalog with per-region assay outcomes, and you must report an enrichment rate versus a defined background rate. The input regions are already experimentally validated enhancers — the skill adds no information and the background comparison is meaningless. The external assay catalog lacks per-region positive/negative outcome labels, so no positive rate can be computed for either foreground or background. The goal is cell-type-specific activity assignment rather than aggregate functional validation of the CRE catalog as a whole. http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Validates computational candidate cis-regulatory elements (CREs) against orthogonal functional annotations — here, ~370,000 candidate CREs from the SnapATAC mouse secondary motor cortex atlas are intersected with VISTA Enhancer Browser transgenic reporter assays, and the fraction of overlaps with reproducible reporter expression (167/256 = 65%) is compared against a background positive rate (9.7%). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Validates computational candidate cis-regulatory elements (CREs) against orthogonal functional annotations — here, ~370,000 candidate CREs from the SnapATAC mouse secondary motor cortex atlas are intersected with VISTA Enhancer Browser transgenic reporter assays, and the fraction of overlaps with reproducible reporter expression (167/256 = 65%) is compared against a background positive rate (9.7%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input regions are already experimentally validated enhancers — the skill adds no information and the background comparison is meaningless. The external assay catalog lacks per-region positive/negative outcome labels, so no positive rate can be computed for either foreground or background. The goal is cell-type-specific activity assignment rather than aggregate functional validation of the CRE catalog as a whole.

skills.description: Use when you have cell-type-specific BAM files for H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 (plus matched input control) and RNA-seq TPM values, and need CT-specific features (EP/PP probabilities, regulatory distances, TPM) for ET pairs.
skills.name: enhancer-probability-prediction
skills.search_text: enhancer-probability-prediction Use when you have cell-type-specific BAM files for H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and H3K4me3 (plus matched input control) and RNA-seq TPM values, and need CT-specific features (EP/PP probabilities, regulatory distances, TPM) for ET pairs. The input is already a feature table (generic or CT-specific features computed) — proceed instead to centrePrediction() No cell-type-specific ChIP-seq for H3K27ac/H3K4me1/H3K4me3 is available for the CT of interest — CT-specific features cannot be computed You only need cell-type-agnostic statistics (Fisher's combined probability, Pearson correlation, genomic distance) — use computeGenericFeatures(pairs) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Computes cell-type-specific enhancer and promoter probability features for enhancer-target (ET) pairs by applying CRUP-EP and CRUP-PP to H3K4me1, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac ChIP-seq (via crupR), and attaching cell-type RNA-seq TPM values, as implemented in CENTRE's computeCellTypeFeatures(). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad687
skills.summary: Computes cell-type-specific enhancer and promoter probability features for enhancer-target (ET) pairs by applying CRUP-EP and CRUP-PP to H3K4me1, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac ChIP-seq (via crupR), and attaching cell-type RNA-seq TPM values, as implemented in CENTRE's computeCellTypeFeatures().
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature table (generic or CT-specific features computed) — proceed instead to centrePrediction() No cell-type-specific ChIP-seq for H3K27ac/H3K4me1/H3K4me3 is available for the CT of interest — CT-specific features cannot be computed You only need cell-type-agnostic statistics (Fisher's combined probability, Pearson correlation, genomic distance) — use computeGenericFeatures(pairs) instead

skills.description: Use when you have a TAD boundary file and ChIP-seq narrowPeak or enhancer/promoter interval files and need per-factor fractions of boundaries anchored by regulatory signals.
skills.name: enhancer-promoter-anchor-fraction-computation
skills.search_text: enhancer-promoter-anchor-fraction-computation Use when you have a TAD boundary file and ChIP-seq narrowPeak or enhancer/promoter interval files and need per-factor fractions of boundaries anchored by regulatory signals. Input is raw Hi-C contact matrix rather than an already-called TAD boundary file — TOAST (toast.py) must first be run to produce boundaries You need enhancer–promoter interaction prediction itself rather than boundary anchoring statistics — use EPIANN model training, not this counting step Cell line is not GM12878 and no matched ENCODE/EPIANN regulatory data exist for that line, since the ratio values are validated only against GM12878 signals http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the proportion (anchoring ratio) of regulatory peaks — transcription factors (CTCF, SMC3, RAD21, POLR2A), histone marks (H3K36me3, H3K9me3, H3K4me3, H3K4me1), Enhancer, and Promoter intervals — that overlap a 20 Kb window centered on each TOAST-called TAD boundary, to quantify boundary regulatory enrichment. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Computes the proportion (anchoring ratio) of regulatory peaks — transcription factors (CTCF, SMC3, RAD21, POLR2A), histone marks (H3K36me3, H3K9me3, H3K4me3, H3K4me1), Enhancer, and Promoter intervals — that overlap a 20 Kb window centered on each TOAST-called TAD boundary, to quantify boundary regulatory enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Hi-C contact matrix rather than an already-called TAD boundary file — TOAST (toast.py) must first be run to produce boundaries You need enhancer–promoter interaction prediction itself rather than boundary anchoring statistics — use EPIANN model training, not this counting step Cell line is not GM12878 and no matched ENCODE/EPIANN regulatory data exist for that line, since the ratio values are validated only against GM12878 signals

skills.description: Use when assigning target genes to enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs (e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in prefrontal cortex) using cell type-specific chromatin loops such as SnapHiC summit BEDPE files from scHi-C/snm3C-seq data.
skills.name: enhancer-promoter-chromatin-loop-linking
skills.search_text: enhancer-promoter-chromatin-loop-linking Use when assigning target genes to enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs (e.g. neuropsychiatric SNPs in prefrontal cortex) using cell type-specific chromatin loops such as SnapHiC summit BEDPE files from scHi-C/snm3C-seq data. Your goal is to call chromatin loops from raw scHi-C contact files rather than to link already-called loops to SNPs — use the SnapHiC pipeline (bin/rwr/hic/interaction/postprocess steps) instead. SNPs are coding or fall outside active enhancer intervals of the cell types with available loop calls, so no enhancer-anchor overlap can be defined. Loop data and SNP/enhancer annotations come from mismatched genome builds (e.g. hg19 BEDPE vs hg38 SNP coordinates) without liftover. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Links enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes by overlapping SNP-containing enhancers with cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) called from single-nucleus methyl-3C-seq data, yielding a deduplicated SNP-gene linkage table with supporting cell types. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Links enhancer-resident noncoding GWAS SNPs to putative target genes by overlapping SNP-containing enhancers with cell type-specific chromatin loops (SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) called from single-nucleus methyl-3C-seq data, yielding a deduplicated SNP-gene linkage table with supporting cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is to call chromatin loops from raw scHi-C contact files rather than to link already-called loops to SNPs — use the SnapHiC pipeline (bin/rwr/hic/interaction/postprocess steps) instead. SNPs are coding or fall outside active enhancer intervals of the cell types with available loop calls, so no enhancer-anchor overlap can be defined. Loop data and SNP/enhancer annotations come from mismatched genome builds (e.g. hg19 BEDPE vs hg38 SNP coordinates) without liftover.

skills.description: Use when scHi-C-derived loop calls (e.g., SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe per cell type) must be connected to promoter-linked genes and tested whether anchors and linked genes show highest activity/expression in the matched cell type.
skills.name: enhancer-promoter-expression-linking
skills.search_text: enhancer-promoter-expression-linking Use when scHi-C-derived loop calls (e.g., SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe per cell type) must be connected to promoter-linked genes and tested whether anchors and linked genes show highest activity/expression in the matched cell type. When loops have not been called per cell type (no *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe outputs); SnapHiC loop calling must precede anchor/promoter quantification. When no cell type-matched epigenomic (ATAC/H3K27ac) or expression reference data exist for the cell types of interest, since matched-vs-unmatched enrichment cannot be computed. When the goal is bulk Hi-C loop detection from population contact maps rather than cell type-specific loops from size-matched single-cell datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Links cell type-specific chromatin loops (identified with SnapHiC from matched-size scHi-C datasets) to their target promoters and validates the links with cell type-matched regulatory signatures: ATAC-seq accessibility, H3K27ac ChIP-seq signal, and FPKM gene expression. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Links cell type-specific chromatin loops (identified with SnapHiC from matched-size scHi-C datasets) to their target promoters and validates the links with cell type-matched regulatory signatures: ATAC-seq accessibility, H3K27ac ChIP-seq signal, and FPKM gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When loops have not been called per cell type (no *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe outputs); SnapHiC loop calling must precede anchor/promoter quantification. When no cell type-matched epigenomic (ATAC/H3K27ac) or expression reference data exist for the cell types of interest, since matched-vs-unmatched enrichment cannot be computed. When the goal is bulk Hi-C loop detection from population contact maps rather than cell type-specific loops from size-matched single-cell datasets.

skills.description: Use when RNAPII ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) loops have already been called with PET count >= 3 and peak support, and each loop must be labeled E-P, P-P, or neither using enhancer/promoter BED annotations.
skills.name: enhancer-promoter-loop-annotation
skills.search_text: enhancer-promoter-loop-annotation Use when RNAPII ChIA-PET (or HiChIP/PLAC-seq) loops have already been called with PET count >= 3 and peak support, and each loop must be labeled E-P, P-P, or neither using enhancer/promoter BED annotations. The underlying loops have not yet been called by ChIA-PIPE (no peak-supported, PET count >= 3 loop set with unique loop IDs exists). The experiment is CTCF ChIA-PET rather than RNAPII, so enhancer/promoter loop semantics do not apply to the anchor biology. The goal is CCD calling or allele-specific loop resolution rather than functional (E-P/P-P) categorization of loops. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Classify called RNAPII ChIA-PET loops (PET count >= 3 with peak support, each with a unique loop ID) into enhancer-promoter (E-P), promoter-promoter (P-P), or neither categories by intersecting anchor coordinates with enhancer and promoter BED files, and emit per-category subset loop files for separate BASIC Browser tracks. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Classify called RNAPII ChIA-PET loops (PET count >= 3 with peak support, each with a unique loop ID) into enhancer-promoter (E-P), promoter-promoter (P-P), or neither categories by intersecting anchor coordinates with enhancer and promoter BED files, and emit per-category subset loop files for separate BASIC Browser tracks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The underlying loops have not yet been called by ChIA-PIPE (no peak-supported, PET count >= 3 loop set with unique loop IDs exists). The experiment is CTCF ChIA-PET rather than RNAPII, so enhancer/promoter loop semantics do not apply to the anchor biology. The goal is CCD calling or allele-specific loop resolution rather than functional (E-P/P-P) categorization of loops.

skills.description: Use when labeled enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. 'data/train/${cell_line}.fasta' with '${cell_line}_y_train.txt' labels) must be classified per cell line, or generic/enhancer-promoter benchmarks must be reproduced.
skills.name: enhancer-sequence-classification
skills.search_text: enhancer-sequence-classification Use when labeled enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. 'data/train/${cell_line}.fasta' with '${cell_line}_y_train.txt' labels) must be classified per cell line, or generic/enhancer-promoter benchmarks must be reproduced. Input is already an extracted feature table — dna2vec_code.py and motif_find.py expect raw FASTA sequences, so skip feature extraction only when 'feature' outputs already exist The goal is transcription-factor motif interpretation rather than classification — use SHAP.py for exploring important motifs instead of the prediction pipeline The target task is promoter or other non-enhancer genomic element classification outside the enhancer/enhancer-promoter scope of this framework http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Train and evaluate Enhancer-MDLF, a multi-input deep learning framework that fuses dna2vec word-vector features with HOCOMOCO v11 motif-frequency features to classify DNA sequences as cell-specific enhancers, with transfer learning for cross-cell-line prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Train and evaluate Enhancer-MDLF, a multi-input deep learning framework that fuses dna2vec word-vector features with HOCOMOCO v11 motif-frequency features to classify DNA sequences as cell-specific enhancers, with transfer learning for cross-cell-line prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an extracted feature table — dna2vec_code.py and motif_find.py expect raw FASTA sequences, so skip feature extraction only when 'feature' outputs already exist The goal is transcription-factor motif interpretation rather than classification — use SHAP.py for exploring important motifs instead of the prediction pipeline The target task is promoter or other non-enhancer genomic element classification outside the enhancer/enhancer-promoter scope of this framework

skills.description: Use when benchmarking whether DNA foundation models capture enhancer-gene regulatory interactions over very long sequences, or when reproducing the DNALONGBENCH ETGP AUROC/AUPRC table.
skills.name: enhancer-target-gene-prediction
skills.search_text: enhancer-target-gene-prediction Use when benchmarking whether DNA foundation models capture enhancer-gene regulatory interactions over very long sequences, or when reproducing the DNALONGBENCH ETGP AUROC/AUPRC table. The task is a different DNALONGBENCH task (eQTL, 3D contact map prediction, regulatory sequence activity prediction, transcription initiation signals) — use that task's specific workflow and metrics instead. The question concerns short-range DNA tasks (< 450 kb context) or transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer), which were excluded here because quadratic self-attention makes long-range tasks infeasible. Only a foundation model is needed without the expert/CNN baselines for comparison — the paper's key finding requires all five models to be reproduced on the same held-out test set. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reproduces the enhancer-target gene prediction (ETGP) benchmark from DNALONGBENCH: a binary classification task over 450,000 bp input sequences (2,602 samples, AUROC metric) evaluated across a task-specific expert model, a CNN baseline, and three fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the enhancer-target gene prediction (ETGP) benchmark from DNALONGBENCH: a binary classification task over 450,000 bp input sequences (2,602 samples, AUROC metric) evaluated across a task-specific expert model, a CNN baseline, and three fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a different DNALONGBENCH task (eQTL, 3D contact map prediction, regulatory sequence activity prediction, transcription initiation signals) — use that task's specific workflow and metrics instead. The question concerns short-range DNA tasks (< 450 kb context) or transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer), which were excluded here because quadratic self-attention makes long-range tasks infeasible. Only a foundation model is needed without the expert/CNN baselines for comparison — the paper's key finding requires all five models to be reproduced on the same held-out test set.

skills.description: Use when you need to predict which candidate cCRE-ELS enhancers within 500 KB of a target gene's TSS actively interact with that gene in a specific cell type, given ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K4me3) and RNA-seq data for that cell type.
skills.name: enhancer-target-pair-classification
skills.search_text: enhancer-target-pair-classification Use when you need to predict which candidate cCRE-ELS enhancers within 500 KB of a target gene's TSS actively interact with that gene in a specific cell type, given ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, H3K4me1, H3K4me3) and RNA-seq data for that cell type. skills.summary: Train and apply a pre-trained XGBoost gradient-boosting classifier (CENTRE) to label enhancer-target (ET) pairs as interacting or not interacting in a cell-type-specific manner, using CT-specific features (CRUP-EP/CRUP-PP probabilities, regulatory distances, RNA-seq TPM) plus generic features (genomic distance, cor_CRUP, Fisher's combined Wilcoxon P-value).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a scored feature table with only generic features (distance, cor_CRUP, combined_tests) — the article shows generic features alone perform worse than the baseline distance method The enhancer-target candidates extend beyond 500 KB — CENTRE limits the ET pair search to a distance of 500 KB and extending this interval requires future methodological improvements No cell-type-specific RNA-seq or H3K27ac/H3K4me1/H3K4me3 ChIP-seq data are available for the CT of interest — the method requires exactly these inputs

skills.description: Use when estimating methylation levels from cfMeDIP/(cf)MeDIP-seq enrichment data where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among linear, sigmoidal, or strand-aware normalization models is needed.
skills.name: enrichment-based-absolute-methylation-estimation
skills.search_text: enrichment-based-absolute-methylation-estimation Use when estimating methylation levels from cfMeDIP/(cf)MeDIP-seq enrichment data where CpG density bias must be corrected, and a choice among linear, sigmoidal, or strand-aware normalization models is needed. Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet passed through MEDIPIPE's QC and alignment module producing duplicate-filtered BAMs Data are not enrichment-based MeDIP-seq (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing), where CpG-density-bias correction of MeDIP signals is not required Estimate CpG-density-corrected relative and absolute methylation levels from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data using MEDIPIPE's three alternative quantification models: MEDIPS (v1.46.0, linear regression), QSEA (v1.20.0, sigmoidal with empirical knowledge), and MEDStrand (v0.0.0.9000, stranded sigmoid model). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Estimate CpG-density-corrected relative and absolute methylation levels from enrichment-based cfMeDIP-seq data using MEDIPIPE's three alternative quantification models: MEDIPS (v1.46.0, linear regression), QSEA (v1.20.0, sigmoidal with empirical knowledge), and MEDStrand (v0.0.0.9000, stranded sigmoid model).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet passed through MEDIPIPE's QC and alignment module producing duplicate-filtered BAMs Data are not enrichment-based MeDIP-seq (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing), where CpG-density-bias correction of MeDIP signals is not required

skills.description: Use when a set of labeled regulatory variants (true cis-eQTL indels vs model-predicted scores) must be tested for enrichment/depletion in interval annotations (promoter-centered chromatin interactions, open chromatin, histone marks) across multiple tissues, with odds-ratio comparison tables and.
skills.name: enrichment-odds-ratio-visualization
skills.search_text: enrichment-odds-ratio-visualization Use when a set of labeled regulatory variants (true cis-eQTL indels vs model-predicted scores) must be tested for enrichment/depletion in interval annotations (promoter-centered chromatin interactions, open chromatin, histone marks) across multiple tissues, with odds-ratio comparison tables and. The input is already a computed odds-ratio or contingency-table summary — only the visualization step applies, not the overlap testing. The query variants are SNVs or other variant classes rather than noncoding small indels (sindels), which is the scope of TIVAN-indel labels and precomputed scores. Regulatory annotations are not interval-based (e.g. point-mutation signature data), since the method relies on interval-overlap contingency tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Reproduces the TIVAN-indel paper's enrichment analysis by testing overlap of true vs predicted nc-sindels with 3DIV PE/PP chromatin interactions, open-chromatin and seven Roadmap histone marks via Fisher's exact test, then comparing median odds ratios (e.g. H3K36me3: 3.71 predicted vs 2.62 true) and visualizing them as boxplots. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad060
skills.summary: Reproduces the TIVAN-indel paper's enrichment analysis by testing overlap of true vs predicted nc-sindels with 3DIV PE/PP chromatin interactions, open-chromatin and seven Roadmap histone marks via Fisher's exact test, then comparing median odds ratios (e.g. H3K36me3: 3.71 predicted vs 2.62 true) and visualizing them as boxplots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a computed odds-ratio or contingency-table summary — only the visualization step applies, not the overlap testing. The query variants are SNVs or other variant classes rather than noncoding small indels (sindels), which is the scope of TIVAN-indel labels and precomputed scores. Regulatory annotations are not interval-based (e.g. point-mutation signature data), since the method relies on interval-overlap contingency tables.

Input is already a feature table or raw model scores rather than DNA sequences needing word2vec/iLearnPlus encoding The task is motif/TFBS interpretation rather than ensemble inference — use feature_importance.rar instead of RF.py/CNN.py/Weighted_average.py Sequences are from species outside the seven covered by the 12 trained datasets in the 'model' folder http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 Run and evaluate the iPro-WAEL weighted average ensemble — a random forest (RF.py, scikit-learn) combined with a CNN (CNN.py, keras 2.3.1/tensorflow 2.0.0) via Weighted_average.py — over word2vec and iLearnPlus-encoded sequence features to produce promoter predictions and discrimination metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac824
skills.summary: Run and evaluate the iPro-WAEL weighted average ensemble — a random forest (RF.py, scikit-learn) combined with a CNN (CNN.py, keras 2.3.1/tensorflow 2.0.0) via Weighted_average.py — over word2vec and iLearnPlus-encoded sequence features to produce promoter predictions and discrimination metrics.

skills.description: Use when CITRUS has been trained multiple times (--run_count 1..10) and a single-run 'hid_tmr' TF activity matrix is too unstable for downstream clustering or TF–tumor-type association testing.

skills.search_text: ensemble-output-aggregation-across-model-runs Use when CITRUS has been trained multiple times (--run_count 1..10) and a single-run 'hid_tmr' TF activity matrix is too unstable for downstream clustering or TF–tumor-type association testing. A single CITRUS run's 'hid_tmr' output is already sufficient and run-to-run variance is not a concern The model was trained on a custom dataset without multiple runs — first regenerate per-run outputs before ensembling The quantity of interest is a deterministic output such as attention weights ('attn_wt') or trained weights ('tf_gene') rather than the stochastic hidden-layer TF activity http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Stabilizes CITRUS-inferred patient-specific transcription factor (TF) activities by running the PyTorch model 10 times and averaging the hidden-layer TF activity ('hid_tmr') across runs via ensemble_TF.py, so downstream analyses (e.g., TF-activity clustering of 5803 TCGA tumors across 17 cancer types) are not driven by the variance of a single training run. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881

skills.name: ensemble-weight-optimization-slsqp
skills.search_text: ensemble-weight-optimization-slsqp Use when fusing probabilistic outputs of two heterogeneous base classifiers (e.g., RF on encoded features and CNN on word2vec features) into a single weighted-average ensemble and the optimal weights must be learned rather than hand-tuned. You have a single base model and no ensemble combination to optimize (e.g., only RF.py or only CNN.py predictions) The base model outputs are hard labels rather than continuous predicted values, making a weighted average and cross-entropy minimization ill-defined No dedicated weighted set with true labels is available to estimate the cross-entropy objective http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Optimizes the weighted-average combination of a random forest (RF) and a CNN classifier by minimizing cross-entropy loss on a dedicated weighted set via SLSQP, as implemented in iPro-WAEL's Weighted_average.py for promoter prediction across seven species. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac824

skills.description: Use when bisulfite-sequencing epiallele data has been reduced to significant methylated cores and you must quantify per-CpG coupling (entanglement/stability index E) and core clonality in each population.
skills.name: entanglement-index-computation
skills.search_text: entanglement-index-computation Use when bisulfite-sequencing epiallele data has been reduced to significant methylated cores and you must quantify per-CpG coupling (entanglement/stability index E) and core clonality in each population. Data are single-CpG methylation levels or unphased bulk methylation calls — phased epihaplotype matrices from bisulfite reads are required No statistically significant mCpG combinations exist after Module 1/2 filtering (chi-square adjusted P-value ≤ 10−9) — cores and their indices cannot be defined The goal is merely profiling single-epiallele abundance, which tools like ampliMethProfiler or methclone already provide without phased-core indices http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Computes the MethCoresProfiler clonality index and the stability/entanglement index (E) that quantify, per CpG and per core, how strongly phased mCpGs are coupled within epiallele families in a bisulfite-sequenced DNA population. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Computes the MethCoresProfiler clonality index and the stability/entanglement index (E) that quantify, per CpG and per core, how strongly phased mCpGs are coupled within epiallele families in a bisulfite-sequenced DNA population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are single-CpG methylation levels or unphased bulk methylation calls — phased epihaplotype matrices from bisulfite reads are required No statistically significant mCpG combinations exist after Module 1/2 filtering (chi-square adjusted P-value ≤ 10−9) — cores and their indices cannot be defined The goal is merely profiling single-epiallele abundance, which tools like ampliMethProfiler or methclone already provide without phased-core indices

skills.description: Use when you have per-locus epiallele proportions from multi-region tumour RRBS data and need a scalar measure of epigenetic heterogeneity (disorder) to compare tumour regions against matched normal tissue.
skills.name: epiallele-entropy-quantification
skills.search_text: epiallele-entropy-quantification Use when you have per-locus epiallele proportions from multi-region tumour RRBS data and need a scalar measure of epigenetic heterogeneity (disorder) to compare tumour regions against matched normal tissue. You need locus-level differential epiallele composition between sample groups rather than a global per-sample heterogeneity summary Loci fail the article's quality filters (median read depth < 100, fewer than six CpGs, > 25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y), since entropy estimates there are not comparable Reads cannot be reasonably assigned at a locus and epialleles have not been inferred via bed_fit/bed_marginal — entropy of raw read patterns is not the paper's statistic http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Quantifies global epigenetic disorder per sample by computing the normalised Shannon entropy of epiallele distributions (phi_s) at each methylation locus, using the bed R package's bed_fit/bed_marginal outputs from multi-region RRBS data, as applied to the CRUK0062 lung tumour (R1-R7 plus matched normal N) in Fig. 5. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Quantifies global epigenetic disorder per sample by computing the normalised Shannon entropy of epiallele distributions (phi_s) at each methylation locus, using the bed R package's bed_fit/bed_marginal outputs from multi-region RRBS data, as applied to the CRUK0062 lung tumour (R1-R7 plus matched normal N) in Fig. 5.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need locus-level differential epiallele composition between sample groups rather than a global per-sample heterogeneity summary Loci fail the article's quality filters (median read depth < 100, fewer than six CpGs, > 25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y), since entropy estimates there are not comparable Reads cannot be reasonably assigned at a locus and epialleles have not been inferred via bed_fit/bed_marginal — entropy of raw read patterns is not the paper's statistic
