skills.search_text: epiallele-family-trajectory-comparison Use when comparing bisulfite amplicon-seq epihaplotype data across two or more conditions to test whether specific families of phased mCpG combinations (methylated cores) expand clonally or remain stochastic between time points or populations. The question concerns single-CpG methylation levels or single-epiallele abundance, which tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler or methclone already quantify without phased-core tracking Input reads are shotgun bisulfite sequencing rather than amplicon-based reads matching the PEAR merge / 400-500 nt length filter workflow The comparison does not require distinguishing clonally expanded epiallele families from stochastic methylation (e.g., one-population descriptive methylation profiling only) http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantify and compare epiallele family trajectories across populations (e.g., P1 vs P90 mouse gut) by extracting methylated cores with MethCoresProfiler and computing its clonality index (core frequency normalized to average population methylation) and stability/entanglement index to distinguish clonally expanded dominant families from stochastic methylation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096

skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns single-CpG methylation levels or single-epiallele abundance, which tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler or methclone already quantify without phased-core tracking Input reads are shotgun bisulfite sequencing rather than amplicon-based reads matching the PEAR merge / 400-500 nt length filter workflow The comparison does not require distinguishing clonally expanded epiallele families from stochastic methylation (e.g., one-population descriptive methylation profiling only)

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. from ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into phased single-molecule CpG methylation states and stable mCpG combinations (cores) traced in complex DNA populations.
skills.name: epiallele-methylation-state-extraction
skills.search_text: epiallele-methylation-state-extraction Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. from ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into phased single-molecule CpG methylation states and stable mCpG combinations (cores) traced in complex DNA populations. The goal is only quantitative methylation assessment of single CpGs or abundance of single epialleles — tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler alone, or methclone suffice and will not resolve phased-core structure Reads have ambiguous CpG calls (gaps, A or G at CpG dinucleotides), fail the ≥98% bisulfite efficiency or ≥60% reference-alignment filters, or fall outside 400–500 nt / ±50% of reference length 10% rare amplified epialleles must be detected — under the tested conditions such low-abundance epialleles escape detection by Modules 1 and 2 http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Extracts single-molecule CpG methylation configurations (binary epihaplotypes) from bisulfite amplicon reads and identifies stable combinations of phased methylated CpGs (methylated cores) shared by all components of epiallele families, using MethCoresProfiler's three R modules plus ampliMethProfiler for read-level methylation calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Extracts single-molecule CpG methylation configurations (binary epihaplotypes) from bisulfite amplicon reads and identifies stable combinations of phased methylated CpGs (methylated cores) shared by all components of epiallele families, using MethCoresProfiler's three R modules plus ampliMethProfiler for read-level methylation calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is only quantitative methylation assessment of single CpGs or abundance of single epialleles — tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler alone, or methclone suffice and will not resolve phased-core structure Reads have ambiguous CpG calls (gaps, A or G at CpG dinucleotides), fail the ≥98% bisulfite efficiency or ≥60% reference-alignment filters, or fall outside 400–500 nt / ±50% of reference length 10% rare amplified epialleles must be detected — under the tested conditions such low-abundance epialleles escape detection by Modules 1 and 2

skills.description: Use when multi-region tumour RRBS data have been processed into decontaminated epiallele profiles t_hat_s per sample and you need a sample-by-sample distance matrix or a tumour phylogenetic tree.
skills.name: epiallele-profile-distance-computation
skills.search_text: epiallele-profile-distance-computation Use when multi-region tumour RRBS data have been processed into decontaminated epiallele profiles t_hat_s per sample and you need a sample-by-sample distance matrix or a tumour phylogenetic tree. Input is raw RRBS reads rather than fitted, decontaminated epiallele profiles phi_q — the Bayesian bed model (bed_fit/bed_marginal) must be run first Samples lack an estimated purity rho, so profiles are contaminated with normal tissue and distances between tumour samples would be biased The goal is single-sample epigenetic disorder quantification (Shannon entropy of phi_s), not between-sample phylogenetic comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0194 Computes a pairwise sample distance matrix from decontaminated tumour epiallele profiles (t_hat_s, i.e. purity-corrected vectors phi_q clipped to [0,1]) and fits a phylogenetic tree with fastme.bal, yielding a Newick-format tumour phylogeny. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Computes a pairwise sample distance matrix from decontaminated tumour epiallele profiles (t_hat_s, i.e. purity-corrected vectors phi_q clipped to [0,1]) and fits a phylogenetic tree with fastme.bal, yielding a Newick-format tumour phylogeny.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RRBS reads rather than fitted, decontaminated epiallele profiles phi_q — the Bayesian bed model (bed_fit/bed_marginal) must be run first Samples lack an estimated purity rho, so profiles are contaminated with normal tissue and distances between tumour samples would be biased The goal is single-sample epigenetic disorder quantification (Shannon entropy of phi_s), not between-sample phylogenetic comparison

skills.description: Use when you need to test whether integrating all epigenetic features with sgRNA sequence improves CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa efficiency prediction versus sequence-only or sequence-plus-one-epigenetic-feature models.
skills.name: epigenetic-feature-ablation-analysis
skills.search_text: epigenetic-feature-ablation-analysis Use when you need to test whether integrating all epigenetic features with sgRNA sequence improves CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa efficiency prediction versus sequence-only or sequence-plus-one-epigenetic-feature models. The goal is feature interpretation/importance ranking rather than ablation performance comparison — use Tree SHAP/DeepSHAP with XGBoost instead Input data lacks epigenetic feature tracks (no ATAC, methylation, RNA expression, or TSS coordinates) so only sequence-only models are feasible The task is benchmarking EpiCas-DL against external predictors (DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest) rather than internal feature ablation http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Ablation analysis skill for EpiCas-DL that systematically removes or adds epigenetic feature channels (nucleosome positioning/TSS distance, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, gene expression) to quantify their contribution to sgRNA editing-efficiency prediction relative to sequence-only encoding. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Ablation analysis skill for EpiCas-DL that systematically removes or adds epigenetic feature channels (nucleosome positioning/TSS distance, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, gene expression) to quantify their contribution to sgRNA editing-efficiency prediction relative to sequence-only encoding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is feature interpretation/importance ranking rather than ablation performance comparison — use Tree SHAP/DeepSHAP with XGBoost instead Input data lacks epigenetic feature tracks (no ATAC, methylation, RNA expression, or TSS coordinates) so only sequence-only models are feasible The task is benchmarking EpiCas-DL against external predictors (DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest) rather than internal feature ablation

skills.description: Use when preparing sgRNA training/prediction inputs for a CNN that must combine target-site sequence with cell-type epigenetic signals (nucleosome, accessibility, methylation, expression) around CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa target sites.
skills.name: epigenetic-feature-matrix-encoding
skills.search_text: epigenetic-feature-matrix-encoding Use when preparing sgRNA training/prediction inputs for a CNN that must combine target-site sequence with cell-type epigenetic signals (nucleosome, accessibility, methylation, expression) around CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa target sites. Prediction runs requiring sequence-only input should use the 4-channel sequence encoding only (e.g. CRISPRoff_seq model), not the full epigenetic matrix Cell lines or epigenetic marks not covered by the available epi_reference tracks — incomplete epigenetic feature information limits model performance Analyses targeting nucleases other than dCas-based epigenome editing systems (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa), where the epigenetic channel semantics do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Encodes sgRNA target sequences and epigenetic context into an 11x40 image-like feature matrix (4 one-hot sequence channels plus nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and gene expression channels) for input to the EpiCas-DL CNN predicting sgRNA activity in CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Encodes sgRNA target sequences and epigenetic context into an 11x40 image-like feature matrix (4 one-hot sequence channels plus nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and gene expression channels) for input to the EpiCas-DL CNN predicting sgRNA activity in CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Prediction runs requiring sequence-only input should use the 4-channel sequence encoding only (e.g. CRISPRoff_seq model), not the full epigenetic matrix Cell lines or epigenetic marks not covered by the available epi_reference tracks — incomplete epigenetic feature information limits model performance Analyses targeting nucleases other than dCas-based epigenome editing systems (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa), where the epigenetic channel semantics do not apply

skills.description: Use when building model inputs from sgRNA genomic coordinates and you need chromosome-position-based epigenetic annotations (ATACdb accessibility, FANTOM TSS distances, WGBS methylation, GEO RNA-seq expression) scaled to a common range.
skills.name: epigenetic-feature-minmax-normalization
skills.search_text: epigenetic-feature-minmax-normalization Use when building model inputs from sgRNA genomic coordinates and you need chromosome-position-based epigenetic annotations (ATACdb accessibility, FANTOM TSS distances, WGBS methylation, GEO RNA-seq expression) scaled to a common range. Input is already a normalized epigenetic feature matrix — re-annotating would duplicate feature assignment Task only requires sequence-based prediction; EpiCas-DL supports sequence-only mode (CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq) without epigenetic features Cell-type-matched ATACdb/methylation/expression tracks do not exist for the target cell line, since the epigenetic features are cell-type dependent http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Assigns seven continuous epigenetic features (4 nucleosome-positioning/TSS distances, 1 chromatin accessibility, 1 DNA methylation, 1 RNA expression) to each sgRNA target site and min–max normalizes them to [0,1] so they can be fed alongside one-hot encoded sgRNA sequences into EpiCas-DL. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Assigns seven continuous epigenetic features (4 nucleosome-positioning/TSS distances, 1 chromatin accessibility, 1 DNA methylation, 1 RNA expression) to each sgRNA target site and min–max normalizes them to [0,1] so they can be fed alongside one-hot encoded sgRNA sequences into EpiCas-DL.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized epigenetic feature matrix — re-annotating would duplicate feature assignment Task only requires sequence-based prediction; EpiCas-DL supports sequence-only mode (CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq) without epigenetic features Cell-type-matched ATACdb/methylation/expression tracks do not exist for the target cell line, since the epigenetic features are cell-type dependent

skills.description: Use when SMITE modules have already been identified (runSpinglass/runBioNet) from scored gene networks and you need to assign pathway meaning and render interpretable subnetwork figures for reporting.
skills.name: epigenome-transcriptome-module-visualization
skills.search_text: epigenome-transcriptome-module-visualization Use when SMITE modules have already been identified (runSpinglass/runBioNet) from scored gene networks and you need to assign pathway meaning and render interpretable subnetwork figures for reporting. Input is a raw scored PvalueAnnotation with no modules yet — run runSpinglass or runBioNet first, since there is nothing to annotate or plot The goal is de novo pathway discovery rather than annotating pre-defined network modules — a standard goseq/gene-set enrichment run on a ranked gene list is simpler and more appropriate The interactome lacks symbol-level gene identifiers matching the module genes — mapping errors will produce empty or misleading module plots http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Annotate and visualize SMITE network modules identified by the spin-glass (igraph) or BioNet/Heinz algorithms from integrated transcriptome/epigenome scores, using KEGG/pathway enrichment (runGOseq) and network plots (plotModule) to interpret dysregulated subnetworks such as cell-cycle/MAPK and chromatin-regulation modules. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Annotate and visualize SMITE network modules identified by the spin-glass (igraph) or BioNet/Heinz algorithms from integrated transcriptome/epigenome scores, using KEGG/pathway enrichment (runGOseq) and network plots (plotModule) to interpret dysregulated subnetworks such as cell-cycle/MAPK and chromatin-regulation modules.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw scored PvalueAnnotation with no modules yet — run runSpinglass or runBioNet first, since there is nothing to annotate or plot The goal is de novo pathway discovery rather than annotating pre-defined network modules — a standard goseq/gene-set enrichment run on a ranked gene list is simpler and more appropriate The interactome lacks symbol-level gene identifiers matching the module genes — mapping errors will produce empty or misleading module plots

skills.description: Use when multi-track epigenomic signals have been reduced to chromatin state annotations and you need compressed state sequences to compute horizontal alignment scores, or to distinguish real epigenomes from randomized negative controls.
skills.name: epigenomic-annotation-data-processing
skills.search_text: epigenomic-annotation-data-processing Use when multi-track epigenomic signals have been reduced to chromatin state annotations and you need compressed state sequences to compute horizontal alignment scores, or to distinguish real epigenomes from randomized negative controls. Input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal (e.g. ChIP-seq bigWig tracks) rather than discrete chromatin state annotations — a chromatin state annotation method such as ChromHMM must be applied first. The goal is vertical (cross-sample, gene-level) alignment rather than horizontal (within-epigenome, 500 kb region) alignment. Sequences are uncompressed and long quiescent stretches would dominate the alignment score — apply the compression step first. http://edamontology.org/topic_3676 Preprocess chromatin state annotations (e.g. ChromHMM output from NIH Roadmap epigenomes) into compressed single-track state sequences suitable for EpiAlign local alignment scoring, including real-vs-randomized negative-control comparison of horizontal alignment scores. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Preprocess chromatin state annotations (e.g. ChromHMM output from NIH Roadmap epigenomes) into compressed single-track state sequences suitable for EpiAlign local alignment scoring, including real-vs-randomized negative-control comparison of horizontal alignment scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal (e.g. ChIP-seq bigWig tracks) rather than discrete chromatin state annotations — a chromatin state annotation method such as ChromHMM must be applied first. The goal is vertical (cross-sample, gene-level) alignment rather than horizontal (within-epigenome, 500 kb region) alignment. Sequences are uncompressed and long quiescent stretches would dominate the alignment score — apply the compression step first.

skills.description: Use when DGW clustering outputs ({prefix}_config.dgw, {prefix}_dataset.pd, {prefix}_linkage.npy, {prefix}_prototypes.pickle, {prefix}_warping_paths.pickle) exist and you need to visually inspect, validate and export shape-based clusters of epigenomic peaks.
skills.name: epigenomic-cluster-exploration
skills.search_text: epigenomic-cluster-exploration Use when DGW clustering outputs ({prefix}_config.dgw, {prefix}_dataset.pd, {prefix}_linkage.npy, {prefix}_prototypes.pickle, {prefix}_warping_paths.pickle) exist and you need to visually inspect, validate and export shape-based clusters of epigenomic peaks. No DGW clustering artefacts (linkage, prototypes, warping paths) exist yet — run the DGW clustering pipeline first The goal is de novo peak calling or alignment without visual/interactive cluster inspection (use MACS2 + dgw clustering command instead) Regions lack any points of interest and POI-based entropy validation is the objective (regions without POI entries are ignored) http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Interactive exploration of DGW-produced epigenomic mark clusters using dgw-explorer: cut the dendrogram, inspect per-cluster prototypes and warped heat-maps, overlay points of interest (e.g. TSS, first splice sites), and export aligned cluster heat-map figures. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Interactive exploration of DGW-produced epigenomic mark clusters using dgw-explorer: cut the dendrogram, inspect per-cluster prototypes and warped heat-maps, overlay points of interest (e.g. TSS, first splice sites), and export aligned cluster heat-map figures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No DGW clustering artefacts (linkage, prototypes, warping paths) exist yet — run the DGW clustering pipeline first The goal is de novo peak calling or alignment without visual/interactive cluster inspection (use MACS2 + dgw clustering command instead) Regions lack any points of interest and POI-based entropy validation is the objective (regions without POI entries are ignored)

skills.description: Use when a task asks to rebuild or validate a regulatory-element database from chromatin accessibility plus matched expression data, and database-level counts (total REMs, associated genes, mean REM length) must be reproduced.
skills.name: epigenomic-dataset-summary-statistics-validation
skills.search_text: epigenomic-dataset-summary-statistics-validation Use when a task asks to rebuild or validate a regulatory-element database from chromatin accessibility plus matched expression data, and database-level counts (total REMs, associated genes, mean REM length) must be reproduced. The task is to query an existing REM resource (e.g. EpiRegio Gene Query or Region Query for a TF of interest) rather than rebuild or validate the underlying database statistics Input data lacks matched chromatin accessibility (DNase1-seq) and gene expression (RNA-seq) samples across multiple cell types, since the StitchIt model requires paired signal-expression variation across samples Only peak-calling-style REM discovery is needed without gene-expression-linked annotation; EpiRegio's StitchIt approach deliberately annotates regions relative to actual gene expression changes, which is a different objective http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the database-level summary statistics of the EpiRegio resource by running the StitchIt algorithm on paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq data from 110 Roadmap and 56 Blueprint samples (46 tissues/cell types) and validating the computed counts against the published reference metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Reproduces the database-level summary statistics of the EpiRegio resource by running the StitchIt algorithm on paired DNase1-seq and RNA-seq data from 110 Roadmap and 56 Blueprint samples (46 tissues/cell types) and validating the computed counts against the published reference metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is to query an existing REM resource (e.g. EpiRegio Gene Query or Region Query for a TF of interest) rather than rebuild or validate the underlying database statistics Input data lacks matched chromatin accessibility (DNase1-seq) and gene expression (RNA-seq) samples across multiple cell types, since the StitchIt model requires paired signal-expression variation across samples Only peak-calling-style REM discovery is needed without gene-expression-linked annotation; EpiRegio's StitchIt approach deliberately annotates regions relative to actual gene expression changes, which is a different objective

skills.description: Use when you have BED-like interval data (methylation, histone marks) plus a gene annotation and need to map each interval to promoter/body/other-TSS categories before combining p-values into gene scores.
skills.name: epigenomic-feature-annotation
skills.search_text: epigenomic-feature-annotation Use when you have BED-like interval data (methylation, histone marks) plus a gene annotation and need to map each interval to promoter/body/other-TSS categories before combining p-values into gene scores. Your data are already gene-level (e.g. a gene x sample expression matrix with gene symbols/RefSeq IDs) and no interval-to-gene mapping is needed — go straight to annotateExpression/scorePval. Intervals cannot be assigned to genes (no genome annotation or coordinates) — the promoter/body/other_tss_distance categorization requires genomic positions. You need de novo peak calling or differential analysis of the raw sequencing data — this skill only annotates already-processed interval tables. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Annotate genomic intervals (promoters, gene bodies, other regulatory features such as H3K4me1 peaks) onto genes with SMITE's makePvalueAnnotation, then attach expression and modification p-values (annotateExpression, annotateModification) so interval-level evidence can be aggregated to gene-level scores. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Annotate genomic intervals (promoters, gene bodies, other regulatory features such as H3K4me1 peaks) onto genes with SMITE's makePvalueAnnotation, then attach expression and modification p-values (annotateExpression, annotateModification) so interval-level evidence can be aggregated to gene-level scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your data are already gene-level (e.g. a gene x sample expression matrix with gene symbols/RefSeq IDs) and no interval-to-gene mapping is needed — go straight to annotateExpression/scorePval. Intervals cannot be assigned to genes (no genome annotation or coordinates) — the promoter/body/other_tss_distance categorization requires genomic positions. You need de novo peak calling or differential analysis of the raw sequencing data — this skill only annotates already-processed interval tables.

skills.description: Use when BHi-Cect enclave loci must be intersected with epigenomic tracks (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1) to test whether activity varies with nestedness along the BPT.
skills.name: epigenomic-feature-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: epigenomic-feature-enrichment-analysis Use when BHi-Cect enclave loci must be intersected with epigenomic tracks (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1) to test whether activity varies with nestedness along the BPT. The Hi-C contact matrix has not yet been clustered with BHi-Cect (Rao_matrix → pow_trans → spec_bipart) — no enclave locus lists exist to intersect with the tracks. Input is already a downstream result table (e.g. GSEA of RNAP2/H3K4me3 prevalence in bottom enclaves or CA of bottom-enclave TF content) rather than BHi-Cect clusters plus raw annotation tracks. The goal is mechanistic interpretation of chromatin architecture (loop extrusion vs phase separation), which the article states cannot be inferred from the present analysis. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0610 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Scores each BHi-Cect enclave's nestedness (NS in [0,1] via 0/0.5/1 anchors with interpolation along the BPT) and normalizes per-enclave overlap counts with DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2 and CTCF/RAD21/CHD1 tracks to quantify epigenomic activity along the BHi-Cect partition tree. Reproduces the reported antagonism: activity progressively enriched with NS in top enclaves, progressively depleted with NS in bottom enclaves. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Scores each BHi-Cect enclave's nestedness (NS in [0,1] via 0/0.5/1 anchors with interpolation along the BPT) and normalizes per-enclave overlap counts with DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2 and CTCF/RAD21/CHD1 tracks to quantify epigenomic activity along the BHi-Cect partition tree. Reproduces the reported antagonism: activity progressively enriched with NS in top enclaves, progressively depleted with NS in bottom enclaves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Hi-C contact matrix has not yet been clustered with BHi-Cect (Rao_matrix → pow_trans → spec_bipart) — no enclave locus lists exist to intersect with the tracks. Input is already a downstream result table (e.g. GSEA of RNAP2/H3K4me3 prevalence in bottom enclaves or CA of bottom-enclave TF content) rather than BHi-Cect clusters plus raw annotation tracks. The goal is mechanistic interpretation of chromatin architecture (loop extrusion vs phase separation), which the article states cannot be inferred from the present analysis.

skills.description: Use when downloaded ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED calls must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-redundant candidate 'peak' regions that serve as binary training targets for a Basset/DeepFun CNN.
skills.name: epigenomic-peak-binarization
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-binarization Use when downloaded ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED calls must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-redundant candidate 'peak' regions that serve as binary training targets for a Basset/DeepFun CNN. The analysis requires quantitative epigenomic signal intensities — DeepFun binarizes peaks and explicitly ignores the quantitative information The question depends on long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact, which the resulting sequence-based model does not consider Input is already a fixed-length, non-redundant feature compendium (e.g. a Basset-ready HDF5 training set) — re-merging would double-process intervals http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into non-redundant 1000 bp genomic training windows for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by symmetric midpoint extension, greedy merging (>200 bp overlap tolerance), and weighted-midpoint center placement, so epigenomic profiles can be binarized as training labels. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into non-redundant 1000 bp genomic training windows for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by symmetric midpoint extension, greedy merging (>200 bp overlap tolerance), and weighted-midpoint center placement, so epigenomic profiles can be binarized as training labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires quantitative epigenomic signal intensities — DeepFun binarizes peaks and explicitly ignores the quantitative information The question depends on long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact, which the resulting sequence-based model does not consider Input is already a fixed-length, non-redundant feature compendium (e.g. a Basset-ready HDF5 training set) — re-merging would double-process intervals

skills.description: Use when comparing peak files from different epigenomic technologies (ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag) against a gold-standard reference to quantify overlap, precision, recall, and annotation differences.
skills.name: epigenomic-peak-file-benchmarking
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-file-benchmarking Use when comparing peak files from different epigenomic technologies (ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, ChIP-seq, CUT&Run, CUT&Tag) against a gold-standard reference to quantify overlap, precision, recall, and annotation differences. skills.summary: Benchmark epigenomic peak files (e.g. ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq, CUT&Tag vs ChIP-seq) using EpiCompare, which computes peak overlaps, precision-recall metrics, and functional annotations against a reference dataset in a single HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) rather than called peak files — EpiCompare operates downstream on peak intervals, not reads Only one peak file is available with no reference or comparison group, since the skill's purpose is contrasting datasets or benchmarking against a gold-standard Input files are already processed feature tables or summary statistics rather than genomic interval (BED/narrowPeak) peak sets

skills.name: epigenomic-peak-file-granges-handling
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-file-granges-handling Use when peak files from epigenomic assays (narrowPeak/BED, e.g., ENCODE ENCFF044JNJ K562 DNase-seq) need to be loaded into R and standardized as GRanges with consistent genome build and blacklist filtering prior to overlap or ChromHMM annotation analysis. skills.description: Use when peak files originate from different genome reference builds (e.g. hg19 and hg38 mixed inputs) or raw BED formats, and they must be imported as GRanges, coordinate-lifted, and standardized before EpiCompare quality-control and benchmarking.
skills.name: epigenomic-peak-granges-manipulation
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-granges-manipulation Use when peak files originate from different genome reference builds (e.g. hg19 and hg38 mixed inputs) or raw BED formats, and they must be imported as GRanges, coordinate-lifted, and standardized before EpiCompare quality-control and benchmarking. All input peak files already share the same genome build and are already GRanges or consistently formatted BED — no liftOver/build harmonization step is needed The goal is Picard duplication-rate summary import — EpiCompare::gather_files with type='picard' imports these as data frames, not as peak GRanges for coordinate manipulation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Import epigenomic peak files (BED, narrowPeak, .stringent.bed.gz) into R as GRanges objects, harmonize their genome builds via rtracklayer liftOver with UCSC over.chain files, and standardize them (drop blacklisted and non-standard chromosomes) so EpiCompare can compare CUT&Run/CUT&Tag/ChIP-seq peak sets in a single QC report. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Import epigenomic peak files (BED, narrowPeak, .stringent.bed.gz) into R as GRanges objects, harmonize their genome builds via rtracklayer liftOver with UCSC over.chain files, and standardize them (drop blacklisted and non-standard chromosomes) so EpiCompare can compare CUT&Run/CUT&Tag/ChIP-seq peak sets in a single QC report.
