skills.description: Use when you need to compare or QC epigenomic peak files (narrowPeak/BED GRanges) across technologies such as ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq, or CUT&Tag/CUT&Run vs a ChIP-seq gold-standard reference.
skills.name: epigenomic-peak-quality-control
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-quality-control Use when you need to compare or QC epigenomic peak files (narrowPeak/BED GRanges) across technologies such as ATAC-seq vs DNase-seq, or CUT&Tag/CUT&Run vs a ChIP-seq gold-standard reference. When the goal is raw read alignment or peak calling rather than comparison/QC of already-called peak files When only one peak file with no reference or comparator is available, since the package's main functionality is to contrast epigenomic datasets When peaks cannot be mapped to a supported genome build (hg19/hg38), since blacklist filtering and annotation depend on it http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Run EpiCompare to quality-control and benchmark epigenomic peak files (e.g. ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq) by generating a single interactive HTML report with General Metrics, Peak Overlap, and Functional Annotation sections. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Run EpiCompare to quality-control and benchmark epigenomic peak files (e.g. ATAC-seq, DNase-seq, CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq) by generating a single interactive HTML report with General Metrics, Peak Overlap, and Functional Annotation sections.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is raw read alignment or peak calling rather than comparison/QC of already-called peak files When only one peak file with no reference or comparator is available, since the package's main functionality is to contrast epigenomic datasets When peaks cannot be mapped to a supported genome build (hg19/hg38), since blacklist filtering and annotation depend on it

skills.description: Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering/alignment methods against a known ground truth: you have seed epigenomic peaks (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) and need a controlled (v, p) noise grid with verifiable cluster labels.
skills.name: epigenomic-peak-simulation
skills.search_text: epigenomic-peak-simulation Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering/alignment methods against a known ground truth: you have seed epigenomic peaks (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) and need a controlled (v, p) noise grid with verifiable cluster labels. When the goal is to validate biological alignment of genomic landmarks (TSS/FSS location entropy) on real data — the paper does that separately on real ENCODE data, not on simulations. When no ground-truth seed-of-origin labels can be defined for the regions — the multi-class MCC against seed labels would be meaningless. When the input is already a fixed experimental dataset without controlled perturbations — no (v, p) grid can be swept and no accuracy benchmark against known patterns is possible. Generates synthetic ChIP-Seq peak benchmark datasets by perturbing seed ENCODE H3K4me3 K562 peak regions with multiplicative Gaussian noise, bin deletion/duplication, and orientation flips, in order to quantify (via multi-class MCC) how well clustering methods recover the known seed-of-origin labels. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Generates synthetic ChIP-Seq peak benchmark datasets by perturbing seed ENCODE H3K4me3 K562 peak regions with multiplicative Gaussian noise, bin deletion/duplication, and orientation flips, in order to quantify (via multi-class MCC) how well clustering methods recover the known seed-of-origin labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to validate biological alignment of genomic landmarks (TSS/FSS location entropy) on real data — the paper does that separately on real ENCODE data, not on simulations. When no ground-truth seed-of-origin labels can be defined for the regions — the multi-class MCC against seed labels would be meaningless. When the input is already a fixed experimental dataset without controlled perturbations — no (v, p) grid can be swept and no accuracy benchmark against known patterns is possible.

skills.description: Use when you have ChromHMM chromatin state sequences for a single Roadmap epigenome and want to find recurrent local chromatin state patterns or -matching genomic regions for a query region.
skills.name: epigenomic-query-search-horizontal-alignment
skills.search_text: epigenomic-query-search-horizontal-alignment Use when you have ChromHMM chromatin state sequences for a single Roadmap epigenome and want to find recurrent local chromatin state patterns or -matching genomic regions for a query region. Your goal is comparing chromatin state patterns across multiple epigenomes (vertical alignment between samples) rather than finding recurrent patterns within a single epigenome Your input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than discrete chromatin state sequences — apply ChromHMM state annotation and the compression step first You need to compare regions at single-nucleotide or sequence (DNA) level; EpiAlign operates only on coarse chromatin state label sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Extract recurrent chromatin state patterns within a single epigenome by dividing it into 500 kb regions and running EpiAlign's Smith-Waterman-style local alignment of each query region against all others, revealing cell-type-specific chromatin patterns. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Extract recurrent chromatin state patterns within a single epigenome by dividing it into 500 kb regions and running EpiAlign's Smith-Waterman-style local alignment of each query region against all others, revealing cell-type-specific chromatin patterns.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is comparing chromatin state patterns across multiple epigenomes (vertical alignment between samples) rather than finding recurrent patterns within a single epigenome Your input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than discrete chromatin state sequences — apply ChromHMM state annotation and the compression step first You need to compare regions at single-nucleotide or sequence (DNA) level; EpiAlign operates only on coarse chromatin state label sequences

skills.description: Use when mapping non-coding regulatory regions (e.g. ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq peaks) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate.
skills.name: epigenomic-sequence-conservation-scoring
skills.search_text: epigenomic-sequence-conservation-scoring Use when mapping non-coding regulatory regions (e.g. ATAC-seq, ChIP-seq, DNase-seq peaks) across species and sequence-based liftOver alone suffers from multi-mapping, low precision, or low mapping rate. When the query regions are coding or the goal is pure sequence alignment rather than regulatory element orthology — existing sequence-conservation methods already address this and AdaLiftOver targets non-coding regulatory regions When no matched orthologous epigenomic datasets exist for the species pair and no training pair is available to learn logistic regression parameters via training_module() http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Prioritize orthologous non-coding regions across species by combining UCSC liftOver candidate target regions with logistic probability scores aggregating epigenomic signal similarity and sequence grammar similarity, so that regulatory (epigenomic) evidence can support or override sequence-based mapping. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Prioritize orthologous non-coding regions across species by combining UCSC liftOver candidate target regions with logistic probability scores aggregating epigenomic signal similarity and sequence grammar similarity, so that regulatory (epigenomic) evidence can support or override sequence-based mapping.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query regions are coding or the goal is pure sequence alignment rather than regulatory element orthology — existing sequence-conservation methods already address this and AdaLiftOver targets non-coding regulatory regions When no matched orthologous epigenomic datasets exist for the species pair and no training pair is available to learn logistic regression parameters via training_module()

skills.description: Use when you have cell type-specific chromatin loops (e.g. SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) plus matched ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and RNA-seq reference data and need to validate loop anchors and linked genes against matched cell type signatures.
skills.name: epigenomic-signal-quantification-at-loop-anchors
skills.search_text: epigenomic-signal-quantification-at-loop-anchors Use when you have cell type-specific chromatin loops (e.g. SnapHiC *.postprocessed.summits.bedpe) plus matched ATAC-seq, H3K27ac and RNA-seq reference data and need to validate loop anchors and linked genes against matched cell type signatures. Loops were not called per cell type (e.g. pooled bulk Hi-C loops), so matched vs. unmatched enrichment is not meaningful No cell type-matched ATAC-seq/H3K27ac/RNA-seq reference data exist for the cell types of interest The goal is loop calling itself rather than downstream validation — use the SnapHiC pipeline steps (bin, rwr, hic, interaction, postprocess) instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Quantifies CPM-normalized ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq signal at chromatin loop anchor regions and FPKM expression of loop-linked promoters, then tests whether cell type-specific loops (called with SnapHiC) are supported by cell type-matched regulatory signatures. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Quantifies CPM-normalized ATAC-seq and H3K27ac ChIP-seq signal at chromatin loop anchor regions and FPKM expression of loop-linked promoters, then tests whether cell type-specific loops (called with SnapHiC) are supported by cell type-matched regulatory signatures.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Loops were not called per cell type (e.g. pooled bulk Hi-C loops), so matched vs. unmatched enrichment is not meaningful No cell type-matched ATAC-seq/H3K27ac/RNA-seq reference data exist for the cell types of interest The goal is loop calling itself rather than downstream validation — use the SnapHiC pipeline steps (bin, rwr, hic, interaction, postprocess) instead

skills.description: Use when a genomic interval has multiple non-independent p-values (e.g. correlated methylation or H3K4me1 probes within one gene) that must be combined into a single valid gene-level significance score.
skills.name: epigenomic-significance-scoring
skills.search_text: epigenomic-significance-scoring Use when a genomic interval has multiple non-independent p-values (e.g. correlated methylation or H3K4me1 probes within one gene) that must be combined into a single valid gene-level significance score. The p-values to combine are already independent — plain Stouffer/Fisher combination suffices and Cholesky whitening is unnecessary The correlation matrix Sigma is not symmetric positive-definite (e.g. fewer observations than probes), making the Cholesky factorization undefined The goal is differential module detection from pre-scored genes with no raw p-values to combine — use module-finding tools instead Assign per-gene significance scores by combining correlated epigenomic (e.g. methylation, histone-mark) and transcriptomic p-values, correcting non-independence via a Cholesky-whitened, Stouffer-based combination as implemented in the SMITE R/Bioconductor package. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Assign per-gene significance scores by combining correlated epigenomic (e.g. methylation, histone-mark) and transcriptomic p-values, correcting non-independence via a Cholesky-whitened, Stouffer-based combination as implemented in the SMITE R/Bioconductor package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The p-values to combine are already independent — plain Stouffer/Fisher combination suffices and Cholesky whitening is unnecessary The correlation matrix Sigma is not symmetric positive-definite (e.g. fewer observations than probes), making the Cholesky factorization undefined The goal is differential module detection from pre-scored genes with no raw p-values to combine — use module-finding tools instead

skills.description: Use when UCSC liftOver or adaptive_liftover has produced many candidate orthologous target regions per query interval and you need to prioritize them by functional regulatory similarity rather than sequence conservation alone.
skills.name: epigenomic-similarity-based-candidate-filtering
skills.search_text: epigenomic-similarity-based-candidate-filtering Use when UCSC liftOver or adaptive_liftover has produced many candidate orthologous target regions per query interval and you need to prioritize them by functional regulatory similarity rather than sequence conservation alone. When the query regions are coding regions or whole genes rather than candidate non-coding regulatory elements — AdaLiftOver targets orthologous regulatory elements via epigenomic signal and sequence grammar conservation. When no matched orthologous functional genomic (epigenome) datasets exist for the species pair and no training data is available to estimate logistic regression parameters. When simple synteny/sequence-conservation mapping suffices and multi-mapping ambiguity is not a concern. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 A filtering skill from AdaLiftOver that prioritizes liftOver candidate target regions by aggregating epigenomic signal similarities (from 67 matched ENCODE human-mouse TF/DNA methylation ChIP-seq and DNase-seq datasets) and sequence grammar similarities into logistic probability scores, then retaining at most best_k regions per query above a score threshold. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: A filtering skill from AdaLiftOver that prioritizes liftOver candidate target regions by aggregating epigenomic signal similarities (from 67 matched ENCODE human-mouse TF/DNA methylation ChIP-seq and DNase-seq datasets) and sequence grammar similarities into logistic probability scores, then retaining at most best_k regions per query above a score threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query regions are coding regions or whole genes rather than candidate non-coding regulatory elements — AdaLiftOver targets orthologous regulatory elements via epigenomic signal and sequence grammar conservation. When no matched orthologous functional genomic (epigenome) datasets exist for the species pair and no training data is available to estimate logistic regression parameters. When simple synteny/sequence-conservation mapping suffices and multi-mapping ambiguity is not a concern.

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon-seq paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into binary epihaplotype tables of phased per-molecule mCpG calls as input for epiallele or methylated-core analysis.
skills.name: epihaplotype-methylation-call-extraction
skills.search_text: epihaplotype-methylation-call-extraction Use when bisulfite amplicon-seq paired-end FASTQ reads (e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) must be converted into binary epihaplotype tables of phased per-molecule mCpG calls as input for epiallele or methylated-core analysis. Data are whole-genome or reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing reads rather than amplicon-scale reads, since ampliMethProfiler and core extraction assume a fixed amplicon reference with known CpG positions Single-nucleotide (non-phased) methylation quantification is the goal — the article notes stable phased epialleles 'cannot be identified' by such techniques, and this skill targets phased per-molecule calls Input is already a binary epihaplotype table ready for MethCoresProfiler Modules 1–3; re-running the extraction steps would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extract per-molecule binary mCpG configurations (epihaplotypes) from bisulfite amplicon-seq reads by merging paired-end FASTQs with PEAR, filtering on quality and length, converting to FASTA with PRINSEQ, and calling methylation states with ampliMethProfiler, producing the binary epihaplotype tables consumed by MethCoresProfiler. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Extract per-molecule binary mCpG configurations (epihaplotypes) from bisulfite amplicon-seq reads by merging paired-end FASTQs with PEAR, filtering on quality and length, converting to FASTA with PRINSEQ, and calling methylation states with ampliMethProfiler, producing the binary epihaplotype tables consumed by MethCoresProfiler.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are whole-genome or reduced-representation bisulfite sequencing reads rather than amplicon-scale reads, since ampliMethProfiler and core extraction assume a fixed amplicon reference with known CpG positions Single-nucleotide (non-phased) methylation quantification is the goal — the article notes stable phased epialleles 'cannot be identified' by such techniques, and this skill targets phased per-molecule calls Input is already a binary epihaplotype table ready for MethCoresProfiler Modules 1–3; re-running the extraction steps would be redundant

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) can match a task-specific expert model on binary classification of long-range eQTL sequences across multiple cell types.
skills.name: eqtl-binary-classification-finetuning
skills.search_text: eqtl-binary-classification-finetuning Use when evaluating whether DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) can match a task-specific expert model on binary classification of long-range eQTL sequences across multiple cell types. The task requires base-pair-resolution regression or 2D structure outputs (e.g., contact map prediction) rather than binary classification — those DNALONGBENCH tasks have different output shapes and metrics Input sequences are short-range (well below 450,000 bp) — simpler short-range benchmarks like Genomic Benchmarks, GUE, or NT Benchmark are more appropriate You intend to evaluate transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — the paper excluded them because quadratic self-attention cost renders 450k bp tasks infeasible http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the DNALONGBENCH eQTL prediction (eQTLP) benchmark by fine-tuning a CNN baseline, HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, and Caduceus-PS on a binary classification task over 450,000 bp sequences (31,282 samples) and comparing their per-cell-type AUROC against the Enformer Expert Model, which averages 0.681 across nine cell types. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the DNALONGBENCH eQTL prediction (eQTLP) benchmark by fine-tuning a CNN baseline, HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, and Caduceus-PS on a binary classification task over 450,000 bp sequences (31,282 samples) and comparing their per-cell-type AUROC against the Enformer Expert Model, which averages 0.681 across nine cell types.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires base-pair-resolution regression or 2D structure outputs (e.g., contact map prediction) rather than binary classification — those DNALONGBENCH tasks have different output shapes and metrics Input sequences are short-range (well below 450,000 bp) — simpler short-range benchmarks like Genomic Benchmarks, GUE, or NT Benchmark are more appropriate You intend to evaluate transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — the paper excluded them because quadratic self-attention cost renders 450k bp tasks infeasible

skills.description: Use when building labeled positive/negative SNP training sets for a non-coding variant prioritization model, sourcing from deltaSVM dsQTLs, HGMD regulatory SNPs, brain eQTLs, or GRASP/DeepSEA-associated SNPs with matched negatives.
skills.name: eqtl-dataset-assembly
skills.search_text: eqtl-dataset-assembly Use when building labeled positive/negative SNP training sets for a non-coding variant prioritization model, sourcing from deltaSVM dsQTLs, HGMD regulatory SNPs, brain eQTLs, or GRASP/DeepSEA-associated SNPs with matched negatives. Your model input is already a curated feature table or pre-scored variant set — this skill is only for assembling the raw labeled training sets You need coding variant prioritization — these sets target whole-genome non-coding variants; gene prioritization (step 2 of iMEGES) uses different gene-based scores You lack access to the upstream sources (deltaSVM, HGMD April 2012, GRASP via DeepSEA, 1000 Genomes) and cannot reproduce the exact counts or frequency matching Assembles the four labeled variant-prioritization training datasets used by iMEGES/ncDeepBrain (dsQTL, HGMD non-coding regulatory, brain eQTL, and DeepSEA-derived GRASP sets), each written as a tab-delimited file with variant identifiers and positive/negative labels. Accurate assembly is critical because class sizes (e.g. 574 positives vs 27,735 negatives) directly drive the deep learning variant score. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7
skills.summary: Assembles the four labeled variant-prioritization training datasets used by iMEGES/ncDeepBrain (dsQTL, HGMD non-coding regulatory, brain eQTL, and DeepSEA-derived GRASP sets), each written as a tab-delimited file with variant identifiers and positive/negative labels. Accurate assembly is critical because class sizes (e.g. 574 positives vs 27,735 negatives) directly drive the deep learning variant score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your model input is already a curated feature table or pre-scored variant set — this skill is only for assembling the raw labeled training sets You need coding variant prioritization — these sets target whole-genome non-coding variants; gene prioritization (step 2 of iMEGES) uses different gene-based scores You lack access to the upstream sources (deltaSVM, HGMD April 2012, GRASP via DeepSEA, 1000 Genomes) and cannot reproduce the exact counts or frequency matching

skills.description: Use when you have per-SNP deepC variant-impact/saliency score tracks and want to test whether a candidate SNP set (e.g. cell-type-specific eQTLs) is enriched for high saliency against a re-sampled, region-matched background via a two-sample KS test.
skills.name: eqtl-saliency-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: eqtl-saliency-enrichment-analysis Use when you have per-SNP deepC variant-impact/saliency score tracks and want to test whether a candidate SNP set (e.g. cell-type-specific eQTLs) is enriched for high saliency against a re-sampled, region-matched background via a two-sample KS test. You have not yet generated per-SNP saliency scores with deepC — run the variant-impact prediction step first, since this skill only re-analyzes existing score tracks. Your candidate variant set is not spatially restricted to open chromatin or CTCF sites, so the ENCODE peak-union background would not be a matched null. You need a direct deepC-vs-Akita comparison — the paper explicitly presents no such benchmark, deferring comparative study to future work. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Tests whether cell-type-specific eQTLs (e.g. GTEx v7 GM12878) have elevated deepC saliency scores relative to randomly re-sampled SNPs from matched open-chromatin/CTCF regions, using a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. This reproduces the deepC paper's finding that saliency can fine-map sequence determinants of chromatin architecture linked to gene expression. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Tests whether cell-type-specific eQTLs (e.g. GTEx v7 GM12878) have elevated deepC saliency scores relative to randomly re-sampled SNPs from matched open-chromatin/CTCF regions, using a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. This reproduces the deepC paper's finding that saliency can fine-map sequence determinants of chromatin architecture linked to gene expression.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have not yet generated per-SNP saliency scores with deepC — run the variant-impact prediction step first, since this skill only re-analyzes existing score tracks. Your candidate variant set is not spatially restricted to open chromatin or CTCF sites, so the ENCODE peak-union background would not be a matched null. You need a direct deepC-vs-Akita comparison — the paper explicitly presents no such benchmark, deferring comparative study to future work.

skills.description: Use when fitting ODE-based gene regulation models with sigmoidal activation and per-gene mRNA decay to smoothed time-course expression data, and a fast, OpenCL-friendly numerical integrator is needed.
skills.name: euler-ode-integration
skills.search_text: euler-ode-integration Use when fitting ODE-based gene regulation models with sigmoidal activation and per-gene mRNA decay to smoothed time-course expression data, and a fast, OpenCL-friendly numerical integrator is needed. The target gene's expression does not change significantly over the whole time-course — the no-change model applies and the gene carries no regulatory information The gene can be fitted by the constant synthesis model (any regulator fits with w = 0 and large b), so it should be excluded as a target You need a complete description of regulatory interactions — time-series expression data cannot in principle provide this and Genexpi should be one of multiple sources of insight http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Integrates the Genexpi gene-regulation ODE dz/dt = k1*f(rho) - k2*z, with sigmoidal activation f(x) = 1/(1+e^-x) and regulatory input rho(t) = sum_j w_j*y_j(t) + b, using the computationally cheap Euler method on subsampled B-spline-smoothed expression curves to infer regulatory interactions from time-course data. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: Integrates the Genexpi gene-regulation ODE dz/dt = k1*f(rho) - k2*z, with sigmoidal activation f(x) = 1/(1+e^-x) and regulatory input rho(t) = sum_j w_j*y_j(t) + b, using the computationally cheap Euler method on subsampled B-spline-smoothed expression curves to infer regulatory interactions from time-course data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target gene's expression does not change significantly over the whole time-course — the no-change model applies and the gene carries no regulatory information The gene can be fitted by the constant synthesis model (any regulator fits with w = 0 and large b), so it should be excluded as a target You need a complete description of regulatory interactions — time-series expression data cannot in principle provide this and Genexpi should be one of multiple sources of insight

skills.description: Use when short-read sequencing data supplied as FASTQ files needs quality assessment — e.g., per-cycle quality scores, read-quality distributions, and QC summaries across many samples rendered in one combined multi-panel report figure.
skills.name: example-dataset-qc-reporting
skills.search_text: example-dataset-qc-reporting Use when short-read sequencing data supplied as FASTQ files needs quality assessment — e.g., per-cycle quality scores, read-quality distributions, and QC summaries across many samples rendered in one combined multi-panel report figure. Input reads are already aligned (e.g., BAM) or provided in a non-FASTQ format, so no FASTQ quality computation applies The goal is read preprocessing (filtering/trimming) rather than generating a visual quality report Only one small FASTQ file needs a quick text-based QC summary rather than a combined multi-panel figure for many files http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generates and plots detailed per-file quality reports for FASTQ files using systemPipeR's seeFastq and seeFastqPlot functions, producing a single combined multi-panel figure that enables visual inspection of large numbers of FASTQ files. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1241-0
skills.summary: Generates and plots detailed per-file quality reports for FASTQ files using systemPipeR's seeFastq and seeFastqPlot functions, producing a single combined multi-panel figure that enables visual inspection of large numbers of FASTQ files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already aligned (e.g., BAM) or provided in a non-FASTQ format, so no FASTQ quality computation applies The goal is read preprocessing (filtering/trimming) rather than generating a visual quality report Only one small FASTQ file needs a quick text-based QC summary rather than a combined multi-panel figure for many files

skills.description: Use when analyzing how the spatial auto-correlation of a binned ChIP-seq signal changes under coarse-graining, e.g. diagnosing whether broad-domain enrichment grows with scale as in H3K27me3 data.
skills.name: exponential-fit-scaling-analysis
skills.search_text: exponential-fit-scaling-analysis Use when analyzing how the spatial auto-correlation of a binned ChIP-seq signal changes under coarse-graining, e.g. diagnosing whether broad-domain enrichment grows with scale as in H3K27me3 data. When the goal is domain calling output (broadPeak.bed) rather than characterizing scale-dependent auto-correlation — run the full RECOGNICER pipeline including domain retrieval and significance determination instead When the signal is synthetic random-placement data expected to keep lambda near 100 kb — the fit is still run, but growth of lambda should NOT be expected or claimed When C(0) (self-correlation/variance) would be included in the fit — the method explicitly ignores C(0) to avoid confounding variance Fits the two-point auto-correlation curve C(r) ~ C0 * exp(-r/lambda) with a single exponential at each coarse-graining scale to extract a characteristic auto-correlation length lambda, and tracks how lambda scales across recursive block transformation rounds (RECOGNICER). Used to distinguish real ChIP-seq long-range correlation growth from synthetic random-placement data. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Fits the two-point auto-correlation curve C(r) ~ C0 * exp(-r/lambda) with a single exponential at each coarse-graining scale to extract a characteristic auto-correlation length lambda, and tracks how lambda scales across recursive block transformation rounds (RECOGNICER). Used to distinguish real ChIP-seq long-range correlation growth from synthetic random-placement data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is domain calling output (broadPeak.bed) rather than characterizing scale-dependent auto-correlation — run the full RECOGNICER pipeline including domain retrieval and significance determination instead When the signal is synthetic random-placement data expected to keep lambda near 100 kb — the fit is still run, but growth of lambda should NOT be expected or claimed When C(0) (self-correlation/variance) would be included in the fit — the method explicitly ignores C(0) to avoid confounding variance

skills.description: Use when 2D single-cell UMI/read count matrices plus cell annotations (donor and cell type) must be converted to pseudobulk and the number of expressed genes per sample counted at specific per-cell thresholds, e.g. to validate expression probability models.
skills.name: expressed-gene-count-thresholding
skills.search_text: expressed-gene-count-thresholding Use when 2D single-cell UMI/read count matrices plus cell annotations (donor and cell type) must be converted to pseudobulk and the number of expressed genes per sample counted at specific per-cell thresholds, e.g. to validate expression probability models. Input is already pseudobulk or bulk expression data — create.pseudobulk aggregation per donor and cell type is unnecessary and inappropriate Goal is differential expression testing (edgeR/limma-voom pseudobulk DE) rather than quantifying how many genes are expressed above a threshold Count data are read-depth normalized transcripts rather than raw UMI counts, since thresholds like count > 0 / count > 10 are defined on per-pseudobulk UMI counts http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Counts the number of expressed genes per pseudobulk sample (donor x cell type) from single-cell UMI count matrices, at user-defined expression thresholds (e.g. UMI count > 0 and count > 10), as implemented in scPower's calculate.gene.counts; these observed counts are used to benchmark predicted expression probabilities. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Counts the number of expressed genes per pseudobulk sample (donor x cell type) from single-cell UMI count matrices, at user-defined expression thresholds (e.g. UMI count > 0 and count > 10), as implemented in scPower's calculate.gene.counts; these observed counts are used to benchmark predicted expression probabilities.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already pseudobulk or bulk expression data — create.pseudobulk aggregation per donor and cell type is unnecessary and inappropriate Goal is differential expression testing (edgeR/limma-voom pseudobulk DE) rather than quantifying how many genes are expressed above a threshold Count data are read-depth normalized transcripts rather than raw UMI counts, since thresholds like count > 0 / count > 10 are defined on per-pseudobulk UMI counts

skills.description: Use when a mean-centered GEO expression matrix has been produced (e.g., by COnTORT's gffMatch step) and you must confirm the transformation did not alter rows/columns or annotation columns before downstream analysis.
skills.name: expression-matrix-dimension-validation
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-dimension-validation Use when a mean-centered GEO expression matrix has been produced (e.g., by COnTORT's gffMatch step) and you must confirm the transformation did not alter rows/columns or annotation columns before downstream analysis. The input is raw, unnormalized GEO data — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO, so mean-centering raw values is out of scope You need per-gene (row-wise) centering or scaling rather than per-experiment (column-wise) mean-centering — this skill specifically centers each GSM experiment column The matrix has not yet been annotated via the GenBank (.gbff) file and joined with gffMatch, so the five-column annotation layout does not yet exist http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Verification step for COnTORT's mean-centered transcriptomic output: after subtracting per-experiment (per-GSM column) means from the organized expression matrix, confirm the resulting tab-delimited file preserves the input dimensions and that each expression column's mean is approximately zero. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Verification step for COnTORT's mean-centered transcriptomic output: after subtracting per-experiment (per-GSM column) means from the organized expression matrix, confirm the resulting tab-delimited file preserves the input dimensions and that each expression column's mean is approximately zero.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw, unnormalized GEO data — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO, so mean-centering raw values is out of scope You need per-gene (row-wise) centering or scaling rather than per-experiment (column-wise) mean-centering — this skill specifically centers each GSM experiment column The matrix has not yet been annotated via the GenBank (.gbff) file and joined with gffMatch, so the five-column annotation layout does not yet exist

skills.description: Use when a raw numeric expression or methylation matrix (e.g., from golubEsets, ALL, HSMMSingleCell) must be cleaned before cola's feature selection and consensus partitioning.
skills.name: expression-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: expression-matrix-preprocessing Use when a raw numeric expression or methylation matrix (e.g., from golubEsets, ALL, HSMMSingleCell) must be cleaned before cola's feature selection and consensus partitioning. The matrix has already been through adjust_matrix() — re-applying would impute a second time and re-filter rows against shifted variance percentiles. You need dataset-specific filtering rules instead of the generic cleaning defaults, e.g. MCF10CA cells with <2 million reads, recount2 genes with <2 reads in >50% of samples, or methylation probes on sex chromosomes/overlapping known SNPs — those are separate per-dataset filter steps. You want to remove ambiguous samples (silhouette score < 0.5); that removal belongs to signature analysis, not to input-matrix preprocessing. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Cleans a numeric gene-expression matrix via cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: removes rows with >25% missing samples, imputes missing values with impute.knn(), winsorizes values at the 5th/95th percentiles, and removes rows with zero variance or variance below the 5th percentile of all row variances. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: Cleans a numeric gene-expression matrix via cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: removes rows with >25% missing samples, imputes missing values with impute.knn(), winsorizes values at the 5th/95th percentiles, and removes rows with zero variance or variance below the 5th percentile of all row variances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix has already been through adjust_matrix() — re-applying would impute a second time and re-filter rows against shifted variance percentiles. You need dataset-specific filtering rules instead of the generic cleaning defaults, e.g. MCF10CA cells with <2 million reads, recount2 genes with <2 reads in >50% of samples, or methylation probes on sex chromosomes/overlapping known SNPs — those are separate per-dataset filter steps. You want to remove ambiguous samples (silhouette score < 0.5); that removal belongs to signature analysis, not to input-matrix preprocessing.

skills.description: Use when a fitted expression prior (gamma.linear.fit.new, disp.fun.general.new, read.umi.fit.new) has just been estimated from pilot scRNA-seq UMI matrices and must be checked before use in experimental design or power calculations.
skills.name: expression-prior-validation-scrnaseq
skills.search_text: expression-prior-validation-scrnaseq Use when a fitted expression prior (gamma.linear.fit.new, disp.fun.general.new, read.umi.fit.new) has just been estimated from pilot scRNA-seq UMI matrices and must be checked before use in experimental design or power calculations. The planned experiment uses read-count (full-length) protocols or cell types with no matching pilot data — data-driven priors only reliably assess sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot study The input is already a published expression prior (e.g. 10X_PBMC_1, Pancreas_alphabeta) rather than a newly fitted prior that needs validation The goal is DEG/eQTL power itself rather than validating the expression-probability component of the model http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validates fitted scPower expression priors (gamma mixture fits, mean-dispersion curves, read-depth-UMI curves) by predicting expressed gene numbers for a cell type and comparing them against observed expressed gene counts from pilot data, ensuring the prior is trustworthy before it is used for power analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Validates fitted scPower expression priors (gamma mixture fits, mean-dispersion curves, read-depth-UMI curves) by predicting expressed gene numbers for a cell type and comparing them against observed expressed gene counts from pilot data, ensuring the prior is trustworthy before it is used for power analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The planned experiment uses read-count (full-length) protocols or cell types with no matching pilot data — data-driven priors only reliably assess sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot study The input is already a published expression prior (e.g. 10X_PBMC_1, Pancreas_alphabeta) rather than a newly fitted prior that needs validation The goal is DEG/eQTL power itself rather than validating the expression-probability component of the model

skills.description: Use when designing or powering an interindividual scRNA-seq DE/eQTL study and you need the probability that a gene passes expression detection thresholds (e.g. min.counts=3, perc.indiv=0.5) at given cells-per-sample and read depth.
skills.name: expression-probability-estimation-from-gamma-mixed-fits
skills.search_text: expression-probability-estimation-from-gamma-mixed-fits Use when designing or powering an interindividual scRNA-seq DE/eQTL study and you need the probability that a gene passes expression detection thresholds (e.g. min.counts=3, perc.indiv=0.5) at given cells-per-sample and read depth. When the goal is single-cell-level (not pseudobulk/interindividual) DE testing power — the model was specifically developed for the pseudobulk approach When a pilot study's priors would be extrapolated far beyond its sample size — data driven priors only reliably assess overall power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data sets When continuous cell annotations (e.g. pseudotime) define the comparison — they would need to be discretized before power analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Estimates the single-cell detection power of a gene (probability it is expressed/observed at a given sequencing depth and cell number) using scPower's zero-inflated gamma-mixed fits of expression rank/mean distributions, which are combined multiplicatively with pseudobulk DE power to yield overall detection power. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Estimates the single-cell detection power of a gene (probability it is expressed/observed at a given sequencing depth and cell number) using scPower's zero-inflated gamma-mixed fits of expression rank/mean distributions, which are combined multiplicatively with pseudobulk DE power to yield overall detection power.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is single-cell-level (not pseudobulk/interindividual) DE testing power — the model was specifically developed for the pseudobulk approach When a pilot study's priors would be extrapolated far beyond its sample size — data driven priors only reliably assess overall power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data sets When continuous cell annotations (e.g. pseudotime) define the comparison — they would need to be discretized before power analysis

skills.description: Use when a planned or pilot scRNA-seq design needs its predicted expressed-gene numbers checked against real data, e.g. subsampled UMI count matrices with per-cell-type annotations available.
skills.name: expression-probability-model-validation
skills.search_text: expression-probability-model-validation Use when a planned or pilot scRNA-seq design needs its predicted expressed-gene numbers checked against real data, e.g. subsampled UMI count matrices with per-cell-type annotations available. Input is a 3d pseudobulk matrix already, or expression priors must be fitted from scratch (use nbinom.estimation/mixed.gamma.estimation workflow instead) The goal is DEG/eQTL power or budget optimization rather than validating expression probability predictions against observed data Data are read-count based or from a non-droplet technology for which the GSE185714-derived UMI priors do not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Validates scPower's expression probability model by comparing predicted numbers of expressed genes per cell type against observed counts from subsampled 10X PBMC UMI count matrices, quantifying agreement with r2 across read-depth conditions. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Validates scPower's expression probability model by comparing predicted numbers of expressed genes per cell type against observed counts from subsampled 10X PBMC UMI count matrices, quantifying agreement with r2 across read-depth conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a 3d pseudobulk matrix already, or expression priors must be fitted from scratch (use nbinom.estimation/mixed.gamma.estimation workflow instead) The goal is DEG/eQTL power or budget optimization rather than validating expression probability predictions against observed data Data are read-count based or from a non-droplet technology for which the GSE185714-derived UMI priors do not apply

skills.description: Use when designing or validating single cell RNA-seq experiments and you need per-gene detection probabilities at a given read depth, cells per individual, and sample size, or when checking that model-predicted expressed gene counts match observed counts in a held-out dataset.
skills.name: expression-probability-prediction
skills.search_text: expression-probability-prediction Use when designing or validating single cell RNA-seq experiments and you need per-gene detection probabilities at a given read depth, cells per individual, and sample size, or when checking that model-predicted expressed gene counts match observed counts in a held-out dataset. The goal is differential expression or eQTL power itself rather than the per-gene expression detection probability component — use the combined scPower power estimation that multiplies expression probability with eQTL power instead The pilot data used to fit priors comes from a different tissue or platform technology than the target counts (priors are UMI/read-count and tissue specific) Continuous cell annotations (e.g. pseudo time) are present and cannot be discretized into donor/cell type categories required by create.pseudobulk http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Predict per-gene cell-type-specific expression probabilities for a scRNA-seq design using scPower's parametric model (gamma mixed expression priors, read-UMI and mean-dispersion fits), and validate predictions by comparing summed predicted versus observed expressed-gene counts (r2 > 0.9) against independent pseudobulk data. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Predict per-gene cell-type-specific expression probabilities for a scRNA-seq design using scPower's parametric model (gamma mixed expression priors, read-UMI and mean-dispersion fits), and validate predictions by comparing summed predicted versus observed expressed-gene counts (r2 > 0.9) against independent pseudobulk data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential expression or eQTL power itself rather than the per-gene expression detection probability component — use the combined scPower power estimation that multiplies expression probability with eQTL power instead The pilot data used to fit priors comes from a different tissue or platform technology than the target counts (priors are UMI/read-count and tissue specific) Continuous cell annotations (e.g. pseudo time) are present and cannot be discretized into donor/cell type categories required by create.pseudobulk

skills.description: Use when training a DNA 6mA site predictor from labeled 41nt sequence benchmarks (e.g. cross-species, rice, M. musculus) and you must select among RandomForest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees, and SVM classifiers via 5-fold cross-validation.
skills.name: extra-trees-classifier-training
skills.search_text: extra-trees-classifier-training Use when training a DNA 6mA site predictor from labeled 41nt sequence benchmarks (e.g. cross-species, rice, M. musculus) and you must select among RandomForest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees, and SVM classifiers via 5-fold cross-validation. Input is already a trained model file or a feature table — this skill is for encoding raw sequences and training, not for prediction or testing (use csDMA_indepedent_testing.py instead) Only a jackknife or LeaveOneOut evaluation is required — use leaveoneout.py rather than classifier selection + training The target species/task is outside DNA 6mA modification prediction, e.g. other epigenomic modification types not covered by the csDMA feature encoding http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Trains the csDMA predictor by benchmarking five classifiers with 5-fold cross-validation on Motif+Kmer+Binary encoded DNA sequence features, then generating the ExtraTrees model file (csDMA.pkl) and a normalization file for downstream prediction of DNA 6mA sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a trained model file or a feature table — this skill is for encoding raw sequences and training, not for prediction or testing (use csDMA_indepedent_testing.py instead) Only a jackknife or LeaveOneOut evaluation is required — use leaveoneout.py rather than classifier selection + training The target species/task is outside DNA 6mA modification prediction, e.g. other epigenomic modification types not covered by the csDMA feature encoding

skills.name: f-test-feature-selection
skills.search_text: f-test-feature-selection Use when a reference scATAC-seq gene score matrix with known cell type labels must be reduced to informative, cell-type-specific genes before training a supervised celltyping model. Input is already a reduced feature table or pre-selected gene set rather than a full gene score matrix There are no annotated cell type labels for the reference data — the F-test requires groups to test gene-score differences against Celltyping will use bin counts as input instead of gene scores http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Selects cell-type-specific genes as model features by applying an F-test to the reference scATAC-seq gene score matrix (produced by the ArchR pipeline), ranking genes by F-statistic and retaining the top 3000 for Cellcano's supervised celltyping models. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Selects cell-type-specific genes as model features by applying an F-test to the reference scATAC-seq gene score matrix (produced by the ArchR pipeline), ranking genes by F-statistic and retaining the top 3000 for Cellcano's supervised celltyping models.

skills.search_text: f1-score-model-comparison Use when comparing a novelty detection model (e.g. GoFAE-DND) against other anomaly detectors and supervised classifiers using F1 scores across imbalanced class ratios of simulated data. Input is experimental nanopore data rather than simulator output — the benchmark F1 values (0.2812, 0.2344) apply to the simulated G4/STR datasets The goal is non-B structure prediction itself, not method benchmarking — use the GoFAE-DND prediction workflow instead A balanced dataset is available, since the benchmark is specifically designed for heavily imbalanced non-B:B ratios down to 0.05 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark F1 scores of GoFAE-DND novelty detection against SVM, LOF, isolation forest, and supervised classifiers across non-B to B-DNA ratios on simulated ONT translocation-time windows, reproducing the comparison behind Fig. 6 and Supp. Table S6. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is experimental nanopore data rather than simulator output — the benchmark F1 values (0.2812, 0.2344) apply to the simulated G4/STR datasets The goal is non-B structure prediction itself, not method benchmarking — use the GoFAE-DND prediction workflow instead A balanced dataset is available, since the benchmark is specifically designed for heavily imbalanced non-B:B ratios down to 0.05

skills.description: Use when comparing differential chromatin interaction detection performance (precision, power, empirical FDR) between original Hi-C replicate pairs and FreeHi-C-augmented replicates called at the same nominal FDR level.
skills.name: false-discovery-rate-control
skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-control Use when comparing differential chromatin interaction detection performance (precision, power, empirical FDR) between original Hi-C replicate pairs and FreeHi-C-augmented replicates called at the same nominal FDR level. You only have a pre-built contact matrix with no raw FASTQ — FreeHi-C requires real Hi-C sequencing data (FASTQ format) as input for training, so matrix-only input cannot be augmented. Your goal is plain differential interaction calling in real replicates, not benchmarking the precision/power/FDR trade-off against spike-in ground truth. Non-Hi-C differential detection tasks (e.g., RNA-seq) where the spike-in module and binPairs machinery do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Augments biological Hi-C replicates with FreeHi-C simulated data so that differential chromatin interaction detection (diffHic or HiCcompare) gains precision and power while empirical false discovery rate stays at the nominal level; performance is quantified against the FreeHi-C spike-in module's known ground truth differential interactions. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-019-0624-3
skills.summary: Augments biological Hi-C replicates with FreeHi-C simulated data so that differential chromatin interaction detection (diffHic or HiCcompare) gains precision and power while empirical false discovery rate stays at the nominal level; performance is quantified against the FreeHi-C spike-in module's known ground truth differential interactions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have a pre-built contact matrix with no raw FASTQ — FreeHi-C requires real Hi-C sequencing data (FASTQ format) as input for training, so matrix-only input cannot be augmented. Your goal is plain differential interaction calling in real replicates, not benchmarking the precision/power/FDR trade-off against spike-in ground truth. Non-Hi-C differential detection tasks (e.g., RNA-seq) where the spike-in module and binPairs machinery do not apply.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to call significant chromatin contacts from covNorm distance-normalized interaction data, i.e. a p-value and FDR are needed for each pairwise contact after removal of distance-dependent background.
skills.name: false-discovery-rate-correction
skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-correction Use when the goal is to call significant chromatin contacts from covNorm distance-normalized interaction data, i.e. a p-value and FDR are needed for each pairwise contact after removal of distance-dependent background. Inter-chromosomal interactions are not covered — the article filters them out since only cis-interactions are analyzed Contacts below coverage cut-offs (default 200 at 40 kb resolution; 200 promoter side / 50 other side for pcHi-C PO-interactions) — low-coverage fragments should be filtered before significance calling Raw (non-normalized) contact maps — the Weibull background must be fit on distance-normalized values, not raw interaction frequencies http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns per-contact statistical significance in the covNorm pipeline by fitting a 3P-Weibull background to distance-normalized Hi-C/pcHi-C contact frequencies and converting fitted p-values (p_result_dist) into Benjamini-Hochberg FDR values (FDR_dist_res) for significant long-range chromatin interaction calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Assigns per-contact statistical significance in the covNorm pipeline by fitting a 3P-Weibull background to distance-normalized Hi-C/pcHi-C contact frequencies and converting fitted p-values (p_result_dist) into Benjamini-Hochberg FDR values (FDR_dist_res) for significant long-range chromatin interaction calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Inter-chromosomal interactions are not covered — the article filters them out since only cis-interactions are analyzed Contacts below coverage cut-offs (default 200 at 40 kb resolution; 200 promoter side / 50 other side for pcHi-C PO-interactions) — low-coverage fragments should be filtered before significance calling Raw (non-normalized) contact maps — the Weibull background must be fit on distance-normalized values, not raw interaction frequencies

skills.description: Use when a driver-discovery candidate list (e.g. DriverPower .result.tsv calls) needs an empirical FDR: intersect calls against known catalogs (CGC, PCAWG-consensus), isolate method-exclusive candidates, and compute the unsupported fraction per category.
skills.name: false-discovery-rate-estimation
skills.search_text: false-discovery-rate-estimation Use when a driver-discovery candidate list (e.g. DriverPower .result.tsv calls) needs an empirical FDR: intersect calls against known catalogs (CGC, PCAWG-consensus), isolate method-exclusive candidates, and compute the unsupported fraction per category. Input is a raw mutation VCF or feature table rather than a called driver candidate list — call drivers first with driverpower model/infer A calibrated, model-based FDR (e.g. from null/permutation q-values) is required rather than an evidence-based empirical estimate on exclusive calls Comparing methods where every candidate is already in CGC or the PCAWG-consensus set — no exclusive calls exist to estimate the rate http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Estimates an empirical false discovery rate for DriverPower driver calls on the PCAWG data set by cataloguing candidates exclusive to DriverPower (absent from CGC and PCAWG-consensus) and treating unsupported exclusives as false positives: 3.2% (7/217) coding and 16.8% (16/95) non-coding. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Estimates an empirical false discovery rate for DriverPower driver calls on the PCAWG data set by cataloguing candidates exclusive to DriverPower (absent from CGC and PCAWG-consensus) and treating unsupported exclusives as false positives: 3.2% (7/217) coding and 16.8% (16/95) non-coding.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw mutation VCF or feature table rather than a called driver candidate list — call drivers first with driverpower model/infer A calibrated, model-based FDR (e.g. from null/permutation q-values) is required rather than an evidence-based empirical estimate on exclusive calls Comparing methods where every candidate is already in CGC or the PCAWG-consensus set — no exclusive calls exist to estimate the rate

skills.description: Use when you have genome-wide in vitro TF binding predictions and a set of experimental in vivo peaks, and need to quantify TP rate, filter corroborated false positives, and test whether remaining FPs sit in nucleosome-occupied regions.
skills.name: false-positive-annotation-against-chromatin-structure
skills.search_text: false-positive-annotation-against-chromatin-structure Use when you have genome-wide in vitro TF binding predictions and a set of experimental in vivo peaks, and need to quantify TP rate, filter corroborated false positives, and test whether remaining FPs sit in nucleosome-occupied regions. You lack experimental in vivo peak data (ChIP-exo/PB-exo) to define true positives, so TP/FP rates cannot be computed. Your target organism has no nucleosome positioning maps available — chromatin-structure explanation of false positives cannot be performed. The transcription factor has no gcPBM training data compatible with gcpbm_regressor.py's required file format. A validation workflow that judges an in vitro-trained transcription factor binding site predictor (DNAffinity gcpbm_regressor) against in vivo peaks (ChIP-exo GSE44604, PB-exo GSE147927) in S. cerevisiae, computing true-positive rate and then explaining residual false positives via G1-phase nucleosome occupancy maps. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: A validation workflow that judges an in vitro-trained transcription factor binding site predictor (DNAffinity gcpbm_regressor) against in vivo peaks (ChIP-exo GSE44604, PB-exo GSE147927) in S. cerevisiae, computing true-positive rate and then explaining residual false positives via G1-phase nucleosome occupancy maps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You lack experimental in vivo peak data (ChIP-exo/PB-exo) to define true positives, so TP/FP rates cannot be computed. Your target organism has no nucleosome positioning maps available — chromatin-structure explanation of false positives cannot be performed. The transcription factor has no gcPBM training data compatible with gcpbm_regressor.py's required file format.

skills.description: Use when simulating or reanalyzing two genomic range sets x and y with no true association, to check whether a null-generation method (block bootstrap vs shuffling) controls FPR near alpha.
skills.name: false-positive-rate-estimation-at-alpha
skills.search_text: false-positive-rate-estimation-at-alpha Use when simulating or reanalyzing two genomic range sets x and y with no true association, to check whether a null-generation method (block bootstrap vs shuffling) controls FPR near alpha. x and y have a true biological association — the simulation and FPR validation assume no true association The goal is point estimation of an overlap rate rather than calibration/type-I-error assessment of a null-generation scheme The input is not interval-valued genomic ranges (e.g. already-summarized p-values without range coordinates) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Estimates the empirical false positive rate of a genomic range overlap test at a nominal significance threshold alpha, comparing block-bootstrapped nulls (bootRanges) against conventional shuffling. It exposes how overly narrow shuffling-based null distributions inflate significance. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Estimates the empirical false positive rate of a genomic range overlap test at a nominal significance threshold alpha, comparing block-bootstrapped nulls (bootRanges) against conventional shuffling. It exposes how overly narrow shuffling-based null distributions inflate significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: x and y have a true biological association — the simulation and FPR validation assume no true association The goal is point estimation of an overlap rate rather than calibration/type-I-error assessment of a null-generation scheme The input is not interval-valued genomic ranges (e.g. already-summarized p-values without range coordinates)

skills.description: Use when starting from Oxford Nanopore raw FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and you need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences (FASTQ) rather than working from pre-base-called reads.
skills.name: fast5-electrolytic-current-decoding
skills.search_text: fast5-electrolytic-current-decoding Use when starting from Oxford Nanopore raw FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and you need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences (FASTQ) rather than working from pre-base-called reads. Input is already base-called FASTQ/BAM sequence data — decoding FAST5 signal would be redundant The task requires base-calling very large genomes — Chiron runs at ~2000 bp/s and is not suitable for large genomes The workflow requires modified-base calling with ONT-supported mods — the Bonito README directs users to dorado instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Base-calling of Oxford Nanopore reads: translating raw electrolytic ion-current signal stored in FAST5 files into nucleotide sequences, using end-to-end deep-learning models such as Chiron's CTC-trained network that bypass error-prone signal segmentation. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100153
skills.summary: Base-calling of Oxford Nanopore reads: translating raw electrolytic ion-current signal stored in FAST5 files into nucleotide sequences, using end-to-end deep-learning models such as Chiron's CTC-trained network that bypass error-prone signal segmentation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already base-called FASTQ/BAM sequence data — decoding FAST5 signal would be redundant The task requires base-calling very large genomes — Chiron runs at ~2000 bp/s and is not suitable for large genomes The workflow requires modified-base calling with ONT-supported mods — the Bonito README directs users to dorado instead

skills.description: Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP reads (.ab1 trace files) must be mapped onto a .fasta reference template so each read cytosine receives a genomic coordinate and per-CpG methylation levels can be tallied.
skills.name: fasta-reference-coordinate-computation
skills.search_text: fasta-reference-coordinate-computation Use when direct-BSP or cloning-BSP reads (.ab1 trace files) must be mapped onto a .fasta reference template so each read cytosine receives a genomic coordinate and per-CpG methylation levels can be tallied. skills.search_text: fisher-combined-pvalue-across-bandwidths Use when temporal genomic/epigenomic series (e.g., PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq features across donor ages 22–93) must be scanned for abrupt age-related change points rather than gradual trends, and per-age significance must be robust to window-size choice. skills.name: fisher-exact-contingency-testing
skills.search_text: fisher-exact-contingency-testing Use when you need to test enrichment of one genomic gene/region set (e.g. histoneHMM differential modification calls) against another (e.g. DESeq-derived DE genes) with a 2x2 contingency table and exact test P-value. Input is already a set of peak-like (narrow) ChIP-seq differential calls, since methods designed for peak-like features generate false positive or negative calls on broad marks like H3K27me3/H3K9me3 The comparison involves ChIP-seq profiles from more than two samples, since histoneHMM's differential calling (and hence the contingency table) is defined for a two-sample contrast Expected overlap counts are so extreme that a chi-square test is appropriate and exact computation is unnecessary http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Quantify whether differentially modified regions from histoneHMM overlap differentially expressed genes more than expected by chance, using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact test in R (stats::fisher.test).
