skills.description: Use when estimating transcript expression from RNA-Seq alignments (SAM/BAM) whose library preparation (NSR priming, WT SOLiD, strand-specific protocols, single- or paired-end) induces non-uniform fragment distribution and quantification bias.
skills.name: fragment-bias-correction
skills.search_text: fragment-bias-correction Use when estimating transcript expression from RNA-Seq alignments (SAM/BAM) whose library preparation (NSR priming, WT SOLiD, strand-specific protocols, single- or paired-end) induces non-uniform fragment distribution and quantification bias. Input is not fragment-level alignment data but already-computed expression estimates or a feature count table — bias correction operates on fragment alignments and reference sequences No reference transcriptome/genome FASTA or annotation is available — Cufflinks --bias-correction and Cuffdiff -b require the reference sequence, and eXpress-D estimation requires a transcript annotation The question is differential expression baseline calling where deliberately uncorrected (RH control) estimates are wanted for comparison — run the uncorrected mode instead of enabling correction http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Likelihood-based simultaneous estimation of RNA-Seq fragment bias parameters and transcript expression levels, as implemented in eXpress-D and Cufflinks/Cuffdiff, to correct sequence and positional bias from non-uniform cDNA fragmentation and priming. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Likelihood-based simultaneous estimation of RNA-Seq fragment bias parameters and transcript expression levels, as implemented in eXpress-D and Cufflinks/Cuffdiff, to correct sequence and positional bias from non-uniform cDNA fragmentation and priming.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not fragment-level alignment data but already-computed expression estimates or a feature count table — bias correction operates on fragment alignments and reference sequences No reference transcriptome/genome FASTA or annotation is available — Cufflinks --bias-correction and Cuffdiff -b require the reference sequence, and eXpress-D estimation requires a transcript annotation The question is differential expression baseline calling where deliberately uncorrected (RH control) estimates are wanted for comparison — run the uncorrected mode instead of enabling correction

skills.description: Use when reconstructing coverage profiles from directionally extended short ChIP-Seq reads and fragment sizes are only known within a size-selection range (e.g. 175-225 bp), so HDF ends are uncertain.
skills.name: fragment-end-linear-down-weighting
skills.search_text: fragment-end-linear-down-weighting Use when reconstructing coverage profiles from directionally extended short ChIP-Seq reads and fragment sizes are only known within a size-selection range (e.g. 175-225 bp), so HDF ends are uncertain. Paired-end data where the true fragment ends are directly observed — HPeak treats both ends together as ONE fragment, so end inference/weighting is unnecessary Analyses requiring strand-aware peak-summit refinement — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak Genome binnings at resolutions other than the fixed bin scheme expected by the HMM (25 bp in this study) without re-validating the weighted profile http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 HPeak's scheme for reconstructing genome-wide ChIP-Seq coverage profiles by extending each short read into a hypothetical DNA fragment (HDF) and linearly down-weighting coverage in the bins covered by the HDF's uncertain end portion, so fragment-length uncertainty does not inflate signal at fragment ends. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: HPeak's scheme for reconstructing genome-wide ChIP-Seq coverage profiles by extending each short read into a hypothetical DNA fragment (HDF) and linearly down-weighting coverage in the bins covered by the HDF's uncertain end portion, so fragment-length uncertainty does not inflate signal at fragment ends.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Paired-end data where the true fragment ends are directly observed — HPeak treats both ends together as ONE fragment, so end inference/weighting is unnecessary Analyses requiring strand-aware peak-summit refinement — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak Genome binnings at resolutions other than the fixed bin scheme expected by the HMM (25 bp in this study) without re-validating the weighted profile

skills.description: Use when sorted BAMs aligned with BWA-MEM (short reads) or minimap2 (long reads) and a bgzipped, indexed variant VCF are ready, and platform-specific fragment files must be produced as input to haplotype phasing tools.
skills.name: fragment-extraction-from-aligned-reads
skills.search_text: fragment-extraction-from-aligned-reads Use when sorted BAMs aligned with BWA-MEM (short reads) or minimap2 (long reads) and a bgzipped, indexed variant VCF are ready, and platform-specific fragment files must be produced as input to haplotype phasing tools. Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned reads — fragments can only be extracted after alignment to a reference and VCF indexing. Goal is phasing from population data or pedigree/trio statistical phasing — ExtractHAIRS produces read-backed fragment files for single individual haplotyping (SIH), not population-level phasing. Variants include structural rearrangements — the linkage graph in this pipeline supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extract variant-supporting fragment files from sorted, indexed BAM alignments and a bgzipped, indexed VCF using the modified ExtractHAIRS utility shipped with SpecHap, applying platform-specific flags for paired-end NGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and ONT data before phasing with SpecHap/HapCUT2. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Extract variant-supporting fragment files from sorted, indexed BAM alignments and a bgzipped, indexed VCF using the modified ExtractHAIRS utility shipped with SpecHap, applying platform-specific flags for paired-end NGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and ONT data before phasing with SpecHap/HapCUT2.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned reads — fragments can only be extracted after alignment to a reference and VCF indexing. Goal is phasing from population data or pedigree/trio statistical phasing — ExtractHAIRS produces read-backed fragment files for single individual haplotyping (SIH), not population-level phasing. Variants include structural rearrangements — the linkage graph in this pipeline supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions.

skills.description: Use when you have a fragment file (from 10X/Hi-C linked reads, paired-end NGS, PacBio SMRT or ONT data) plus a VCF of heterozygous variants and need to build SpecHap's linkage graph for spectral-based haplotype assembly.
skills.name: fragment-file-parsing
skills.search_text: fragment-file-parsing Use when you have a fragment file (from 10X/Hi-C linked reads, paired-end NGS, PacBio SMRT or ONT data) plus a VCF of heterozygous variants and need to build SpecHap's linkage graph for spectral-based haplotype assembly. Ploidy is higher than diploid — the article states the current graph bisection model might not fit when ploidy increases The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — the current linkage graph supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions, not genome rearrangements You already have a phased haplotype or VCF with phase blocks and do not need fragment-level linkage reconstruction http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parses the position-sorted fragment file produced by ExtractHair (modified from HapCUT2) and converts fragment-observed heterozygous variant loci into a weighted undirected linkage graph whose edge weights are truncated log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) computed from fragment Phred probabilities, as used by SpecHap for spectral phasing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Parses the position-sorted fragment file produced by ExtractHair (modified from HapCUT2) and converts fragment-observed heterozygous variant loci into a weighted undirected linkage graph whose edge weights are truncated log-likelihood ratios (LLRs) computed from fragment Phred probabilities, as used by SpecHap for spectral phasing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Ploidy is higher than diploid — the article states the current graph bisection model might not fit when ploidy increases The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — the current linkage graph supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions, not genome rearrangements You already have a phased haplotype or VCF with phase blocks and do not need fragment-level linkage reconstruction

skills.description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment alignments (BAM) must be classified by insert size and converted into single-nucleotide-resolution midpoint count tracks (bedGraph) to feed RoboCOP's HMM.
skills.name: fragment-midpoint-signal-aggregation
skills.search_text: fragment-midpoint-signal-aggregation Use when paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment alignments (BAM) must be classified by insert size and converted into single-nucleotide-resolution midpoint count tracks (bedGraph) to feed RoboCOP's HMM. Input is single-end sequencing data without paired-end fragment start/end coordinates, since midpoints cannot be computed The chromatin accessibility data are already reduced to occupancy or peak calls rather than raw paired-end fragments The downstream model does not consume per-base midpoint count observables (e.g. peak-calling workflows such as MACS2 followed by FIMO labeling) http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Reduces paired-end chromatin accessibility fragments (MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) into two 1-D genomic count signals by classifying fragments by insert size (nucFrags vs. shortFrags) and aggregating per-base fragment midpoint counts, which serve as the multivariate observables consumed by RoboCOP's HMM. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Reduces paired-end chromatin accessibility fragments (MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) into two 1-D genomic count signals by classifying fragments by insert size (nucFrags vs. shortFrags) and aggregating per-base fragment midpoint counts, which serve as the multivariate observables consumed by RoboCOP's HMM.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-end sequencing data without paired-end fragment start/end coordinates, since midpoints cannot be computed The chromatin accessibility data are already reduced to occupancy or peak calls rather than raw paired-end fragments The downstream model does not consume per-base midpoint count observables (e.g. peak-calling workflows such as MACS2 followed by FIMO labeling)

skills.description: Use when mapped BAM alignments from a NEAT ChIPseq or RNAseq pipeline need fragment-size bounds and duplicate-read handling applied before peakcalling, per parameters set in AdvancedSettings.txt.
skills.name: fragment-size-filtering-chipseq
skills.search_text: fragment-size-filtering-chipseq Use when mapped BAM alignments from a NEAT ChIPseq or RNAseq pipeline need fragment-size bounds and duplicate-read handling applied before peakcalling, per parameters set in AdvancedSettings.txt. Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been mapped — NEAT's 'map' module (bwa/bowtie) must run before filtering The goal is configuring how peaks are called rather than filtering reads — that is the separate 'peakcalling' module Reads still need renaming, unzipping, or QC — use NEAT's 'unzip', 'rename', or 'QC' modules first http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Filters aligned ChIPseq/RNAseq BAM files in NEAT's 'filter' module by applying user-specified duplicate-read management and minimum/maximum fragment size thresholds, implemented with samtools view/rmdup/sort/index. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Filters aligned ChIPseq/RNAseq BAM files in NEAT's 'filter' module by applying user-specified duplicate-read management and minimum/maximum fragment size thresholds, implemented with samtools view/rmdup/sort/index.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ that has not yet been mapped — NEAT's 'map' module (bwa/bowtie) must run before filtering The goal is configuring how peaks are called rather than filtering reads — that is the separate 'peakcalling' module Reads still need renaming, unzipping, or QC — use NEAT's 'unzip', 'rename', or 'QC' modules first

skills.description: Use when processing paired-end cfMeDIP-seq BAMs within MEDIPIPE's alignment/QC module and you need insert-size distributions and fragmentation-ratio QC tables from duplicate-removed alignments.
skills.name: fragment-size-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: fragment-size-ratio-computation Use when processing paired-end cfMeDIP-seq BAMs within MEDIPIPE's alignment/QC module and you need insert-size distributions and fragmentation-ratio QC tables from duplicate-removed alignments. Input library is single-end — insert-size estimation and short-to-long ratio computation are performed for paired-end data only Alignment and duplicate removal have not yet been performed (no filtered, duplicate-removed sorted BAM exists) Task is methylation quantification or sample aggregation rather than alignment/QC metrics generation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A cfMeDIP-seq QC skill from MEDIPIPE that estimates fragment sizes with Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics and computes short-to-long fragmentation size ratios in consecutive 1 Mb and 5 Mb windows (Cristiano et al. 2019) as cell-free DNA fragmentation-quality metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: A cfMeDIP-seq QC skill from MEDIPIPE that estimates fragment sizes with Picard CollectInsertSizeMetrics and computes short-to-long fragmentation size ratios in consecutive 1 Mb and 5 Mb windows (Cristiano et al. 2019) as cell-free DNA fragmentation-quality metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input library is single-end — insert-size estimation and short-to-long ratio computation are performed for paired-end data only Alignment and duplicate removal have not yet been performed (no filtered, duplicate-removed sorted BAM exists) Task is methylation quantification or sample aggregation rather than alignment/QC metrics generation

skills.description: Use when calling broad ChIP-seq domains (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3) with RECOGNICER from BED-format mapped reads and you must set or sensitivity-test the fragment-size shift and window-size parameters.
skills.name: fragment-size-read-shifting
skills.search_text: fragment-size-read-shifting Use when calling broad ChIP-seq domains (e.g. H3K27me3/H3K9me3) with RECOGNICER from BED-format mapped reads and you must set or sensitivity-test the fragment-size shift and window-size parameters. The goal is calling punctate/narrow ChIP-seq peaks rather than broad kb-to-Mb enrichment domains (RECOGNICER is designed for broad-domain identification) Input reads are already strand-shifted or paired-end fragments with inferred centers, so an additional half-fragment 5' shift would double-shift reads You need to vary parameters beyond FRAGMENT_SIZE/WINDOW_SIZE such as the block transformation factor or termination criteria — the README strongly recommends not changing other parameters http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Shift each mapped single-end ChIP-seq read from its 5' end by half the DNA fragment size (RECOGNICER default FRAGMENT_SIZE=150 bp, mononucleosome) within equal-sized non-overlapping windows (default WINDOW_SIZE=200 bp) before broad-domain calling, and verify that resulting domain calls are robust to these two parameters. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Shift each mapped single-end ChIP-seq read from its 5' end by half the DNA fragment size (RECOGNICER default FRAGMENT_SIZE=150 bp, mononucleosome) within equal-sized non-overlapping windows (default WINDOW_SIZE=200 bp) before broad-domain calling, and verify that resulting domain calls are robust to these two parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calling punctate/narrow ChIP-seq peaks rather than broad kb-to-Mb enrichment domains (RECOGNICER is designed for broad-domain identification) Input reads are already strand-shifted or paired-end fragments with inferred centers, so an additional half-fragment 5' shift would double-shift reads You need to vary parameters beyond FRAGMENT_SIZE/WINDOW_SIZE such as the block transformation factor or termination criteria — the README strongly recommends not changing other parameters

skills.description: Use when you have per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metrics (FRiP, peak number, fragment size, PBC) and need to test whether metric associations hold within literature-based assay categories rather than globally.
skills.name: frip-peak-count-association-analysis
skills.search_text: frip-peak-count-association-analysis Use when you have per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metrics (FRiP, peak number, fragment size, PBC) and need to test whether metric associations hold within literature-based assay categories rather than globally. Input is raw FASTQ/BAM without run ChiLin QC outputs (no id_frip./id_frag. JSON statistics) — run the ChiLin pipeline first to produce FRiP and fragment-size metrics The goal is QC of a single sample rather than cross-sample metric association analysis across an atlas of many samples Samples cannot be assigned to one of the literature-based assay categories, since the correlations are category-specific and pooling them would mask the histone-modification discrepancy http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the ChiLin quality-atlas finding that FRiP scores correlate with peak number for chromatin accessibility, transcription factor and chromatin regulator samples but not histone modification samples (correlation ~0.37), and that DNase-seq FRiP anti-correlates with estimated fragment size. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Reproduces the ChiLin quality-atlas finding that FRiP scores correlate with peak number for chromatin accessibility, transcription factor and chromatin regulator samples but not histone modification samples (correlation ~0.37), and that DNase-seq FRiP anti-correlates with estimated fragment size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/BAM without run ChiLin QC outputs (no id_frip./id_frag. JSON statistics) — run the ChiLin pipeline first to produce FRiP and fragment-size metrics The goal is QC of a single sample rather than cross-sample metric association analysis across an atlas of many samples Samples cannot be assigned to one of the literature-based assay categories, since the correlations are category-specific and pooling them would mask the histone-modification discrepancy

skills.description: Use when QC of ChIP-seq replicates requires FRiP scores: MACS2 narrow/broad peaks are available and read enrichment in peaks must be quantified on equally subsampled BAMs.
skills.name: frip-score-calculation-on-subsampled-bams
skills.search_text: frip-score-calculation-on-subsampled-bams Use when QC of ChIP-seq replicates requires FRiP scores: MACS2 narrow/broad peaks are available and read enrichment in peaks must be quantified on equally subsampled BAMs. Input data is DNase-seq processed through the DNase-seq QC branch rather than ChIP-seq peak-based QC, where this peak-overlap FRiP step is not the defining metric Peaks have not yet been called — FRiP requires MACS2 narrowPeak/broadPeak files, so running it on unmapped or unfiltered BAMs alone is wrong BAMs are full-depth and not subsampled to 4,000,000 reads, making FRiP values incomparable across replicates with different library depths http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Compute the Fraction of Reads in Peaks (FRiP) QC metric for each ChIP-seq treatment and control replicate by intersecting MACS2 peak calls with 4,000,000-read subsampled BAMs, as implemented in the ChiLin pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Compute the Fraction of Reads in Peaks (FRiP) QC metric for each ChIP-seq treatment and control replicate by intersecting MACS2 peak calls with 4,000,000-read subsampled BAMs, as implemented in the ChiLin pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is DNase-seq processed through the DNase-seq QC branch rather than ChIP-seq peak-based QC, where this peak-overlap FRiP step is not the defining metric Peaks have not yet been called — FRiP requires MACS2 narrowPeak/broadPeak files, so running it on unmapped or unfiltered BAMs alone is wrong BAMs are full-depth and not subsampled to 4,000,000 reads, making FRiP values incomparable across replicates with different library depths

skills.description: Use when you need a quality/robustness metric for broad-domain ChIP-seq calls — e.g. verifying that total aggregate domain length and FRIP remain invariant under sequencing-depth downsampling (17.23M → 4M reads) of H3K27me3 data.
skills.name: frip-score-computation
skills.search_text: frip-score-computation Use when you need a quality/robustness metric for broad-domain ChIP-seq calls — e.g. verifying that total aggregate domain length and FRIP remain invariant under sequencing-depth downsampling (17.23M → 4M reads) of H3K27me3 data. No called peak/domain set exists yet — FRIP is computed relative to RECOGNICER's fdr0.01 broadPeak output, so the domain-calling pipeline must run first The ChIP target is narrow/punctate enrichment rather than broad kb-to-Mb domains like H3K27me3/H3K9me3, where this skill's invariance rationale is grounded http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the FRIP (fraction of reads in peaks) score for RECOGNICER broad-domain ChIP-seq calls, using the fraction of ChIP reads falling inside significant H3K27me3 domains relative to total mapped reads. In the RECOGNICER paper it serves as a robustness metric: FRIP stays at the same level when the CD4+ T cell H3K27me3 dataset is downsampled from 17.23M to 4M reads. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Computes the FRIP (fraction of reads in peaks) score for RECOGNICER broad-domain ChIP-seq calls, using the fraction of ChIP reads falling inside significant H3K27me3 domains relative to total mapped reads. In the RECOGNICER paper it serves as a robustness metric: FRIP stays at the same level when the CD4+ T cell H3K27me3 dataset is downsampled from 17.23M to 4M reads.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No called peak/domain set exists yet — FRIP is computed relative to RECOGNICER's fdr0.01 broadPeak output, so the domain-calling pipeline must run first The ChIP target is narrow/punctate enrichment rather than broad kb-to-Mb domains like H3K27me3/H3K9me3, where this skill's invariance rationale is grounded

skills.description: Use when a ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs a per-sample enrichment QC score, or when deciding whether a 1% FRiP threshold is an appropriate pass/fail criterion for ChIP versus input control samples.
skills.name: frip-score-thresholding
skills.search_text: frip-score-thresholding Use when a ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs a per-sample enrichment QC score, or when deciding whether a 1% FRiP threshold is an appropriate pass/fail criterion for ChIP versus input control samples. The sample has no called peaks yet — FRiP requires peaks from the merged peak calling step and cannot be computed on raw reads alone The goal is fragment-size or PCR-duplicate QC — ChiLin handles those separately via macs2 fragment size estimation (step 3) and PBC evaluation (step 4), not via FRiP Peaks number fewer than 200 for downstream steps such as MDSeqPos motif analysis — ChiLin skips those steps automatically; FRiP is not a substitute for them http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assesses ChIP-seq/DNase-seq sample enrichment quality by computing the fraction of reads in peaks (FRiP) and evaluating it against a 1% FRiP cutoff, which the ChiLin quality atlas validated as a proper ChIP enrichment reference. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Assesses ChIP-seq/DNase-seq sample enrichment quality by computing the fraction of reads in peaks (FRiP) and evaluating it against a 1% FRiP cutoff, which the ChiLin quality atlas validated as a proper ChIP enrichment reference.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sample has no called peaks yet — FRiP requires peaks from the merged peak calling step and cannot be computed on raw reads alone The goal is fragment-size or PCR-duplicate QC — ChiLin handles those separately via macs2 fragment size estimation (step 3) and PBC evaluation (step 4), not via FRiP Peaks number fewer than 200 for downstream steps such as MDSeqPos motif analysis — ChiLin skips those steps automatically; FRiP is not a substitute for them

skills.description: Use when you have a deduplicated list of gene IDs linked to a transcription factor's binding regions (e.g. from EpiRegio Region Query of ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and want to identify enriched GO terms or KEGG pathways explaining the TF's function.
skills.name: functional-enrichment-analysis-go-terms
skills.search_text: functional-enrichment-analysis-go-terms Use when you have a deduplicated list of gene IDs linked to a transcription factor's binding regions (e.g. from EpiRegio Region Query of ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) and want to identify enriched GO terms or KEGG pathways explaining the TF's function. The input is already an enrichment result or pathway-term table rather than a raw gene ID list. The goal is to identify enriched TF binding motifs in DNA sequences rather than enriched functions of a gene list — use a motif enrichment tool such as PASTAA instead. The gene list contains duplicate IDs and cannot be deduplicated first, since duplicates are only considered once by g:Profiler and would misrepresent the input set. http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3656 Run GO term and KEGG pathway enrichment on a gene list derived from ChIP-seq-bound regulatory elements (e.g. ARID3A target genes from ENCODE peaks ENCFF002CVL) using g:Profiler with default parameters and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 0.05, to infer biological function of the TF's regulatory network. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Run GO term and KEGG pathway enrichment on a gene list derived from ChIP-seq-bound regulatory elements (e.g. ARID3A target genes from ENCODE peaks ENCFF002CVL) using g:Profiler with default parameters and Benjamini–Hochberg FDR 0.05, to infer biological function of the TF's regulatory network.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already an enrichment result or pathway-term table rather than a raw gene ID list. The goal is to identify enriched TF binding motifs in DNA sequences rather than enriched functions of a gene list — use a motif enrichment tool such as PASTAA instead. The gene list contains duplicate IDs and cannot be deduplicated first, since duplicates are only considered once by g:Profiler and would misrepresent the input set.

skills.description: Use when you already have DriverPower burden-test-only calls and per-element functional impact scores (e.g. averaged per-mutation CADD PHRED per binID) and want to re-rank/infer drivers with functional adjustment to boost precision.
skills.name: functional-impact-score-adjustment-of-driver-calls
skills.search_text: functional-impact-score-adjustment-of-driver-calls Use when you already have DriverPower burden-test-only calls and per-element functional impact scores (e.g. averaged per-mutation CADD PHRED per binID) and want to re-rank/infer drivers with functional adjustment to boost precision. No functional impact scores are available for the tested elements — running without --funcScore is the burden-only baseline, not this skill. Functional score schemes are biased toward coding mutations, so applying this to poorly scored non-coding elements may not improve calls (article notes the bias in discussion). You only need the background mutation rate model — use 'driverpower model' instead of the functional-adjusted infer step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Posterior functional adjustment of DriverPower driver calls: re-run 'driverpower infer' with per-element functional impact scores (CADD, DANN, EIGEN, LINSIGHT) via --funcScore/--funcScoreCut to refine the burden-test-only candidate set. Incorporating functional evidence increases driver-discovery precision, e.g. in Panc-AdenoCA it gained ACVR1B, RBM10 and ZFP36L2 and removed the likely false positive FAU. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Posterior functional adjustment of DriverPower driver calls: re-run 'driverpower infer' with per-element functional impact scores (CADD, DANN, EIGEN, LINSIGHT) via --funcScore/--funcScoreCut to refine the burden-test-only candidate set. Incorporating functional evidence increases driver-discovery precision, e.g. in Panc-AdenoCA it gained ACVR1B, RBM10 and ZFP36L2 and removed the likely false positive FAU.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No functional impact scores are available for the tested elements — running without --funcScore is the burden-only baseline, not this skill. Functional score schemes are biased toward coding mutations, so applying this to poorly scored non-coding elements may not improve calls (article notes the bias in discussion). You only need the background mutation rate model — use 'driverpower model' instead of the functional-adjusted infer step.

skills.description: Use when non-coding SNVs must be converted from VCF/BED coordinates into a per-variant functional feature matrix to train or apply a brain-disorder variant prioritization score like ncDeepBrain.
skills.name: functional-variant-annotation-annovar
skills.search_text: functional-variant-annotation-annovar Use when non-coding SNVs must be converted from VCF/BED coordinates into a per-variant functional feature matrix to train or apply a brain-disorder variant prioritization score like ncDeepBrain. The task is step-2 gene prioritization, which instead integrates ncDeepBrain score with RVIS, GTEx, haploinsufficiency, Phenolyzer, CNV and de novo mutation gene-level scores Input is already an assembled feature table for model training, so re-annotation with ANNOVAR is redundant Variants are coding; this skill targets whole-genome non-coding variants for brain-function impact scoring http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotate non-coding variants with ANNOVAR and assemble the iMEGES 11-feature matrix (EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM, GNOMAD frequency, brain eQTLs, and PsychENCODE/Roadmap enhancer-promoter indicators) that feeds the ncDeepBrain deep learning variant score. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7

skills.description: Use when you have genomic region sets (e.g. HOT vs COLD intervals) in FASTA or BED+reference form and need sequence-composition features (GC content, GC skew, CpG O/E, k-mer frequencies) for classification.
skills.name: gc-content-and-skew-calculation
skills.search_text: gc-content-and-skew-calculation Use when you have genomic region sets (e.g. HOT vs COLD intervals) in FASTA or BED+reference form and need sequence-composition features (GC content, GC skew, CpG O/E, k-mer frequencies) for classification. Input is already a numeric feature table or a precomputed feature matrix — this skill computes sequence-composition features from raw genomic regions, which would be redundant. The goal is functional or motif-level characterization of HOT regions (e.g. canonical TF motif enrichment, R-loop or G-quadruplex annotation) rather than sequence-composition discrimination features. Regions lack an available reference genome or extracted sequences, so GC/k-mer/CpG O/E statistics cannot be computed. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Computes per-region GC content, GC skew, CpG observed/expected ratio, and k-mer frequency vectors (k = 2, 3, 4) over HOT and COLD genomic regions, producing the feature matrix used to discriminate HOT regions and identify GC/CpG-rich k-mers as top predictive features. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Computes per-region GC content, GC skew, CpG observed/expected ratio, and k-mer frequency vectors (k = 2, 3, 4) over HOT and COLD genomic regions, producing the feature matrix used to discriminate HOT regions and identify GC/CpG-rich k-mers as top predictive features.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numeric feature table or a precomputed feature matrix — this skill computes sequence-composition features from raw genomic regions, which would be redundant. The goal is functional or motif-level characterization of HOT regions (e.g. canonical TF motif enrichment, R-loop or G-quadruplex annotation) rather than sequence-composition discrimination features. Regions lack an available reference genome or extracted sequences, so GC/k-mer/CpG O/E statistics cannot be computed.

skills.description: Use when comparing bias correction across organisms or protocols to decide whether GC normalization suffices as a bias proxy, or when diagnosing whether observed expression shifts in RNA-Seq track transcript GC content.
skills.name: gc-content-bias-correlation
skills.search_text: gc-content-bias-correlation Use when comparing bias correction across organisms or protocols to decide whether GC normalization suffices as a bias proxy, or when diagnosing whether observed expression shifts in RNA-Seq track transcript GC content. The analysis goal is improving expression accuracy via qRT-PCR benchmarking rather than characterizing whether GC content tracks sequence-specific bias — use the qRT-PCR correlation skill instead Only a single organism/protocol is available and no cross-organism contrast (e.g. human vs. yeast) is intended, so the proxy-vs-direct comparison cannot be framed The data are not RNA-Seq fragment alignments (e.g. NanoString counts or microarray intensities), for which effective-length bias is undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Quantifies whether GC-content-derived bias acts as a proxy for sequence-specific fragment bias in RNA-Seq by computing the correlation between the log fold change in effective length (bias-corrected vs. uncorrected eXpress/eXpress-D estimates) and transcript GC content, per dataset. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Quantifies whether GC-content-derived bias acts as a proxy for sequence-specific fragment bias in RNA-Seq by computing the correlation between the log fold change in effective length (bias-corrected vs. uncorrected eXpress/eXpress-D estimates) and transcript GC content, per dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is improving expression accuracy via qRT-PCR benchmarking rather than characterizing whether GC content tracks sequence-specific bias — use the qRT-PCR correlation skill instead Only a single organism/protocol is available and no cross-organism contrast (e.g. human vs. yeast) is intended, so the proxy-vs-direct comparison cannot be framed The data are not RNA-Seq fragment alignments (e.g. NanoString counts or microarray intensities), for which effective-length bias is undefined

skills.name: gc-decile-stratified-parameter-estimation
skills.search_text: gc-decile-stratified-parameter-estimation Use when calling RNA-binding sites from CLIP/eCLIP data by testing tiled transcriptomic windows for IP-over-input enrichment and you need GC-bias-aware, overdispersion-calibrated nulls rather than peak calling. The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample — Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing without these controls The goal is de novo peak discovery on unannotated regions rather than testing windows over annotated transcripts/repetitive elements The annotation GFF has not been cleaned to one best transcript per gene — window selection and interpretability degrade http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits GC-decile-stratified beta-binomial models to CLIP/IP vs. input read-start counts in tiled transcriptomic windows, estimating overdispersion (rho) separately per GC content bin so that enrichment p-values account for GC bias and count overdispersion in eCLIP data. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Fits GC-decile-stratified beta-binomial models to CLIP/IP vs. input read-start counts in tiled transcriptomic windows, estimating overdispersion (rho) separately per GC content bin so that enrichment p-values account for GC bias and count overdispersion in eCLIP data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample — Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing without these controls The goal is de novo peak discovery on unannotated regions rather than testing windows over annotated transcripts/repetitive elements The annotation GFF has not been cleaned to one best transcript per gene — window selection and interpretability degrade

skills.description: Use when TFBS motif instances from CNN motif detectors must be retained by statistical significance rather than a subjective signal cutoff — i.e., when per-motif occurrence probabilities from GC-matched 101-bp background bins are needed to compute binomial P-values.
skills.name: gc-matched-background-sampling
skills.search_text: gc-matched-background-sampling Use when TFBS motif instances from CNN motif detectors must be retained by statistical significance rather than a subjective signal cutoff — i.e., when per-motif occurrence probabilities from GC-matched 101-bp background bins are needed to compute binomial P-values. Peak sequences are not 101 bp (e.g. 1001-bp GCNN runs with peak_flank 500): the supplied 101-bp background bins would not match peak length or GC distribution, so a newly matched background is required. The goal is motif-to-database similarity scoring (TOMTOM against documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs) rather than statistical significance of TFBS counts against genomic background. Working outside the supplied human ENCODE/GRCh37.p13 setup with no ability to construct a GC-matched background of matching length and composition. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs DESSO's GC-matched background sampling, in which 500,000 GC-matched 101-bp genomic bins (encode_101_background) supply the per-motif occurrence probabilities for the binomial P-value model that replaces subjective motif signal cutoffs in TFBS identification. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Reconstructs DESSO's GC-matched background sampling, in which 500,000 GC-matched 101-bp genomic bins (encode_101_background) supply the per-motif occurrence probabilities for the binomial P-value model that replaces subjective motif signal cutoffs in TFBS identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peak sequences are not 101 bp (e.g. 1001-bp GCNN runs with peak_flank 500): the supplied 101-bp background bins would not match peak length or GC distribution, so a newly matched background is required. The goal is motif-to-database similarity scoring (TOMTOM against documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs) rather than statistical significance of TFBS counts against genomic background. Working outside the supplied human ENCODE/GRCh37.p13 setup with no ability to construct a GC-matched background of matching length and composition.

skills.description: Use when a Hi-C cis-contact map must be encoded as a graph (nodes/edges weighted by contact counts) to train or evaluate a graph-only CTCF loop-calling classifier, e.g. as a uni-modal baseline for view-complementarity tests.
skills.name: gcn-graph-based-loop-classifier-training
skills.search_text: gcn-graph-based-loop-classifier-training Use when a Hi-C cis-contact map must be encoded as a graph (nodes/edges weighted by contact counts) to train or evaluate a graph-only CTCF loop-calling classifier, e.g. as a uni-modal baseline for view-complementarity tests. Input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with it The analysis goal is image-view loop calling — the article reports distinct preferences for matrix density by graph-based vs image-based models, so the GCN branch alone is not a substitute for the U-Net image branch Applying a pre-trained model to a cell line whose sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository, without retraining or downsampling alignment Trains a GCN-only branch of GILoop that treats the Hi-C intra-chromosomal contact matrix as a graph to call CTCF-mediated loops, serving as the graph-view baseline against the fused dual-branch model. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Trains a GCN-only branch of GILoop that treats the Hi-C intra-chromosomal contact matrix as a graph to call CTCF-mediated loops, serving as the graph-view baseline against the fused dual-branch model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with it The analysis goal is image-view loop calling — the article reports distinct preferences for matrix density by graph-based vs image-based models, so the GCN branch alone is not a substitute for the U-Net image branch Applying a pre-trained model to a cell line whose sequencing depth differs from any pre-trained model in the repository, without retraining or downsampling alignment

skills.description: Use when evaluating how a graph-based loop caller's PR-AUC and smoothness (MAD) change across Hi-C sequencing depths, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch robustness on downsampled contact maps.
skills.name: gcn-loop-calling-inference
skills.search_text: gcn-loop-calling-inference Use when evaluating how a graph-based loop caller's PR-AUC and smoothness (MAD) change across Hi-C sequencing depths, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch robustness on downsampled contact maps. The input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with it The goal is to evaluate the image-based (U-Net) branch, whose PR-AUC falls rather than rises as depth decreases The contact maps are raw unnormalized matrices fed via demo_from_processed.py, which expects KR-normalized O/E matrices and applies no preprocessing http://edamontology.org/topic_3912 Run inference with the trained graph-convolutional (GCN) branch of GILoop on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, score candidate CTCF-mediated loops, and quantify depth-dependent behavior via PR-AUC and Mean Average Distance (MAD). This reproduces the paper's finding that GCN performance rises as sequencing depth decreases, peaking around 260 million cis-contacts. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Run inference with the trained graph-convolutional (GCN) branch of GILoop on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, score candidate CTCF-mediated loops, and quantify depth-dependent behavior via PR-AUC and Mean Average Distance (MAD). This reproduces the paper's finding that GCN performance rises as sequencing depth decreases, peaking around 260 million cis-contacts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and is not capable of dealing with it The goal is to evaluate the image-based (U-Net) branch, whose PR-AUC falls rather than rises as depth decreases The contact maps are raw unnormalized matrices fed via demo_from_processed.py, which expects KR-normalized O/E matrices and applies no preprocessing

skills.name: genbank-annotation-matching
skills.search_text: genbank-annotation-matching Use when GEO series expression tables must be anchored to official gene annotations: you have a GenBank .gbff for the organism and GEOparse-organized per-series tables whose gene identifiers need to be matched, filtered, and annotated before joining. The data have not yet been organized by GEOannotate — gffMatch expects GEOparse-organized series tables, not raw .soft.gz GSE files No GenBank .gbff annotation file exists for the organism — COnTORT requires the user to provide it and cannot anchor expression data to annotations without it The goal is raw expression retrieval without gene-anchoring, e.g. downloading only processed GEO data via the FTP mirror steps http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 COnTORT's gffMatch step matches GEOparse-organized GEO expression data against dictionaries built from a user-provided GenBank (.gbff) file, retaining only rows whose genes match GenBank annotations and prepending five annotation columns (Locus_Tag, Old_Locus_Tag, Gene_Name, Gene_Synonyms, Product) that later serve as join keys. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: COnTORT's gffMatch step matches GEOparse-organized GEO expression data against dictionaries built from a user-provided GenBank (.gbff) file, retaining only rows whose genes match GenBank annotations and prepending five annotation columns (Locus_Tag, Old_Locus_Tag, Gene_Name, Gene_Synonyms, Product) that later serve as join keys.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data have not yet been organized by GEOannotate — gffMatch expects GEOparse-organized series tables, not raw .soft.gz GSE files No GenBank .gbff annotation file exists for the organism — COnTORT requires the user to provide it and cannot anchor expression data to annotations without it The goal is raw expression retrieval without gene-anchoring, e.g. downloading only processed GEO data via the FTP mirror steps

skills.description: Use when running Delila-PY on a new organism: you have an NCBI GenBank file (e.g., NC_007493.2 for R. sphaeroides) and must create the Delila libraries that the delila program consumes to build a book of sequences.

skills.search_text: genbank-sequence-library-generation Use when running Delila-PY on a new organism: you have an NCBI GenBank file (e.g., NC_007493.2 for R. sphaeroides) and must create the Delila libraries that the delila program consumes to build a book of sequences. skills.name: gencode-annotation-parsing
skills.search_text: gencode-annotation-parsing Use when a genomic interval catalog (e.g., eccDNAs from AmpliconArchitect) must be intersected with GENCODE gene annotations to assign overlapping genes, with per-pair overlap ratios quantifying reciprocal coverage. skills.name: gene-annotation-strand-orientation-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-annotation-strand-orientation-mapping Use when you have strand-annotated BED files of motifs (e.g. TFBSs) and gene regions and need to test whether motif orientation is biased relative to transcriptional direction within transcribed regions. The goal is consecutive-occurrence asymmetry of a single feature, or pairwise asymmetry between two motifs in proximity — use Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns or pairwise_asymmetries instead of contained_asymmetries. skills.summary: Maps strand-annotated motifs (e.g. TFBSs) onto strand-annotated gene regions (GENCODE v33, hg38) using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries function to compute transcriptional strand asymmetry ratios and detect non-random motif orientation relative to transcription direction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is consecutive-occurrence asymmetry of a single feature, or pairwise asymmetry between two motifs in proximity — use Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns or pairwise_asymmetries instead of contained_asymmetries. skills.search_text: gene-expression-methylation-integration Use when integrating matched transcriptomic and epigenomic (methylation) p-value data to score genes, detect dysregulated network modules, or compare module-detection methods such as SMITE and FEM. skills.description: Use when you have a measured gene-expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GDS38, GSE44415) that must be converted into continuous smooth curves prior to ODE model fitting or regulon scoring.
skills.name: gene-expression-time-series-smoothing
skills.search_text: gene-expression-time-series-smoothing Use when you have a measured gene-expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GDS38, GSE44415) that must be converted into continuous smooth curves prior to ODE model fitting or regulon scoring. Data are not a time series (Genexpi/CyDataseries is specific to time-course expression data; Cytoscape does not natively support time series). The downstream analysis is a eukaryotic regulator-complex problem such as MBP1/SWI4/SWI6 in yeast, where the sigmoidal single-regulator model gave random-indistinguishable results. You need statistical uncertainty quantification — the smoothing-plus-thresholds approach masks uncertainty in the data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Smooth noisy gene-expression time-course profiles by linear regression on a B-spline basis before ODE-based regulator inference with Genexpi, so that fitted regulation models can be integrated cheaply with the Euler method on continuous curves. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: Smooth noisy gene-expression time-course profiles by linear regression on a B-spline basis before ODE-based regulator inference with Genexpi, so that fitted regulation models can be integrated cheaply with the Euler method on continuous curves.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not a time series (Genexpi/CyDataseries is specific to time-course expression data; Cytoscape does not natively support time series). The downstream analysis is a eukaryotic regulator-complex problem such as MBP1/SWI4/SWI6 in yeast, where the sigmoidal single-regulator model gave random-indistinguishable results. You need statistical uncertainty quantification — the smoothing-plus-thresholds approach masks uncertainty in the data.
