skills.name: gene-level-p-value-reproduction
skills.search_text: gene-level-p-value-reproduction Use when validating DriverPower-exclusive non-coding driver candidates by testing whether genes linked to mutated candidate elements show differential expression after correcting for copy number (SCNA) and tissue type. Input is already a background mutation model output (train_feature.hdf5 / response table) from the DriverPower model/infer pipeline — this skill models expression, not mutation burden The goal is to call new driver elements with burden tests rather than to validate expression effects of already-called candidates Only RNA-seq data without matched somatic MUT and SCNA calls are available, so the copy-number-corrected model cannot be fit http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the copy-number-corrected differential expression p values reported in the DriverPower paper (e.g. SGK1 p = 3e-13 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 p = 0.012 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) by fitting quasi-Poisson GLMs to PCAWG per-sample FPKM-UQ expression with mutation (MUT), copy-number (SCNA) and tissue covariates and performing likelihood ratio tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Reproduces the copy-number-corrected differential expression p values reported in the DriverPower paper (e.g. SGK1 p = 3e-13 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 p = 0.012 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) by fitting quasi-Poisson GLMs to PCAWG per-sample FPKM-UQ expression with mutation (MUT), copy-number (SCNA) and tissue covariates and performing likelihood ratio tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a background mutation model output (train_feature.hdf5 / response table) from the DriverPower model/infer pipeline — this skill models expression, not mutation burden The goal is to call new driver elements with burden tests rather than to validate expression effects of already-called candidates Only RNA-seq data without matched somatic MUT and SCNA calls are available, so the copy-number-corrected model cannot be fit

skills.description: Use when you have per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists from one-vs-rest SAM differential expression and need GO terms explaining the biology of each cluster.
skills.name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis Use when you have per-cluster up-/down-regulated gene lists from one-vs-rest SAM differential expression and need GO terms explaining the biology of each cluster. Input gene lists are not from a differential expression step — enrichment of unfiltered, genome-wide gene lists yields meaningless term over-representation Gene identifiers are not mappable to gene symbols (EnrichR module requires symbols; mygene 'scopes' must match the identifier format) The goal is de novo pathway discovery beyond GO — a customizable EnrichR database could be used instead, but the article only grounds GO enrichment http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3407 EnrichR-based GO enrichment of cluster-specific differentially expressed gene lists, as implemented in the SRIQ pipeline's Python/EnrichR module, to attribute biological programs (e.g., cell cycle, immune response) to unsupervised clusters such as the SRIQ core clusters in TCGA LUAD. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: EnrichR-based GO enrichment of cluster-specific differentially expressed gene lists, as implemented in the SRIQ pipeline's Python/EnrichR module, to attribute biological programs (e.g., cell cycle, immune response) to unsupervised clusters such as the SRIQ core clusters in TCGA LUAD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input gene lists are not from a differential expression step — enrichment of unfiltered, genome-wide gene lists yields meaningless term over-representation Gene identifiers are not mappable to gene symbols (EnrichR module requires symbols; mygene 'scopes' must match the identifier format) The goal is de novo pathway discovery beyond GO — a customizable EnrichR database could be used instead, but the article only grounds GO enrichment

skills.description: Use when you have a BIT output rank table (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) of TRs ranked by BIT score from perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type-specific epigenomic query regions and need to test GO BP enrichment of the top candidates.
skills.name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis Use when you have a BIT output rank table (e.g., mm10_RUNX1_rank_table.csv) of TRs ranked by BIT score from perturbation, cancer-type, or cell-type-specific epigenomic query regions and need to test GO BP enrichment of the top candidates. Input is not a ranked TR list from BIT but raw sequencing data (FASTQ, BAM) or peak files — those must first be processed through the BIT pipeline (peak calling, differential accessibility, BIT scoring) You need motif- or sequence-based functional annotation rather than gene-set over-representation of known TR gene symbols Query regions are from an organism without an appropriate Bioconductor org.*.eg.db annotation package http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Over-representation analysis of Gene Ontology biological-process terms among top-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) from BIT output rank tables, using clusterProfiler's one-sided Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction to ask whether BIT's top TRs are enriched for processes relevant to the perturbed biological context. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Over-representation analysis of Gene Ontology biological-process terms among top-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) from BIT output rank tables, using clusterProfiler's one-sided Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction to ask whether BIT's top TRs are enriched for processes relevant to the perturbed biological context.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a ranked TR list from BIT but raw sequencing data (FASTQ, BAM) or peak files — those must first be processed through the BIT pipeline (peak calling, differential accessibility, BIT scoring) You need motif- or sequence-based functional annotation rather than gene-set over-representation of known TR gene symbols Query regions are from an organism without an appropriate Bioconductor org.*.eg.db annotation package

skills.description: Use when you have a ranked list of genes from EpiAlign differential alignment (Wilcoxon P-values comparing within-tissue vs cross-tissue alignment scores) and need functional interpretation via GO terms or validation against known tissue-specific gene labels.
skills.name: gene-ontology-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-enrichment-interpretation Use when you have a ranked list of genes from EpiAlign differential alignment (Wilcoxon P-values comparing within-tissue vs cross-tissue alignment scores) and need functional interpretation via GO terms or validation against known tissue-specific gene labels. The input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices or uncompressed chromatin state sequences — run EpiAlign's compressed Smith-Waterman alignment and Wilcoxon ranking first; GO enrichment only consumes ranked gene lists. The goal is to compare chromatin state sequences or epigenomic samples directly rather than functionally interpret an already-ranked gene list. The gene list is not ranked by a statistical criterion (e.g. differential alignment P-values) — GOrilla expects genes ordered by score for its enrichment model. http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Interpret ranked gene lists produced by EpiAlign differential chromatin-state alignment by running Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment (e.g. GOrilla) on the top genes with the smallest P-values, and validating enrichment against known tissue-specific gene sets. This connects alignment-derived chromatin patterns to biological function. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Interpret ranked gene lists produced by EpiAlign differential chromatin-state alignment by running Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment (e.g. GOrilla) on the top genes with the smallest P-values, and validating enrichment against known tissue-specific gene sets. This connects alignment-derived chromatin patterns to biological function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices or uncompressed chromatin state sequences — run EpiAlign's compressed Smith-Waterman alignment and Wilcoxon ranking first; GO enrichment only consumes ranked gene lists. The goal is to compare chromatin state sequences or epigenomic samples directly rather than functionally interpret an already-ranked gene list. The gene list is not ranked by a statistical criterion (e.g. differential alignment P-values) — GOrilla expects genes ordered by score for its enrichment model.

skills.description: Use when genes have been assigned to CscoreTool-M sub-compartments (e.g., C10_2 or C10_1 from a 10-sub-compartment run on Hi-C data) and you need to test whether these sub-compartments are enriched for housekeeping or cell-type-specific biological functions.
skills.name: gene-ontology-enrichment-of-sub-compartments
skills.search_text: gene-ontology-enrichment-of-sub-compartments Use when genes have been assigned to CscoreTool-M sub-compartments (e.g., C10_2 or C10_1 from a 10-sub-compartment run on Hi-C data) and you need to test whether these sub-compartments are enriched for housekeeping or cell-type-specific biological functions. Input is raw Hi-C summary data and sub-compartments have not yet been inferred — run CscoreTool-M first; this skill starts from cscore.txt assignments The goal is quantifying intra-population heterogeneity (Shannon information content over probability scores) rather than functional interpretation of sub-compartment gene content Genomic windows contain no genes or no reads — regions with no reads are not shown in the cscore outputs, leaving nothing to assign for GO analysis Annotates CscoreTool-M 3D genome sub-compartments by performing Gene Ontology enrichment on genes assigned to each sub-compartment, demonstrating that sub-compartments correspond to housekeeping or cell-type-specific functions. This validates the biological interpretability of probabilistic sub-compartment assignments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Annotates CscoreTool-M 3D genome sub-compartments by performing Gene Ontology enrichment on genes assigned to each sub-compartment, demonstrating that sub-compartments correspond to housekeeping or cell-type-specific functions. This validates the biological interpretability of probabilistic sub-compartment assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Hi-C summary data and sub-compartments have not yet been inferred — run CscoreTool-M first; this skill starts from cscore.txt assignments The goal is quantifying intra-population heterogeneity (Shannon information content over probability scores) rather than functional interpretation of sub-compartment gene content Genomic windows contain no genes or no reads — regions with no reads are not shown in the cscore outputs, leaving nothing to assign for GO analysis

skills.description: Use when you have two gene/region sets (e.g., differentially modified regions from ChIP-seq and differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq) mapped to a common identifier and need to quantify overlap significance and GO enrichment.
skills.name: gene-overlap-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-overlap-enrichment-analysis Use when you have two gene/region sets (e.g., differentially modified regions from ChIP-seq and differentially expressed genes from RNA-seq) mapped to a common identifier and need to quantify overlap significance and GO enrichment. You need to detect differentially modified regions themselves rather than test overlap of existing calls — use histoneHMM's bivariate HMM workflow instead Peak-like histone marks (narrow punctate ChIP-seq signals) rather than broad modifications like H3K27me3/H3K9me3 are the input, since competing peak-caller-based region sets behave differently on broad marks Only one gene set exists (no DE gene list), making a 2x2 contingency table undefined http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Statistical testing of whether differentially modified histone regions overlap with differentially expressed genes more than expected, using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact test, followed by GO enrichment of the overlapping gene set. This is the validation strategy the histoneHMM paper used to show its calls are functionally relevant versus competing methods. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Statistical testing of whether differentially modified histone regions overlap with differentially expressed genes more than expected, using 2x2 contingency tables and Fisher's exact test, followed by GO enrichment of the overlapping gene set. This is the validation strategy the histoneHMM paper used to show its calls are functionally relevant versus competing methods.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to detect differentially modified regions themselves rather than test overlap of existing calls — use histoneHMM's bivariate HMM workflow instead Peak-like histone marks (narrow punctate ChIP-seq signals) rather than broad modifications like H3K27me3/H3K9me3 are the input, since competing peak-caller-based region sets behave differently on broad marks Only one gene set exists (no DE gene list), making a 2x2 contingency table undefined

skills.description: Use when patient SVs (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) in hg19 coordinates need candidate causative genes and coding or long-range pathomechanisms assigned in a phenotype-specific cellular context.
skills.name: gene-pathomechanism-interpretation
skills.search_text: gene-pathomechanism-interpretation Use when patient SVs (inversions, translocations, deletions, duplications) in hg19 coordinates need candidate causative genes and coding or long-range pathomechanisms assigned in a phenotype-specific cellular context. The phenotype of interest is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The pathomechanism depends on an enhancer not detectable in POSTRE's bulk tissue data (e.g. the ZRS enhancer within whole limb buds, so SHH duplication cases fail) Only a single SV needs quick analysis without installation — the online version supports Single SV submissions, but Multiple SV submissions require local installation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Interpret structural variant (SV) predictions into concrete causative genes and pathomechanisms (coding gene deletion vs long-range enhancer disconnection/adoption) using POSTRE's cell type-specific outputs, comparing Standard and High-Specificity running modes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Interpret structural variant (SV) predictions into concrete causative genes and pathomechanisms (coding gene deletion vs long-range enhancer disconnection/adoption) using POSTRE's cell type-specific outputs, comparing Standard and High-Specificity running modes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The phenotype of interest is recessive — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The pathomechanism depends on an enhancer not detectable in POSTRE's bulk tissue data (e.g. the ZRS enhancer within whole limb buds, so SHH duplication cases fail) Only a single SV needs quick analysis without installation — the online version supports Single SV submissions, but Multiple SV submissions require local installation

skills.description: Use when you have a SnapATAC snap object for scATAC-seq cells plus matched scRNA-seq expression and need to connect distal accessible peaks to putative target genes, e.g. building a cis-regulatory network from the 10X_PBMC_15K PBMC dataset.
skills.name: gene-peak-pair-association-modeling
skills.search_text: gene-peak-pair-association-modeling Use when you have a SnapATAC snap object for scATAC-seq cells plus matched scRNA-seq expression and need to connect distal accessible peaks to putative target genes, e.g. building a cis-regulatory network from the 10X_PBMC_15K PBMC dataset. Input is raw FASTQ/BAM — pre-processing (alignment, duplicate removal, snap-file creation) belongs to SnapTools, not this linkage step Goal is dimensionality reduction, clustering, batch correction, or motif analysis rather than enhancer–gene assignment No matched scRNA-seq expression data are available to impute gene expression, so gene activity cannot be modeled for the same cells http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Fits a logistic-regression association between imputed gene expression (from matched scRNA-seq) and binarized distal enhancer accessibility in SnapATAC to link candidate regulatory elements to putative target genes. This is the enhancer–gene linkage step, benchmarked against monocyte cis-eQTLs (AUROC 0.66, AUPRC 0.68). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Fits a logistic-regression association between imputed gene expression (from matched scRNA-seq) and binarized distal enhancer accessibility in SnapATAC to link candidate regulatory elements to putative target genes. This is the enhancer–gene linkage step, benchmarked against monocyte cis-eQTLs (AUROC 0.66, AUPRC 0.68).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ/BAM — pre-processing (alignment, duplicate removal, snap-file creation) belongs to SnapTools, not this linkage step Goal is dimensionality reduction, clustering, batch correction, or motif analysis rather than enhancer–gene assignment No matched scRNA-seq expression data are available to impute gene expression, so gene activity cannot be modeled for the same cells

skills.description: Use when a candidate gene must be scored for its association with a structural-variant-associated phenotype group (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) using HPO/MPO gene-phenotype annotations.
skills.name: gene-phenotype-annotation-mapping
skills.search_text: gene-phenotype-annotation-mapping Use when a candidate gene must be scored for its association with a structural-variant-associated phenotype group (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) using HPO/MPO gene-phenotype annotations. When the phenotype of interest falls outside the phenotype groups POSTRE supports (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) — the module only scores those predefined groups. When the goal is to predict SV pathogenic mechanisms (coding vs long-range) — POSTRE's cell type-specific enhancer/TAD analysis handles that, not this annotation-mapping step. When experimental validation of a gene-phenotype link is needed — this skill only aggregates curated ontology annotations, not functional evidence. http://edamontology.org/topic_0219 Reconstructs POSTRE's genePhenoScore module by parsing HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) resources to link human genes to the four POSTRE reference phenotype groups (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) and score each gene-phenotype pair as 1 (human HPO), 0.5 (mouse ortholog MPO only, Standard Running Mode), or 0. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Reconstructs POSTRE's genePhenoScore module by parsing HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) resources to link human genes to the four POSTRE reference phenotype groups (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) and score each gene-phenotype pair as 1 (human HPO), 0.5 (mouse ortholog MPO only, Standard Running Mode), or 0.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the phenotype of interest falls outside the phenotype groups POSTRE supports (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) — the module only scores those predefined groups. When the goal is to predict SV pathogenic mechanisms (coding vs long-range) — POSTRE's cell type-specific enhancer/TAD analysis handles that, not this annotation-mapping step. When experimental validation of a gene-phenotype link is needed — this skill only aggregates curated ontology annotations, not functional evidence.

skills.description: Use when you have non-coding variants already scored by a brain-variant prioritizer (ncDeepBrain) and need to assign per-gene susceptibility probabilities by linking variants to genes and training a deep network on gene-level features.
skills.name: gene-prioritization-deep-learning
skills.search_text: gene-prioritization-deep-learning Use when you have non-coding variants already scored by a brain-variant prioritizer (ncDeepBrain) and need to assign per-gene susceptibility probabilities by linking variants to genes and training a deep network on gene-level features. You need to score individual non-coding variants rather than prioritize genes — that is iMEGES step 1 (ncDeepBrain variant prioritization) Your regulatory candidates act via distal elements where assigning a variant to its closest gene within 100 kb is inappropriate (e.g. enhancers regulating non-nearest genes) Input is already a per-gene prioritized ranking with no variant-level ncDeepBrain scores to integrate http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Second step of iMEGES: a Keras/TensorFlow multilayer neural network integrates the ncDeepBrain non-coding variant score with general gene scores (RVIS, GTEx, haploinsufficiency) and disease-specific scores (Phenolyzer, CNV, de novo mutation) to output an iMEGES gene score — a susceptibility probability per mutated gene for mental disorders. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7
skills.summary: Second step of iMEGES: a Keras/TensorFlow multilayer neural network integrates the ncDeepBrain non-coding variant score with general gene scores (RVIS, GTEx, haploinsufficiency) and disease-specific scores (Phenolyzer, CNV, de novo mutation) to output an iMEGES gene score — a susceptibility probability per mutated gene for mental disorders.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to score individual non-coding variants rather than prioritize genes — that is iMEGES step 1 (ncDeepBrain variant prioritization) Your regulatory candidates act via distal elements where assigning a variant to its closest gene within 100 kb is inappropriate (e.g. enhancers regulating non-nearest genes) Input is already a per-gene prioritized ranking with no variant-level ncDeepBrain scores to integrate

skills.description: Use when a set of SVs with known disease-causative genes (positive controls) must be scored by multiple pathogenicity classifiers and ranked-gene agreement between tools (e.g. POSTRE vs TADEUS2) quantified.
skills.name: gene-ranking-comparison-across-tools
skills.search_text: gene-ranking-comparison-across-tools Use when a set of SVs with known disease-causative genes (positive controls) must be scored by multiple pathogenicity classifiers and ranked-gene agreement between tools (e.g. POSTRE vs TADEUS2) quantified. The SVs act through non-coding long-range mechanisms and TADA is being compared without restriction — TADA is reported as inappropriate for non-coding (e.g. long-range) pathomechanisms The task is recessive-disorder SV interpretation — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated Only a single tool's predictions are available with no comparator cohort — sensitivity/(1-specificity) ratios and ranking agreement require both positive controls and a second classifier such as TADeus2 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark a candidate SV pathogenicity predictor (POSTRE) against competing classifiers (TADA, STRVCTVRE, SVScore, CADD-SV, TADeus2) by comparing which tool ranks the correct disease-causative gene on a set of positive-control structural variants. Provides the reproduction of Figure 6's head-to-head gene-ranking agreement metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Benchmark a candidate SV pathogenicity predictor (POSTRE) against competing classifiers (TADA, STRVCTVRE, SVScore, CADD-SV, TADeus2) by comparing which tool ranks the correct disease-causative gene on a set of positive-control structural variants. Provides the reproduction of Figure 6's head-to-head gene-ranking agreement metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SVs act through non-coding long-range mechanisms and TADA is being compared without restriction — TADA is reported as inappropriate for non-coding (e.g. long-range) pathomechanisms The task is recessive-disorder SV interpretation — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated Only a single tool's predictions are available with no comparator cohort — sensitivity/(1-specificity) ratios and ranking agreement require both positive controls and a second classifier such as TADeus2

skills.description: Use when a query gene's chromatin state sequence must be compared against every protein-coding gene region in one Roadmap/ChromHMM-annotated sample to produce a ranked local-alignment score table identifying the -matching gene region.
skills.name: gene-region-alignment-score-ranking
skills.search_text: gene-region-alignment-score-ranking Use when a query gene's chromatin state sequence must be compared against every protein-coding gene region in one Roadmap/ChromHMM-annotated sample to produce a ranked local-alignment score table identifying the -matching gene region. The goal is cross-sample comparison of all genes between pairs of epigenomes with downstream Wilcoxon testing and GO enrichment, not ranking regions against a single query gene. The sequences are uncompressed chromatin state sequences and long quiescent stretches should dominate; skipping the compression step changes which gene ranks best. The input is a 500 kb region-level 'horizontal' alignment query across an epigenome rather than a gene-region ranking task. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Ranks all protein-coding gene regions in a Roadmap sample by EpiAlign local alignment score against a query gene's compressed ChromHMM chromatin state sequence, so the best epigenomically similar gene region can be identified (e.g. NRG3 aligns best with GRIA1 in brain sample E071). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Ranks all protein-coding gene regions in a Roadmap sample by EpiAlign local alignment score against a query gene's compressed ChromHMM chromatin state sequence, so the best epigenomically similar gene region can be identified (e.g. NRG3 aligns best with GRIA1 in brain sample E071).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cross-sample comparison of all genes between pairs of epigenomes with downstream Wilcoxon testing and GO enrichment, not ranking regions against a single query gene. The sequences are uncompressed chromatin state sequences and long quiescent stretches should dominate; skipping the compression step changes which gene ranks best. The input is a 500 kb region-level 'horizontal' alignment query across an epigenome rather than a gene-region ranking task.

skills.description: Use when validating a gene regulatory network inference method on time-course expression data against a curated reference regulon set, especially to compare two methods and a random baseline per transcription factor.
skills.name: gene-regulatory-network-method-comparison
skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-method-comparison Use when validating a gene regulatory network inference method on time-course expression data against a curated reference regulon set, especially to compare two methods and a random baseline per transcription factor. The study system has no curated reference regulons (e.g. no YEASTRACT/Subtiwiki equivalent), since recovery proportions cannot be computed against documented regulations. Expression data are not time-course measurements; Genexpi's ODE model and smoothing assume expression profiles over time. The transcription factors of interest are known to regulate in complexes (e.g. MBP1/SWI4/SWI6), where Genexpi's single-regulator model is expected to break and yield random-indistinguishable results. http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A benchmarking skill that compares inferred regulons (e.g. Genexpi vs TD-ARACNE vs a random baseline) against curated reference regulons from databases such as YEASTRACT, quantifying the per-transcription-factor proportion of documented regulations recovered at or above chance level. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill that compares inferred regulons (e.g. Genexpi vs TD-ARACNE vs a random baseline) against curated reference regulons from databases such as YEASTRACT, quantifying the per-transcription-factor proportion of documented regulations recovered at or above chance level.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The study system has no curated reference regulons (e.g. no YEASTRACT/Subtiwiki equivalent), since recovery proportions cannot be computed against documented regulations. Expression data are not time-course measurements; Genexpi's ODE model and smoothing assume expression profiles over time. The transcription factors of interest are known to regulate in complexes (e.g. MBP1/SWI4/SWI6), where Genexpi's single-regulator model is expected to break and yield random-indistinguishable results.

skills.description: Use when a time-series expression dataset (e.g., mouse liver regeneration GSE95135) has been mined with TSMiner and you need machine-readable tables of time-specific activators/repressors and their interacting KEGG pathways.
skills.name: gene-regulatory-network-table-export
skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-network-table-export Use when a time-series expression dataset (e.g., mouse liver regeneration GSE95135) has been mined with TSMiner and you need machine-readable tables of time-specific activators/repressors and their interacting KEGG pathways. The expression data are not time-series, since TSMiner constructs time-specific regulatory networks specifically from time-series expression profiles You only have clustering or static co-expression analysis goals — clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways, but TSMiner's export targets time-specific TF–pathway events The input TF–TG interaction file mixes positively and negatively correlated interactions without separation, since TSMiner requires them processed separately http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Export time-specific TF–pathway interaction network tables from TSMiner runs on time-series RNA-seq data, separately for positively correlated (activators) and negatively correlated (repressors) TF–TG interactions. Tables list each transcription factor with its activation/repression time point and the significantly interacting KEGG pathways. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Export time-specific TF–pathway interaction network tables from TSMiner runs on time-series RNA-seq data, separately for positively correlated (activators) and negatively correlated (repressors) TF–TG interactions. Tables list each transcription factor with its activation/repression time point and the significantly interacting KEGG pathways.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are not time-series, since TSMiner constructs time-specific regulatory networks specifically from time-series expression profiles You only have clustering or static co-expression analysis goals — clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways, but TSMiner's export targets time-specific TF–pathway events The input TF–TG interaction file mixes positively and negatively correlated interactions without separation, since TSMiner requires them processed separately

skills.description: Use when fitting gene-regulator ODE parameters to smoothed time-course expression profiles (e.g. SigB regulon targets) and you need to compare regularized vs. unregularized fits or enforce biologically interpretable parameter bounds.
skills.name: gene-regulatory-ode-parameter-fitting
skills.search_text: gene-regulatory-ode-parameter-fitting Use when fitting gene-regulator ODE parameters to smoothed time-course expression profiles (e.g. SigB regulon targets) and you need to compare regularized vs. unregularized fits or enforce biologically interpretable parameter bounds. Genes whose expression does not change significantly over the whole time range (no change model) — Genexpi contains no information in that case and such genes are excluded as regulators and targets Genes that could be fitted by the constant synthesis model (any regulator fits with w = 0 and large b) — excluded as targets Eukaryotic time-course data where full validation is lacking — the article states Genexpi was designed for bacterial regulons and can be employed for eukaryotic data only with caution http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2259 Fits ODE model parameters (b, k1, w, ρ) for gene-regulator pairs to smoothed time-course expression data via simulated annealing in Genexpi, with a regularization term r(β) that discriminates candidate models and forces parameters into biologically interpretable ranges. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: Fits ODE model parameters (b, k1, w, ρ) for gene-regulator pairs to smoothed time-course expression data via simulated annealing in Genexpi, with a regularization term r(β) that discriminates candidate models and forces parameters into biologically interpretable ranges.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Genes whose expression does not change significantly over the whole time range (no change model) — Genexpi contains no information in that case and such genes are excluded as regulators and targets Genes that could be fitted by the constant synthesis model (any regulator fits with w = 0 and large b) — excluded as targets Eukaryotic time-course data where full validation is lacking — the article states Genexpi was designed for bacterial regulons and can be employed for eukaryotic data only with caution

skills.description: Use when input is scATAC-seq raw data (fragment file or bam file) or gene score matrices, and you need to build Cellcano-ready reference/target matrices with F-test-selected features before supervised celltyping.
skills.name: gene-score-matrix-processing
skills.search_text: gene-score-matrix-processing Use when input is scATAC-seq raw data (fragment file or bam file) or gene score matrices, and you need to build Cellcano-ready reference/target matrices with F-test-selected features before supervised celltyping. Input is already an F-test-filtered feature table or 'selected_features.csv' exists with the 3000 genes The input is single-cell gene expression (scRNA-seq) data rather than scATAC-seq-derived gene scores You need cross-modality prediction (scRNA-seq reference for scATAC-seq target) — the article states this is planned but not implemented in Cellcano http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Prepare scATAC-seq gene score matrices for Cellcano celltyping by converting raw fragment/bam files into gene scores with ArchR and selecting cell-type-specific features from the reference matrix via an F-test (top 3000 genes). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Prepare scATAC-seq gene score matrices for Cellcano celltyping by converting raw fragment/bam files into gene scores with ArchR and selecting cell-type-specific features from the reference matrix via an F-test (top 3000 genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an F-test-filtered feature table or 'selected_features.csv' exists with the 3000 genes The input is single-cell gene expression (scRNA-seq) data rather than scATAC-seq-derived gene scores You need cross-modality prediction (scRNA-seq reference for scATAC-seq target) — the article states this is planned but not implemented in Cellcano

skills.description: Use when evaluating which scATAC-seq input representation (ArchR-derived gene scores vs. 500-bp fixed-size bin counts) yields better Cellcano celltype prediction accuracy across benchmark tasks, especially mouse brain reference-target pairs from Fig 2.
skills.name: gene-score-vs-bin-accuracy-comparison
skills.search_text: gene-score-vs-bin-accuracy-comparison Use when evaluating which scATAC-seq input representation (ArchR-derived gene scores vs. 500-bp fixed-size bin counts) yields better Cellcano celltype prediction accuracy across benchmark tasks, especially mouse brain reference-target pairs from Fig 2. The goal is comparing Cellcano against other celltyping methods (Seurat, Signac, scJoint, EpiAnno) rather than comparing Cellcano's own input representations The tasks are human PBMC tasks or other non-mouse-brain tasks for which the 63-task / 62-win validation result does not apply Raw scATAC-seq data (fragment or bam files) needs processing first — run the ArchR pipeline to obtain gene scores before this accuracy comparison is meaningful http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A benchmark-comparison skill for Cellcano scATAC-seq celltyping that tabulates prediction accuracy using gene scores as input versus genome-wide fixed-size 500-bp bin counts, based on the Figure 2a-b Source Data of the Nature Communications Cellcano paper. It quantifies how often gene scores outperform bins across the 63 mouse brain celltyping tasks. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: A benchmark-comparison skill for Cellcano scATAC-seq celltyping that tabulates prediction accuracy using gene scores as input versus genome-wide fixed-size 500-bp bin counts, based on the Figure 2a-b Source Data of the Nature Communications Cellcano paper. It quantifies how often gene scores outperform bins across the 63 mouse brain celltyping tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is comparing Cellcano against other celltyping methods (Seurat, Signac, scJoint, EpiAnno) rather than comparing Cellcano's own input representations The tasks are human PBMC tasks or other non-mouse-brain tasks for which the 63-task / 62-win validation result does not apply Raw scATAC-seq data (fragment or bam files) needs processing first — run the ArchR pipeline to obtain gene scores before this accuracy comparison is meaningful

skills.description: Use when genes must be ranked by epigenomic signal (e.g. RNAP2 or H3K4me3 ChIP-seq prevalence) within chromosome clusters such as BHi-Cect bottom enclaves, and tested for GO-term enrichment via GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-analysis Use when genes must be ranked by epigenomic signal (e.g. RNAP2 or H3K4me3 ChIP-seq prevalence) within chromosome clusters such as BHi-Cect bottom enclaves, and tested for GO-term enrichment via GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. The analysis goal is contiguous TAD-level segmentation of Hi-C data rather than non-contiguous, deeply interwoven enclave clusters — BHi-Cect explicitly clusters without imposing genomic contiguity ChIP-seq signal has not been aggregated per enclave; GSEA requires per-gene (or per-enclave) ranked lists, not raw contact matrices The cell lines or marks differ from RNAP2/IMR90 and H3K4me3/K562 without re-validating the expected enrichment categories http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Runs GSEA with Gene Ontology gene sets on gene lists ranked by RNAP2 (IMR90) or H3K4me3 (K562) ChIP-seq signal prevalence in bottom enclaves identified by the BHi-Cect hierarchical clustering of Hi-C data, linking chromosome enclave structure to enriched biological functions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Runs GSEA with Gene Ontology gene sets on gene lists ranked by RNAP2 (IMR90) or H3K4me3 (K562) ChIP-seq signal prevalence in bottom enclaves identified by the BHi-Cect hierarchical clustering of Hi-C data, linking chromosome enclave structure to enriched biological functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is contiguous TAD-level segmentation of Hi-C data rather than non-contiguous, deeply interwoven enclave clusters — BHi-Cect explicitly clusters without imposing genomic contiguity ChIP-seq signal has not been aggregated per enclave; GSEA requires per-gene (or per-enclave) ranked lists, not raw contact matrices The cell lines or marks differ from RNAP2/IMR90 and H3K4me3/K562 without re-validating the expected enrichment categories

skills.description: Use when you have a BED list of ChIP-seq peaks (e.g. bivalent H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+ peaks in mESCs) and need to identify enriched biological functions such as developmental GO categories.
skills.name: gene-set-enrichment-interpretation
skills.search_text: gene-set-enrichment-interpretation Use when you have a BED list of ChIP-seq peaks (e.g. bivalent H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+ peaks in mESCs) and need to identify enriched biological functions such as developmental GO categories. Input is already a gene list with no peak coordinates — the matchpeaksgenes peak-to-TSS mapping step is unnecessary The genome/organism has no RefSeq annotation available from UCSC or the consortium, since SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations Peak-to-gene assignment should use gene-body or other distance rules rather than a 2500 bp promoter window around the TSS http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Derive functional interpretation from a set of genomic regions by first mapping them to genes with SeqCode matchpeaksgenes (RefSeq annotations, 2500 bp TSS window), then running GO Biological Process enrichment with Enrichr and ranking terms by combined score. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Derive functional interpretation from a set of genomic regions by first mapping them to genes with SeqCode matchpeaksgenes (RefSeq annotations, 2500 bp TSS window), then running GO Biological Process enrichment with Enrichr and ranking terms by combined score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene list with no peak coordinates — the matchpeaksgenes peak-to-TSS mapping step is unnecessary The genome/organism has no RefSeq annotation available from UCSC or the consortium, since SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations Peak-to-gene assignment should use gene-body or other distance rules rather than a 2500 bp promoter window around the TSS

skills.description: Use when you have two or more differential-expression-derived gene lists (e.g., H-NS regulons from GSE136050 RNA-seq and a published 308-gene LuxR regulon) and need to compute and validate their overlap count.
skills.name: gene-set-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: gene-set-overlap-analysis Use when you have two or more differential-expression-derived gene lists (e.g., H-NS regulons from GSE136050 RNA-seq and a published 308-gene LuxR regulon) and need to compute and validate their overlap count. Input is already a precomputed overlap/Venn result rather than raw gene lists requiring identifier harmonization and intersection The regulon gene lists were derived with different expression thresholds (not >2-fold, P < 0.05), which would change the expected 178-gene overlap count You need ChIP-seq peak-level overlap analysis with genomic coordinate logic rather than gene-set list intersection (note the README scripts such as findOverlaps.pl were built for Macs2 peak overlaps) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Computes the set intersection between two regulon gene lists — here, the RNA-seq-derived H-NS regulons (wild-type and ΔluxR backgrounds) and the previously identified 308-gene LuxR regulon in V. harveyi — to quantify regulatory overlap using the Perl scripts deposited at github.com/Juliacvk/LuxR_H-NS. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Computes the set intersection between two regulon gene lists — here, the RNA-seq-derived H-NS regulons (wild-type and ΔluxR backgrounds) and the previously identified 308-gene LuxR regulon in V. harveyi — to quantify regulatory overlap using the Perl scripts deposited at github.com/Juliacvk/LuxR_H-NS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a precomputed overlap/Venn result rather than raw gene lists requiring identifier harmonization and intersection The regulon gene lists were derived with different expression thresholds (not >2-fold, P < 0.05), which would change the expected 178-gene overlap count You need ChIP-seq peak-level overlap analysis with genomic coordinate logic rather than gene-set list intersection (note the README scripts such as findOverlaps.pl were built for Macs2 peak overlaps)

skills.description: Use when you have per-donor flow cytometry cell population proportion data plus donor metadata (continuous age, sex) and need to quantify which factor — age, sex, or their interaction — is most strongly associated with each PBMC cell subset.
skills.name: generalized-linear-model-regression
skills.search_text: generalized-linear-model-regression Use when you have per-donor flow cytometry cell population proportion data plus donor metadata (continuous age, sex) and need to quantify which factor — age, sex, or their interaction — is most strongly associated with each PBMC cell subset. Input is already aggregated summary statistics rather than per-donor cell proportions — GLM ranking of factor associations requires donor-level variation The question is about molecular or single-cell aging signatures (ATAC-seq/RNA-seq loci, sorted cells), not bulk flow cytometry composition of PBMCs Testing within-donor longitudinal change — this skill models cross-sectional between-donor variation (age-matched male and female donors), not repeated measures Fits per-cell-population generalized linear models of flow cytometry PBMC cell proportions against age (continuous or age-group factor), sex, and an age-by-sex interaction to rank which individual-level factor most strongly drives each immune cell composition change in the 172-donor Márquez et al. cohort. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Fits per-cell-population generalized linear models of flow cytometry PBMC cell proportions against age (continuous or age-group factor), sex, and an age-by-sex interaction to rank which individual-level factor most strongly drives each immune cell composition change in the 172-donor Márquez et al. cohort.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aggregated summary statistics rather than per-donor cell proportions — GLM ranking of factor associations requires donor-level variation The question is about molecular or single-cell aging signatures (ATAC-seq/RNA-seq loci, sorted cells), not bulk flow cytometry composition of PBMCs Testing within-donor longitudinal change — this skill models cross-sectional between-donor variation (age-matched male and female donors), not repeated measures

skills.description: Use when modeling ChIP-Seq HDF per-bin count data whose enriched-state distribution is overdispersed relative to Poisson and whose background contains excess zeros, requiring GP/ZIP emissions for HMM-based bin classification.
skills.name: generalized-poisson-emission-density-estimation
skills.search_text: generalized-poisson-emission-density-estimation Use when modeling ChIP-Seq HDF per-bin count data whose enriched-state distribution is overdispersed relative to Poisson and whose background contains excess zeros, requiring GP/ZIP emissions for HMM-based bin classification. The input is not directionally extended short-read coverage (HDF counts per fixed bin), e.g. it is already a peak list or feature table Comparative histone modification data better suited to ChIPDiff, which is restricted to that analysis per the article A quantification of false detection rate is the primary goal, since the HMM-based method is not well-suited for quantifying FDR http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit Generalized Poisson (GP) and zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission densities to per-bin HDF coverage counts so a two-state HMM can classify 25 bp bins as ChIP-enriched or background in HPeak-style ChIP-Seq peak calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Fit Generalized Poisson (GP) and zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission densities to per-bin HDF coverage counts so a two-state HMM can classify 25 bp bins as ChIP-enriched or background in HPeak-style ChIP-Seq peak calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not directionally extended short-read coverage (HDF counts per fixed bin), e.g. it is already a peak list or feature table Comparative histone modification data better suited to ChIPDiff, which is restricted to that analysis per the article A quantification of false detection rate is the primary goal, since the HMM-based method is not well-suited for quantifying FDR

skills.description: Use when benchmark pairs or annotations are given on an older assembly (e.g. hg19 BENGI) but features were computed on a newer one (hg38 cCREs-ELS/GENCODE v40), requiring coordinate conversion and per-pair feature averaging before cross-method comparison.
skills.name: genome-assembly-liftover-feature-harmonization
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-liftover-feature-harmonization Use when benchmark pairs or annotations are given on an older assembly (e.g. hg19 BENGI) but features were computed on a newer one (hg38 cCREs-ELS/GENCODE v40), requiring coordinate conversion and per-pair feature averaging before cross-method comparison. Pairs and genomic features are already expressed on the same assembly and registry (e.g. fully hg38 cCREs-ELS/GENCODE v40), so no cross-assembly harmonization is needed Candidate interactions extend beyond 500 KB, since the CENTRE pipeline explicitly restricts the ET pair search to that interval http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Lifts enhancer-target (ET) pairs between genome assemblies (hg19→hg38) with the UCSC Genome Browser liftover facility, re-anchors them on the ENCODE cCRE Registry v2 and GENCODE TSSs, and harmonizes CENTRE hg38 feature values onto the hg19 BENGI annotation so legacy benchmark models like TargetFinder can be compared against CENTRE. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad687
skills.summary: Lifts enhancer-target (ET) pairs between genome assemblies (hg19→hg38) with the UCSC Genome Browser liftover facility, re-anchors them on the ENCODE cCRE Registry v2 and GENCODE TSSs, and harmonizes CENTRE hg38 feature values onto the hg19 BENGI annotation so legacy benchmark models like TargetFinder can be compared against CENTRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Pairs and genomic features are already expressed on the same assembly and registry (e.g. fully hg38 cCREs-ELS/GENCODE v40), so no cross-assembly harmonization is needed Candidate interactions extend beyond 500 KB, since the CENTRE pipeline explicitly restricts the ET pair search to that interval

skills.description: Use when the goal is to regenerate or replicate a published long-read (Oxford Nanopore) genome assembly pipeline from a released repository, specifically the polished E. coli assembly from the 2015 Nature Methods nanopore article.
skills.name: genome-assembly-polishing
skills.search_text: genome-assembly-polishing Use when the goal is to regenerate or replicate a published long-read (Oxford Nanopore) genome assembly pipeline from a released repository, specifically the polished E. coli assembly from the 2015 Nature Methods nanopore article. You only need basecalling model training or modified-base detection — use nanoporetech/taiyaki or nanoporetech/bonito instead of this assembly pipeline. Your data is not the public E. coli nanopore/short-read pair from the 2015 paper and you have not adapted the Makefile's ENA download and pinned software versions. You need a reimplementation of individual correction/assembly/polishing tools rather than a reproducible Makefile-driven run of the exact published pipeline. http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the polished nanopore E. coli genome assembly from the 2015 Nature Methods paper by running the jts/nanopore-paper-analysis repository's end-to-end Makefile, which error-corrects long reads, assembles contigs, and polishes them into polished_genome.fasta. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100153
skills.summary: Reproduces the polished nanopore E. coli genome assembly from the 2015 Nature Methods paper by running the jts/nanopore-paper-analysis repository's end-to-end Makefile, which error-corrects long reads, assembles contigs, and polishes them into polished_genome.fasta.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need basecalling model training or modified-base detection — use nanoporetech/taiyaki or nanoporetech/bonito instead of this assembly pipeline. Your data is not the public E. coli nanopore/short-read pair from the 2015 paper and you have not adapted the Makefile's ENA download and pinned software versions. You need a reimplementation of individual correction/assembly/polishing tools rather than a reproducible Makefile-driven run of the exact published pipeline.

skills.description: Use when a SeqCode command (e.g. scorePhastCons, produceTSSplots) requires the chromInfo, refGene, or a conservation track for a specific assembly (e.g. mouse mm9) that must first be downloaded and uncompressed from UCSC.
skills.name: genome-browser-track-retrieval
skills.search_text: genome-browser-track-retrieval Use when a SeqCode command (e.g. scorePhastCons, produceTSSplots) requires the chromInfo, refGene, or a conservation track for a specific assembly (e.g. mouse mm9) that must first be downloaded and uncompressed from UCSC. The analysis targets an organism or assembly for which UCSC does not distribute the required track (e.g. no phastCons track for the assembly) or the annotation is not RefSeq-based The input is already a processed per-region score or signal table — track retrieval is a pre-analysis data acquisition step, not a scoring or plotting step The workflow needs genome-wide profiles in bigWig format, which SeqCode does not support and defers to future versions http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Retrieve and prepare genome-assembly-specific reference files (chromosome size list, RefSeq refGene annotations, and tracks such as phastCons30way conservation) from the UCSC genome browser downloads so that SeqCode command-line applications can run on a chosen genome release. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Retrieve and prepare genome-assembly-specific reference files (chromosome size list, RefSeq refGene annotations, and tracks such as phastCons30way conservation) from the UCSC genome browser downloads so that SeqCode command-line applications can run on a chosen genome release.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets an organism or assembly for which UCSC does not distribute the required track (e.g. no phastCons track for the assembly) or the annotation is not RefSeq-based The input is already a processed per-region score or signal table — track retrieval is a pre-analysis data acquisition step, not a scoring or plotting step The workflow needs genome-wide profiles in bigWig format, which SeqCode does not support and defers to future versions

skills.description: Use when encoding enhancer DNA sequences (SEs/TEs) into dna2vec feature vectors and you must decide which pre-trained embedding matrix (human hg19 vs mouse mm9) corresponds to each cell-line dataset.
skills.name: genome-build-correspondence-human-mouse
skills.search_text: genome-build-correspondence-human-mouse Use when encoding enhancer DNA sequences (SEs/TEs) into dna2vec feature vectors and you must decide which pre-trained embedding matrix (human hg19 vs mouse mm9) corresponds to each cell-line dataset. The enhancer coordinates or sequences are already provided as an encoded feature/matrix table rather than raw FASTA sequences The target organism or genome build is neither human hg19 nor mouse mm9 and no pre-trained embedding matrix is available (a new dna2vec model would need to be trained first) The downstream task uses ChIP-seq or other non-sequence features rather than dna2vec sequence embeddings http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Matches each enhancer dataset to the correct genome build so pre-trained dna2vec k-mer embedding matrices are applied consistently: human cell lines use hg19 and mouse cell lines use mm9 when encoding SE/TE sequences in the DeepSE pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.ygeno.2021.10.007
skills.summary: Matches each enhancer dataset to the correct genome build so pre-trained dna2vec k-mer embedding matrices are applied consistently: human cell lines use hg19 and mouse cell lines use mm9 when encoding SE/TE sequences in the DeepSE pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The enhancer coordinates or sequences are already provided as an encoded feature/matrix table rather than raw FASTA sequences The target organism or genome build is neither human hg19 nor mouse mm9 and no pre-trained embedding matrix is available (a new dna2vec model would need to be trained first) The downstream task uses ChIP-seq or other non-sequence features rather than dna2vec sequence embeddings

skills.description: Use when multiple ChIP-seq samples with spike-in chromatin must be compared genome-wide and a common fixed-size bin grid (e.g. 1000-bp bins of hg19 and FLY-suffixed dm3 from ChromInfo.txt) is needed before per-bin counting and normalization.
skills.name: genome-chromosome-coordinate-segmentation
skills.search_text: genome-chromosome-coordinate-segmentation Use when multiple ChIP-seq samples with spike-in chromatin must be compared genome-wide and a common fixed-size bin grid (e.g. 1000-bp bins of hg19 and FLY-suffixed dm3 from ChromInfo.txt) is needed before per-bin counting and normalization. The analysis targets a pre-selected subset of loci or peak intervals rather than genome-wide binned signal — spikChIP normalizes over the complete genome and its bin grid is designed for that scope No ChromInfo chromosome-size file exists for the assembly, since spikChIP derives the binning grid directly from this list Downstream analysis already consumes a feature/count table at another resolution and does not need re-segmentation into fixed bins http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Segments the sample (e.g. hg19) and spike-in (e.g. dm3) genomes into fixed-size genomic bins (1000 bp in the H3K79me2 Jurkat series) driven by a ChromInfo chromosome list, creating the coordinate grid on which per-bin read counts and spikChIP normalization are computed. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Segments the sample (e.g. hg19) and spike-in (e.g. dm3) genomes into fixed-size genomic bins (1000 bp in the H3K79me2 Jurkat series) driven by a ChromInfo chromosome list, creating the coordinate grid on which per-bin read counts and spikChIP normalization are computed.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a pre-selected subset of loci or peak intervals rather than genome-wide binned signal — spikChIP normalizes over the complete genome and its bin grid is designed for that scope No ChromInfo chromosome-size file exists for the assembly, since spikChIP derives the binning grid directly from this list Downstream analysis already consumes a feature/count table at another resolution and does not need re-segmentation into fixed bins

skills.description: Use when preparing a reference genome (e.g., hg19/hg38, mm9/mm10 as multi-fasta or per-chromosome directory) before running Msuite alignment or the CT/GA-rich region benchmark, so converted indices exist for 3-letter or 4-letter TAPS/BS modes.
skills.name: genome-index-building
skills.search_text: genome-index-building Use when preparing a reference genome (e.g., hg19/hg38, mm9/mm10 as multi-fasta or per-chromosome directory) before running Msuite alignment or the CT/GA-rich region benchmark, so converted indices exist for 3-letter or 4-letter TAPS/BS modes. The reference genome or annotation is not yet in FASTA/RefSeq form (e.g., GFF/GTF-only annotation) — convert formats first You only intend to align with Bismark or BWA-meth without Msuite — those tools build their own bowtie2-based conversion indices You are re-running Msuite on an existing sample and an index for that Genome.ID already exists under the Msuite index directory http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Build Msuite-compatible genome indices from a reference FASTA and RefSeq annotation using build.index.sh, which converts cytosines (3- or 4-letter modes) and constructs separate Watson- and Crick-strand bowtie2 FM indices for DNA methylation read alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Build Msuite-compatible genome indices from a reference FASTA and RefSeq annotation using build.index.sh, which converts cytosines (3- or 4-letter modes) and constructs separate Watson- and Crick-strand bowtie2 FM indices for DNA methylation read alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The reference genome or annotation is not yet in FASTA/RefSeq form (e.g., GFF/GTF-only annotation) — convert formats first You only intend to align with Bismark or BWA-meth without Msuite — those tools build their own bowtie2-based conversion indices You are re-running Msuite on an existing sample and an index for that Genome.ID already exists under the Msuite index directory

skills.description: Use when aligning bisulfite-treated reads (e.g. WGBS FASTQ against hg19) with BiSpark, since the 'three-letter' aligner requires a pre-converted, Bowtie2-indexed reference stored in HDFS before alignment can start.
skills.name: genome-index-preparation-three-letter-conversion
skills.search_text: genome-index-preparation-three-letter-conversion Use when aligning bisulfite-treated reads (e.g. WGBS FASTQ against hg19) with BiSpark, since the 'three-letter' aligner requires a pre-converted, Bowtie2-indexed reference stored in HDFS before alignment can start. Using a single-node aligner such as Bismark that performs its own bisulfite conversions internally — this HDFS-based index preparation is specific to BiSpark. The reference genome is already provided as a pre-built bisulfite index from another tool; BiSpark's build_index performs its own four conversions and Bowtie2 indexing. Only simulating or benchmarking alignment timing where index construction must be excluded — build the index beforehand so runtime is measured only on the alignment phase. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Prepare a bisulfite-aware reference genome index for BiSpark by performing the four CT/GA conversions of the 'three-letter' algorithm and indexing with Bowtie2, then storing the converted index in HDFS for multi-node sharing across the Spark cluster. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2498-2
skills.summary: Prepare a bisulfite-aware reference genome index for BiSpark by performing the four CT/GA conversions of the 'three-letter' algorithm and indexing with Bowtie2, then storing the converted index in HDFS for multi-node sharing across the Spark cluster.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Using a single-node aligner such as Bismark that performs its own bisulfite conversions internally — this HDFS-based index preparation is specific to BiSpark. The reference genome is already provided as a pre-built bisulfite index from another tool; BiSpark's build_index performs its own four conversions and Bowtie2 indexing. Only simulating or benchmarking alignment timing where index construction must be excluded — build the index beforehand so runtime is measured only on the alignment phase.

skills.search_text: genome-tiling-chunk-overhang-configuration Use when preparing a ChIP-Seq count dataset for genome-wide GAM fitting with GenoGAM, i.e. when BAM alignments must be tiled into overlapping intervals of fixed chunkSize/overhangSize and written to an HDF5 backend.
