skills.name: genome-wide-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: genome-wide-correlation-analysis Use when you have CscoreTool-M *_cscore.txt outputs and a reference set of compartment/sub-compartment scores for the same 500kb hg38 windows and need a genome-wide Pearson correlation to judge inference accuracy or depth robustness. Input is raw Hi-C reads or an unprocessed HiCsummary file with no compartment scores yet inferred — run CscoreTool-M first before any correlation assessment Comparing scores across differently sized or non-matching genomic window sets (e.g. Rabl-positioned 500kb windows vs. another binning) where window-to-window correspondence is undefined Evaluating sub-compartment categorical assignments rather than continuous compartment scores — the correlation applies to score values, not label concordance http://edamontology.org/topic_3922 Quantifies agreement between CscoreTool-M re-inferred sub-compartment scores and a reference 5-compartment model by computing genome-wide Pearson correlations across genomic windows, e.g. across simulated Hi-C datasets at 1x, 0.1x, and 0.01x sequencing depth. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between CscoreTool-M re-inferred sub-compartment scores and a reference 5-compartment model by computing genome-wide Pearson correlations across genomic windows, e.g. across simulated Hi-C datasets at 1x, 0.1x, and 0.01x sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Hi-C reads or an unprocessed HiCsummary file with no compartment scores yet inferred — run CscoreTool-M first before any correlation assessment Comparing scores across differently sized or non-matching genomic window sets (e.g. Rabl-positioned 500kb windows vs. another binning) where window-to-window correspondence is undefined Evaluating sub-compartment categorical assignments rather than continuous compartment scores — the correlation applies to score values, not label concordance

skills.description: Use when reproducing or validating published genome-wide differential ChIP-seq region calls for broad histone marks (e.g., H3K9me3/H3K27me3) with histoneHMM and a quantitative target such as total differential Mb or genome fraction.
skills.name: genome-wide-differential-region-validation
skills.search_text: genome-wide-differential-region-validation Use when reproducing or validating published genome-wide differential ChIP-seq region calls for broad histone marks (e.g., H3K9me3/H3K27me3) with histoneHMM and a quantitative target such as total differential Mb or genome fraction. The histone mark produces sharp peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse modifications, where peak-calling methods are more appropriate The input is already a list of called regions or a feature table rather than replicate BAM alignments, so no binning/HMM fitting is needed Only a single-sample modification call is required, not a two-sample differential comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates genome-wide differential histone-modification region calls by reproducing a histoneHMM bivariate HMM run (e.g., H3K9me3 male vs female CD-1 mouse liver ChIP-seq from ENA SRP018808) and checking that the merged differential-region span reproduces the reported value (~121.89 Mb, 4.6% of the mouse genome). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Validates genome-wide differential histone-modification region calls by reproducing a histoneHMM bivariate HMM run (e.g., H3K9me3 male vs female CD-1 mouse liver ChIP-seq from ENA SRP018808) and checking that the merged differential-region span reproduces the reported value (~121.89 Mb, 4.6% of the mouse genome).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The histone mark produces sharp peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse modifications, where peak-calling methods are more appropriate The input is already a list of called regions or a feature table rather than replicate BAM alignments, so no binning/HMM fitting is needed Only a single-sample modification call is required, not a two-sample differential comparison

skills.description: Use when you need base-level smoothing and significance/peak calls for ChIP-Seq protein-DNA occupancy across whole chromosomes or gigabase-scale genomes (e.g., TF binding, genotype contrasts) without ad-hoc binning or windowing.
skills.name: genome-wide-gam-smoothing-fit
skills.search_text: genome-wide-gam-smoothing-fit Use when you need base-level smoothing and significance/peak calls for ChIP-Seq protein-DNA occupancy across whole chromosomes or gigabase-scale genomes (e.g., TF binding, genotype contrasts) without ad-hoc binning or windowing. Input is a gene- or region-level count table (e.g., an RNA-Seq expression matrix) rather than per-position ChIP-Seq counts — GenoGAM models read count frequencies as smooth functions along chromosomes. A quick exploratory fit on data lacking the factorial genotype/treatment structure assumed by the design ~ s(x) + s(x, by = genotype) — the fitting path and the s(x):genotype term interpretability depend on it. You only need alignment or read counting — this skill starts from aligned BAM files and an experiment design. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Fit genome-wide generalized additive models (GAMs) to ChIP-Seq read counts with GenoGAM 2.0: build an HDF5-backed GenoGAMDataSet, compute size factors, and fit smooth count functions per genomic tile (SuperLU sparse solver, mgcv framework) to obtain base-level fits, position-wise log p-values, and called peaks at gigabase scale. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Fit genome-wide generalized additive models (GAMs) to ChIP-Seq read counts with GenoGAM 2.0: build an HDF5-backed GenoGAMDataSet, compute size factors, and fit smooth count functions per genomic tile (SuperLU sparse solver, mgcv framework) to obtain base-level fits, position-wise log p-values, and called peaks at gigabase scale.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene- or region-level count table (e.g., an RNA-Seq expression matrix) rather than per-position ChIP-Seq counts — GenoGAM models read count frequencies as smooth functions along chromosomes. A quick exploratory fit on data lacking the factorial genotype/treatment structure assumed by the design ~ s(x) + s(x, by = genotype) — the fitting path and the s(x):genotype term interpretability depend on it. You only need alignment or read counting — this skill starts from aligned BAM files and an experiment design.

skills.description: Use when comparing TF binding site predictions from chromatin occupancy models (RoboCOP, COMPETE, MACS2+FIMO/FIMO baselines) against ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, or ORGANIC annotations to quantify and rank method accuracy.
skills.name: genome-wide-occupancy-profile-scoring
skills.search_text: genome-wide-occupancy-profile-scoring Use when comparing TF binding site predictions from chromatin occupancy models (RoboCOP, COMPETE, MACS2+FIMO/FIMO baselines) against ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, or ORGANIC annotations to quantify and rank method accuracy. The task is generating occupancy profiles themselves rather than scoring/benchmarking predictions against ChIP ground truth No ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, or ORGANIC ground truth annotations are available for the TFs being evaluated Predictions are from organisms or assays other than the yeast MNase-seq/ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility context supported by RoboCOP/COMPETE http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Benchmark genome-wide probabilistic TF binding site predictions (e.g. from RoboCOP, COMPETE, or MACS2+FIMO baselines) by ranking predicted sites per TF and computing AUPR against ChIP-chip/ChIP-exo/ORGANIC ground truth annotations, as done for the RoboCOP yeast chromatin occupancy profiles. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Benchmark genome-wide probabilistic TF binding site predictions (e.g. from RoboCOP, COMPETE, or MACS2+FIMO baselines) by ranking predicted sites per TF and computing AUPR against ChIP-chip/ChIP-exo/ORGANIC ground truth annotations, as done for the RoboCOP yeast chromatin occupancy profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is generating occupancy profiles themselves rather than scoring/benchmarking predictions against ChIP ground truth No ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, or ORGANIC ground truth annotations are available for the TFs being evaluated Predictions are from organisms or assays other than the yeast MNase-seq/ATAC-seq chromatin accessibility context supported by RoboCOP/COMPETE

skills.description: Use when filtered .bam/.bai alignments from a ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline must be converted into compressed genome-browser tracks (.wig/.bigwig) or compact GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis.
skills.name: genome-wide-signal-binning
skills.search_text: genome-wide-signal-binning Use when filtered .bam/.bai alignments from a ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline must be converted into compressed genome-browser tracks (.wig/.bigwig) or compact GRanges objects for visualization and downstream analysis. Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned reads — binning requires aligned, filtered .bam/.bai output from NEAT's 'map' and 'filter' modules. The goal is peak calling or ChIP-rx normalization rather than visualization tracks — use the 'peakcalling' or 'chiprx' modules instead. Input is already a browser track (.wig/.bigwig) or a GRanges object — re-binning would duplicate existing outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 NEAT's genome-track generation step bins filtered NGS alignments genome-wide into compressed small-size wiggle (.wig) and bigwig browser tracks plus compact R/Bioconductor GRanges objects, replacing multi-GB .bam files with easily shared small files. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: NEAT's genome-track generation step bins filtered NGS alignments genome-wide into compressed small-size wiggle (.wig) and bigwig browser tracks plus compact R/Bioconductor GRanges objects, replacing multi-GB .bam files with easily shared small files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned reads — binning requires aligned, filtered .bam/.bai output from NEAT's 'map' and 'filter' modules. The goal is peak calling or ChIP-rx normalization rather than visualization tracks — use the 'peakcalling' or 'chiprx' modules instead. Input is already a browser track (.wig/.bigwig) or a GRanges object — re-binning would duplicate existing outputs.

skills.description: Use when an in vitro trained TF affinity model (e.g. DNAffinity on gcPBM data for CBF1) must be applied genome-wide to predict in vivo binding sites and validated against exo peak calls.
skills.name: genome-wide-tfbs-prediction-scanning
skills.search_text: genome-wide-tfbs-prediction-scanning Use when an in vitro trained TF affinity model (e.g. DNAffinity on gcPBM data for CBF1) must be applied genome-wide to predict in vivo binding sites and validated against exo peak calls. The goal is to predict in vitro binding affinities from uPBM or HT-SELEX data — use upbm_regressor.py or selex_regressor.py pipelines instead of the gcPBM genome-wide scan No exo (ChIP-exo/PB-exo) peak data or nucleosome maps exist for the organism, so TP/FP validation and chromatin-structure correction cannot be performed The transcription factor of interest is not represented in the DNAffinity protein parameter database (no gcPBM training data and frequency matrix available) http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Scores transcription factor binding affinity genome-wide using the DNAffinity gcPBM-trained random forest regressor, thresholds the scores into a discrete TFBS map, and validates it against ChIP-exo (GSE44604) and PB-exo (GSE147927) peaks with nucleosome occupancy overlays. Demonstrated for CBF1 in S. cerevisiae, achieving >94% true positive rate and a ~7% real false positive rate. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Scores transcription factor binding affinity genome-wide using the DNAffinity gcPBM-trained random forest regressor, thresholds the scores into a discrete TFBS map, and validates it against ChIP-exo (GSE44604) and PB-exo (GSE147927) peaks with nucleosome occupancy overlays. Demonstrated for CBF1 in S. cerevisiae, achieving >94% true positive rate and a ~7% real false positive rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to predict in vitro binding affinities from uPBM or HT-SELEX data — use upbm_regressor.py or selex_regressor.py pipelines instead of the gcPBM genome-wide scan No exo (ChIP-exo/PB-exo) peak data or nucleosome maps exist for the organism, so TP/FP validation and chromatin-structure correction cannot be performed The transcription factor of interest is not represented in the DNAffinity protein parameter database (no gcPBM training data and frequency matrix available)

skills.description: Use when reproducing a DNALONGBENCH long-range task (eQTL, RSAP, TISP, contact map, enhancer-target gene) and raw bed-file data downloaded from a Dataverse DOI must be converted into train/valid/test loaders for model training and inference.
skills.name: genomic-bed-data-loading
skills.search_text: genomic-bed-data-loading Use when reproducing a DNALONGBENCH long-range task (eQTL, RSAP, TISP, contact map, enhancer-target gene) and raw bed-file data downloaded from a Dataverse DOI must be converted into train/valid/test loaders for model training and inference. The analysis targets a short-range DNA benchmark (e.g. Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE, BEND, LRB) rather than a DNALONGBENCH long-range task — the splits and tfr reformulation are specific to this benchmark. The model is a pretrained DNA foundation model used zero-shot for generation (e.g. GENERator sequence generation), which does not consume the supervised train/valid/test loaders. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Load DNALONGBENCH long-range genomic prediction task data (bed-file-derived eQTL, TISP, RSAP sets distributed via Dataverse DOIs) into train/valid/test PyTorch loaders using dnalongbench.utils.load_data, so that CNN, HyenaDNA, and Caduceus models can be fine-tuned and evaluated on the correct held-out splits. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Load DNALONGBENCH long-range genomic prediction task data (bed-file-derived eQTL, TISP, RSAP sets distributed via Dataverse DOIs) into train/valid/test PyTorch loaders using dnalongbench.utils.load_data, so that CNN, HyenaDNA, and Caduceus models can be fine-tuned and evaluated on the correct held-out splits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets a short-range DNA benchmark (e.g. Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE, BEND, LRB) rather than a DNALONGBENCH long-range task — the splits and tfr reformulation are specific to this benchmark. The model is a pretrained DNA foundation model used zero-shot for generation (e.g. GENERator sequence generation), which does not consume the supervised train/valid/test loaders.

skills.description: Use when strand-oriented genomic features (e.g. GENCODE v33 genes, PolyASite PAS clusters, UCSC tfbsConsSites TFBSs, JASPAR/FIMO motif tracks) must be converted into 4-column BED files before running Asymmetron asymmetry analyses.
skills.name: genomic-bed-file-strand-annotation
skills.search_text: genomic-bed-file-strand-annotation Use when strand-oriented genomic features (e.g. GENCODE v33 genes, PolyASite PAS clusters, UCSC tfbsConsSites TFBSs, JASPAR/FIMO motif tracks) must be converted into 4-column BED files before running Asymmetron asymmetry analyses. The feature is palindromic, so no biologically meaningful '+'/'-' orientation can be assigned (Asymmetron's asymmetries rely on non-palindromic orientation) The analysis goal is nucleotide-composition or mutation strand asymmetry computed from sequences rather than strand-assigned BED features The feature lacks strand annotation entirely and there is no overlapping oriented element to derive orientation from — that is the separate Asymmetron 'orientation' function's task http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Prepares strand-annotated BED files (chromosome, start, end, +/− strand) for DNA features such as TFBSs, polyadenylation signals, transposable elements and gene regions so they can be consumed by Asymmetron's consecutive, contained and pairwise strand-asymmetry functions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Prepares strand-annotated BED files (chromosome, start, end, +/− strand) for DNA features such as TFBSs, polyadenylation signals, transposable elements and gene regions so they can be consumed by Asymmetron's consecutive, contained and pairwise strand-asymmetry functions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature is palindromic, so no biologically meaningful '+'/'-' orientation can be assigned (Asymmetron's asymmetries rely on non-palindromic orientation) The analysis goal is nucleotide-composition or mutation strand asymmetry computed from sequences rather than strand-assigned BED features The feature lacks strand annotation entirely and there is no overlapping oriented element to derive orientation from — that is the separate Asymmetron 'orientation' function's task

skills.name: genomic-bin-assignment-from-chromosome-sizes
skills.search_text: genomic-bin-assignment-from-chromosome-sizes Use when a PET/interaction bedpe file must be aggregated into a fixed-bin (e.g. 10 kb) 2D contact map whose bin grid is bounded by a chromosome sizes file such as chrom_hg19.sizes. The goal is significant chromatin loop calling from peaks rather than a binned contact matrix — use the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Interaction module instead Input is already a dense or sparse contact matrix and only rendering/normalization is needed The bedpe coordinate genome build does not match the chromosome sizes file, so bin coordinates would be inconsistent http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Converts a PCR-duplicate-removed PET bedpe file into a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix by assigning each PET end to fixed-size genome bins defined by a tab-delimited chromosome sizes file, storing the result in the sparse triplet tuple format shared with HiC-Pro. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Converts a PCR-duplicate-removed PET bedpe file into a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix by assigning each PET end to fixed-size genome bins defined by a tab-delimited chromosome sizes file, storing the result in the sparse triplet tuple format shared with HiC-Pro.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is significant chromatin loop calling from peaks rather than a binned contact matrix — use the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Interaction module instead Input is already a dense or sparse contact matrix and only rendering/normalization is needed The bedpe coordinate genome build does not match the chromosome sizes file, so bin coordinates would be inconsistent

skills.description: Use when raw single-cell ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq reads (FASTQ→BAM/BED) or per-cell alignment files must be converted into a cell-by-region count matrix binned across the genome for downstream clustering.
skills.name: genomic-bin-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: genomic-bin-count-aggregation Use when raw single-cell ChIP-seq/ATAC-seq reads (FASTQ→BAM/BED) or per-cell alignment files must be converted into a cell-by-region count matrix binned across the genome for downstream clustering. Input is already a normalized feature table or reduced-dimension representation (e.g. PCA/t-SNE output) — no bin aggregation is needed. The goal is peak-level analysis requiring a user-supplied peak set but no BED peaks or BAM files are available (the peak-calling module requires one BAM per sample). Data are bulk ChIP-seq reads without single-cell barcodes — the 1600-read-per-cell and top-5%-coverage cell filters do not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Reconstructs ChromSCape's count-matrix generation from single-cell epigenomic inputs (gzipped single-cell BED/BAM files), aggregating signal into mark-dependent genomic bins (50 kbp for broad marks like H3K27me3, 5 kbp or gene TSS ±2500 bp using Gencode_hg38_v26 for sharp marks), then applying QC cell and region filters and normalizing by total read count and region size. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Reconstructs ChromSCape's count-matrix generation from single-cell epigenomic inputs (gzipped single-cell BED/BAM files), aggregating signal into mark-dependent genomic bins (50 kbp for broad marks like H3K27me3, 5 kbp or gene TSS ±2500 bp using Gencode_hg38_v26 for sharp marks), then applying QC cell and region filters and normalizing by total read count and region size.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized feature table or reduced-dimension representation (e.g. PCA/t-SNE output) — no bin aggregation is needed. The goal is peak-level analysis requiring a user-supplied peak set but no BED peaks or BAM files are available (the peak-calling module requires one BAM per sample). Data are bulk ChIP-seq reads without single-cell barcodes — the 1600-read-per-cell and top-5%-coverage cell filters do not apply.

skills.description: Use when you already have per-bin node embeddings from a GAE trained on 400×400 Hi-C submatrices and need an unsupervised cluster label per genomic bin to delineate TAD boundaries.
skills.name: genomic-bin-labeling
skills.search_text: genomic-bin-labeling Use when you already have per-bin node embeddings from a GAE trained on 400×400 Hi-C submatrices and need an unsupervised cluster label per genomic bin to delineate TAD boundaries. Input is raw Hi-C contact counts rather than trained GAE embeddings — clustering raw matrices is not what this skill does The goal is supervised bin classification with known labels; HDBSCAN here runs in unsupervised mode and cannot use ground-truth labels The analysis targets features other than genomic bins (e.g. EPI pair prediction in EPIANN), where per-bin TAD labeling is irrelevant http://edamontology.org/topic_3473 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Labels each genomic bin of a Hi-C contact matrix by running unsupervised HDBSCAN on the 16-dimensional graph auto-encoder (GAE) embeddings that TOAST derives from non-overlapping 400×400 submatrices; contiguous regions sharing a label (and longer than 200 Kb) become TADs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Labels each genomic bin of a Hi-C contact matrix by running unsupervised HDBSCAN on the 16-dimensional graph auto-encoder (GAE) embeddings that TOAST derives from non-overlapping 400×400 submatrices; contiguous regions sharing a label (and longer than 200 Kb) become TADs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Hi-C contact counts rather than trained GAE embeddings — clustering raw matrices is not what this skill does The goal is supervised bin classification with known labels; HDBSCAN here runs in unsupervised mode and cannot use ground-truth labels The analysis targets features other than genomic bins (e.g. EPI pair prediction in EPIANN), where per-bin TAD labeling is irrelevant

skills.description: Use when aligned ChIP-seq BAM files for experimental and spike-in genomes must be converted into genome-wide binned read-count tables (e.g. chromosome-start-end-count rows at 1-kbp resolution) before cross-condition normalization.
skills.name: genomic-bin-read-counting
skills.search_text: genomic-bin-read-counting Use when aligned ChIP-seq BAM files for experimental and spike-in genomes must be converted into genome-wide binned read-count tables (e.g. chromosome-start-end-count rows at 1-kbp resolution) before cross-condition normalization. Input is still raw FASTQ — reads must first be mapped with Bowtie (multi-locus reads discarded) and filtered with Samtools before bin counting The analysis goal is peak-level or per-gene quantification rather than genome-wide binned signal (e.g. differential binding on MACS2 peaks only) No reference chromosome-size file is available — the bin segmentation depends entirely on the ChromInfo.txt chromosome list http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Segments the sample (e.g. human hg19) and spike-in (e.g. fruit fly dm3 with 'FLY' suffix) genomes into non-overlapping 1-kbp bins and counts reads inside each bin (average and maximum values) with SeqCode, producing the per-bin count tables that spikChIP subsequently normalizes with RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAGREMOVAL and SPIKCHIP approaches. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Segments the sample (e.g. human hg19) and spike-in (e.g. fruit fly dm3 with 'FLY' suffix) genomes into non-overlapping 1-kbp bins and counts reads inside each bin (average and maximum values) with SeqCode, producing the per-bin count tables that spikChIP subsequently normalizes with RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAGREMOVAL and SPIKCHIP approaches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ — reads must first be mapped with Bowtie (multi-locus reads discarded) and filtered with Samtools before bin counting The analysis goal is peak-level or per-gene quantification rather than genome-wide binned signal (e.g. differential binding on MACS2 peaks only) No reference chromosome-size file is available — the bin segmentation depends entirely on the ChromInfo.txt chromosome list

skills.description: Use when preparing a spikChIP or similar spike-in ChIP-seq pipeline: before counting reads per bin or classifying bins as peaks/background, the sample and spike-in genomes must be divided into fixed-size bins from a ChromInfo chromosome list.
skills.name: genomic-bin-segmentation
skills.search_text: genomic-bin-segmentation Use when preparing a spikChIP or similar spike-in ChIP-seq pipeline: before counting reads per bin or classifying bins as peaks/background, the sample and spike-in genomes must be divided into fixed-size bins from a ChromInfo chromosome list. When analysis targets only a pre-defined subset of loci or already-provided peak intervals rather than the complete genome — spikChIP normalization is genome-wide over bins When peaks themselves define the analysis units directly and no per-bin read counting is needed downstream When the genome assemblies lack a complete ChromInfo chromosome length list, since bins follow the declared chromosome names and sizes http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Segmentation of the sample (e.g. hg19 human) and spike-in (e.g. dm3 fly) genomes into fixed-size bins (default 1,000 bp, tunable via the -k option of spikChIP) using the chromosome name/length list in ChromInfo.txt, so that ChIP-seq reads and MACS2-called peaks can be assigned per-bin in downstream normalization. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Segmentation of the sample (e.g. hg19 human) and spike-in (e.g. dm3 fly) genomes into fixed-size bins (default 1,000 bp, tunable via the -k option of spikChIP) using the chromosome name/length list in ChromInfo.txt, so that ChIP-seq reads and MACS2-called peaks can be assigned per-bin in downstream normalization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When analysis targets only a pre-defined subset of loci or already-provided peak intervals rather than the complete genome — spikChIP normalization is genome-wide over bins When peaks themselves define the analysis units directly and no per-bin read counting is needed downstream When the genome assemblies lack a complete ChromInfo chromosome length list, since bins follow the declared chromosome names and sizes

skills.description: Use when preparing BAM/Bed ChIP-seq alignments of broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) as fixed-width binned read counts before HMM-based modification or differential-modification calling.
skills.name: genomic-binning-read-counting
skills.search_text: genomic-binning-read-counting Use when preparing BAM/Bed ChIP-seq alignments of broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) as fixed-width binned read counts before HMM-based modification or differential-modification calling. Analyzing sharp, peak-like histone marks or transcription-factor ChIP-seq where peak-calling on individual fragments is appropriate rather than broad-footprint bin aggregation Input is already a binned count table or feature-level count matrix that does not need genome partitioning Experiments requiring base-pair resolution signal tracks rather than 1000 bp fixed-width enrichment classification http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Partitions a genome into equally sized bins (1000 bp default) and aggregates ChIP-seq short-read counts per bin, producing the binned bivariate read-count table that histoneHMM uses for its Hidden Markov Model classification. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Partitions a genome into equally sized bins (1000 bp default) and aggregates ChIP-seq short-read counts per bin, producing the binned bivariate read-count table that histoneHMM uses for its Hidden Markov Model classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing sharp, peak-like histone marks or transcription-factor ChIP-seq where peak-calling on individual fragments is appropriate rather than broad-footprint bin aggregation Input is already a binned count table or feature-level count matrix that does not need genome partitioning Experiments requiring base-pair resolution signal tracks rather than 1000 bp fixed-width enrichment classification

skills.description: Use when building a DiffBind workflow on ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq peaks (e.g., mouse/mm10 cKO-vs-WT samples) before counting reads over consensus peaks, to exclude ENCODE blacklist artifact regions from downstream DAR generation.
skills.name: genomic-blacklist-filtering
skills.search_text: genomic-blacklist-filtering Use when building a DiffBind workflow on ATAC-seq or ChIP-seq peaks (e.g., mouse/mm10 cKO-vs-WT samples) before counting reads over consensus peaks, to exclude ENCODE blacklist artifact regions from downstream DAR generation. The peak data are on a different genome build than the blacklist constant (e.g., hg38 data with DBA_BLACKLIST_MM10) — use the matching blacklist instead The input is already a finalized DAR report or BED file; blacklist removal must occur upstream, before dba.count and differential analysis Working outside DiffBind (e.g., single-cell ArchR sgRNA pipelines), where blacklist handling follows a different tool-specific mechanism http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Removes ENCODE blacklist regions from a peak set during differential accessibility analysis in DiffBind, so that artifact-prone genomic loci (e.g., centromeric and high-signal mm10 regions) do not contaminate the differentially accessible region (DAR) set used as input to BIT. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Removes ENCODE blacklist regions from a peak set during differential accessibility analysis in DiffBind, so that artifact-prone genomic loci (e.g., centromeric and high-signal mm10 regions) do not contaminate the differentially accessible region (DAR) set used as input to BIT.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak data are on a different genome build than the blacklist constant (e.g., hg38 data with DBA_BLACKLIST_MM10) — use the matching blacklist instead The input is already a finalized DAR report or BED file; blacklist removal must occur upstream, before dba.count and differential analysis Working outside DiffBind (e.g., single-cell ArchR sgRNA pipelines), where blacklist handling follows a different tool-specific mechanism

skills.description: Use when preparing narrowPeak/BED peak files (ChIP-seq, CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ATAC-seq, DNase-seq) for cross-dataset comparison or QC, so that artifactual peaks in ENCODE blacklisted regions (hg19/hg38) do not bias overlap statistics, correlation plots, or ChromHMM/ChIPseeker annotations.

Your peaks are on a non-human genome (mouse, fly, etc.) — EpiCompare's bundled blacklists are human hg19/hg38 only You are performing raw signal/fragment-level QC (e.g. Picard duplication-rate inspection) rather than peak-level comparisons, where blacklist filtering is not the primary step http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 A QC preprocessing step in EpiCompare that removes peak regions overlapping ENCODE blacklisted genomic regions and peaks on non-standard chromosomes (e.g. chrUn, alt contigs) from each peak file before any overlap, correlation, or functional-annotation analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049

skills.description: Use when validating a coordinate-level genome-wide prediction (e.g. called nucleosome dyads) against high-precision reference annotations, and you need a distance-thresholded precision-recall curve.
skills.name: genomic-coordinate-distance-matching
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-distance-matching Use when validating a coordinate-level genome-wide prediction (e.g. called nucleosome dyads) against high-precision reference annotations, and you need a distance-thresholded precision-recall curve. Input predictions are not coordinate-level calls (e.g. only continuous occupancy scores without extracted dyad positions) — the method requires discrete coordinates to distance-match against reference dyads. No high-precision reference annotations exist for the organism; the ground truth here is specifically the chemical cleavage (Brogaard et al.) dyad set for S. cerevisiae. Evaluating TF binding site predictions rather than nucleosome positioning — those are validated against ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, and ORGANIC annotations instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A validation procedure that matches predicted genomic coordinates (e.g. RoboCOP_MNase nucleosome dyads) to ground-truth annotations by genomic distance, counting a prediction as a true positive only when it falls within a fixed bp window of a reference coordinate, then computing precision and recall. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: A validation procedure that matches predicted genomic coordinates (e.g. RoboCOP_MNase nucleosome dyads) to ground-truth annotations by genomic distance, counting a prediction as a true positive only when it falls within a fixed bp window of a reference coordinate, then computing precision and recall.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input predictions are not coordinate-level calls (e.g. only continuous occupancy scores without extracted dyad positions) — the method requires discrete coordinates to distance-match against reference dyads. No high-precision reference annotations exist for the organism; the ground truth here is specifically the chemical cleavage (Brogaard et al.) dyad set for S. cerevisiae. Evaluating TF binding site predictions rather than nucleosome positioning — those are validated against ChIP-chip, ChIP-exo, and ORGANIC annotations instead.

skills.name: genomic-coordinate-sorting
skills.search_text: genomic-coordinate-sorting Use when a fragment file produced by ExtractHair (modified from HapCUT2) must be sorted consistently with VCF variant order before SpecHap linkage-graph construction or haplotype phasing. The fragment file is already confirmed sorted consistently with the VCF order — re-sorting adds no information and risks reordering new-format fragment blocks incorrectly. The goal is haplotype assembly itself (allele partitioning via the Fiedler Vector) rather than input-order normalization — use the SpecHap phasing workflow instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Position-sorts fragment files so that genomic coordinates follow the same variant ordering as the VCF, a prerequisite for SpecHap's linkage-graph construction, where nodes are heterozygous loci and edges carry truncated log-likelihood-ratio weights. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Position-sorts fragment files so that genomic coordinates follow the same variant ordering as the VCF, a prerequisite for SpecHap's linkage-graph construction, where nodes are heterozygous loci and edges carry truncated log-likelihood-ratio weights.

skills.description: Use when integrating epigenomic p-values (e.g., DNA methylation) whose assay sites are spatially non-independent, and you need to quantify or visualize how correlation between adjacent CpG p-values decays with genomic distance before combining p-values.
skills.name: genomic-correlation-decay-visualization
skills.search_text: genomic-correlation-decay-visualization Use when integrating epigenomic p-values (e.g., DNA methylation) whose assay sites are spatially non-independent, and you need to quantify or visualize how correlation between adjacent CpG p-values decays with genomic distance before combining p-values. The input data are independent p-values with no spatial/genomic adjacency structure — the correlation decay estimate has no meaning The goal is module identification or network scoring rather than characterizing the correlation structure of the input p-values Methylation data have already been processed into a correlation-corrected combined score by SMITE (annotateModification with mod_corr=TRUE already run) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reproduces SMITE's Monte Carlo estimation of the average Pearson correlation between adjacent DNA methylation p-values, tabulated in genomic distance bins, and visualizes how that correlation decays with increasing CpG-to-CpG distance in the T. gondii HFF dataset. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Reproduces SMITE's Monte Carlo estimation of the average Pearson correlation between adjacent DNA methylation p-values, tabulated in genomic distance bins, and visualizes how that correlation decays with increasing CpG-to-CpG distance in the T. gondii HFF dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input data are independent p-values with no spatial/genomic adjacency structure — the correlation decay estimate has no meaning The goal is module identification or network scoring rather than characterizing the correlation structure of the input p-values Methylation data have already been processed into a correlation-corrected combined score by SMITE (annotateModification with mod_corr=TRUE already run)

skills.search_text: genomic-count-matrix-construction Use when raw ChIP-Seq BAM alignments plus an experiment design file must be converted into a tiled, normalized count matrix too large for memory, as preprocessing before GAM model fitting. Data are already a normalized count matrix or feature table and only model fitting (genogam()) or significance testing is needed The dataset is small enough to fit in memory and HDF5 out-of-core overhead is unnecessary (e.g. MulticoreParam suffices for yeast-scale data) The analysis requires peak calling rather than smooth-function modeling of count frequencies along chromosomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Builds an out-of-core, HDF5-backed genomic count matrix from raw ChIP-Seq BAM alignments using GenoGAM 2.0: reads are converted to per-position counts, split into genomic tiles (chunkSize/overhangSize), and DESeq2-style size factors are attached for sequencing-depth normalization. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Builds an out-of-core, HDF5-backed genomic count matrix from raw ChIP-Seq BAM alignments using GenoGAM 2.0: reads are converted to per-position counts, split into genomic tiles (chunkSize/overhangSize), and DESeq2-style size factors are attached for sequencing-depth normalization.

skills.summary: Generates single-nucleotide-resolution 1-D genomic count tracks from paired-end chromatin accessibility fragment alignments by partitioning fragments into nucleosomal and subnucleosomal classes and aggregating their midpoint counts, producing the multivariate observables consumed by RoboCOP's HMM.

Input is raw or coverage-normalized contact data that has not yet passed covNormRpkg::normDistance, since the Weibull null must be fit on distance-normalized values Inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions, since covNorm's significance calling here focuses on cis-interactions only Contacts already carrying significance calls from a different null model (e.g. Fit-Hi-C or Mango output) that would be mixed with p_result_dist/FDR_dist_res columns http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Call statistically significant chromatin contacts from distance-normalized Hi-C/capture Hi-C data by fitting a three-parameter Weibull null distribution to the genomic-distance-dependent background and computing per-contact p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, as implemented in covNorm's contactPval step. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Call statistically significant chromatin contacts from distance-normalized Hi-C/capture Hi-C data by fitting a three-parameter Weibull null distribution to the genomic-distance-dependent background and computing per-contact p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, as implemented in covNorm's contactPval step.

skills.description: Use when calling broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains (e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb) and you must convert multi-scale coarse-grained '1' blocks into precisely bounded candidate domains prior to Poisson/FDR significance assessment.
skills.name: genomic-domain-boundary-refinement
skills.search_text: genomic-domain-boundary-refinement Use when calling broad ChIP-seq enrichment domains (e.g., H3K27me3/H3K9me3, kb-to-Mb) and you must convert multi-scale coarse-grained '1' blocks into precisely bounded candidate domains prior to Poisson/FDR significance assessment. Sharp, punctuate transcription-factor ChIP-seq peaks are the target — RECOGNICER is designed for broad domains (kb–Mb) like H3K27me3/H3K9me3, not local point-source peak calling Two biologically distinct domains separated by fine-scale gaps must be kept strictly separate — coarse-graining can falsely merge them into one coarse-scale domain Parallel RECOGNICER runs from the same directory are needed — hard-coded temporary file names make concurrent instances from one directory interfere and produce absurd outcomes http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 RECOGNICER's domain retrieval and boundary determination step: after recursive L=3 block-transform coarse-graining, fine-scale '1' blocks are clustered under coarse-scale '1' blocks and candidate broad-domain boundaries are shrunk/expanded, merged, and gap-closed before significance testing. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: RECOGNICER's domain retrieval and boundary determination step: after recursive L=3 block-transform coarse-graining, fine-scale '1' blocks are clustered under coarse-scale '1' blocks and candidate broad-domain boundaries are shrunk/expanded, merged, and gap-closed before significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sharp, punctuate transcription-factor ChIP-seq peaks are the target — RECOGNICER is designed for broad domains (kb–Mb) like H3K27me3/H3K9me3, not local point-source peak calling Two biologically distinct domains separated by fine-scale gaps must be kept strictly separate — coarse-graining can falsely merge them into one coarse-scale domain Parallel RECOGNICER runs from the same directory are needed — hard-coded temporary file names make concurrent instances from one directory interfere and produce absurd outcomes

skills.summary: Quantifies epigenomic annotation coverage of chromosome clusters by intersecting BHi-Cect enclave loci with tracks (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1) and normalizing overlap counts per enclave. skills.search_text: genomic-interval-promoter-assignment Use when you have a set of ChIP-seq peak intervals (e.g., MACs2 output for two regulators) plus RNA-seq differential expression calls, and you need to assign peaks to promoters/ORFs and count co-regulated, co-occupied loci. skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a DTW-based clustering/alignment of epigenomic peak regions has sharpened the positions of annotated genomic landmarks (TSS, FSS) within each cluster.
skills.name: genomic-landmark-position-histogramming
skills.search_text: genomic-landmark-position-histogramming Use when evaluating whether a DTW-based clustering/alignment of epigenomic peak regions has sharpened the positions of annotated genomic landmarks (TSS, FSS) within each cluster. Regions where the landmark positions are not fully contained — only regions where all POI points overlap completely with the main region are valid for matching Peaks excluded by the DGW filters (length < 5 or > 1000 bins, fewer than 10 counts, or no bin with more than 10 reads) — the POI statistics would not reflect the clustered data When the goal is landmark-free unsupervised alignment quality assessment rather than validation against annotated genomic features Overlay points of interest (e.g. transcription start sites, first splice sites) on DGW-explorer cluster heat-maps and build per-cluster position histograms of these landmarks before and after DTW warping to quantify alignment quality. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Overlay points of interest (e.g. transcription start sites, first splice sites) on DGW-explorer cluster heat-maps and build per-cluster position histograms of these landmarks before and after DTW warping to quantify alignment quality.

skills.description: Use when running SnapHiC (or similar loop-calling pipelines) on scHi-C/sn-m3C-seq contact files and you must restrict loop candidate calling to bins with adequate mappability, excluding ENCODE blacklist overlaps.
skills.name: genomic-mappability-and-blacklist-filtering
skills.search_text: genomic-mappability-and-blacklist-filtering Use when running SnapHiC (or similar loop-calling pipelines) on scHi-C/sn-m3C-seq contact files and you must restrict loop candidate calling to bins with adequate mappability, excluding ENCODE blacklist overlaps. Your analysis is not bin-based Hi-C loop calling — e.g., RNA-seq quantification or 3D genome reconstruction with Dip-C, where blacklist filtering serves a different purpose and must be applied separately Your bin resolution or restriction enzyme differs from the provided files (e.g., not 10-kb with MboI) and you have not downloaded the matching mappability features — reusing mismatched filter files would exclude the wrong bins The genome build of the contact files does not match the filter file's build (mm10 vs hg19 vs hg38), which would misalign exclusions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Excludes low-mappability genomic bins and ENCODE blacklist regions from single-cell Hi-C loop calling by supplying a pre-binned filter-regions BED file (e.g., 10-kb bins with mappability <=0.8 under the MboI restriction enzyme) to SnapHiC, preventing spurious loop candidates in poorly mappable or artifact-prone regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Excludes low-mappability genomic bins and ENCODE blacklist regions from single-cell Hi-C loop calling by supplying a pre-binned filter-regions BED file (e.g., 10-kb bins with mappability <=0.8 under the MboI restriction enzyme) to SnapHiC, preventing spurious loop candidates in poorly mappable or artifact-prone regions.

skills.description: Use when a raw numeric expression/methylation matrix destined for cola consensus partitioning contains missing values, extreme outliers, or rows with very small variance that would distort row-wise scaling and feature selection.
skills.name: genomic-matrix-missing-value-filtering
skills.search_text: genomic-matrix-missing-value-filtering Use when a raw numeric expression/methylation matrix destined for cola consensus partitioning contains missing values, extreme outliers, or rows with very small variance that would distort row-wise scaling and feature selection. The matrix is already fully preprocessed (no NAs, rows already variance-filtered) — re-running winsorization and variance filtering would drop informative rows and clamp true extremes. The analysis goal is dataset-specific sample/cell QC rather than matrix preprocessing — e.g., removing cells with <2 million reads or non-protein-coding genes in the MCF10CA scRNA-Seq workflow, which uses different per-dataset filter steps. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Sequentially cleans a numeric genomic data matrix (genes x samples) via cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: remove rows with >25% missing values, kNN-impute remaining NAs, winsorize at the 5th/95th percentiles, and drop zero-variance and low-variance (below the 5th variance percentile) rows. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: Sequentially cleans a numeric genomic data matrix (genes x samples) via cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: remove rows with >25% missing values, kNN-impute remaining NAs, winsorize at the 5th/95th percentiles, and drop zero-variance and low-variance (below the 5th variance percentile) rows.

skills.description: Use when testing enrichment or correlation of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTL peaks vs GWAS SNPs, DEG vs differential accessibility peaks, CRE-gene correlations across pseudo-bulk cell types) against a null and conventional shuffling is at risk of an overly narrow null distribution.
skills.name: genomic-range-block-bootstrap
skills.search_text: genomic-range-block-bootstrap Use when testing enrichment or correlation of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTL peaks vs GWAS SNPs, DEG vs differential accessibility peaks, CRE-gene correlations across pseudo-bulk cell types) against a null and conventional shuffling is at risk of an overly narrow null distribution. When the hypothesis test tolerates an unsegmented, exchangeable null — conventional shuffling (bootstrap.R) is what the paper compares against, and it is faster though it over-estimates significance (z=18.5 vs ~4) When inputs are not genomic ranges with a genome segmentation available — segmented block bootstrap requires a GRanges partition to sample blocks within matching segmentation states When comparing running time on genome-scale statistics against GSC is the goal — that is a separate benchmark (bootranges_vs_GSC.R), not the bootstrap itself http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates null sets of genomic ranges via segmented block bootstrap (bootRanges in the R/Bioconductor package nullranges), sampling blocks of length Lb within genome-segmentation states so that null ranges preserve local genomic correlation structure and yield more reliable null distributions than shuffling or permutation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Generates null sets of genomic ranges via segmented block bootstrap (bootRanges in the R/Bioconductor package nullranges), sampling blocks of length Lb within genome-segmentation states so that null ranges preserve local genomic correlation structure and yield more reliable null distributions than shuffling or permutation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the hypothesis test tolerates an unsegmented, exchangeable null — conventional shuffling (bootstrap.R) is what the paper compares against, and it is faster though it over-estimates significance (z=18.5 vs ~4) When inputs are not genomic ranges with a genome segmentation available — segmented block bootstrap requires a GRanges partition to sample blocks within matching segmentation states When comparing running time on genome-scale statistics against GSC is the goal — that is a separate benchmark (bootranges_vs_GSC.R), not the bootstrap itself

skills.search_text: genomic-range-enrichment-analysis Use when testing enrichment of overlaps between genomic range sets (e.g. caQTL SNPs vs chromatin accessibility peaks, or DEGs vs DA peaks) and when permutation-based nulls seem too narrow or thresholds need optimization. When the analysis goal is a simple single overlap P-value rather than a null-distribution comparison or threshold optimization — a plain permutation test may suffice, though it risks over-estimating significance. When range sets lack genomic coordinates or cannot be represented as GRanges objects. When testing mean correlations across cell types from Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression data (multiomicsCor.R), which is a distinct analysis in the same paper. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Applies bootRanges block bootstrapping of genomic ranges to compute null distributions of overlap statistics for enrichment testing, and fits penalized splines to recover optimized significance thresholds (e.g. SNP -log10(P) > 8, gene |logFC| > 2). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190

skills.search_text: genomic-range-overlap-statistics Use when testing whether an observed overlap between two genomic range sets (e.g. caQTL/SNP sets and peaks, or CREs and genes) is significant relative to a null that accounts for genomic structure, using GRanges objects in R/Bioconductor.
