skills.name: hic-compartment-score-quantile-normalization-across-replicates
skills.search_text: hic-compartment-score-quantile-normalization-across-replicates Use when comparing Hi-C compartment scores (e.g., PC1 at 100 kb bins) across two or more conditions or replicates (e.g., mouse ESC vs NPC) so scores are on a common scale before significance testing. A single Hi-C map is being analyzed with no cross-map or cross-replicate comparison — plain PCA per map suffices and quantile normalization across maps is meaningless Single-cell Hi-C maps are used without pseudo-bulk aggregation — sparsity of single-cell contact maps makes per-cell compartment scores unreliable (dcHiC instead uses pseudo-bulk profiles from ~100 cells per condition) The goal is differential loop/contact detection rather than compartmentalization — Fit-Hi-C-based differential interaction analysis is the appropriate tool http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 dcHiC's two-step procedure for making compartment scores comparable across multiple Hi-C maps: after computing PC1 scores via distance-normalized correlation matrices and a parallelized partial SVD (Filebacked Big Matrix), quantile normalization is applied across all input maps/replicates so that downstream multivariate differential testing (Mahalanobis distance) is valid. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: dcHiC's two-step procedure for making compartment scores comparable across multiple Hi-C maps: after computing PC1 scores via distance-normalized correlation matrices and a parallelized partial SVD (Filebacked Big Matrix), quantile normalization is applied across all input maps/replicates so that downstream multivariate differential testing (Mahalanobis distance) is valid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A single Hi-C map is being analyzed with no cross-map or cross-replicate comparison — plain PCA per map suffices and quantile normalization across maps is meaningless Single-cell Hi-C maps are used without pseudo-bulk aggregation — sparsity of single-cell contact maps makes per-cell compartment scores unreliable (dcHiC instead uses pseudo-bulk profiles from ~100 cells per condition) The goal is differential loop/contact detection rather than compartmentalization — Fit-Hi-C-based differential interaction analysis is the appropriate tool

skills.description: Use when you have replicated pairwise Hi-C contact maps (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb) with known full-depth dcHiC calls and need to determine the minimum sequencing depth at which differential compartments remain recoverable.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-downsampling
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-downsampling Use when you have replicated pairwise Hi-C contact maps (e.g., ESC vs NPC at 100 kb) with known full-depth dcHiC calls and need to determine the minimum sequencing depth at which differential compartments remain recoverable. Input consists of single-cell Hi-C maps without pseudo-bulk aggregation — the paper notes compartment identification is limited by sparsity of single-cell contact maps, making down-sampling recall curves ill-defined You lack a full-depth reference call set; recall cannot be computed without the full-depth differential bins Analysis target is differential loops or interactions (Fit-Hi-C output) rather than compartment calls — down-sampling effects on contacts are a different question http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Systematically down-samples Hi-C replicates to fractions of their original sequencing depth and re-runs dcHiC's differential compartment pipeline to quantify how many significant compartment calls are retained (recall) as depth decreases. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Systematically down-samples Hi-C replicates to fractions of their original sequencing depth and re-runs dcHiC's differential compartment pipeline to quantify how many significant compartment calls are retained (recall) as depth decreases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input consists of single-cell Hi-C maps without pseudo-bulk aggregation — the paper notes compartment identification is limited by sparsity of single-cell contact maps, making down-sampling recall curves ill-defined You lack a full-depth reference call set; recall cannot be computed without the full-depth differential bins Analysis target is differential loops or interactions (Fit-Hi-C output) rather than compartment calls — down-sampling effects on contacts are a different question

skills.description: Use when a deeply sequenced Hi-C dataset must be reduced to controlled sequencing-depth levels to test how data depth affects a structure-prediction or interaction-detection model.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-downsampling-and-realignment
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-downsampling-and-realignment Use when a deeply sequenced Hi-C dataset must be reduced to controlled sequencing-depth levels to test how data depth affects a structure-prediction or interaction-detection model. Input Hi-C data is already low-depth or low-resolution — deepC with chromatin-feature pre-seeding is designed to 'predict intricate chromatin interactions even when trained on low depth, low resolution Hi-C data', so no controlled downsampling is needed The goal is benchmarking deepC against alternative models (e.g. Akita) — the paper explicitly defers such comparison to future work The task is TAD identification from raw Hi-C (e.g. TopDom domain calling) rather than sequence-based interaction prediction Subsamples deeply sequenced Hi-C data (e.g. GM12878 from GSE63525) to defined valid-contact depths (1 billion, 100 million, 10 million) and realigns/prepares contact matrices with HiC-Pro, so that deepC models can be retrained on lower-depth data to test whether chromatin structure is still learnable. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Subsamples deeply sequenced Hi-C data (e.g. GM12878 from GSE63525) to defined valid-contact depths (1 billion, 100 million, 10 million) and realigns/prepares contact matrices with HiC-Pro, so that deepC models can be retrained on lower-depth data to test whether chromatin structure is still learnable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C data is already low-depth or low-resolution — deepC with chromatin-feature pre-seeding is designed to 'predict intricate chromatin interactions even when trained on low depth, low resolution Hi-C data', so no controlled downsampling is needed The goal is benchmarking deepC against alternative models (e.g. Akita) — the paper explicitly defers such comparison to future work The task is TAD identification from raw Hi-C (e.g. TopDom domain calling) rather than sequence-based interaction prediction

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C contact maps (.cool files or Juicer dump text) must be loaded, KR-normalized, converted to O/E matrices, and sequencedepth-aligned before patch sampling or loop calling.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-loading-and-normalization
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-loading-and-normalization Use when raw Hi-C contact maps (.cool files or Juicer dump text) must be loaded, KR-normalized, converted to O/E matrices, and sequencedepth-aligned before patch sampling or loop calling. Input is already a KR-normalized O/E matrix from a Juicer dump — use the processed-data path (demo_from_processed.py) and skip preprocessing entirely Data is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the paper states the tool 'is still not capable enough to deal with' it Only the downstream model branch is needed and the input matrix will be consumed directly by the GCN in 'lazy' non-downsampling mode Loads Hi-C intra-chromosomal (cis) contact maps from .cool files or Juicer dump text, aligns sequencing depth, and produces KR-normalized O/E matrices that GILoop then tiles into paired image and graph training patches. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Loads Hi-C intra-chromosomal (cis) contact maps from .cool files or Juicer dump text, aligns sequencing depth, and produces KR-normalized O/E matrices that GILoop then tiles into paired image and graph training patches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a KR-normalized O/E matrix from a Juicer dump — use the processed-data path (demo_from_processed.py) and skip preprocessing entirely Data is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the paper states the tool 'is still not capable enough to deal with' it Only the downstream model branch is needed and the input matrix will be consumed directly by the GCN in 'lazy' non-downsampling mode

skills.description: Use when you have a .cool/.hic genome-wide contact map at ~10 kb resolution plus a bedpe positive training set from an orthogonal assay (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need supervised chromatin loop predictions.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-loop-prediction
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-loop-prediction Use when you have a .cool/.hic genome-wide contact map at ~10 kb resolution plus a bedpe positive training set from an orthogonal assay (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need supervised chromatin loop predictions. When no orthogonal positive interaction data (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) is available to define the training set — although ~200 manually annotated loops were shown sufficient, no positive set means no supervised model When the goal is generic statistical enrichment calling rather than supervised classification — enrichment tools like HiCCUPS or Fit-Hi-C may be more appropriate When interactions are below the 6-bin lower distance bound or above the 300-bin upper bound (default score_chromosome distance limits) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Predict genome-wide chromatin loops from a Hi-C contact map by training Peakachu random forest models on an orthogonal positive interaction set (e.g. CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe), scoring every 10 kb pixel, and pooling probabilities into non-redundant loop calls. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Predict genome-wide chromatin loops from a Hi-C contact map by training Peakachu random forest models on an orthogonal positive interaction set (e.g. CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe), scoring every 10 kb pixel, and pooling probabilities into non-redundant loop calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no orthogonal positive interaction data (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) is available to define the training set — although ~200 manually annotated loops were shown sufficient, no positive set means no supervised model When the goal is generic statistical enrichment calling rather than supervised classification — enrichment tools like HiCCUPS or Fit-Hi-C may be more appropriate When interactions are below the 6-bin lower distance bound or above the 300-bin upper bound (default score_chromosome distance limits)

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C contact frequency matrices (e.g. KR-normalized 5 kb bins) must be converted into distance-aware, percentile-binned skeleton labels to train or run inference with deepC.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-percentile-normalization
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-percentile-normalization Use when raw Hi-C contact frequency matrices (e.g. KR-normalized 5 kb bins) must be converted into distance-aware, percentile-binned skeleton labels to train or run inference with deepC. Input is not Hi-C contact data (e.g. ChIP-seq tracks, sequence FASTA) — the skeleton scheme is defined only over distance-stratified contact frequencies The contact maps are not KR-normalized or are at a different bin resolution than 5 kb — percentile classes would not match the deepC training distribution A continuous-valued interaction target is needed (e.g. for regression models like Akita) rather than deepC's discrete 10-class skeleton Computes the deepC 'skeleton' by percentile-normalizing KR-normalized 5 kb Hi-C contact maps stratified by genomic distance, yielding discrete 1–10 interaction classes used as training targets for sequence-based chromatin interaction prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Computes the deepC 'skeleton' by percentile-normalizing KR-normalized 5 kb Hi-C contact maps stratified by genomic distance, yielding discrete 1–10 interaction classes used as training targets for sequence-based chromatin interaction prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not Hi-C contact data (e.g. ChIP-seq tracks, sequence FASTA) — the skeleton scheme is defined only over distance-stratified contact frequencies The contact maps are not KR-normalized or are at a different bin resolution than 5 kb — percentile classes would not match the deepC training distribution A continuous-valued interaction target is needed (e.g. for regression models like Akita) rather than deepC's discrete 10-class skeleton

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C matrices from new cell types must be reformatted into the DNALONGBENCH/Akita 448x448 contact map .tfr format so that load_data(task_name='contact_map_prediction') can consume them.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-preprocessing
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-preprocessing Use when raw Hi-C matrices from new cell types must be reformatted into the DNALONGBENCH/Akita 448x448 contact map .tfr format so that load_data(task_name='contact_map_prediction') can consume them. The cell line already has .tfr files shipped with DNALONGBENCH (e.g., the HFF subset) — no reprocessing is needed, just load directly. The prediction task is not contact map prediction (e.g., enhancer-target gene or eQTL tasks), which use different input lengths (450,000 bp) and output shapes than the 448x448 contact maps. Extends the DNALONGBENCH contact map prediction task beyond its five primary cell lines (HFF, H1hESC, GM12878, IMR90, HCT116) by downloading raw 4DN Hi-C data for additional cell lines (e.g., HAP1, HeLa, HepG2, K562) and converting it into Akita-style 448x448 binned contact map targets serialized as TensorFlow record (.tfr) files. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Extends the DNALONGBENCH contact map prediction task beyond its five primary cell lines (HFF, H1hESC, GM12878, IMR90, HCT116) by downloading raw 4DN Hi-C data for additional cell lines (e.g., HAP1, HeLa, HepG2, K562) and converting it into Akita-style 448x448 binned contact map targets serialized as TensorFlow record (.tfr) files.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The cell line already has .tfr files shipped with DNALONGBENCH (e.g., the HFF subset) — no reprocessing is needed, just load directly. The prediction task is not contact map prediction (e.g., enhancer-target gene or eQTL tasks), which use different input lengths (450,000 bp) and output shapes than the 448x448 contact maps.

skills.description: Use when you have two 40 kb-resolution Hi-C contact maps (e.g., biological replicates, normalized vs reference, or downsampled vs full data) and need a single reproducibility score to compare normalization methods or sequencing-depth robustness.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-reproducibility-scoring
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-reproducibility-scoring Use when you have two 40 kb-resolution Hi-C contact maps (e.g., biological replicates, normalized vs reference, or downsampled vs full data) and need a single reproducibility score to compare normalization methods or sequencing-depth robustness. Input is a single contact map with no second replicate or reference map to compare against — reproducibility scoring requires a map pair. Contact maps are at a resolution other than the 40 kb used in the covNorm benchmarks without re-validating the coverage cut-off of 200, or data still contain zero-valued fragment pairs and unfiltered low-coverage fragments. The goal is differential interaction calling or compartment analysis rather than a between-map reproducibility metric. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Quantify reproducibility between two Hi-C/capture Hi-C contact maps using HiC-spector's eigenvector-decomposition-based score (get_reproducibility / run_reproducibility_v2.py with num_evec = 20), the metric covNorm's normalization performance was benchmarked against (e.g., GM19204 vs GM19240 chr17 at 40 kb resolution). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Quantify reproducibility between two Hi-C/capture Hi-C contact maps using HiC-spector's eigenvector-decomposition-based score (get_reproducibility / run_reproducibility_v2.py with num_evec = 20), the metric covNorm's normalization performance was benchmarked against (e.g., GM19204 vs GM19240 chr17 at 40 kb resolution).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single contact map with no second replicate or reference map to compare against — reproducibility scoring requires a map pair. Contact maps are at a resolution other than the 40 kb used in the covNorm benchmarks without re-validating the coverage cut-off of 200, or data still contain zero-valued fragment pairs and unfiltered low-coverage fragments. The goal is differential interaction calling or compartment analysis rather than a between-map reproducibility metric.

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into fixed-resolution (5 kb skeleton) binned interaction targets to train a sequence-based chromatin interaction predictor such as deepC.
skills.name: hic-contact-map-target-processing
skills.search_text: hic-contact-map-target-processing Use when raw Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into fixed-resolution (5 kb skeleton) binned interaction targets to train a sequence-based chromatin interaction predictor such as deepC. When the goal is TAD boundary calling from an existing Hi-C matrix rather than generating training targets — a dedicated tool such as TopDom is the appropriate choice When Hi-C data are already provided at the target resolution (5 kb skeleton) and only model training is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Processes Hi-C contact data (e.g. Rao et al. GM12878/K562, GEO GSE63525) into 5 kb-resolution binned skeleton target tracks used to train deepC chromatin interaction models, using pysam/pybedtools for genomic interval handling and R scripts for Hi-C downstream analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Processes Hi-C contact data (e.g. Rao et al. GM12878/K562, GEO GSE63525) into 5 kb-resolution binned skeleton target tracks used to train deepC chromatin interaction models, using pysam/pybedtools for genomic interval handling and R scripts for Hi-C downstream analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is TAD boundary calling from an existing Hi-C matrix rather than generating training targets — a dedicated tool such as TopDom is the appropriate choice When Hi-C data are already provided at the target resolution (5 kb skeleton) and only model training is required

skills.description: Use when you have a PCR-duplicate-removed ChIA-PET bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe) and need a genome-binned 2D contact map for visualization instead of, or in addition to, loop calls.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-construction
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-construction Use when you have a PCR-duplicate-removed ChIA-PET bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe) and need a genome-binned 2D contact map for visualization instead of, or in addition to, loop calls. You need significant chromatin loop calls with PET counts, peak depths, MICC post-probabilities and FDR (use bedpe2Interaction + MICC2.R instead) Input is still raw fastq or unfiltered SAM files — the full ChIA-PET2 pipeline (trimLinker, mapping, buildBedpe, removeDup) must run first Input interaction data is not in bedpe PET format and cannot be assigned to genomic bin pairs by PET ends http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Build a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix from ChIA-PET data using the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Matrix module, which bins PET ends at a fixed binsize (e.g. 10000 bp) and aggregates counts per bin pair into a triplet sparse matrix compatible with HiC-Pro/HiCPlotter. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Build a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix from ChIA-PET data using the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Matrix module, which bins PET ends at a fixed binsize (e.g. 10000 bp) and aggregates counts per bin pair into a triplet sparse matrix compatible with HiC-Pro/HiCPlotter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need significant chromatin loop calls with PET counts, peak depths, MICC post-probabilities and FDR (use bedpe2Interaction + MICC2.R instead) Input is still raw fastq or unfiltered SAM files — the full ChIA-PET2 pipeline (trimLinker, mapping, buildBedpe, removeDup) must run first Input interaction data is not in bedpe PET format and cannot be assigned to genomic bin pairs by PET ends

skills.description: Use when benchmarking loop callers across sequencing depths, training GILoop branches at their preferred matrix density (GCN at 10%, U-Net at full depth), or testing robustness of CTCF loop calling on sparse Hi-C libraries.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-downsampling
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-downsampling Use when benchmarking loop callers across sequencing depths, training GILoop branches at their preferred matrix density (GCN at 10%, U-Net at full depth), or testing robustness of CTCF loop calling on sparse Hi-C libraries. Input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the article states GILoop 'only focuses on bulk Hi-C' and 'is still not capable enough' for scHi-C The targeted cell line's sequencing depth already matches one of the pre-trained models in the GILoop repository, in which case downsampling only adds pre-processing overhead You are using the 'lazy' non-downsampling training mode, which directly trains the GCN branch on the input matrix http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Downsamples Hi-C intra-chromosomal contact maps to controlled sequencing depths (e.g. 20% = 520M cis-reads, 1.5% = 39M cis-reads) using the matrix downsampling function provided in the GILoop repository, enabling depth-controlled evaluation of loop-calling performance and training at experimentally optimal matrix density. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Downsamples Hi-C intra-chromosomal contact maps to controlled sequencing depths (e.g. 20% = 520M cis-reads, 1.5% = 39M cis-reads) using the matrix downsampling function provided in the GILoop repository, enabling depth-controlled evaluation of loop-calling performance and training at experimentally optimal matrix density.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) — the article states GILoop 'only focuses on bulk Hi-C' and 'is still not capable enough' for scHi-C The targeted cell line's sequencing depth already matches one of the pre-trained models in the GILoop repository, in which case downsampling only adds pre-processing overhead You are using the 'lazy' non-downsampling training mode, which directly trains the GCN branch on the input matrix

skills.description: Use when raw (non-imputed) bulk or single-cell Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into weighted-graph inputs for structural-entropy-based TLD/TAD prediction, including sparse single-cell data.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-graph-modeling
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-graph-modeling Use when raw (non-imputed) bulk or single-cell Hi-C contact matrices must be converted into weighted-graph inputs for structural-entropy-based TLD/TAD prediction, including sparse single-cell data. The task requires imputation-based single-cell TLD predictors (scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, HiCS) rather than imputation-free structural-entropy decoding — deDoc2 decodes TLDs with no need of data imputation. The input is already a normalized or processed contact map and the goal is metric computation (AMI, WS, structural entropy, modularity) rather than TLD prediction. Genome-wide inter-chromosomal contacts are the target — the format is n×n intra-chromosome matrices only. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Model raw intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact maps as weighted graphs so that TAD-like domains (TLDs) can be predicted by globally minimizing 2D structural entropy with deDoc2 (deDoc2.w on the whole matrix, deDoc2.s in 10 Mb sliding windows), with no data imputation required. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Model raw intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact maps as weighted graphs so that TAD-like domains (TLDs) can be predicted by globally minimizing 2D structural entropy with deDoc2 (deDoc2.w on the whole matrix, deDoc2.s in 10 Mb sliding windows), with no data imputation required.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires imputation-based single-cell TLD predictors (scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, HiCS) rather than imputation-free structural-entropy decoding — deDoc2 decodes TLDs with no need of data imputation. The input is already a normalized or processed contact map and the goal is metric computation (AMI, WS, structural entropy, modularity) rather than TLD prediction. Genome-wide inter-chromosomal contacts are the target — the format is n×n intra-chromosome matrices only.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking TAD/TLD predictors for robustness on sparse Hi-C data, e.g., single-cell-level downsampled bulk Hi-C matrices (0.025% sampling rate, 40 kb binsize), by comparing predictions on noisy vs. original matrices.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-noise-perturbation
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-noise-perturbation Use when benchmarking TAD/TLD predictors for robustness on sparse Hi-C data, e.g., single-cell-level downsampled bulk Hi-C matrices (0.025% sampling rate, 40 kb binsize), by comparing predictions on noisy vs. original matrices. When the input is experimental single-cell Hi-C data whose noise characteristics you want to measure rather than simulate — this skill only evaluates predictor robustness to synthetic noise When the goal is absolute accuracy of TLD boundary positions against an annotated ground truth (e.g., ChIP-seq boundary validation) rather than stability under perturbation When matrices are so sparse that few or no rows/columns have at least one nonzero entry, making the diagonal-wise noise sampling restriction ill-defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A robustness benchmarking protocol that injects controlled noise (10%, 20%, 40% of contacts, sampled per secondary diagonal from distance-dependent contact probabilities) into downsampled Hi-C contact matrices and quantifies preservation of TLD predictions via adjusted mutual information (AMI) and weighted similarity (WS). epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: A robustness benchmarking protocol that injects controlled noise (10%, 20%, 40% of contacts, sampled per secondary diagonal from distance-dependent contact probabilities) into downsampled Hi-C contact matrices and quantifies preservation of TLD predictions via adjusted mutual information (AMI) and weighted similarity (WS).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the input is experimental single-cell Hi-C data whose noise characteristics you want to measure rather than simulate — this skill only evaluates predictor robustness to synthetic noise When the goal is absolute accuracy of TLD boundary positions against an annotated ground truth (e.g., ChIP-seq boundary validation) rather than stability under perturbation When matrices are so sparse that few or no rows/columns have at least one nonzero entry, making the diagonal-wise noise sampling restriction ill-defined

skills.description: Use when raw .hic files (e.g., GM12878 accession 4DNFI1UEG1HD from 4DN/GSE63525) must be dumped into NxN KR-normalized matrices and chunked into 400x400 submatrices before GAE-based TAD calling.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-preprocessing
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-preprocessing Use when raw .hic files (e.g., GM12878 accession 4DNFI1UEG1HD from 4DN/GSE63525) must be dumped into NxN KR-normalized matrices and chunked into 400x400 submatrices before GAE-based TAD calling. Input is already an NxN tab-separated intra-chromosomal contact matrix — only the 400×400 diagonal partitioning step is needed, not .hic dumping Data are not Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., the EPIANN enhancer-promoter CSV dataset referenced in the README) — this preprocessing produces graph adjacency matrices, not epigenomic interaction tables http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Preprocess Hi-C data into tab-separated N×N intra-chromosomal contact matrices and partition them along the diagonal into non-overlapping 400×400 submatrices, the input format required by TOAST's graph auto-encoder TAD identification pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Preprocess Hi-C data into tab-separated N×N intra-chromosomal contact matrices and partition them along the diagonal into non-overlapping 400×400 submatrices, the input format required by TOAST's graph auto-encoder TAD identification pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an NxN tab-separated intra-chromosomal contact matrix — only the 400×400 diagonal partitioning step is needed, not .hic dumping Data are not Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., the EPIANN enhancer-promoter CSV dataset referenced in the README) — this preprocessing produces graph adjacency matrices, not epigenomic interaction tables

skills.description: Use when input is a raw intra-chromosome Hi-C contact matrix (n×n or sparse edge format) from bulk or single-cell data and hierarchical TAD/TLD boundaries must be predicted, especially for sparse scHi-C where imputation is undesirable.
skills.name: hic-contact-matrix-tld-detection
skills.search_text: hic-contact-matrix-tld-detection Use when input is a raw intra-chromosome Hi-C contact matrix (n×n or sparse edge format) from bulk or single-cell data and hierarchical TAD/TLD boundaries must be predicted, especially for sparse scHi-C where imputation is undesirable. When the goal is bulk TAD calling on dense, well-covered Hi-C and higher-dimensional structural entropy tools suffice — deDoc2 is designed for reliable hierarchical TLD prediction in sparse single cells When input is already a TLD/TAD boundary table rather than a contact matrix — deDoc2 requires raw Hi-C contact data as a weighted graph When a sufficient number of TLDs cannot be identified from the cell's data (e.g., the '2n DNA' stage in the cell-cycle analysis) — such cells should be excluded rather than forced through the pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Detect hierarchical TAD-like domains (TLDs) from single-cell or sparse Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2, a structural-information-theory tool that minimizes 2D structural entropy via dynamic programming, without requiring data imputation. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Detect hierarchical TAD-like domains (TLDs) from single-cell or sparse Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2, a structural-information-theory tool that minimizes 2D structural entropy via dynamic programming, without requiring data imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is bulk TAD calling on dense, well-covered Hi-C and higher-dimensional structural entropy tools suffice — deDoc2 is designed for reliable hierarchical TLD prediction in sparse single cells When input is already a TLD/TAD boundary table rather than a contact matrix — deDoc2 requires raw Hi-C contact data as a weighted graph When a sufficient number of TLDs cannot be identified from the cell's data (e.g., the '2n DNA' stage in the cell-cycle analysis) — such cells should be excluded rather than forced through the pipeline

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) need bias removal, distance-background normalization, or significance calling of cis long-range contacts.
skills.name: hic-contact-normalization
skills.search_text: hic-contact-normalization Use when raw Hi-C or capture Hi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) need bias removal, distance-background normalization, or significance calling of cis long-range contacts. Input is already a normalized contact map or .hic matrix rather than raw fragment-pair coverage/frequency tables — use map-balancing methods like ICE/SCN (iced) or HiC-spector instead Analysis targets inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions — the method filters to cis-interactions only Promoter-capture Hi-C PO-interactions with unbalanced promoter/other coverage — use the dedicated normCoverage cov1_thresh=200, cov2_thresh=50 variant, not the symmetric Hi-C default http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Coverage-based implicit normalization of Hi-C and capture Hi-C data using covNorm: a negative binomial GLM removes fragment-coverage biases, a three-parameter Weibull fit removes the distance-dependent background, and per-contact p-values (FDR-adjusted) call significant long-range chromatin contacts. Benchmarking against Fit-Hi-C/ICE/SCN uses HiC-spector scores and reproducibility of significant contacts between biological replicates. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Coverage-based implicit normalization of Hi-C and capture Hi-C data using covNorm: a negative binomial GLM removes fragment-coverage biases, a three-parameter Weibull fit removes the distance-dependent background, and per-contact p-values (FDR-adjusted) call significant long-range chromatin contacts. Benchmarking against Fit-Hi-C/ICE/SCN uses HiC-spector scores and reproducibility of significant contacts between biological replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized contact map or .hic matrix rather than raw fragment-pair coverage/frequency tables — use map-balancing methods like ICE/SCN (iced) or HiC-spector instead Analysis targets inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions — the method filters to cis-interactions only Promoter-capture Hi-C PO-interactions with unbalanced promoter/other coverage — use the dedicated normCoverage cov1_thresh=200, cov2_thresh=50 variant, not the symmetric Hi-C default

skills.description: Use when comparing Hi-C datasets (e.g., ESC vs NPC) and you need loop-level differences, not just compartment-level calls, specifically for interactions anchored in bins flagged as significant differential compartments.
skills.name: hic-differential-interaction-testing
skills.search_text: hic-differential-interaction-testing Use when comparing Hi-C datasets (e.g., ESC vs NPC) and you need loop-level differences, not just compartment-level calls, specifically for interactions anchored in bins flagged as significant differential compartments. You only need compartment-level A/B differences — use dcHiC's differential compartment analysis instead, since this skill is scoped to interactions anchored in differential compartments You have only a single Hi-C contact map (no condition comparison) — differential interaction testing requires two or more contact maps Your input is raw Hi-C contact matrices without prior significant interaction calls — Fit-Hi-C (or HiCCUPS/Mustache) loop calling must be run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Identify chromatin interactions (significant contacts or loops) whose contact strength differs across conditions, by first filtering the interaction set for anchors overlapping significant differential compartments and then testing each retained interaction with a multivariate outlier statistic, as implemented in dcHiC's differential interaction feature. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Identify chromatin interactions (significant contacts or loops) whose contact strength differs across conditions, by first filtering the interaction set for anchors overlapping significant differential compartments and then testing each retained interaction with a multivariate outlier statistic, as implemented in dcHiC's differential interaction feature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need compartment-level A/B differences — use dcHiC's differential compartment analysis instead, since this skill is scoped to interactions anchored in differential compartments You have only a single Hi-C contact map (no condition comparison) — differential interaction testing requires two or more contact maps Your input is raw Hi-C contact matrices without prior significant interaction calls — Fit-Hi-C (or HiCCUPS/Mustache) loop calling must be run first

skills.description: Use when you have coverage-normalized Hi-C fragment-pair tables (bias-removed residuals with freq and dist columns) and need to remove the genomic distance-dependent background to obtain distance-normalized interaction frequencies.
skills.name: hic-distance-dependent-background-normalization
skills.search_text: hic-distance-dependent-background-normalization Use when you have coverage-normalized Hi-C fragment-pair tables (bias-removed residuals with freq and dist columns) and need to remove the genomic distance-dependent background to obtain distance-normalized interaction frequencies. Input is still raw interaction frequency data that has not passed covNormRpkg::normCoverage; the distance normalization assumes bias-removed residuals Rij Interaction pairs lie beyond the max_dist cutoff (e.g. > 2 Mb) and are not meant to be distance-normalized Working with inter-chromosomal interactions; the article's pipeline focuses on cis-interactions only, as inter-chromosomal interactions were filtered upstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Performs the genomic distance-dependent background normalization step of the covNorm R package (covNormRpkg::normDistance), which removes the expected distance-decay of Hi-C ligation frequencies after coverage normalization, producing the dist_res column of distance-normalized interaction frequencies. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Performs the genomic distance-dependent background normalization step of the covNorm R package (covNormRpkg::normDistance), which removes the expected distance-decay of Hi-C ligation frequencies after coverage normalization, producing the dist_res column of distance-normalized interaction frequencies.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw interaction frequency data that has not passed covNormRpkg::normCoverage; the distance normalization assumes bias-removed residuals Rij Interaction pairs lie beyond the max_dist cutoff (e.g. > 2 Mb) and are not meant to be distance-normalized Working with inter-chromosomal interactions; the article's pipeline focuses on cis-interactions only, as inter-chromosomal interactions were filtered upstream

skills.description: Use when raw chromosome-wise Hi-C contact maps (up to 10 kb resolution) must be prepared for PCA/SVD compartment calling, so that distance-decay effects are removed before eigen-decomposition.
skills.name: hic-distance-normalization-to-correlation-matrices
skills.search_text: hic-distance-normalization-to-correlation-matrices Use when raw chromosome-wise Hi-C contact maps (up to 10 kb resolution) must be prepared for PCA/SVD compartment calling, so that distance-decay effects are removed before eigen-decomposition. The goal is differential interaction / loop significance testing (that is Fit-Hi-C's role), not compartment computation The data are sparse single-cell Hi-C maps without prior pseudo-bulk aggregation, where compartment identification is unreliable due to sparsity Compartment scores have already been computed and quantile-normalized across samples (proceed directly to Mahalanobis-distance differential analysis) Preprocessing step in dcHiC's compartment pipeline: each chromosome-wise Hi-C contact matrix is distance-normalized by observed/expected at each genomic distance and converted into a correlation matrix, which is the standard input for eigen/SVD-based A/B compartment scoring. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Preprocessing step in dcHiC's compartment pipeline: each chromosome-wise Hi-C contact matrix is distance-normalized by observed/expected at each genomic distance and converted into a correlation matrix, which is the standard input for eigen/SVD-based A/B compartment scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is differential interaction / loop significance testing (that is Fit-Hi-C's role), not compartment computation The data are sparse single-cell Hi-C maps without prior pseudo-bulk aggregation, where compartment identification is unreliable due to sparsity Compartment scores have already been computed and quantile-normalized across samples (proceed directly to Mahalanobis-distance differential analysis)

skills.description: Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ files must be adapter- and quality-trimmed before alignment, e.g. at the start of a Microcket run on MuSC Hi-C libraries from GSE189841.
skills.name: hic-fastq-adapter-trimming
skills.search_text: hic-fastq-adapter-trimming Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ files must be adapter- and quality-trimmed before alignment, e.g. at the start of a Microcket run on MuSC Hi-C libraries from GSE189841. Input reads are not 3D-genomics (Hi-C/Micro-C/ChIA-PET) paired-end data, e.g. RNA-seq data where STAR-based workflows are expected instead Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered, so Ktrim trimming would be redundant Input is not FASTQ (e.g. already-aligned BAM files or processed .pairs files), which should skip trimming and go straight to filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Performs adapter and quality trimming of paired-end Hi-C FASTQ reads as the first step of the Microcket pipeline, using Ktrim with the sequencing-kit-appropriate adapter settings so that only clean reads proceed to stitching (FLASH) and alignment (BWA). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2025.103962
skills.summary: Performs adapter and quality trimming of paired-end Hi-C FASTQ reads as the first step of the Microcket pipeline, using Ktrim with the sequencing-kit-appropriate adapter settings so that only clean reads proceed to stitching (FLASH) and alignment (BWA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are not 3D-genomics (Hi-C/Micro-C/ChIA-PET) paired-end data, e.g. RNA-seq data where STAR-based workflows are expected instead Reads are already adapter-trimmed and quality-filtered, so Ktrim trimming would be redundant Input is not FASTQ (e.g. already-aligned BAM files or processed .pairs files), which should skip trimming and go straight to filtering

skills.description: Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files (e.g. from extractHAIRS --hic 1) for haplotype assembly and you need to drop putative trans-homolog linkage errors before phasing with SpecHap.
skills.name: hic-fragment-filtering
skills.search_text: hic-fragment-filtering Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files (e.g. from extractHAIRS --hic 1) for haplotype assembly and you need to drop putative trans-homolog linkage errors before phasing with SpecHap. Input fragments are from WGS, PacBio SMRT, ONP, or 10X linked-reads rather than proximity-ligation (Hi-C) data — the 40 Mbp insertion-size cutoff is specific to Hi-C trans-interaction error Variants/fragments target a non-diploid organism — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy, so downstream phasing (and hence this filtering step feeding it) is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Filters Hi-C fragment files prior to haplotype assembly by removing read pairs whose inferred insertion size spans more than 40 Mbp, thereby excluding trans interactions between homologous chromosomes that SpecHap treats as errors rather than modeling explicitly. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Filters Hi-C fragment files prior to haplotype assembly by removing read pairs whose inferred insertion size spans more than 40 Mbp, thereby excluding trans interactions between homologous chromosomes that SpecHap treats as errors rather than modeling explicitly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input fragments are from WGS, PacBio SMRT, ONP, or 10X linked-reads rather than proximity-ligation (Hi-C) data — the 40 Mbp insertion-size cutoff is specific to Hi-C trans-interaction error Variants/fragments target a non-diploid organism — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy, so downstream phasing (and hence this filtering step feeding it) is inappropriate

skills.description: Use when you have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices) and must assign a density-based cluster label to every genomic bin without specifying the number of clusters.
skills.name: hic-graph-embedding-analysis
skills.search_text: hic-graph-embedding-analysis Use when you have low-dimensional node embeddings (e.g., 16-dim GAE output from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices) and must assign a density-based cluster label to every genomic bin without specifying the number of clusters. Input is a raw NxN Hi-C contact matrix rather than trained GAE embeddings — clustering should operate on the embedding, not the contact matrix directly The number of clusters must be fixed a priori or labels must be generated by a supervised model — HDBSCAN here is run in unsupervised mode with automatic cluster discovery http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Clusters 16-dimensional graph auto-encoder (GAE) embeddings of Hi-C genomic bins with unsupervised HDBSCAN to assign one label per bin, forming the clustering module of the TOAST TAD-identification pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Clusters 16-dimensional graph auto-encoder (GAE) embeddings of Hi-C genomic bins with unsupervised HDBSCAN to assign one label per bin, forming the clustering module of the TOAST TAD-identification pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw NxN Hi-C contact matrix rather than trained GAE embeddings — clustering should operate on the embedding, not the contact matrix directly The number of clusters must be fixed a priori or labels must be generated by a supervised model — HDBSCAN here is run in unsupervised mode with automatic cluster discovery

skills.description: Use when you have per-bin cluster labels from an N×N intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix and need to delineate TAD boundaries as genomic intervals for downstream visualization or evaluation.
skills.name: hic-matrix-resolution-to-bin-length-conversion
skills.search_text: hic-matrix-resolution-to-bin-length-conversion Use when you have per-bin cluster labels from an N×N intra-chromosomal Hi-C contact matrix and need to delineate TAD boundaries as genomic intervals for downstream visualization or evaluation. Input is still a raw NxN contact matrix — clustering via the GAE + HDBSCAN modules must run first before boundary delineation Regions of interest are shorter than 200 Kb, e.g. sub-TAD or loop-scale features — the TOAST length filter will discard them You need statistically parameterized TAD calls (e.g. Armatus, TopDom, TADbit dynamic-programming or statistical methods) rather than label-based contiguous-region delineation http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Converts per-bin HDBSCAN cluster labels from the TOAST pipeline into genomic TAD boundaries by grouping contiguous same-label bins, converting bin counts to genomic length via the Hi-C matrix resolution (e.g., 50/25/5 Kb), and retaining only regions exceeding 200 Kb. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Converts per-bin HDBSCAN cluster labels from the TOAST pipeline into genomic TAD boundaries by grouping contiguous same-label bins, converting bin counts to genomic length via the Hi-C matrix resolution (e.g., 50/25/5 Kb), and retaining only regions exceeding 200 Kb.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still a raw NxN contact matrix — clustering via the GAE + HDBSCAN modules must run first before boundary delineation Regions of interest are shorter than 200 Kb, e.g. sub-TAD or loop-scale features — the TOAST length filter will discard them You need statistically parameterized TAD calls (e.g. Armatus, TopDom, TADbit dynamic-programming or statistical methods) rather than label-based contiguous-region delineation

skills.description: Use when a ChIA-PET bedpe interaction file (e.g. in.rmDup.bedpe) needs to be binned into a genome-wide 2D contact matrix for heatmap-style visualization with Hi-C tools such as HiCPlotter.
skills.name: hic-matrix-visualization-compatibility
skills.search_text: hic-matrix-visualization-compatibility Use when a ChIA-PET bedpe interaction file (e.g. in.rmDup.bedpe) needs to be binned into a genome-wide 2D contact matrix for heatmap-style visualization with Hi-C tools such as HiCPlotter. The input is raw FASTQ or SAM data — the bedpe2Matrix step requires a duplicate-removed bedpe file, which is produced by upstream ChIA-PET2 steps (trimLinker, buildBedpe, removeDup) The goal is significant chromatin loop calling rather than a binned contact map — use ChIA-PET2's bedpe2Interaction/MICC2.R pathway instead The visualization target requires a dense/cool-format Hi-C matrix rather than sparse triplet format http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Matrix step that converts a PCR-duplicate-removed PET bedpe file into a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix, stored in HiC-Pro-compatible triplet sparse format so the contact map can be rendered by HiCPlotter. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Reconstructs the ChIA-PET2 bedpe2Matrix step that converts a PCR-duplicate-removed PET bedpe file into a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix, stored in HiC-Pro-compatible triplet sparse format so the contact map can be rendered by HiCPlotter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw FASTQ or SAM data — the bedpe2Matrix step requires a duplicate-removed bedpe file, which is produced by upstream ChIA-PET2 steps (trimLinker, buildBedpe, removeDup) The goal is significant chromatin loop calling rather than a binned contact map — use ChIA-PET2's bedpe2Interaction/MICC2.R pathway instead The visualization target requires a dense/cool-format Hi-C matrix rather than sparse triplet format

skills.description: Use when preparing Hi-C cis-contact matrices as training inputs for dual-branch loop callers like GILoop, i.e. when a contact map must be converted into paired image-view patches and graph-view adjacency samples.
skills.name: hic-patch-sampling-and-tiling
skills.search_text: hic-patch-sampling-and-tiling Use when preparing Hi-C cis-contact matrices as training inputs for dual-branch loop callers like GILoop, i.e. when a contact map must be converted into paired image-view patches and graph-view adjacency samples. Input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop is stated to be 'still not capable enough' to deal with extremely sparse scHi-C Input matrices are raw or non-KR-normalized and only the demo_from_processed.py path is used, since that script applies no preprocessing and expects KR-normalized O/E matrices The goal is loop calling with a single-view tool (e.g. SIP, Chromosight, Peakachu) that does not require paired image/graph sample construction http://edamontology.org/topic_3922 Transforms KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C cis-contact maps into paired image patches and graph adjacency samples for GILoop's dual-branch (GCN + image) model, using O/E distance normalization and diagonal/off-diagonal patch sampling. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: Transforms KR-normalized intra-chromosomal Hi-C cis-contact maps into paired image patches and graph adjacency samples for GILoop's dual-branch (GCN + image) model, using O/E distance normalization and diagonal/off-diagonal patch sampling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop is stated to be 'still not capable enough' to deal with extremely sparse scHi-C Input matrices are raw or non-KR-normalized and only the demo_from_processed.py path is used, since that script applies no preprocessing and expects KR-normalized O/E matrices The goal is loop calling with a single-view tool (e.g. SIP, Chromosight, Peakachu) that does not require paired image/graph sample construction

skills.description: Use when you need to determine how many Hi-C sub-compartments are statistically supported at reduced sequencing depth, or to test the robustness of sub-compartment inference to read-depth reduction by sweeping N_subcompartment and comparing AIC minima.
skills.name: hic-read-depth-downsampling
skills.search_text: hic-read-depth-downsampling Use when you need to determine how many Hi-C sub-compartments are statistically supported at reduced sequencing depth, or to test the robustness of sub-compartment inference to read-depth reduction by sweeping N_subcompartment and comparing AIC minima. Input Hi-C data is already low-depth; down-sampling further would leave too few interactions for stable sub-compartment inference The goal is to call a fixed number of sub-compartments rather than to statistically select the optimal number via likelihood/AIC The analysis targets a method other than CscoreTool-M whose log-likelihood over N_subcompartment is not exposed, since AIC = 2k - 2lnL cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Down-sample high-resolution Hi-C contact data (e.g. GM12878 from Rao 2014) to reduced read depths such as 0.1x and 0.01x, then re-run CscoreTool-M across candidate sub-compartment counts and select the statistically optimal number via Akaike Information Criterion (AIC = 2k - 2lnL). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Down-sample high-resolution Hi-C contact data (e.g. GM12878 from Rao 2014) to reduced read depths such as 0.1x and 0.01x, then re-run CscoreTool-M across candidate sub-compartment counts and select the statistically optimal number via Akaike Information Criterion (AIC = 2k - 2lnL).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C data is already low-depth; down-sampling further would leave too few interactions for stable sub-compartment inference The goal is to call a fixed number of sub-compartments rather than to statistically select the optimal number via likelihood/AIC The analysis targets a method other than CscoreTool-M whose log-likelihood over N_subcompartment is not exposed, since AIC = 2k - 2lnL cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when you must choose how many sub-compartments CscoreTool-M should infer for a Hi-C dataset at 100 kb resolution, e.g. testing 0.1x/0.01x down-sampled GM12878 contacts against candidate compartment counts.
skills.name: hic-sub-compartment-model-order-sweep
skills.search_text: hic-sub-compartment-model-order-sweep Use when you must choose how many sub-compartments CscoreTool-M should infer for a Hi-C dataset at 100 kb resolution, e.g. testing 0.1x/0.01x down-sampled GM12878 contacts against candidate compartment counts. The goal is a single pre-specified sub-compartment count for a high-depth dataset rather than model-order selection on sparse (down-sampled) data The input is not Hi-C interaction data in HiCsummary format, or no equal-length Rabl-position windows bed file can be constructed The question is calling which sub-compartment a region belongs to rather than how many sub-compartments the model should use http://edamontology.org/topic_3922 Determines the statistically optimal number of Hi-C sub-compartments for CscoreTool-M by sweeping the N_subcompartment argument and selecting the model order that minimizes AIC = 2k - 2lnL on down-sampled GM12878 Hi-C data. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Determines the statistically optimal number of Hi-C sub-compartments for CscoreTool-M by sweeping the N_subcompartment argument and selecting the model order that minimizes AIC = 2k - 2lnL on down-sampled GM12878 Hi-C data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single pre-specified sub-compartment count for a high-depth dataset rather than model-order selection on sparse (down-sampled) data The input is not Hi-C interaction data in HiCsummary format, or no equal-length Rabl-position windows bed file can be constructed The question is calling which sub-compartment a region belongs to rather than how many sub-compartments the model should use

skills.description: Use when Hi-C interaction summary data (HOMER HiCsummary format) must be segmented into more than the canonical A/B compartments — e.g. inferring 5–10 sub-compartments, quantifying cell-population heterogeneity, or deconvolving mixed cell-type samples into cell-type-specific profiles.
skills.name: hic-subcompartment-probabilistic-inference
skills.search_text: hic-subcompartment-probabilistic-inference Use when Hi-C interaction summary data (HOMER HiCsummary format) must be segmented into more than the canonical A/B compartments — e.g. inferring 5–10 sub-compartments, quantifying cell-population heterogeneity, or deconvolving mixed cell-type samples into cell-type-specific profiles. Input is not raw Hi-C interaction summary data but already-computed compartment calls or feature tables — CscoreTool-M requires a HOMER-format HiCsummary of individual interactions Only a binary A/B compartment assignment is needed; simpler PCA-based approaches (e.g. HOMER runHiCpca.pl) suffice for two compartments The sample is a single homogeneous cell type where population heterogeneity deconvolution is not the goal — the multi-sub-compartment model adds complexity without benefit http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Probabilistic-modeling-based inference of multiple 3D genome sub-compartments from Hi-C data using CscoreTool-M, which outputs per-window compartment scores (Cscores) interpretable as probabilities of a region belonging to a specific sub-compartment. Enables deconvolution of mixed cell populations into cell-type-specific sub-compartments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Probabilistic-modeling-based inference of multiple 3D genome sub-compartments from Hi-C data using CscoreTool-M, which outputs per-window compartment scores (Cscores) interpretable as probabilities of a region belonging to a specific sub-compartment. Enables deconvolution of mixed cell populations into cell-type-specific sub-compartments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw Hi-C interaction summary data but already-computed compartment calls or feature tables — CscoreTool-M requires a HOMER-format HiCsummary of individual interactions Only a binary A/B compartment assignment is needed; simpler PCA-based approaches (e.g. HOMER runHiCpca.pl) suffice for two compartments The sample is a single homogeneous cell type where population heterogeneity deconvolution is not the goal — the multi-sub-compartment model adds complexity without benefit

skills.description: Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ libraries need alignment, valid-pair filtering, and QC statistics comparable to Table 1 alignment rates, e.g. replicating MuSC Hi-C stats from GSE189841.
skills.name: hic-valid-pairs-filtering-statistics
skills.search_text: hic-valid-pairs-filtering-statistics Use when paired-end Hi-C (or Micro-C/ChIA-PET) FASTQ libraries need alignment, valid-pair filtering, and QC statistics comparable to Table 1 alignment rates, e.g. replicating MuSC Hi-C stats from GSE189841. Input is not 3D-genomics data (Hi-C, Micro-C, ChIA-PET, or derivative protocols) — e.g. bulk RNA-seq data, where STAR rather than the Microcket BWA chain is the article's suggested aligner You only need to visualize contact maps without regenerating valid-pair statistics from FASTQ — start from existing .hic/pairs files with JuicerTools/cooler instead The reference genome is hg38 and Microcket's packaged hg38 annotation files do not match your chosen FASTA build, requiring custom .info/.sam.header preparation outside this skill's validated path http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Align paired-end Hi-C FASTQ libraries with the Microcket package (Ktrim/FLASH pre-processing + BWA alignment to mm10) and compile the valid-pairs filtering statistics (Total, Ktrim, Unique, Mappable, Self-circle, Cis/Trans fractions) from the Microcket.<sid>.final.stat QC files, as demonstrated for MuSC QSC (GSM5708470) and FISC (GSM5708476) libraries. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2025.103962
skills.summary: Align paired-end Hi-C FASTQ libraries with the Microcket package (Ktrim/FLASH pre-processing + BWA alignment to mm10) and compile the valid-pairs filtering statistics (Total, Ktrim, Unique, Mappable, Self-circle, Cis/Trans fractions) from the Microcket.<sid>.final.stat QC files, as demonstrated for MuSC QSC (GSM5708470) and FISC (GSM5708476) libraries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not 3D-genomics data (Hi-C, Micro-C, ChIA-PET, or derivative protocols) — e.g. bulk RNA-seq data, where STAR rather than the Microcket BWA chain is the article's suggested aligner You only need to visualize contact maps without regenerating valid-pair statistics from FASTQ — start from existing .hic/pairs files with JuicerTools/cooler instead The reference genome is hg38 and Microcket's packaged hg38 annotation files do not match your chosen FASTA build, requiring custom .info/.sam.header preparation outside this skill's validated path

skills.description: Use when you have a high-resolution (e.g., 10 kb) normalized Hi-C matrix in .hic or .cool format and need to call statistically enriched loop pixels with a local Poisson background model, or when benchmarking loop callers against each other.
skills.name: hiccups-local-poisson-background-loop-detection
skills.search_text: hiccups-local-poisson-background-loop-detection Use when you have a high-resolution (e.g., 10 kb) normalized Hi-C matrix in .hic or .cool format and need to call statistically enriched loop pixels with a local Poisson background model, or when benchmarking loop callers against each other. Input Hi-C data is at very low sequencing depth (e.g., 1.5% down-sampled), where Fit-Hi-C with q-value < 1e-5 retains no interactions and HiCCUPS with default parameters outputs less than 1/3 of the Peakachu loops The goal is de novo loop prediction in a platform lacking dedicated tools (e.g., DNA SPRITE) rather than enrichment-based calling on a Hi-C matrix You need robust calling at ~30 million intrachromosomal reads, where Peakachu's supervised model rather than Poisson enrichment is the appropriate choice http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect chromatin loops in Hi-C contact maps using HiCCUPS, an enrichment-based method that incorporates local background into its model via a Poisson test, and benchmark the resulting loop set against Peakachu and Fit-Hi-C predictions using three-way overlap and orthogonal validation ratios. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Detect chromatin loops in Hi-C contact maps using HiCCUPS, an enrichment-based method that incorporates local background into its model via a Poisson test, and benchmark the resulting loop set against Peakachu and Fit-Hi-C predictions using three-way overlap and orthogonal validation ratios.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C data is at very low sequencing depth (e.g., 1.5% down-sampled), where Fit-Hi-C with q-value < 1e-5 retains no interactions and HiCCUPS with default parameters outputs less than 1/3 of the Peakachu loops The goal is de novo loop prediction in a platform lacking dedicated tools (e.g., DNA SPRITE) rather than enrichment-based calling on a Hi-C matrix You need robust calling at ~30 million intrachromosomal reads, where Peakachu's supervised model rather than Poisson enrichment is the appropriate choice

skills.description: Use when processing paired-end HiChIP or PLAC-seq FASTQ data whose junction sequence between the two genomic tags differs from the ChIA-PET bridge linker and needs assay-aware linker scanning before mapping.
skills.name: hichip-plac-seq-pseudolinker-handling
skills.search_text: hichip-plac-seq-pseudolinker-handling Use when processing paired-end HiChIP or PLAC-seq FASTQ data whose junction sequence between the two genomic tags differs from the ChIA-PET bridge linker and needs assay-aware linker scanning before mapping. Input data has already been linker-filtered and partitioned (e.g., only full-PET reads remain) — proceed directly to mapping instead Data type lacks a junction sequence between two genomic tags (e.g., non-ligation assays) — the linker-scan categorization logic does not apply Configure ChIA-PIPE's linker-filtering stage (via the CPU linker_filter module) so that paired-end reads from related chromatin-mapping assays whose junction sequence between the two genomic tags differs from the classic ChIA-PET bridge linker — e.g., HiChIP and PLAC-seq — are correctly scanned and partitioned. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Configure ChIA-PIPE's linker-filtering stage (via the CPU linker_filter module) so that paired-end reads from related chromatin-mapping assays whose junction sequence between the two genomic tags differs from the classic ChIA-PET bridge linker — e.g., HiChIP and PLAC-seq — are correctly scanned and partitioned.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data has already been linker-filtered and partitioned (e.g., only full-PET reads remain) — proceed directly to mapping instead Data type lacks a junction sequence between two genomic tags (e.g., non-ligation assays) — the linker-scan categorization logic does not apply

skills.description: Use when you need to build or reimplement an HMM/state-space model that jointly scores nucleosome and transcription factor occupancy genome-wide from paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genomic sequence.
skills.name: hidden-markov-model-implementation
skills.search_text: hidden-markov-model-implementation Use when you need to build or reimplement an HMM/state-space model that jointly scores nucleosome and transcription factor occupancy genome-wide from paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genomic sequence. When the goal is peak calling or footprint identification followed by TF labeling (e.g. MACS2 + FIMO) rather than a joint probabilistic occupancy model — RoboCOP is an alternative to that approach When accessibility data are not paired-end MNase-seq/ATAC-seq fragment data, since the negative-binomial emission model over fragment midpoints is tailored to those assays http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Implement the multivariate hidden Markov model underlying RoboCOP, which integrates nucleotide sequence (PWM and dinucleotide emission models) with chromatin accessibility data (negative-binomial fragment midpoint counts) to jointly compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and ~150 TFs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Implement the multivariate hidden Markov model underlying RoboCOP, which integrates nucleotide sequence (PWM and dinucleotide emission models) with chromatin accessibility data (negative-binomial fragment midpoint counts) to jointly compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and ~150 TFs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is peak calling or footprint identification followed by TF labeling (e.g. MACS2 + FIMO) rather than a joint probabilistic occupancy model — RoboCOP is an alternative to that approach When accessibility data are not paired-end MNase-seq/ATAC-seq fragment data, since the negative-binomial emission model over fragment midpoints is tailored to those assays

skills.description: Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq reads plus genome sequence for S. cerevisiae and need probabilistic nucleosome/TF occupancy scores or dyad positions across the genome.
skills.name: hidden-markov-model-occupancy-inference
skills.search_text: hidden-markov-model-occupancy-inference Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq reads plus genome sequence for S. cerevisiae and need probabilistic nucleosome/TF occupancy scores or dyad positions across the genome. You only need peak calling or footprint identification plus motif labeling — the article contrasts RoboCOP with a MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling pipeline, which performs notably worse You need a method that jointly models many factors from multiple data types beyond MNase-seq/ATAC-seq accessibility — RoboCOP currently uses only MNase-seq or ATAC-seq You require versioned, quantified sequencing-depth guidance — the article does not state depth requirements beyond noting accuracy improves with deeper sequencing http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3176 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Run RoboCOP, a multivariate HMM that integrates chromatin accessibility data (paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence, to compute a genome-wide probabilistic occupancy landscape of nucleosomes and transcription factors at single-nucleotide resolution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Run RoboCOP, a multivariate HMM that integrates chromatin accessibility data (paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence, to compute a genome-wide probabilistic occupancy landscape of nucleosomes and transcription factors at single-nucleotide resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need peak calling or footprint identification plus motif labeling — the article contrasts RoboCOP with a MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling pipeline, which performs notably worse You need a method that jointly models many factors from multiple data types beyond MNase-seq/ATAC-seq accessibility — RoboCOP currently uses only MNase-seq or ATAC-seq You require versioned, quantified sequencing-depth guidance — the article does not state depth requirements beyond noting accuracy improves with deeper sequencing

skills.description: Use when short-read ChIP-Seq coverage has been binned (e.g., 25 bp HDF counts) and consecutive bins must be statistically classified into enriched vs. background states with a probability model that explicitly captures overdispersion and excess zeros.
skills.name: hidden-markov-model-viterbi-implementation
skills.search_text: hidden-markov-model-viterbi-implementation Use when short-read ChIP-Seq coverage has been binned (e.g., 25 bp HDF counts) and consecutive bins must be statistically classified into enriched vs. background states with a probability model that explicitly captures overdispersion and excess zeros. Input is a comparative histone modification dataset better served by ChIPDiff, which HPeak's authors note is 'restricted to analyzing comparative histone modification data' Reads of different orientation within a peak must be distinguished to pinpoint peak summits — the current HPeak algorithm does not use orientation information The analysis requires a well-calibrated false detection rate; the paper notes the method 'is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate' http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implement a two-state hidden Markov model (as in HPeak) over fixed-length genomic bin coverage, with a Generalized Poisson emission for the ChIP-enriched state and a zero-inflated Poisson emission for the background state, using Viterbi-based parameter estimation to classify each 25 bp bin as enriched or background. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Implement a two-state hidden Markov model (as in HPeak) over fixed-length genomic bin coverage, with a Generalized Poisson emission for the ChIP-enriched state and a zero-inflated Poisson emission for the background state, using Viterbi-based parameter estimation to classify each 25 bp bin as enriched or background.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a comparative histone modification dataset better served by ChIPDiff, which HPeak's authors note is 'restricted to analyzing comparative histone modification data' Reads of different orientation within a peak must be distinguished to pinpoint peak summits — the current HPeak algorithm does not use orientation information The analysis requires a well-calibrated false detection rate; the paper notes the method 'is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate'

skills.description: Use when you have a BHi-Cect nested cluster list plus ChIP-seq tracks and want to know which GO biological functions are enriched among genes whose loci fall into specific bottom enclaves.
skills.name: hierarchical-chromosome-cluster-functional-annotation
skills.search_text: hierarchical-chromosome-cluster-functional-annotation Use when you have a BHi-Cect nested cluster list plus ChIP-seq tracks and want to know which GO biological functions are enriched among genes whose loci fall into specific bottom enclaves. You need mechanistic details of chromatin dynamics (e.g. loop extrusion vs phase separation) — the analysis cannot infer these You want TAD-style contiguous-domain calling — BHi-Cect enclaves are mostly non-contiguous and interwoven, so this skill annotates clusters, not contiguity-bounded TADs http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Annotates BHi-Cect chromosome hierarchy clusters (bottom enclaves) functionally by aggregating ChIP-seq signal (RNAP2 in IMR90, H3K4me3 in K562) per enclave, ranking genes, and running GO gene-set GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Annotates BHi-Cect chromosome hierarchy clusters (bottom enclaves) functionally by aggregating ChIP-seq signal (RNAP2 in IMR90, H3K4me3 in K562) per enclave, ranking genes, and running GO gene-set GSEA with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need mechanistic details of chromatin dynamics (e.g. loop extrusion vs phase separation) — the analysis cannot infer these You want TAD-style contiguous-domain calling — BHi-Cect enclaves are mostly non-contiguous and interwoven, so this skill annotates clusters, not contiguity-bounded TADs

skills.description: Use when a sparse single-cell count matrix (scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq bins or peaks) with known or hypothesized sub-populations must be grouped via hierarchical clustering on a PCA/feature-space embedding and quantitatively benchmarked by ARI.
