skills.search_text: hierarchical-clustering-of-epigenomic-profiles Use when a sparse single-cell count matrix (scChIP-seq/scATAC-seq bins or peaks) with known or hypothesized sub-populations must be grouped via hierarchical clustering on a PCA/feature-space embedding and quantitatively benchmarked by ARI. Input is already a reduced feature/embedding matrix from a method other than those being benchmarked and no ground-truth labels exist for ARI computation The dataset is bulk ChIP-seq or lacks single-cell resolution — the article notes existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are not fit for these sparse single-cell data, and vice versa this benchmark targets single-cell profiles The goal is differential enrichment or gene/pathway interpretation downstream of known clusters rather than cluster discovery or method benchmarking http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Clusters single-cell epigenomic profiles (e.g., an in-silico H3K27me3 scChIP-seq mix of Jurkat, Ramos, HBCx-22 and MDA-MB-468) by applying hierarchical clustering on each method's reduced feature space (e.g., ChromSCape's 50 retained PCs) and scoring separation against known cell-line labels with the adjusted Rand index (ARI). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Clusters single-cell epigenomic profiles (e.g., an in-silico H3K27me3 scChIP-seq mix of Jurkat, Ramos, HBCx-22 and MDA-MB-468) by applying hierarchical clustering on each method's reduced feature space (e.g., ChromSCape's 50 retained PCs) and scoring separation against known cell-line labels with the adjusted Rand index (ARI).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a reduced feature/embedding matrix from a method other than those being benchmarked and no ground-truth labels exist for ARI computation The dataset is bulk ChIP-seq or lacks single-cell resolution — the article notes existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are not fit for these sparse single-cell data, and vice versa this benchmark targets single-cell profiles The goal is differential enrichment or gene/pathway interpretation downstream of known clusters rather than cluster discovery or method benchmarking

skills.description: Use when a large set of predicted sequence motifs (e.g. DESSO motifs from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets) must be de-duplicated into representative motifs and classified as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or as novel.
skills.name: hierarchical-clustering-of-pwm-motifs
skills.search_text: hierarchical-clustering-of-pwm-motifs Use when a large set of predicted sequence motifs (e.g. DESSO motifs from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets) must be de-duplicated into representative motifs and classified as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or as novel. When motifs are already curated or few in number, making clustering unnecessary — match each motif directly against JASPAR/TRANSFAC instead When the goal is de novo motif discovery from ChIP-seq peaks (use DESSO's train.py/predict.py first; clustering operates on the predicted motif output) When clustering DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than sequence PWMs, unless shape-specific similarity is desired http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Groups a large collection of predicted PWM motifs by computing all-against-all TOMTOM similarity scores and applying hierarchical clustering (Supplementary Method S1), then labels each resulting cluster as known or undocumented by matching against JASPAR and TRANSFAC. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Groups a large collection of predicted PWM motifs by computing all-against-all TOMTOM similarity scores and applying hierarchical clustering (Supplementary Method S1), then labels each resulting cluster as known or undocumented by matching against JASPAR and TRANSFAC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When motifs are already curated or few in number, making clustering unnecessary — match each motif directly against JASPAR/TRANSFAC instead When the goal is de novo motif discovery from ChIP-seq peaks (use DESSO's train.py/predict.py first; clustering operates on the predicted motif output) When clustering DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than sequence PWMs, unless shape-specific similarity is desired

skills.description: Use when a dendrogram from complete-linkage agglomerative clustering of DTW-aligned peak profiles must be cut into clusters whose count reflects true underlying patterns or is chosen interactively near the leaves.
skills.name: hierarchical-dendrogram-cutting
skills.search_text: hierarchical-dendrogram-cutting Use when a dendrogram from complete-linkage agglomerative clustering of DTW-aligned peak profiles must be cut into clusters whose count reflects true underlying patterns or is chosen interactively near the leaves. The input peaks have not been DTW-warped and contain substantial noise/modifications (v or p above ~0.15) — the article shows standard hierarchical clustering without warping degrades badly (MCC ~0.294 at v=0.40, p=0.40) A fixed, validated cluster count is required but only a purely automatic cut with no ground truth or interactive inspection is possible — the article notes cutting the dendrogram 'at an appropriate level is a difficult choice' The data are already grouped by an external annotation (e.g. known TSS labels) and clustering would only duplicate existing structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Cut agglomerative hierarchical clustering dendrograms (built with complete linkage over DTW-warped or raw epigenomic peak profiles) at an appropriate level to recover meaningful clusters of genomic regions, as used by DGW both in simulation validation (5 clusters) and interactive dgw-explorer analysis (45 clusters). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Cut agglomerative hierarchical clustering dendrograms (built with complete linkage over DTW-warped or raw epigenomic peak profiles) at an appropriate level to recover meaningful clusters of genomic regions, as used by DGW both in simulation validation (5 clusters) and interactive dgw-explorer analysis (45 clusters).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input peaks have not been DTW-warped and contain substantial noise/modifications (v or p above ~0.15) — the article shows standard hierarchical clustering without warping degrades badly (MCC ~0.294 at v=0.40, p=0.40) A fixed, validated cluster count is required but only a purely automatic cut with no ground truth or interactive inspection is possible — the article notes cutting the dendrogram 'at an appropriate level is a difficult choice' The data are already grouped by an external annotation (e.g. known TSS labels) and clustering would only duplicate existing structure

skills.description: Use when you have a dense node-embedding matrix (e.g. 16-dim per bin from a GAE encoder) and need per-point cluster labels without pre-specifying the number of clusters, including density-varying structure and noise points.
skills.name: hierarchical-density-noise-handling
skills.search_text: hierarchical-density-noise-handling Use when you have a dense node-embedding matrix (e.g. 16-dim per bin from a GAE encoder) and need per-point cluster labels without pre-specifying the number of clusters, including density-varying structure and noise points. The number of clusters is known in advance and you need centroid-based assignment rather than density-based hierarchical extraction Input is the raw Hi-C contact matrix rather than a trained GAE embedding — TOAST applies HDBSCAN only to the embeddings, not the 400x400 submatrices directly Every point must be assigned a meaningful cluster (HDBSCAN will flag low-density points as noise, which here translates to unclustered genomic bins) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Assigns a cluster label to every genomic bin by running HDBSCAN in unsupervised mode on 16-dimensional GAE embeddings derived from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices, letting the hierarchical density-based algorithm automatically discover clusters of varying densities and flag low-density bins as noise. This is the clustering step of TOAST that turns continuous embeddings into discrete labels from which TADs are delineated. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.09.019
skills.summary: Assigns a cluster label to every genomic bin by running HDBSCAN in unsupervised mode on 16-dimensional GAE embeddings derived from 400x400 Hi-C submatrices, letting the hierarchical density-based algorithm automatically discover clusters of varying densities and flag low-density bins as noise. This is the clustering step of TOAST that turns continuous embeddings into discrete labels from which TADs are delineated.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters is known in advance and you need centroid-based assignment rather than density-based hierarchical extraction Input is the raw Hi-C contact matrix rather than a trained GAE embedding — TOAST applies HDBSCAN only to the embeddings, not the 400x400 submatrices directly Every point must be assigned a meaningful cluster (HDBSCAN will flag low-density points as noise, which here translates to unclustered genomic bins)

skills.description: Use when you need to organize drugs by similarity of their RePhine TR response signatures and validate that drugs with the same mechanism of action (e.g., MEK, RAF, EGFR inhibitors) co-cluster.
skills.name: hierarchical-drug-clustering-ward-d
skills.search_text: hierarchical-drug-clustering-ward-d Use when you need to organize drugs by similarity of their RePhine TR response signatures and validate that drugs with the same mechanism of action (e.g., MEK, RAF, EGFR inhibitors) co-cluster. TR-drug associations are needed as independent biomarkers rather than a global drug-similarity view (use RePhine's uniP/multiP candidate ranking instead) Reliable ChIP-seq target information is unavailable or has too few targets, which would mislead TR identification downstream of RePhine Post-treatment/acquired-resistance dynamics are the target of the analysis — CCLE lacks post-treatment data, so secondary resistance (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation with erlotinib) cannot be captured http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Clusters CCLE drugs by mechanism of action using RePhine-derived TR response signatures (-Log10 uniP with direction) via hierarchical clustering in R's hclust, reproducing the Figure 3A grouping where MEK/RAF/MET inhibitors co-cluster. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008

skills.when_to_use_negative: TR-drug associations are needed as independent biomarkers rather than a global drug-similarity view (use RePhine's uniP/multiP candidate ranking instead) Reliable ChIP-seq target information is unavailable or has too few targets, which would mislead TR identification downstream of RePhine Post-treatment/acquired-resistance dynamics are the target of the analysis — CCLE lacks post-treatment data, so secondary resistance (e.g., acquired STAT3 activation with erlotinib) cannot be captured

skills.description: Use when you already have a BHi-Cect tree (nested list plus named locus-per-cluster list) and need to quantify each cluster's nested position and test whether nesting within global clusters associates with epigenomic activity (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1).
skills.name: hierarchical-nestedness-scoring
skills.search_text: hierarchical-nestedness-scoring Use when you already have a BHi-Cect tree (nested list plus named locus-per-cluster list) and need to quantify each cluster's nested position and test whether nesting within global clusters associates with epigenomic activity (DNase, LAD, ChromHMM, CAGE, RNA-seq, TF, RNAP2, CTCF/RAD21/CHD1). Input Hi-C data has not yet been clustered by BHi-Cect — the NS score requires the BPT tree and cluster-loci lists as prerequisites You need contiguous, coordinate-adjacent segmentation such as TADs — enclaves are mostly non-contiguous, deeply interwoven clusters that TAD-based contiguity-assuming methods mask No epigenomic annotation tracks are available for the cell line, in which case only the NS scoring step (not the enrichment contrast) can be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Computes a nestedness (NS) score for every cluster in a BHi-Cect partition tree (BPT) by anchoring top enclaves, intermediate nodes, and bottom enclaves/leaves at 0/0.5/1, then contrasts the NS score against epigenomic activity of the underlying DNA to reproduce the top- versus bottom-enclave antagonism. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Computes a nestedness (NS) score for every cluster in a BHi-Cect partition tree (BPT) by anchoring top enclaves, intermediate nodes, and bottom enclaves/leaves at 0/0.5/1, then contrasts the NS score against epigenomic activity of the underlying DNA to reproduce the top- versus bottom-enclave antagonism.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input Hi-C data has not yet been clustered by BHi-Cect — the NS score requires the BPT tree and cluster-loci lists as prerequisites You need contiguous, coordinate-adjacent segmentation such as TADs — enclaves are mostly non-contiguous, deeply interwoven clusters that TAD-based contiguity-assuming methods mask No epigenomic annotation tracks are available for the cell line, in which case only the NS scoring step (not the enrichment contrast) can be performed

skills.description: Use when you have mESC (or analogous) ChIP-seq BAM files for chromatin marks plus ranked RNA-seq expression data and need to test whether mark signal correlates with gene expression groups (high/moderate/silent).
skills.name: histone-mark-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: histone-mark-correlation-analysis Use when you have mESC (or analogous) ChIP-seq BAM files for chromatin marks plus ranked RNA-seq expression data and need to test whether mark signal correlates with gene expression groups (high/moderate/silent). The input is already a feature/coverage table or processed bigWig profiles — SeqCode expects BAM/SAM mapped reads plus chromInfo/refGene annotations, and bigwig generation is explicitly not supported. The analysis needs genome-browser visualization tracks or spike-in-corrected peak overlap statistics rather than signal-versus-expression-group comparison via boxplots. The ChIP-seq experiment includes spike-in material that requires manual spike-in normalization and your comparison design does not allow supplying that factor. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduces the correlation between normalized ChIP-seq signal of active (H3K4me3, H3K36me3, Ser5P, Ser2P) and repressive (H3K27me3, Suz12, Jarid2, Ring1b, H2Aub) chromatin marks and RNA-seq-defined expression classes of RefSeq genes, as demonstrated in the SeqCode article's Fig. 6 workflow using recoverChIPlevels and R-based boxplots. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Reproduces the correlation between normalized ChIP-seq signal of active (H3K4me3, H3K36me3, Ser5P, Ser2P) and repressive (H3K27me3, Suz12, Jarid2, Ring1b, H2Aub) chromatin marks and RNA-seq-defined expression classes of RefSeq genes, as demonstrated in the SeqCode article's Fig. 6 workflow using recoverChIPlevels and R-based boxplots.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a feature/coverage table or processed bigWig profiles — SeqCode expects BAM/SAM mapped reads plus chromInfo/refGene annotations, and bigwig generation is explicitly not supported. The analysis needs genome-browser visualization tracks or spike-in-corrected peak overlap statistics rather than signal-versus-expression-group comparison via boxplots. The ChIP-seq experiment includes spike-in material that requires manual spike-in normalization and your comparison design does not allow supplying that factor.

skills.name: histone-mark-odds-ratio-computation
skills.search_text: histone-mark-odds-ratio-computation Use when you have two sets of genomic intervals (e.g., true vs predicted regulatory indels) plus interval annotations for chromatin interactions or histone marks and need per-feature enrichment odds ratios. When the goal is to predict nc-sindel regulatory scores rather than quantify their regional enrichment — use the TIVAN-indel train.py/predict.py pipeline instead When annotations lack interval coordinates (e.g., only per-variant scores), since the contingency-table logic requires interval-overlap of sindels against regulatory features http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Quantifies enrichment or depletion of noncoding small indel (nc-sindel) label sets — true GTEx cis-eQTL labels and TIVAN-indel predicted scores — in regulatory regions (3DIV PE/PP promoter-centered interactions, Roadmap open chromatin, and seven histone marks) by building 2x2 contingency tables and applying Fisher's exact test to obtain odds ratios. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad060

skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to predict nc-sindel regulatory scores rather than quantify their regional enrichment — use the TIVAN-indel train.py/predict.py pipeline instead When annotations lack interval coordinates (e.g., only per-variant scores), since the contingency-table logic requires interval-overlap of sindels against regulatory features

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad diffuse histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3, H3K36me3, H3K79me2) between two samples/cell lines and peak-style callers would yield false positives/negatives.
skills.name: histone-modification-differential-region-calling
skills.search_text: histone-modification-differential-region-calling Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad diffuse histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3, H3K36me3, H3K79me2) between two samples/cell lines and peak-style callers would yield false positives/negatives. The histone mark has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods that search for peak-like features are the intended use case, and applying peak-style reasoning here generates many false positive or false negative calls Only a single sample needs modification calling without a two-sample comparison, and the univariate mode (run.univariate.hmm) alone would suffice The input is already a binned read-count feature table with no underlying BAM alignments for the comparison of interest http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply histoneHMM, a bivariate Hidden Markov Model R/C++ package, to call differentially modified histone regions between two ChIP-seq samples with broad genomic footprints (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3). The method aggregates short reads into 1000 bp binned bivariate read counts and probabilistically classifies bins as modified in both, unmodified in both, or differentially modified. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Apply histoneHMM, a bivariate Hidden Markov Model R/C++ package, to call differentially modified histone regions between two ChIP-seq samples with broad genomic footprints (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3). The method aggregates short reads into 1000 bp binned bivariate read counts and probabilistically classifies bins as modified in both, unmodified in both, or differentially modified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The histone mark has sharp, peak-like footprints rather than broad diffuse domains — methods that search for peak-like features are the intended use case, and applying peak-style reasoning here generates many false positive or false negative calls Only a single sample needs modification calling without a two-sample comparison, and the univariate mode (run.univariate.hmm) alone would suffice The input is already a binned read-count feature table with no underlying BAM alignments for the comparison of interest

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) between two samples to call modified or differentially modified regions, and peak-style callers would misclassify diffuse signals.
skills.name: histone-modification-em-mixture-fitting
skills.search_text: histone-modification-em-mixture-fitting Use when comparing ChIP-seq profiles of broad histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) between two samples to call modified or differentially modified regions, and peak-style callers would misclassify diffuse signals. The target histone mark produces sharp peak-like features rather than broad genomic footprints — methods designed for peak-like features are the article's stated motivation, and vice versa for narrow marks this HMM is not the intended tool Input is already a feature/bin count matrix rather than aligned BAM reads — binning and count aggregation steps would be redundant and should be skipped The analysis requires more than two ChIP-seq samples compared simultaneously — the bivariate HMM is defined for a two-sample comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Fit a bivariate Hidden Markov Model to binned ChIP-seq read counts from two samples using histoneHMM, estimating emission distributions via EM, transition probabilities via Baum-Welch, and per-bin posterior modification probabilities via the forward-backward algorithm, to classify genomic bins as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Fit a bivariate Hidden Markov Model to binned ChIP-seq read counts from two samples using histoneHMM, estimating emission distributions via EM, transition probabilities via Baum-Welch, and per-bin posterior modification probabilities via the forward-backward algorithm, to classify genomic bins as modified in both samples, unmodified in both, or differentially modified.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target histone mark produces sharp peak-like features rather than broad genomic footprints — methods designed for peak-like features are the article's stated motivation, and vice versa for narrow marks this HMM is not the intended tool Input is already a feature/bin count matrix rather than aligned BAM reads — binning and count aggregation steps would be redundant and should be skipped The analysis requires more than two ChIP-seq samples compared simultaneously — the bivariate HMM is defined for a two-sample comparison

skills.description: Use when a qPCR-validated or otherwise gold-standard ChIP-seq dataset of a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) is available and you need to quantify which peak caller detects modified versus unmodified regions via sensitivity-specificity/ROC analysis.
skills.name: histone-modification-peak-calling-comparison
skills.search_text: histone-modification-peak-calling-comparison Use when a qPCR-validated or otherwise gold-standard ChIP-seq dataset of a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) is available and you need to quantify which peak caller detects modified versus unmodified regions via sensitivity-specificity/ROC analysis. The mark has narrow, peak-like footprints (e.g. transcription factor binding or H3K4me3-like sharp peaks) — methods that search for peak-like features were designed for that regime, and the paper's rationale applies to broad diffuse modifications like H3K27me3 The goal is differential calling between two samples rather than single-sample modified-region detection — histoneHMM's bivariate differential mode, not this ROC benchmark, is the right tool No gold-standard (qPCR-validated) region set exists, so sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed against a truth set http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark histoneHMM's single-sample HMM-based calling of broad histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3) against competing peak callers (MACS2 broad, Zinba, SICER, BroadPeak, Rseg) by sweeping score thresholds and building ROC curves over qPCR-validated regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Benchmark histoneHMM's single-sample HMM-based calling of broad histone modifications (e.g. H3K27me3) against competing peak callers (MACS2 broad, Zinba, SICER, BroadPeak, Rseg) by sweeping score thresholds and building ROC curves over qPCR-validated regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The mark has narrow, peak-like footprints (e.g. transcription factor binding or H3K4me3-like sharp peaks) — methods that search for peak-like features were designed for that regime, and the paper's rationale applies to broad diffuse modifications like H3K27me3 The goal is differential calling between two samples rather than single-sample modified-region detection — histoneHMM's bivariate differential mode, not this ROC benchmark, is the right tool No gold-standard (qPCR-validated) region set exists, so sensitivity/specificity cannot be computed against a truth set

skills.description: Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering or alignment methods and you need ground-truth-labelled synthetic peak profiles derived from real ChIP-Seq (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) seed regions with known cluster-of-origin labels.
skills.name: histone-modification-peak-profile-processing
skills.search_text: histone-modification-peak-profile-processing Use when benchmarking peak-shape clustering or alignment methods and you need ground-truth-labelled synthetic peak profiles derived from real ChIP-Seq (e.g. ENCODE H3K4me3 K562) seed regions with known cluster-of-origin labels. Your input is already a curated set of real peak regions to be clustered for biological interpretation — this skill only creates synthetic ground-truth benchmarks You need to detect enriched regions from raw BAM files — use a peak caller such as MACS2 first; simulation assumes peak regions with binned read counts already exist The task requires multi-mark (e.g. H3K4me3 + H3K9ac) joint simulation — the described procedure perturbs single-mark H3K4me3 seed profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 A simulation-based workflow for generating synthetic histone-modification peak-profile datasets seeded from real ENCODE H3K4me3 read-count profiles, perturbing them with multiplicative Gaussian noise, bin duplication/deletion, and orientation flips to create labelled benchmark data for clustering evaluation. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: A simulation-based workflow for generating synthetic histone-modification peak-profile datasets seeded from real ENCODE H3K4me3 read-count profiles, perturbing them with multiplicative Gaussian noise, bin duplication/deletion, and orientation flips to create labelled benchmark data for clustering evaluation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a curated set of real peak regions to be clustered for biological interpretation — this skill only creates synthetic ground-truth benchmarks You need to detect enriched regions from raw BAM files — use a peak caller such as MACS2 first; simulation assumes peak regions with binned read counts already exist The task requires multi-mark (e.g. H3K4me3 + H3K9ac) joint simulation — the described procedure perturbs single-mark H3K4me3 seed profiles

skills.description: Use when you have two BED-format ChIP-seq peak lists (chromosome, start, end) for different histone marks and need to partition their union into mark-specific and overlapping classes (e.g. active/bivalent/silent promoters).
skills.name: histone-modification-peak-set-processing
skills.search_text: histone-modification-peak-set-processing Use when you have two BED-format ChIP-seq peak lists (chromosome, start, end) for different histone marks and need to partition their union into mark-specific and overlapping classes (e.g. active/bivalent/silent promoters). Input is raw sequencing reads rather than called peak lists — peak calling (e.g. MACS) must be performed first The goal is signal visualization (meta-plots, heatmaps, TSS maps) rather than overlap classification of two peak sets Only one histone mark or ChIP-seq peak set is available, since class assignment requires comparing two sets Classifies ChIP-seq peak sets of two histone marks into mutually exclusive overlap classes using SeqCode's matchpeaks command: for mESC H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 peaks this yields active (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3–), bivalent (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+), and silent (H3K4me3–/H3K27me3+) classes. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Classifies ChIP-seq peak sets of two histone marks into mutually exclusive overlap classes using SeqCode's matchpeaks command: for mESC H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 peaks this yields active (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3–), bivalent (H3K4me3+/H3K27me3+), and silent (H3K4me3–/H3K27me3+) classes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads rather than called peak lists — peak calling (e.g. MACS) must be performed first The goal is signal visualization (meta-plots, heatmaps, TSS maps) rather than overlap classification of two peak sets Only one histone mark or ChIP-seq peak set is available, since class assignment requires comparing two sets

skills.description: Use when reproducing or auditing histoneHMM's emission model: you have binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts from two samples (e.g. BN vs SHR) and need to verify the four-component copula fit yields coherent modified/unmodified/differential state classes.
skills.name: histone-modification-state-structure-verification
skills.search_text: histone-modification-state-structure-verification Use when reproducing or auditing histoneHMM's emission model: you have binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts from two samples (e.g. BN vs SHR) and need to verify the four-component copula fit yields coherent modified/unmodified/differential state classes. Input is raw BAM/bed reads rather than preprocessed binned read counts — run the histoneHMM preprocessing (preprocess.for.hmm, countBamInGRanges, truncation at the upper 0.1 percentile) first The analysis goal is peak-like modification calling in a single sample with narrow marks, where broad-footprint bivariate differential modeling is not the appropriate scope Only one ChIP-seq sample is available — the Gaussian-copula coupling requires two samples to construct the bivariate emission density http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reconstructs and verifies the Gaussian-copula bivariate emission model underlying histoneHMM, confirming that the four mixture components of the coupled zero-inflated negative-binomial marginals map onto the modified-in-both, unmodified-in-both, and differentially-modified state classes. This validates the probabilistic state structure that drives histoneHMM's three-state genomic region classifications. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Reconstructs and verifies the Gaussian-copula bivariate emission model underlying histoneHMM, confirming that the four mixture components of the coupled zero-inflated negative-binomial marginals map onto the modified-in-both, unmodified-in-both, and differentially-modified state classes. This validates the probabilistic state structure that drives histoneHMM's three-state genomic region classifications.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw BAM/bed reads rather than preprocessed binned read counts — run the histoneHMM preprocessing (preprocess.for.hmm, countBamInGRanges, truncation at the upper 0.1 percentile) first The analysis goal is peak-like modification calling in a single sample with narrow marks, where broad-footprint bivariate differential modeling is not the appropriate scope Only one ChIP-seq sample is available — the Gaussian-copula coupling requires two samples to construct the bivariate emission density

skills.description: Use when a new ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs QC assessment against historical public data, or when validating whether read-layer metrics (FastQC score, mapped ratio, PBC) are assay-type independent.
skills.name: historical-qc-atlas-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: historical-qc-atlas-benchmark-comparison Use when a new ChIP-seq or DNase-seq sample needs QC assessment against historical public data, or when validating whether read-layer metrics (FastQC score, mapped ratio, PBC) are assay-type independent. The analysis goal is peak-level or peak-layer QC (FRiP score, replicate peak overlap/correlation, fragment size estimation) rather than read-layer metrics. Input data is not ChIP-seq or DNase-seq (e.g. RNA-seq or ATAC-seq), since the atlas cutoffs were derived specifically from ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples. Only a handful of samples exist, so cumulative distribution statistics over the eight categories cannot be meaningfully estimated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Reproduces ChiLin's read-layer QC quality atlas by computing cumulative distributions of FastQC sequence quality scores, uniquely mapped read ratios (bwa), and PBC values over thousands of public ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples, deriving assay-type-insensitive cutoffs (quality score >25, unique ratio >0.5, PBC >0.8), and benchmarking new samples against these historical distributions. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Reproduces ChiLin's read-layer QC quality atlas by computing cumulative distributions of FastQC sequence quality scores, uniquely mapped read ratios (bwa), and PBC values over thousands of public ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples, deriving assay-type-insensitive cutoffs (quality score >25, unique ratio >0.5, PBC >0.8), and benchmarking new samples against these historical distributions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is peak-level or peak-layer QC (FRiP score, replicate peak overlap/correlation, fragment size estimation) rather than read-layer metrics. Input data is not ChIP-seq or DNase-seq (e.g. RNA-seq or ATAC-seq), since the atlas cutoffs were derived specifically from ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples. Only a handful of samples exist, so cumulative distribution statistics over the eight categories cannot be meaningfully estimated.

skills.description: Use when calling protein-DNA binding sites from ChIP-Seq BED or ELAND read files (single-end or paired-end), especially when reproducing HPeak peak counts or comparing peak callers on datasets such as STAT1, NRSF, H3K4me3, or H3K27me3.
skills.name: hmm-based-enriched-region-detection
skills.search_text: hmm-based-enriched-region-detection Use when calling protein-DNA binding sites from ChIP-Seq BED or ELAND read files (single-end or paired-end), especially when reproducing HPeak peak counts or comparing peak callers on datasets such as STAT1, NRSF, H3K4me3, or H3K27me3. Data are comparative histone-modification differences only — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to that comparative setting, not HPeak. You need strand/orientation-aware summit refinement — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak. Your primary goal is a well-calibrated false detection rate — the paper states HPeak's model is not well-suited for quantifying FDR. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detect ChIP-enriched genomic regions from ChIP-Seq short-read data with HPeak, a two-state Hidden Markov Model that models read-enriched blocks against background using GP and ZIP emission distributions applied to a 25-bp binned HDF coverage profile. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Detect ChIP-enriched genomic regions from ChIP-Seq short-read data with HPeak, a two-state Hidden Markov Model that models read-enriched blocks against background using GP and ZIP emission distributions applied to a 25-bp binned HDF coverage profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are comparative histone-modification differences only — the article notes ChIPDiff is the method restricted to that comparative setting, not HPeak. You need strand/orientation-aware summit refinement — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak. Your primary goal is a well-calibrated false detection rate — the paper states HPeak's model is not well-suited for quantifying FDR.

skills.description: Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genome sequence and need probabilistic genome-wide occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors, especially to benchmark against NucleoATAC, DANPOS2, or MACS2+FIMO.
skills.name: hmm-based-occupancy-modeling
skills.search_text: hmm-based-occupancy-modeling Use when you have paired-end MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq data plus genome sequence and need probabilistic genome-wide occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors, especially to benchmark against NucleoATAC, DANPOS2, or MACS2+FIMO. You only need a small set of TF binding sites from peak calling — a MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling pipeline is the alternative the paper benchmarks against, though RoboCOP outperforms it Your data are single-end or not chromatin accessibility data (MNase-seq/ATAC-seq) — RoboCOP currently uses only MNase-seq or ATAC-seq as input You need occupancy profiles for organisms/data types outside the model's current scope (yeast, paired-end MNase-seq/ATAC-seq) without adapting the model http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Apply RoboCOP, a multivariate state space/hidden Markov model that integrates chromatin accessibility data (MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence, to jointly compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy scores for nucleosomes and hundreds of DNA-binding factors at single-nucleotide resolution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Apply RoboCOP, a multivariate state space/hidden Markov model that integrates chromatin accessibility data (MNase-seq and/or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence, to jointly compute genome-wide probabilistic occupancy scores for nucleosomes and hundreds of DNA-binding factors at single-nucleotide resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a small set of TF binding sites from peak calling — a MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling pipeline is the alternative the paper benchmarks against, though RoboCOP outperforms it Your data are single-end or not chromatin accessibility data (MNase-seq/ATAC-seq) — RoboCOP currently uses only MNase-seq or ATAC-seq as input You need occupancy profiles for organisms/data types outside the model's current scope (yeast, paired-end MNase-seq/ATAC-seq) without adapting the model

skills.description: Use when calling protein-DNA binding peaks from short-read ChIP-Seq data with explicit statistical modeling of sequencing noise, or when reproducing HPeak peak counts and motif-enrichment comparisons against other peak-callers on datasets like the NRSF ChIP-Seq data.
skills.name: hmm-coverage-profile-modeling
skills.search_text: hmm-coverage-profile-modeling Use when calling protein-DNA binding peaks from short-read ChIP-Seq data with explicit statistical modeling of sequencing noise, or when reproducing HPeak peak counts and motif-enrichment comparisons against other peak-callers on datasets like the NRSF ChIP-Seq data. Analyzing comparative histone modification ChIP data — the article notes ChIPDiff is designed specifically for that comparative setting, not standard binding-site peak calling. Quantifying false detection rate is a primary goal — the article states 'our method is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', so comparisons may disadvantage some methods. The input is already a peak list or motif enrichment table rather than raw short-read alignments. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Model ChIP-Seq read coverage as a two-state Hidden Markov Model over fixed-length genomic bins to statistically distinguish ChIP-enriched regions from background noise, using a Generalized Poisson emission for enriched bins and a Zero-Inflated Poisson emission for background bins (as implemented in HPeak). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Model ChIP-Seq read coverage as a two-state Hidden Markov Model over fixed-length genomic bins to statistically distinguish ChIP-enriched regions from background noise, using a Generalized Poisson emission for enriched bins and a Zero-Inflated Poisson emission for background bins (as implemented in HPeak).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Analyzing comparative histone modification ChIP data — the article notes ChIPDiff is designed specifically for that comparative setting, not standard binding-site peak calling. Quantifying false detection rate is a primary goal — the article states 'our method is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', so comparisons may disadvantage some methods. The input is already a peak list or motif enrichment table rather than raw short-read alignments.

skills.description: Use when you have histoneHMM differential calls for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K9me3 female-vs-mouse male) and need to evaluate them against a defined gene set by base-pair and gene-count overlap.
skills.name: hmm-differential-call-post-processing
skills.search_text: hmm-differential-call-post-processing Use when you have histoneHMM differential calls for a broad histone mark (e.g. H3K9me3 female-vs-mouse male) and need to evaluate them against a defined gene set by base-pair and gene-count overlap. The input is single-sample modified-region calls rather than two-sample differential calls from get.differential.regions The target annotation includes exons/UTRs and the benchmark requires gene-body-only overlaps, so raw exon-level annotation would change the base-pair denominators The goal is peak-like (narrow) mark analysis; the article notes methods searching for peak-like features on broad marks such as H3K27me3/H3K9me3 generate false positives/negatives http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Post-process histoneHMM differential region calls (from get.differential.regions, exported as BED) by converting them to GenomicRanges with bed2GR and intersecting them with gene annotations loaded via gff2GR to quantify functional overlap, e.g. percent of X-inactivated gene base pairs and genes called differentially modified. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6

skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-sample modified-region calls rather than two-sample differential calls from get.differential.regions The target annotation includes exons/UTRs and the benchmark requires gene-body-only overlaps, so raw exon-level annotation would change the base-pair denominators The goal is peak-like (narrow) mark analysis; the article notes methods searching for peak-like features on broad marks such as H3K27me3/H3K9me3 generate false positives/negatives

skills.description: Use when calling ChIP-Seq peaks with a two-state HMM over 25 bp HDF coverage bins and you need defensible starting values for transition and GP/ZIP emission parameters prior to Viterbi refinement.
skills.name: hmm-initialization-from-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: hmm-initialization-from-summary-statistics Use when calling ChIP-Seq peaks with a two-state HMM over 25 bp HDF coverage bins and you need defensible starting values for transition and GP/ZIP emission parameters prior to Viterbi refinement. You need to quantify a false detection rate for called peaks — the paper states the method 'is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', so evaluation-focused pipelines should not rely on it for FDR You need peak summits distinguished by read orientation — HPeak 'does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak', a feature deferred to a future release You need a refined distributional fit comparison (e.g., Poisson vs NB vs GP/ZIP) rather than peak classification — the paper's distribution-fitting analyses are descriptive support, not the classification task itself http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Initialize HPeak's two-state hidden Markov model (ChIP-enriched state with Generalized Poisson emissions, background state with zero-inflated Poisson emissions) using quick, rough parameter estimates computed from summary statistics of per-bin HDF coverage counts, before refining them with Viterbi-based estimation. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Initialize HPeak's two-state hidden Markov model (ChIP-enriched state with Generalized Poisson emissions, background state with zero-inflated Poisson emissions) using quick, rough parameter estimates computed from summary statistics of per-bin HDF coverage counts, before refining them with Viterbi-based estimation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to quantify a false detection rate for called peaks — the paper states the method 'is not well-suited for quantifying false detection rate', so evaluation-focused pipelines should not rely on it for FDR You need peak summits distinguished by read orientation — HPeak 'does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak', a feature deferred to a future release You need a refined distributional fit comparison (e.g., Poisson vs NB vs GP/ZIP) rather than peak classification — the paper's distribution-fitting analyses are descriptive support, not the classification task itself

skills.search_text: hmm-posterior-decoding-forward-backward Use when you need probabilistic, per-genomic-region classifications of ChIP-seq enrichment for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3, H3K9me3) rather than binary peak calls, in one- or two-sample comparisons. skills.when_to_use_negative: The signal consists of sharp, peak-like features (e.g. transcription factor or H3K4me3-like punctate marks) where peak-calling methods are appropriate and the broad-footprint binning model adds no benefit You need only a single input already reduced to a feature or region table — the skill expects raw aligned reads (BAM) aggregated over genomic bins You require fully deterministic binary state assignments without uncertainty; use Viterbi decoding (hmm.viterbi) instead of posterior decoding

skills.search_text: hns-doublet-peak-detection Use when ChIP-seq peak coordinates need to be scanned for paired peaks (doublets) with an intervening trough, or when relating doublet peaks to a second transcription factor's ChIP-seq binding sites within a fixed genomic distance. skills.description: Use when a promoter or intergenic FASTA must be scanned for H-NS nucleation motifs to test whether H-NS binding sites overlap established LuxR binding sites, as for PluxCDABE.
skills.name: hns-nucleation-site-prediction
skills.search_text: hns-nucleation-site-prediction Use when a promoter or intergenic FASTA must be scanned for H-NS nucleation motifs to test whether H-NS binding sites overlap established LuxR binding sites, as for PluxCDABE. skills.summary: In silico validation of predicted candidate cancer drivers by one-sided Fisher exact (hypergeometric) enrichment of each per-sample driver list against compendia of known oncogenes and tumor suppressors, with FDR correction, as used to validate iEDGE Rank-1 cis drivers across 19 TCGA cancer types.
