skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq/DNase counts in peaks vary between cells or samples and de novo motif discovery is the goal: rank bias-corrected k-mer deviations by covariance, assemble PWMs with assembleKmers, then match to JASPAR via pwmDistance.

skills.search_text: kmer-variability-deviation-analysis Use when scATAC-seq/DNase counts in peaks vary between cells or samples and de novo motif discovery is the goal: rank bias-corrected k-mer deviations by covariance, assemble PWMs with assembleKmers, then match to JASPAR via pwmDistance. The task is scoring a curated known-motif collection (e.g., getJasparMotifs/human_pwms_v1) rather than discovering de novo motifs — matchMotifs + computeDeviations is the appropriate path. You have not yet run the first round: anchor selection depends on first-round prediction entropies, so no pseudo labels or anchors exist to train the KD model. skills.search_text: lda-collapsed-gibbs-sampler-execution Use when a cisTopic object holding a binarized accessibility matrix (e.g. 5,335 PBMC cells × ~97k regions) is ready and a sweep of LDA topic models across a topic-number grid is required for subsequent model selection. skills.summary: Fit a grid of Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic models on a binary single-cell accessibility matrix using cisTopic's runModels(), which applies LDA with a collapsed Gibbs sampler (Griffiths & Steyvers, 2004, via the lda package) over a range of topic numbers so model selection by log likelihood is possible downstream.

skills.description: Use when cisTopic has fitted multiple LDA models (e.g. 2–40 topics via runModels) on single-cell ATAC-seq data and you must pick one optimal topic number for downstream cell-state and cis-regulatory topic analysis.
skills.name: lda-log-likelihood-comparison
skills.search_text: lda-log-likelihood-comparison Use when cisTopic has fitted multiple LDA models (e.g. 2–40 topics via runModels) on single-cell ATAC-seq data and you must pick one optimal topic number for downstream cell-state and cis-regulatory topic analysis. When only a single model with a fixed topic number has been fitted — there is nothing to compare and selectModel has no basis for selection When log-likelihood curves have not stabilized after burnin — comparisons of final likelihoods would be unreliable and models should be refit with more iterations When working in the pycisTopic (Python) ecosystem, which replaced the deprecated cisTopic R package and uses different model selection tooling http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Selects the optimal LDA topic model in cisTopic by comparing final-iteration log likelihoods (P(D|T)) across models built with different topic counts, choosing the model with the highest log likelihood (ties broken toward fewer topics). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-019-0367-1
skills.summary: Selects the optimal LDA topic model in cisTopic by comparing final-iteration log likelihoods (P(D|T)) across models built with different topic counts, choosing the model with the highest log likelihood (ties broken toward fewer topics).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single model with a fixed topic number has been fitted — there is nothing to compare and selectModel has no basis for selection When log-likelihood curves have not stabilized after burnin — comparisons of final likelihoods would be unreliable and models should be refit with more iterations When working in the pycisTopic (Python) ecosystem, which replaced the deprecated cisTopic R package and uses different model selection tooling

skills.name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cross-validation Use when benchmarking cross-species regulatory-element mapping accuracy with matched orthologous functional genomic datasets (e.g. 67 matched human-mouse ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq sets), where each dataset must be held out in turn. When only one query dataset is available per species pair, so excluding it would leave no epigenomic signal repertoire for similarity calculations When the goal is de novo mapping without matched orthologous epigenome data to serve as LOOCV ground truth http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 A LOOCV protocol for benchmarking AdaLiftOver: for each matched epigenome dataset, map its query regions to the orthologous genome while excluding that dataset from epigenomic signal similarity calculations, then score precision/AUROC/AUPR across all folds. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: A LOOCV protocol for benchmarking AdaLiftOver: for each matched epigenome dataset, map its query regions to the orthologous genome while excluding that dataset from epigenomic signal similarity calculations, then score precision/AUROC/AUPR across all folds.

skills.search_text: leave-one-out-cross-validation-of-calibration-models Use when you have calibration data on standard controls of known methylation percentage (e.g. 0–100% AMP dilutions) measured across multiple CpGs and need to compare predictive performance of competing calibration models per assay. skills.description: Use when a snap-format scATAC-seq dataset has been filtered and dimensionality-reduced (e.g. via runDimReduct on the Jaccard-normalized cell-by-bin matrix) and you need unsupervised cell-type clustering without prior peak annotation.
skills.name: leiden-clustering-of-single-cell-data
skills.search_text: leiden-clustering-of-single-cell-data Use when a snap-format scATAC-seq dataset has been filtered and dimensionality-reduced (e.g. via runDimReduct on the Jaccard-normalized cell-by-bin matrix) and you need unsupervised cell-type clustering without prior peak annotation. Input is already a peak-based feature matrix or aggregate population-level peak annotation — the article argues peak-based approaches bias toward abundant cell types and require robust aggregate signals You need a scaled pipeline beyond the legacy stack — SnapATAC 2.0 (scverse/SnapATAC2) is the maintained successor, and legacy SnapATAC requires R >= 3.4.0 & < 3.6.0 (rhdf5 incompatibility with 3.6) Cells have not been filtered or dimensionality-reduced; clustering raw sparse profiles (5–15% of peaks detected per cell) is the very problem this skill presumes you have already mitigated http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Cluster single-cell ATAC-seq cells using the Leiden algorithm, as implemented in SnapATAC's runCluster on dimensionality-reduced cell-by-bin embeddings, to dissect cellular heterogeneity into discrete cell populations. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Cluster single-cell ATAC-seq cells using the Leiden algorithm, as implemented in SnapATAC's runCluster on dimensionality-reduced cell-by-bin embeddings, to dissect cellular heterogeneity into discrete cell populations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-based feature matrix or aggregate population-level peak annotation — the article argues peak-based approaches bias toward abundant cell types and require robust aggregate signals You need a scaled pipeline beyond the legacy stack — SnapATAC 2.0 (scverse/SnapATAC2) is the maintained successor, and legacy SnapATAC requires R >= 3.4.0 & < 3.6.0 (rhdf5 incompatibility with 3.6) Cells have not been filtered or dimensionality-reduced; clustering raw sparse profiles (5–15% of peaks detected per cell) is the very problem this skill presumes you have already mitigated

skills.description: Use when motif-based (BOM) predictions transfer across species and you need to quantify how many predicted CREs lack detectable cross-species sequence alignment, as in mouse-trained models tested on human fetal CREs.
skills.name: liftover-genomic-coordinate-mapping
skills.search_text: liftover-genomic-coordinate-mapping Use when motif-based (BOM) predictions transfer across species and you need to quantify how many predicted CREs lack detectable cross-species sequence alignment, as in mouse-trained models tested on human fetal CREs. The question is motif importance or SHAP-based interpretation within a single species/condition, not cross-species coordinate correspondence. Input is a motif count matrix or model training output rather than genomic coordinates of predicted elements. The CREs are known a priori to be sequence-homologous across species, so the alignment-dependence assessment is moot. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Maps correctly predicted cross-species cis-regulatory elements between genomes (human-to-mouse) using UCSC liftOver at strict (minMatch 0.95) and relaxed (minMatch 0.6) alignment thresholds, to test whether motif-based BOM predictions depend on detectable mouse-human sequence alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Maps correctly predicted cross-species cis-regulatory elements between genomes (human-to-mouse) using UCSC liftOver at strict (minMatch 0.95) and relaxed (minMatch 0.6) alignment thresholds, to test whether motif-based BOM predictions depend on detectable mouse-human sequence alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is motif importance or SHAP-based interpretation within a single species/condition, not cross-species coordinate correspondence. Input is a motif count matrix or model training output rather than genomic coordinates of predicted elements. The CREs are known a priori to be sequence-homologous across species, so the alignment-dependence assessment is moot.

skills.description: Use when fine-mapped SNP coordinates (e.g., hg38 GWAS SNPs) must be lifted to another genome (e.g., mouse mm10) and a head-to-head mapping-rate vs. precision comparison of UCSC liftOver and AdaLiftOver is needed.
skills.name: liftover-mapping-rate-precision-comparison
skills.search_text: liftover-mapping-rate-precision-comparison Use when fine-mapped SNP coordinates (e.g., hg38 GWAS SNPs) must be lifted to another genome (e.g., mouse mm10) and a head-to-head mapping-rate vs. precision comparison of UCSC liftOver and AdaLiftOver is needed. Query regions are protein-coding or otherwise well-conserved intervals where standard UCSC liftOver is sufficient and epigenomic signal data for the target organism is unavailable. No orthologous functional genomic datasets exist for the target species, since AdaLiftOver's scoring depends on epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarities computed from matched datasets. The analysis needs a single-method coordinate conversion rather than a benchmark comparison of mapping rate versus precision. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks UCSC liftOver against AdaLiftOver for mapping fine-mapped GWAS SNPs across species (e.g., hg38 SCZ SNPs to mouse mm10), tabulating mapped-SNP counts, mapping rates, and average precision to quantify the trade-off between mapping more SNPs and mapping functionally similar loci. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Benchmarks UCSC liftOver against AdaLiftOver for mapping fine-mapped GWAS SNPs across species (e.g., hg38 SCZ SNPs to mouse mm10), tabulating mapped-SNP counts, mapping rates, and average precision to quantify the trade-off between mapping more SNPs and mapping functionally similar loci.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Query regions are protein-coding or otherwise well-conserved intervals where standard UCSC liftOver is sufficient and epigenomic signal data for the target organism is unavailable. No orthologous functional genomic datasets exist for the target species, since AdaLiftOver's scoring depends on epigenomic signal and sequence grammar similarities computed from matched datasets. The analysis needs a single-method coordinate conversion rather than a benchmark comparison of mapping rate versus precision.

skills.description: Use when comparing cross-species regulatory-element mapping precision of AdaLiftOver vs UCSC liftOver, or when validating liftOver-based SNP-to-gene mappings against a known positive-control gene list such as BMD genes.
skills.name: liftover-precision-benchmarking
skills.search_text: liftover-precision-benchmarking Use when comparing cross-species regulatory-element mapping precision of AdaLiftOver vs UCSC liftOver, or when validating liftOver-based SNP-to-gene mappings against a known positive-control gene list such as BMD genes. When the query regions are coding/exonic and standard UCSC liftOver chain mapping is sufficient — AdaLiftOver targets orthologous non-coding regulatory elements When no matched human-target-species epigenomic datasets or training data are available to estimate logistic regression parameters and an optimal score threshold When the goal is coordinate conversion only (no prioritization of candidate target regions by regulatory similarity) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Benchmark the precision of AdaLiftOver's epigenome- and grammar-aware orthologous mapping against UCSC liftOver using curated positive-control gene sets, as demonstrated by mapping fine-mapped human BMD GWAS SNPs (PIP ≥ 0.001) to mouse and scoring recovery of 90 BMD genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Benchmark the precision of AdaLiftOver's epigenome- and grammar-aware orthologous mapping against UCSC liftOver using curated positive-control gene sets, as demonstrated by mapping fine-mapped human BMD GWAS SNPs (PIP ≥ 0.001) to mouse and scoring recovery of 90 BMD genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the query regions are coding/exonic and standard UCSC liftOver chain mapping is sufficient — AdaLiftOver targets orthologous non-coding regulatory elements When no matched human-target-species epigenomic datasets or training data are available to estimate logistic regression parameters and an optimal score threshold When the goal is coordinate conversion only (no prioritization of candidate target regions by regulatory similarity)

skills.description: Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split into bifurcation groups to define candidate branching points of a tree-structure (input-output hidden Markov) model prior to Baum-Welch training, as in TSMiner's LR mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq analysis.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-test-gene-set-partitioning
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-test-gene-set-partitioning Use when a time-series expression matrix must be split into bifurcation groups to define candidate branching points of a tree-structure (input-output hidden Markov) model prior to Baum-Welch training, as in TSMiner's LR mouse liver regeneration RNA-seq analysis. The expression data are not time-series (no successive time points), so fold changes relative to a preceding time point and the nc comparison vector cannot be computed The goal is static clustering of profiles without a tree-structure model — the article notes clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways, so this partitioning is instead intended to seed bifurcations of a time-specific regulatory model http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A statistical partitioning step from TSMiner that classifies genes at candidate bifurcation time points of a time-series expression matrix (up-, down-, or unchanged relative to the preceding time point) and applies a likelihood ratio test to divide the gene set G into groups, defining the candidate branching (split) points of a tree-structure model. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: A statistical partitioning step from TSMiner that classifies genes at candidate bifurcation time points of a time-series expression matrix (up-, down-, or unchanged relative to the preceding time point) and applies a likelihood ratio test to divide the gene set G into groups, defining the candidate branching (split) points of a tree-structure model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are not time-series (no successive time points), so fold changes relative to a preceding time point and the nc comparison vector cannot be computed The goal is static clustering of profiles without a tree-structure model — the article notes clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways, so this partitioning is instead intended to seed bifurcations of a time-specific regulatory model

skills.description: Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's target gene is differentially expressed between samples mutated in that element and wild-type samples, while explicitly correcting for somatic copy-number state (SCNA) and tumour tissue label.
skills.name: likelihood-ratio-testing
skills.search_text: likelihood-ratio-testing Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's target gene is differentially expressed between samples mutated in that element and wild-type samples, while explicitly correcting for somatic copy-number state (SCNA) and tumour tissue label. Input is already a raw mutation burden feature table for DriverPower's model/infer subcommands rather than per-sample expression quantifications Only ~3.7% of the genome was studied; do not use this to assess driver activity for regulatory elements without expression or SCNA annotations Tumour types with fewer than 30 samples lack statistical power for reliable GLM-based expression testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Nested-model likelihood ratio testing to obtain copy-number-corrected differential expression p values for DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates, e.g. SGK1 and GPR126, from PCAWG FPKM-UQ expression data. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Nested-model likelihood ratio testing to obtain copy-number-corrected differential expression p values for DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates, e.g. SGK1 and GPR126, from PCAWG FPKM-UQ expression data.

skills.description: Use when paired copy-number/alteration calls (e.g., GISTIC2.0 focal SCNA peaks) and a log2 gene-expression matrix over the same tumor samples must be tested for cis/trans differential expression with limma linear models.
skills.name: limma-linear-model-testing
skills.search_text: limma-linear-model-testing Use when paired copy-number/alteration calls (e.g., GISTIC2.0 focal SCNA peaks) and a log2 gene-expression matrix over the same tumor samples must be tested for cis/trans differential expression with limma linear models. Samples are unpaired or alteration status and expression profiles do not share sample identifiers, so alteration-positive/negative groups cannot be formed The goal is mediation analysis of cis-to-trans effects rather than the upstream cis/trans differential-expression signature (use the iEDGE mediation/Sobel module instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Differential-expression testing of cis and trans genes against epi-DNA alteration status using limma-based linear models, as implemented in iEDGE's iEDGE_DE module (e.g., reproducing TCGA BRCA focal SCNA signatures in Supplemental Tables S1 and S2). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Differential-expression testing of cis and trans genes against epi-DNA alteration status using limma-based linear models, as implemented in iEDGE's iEDGE_DE module (e.g., reproducing TCGA BRCA focal SCNA signatures in Supplemental Tables S1 and S2).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples are unpaired or alteration status and expression profiles do not share sample identifiers, so alteration-positive/negative groups cannot be formed The goal is mediation analysis of cis-to-trans effects rather than the upstream cis/trans differential-expression signature (use the iEDGE mediation/Sobel module instead)

skills.description: Use when Skipper has flagged enriched repetitive elements in eCLIP IP-vs-input experiments and you need to characterize binding orientation and evolutionary age of LINE1 elements for specific RBPs such as MATR3 or SAFB2.
skills.name: line1-strand-and-age-stratification-analysis
skills.search_text: line1-strand-and-age-stratification-analysis Use when Skipper has flagged enriched repetitive elements in eCLIP IP-vs-input experiments and you need to characterize binding orientation and evolutionary age of LINE1 elements for specific RBPs such as MATR3 or SAFB2. The eCLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, so Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model for enrichment testing The goal is transcriptomic (gene-region) binding site detection rather than multi-mapping repetitive-element binding Input samples have not yet been run through the Skipper Snakemake pipeline to produce per-element enrichment statistics http://edamontology.org/topic_0114 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Stratifies Skipper-detected enriched LINE1 repetitive elements by genomic strand and element age to verify reported RBP binding patterns (e.g., MATR3 and SAFB2 preferential strand/age enrichment) after beta-binomial enrichment testing of RepeatMasker-annotated elements across eCLIP datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Stratifies Skipper-detected enriched LINE1 repetitive elements by genomic strand and element age to verify reported RBP binding patterns (e.g., MATR3 and SAFB2 preferential strand/age enrichment) after beta-binomial enrichment testing of RepeatMasker-annotated elements across eCLIP datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The eCLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, so Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model for enrichment testing The goal is transcriptomic (gene-region) binding site detection rather than multi-mapping repetitive-element binding Input samples have not yet been run through the Skipper Snakemake pipeline to produce per-element enrichment statistics

skills.description: Use when evaluating how one prediction parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) affects accuracy (AUC) across multiple conditions, and confounders like peak filtering method or masking covariate must be controlled.
skills.name: linear-model-covariate-adjustment
skills.search_text: linear-model-covariate-adjustment Use when evaluating how one prediction parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) affects accuracy (AUC) across multiple conditions, and confounders like peak filtering method or masking covariate must be controlled. When the design varies only one factor with no confounding covariates — a simple paired comparison suffices and the nested-model machinery is unnecessary. When the outcome is not a continuous performance metric such as AUC but raw peak counts or sequence-level predictions — the lm formula and nesting structure would need to be redefined. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fit a full linear model on AUC values that includes the parameter of interest (minimal TPX length) alongside covariates (peak filtering method, ssRNA, n peaks), then compare it to a nested model without that term using R's anova to isolate the parameter's contribution while controlling for confounders. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Fit a full linear model on AUC values that includes the parameter of interest (minimal TPX length) alongside covariates (peak filtering method, ssRNA, n peaks), then compare it to a nested model without that term using R's anova to isolate the parameter's contribution while controlling for confounders.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the design varies only one factor with no confounding covariates — a simple paired comparison suffices and the nested-model machinery is unnecessary. When the outcome is not a continuous performance metric such as AUC but raw peak counts or sequence-level predictions — the lm formula and nesting structure would need to be redefined.

skills.description: Use when you have paired chromatin accessibility (DNase1-seq) and RNA-seq expression data across many samples/cell types and need to identify putative REMs that explain expression variation of specific genes.
skills.name: linear-regression-gene-expression-modeling
skills.search_text: linear-regression-gene-expression-modeling Use when you have paired chromatin accessibility (DNase1-seq) and RNA-seq expression data across many samples/cell types and need to identify putative REMs that explain expression variation of specific genes. Input is a single sample without matched DNase1-seq accessibility and RNA-seq expression across multiple conditions — the linear model requires variation across samples to correlate signal with expression. The goal is de novo peak calling from raw reads rather than annotating regions in relation to actual gene expression changes; StitchIt is not a peak caller. You already have REM–gene associations and only need retrieval or TF motif analysis — use EpiRegio's Gene Query / Region Query instead of refitting the model. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits the STITCHIT linear model that partitions a gene's search window into regions whose depth-normalized DNase1-seq signal correlates with gene expression (transcripts per million), yielding regulatory elements (REMs) with regression coefficients. This is the core gene-centric approach behind EpiRegio's REM–gene associations. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Fits the STITCHIT linear model that partitions a gene's search window into regions whose depth-normalized DNase1-seq signal correlates with gene expression (transcripts per million), yielding regulatory elements (REMs) with regression coefficients. This is the core gene-centric approach behind EpiRegio's REM–gene associations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single sample without matched DNase1-seq accessibility and RNA-seq expression across multiple conditions — the linear model requires variation across samples to correlate signal with expression. The goal is de novo peak calling from raw reads rather than annotating regions in relation to actual gene expression changes; StitchIt is not a peak caller. You already have REM–gene associations and only need retrieval or TF motif analysis — use EpiRegio's Gene Query / Region Query instead of refitting the model.

skills.description: Use when building the weighted undirected linkage graph that SpecHap needs for spectral haplotype phasing, starting from extractHAIRS fragment files (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, paired-end NGS).
skills.name: linkage-graph-construction
skills.search_text: linkage-graph-construction Use when building the weighted undirected linkage graph that SpecHap needs for spectral haplotype phasing, starting from extractHAIRS fragment files (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, paired-end NGS). The linkage graph already exists — rebuilding edges is redundant before running SpecHap on the fragment file Ploidy greater than 2: the article states the current graph bisection model might not fit when the ploidy increases Haplotype-resolved structural variation or genome rearrangements: SpecHap supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions, so no rearrangement-aware linkage graph can be built http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reconstructs SpecHap's linkage graph: heterozygous variant loci become nodes of an undirected graph whose edge weights are truncated log-likelihood ratios, weight = max(log(p(H1)/p(H2)), 0), computed from fragment Phred probabilities. This graph is the representation on which SpecHap's Fiedler-Vector-guided spectral partitioning operates. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Reconstructs SpecHap's linkage graph: heterozygous variant loci become nodes of an undirected graph whose edge weights are truncated log-likelihood ratios, weight = max(log(p(H1)/p(H2)), 0), computed from fragment Phred probabilities. This graph is the representation on which SpecHap's Fiedler-Vector-guided spectral partitioning operates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The linkage graph already exists — rebuilding edges is redundant before running SpecHap on the fragment file Ploidy greater than 2: the article states the current graph bisection model might not fit when the ploidy increases Haplotype-resolved structural variation or genome rearrangements: SpecHap supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions, so no rearrangement-aware linkage graph can be built

skills.description: Use when phasing diploid SNVs from fragment files generated by WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT or Oxford Nanopore data, and you want a spectral graph-theory alternative to MEC/max-cut iterative optimization.
skills.name: linkage-graph-spectral-eigendecomposition
skills.search_text: linkage-graph-spectral-eigendecomposition Use when phasing diploid SNVs from fragment files generated by WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT or Oxford Nanopore data, and you want a spectral graph-theory alternative to MEC/max-cut iterative optimization. The organism is polyploid or more than two haplotypes are expected — the current graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy. The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation determination — the linkage graph only supports SNPs and short insertions/deletions. A guarantee of an optimal phasing solution is required — SpecHap provides no optimality guarantee and interval size affects the result. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Infers diploid haplotypes by building a linkage graph from fragment data and partitioning alleles via the sign of the Fiedler (second eigenvector) vector, computed with ARPACK, using recursive spectral bisection when a block does not resolve directly. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Infers diploid haplotypes by building a linkage graph from fragment data and partitioning alleles via the sign of the Fiedler (second eigenvector) vector, computed with ARPACK, using recursive spectral bisection when a block does not resolve directly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism is polyploid or more than two haplotypes are expected — the current graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy. The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation determination — the linkage graph only supports SNPs and short insertions/deletions. A guarantee of an optimal phasing solution is required — SpecHap provides no optimality guarantee and interval size affects the result.

skills.description: Use when phasing 10× linked-read data (e.g. with SpecHap or HapCUT2) and fragments must be filtered so that barcoded fragments spanning distant loci or low-quality reads do not corrupt haplotype blocks.
skills.name: linked-read-fragment-filtering
skills.search_text: linked-read-fragment-filtering Use when phasing 10× linked-read data (e.g. with SpecHap or HapCUT2) and fragments must be filtered so that barcoded fragments spanning distant loci or low-quality reads do not corrupt haplotype blocks. Input is Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, or Oxford Nanopore data rather than 10× linked-reads — the barcode-span and MAPQ heuristics are 10X-specific Input fragments have not been extracted from the linked-reads BAM yet; run extractHAIRS fragment extraction first The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Implements SpecHap's variant and barcode filtering heuristics for 10× linked-read phasing, countering the problem that reads sharing a barcode may originate from different DNA molecules. Variants failing allele depth/quality thresholds are removed, and fragments failing MAPQ, barcode-span, and block-size constraints are dropped before phasing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Implements SpecHap's variant and barcode filtering heuristics for 10× linked-read phasing, countering the problem that reads sharing a barcode may originate from different DNA molecules. Variants failing allele depth/quality thresholds are removed, and fragments failing MAPQ, barcode-span, and block-size constraints are dropped before phasing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, or Oxford Nanopore data rather than 10× linked-reads — the barcode-span and MAPQ heuristics are 10X-specific Input fragments have not been extracted from the linked-reads BAM yet; run extractHAIRS fragment extraction first The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions

skills.description: Use when you need read-level methylation linkage (0/1/- encoding per CpG column) across spatially linked CpGs in defined BED regions from Bismark SAM alignments, e.g. to test whether methylation changes reflect altered cellular populations.
skills.name: linked-read-methylation-extraction
skills.search_text: linked-read-methylation-extraction Use when you need read-level methylation linkage (0/1/- encoding per CpG column) across spatially linked CpGs in defined BED regions from Bismark SAM alignments, e.g. to test whether methylation changes reflect altered cellular populations. Input alignments were produced by a non-bisulfite aligner and lack Bismark XM/XG tags or a SAM header — extract_CpG_data.py requires these for methylation calling The goal is group-level differential methylation testing rather than read-level linkage — use combine_CpG_sites.py and findDMRs.r downstream instead Input is raw FASTQ without alignment — Bismark alignment must be performed first, and Bismark 0.16.0 should be avoided in favor of 0.15.0 due to an ambiguous-alignment bug http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extract per-read, spatially-linked methylation states at CpG sites within user-defined genomic regions from Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq data using DMRfinder's extract_CpG_data.py with the -n BED option, enabling assessment of whether methylation differences occur in a nonrandom pattern across linked CpGs. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Extract per-read, spatially-linked methylation states at CpG sites within user-defined genomic regions from Bismark-aligned MethylC-seq data using DMRfinder's extract_CpG_data.py with the -n BED option, enabling assessment of whether methylation differences occur in a nonrandom pattern across linked CpGs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments were produced by a non-bisulfite aligner and lack Bismark XM/XG tags or a SAM header — extract_CpG_data.py requires these for methylation calling The goal is group-level differential methylation testing rather than read-level linkage — use combine_CpG_sites.py and findDMRs.r downstream instead Input is raw FASTQ without alignment — Bismark alignment must be performed first, and Bismark 0.16.0 should be avoided in favor of 0.15.0 due to an ambiguous-alignment bug

skills.description: Use when starting from raw paired-end ChIA-PET FASTQ reads (e.g., LDK0004-ds_*.fastq.gz) and you must detect the bridge linker and categorize read pairs before mapping.
skills.name: linker-filtering-qc-count-reporting
skills.search_text: linker-filtering-qc-count-reporting Use when starting from raw paired-end ChIA-PET FASTQ reads (e.g., LDK0004-ds_*.fastq.gz) and you must detect the bridge linker and categorize read pairs before mapping. Input reads are already linker-filtered or already aligned (e.g., BAM files); this skill operates on raw paired-end FASTQ reads Library design has no bridge linker junction between genomic tags, so the three-way linker categorization does not apply First ChIA-PIPE processing step that scans each paired-end ChIA-PET read for the bridge linker sequence between the two genomic tags and partitions read pairs into three categories, reporting per-category counts for quality control. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: First ChIA-PIPE processing step that scans each paired-end ChIA-PET read for the bridge linker sequence between the two genomic tags and partitions read pairs into three categories, reporting per-category counts for quality control.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input reads are already linker-filtered or already aligned (e.g., BAM files); this skill operates on raw paired-end FASTQ reads Library design has no bridge linker junction between genomic tags, so the three-way linker categorization does not apply

skills.description: Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET FASTQ reads and you must quantify how much PET rescue a fuzzy linker search (e.g., -e 1 vs -e 0) yields before fixing the trimming stringency.
skills.name: linker-mismatch-sensitivity-benchmarking
skills.search_text: linker-mismatch-sensitivity-benchmarking Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET FASTQ reads and you must quantify how much PET rescue a fuzzy linker search (e.g., -e 1 vs -e 0) yields before fixing the trimming stringency. Data were generated by the half-linker ChIA-PET protocol; bridge-linker mode and the linkerA/linkerB settings of ACGCGATATCTTATCTGACT do not apply. Reads are already linker-trimmed and the task is a downstream ChIA-PET2 step (read alignment, PET filtering, PCR duplicate removal, peak or loop calling). The goal is tuning chromatin loop-calling significance thresholds to balance sensitivity and specificity of loop calls, not quantifying linker-trimming PET rescue. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3391 Benchmarks the sensitivity of ChIA-PET bridge-linker trimming by re-running ChIA-PET2 trimLinker at increasing linker-search mismatch allowances (-e) and comparing rescued PET counts and valid PET ratios reported in output.trim.stat. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Benchmarks the sensitivity of ChIA-PET bridge-linker trimming by re-running ChIA-PET2 trimLinker at increasing linker-search mismatch allowances (-e) and comparing rescued PET counts and valid PET ratios reported in output.trim.stat.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were generated by the half-linker ChIA-PET protocol; bridge-linker mode and the linkerA/linkerB settings of ACGCGATATCTTATCTGACT do not apply. Reads are already linker-trimmed and the task is a downstream ChIA-PET2 step (read alignment, PET filtering, PCR duplicate removal, peak or loop calling). The goal is tuning chromatin loop-calling significance thresholds to balance sensitivity and specificity of loop calls, not quantifying linker-trimming PET rescue.

skills.description: Use when building or reproducing an integrated catalog that combines pipeline-derived records with literature-curation records and you must reconcile provenance and emit aggregate statistics.
skills.name: literature-curated-data-harmonization
skills.search_text: literature-curated-data-harmonization Use when building or reproducing an integrated catalog that combines pipeline-derived records with literature-curation records and you must reconcile provenance and emit aggregate statistics. All eccDNAs in the working set come from a single provenance (e.g. only AmpliconArchitect output) and no literature-curation set exists to merge The task is to identify new eccDNAs from raw WGS data rather than harmonize and summarize an existing catalog The input is already a harmonized summary table (e.g. existing Supplementary Tables S2-S5) — re-merging would double-count entries http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Merges computationally identified elements (WGS/AmpliconArchitect-derived eccDNAs) with manually curated entries extracted from published literature into a single harmonized catalog, then computes unified summary statistics (counts, provenance split, size/segment/copy-number distributions) suitable for tabular reporting. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Merges computationally identified elements (WGS/AmpliconArchitect-derived eccDNAs) with manually curated entries extracted from published literature into a single harmonized catalog, then computes unified summary statistics (counts, provenance split, size/segment/copy-number distributions) suitable for tabular reporting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All eccDNAs in the working set come from a single provenance (e.g. only AmpliconArchitect output) and no literature-curation set exists to merge The task is to identify new eccDNAs from raw WGS data rather than harmonize and summarize an existing catalog The input is already a harmonized summary table (e.g. existing Supplementary Tables S2-S5) — re-merging would double-count entries

skills.description: Use when building or extending a cell taxonomy reference database of literature-curated marker genes (like CellMatch) to support automatic cluster annotation in scRNA-seq pipelines such as scCATCH.
skills.name: literature-marker-gene-curation
skills.search_text: literature-marker-gene-curation Use when building or extending a cell taxonomy reference database of literature-curated marker genes (like CellMatch) to support automatic cluster annotation in scRNA-seq pipelines such as scCATCH. When a tissue-specific, literature-curated reference such as CellMatch already covers your tissue — extend or use it rather than rebuilding from scratch When markers come from a species other than human or mouse without a supported conversion path — the base CellMatch is human and mouse only (custom-species support requires the scCATCH wiki workflow) When the task is de novo marker identification from expression data (e.g., one-against-all Wilcoxon testing) rather than curation from published knowledge http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Curate literature-reported, tissue-specific cell marker genes for human and mouse into a unified reference table (e.g., scCATCH's CellMatch) that links each marker gene to cell type, subtype, tissue, species, and supporting reference, enabling evidence-based automatic cell type annotation. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Curate literature-reported, tissue-specific cell marker genes for human and mouse into a unified reference table (e.g., scCATCH's CellMatch) that links each marker gene to cell type, subtype, tissue, species, and supporting reference, enabling evidence-based automatic cell type annotation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a tissue-specific, literature-curated reference such as CellMatch already covers your tissue — extend or use it rather than rebuilding from scratch When markers come from a species other than human or mouse without a supported conversion path — the base CellMatch is human and mouse only (custom-species support requires the scCATCH wiki workflow) When the task is de novo marker identification from expression data (e.g., one-against-all Wilcoxon testing) rather than curation from published knowledge

skills.description: Use when reproducing the TSMiner mouse LR case analysis (GSE95135 partial hepatectomy RNA-seq) or when rebuilding the text-mined reference sets of 113 LR-associated TFs and 58 KEGG pathways for sensitivity evaluation.
skills.name: liver-regeneration-case-analysis-reproduction
skills.search_text: liver-regeneration-case-analysis-reproduction Use when reproducing the TSMiner mouse LR case analysis (GSE95135 partial hepatectomy RNA-seq) or when rebuilding the text-mined reference sets of 113 LR-associated TFs and 58 KEGG pathways for sensitivity evaluation. Input expression profiles are not time-series (no ordered time points), so no time-specific regulatory network can be constructed The goal is a novel regulatory-network discovery for a different organism or perturbation rather than reproducing the documented mouse LR case analysis with default parameters Only static TF-gene associations are available without pathway gene sets (KEGG/Reactome) — TSMiner's TF-pathway interaction output depends on the gene annotation files http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Reproduces the TSMiner case analysis of mouse liver regeneration (LR): running the packaged example on the mouse LR RNA-seq time-series data and, in parallel, rebuilding the curated reference sets (113 known LR-associated TFs and 58 known LR-associated KEGG pathways) used to benchmark TSMiner's sensitivity against DREM 2.0 and clustering tools. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Reproduces the TSMiner case analysis of mouse liver regeneration (LR): running the packaged example on the mouse LR RNA-seq time-series data and, in parallel, rebuilding the curated reference sets (113 known LR-associated TFs and 58 known LR-associated KEGG pathways) used to benchmark TSMiner's sensitivity against DREM 2.0 and clustering tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input expression profiles are not time-series (no ordered time points), so no time-specific regulatory network can be constructed The goal is a novel regulatory-network discovery for a different organism or perturbation rather than reproducing the documented mouse LR case analysis with default parameters Only static TF-gene associations are available without pathway gene sets (KEGG/Reactome) — TSMiner's TF-pathway interaction output depends on the gene annotation files

skills.description: Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. Triplexator potential match-count vs thermal stability) for lncRNA binding sites, or when validating that a stability-based TPX score discriminates experimentally supported peaks from matched genomic negatives.
skills.name: lncrna-binding-site-analysis
skills.search_text: lncrna-binding-site-analysis Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. Triplexator potential match-count vs thermal stability) for lncRNA binding sites, or when validating that a stability-based TPX score discriminates experimentally supported peaks from matched genomic negatives. The goal is to compare whole prediction tools (3plex vs TriplexFPP, TriplexAligner) rather than scoring strategies within one tool — the paper found no good agreement between 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions and only 2 of 7 lncRNAs had IDR conservative peaks usable for tool comparison Predicting de novo TPX interactions without experimentally validated positive regions and matched negatives — AUC benchmarking requires a defined positive/negative peak framework Integrating RNA secondary-structure masking as the primary variable — that is a separate 3plex evaluation axis (ss10/ss20/ss50 masking extents), distinct from the stability-vs-match-count scoring comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark competing lncRNA:dsDNA triplex (TPX) scoring strategies — match-count-based Triplexator potential versus 3plex's thermal-stability-derived scoring — on validated RNA:DNA binding peaks using ROC/AUC analysis. Grounded in the 3plex paper's demonstration that stability-derived measures outperform simple match counts. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Benchmark competing lncRNA:dsDNA triplex (TPX) scoring strategies — match-count-based Triplexator potential versus 3plex's thermal-stability-derived scoring — on validated RNA:DNA binding peaks using ROC/AUC analysis. Grounded in the 3plex paper's demonstration that stability-derived measures outperform simple match counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to compare whole prediction tools (3plex vs TriplexFPP, TriplexAligner) rather than scoring strategies within one tool — the paper found no good agreement between 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions and only 2 of 7 lncRNAs had IDR conservative peaks usable for tool comparison Predicting de novo TPX interactions without experimentally validated positive regions and matched negatives — AUC benchmarking requires a defined positive/negative peak framework Integrating RNA secondary-structure masking as the primary variable — that is a separate 3plex evaluation axis (ss10/ss20/ss50 masking extents), distinct from the stability-vs-match-count scoring comparison

skills.description: Use when predicting RNA:DNA:DNA triplex interactions between an lncRNA transcript (ssRNA FASTA) and genomic/promoter regions (dsDNA multi-FASTA), needing Hoogsteen-rule scanning, RNA secondary-structure masking, and thermal-stability scoring.
skills.name: lncrna-genomic-triplex-prediction
skills.search_text: lncrna-genomic-triplex-prediction Use when predicting RNA:DNA:DNA triplex interactions between an lncRNA transcript (ssRNA FASTA) and genomic/promoter regions (dsDNA multi-FASTA), needing Hoogsteen-rule scanning, RNA secondary-structure masking, and thermal-stability scoring. You need a classification of triplex-forming potential from a CNN trained on experimental TPX data rather than rule-based scanning — use TriplexFPP instead (note: 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions did not agree well, and TriplexFPP failed to identify known TPX-forming lncRNAs such as CDKN2B-AS1, MEG3, NEAT1 and TERC). Input ssRNA.fa contains more than one sequence — the 3plex required-argument format demands a single RNA sequence. The question is peak reproducibility or replicate handling of RNA:DNA interaction datasets (IDR conservative/optimal, Overlap, Top1000 filtering) rather than triplex prediction itself. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Predict ssRNA:dsDNA triple-helix (TPX) interactions in silico with 3plex, a pipeline integrating Triplexator-style Hoogsteen pairing rules, RNAplfold single-strandedness masking, and LongTarget-derived thermal stability scoring for triplex-forming lncRNAs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Predict ssRNA:dsDNA triple-helix (TPX) interactions in silico with 3plex, a pipeline integrating Triplexator-style Hoogsteen pairing rules, RNAplfold single-strandedness masking, and LongTarget-derived thermal stability scoring for triplex-forming lncRNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need a classification of triplex-forming potential from a CNN trained on experimental TPX data rather than rule-based scanning — use TriplexFPP instead (note: 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions did not agree well, and TriplexFPP failed to identify known TPX-forming lncRNAs such as CDKN2B-AS1, MEG3, NEAT1 and TERC). Input ssRNA.fa contains more than one sequence — the 3plex required-argument format demands a single RNA sequence. The question is peak reproducibility or replicate handling of RNA:DNA interaction datasets (IDR conservative/optimal, Overlap, Top1000 filtering) rather than triplex prediction itself.

skills.description: Use when lncRNAs have experimentally determined genomic binding sites (e.g. ChIRP/CHART/RADICL-seq peaks) but no prior triplex-mechanism evidence, and the goal is to quantify statistical support for DNA binding via TPX formation.
skills.name: lncrna-tpx-evidence-classification
skills.search_text: lncrna-tpx-evidence-classification Use when lncRNAs have experimentally determined genomic binding sites (e.g. ChIRP/CHART/RADICL-seq peaks) but no prior triplex-mechanism evidence, and the goal is to quantify statistical support for DNA binding via TPX formation. When the lncRNA already has experimentally validated triplex evidence — the skill targets lncRNAs lacking prior TPX evidence When binding data are raw FASTQ only — peaks must first be called and filtered (e.g. IDR conservative) before ROC/AUC evaluation When no matched negative regions can be generated (e.g. targets cover most of the mappable genome), since AUC enrichment testing requires positives vs shuffled controls http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Classifies lncRNAs as triplex (TPX) DNA-binders by running 3plex over their experimental binding peaks versus matched negative regions, then aggregating per-lncRNA ROC/AUC evidence into tiered classification (e.g. AUC>0.8 strong, AUC>0.7 good, FDR<e-10). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Classifies lncRNAs as triplex (TPX) DNA-binders by running 3plex over their experimental binding peaks versus matched negative regions, then aggregating per-lncRNA ROC/AUC evidence into tiered classification (e.g. AUC>0.8 strong, AUC>0.7 good, FDR<e-10).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the lncRNA already has experimentally validated triplex evidence — the skill targets lncRNAs lacking prior TPX evidence When binding data are raw FASTQ only — peaks must first be called and filtered (e.g. IDR conservative) before ROC/AUC evaluation When no matched negative regions can be generated (e.g. targets cover most of the mappable genome), since AUC enrichment testing requires positives vs shuffled controls

skills.description: Use when a study needs canonical lncRNA transcript sequences (e.g. the 7 TPX-validated lncRNAs MEG3, Meg3, lncSmad7, NEAT1, TERC, CDKN2B-AS1) from a fixed annotation release before running sequence-based prediction tools.
skills.name: lncrna-transcript-sequence-retrieval
skills.search_text: lncrna-transcript-sequence-retrieval Use when a study needs canonical lncRNA transcript sequences (e.g. the 7 TPX-validated lncRNAs MEG3, Meg3, lncSmad7, NEAT1, TERC, CDKN2B-AS1) from a fixed annotation release before running sequence-based prediction tools. The analysis targets coding-gene promoters or DNA regions only and no ssRNA sequence is needed (3plex dsDNA.fa input comes from genomic intervals, not lncRNA transcripts) A published lncRNA isoform has been experimentally characterized and a specific non-longest transcript should be used instead of the longest-transcript heuristic The annotation release must differ from the rest of the pipeline (mixing GENCODE v32 coordinates with other builds breaks bedtools-shuffled negative matching) http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Retrieves the longest transcript FASTA sequences for target lncRNAs from a genome annotation release (GENCODE v32) as the ssRNA input required for downstream triplex (TPX) prediction with 3plex and RNAplfold-based secondary-structure masking. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Retrieves the longest transcript FASTA sequences for target lncRNAs from a genome annotation release (GENCODE v32) as the ssRNA input required for downstream triplex (TPX) prediction with 3plex and RNAplfold-based secondary-structure masking.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets coding-gene promoters or DNA regions only and no ssRNA sequence is needed (3plex dsDNA.fa input comes from genomic intervals, not lncRNA transcripts) A published lncRNA isoform has been experimentally characterized and a specific non-longest transcript should be used instead of the longest-transcript heuristic The annotation release must differ from the rest of the pipeline (mixing GENCODE v32 coordinates with other builds breaks bedtools-shuffled negative matching)

skills.description: Use when testing enrichment or overlap of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTLs/SNPs, CREs, ATAC peaks) against a segmentation where naive shuffling would overstate significance due to spatial correlation.
skills.name: local-correlation-structure-preservation
skills.search_text: local-correlation-structure-preservation Use when testing enrichment or overlap of genomic ranges (e.g. caQTLs/SNPs, CREs, ATAC peaks) against a segmentation where naive shuffling would overstate significance due to spatial correlation. When ranges are independent of genomic location such that simple shuffling or permutation suffices — though the paper shows shuffling may give overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance, bootstrapping adds cost unnecessary if no spatial correlation exists When no meaningful genome segmentation is available and block placement cannot be constrained to like-state segments When the goal is conventional (non-segmented) permutation-based overlap testing — bootstrap.R in the repo covers that baseline instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates null sets of genomic ranges via segmented block bootstrap (bootRanges in the nullranges R/Bioconductor package) so that resampled ranges preserve the local genomic correlation structure of the original query, producing more reliable null distributions for enrichment testing than shuffling or permutation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Generates null sets of genomic ranges via segmented block bootstrap (bootRanges in the nullranges R/Bioconductor package) so that resampled ranges preserve the local genomic correlation structure of the original query, producing more reliable null distributions for enrichment testing than shuffling or permutation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When ranges are independent of genomic location such that simple shuffling or permutation suffices — though the paper shows shuffling may give overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance, bootstrapping adds cost unnecessary if no spatial correlation exists When no meaningful genome segmentation is available and block placement cannot be constrained to like-state segments When the goal is conventional (non-segmented) permutation-based overlap testing — bootstrap.R in the repo covers that baseline instead

skills.description: Use when comparing ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. GSK126-treated H3K27me3, fulvestrant ER, EPZ5676 H3K79me2 series) where spike-in ChIP-Rx or tag removal normalization overcorrects background signal between conditions.
skills.name: local-regression-signal-correction
skills.search_text: local-regression-signal-correction Use when comparing ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. GSK126-treated H3K27me3, fulvestrant ER, EPZ5676 H3K79me2 series) where spike-in ChIP-Rx or tag removal normalization overcorrects background signal between conditions. ChIP-seq data without exogenous spike-in chromatin (no fly/human H2Av spike-in reads available) — traditional or spike-in-free methods must be used instead Single-sample analysis with no condition to compare — spikChIP normalizes across multiple conditions via the LOESS regression between samples A normalization that must be applied uniformly across all genomic signal is required (e.g. you want ChIP-Rx-style global scaling, which spikChIP deliberately avoids to protect background regions) http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Apply spikChIP's LOESS (local regression) normalization to ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous Drosophila spike-in chromatin, gradually applying the spike-in-derived correction factor from background to enriched bins so that non-occupied regions are not overcorrected, unlike ChIP-Rx or tag removal. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Apply spikChIP's LOESS (local regression) normalization to ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous Drosophila spike-in chromatin, gradually applying the spike-in-derived correction factor from background to enriched bins so that non-occupied regions are not overcorrected, unlike ChIP-Rx or tag removal.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ChIP-seq data without exogenous spike-in chromatin (no fly/human H2Av spike-in reads available) — traditional or spike-in-free methods must be used instead Single-sample analysis with no condition to compare — spikChIP normalizes across multiple conditions via the LOESS regression between samples A normalization that must be applied uniformly across all genomic signal is required (e.g. you want ChIP-Rx-style global scaling, which spikChIP deliberately avoids to protect background regions)

skills.description: Use when RRBS-derived per-locus epiallele frequency vectors (phi_s from bed_marginal) are available for matched normal and multi-region tumour samples and the goal is to find loci whose epiallele composition differs significantly between normal and cancer tissue.
skills.name: loci-significance-testing
skills.search_text: loci-significance-testing Use when RRBS-derived per-locus epiallele frequency vectors (phi_s from bed_marginal) are available for matched normal and multi-region tumour samples and the goal is to find loci whose epiallele composition differs significantly between normal and cancer tissue. Reads are not phased across disjoint loci — do not interpret epiallele composition differences as spanning multiple distant CpGs (a stated limitation of the approach) The data come from a single locus failing the paper's filters (median depth < 100, fewer than 6 CpGs, >25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y) — insufficient read support invalidates the comparison Tumour regions lack an estimated purity rho, so decontamination cannot be performed and raw phi_q profiles would be confounded by normal tissue contamination http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Tests whether the decontaminated tumour epiallele composition differs significantly from the matched normal composition at individual CpG loci, flagging the loci where differences are significant. This operationalises the paper's goal of identifying epialleles that differ between normal and cancer tissue. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Tests whether the decontaminated tumour epiallele composition differs significantly from the matched normal composition at individual CpG loci, flagging the loci where differences are significant. This operationalises the paper's goal of identifying epialleles that differ between normal and cancer tissue.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reads are not phased across disjoint loci — do not interpret epiallele composition differences as spanning multiple distant CpGs (a stated limitation of the approach) The data come from a single locus failing the paper's filters (median depth < 100, fewer than 6 CpGs, >25% missing data, or chromosomes X/Y) — insufficient read support invalidates the comparison Tumour regions lack an estimated purity rho, so decontamination cannot be performed and raw phi_q profiles would be confounded by normal tissue contamination

skills.description: Use when bulk-downloaded GEO series expression data must be keyed to an organism's gene annotations via locus tags before downstream joins, correlation, or cross-experiment comparison.
skills.name: locus-tag-join-annotation-integration
skills.search_text: locus-tag-join-annotation-integration Use when bulk-downloaded GEO series expression data must be keyed to an organism's gene annotations via locus tags before downstream joins, correlation, or cross-experiment comparison. The organism has no GenBank .gbff annotation file available — the match step retains only rows with GenBank annotation matches, so unannotated genes would be dropped. The GEO data of interest are raw or unnormalized — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrates GEO-organized gene expression tables with a user-provided GenBank (.gbff) annotation file by matching locus tags, producing a single tab-delimited matrix whose first five columns carry GenBank annotation (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product) and whose remaining columns hold per-GSM expression values. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Integrates GEO-organized gene expression tables with a user-provided GenBank (.gbff) annotation file by matching locus tags, producing a single tab-delimited matrix whose first five columns carry GenBank annotation (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product) and whose remaining columns hold per-GSM expression values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism has no GenBank .gbff annotation file available — the match step retains only rows with GenBank annotation matches, so unannotated genes would be dropped. The GEO data of interest are raw or unnormalized — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO.

skills.description: Use when moving-window age-comparison tests (e.g., MANOVA on windowed profiles) yield noisy per-age p-value curves that must be smoothed across several bandwidths and combined before calling breakpoint ages.
skills.name: loess-smoothing-of-pvalue-curves
skills.search_text: loess-smoothing-of-pvalue-curves Use when moving-window age-comparison tests (e.g., MANOVA on windowed profiles) yield noisy per-age p-value curves that must be smoothed across several bandwidths and combined before calling breakpoint ages. Data are not temporally ordered by age (e.g., a case/control or single-time-point comparison) — moving-window breakpoint statistics and their smoothing do not apply The per-age p-value curve is already smooth and monotone; single-span LOESS or no smoothing suffices and the 11-bandwidth Fisher combination would add unnecessary complexity http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Non-parametric LOESS smoothing of per-age p-value curves across multiple bandwidths, followed by Fisher's-method combination, to stabilize noisy moving-window breakpoint statistics in temporal epigenomic (PBMC ATAC/RNA) aging data. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Non-parametric LOESS smoothing of per-age p-value curves across multiple bandwidths, followed by Fisher's-method combination, to stabilize noisy moving-window breakpoint statistics in temporal epigenomic (PBMC ATAC/RNA) aging data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not temporally ordered by age (e.g., a case/control or single-time-point comparison) — moving-window breakpoint statistics and their smoothing do not apply The per-age p-value curve is already smooth and monotone; single-span LOESS or no smoothing suffices and the 11-bandwidth Fisher combination would add unnecessary complexity

skills.description: Use when estimating eQTL detection power for low-expressed genes (pseudobulk mean < 5) where scPower's analytic eQTL power is inaccurate, or when validating analytic power with empirical simulation.
skills.name: log-count-linear-regression-eqtl-testing
skills.search_text: log-count-linear-regression-eqtl-testing Use when estimating eQTL detection power for low-expressed genes (pseudobulk mean < 5) where scPower's analytic eQTL power is inaccurate, or when validating analytic power with empirical simulation. Gene pseudobulk mean counts are high enough (mean >= 5) for the analytic linear-model eQTL power approximation to be accurate — use scPower's analytic power functions directly The goal is to scan many experimental design options for optimization — scPower's analytic method is designed for this; simulation-based runs are too slow Data sets with hundreds of samples are required (typical eQTL study sizes) — simulation becomes impractical in runtime and memory http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 A simulation-based eQTL power estimation approach for genes whose pseudobulk mean expression (mean < 5) is too low for scPower's analytic linear-model approximation, using repeated negative binomial count simulation followed by linear regression of log-transformed counts on genotype. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: A simulation-based eQTL power estimation approach for genes whose pseudobulk mean expression (mean < 5) is too low for scPower's analytic linear-model approximation, using repeated negative binomial count simulation followed by linear regression of log-transformed counts on genotype.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Gene pseudobulk mean counts are high enough (mean >= 5) for the analytic linear-model eQTL power approximation to be accurate — use scPower's analytic power functions directly The goal is to scan many experimental design options for optimization — scPower's analytic method is designed for this; simulation-based runs are too slow Data sets with hundreds of samples are required (typical eQTL study sizes) — simulation becomes impractical in runtime and memory

skills.description: Use when comparing two algorithms' runtime/memory behavior across increasing problem sizes and you need empirical complexity estimates (log-log slopes) plus speedup ratios at matched sizes to validate complexity claims.
skills.name: log-log-scaling-slope-analysis
skills.search_text: log-log-scaling-slope-analysis Use when comparing two algorithms' runtime/memory behavior across increasing problem sizes and you need empirical complexity estimates (log-log slopes) plus speedup ratios at matched sizes to validate complexity claims. You need absolute wall-clock performance on a specific production workload rather than empirical complexity scaling across problem sizes The two methods cannot be run on identical fitted objects, so ratios at matched parameter counts would be confounded The workload is parallelized across many cores — the paper's claim (2-orders-of-magnitude gap, slope ratio ~4x) was established on a single core http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmark-scaling analysis that tabulates runtime and peak memory versus problem size (e.g. number of parameters per tile), fits log-log scaling slopes to estimate empirical complexity, and compares method ratios at matched sizes — as done in GenoGAM 2.0 (Fig. 3) to show the sparse inverse subset algorithm computes standard errors ~2 orders of magnitude faster than the indirect Simon Wood method, with linear runtime (vs quadratic) and a ~4x shallower memory slope. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Benchmark-scaling analysis that tabulates runtime and peak memory versus problem size (e.g. number of parameters per tile), fits log-log scaling slopes to estimate empirical complexity, and compares method ratios at matched sizes — as done in GenoGAM 2.0 (Fig. 3) to show the sparse inverse subset algorithm computes standard errors ~2 orders of magnitude faster than the indirect Simon Wood method, with linear runtime (vs quadratic) and a ~4x shallower memory slope.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need absolute wall-clock performance on a specific production workload rather than empirical complexity scaling across problem sizes The two methods cannot be run on identical fitted objects, so ratios at matched parameter counts would be confounded The workload is parallelized across many cores — the paper's claim (2-orders-of-magnitude gap, slope ratio ~4x) was established on a single core

skills.description: Use when two patient groups (e.g., high vs low EGFR expression in TCGA-LGG) have overall survival time and vital status, and you must test survival differences with a log-rank test.
skills.name: log-rank-significance-testing
skills.search_text: log-rank-significance-testing Use when two patient groups (e.g., high vs low EGFR expression in TCGA-LGG) have overall survival time and vital status, and you must test survival differences with a log-rank test. Clinical table lacks survival time or vital status fields, so the merged survival dataset would be empty after dropping missing samples. The analysis goal is detecting eccDNA elements from WGS data with AmpliconArchitect rather than testing expression–prognosis association. More than two stratification groups are planned, since the workflow as specified fits exactly two Kaplan–Meier curves and one pairwise logrank_test. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A Kaplan–Meier survival analysis skill that stratifies cancer patients by a gene's expression level (e.g., EGFR in TCGA-LGG) using a mean/median cutoff, fits per-group KM curves with lifelines, and computes a log-rank p-value to test whether high expression is associated with prognosis. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: A Kaplan–Meier survival analysis skill that stratifies cancer patients by a gene's expression level (e.g., EGFR in TCGA-LGG) using a mean/median cutoff, fits per-group KM curves with lifelines, and computes a log-rank p-value to test whether high expression is associated with prognosis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clinical table lacks survival time or vital status fields, so the merged survival dataset would be empty after dropping missing samples. The analysis goal is detecting eccDNA elements from WGS data with AmpliconArchitect rather than testing expression–prognosis association. More than two stratification groups are planned, since the workflow as specified fits exactly two Kaplan–Meier curves and one pairwise logrank_test.

skills.description: Use when differential accessibility peaks and differential expression gene sets need objective significance thresholds for enrichment analysis, rather than arbitrary logFC or P-value cutoffs.
skills.name: logfc-threshold-optimization
skills.search_text: logfc-threshold-optimization Use when differential accessibility peaks and differential expression gene sets need objective significance thresholds for enrichment analysis, rather than arbitrary logFC or P-value cutoffs. The analysis only needs a fixed a priori cutoff (e.g. p < 0.05); this skill is for data-driven threshold selection, not hypothesis testing at a preset alpha The genomic ranges come from a design where local genomic correlation structure must not be preserved by block bootstrapping, or a conventional shuffling null (bootstrap.R) is explicitly required http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A bootRanges-based spline method that identifies data-driven significance cutoffs for differential analysis — SNPs with -log10(P-value) > 8 and genes with |logFC| > 2 — by finding where the observed penalized-spline GLM fit of overlap counts diverges from the block-bootstrap null envelope. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: A bootRanges-based spline method that identifies data-driven significance cutoffs for differential analysis — SNPs with -log10(P-value) > 8 and genes with |logFC| > 2 — by finding where the observed penalized-spline GLM fit of overlap counts diverges from the block-bootstrap null envelope.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis only needs a fixed a priori cutoff (e.g. p < 0.05); this skill is for data-driven threshold selection, not hypothesis testing at a preset alpha The genomic ranges come from a design where local genomic correlation structure must not be preserved by block bootstrapping, or a conventional shuffling null (bootstrap.R) is explicitly required

skills.description: Use when candidate target regions have already been generated by adaptive liftOver and both epigenomic signal similarities (from matched orthologous ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq datasets) and sequence grammar similarities (motif scanning with jaspar_pfm_list) are available to be scored and filtered.
skills.name: logistic-probability-aggregation-of-feature-similarities
skills.search_text: logistic-probability-aggregation-of-feature-similarities Use when candidate target regions have already been generated by adaptive liftOver and both epigenomic signal similarities (from matched orthologous ENCODE ChIP-seq/DNase-seq datasets) and sequence grammar similarities (motif scanning with jaspar_pfm_list) are available to be scored and filtered. The task is a plain cross-species interval mapping without functional prioritization — direct UCSC liftOver alone suffices and the scoring/filtering layer is unnecessary No matched orthologous functional genomic datasets are available for the species pair and no parameters can be trained via training_module(), so similarities cannot be computed Input is a list of orthologous pairs already validated; scoring candidates is redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Aggregates epigenomic signal similarities and sequence grammar similarities between query regions and candidate target regions into logistic regression probability scores in AdaLiftOver, then filters scored candidates with gr_candidate_filter() to retain the best_k regions per query above a score threshold. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Aggregates epigenomic signal similarities and sequence grammar similarities between query regions and candidate target regions into logistic regression probability scores in AdaLiftOver, then filters scored candidates with gr_candidate_filter() to retain the best_k regions per query above a score threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is a plain cross-species interval mapping without functional prioritization — direct UCSC liftOver alone suffices and the scoring/filtering layer is unnecessary No matched orthologous functional genomic datasets are available for the species pair and no parameters can be trained via training_module(), so similarities cannot be computed Input is a list of orthologous pairs already validated; scoring candidates is redundant

skills.description: Use when mapping epigenome peaks for a model organism other than mouse (e.g., rat) with no pre-fit parameters, or when refitting parameters on labeled data from a specific tissue/experiment.
skills.name: logistic-regression-parameter-training
skills.search_text: logistic-regression-parameter-training Use when mapping epigenome peaks for a model organism other than mouse (e.g., rat) with no pre-fit parameters, or when refitting parameters on labeled data from a specific tissue/experiment. When mapping mouse query regions with the provided 67 ENCODE epigenome datasets, since default LOOCV-trained parameters already perform comparably to refit ones When inputs are raw sequencing reads or unaligned peaks — candidate target regions and similarity scores must be computed before training When no matched human-mouse (or human-model-organism) orthologous epigenome datasets exist to provide positive/negative labels http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 AdaLiftOver's training_module() estimates logistic regression parameters and an optimal score threshold from a pair of matched epigenome datasets, so candidate target regions can be scored and filtered without relying on the default LOOCV-derived parameters. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: AdaLiftOver's training_module() estimates logistic regression parameters and an optimal score threshold from a pair of matched epigenome datasets, so candidate target regions can be scored and filtered without relying on the default LOOCV-derived parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When mapping mouse query regions with the provided 67 ENCODE epigenome datasets, since default LOOCV-trained parameters already perform comparably to refit ones When inputs are raw sequencing reads or unaligned peaks — candidate target regions and similarity scores must be computed before training When no matched human-mouse (or human-model-organism) orthologous epigenome datasets exist to provide positive/negative labels

skills.description: Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., TISP, contact map prediction, eQTL, enhancer-target gene, regulatory sequence activity), or when reproducing PCC/SCC/AUROC benchmark tables.
skills.name: long-range-dna-benchmark-evaluation
skills.search_text: long-range-dna-benchmark-evaluation Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., TISP, contact map prediction, eQTL, enhancer-target gene, regulatory sequence activity), or when reproducing PCC/SCC/AUROC benchmark tables.
