The task involves only short-range DNA sequences without long-range dependencies — the benchmark's motivation is that existing benchmarks lack ultra-long tasks like contact map prediction Transformer-based DNA foundation models such as DNABERT-1/2 or Nucleotide Transformer are required, since quadratic self-attention makes these tasks infeasible for them and they were excluded from the benchmark Only one model is being evaluated with no baseline comparison — the protocol is designed for cross-model benchmark comparison against an expert model http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 A standardized evaluation protocol from DNALONGBENCH for benchmarking DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a CNN baseline and task-specific expert models on five long-range genomic prediction tasks with inputs up to 1,000,000 bp. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: A standardized evaluation protocol from DNALONGBENCH for benchmarking DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a CNN baseline and task-specific expert models on five long-range genomic prediction tasks with inputs up to 1,000,000 bp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task involves only short-range DNA sequences without long-range dependencies — the benchmark's motivation is that existing benchmarks lack ultra-long tasks like contact map prediction Transformer-based DNA foundation models such as DNABERT-1/2 or Nucleotide Transformer are required, since quadratic self-attention makes these tasks infeasible for them and they were excluded from the benchmark Only one model is being evaluated with no baseline comparison — the protocol is designed for cross-model benchmark comparison against an expert model

skills.description: Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert architectures on genomic prediction tasks whose input sequences span long ranges (up to 1,000,000 bp), e.g. eQTL binary classification over 450,000-bp inputs.
skills.name: long-range-genomic-dependency-benchmarking
skills.search_text: long-range-genomic-dependency-benchmarking Use when comparing fine-tuned DNA foundation models against task-specific expert architectures on genomic prediction tasks whose input sequences span long ranges (up to 1,000,000 bp), e.g. eQTL binary classification over 450,000-bp inputs. The task involves only short-range sequences — existing benchmarks (Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE) already cover short-range tasks, and DNALONGBENCH targets long-range dependencies up to 1 million bp You need to evaluate transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — the quadratic self-attention cost renders these long-range tasks infeasible for such models You only need pretrained-model inference or embeddings without fine-tuning and test-split metric evaluation against expert-model baselines http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Benchmark DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a task-specific expert model (Enformer) and a CNN baseline on DNALONGBENCH, a suite of five genomics tasks with long-range dependencies up to 1 million bp, using AUROC (eQTL, enhancer-target) and task-appropriate metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Benchmark DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a task-specific expert model (Enformer) and a CNN baseline on DNALONGBENCH, a suite of five genomics tasks with long-range dependencies up to 1 million bp, using AUROC (eQTL, enhancer-target) and task-appropriate metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task involves only short-range sequences — existing benchmarks (Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE) already cover short-range tasks, and DNALONGBENCH targets long-range dependencies up to 1 million bp You need to evaluate transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — the quadratic self-attention cost renders these long-range tasks infeasible for such models You only need pretrained-model inference or embeddings without fine-tuning and test-split metric evaluation against expert-model baselines

skills.description: Use when evaluating or comparing sequence models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., enhancer-target gene prediction, eQTL, contact map), or when deciding whether a DNA foundation model can replace a task-specific expert model.
skills.name: long-range-genomic-sequence-modeling
skills.search_text: long-range-genomic-sequence-modeling Use when evaluating or comparing sequence models on genomic prediction tasks with long-range dependencies (e.g., enhancer-target gene prediction, eQTL, contact map), or when deciding whether a DNA foundation model can replace a task-specific expert model. Your task involves only short-range sequences or base-pair-resolution without long-range dependencies — other benchmarks (Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE) cover short-range tasks You need transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — these were excluded from DNALONGBENCH evaluation because quadratic self-attention cost renders 450k–1M bp tasks infeasible You require structure-related tasks needing ultra-long sequences beyond the five DNALONGBENCH tasks — the suite covers only enhancer-target gene, eQTL, 3D genome organization, regulatory sequence activity, and transcription initiation signals http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Benchmark fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a CNN baseline and a task-specific expert model on DNALONGBENCH long-range DNA prediction tasks (e.g., enhancer-target gene prediction on 450,000 bp inputs) using AUROC and AUPRC. Rationale: quantify whether foundation models can capture long-range genomic dependencies up to 1 million base pairs. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Benchmark fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) against a CNN baseline and a task-specific expert model on DNALONGBENCH long-range DNA prediction tasks (e.g., enhancer-target gene prediction on 450,000 bp inputs) using AUROC and AUPRC. Rationale: quantify whether foundation models can capture long-range genomic dependencies up to 1 million base pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your task involves only short-range sequences or base-pair-resolution without long-range dependencies — other benchmarks (Genomic Benchmarks, NT Benchmark, GUE) cover short-range tasks You need transformer-based DNA foundation models (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) — these were excluded from DNALONGBENCH evaluation because quadratic self-attention cost renders 450k–1M bp tasks infeasible You require structure-related tasks needing ultra-long sequences beyond the five DNALONGBENCH tasks — the suite covers only enhancer-target gene, eQTL, 3D genome organization, regulatory sequence activity, and transcription initiation signals

skills.description: Use when a structural variant from a congenital abnormality patient lacks a coding explanation and you need to identify the affected gene via a long-range regulatory mechanism in a phenotype-matched cell type.
skills.name: long-range-regulatory-mechanism-annotation
skills.search_text: long-range-regulatory-mechanism-annotation Use when a structural variant from a congenital abnormality patient lacks a coding explanation and you need to identify the affected gene via a long-range regulatory mechanism in a phenotype-matched cell type. The SV is expected to act through a coding mechanism (e.g. truncating deletion within a gene body) and long-range regulatory annotation is not the analytical goal The relevant cell type or developmental stage lacks enhancer/TAD/expression data in POSTRE's supported phenotypes—e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so POSTRE fails on the SHH duplication case The phenotype under study is recessive; POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Annotates structural variants with long-range (enhancer-driven) pathomechanisms—such as enhancer disconnection and enhancer adoption—by scoring SVs against cell-type-specific enhancer, TAD and gene-expression data using POSTRE, thereby predicting causative genes for non-coding SVs in congenital abnormality patients. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Annotates structural variants with long-range (enhancer-driven) pathomechanisms—such as enhancer disconnection and enhancer adoption—by scoring SVs against cell-type-specific enhancer, TAD and gene-expression data using POSTRE, thereby predicting causative genes for non-coding SVs in congenital abnormality patients.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV is expected to act through a coding mechanism (e.g. truncating deletion within a gene body) and long-range regulatory annotation is not the analytical goal The relevant cell type or developmental stage lacks enhancer/TAD/expression data in POSTRE's supported phenotypes—e.g. bulk whole limb bud data cannot identify the ZRS enhancer, so POSTRE fails on the SHH duplication case The phenotype under study is recessive; POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated

skills.description: Use when preparing PacBio SMRT (or other long-read) BAM alignments plus a position-sorted, bgzipped VCF as input for diploid haplotype phasing with SpecHap; the phaser consumes fragments, not alignments.
skills.name: long-read-fragment-extraction-pacbio
skills.search_text: long-read-fragment-extraction-pacbio Use when preparing PacBio SMRT (or other long-read) BAM alignments plus a position-sorted, bgzipped VCF as input for diploid haplotype phasing with SpecHap; the phaser consumes fragments, not alignments. Input is already a fragment file or a phased VCF — extraction would duplicate preprocessing The downstream phaser is not fragment-based (e.g. trio/LD-based statistical phasing), which does not consume extractHAIRS output Variants come from a polyploid organism — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extract read-fragment linkage data from PacBio SMRT long-read alignments using the HapCUT2-derived ExtractHair utility with '--pacbio 1' settings, producing the coordinate-sorted fragment file that SpecHap requires as phasing input. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Extract read-fragment linkage data from PacBio SMRT long-read alignments using the HapCUT2-derived ExtractHair utility with '--pacbio 1' settings, producing the coordinate-sorted fragment file that SpecHap requires as phasing input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a fragment file or a phased VCF — extraction would duplicate preprocessing The downstream phaser is not fragment-based (e.g. trio/LD-based statistical phasing), which does not consume extractHAIRS output Variants come from a polyploid organism — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy

skills.description: Use when preparing Hi-C proximity-ligation read data for diploid haplotype assembly with SpecHap, and trans-homolog interactions (inferred insertion > 40 Mbp) must be removed from fragment input.
skills.name: long-read-fragment-preprocessing
skills.search_text: long-read-fragment-preprocessing Use when preparing Hi-C proximity-ligation read data for diploid haplotype assembly with SpecHap, and trans-homolog interactions (inferred insertion > 40 Mbp) must be removed from fragment input. Input fragments come from PacBio SMRT, ONT, WGS, or 10X linked-reads — the 40 Mbp trans-homolog insertion-size cutoff is specific to Hi-C proximity-ligation data Fragments have already been filtered for insertion size or were not produced in Hi-C mode (--hic 1), so insertion-size inference between paired loci is not applicable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Preprocess Hi-C fragment files for SpecHap phasing by generating fragments with extractHAIRS (HapCUT2) in Hi-C mode, numerically sorting them, and filtering out read pairs whose inferred insertion size exceeds 40 Mbp to exclude trans-homolog interactions treated as errors. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Preprocess Hi-C fragment files for SpecHap phasing by generating fragments with extractHAIRS (HapCUT2) in Hi-C mode, numerically sorting them, and filtering out read pairs whose inferred insertion size exceeds 40 Mbp to exclude trans-homolog interactions treated as errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input fragments come from PacBio SMRT, ONT, WGS, or 10X linked-reads — the 40 Mbp trans-homolog insertion-size cutoff is specific to Hi-C proximity-ligation data Fragments have already been filtered for insertion size or were not produced in Hi-C mode (--hic 1), so insertion-size inference between paired loci is not applicable

skills.description: Use when the goal is to regenerate or produce a polished genome assembly from nanopore long reads (optionally with Illumina short reads for correction/polishing) using a reproducible, end-to-end pipeline.
skills.name: long-read-genome-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-genome-assembly Use when the goal is to regenerate or produce a polished genome assembly from nanopore long reads (optionally with Illumina short reads for correction/polishing) using a reproducible, end-to-end pipeline. The goal is basecalling or model training from raw FAST5 signal data (use taiyaki/bonito instead) Reads are short-read-only (Illumina) with no long-read data available A quick draft assembly without reproducible software versions is acceptable and the full ENA-download pipeline is unnecessary overhead http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Assembles a complete genome from Oxford Nanopore long reads using a Makefile-driven pipeline (correct-then-assemble or assemble-then-correct strategies) with short-read error correction and polishing, reproducing the 2015 Nature Methods E. coli nanopore assembly. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100153
skills.summary: Assembles a complete genome from Oxford Nanopore long reads using a Makefile-driven pipeline (correct-then-assemble or assemble-then-correct strategies) with short-read error correction and polishing, reproducing the 2015 Nature Methods E. coli nanopore assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is basecalling or model training from raw FAST5 signal data (use taiyaki/bonito instead) Reads are short-read-only (Illumina) with no long-read data available A quick draft assembly without reproducible software versions is acceptable and the full ENA-download pipeline is unnecessary overhead

skills.description: Use when you have a bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF plus a sorted fragment file (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, or paired-end NGS) and need fast, memory-efficient diploid phasing, especially for error-prone third-generation long reads.
skills.name: long-read-haplotype-assembly
skills.search_text: long-read-haplotype-assembly Use when you have a bgzipped, tabix-indexed VCF plus a sorted fragment file (10X/Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT, or paired-end NGS) and need fast, memory-efficient diploid phasing, especially for error-prone third-generation long reads. The organism is polyploid: the current graph bisection model assumes two haplotypes and does not fit when ploidy increases. You need haplotype-resolved structural variation: SpecHap supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions; a linkage graph incorporating genome rearrangements is not yet implemented. You require a guaranteed optimal phasing solution: SpecHap provides no optimality guarantee and results depend on the interval size parameter. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Assemble diploid haplotypes from sequencing fragments using SpecHap, which transforms single individual haplotyping (SIH) into a linear algebra problem via spectral graph theory, partitioning variants of the linkage graph by Fiedler-vector sign rather than iteratively optimizing MEC or haplotype likelihood. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Assemble diploid haplotypes from sequencing fragments using SpecHap, which transforms single individual haplotyping (SIH) into a linear algebra problem via spectral graph theory, partitioning variants of the linkage graph by Fiedler-vector sign rather than iteratively optimizing MEC or haplotype likelihood.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The organism is polyploid: the current graph bisection model assumes two haplotypes and does not fit when ploidy increases. You need haplotype-resolved structural variation: SpecHap supports only SNPs, short insertions and deletions; a linkage graph incorporating genome rearrangements is not yet implemented. You require a guaranteed optimal phasing solution: SpecHap provides no optimality guarantee and results depend on the interval size parameter.

skills.description: Use when phasing diploid individuals from PacBio SMRT, ONT, Hi-C, 10x linked-reads, or paired-end NGS data and you need to build SpecHap, extract fragments with ExtractHair, and run the phaser on position-sorted bgzipped VCF plus fragment files.
skills.name: long-read-phasing-workflow-configuration
skills.search_text: long-read-phasing-workflow-configuration Use when phasing diploid individuals from PacBio SMRT, ONT, Hi-C, 10x linked-reads, or paired-end NGS data and you need to build SpecHap, extract fragments with ExtractHair, and run the phaser on position-sorted bgzipped VCF plus fragment files. Ploidy is higher than diploid — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — SIH tools including SpecHap support only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Input fragments are not sorted consistently with the position-sorted bgzipped VCF — sort order must match before running http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Configures a haplotype phasing workflow (SpecHap) for long-read and multi-platform WGS data: building SpecHap and its ExtractHair fragment extractor with pinned htslib (26229a3) and samtools (255f97d) submodules, generating technology-specific fragment files, and running phasing against bgzipped VCF inputs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Configures a haplotype phasing workflow (SpecHap) for long-read and multi-platform WGS data: building SpecHap and its ExtractHair fragment extractor with pinned htslib (26229a3) and samtools (255f97d) submodules, generating technology-specific fragment files, and running phasing against bgzipped VCF inputs.

skills.name: low-information-sequence-filtering
skills.search_text: low-information-sequence-filtering Use when running the Delila-PY pipeline and, after cycle 1's malign/malin alignment, some input sequences from the ChIP-derived sites file show information content of 0 bits or less, contaminating the motif with non-matching sequences. The input is already a curated set of previously identified binding sites with uniformly positive information content, so the ri-based ≤0-bit filter would remove nothing The goal is de novo motif discovery without positional boundaries — generic tools like MEME (expectation maximization) or BioProspector (Gibbs sampling) fit better and require no GenBank plus sites-file setup Sequences are unaligned and cycle 1 (malign/malin) has not been run — the ri filter operates on per-sequence information content from the cycle-1-aligned book Delila-PY's cycle-2 filtering step, which computes per-sequence information content (alist, encode, cmp, rseq) and removes poorly matching sequences with ≤0 bits using the ri program before regenerating the book with delila, so that the final motif (cycle 3) is built only from sequences that carry positive information. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: Delila-PY's cycle-2 filtering step, which computes per-sequence information content (alist, encode, cmp, rseq) and removes poorly matching sequences with ≤0 bits using the ri program before regenerating the book with delila, so that the final motif (cycle 3) is built only from sequences that carry positive information.

skills.search_text: macs2-chip-seq-peak-calling Use when processing deduplicated ChIA-PET bedpe/PET data through the ChIA-PET2 pipeline and ChIP-seq-like anchor peaks must be defined before interaction (loop) calling. skills.search_text: methylation-array-probe-preprocessing Use when the input is a raw Illumina 450K methylation beta-value matrix (probes x samples, e.g. from GEO GSE36278) containing sex-chromosome probes, SNP-overlapping probes, missing values, outliers, and low-variance rows prior to cola consensus partitioning. The matrix is already preprocessed (missing values imputed, outliers adjusted, low-variance rows removed) — re-running adjust_matrix() would not change it The input is a single-cell RNA-Seq matrix (e.g. MCF10CA), where cola instead filters cells with <2 million reads and non-protein-coding genes, not methylation probes Only feature selection or consensus partitioning is needed and the matrix has already passed through this preprocessing step http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Preprocess Illumina DNA methylation array matrices (e.g. the GBM 450K dataset GSE36278) with cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: drop sex-chromosome and SNP-overlapping probes, impute missing values, winsorize outliers, and remove low-variance rows so that top-value feature selection (SD vs ATC) operates on a clean probe matrix. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: Preprocess Illumina DNA methylation array matrices (e.g. the GBM 450K dataset GSE36278) with cola's adjust_matrix() before consensus partitioning: drop sex-chromosome and SNP-overlapping probes, impute missing values, winsorize outliers, and remove low-variance rows so that top-value feature selection (SD vs ATC) operates on a clean probe matrix.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The matrix is already preprocessed (missing values imputed, outliers adjusted, low-variance rows removed) — re-running adjust_matrix() would not change it The input is a single-cell RNA-Seq matrix (e.g. MCF10CA), where cola instead filters cells with <2 million reads and non-protein-coding genes, not methylation probes Only feature selection or consensus partitioning is needed and the matrix has already passed through this preprocessing step

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP = 0/25/50/75/100%) and apparent post-PCR methylation levels per CpG need bias-corrected calibration curves.
skills.name: methylation-calibration-curve-fitting
skills.search_text: methylation-calibration-curve-fitting Use when bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing data include standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. AMP = 0/25/50/75/100%) and apparent post-PCR methylation levels per CpG need bias-corrected calibration curves. The data contain no standard controls with known methylation percentages, so no AMP-dependent calibration curve can be derived The goal is 'one-at-a-time' CpG calibration or calibration of average methylation across CpGs — MethylCal's advantage comes from joint modelling of all CpGs Methylation levels are already PCR-bias corrected; only downstream differential testing is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Fits Bayesian calibration curves (MethylCal, INLA-based) for PCR-bias correction of bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation levels, jointly modelling all CpGs within a CGI or DMR, and benchmarks them against the Warnecke hyperbolic and Moskalev CPR baselines. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Fits Bayesian calibration curves (MethylCal, INLA-based) for PCR-bias correction of bisulfite amplicon sequencing methylation levels, jointly modelling all CpGs within a CGI or DMR, and benchmarks them against the Warnecke hyperbolic and Moskalev CPR baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data contain no standard controls with known methylation percentages, so no AMP-dependent calibration curve can be derived The goal is 'one-at-a-time' CpG calibration or calibration of average methylation across CpGs — MethylCal's advantage comes from joint modelling of all CpGs Methylation levels are already PCR-bias corrected; only downstream differential testing is needed

skills.description: Use when bisulfite sequencing reads (e.g. FASTA epiallele tables from DDO1/DAO amplicons) have been processed with both single-epiallele tools and MethCoresProfiler, and the goal is to demonstrate that epiallele frequency distributions alone miss stable methylation cores.
skills.name: methylation-core-cross-tool-comparison
skills.search_text: methylation-core-cross-tool-comparison Use when bisulfite sequencing reads (e.g. FASTA epiallele tables from DDO1/DAO amplicons) have been processed with both single-epiallele tools and MethCoresProfiler, and the goal is to demonstrate that epiallele frequency distributions alone miss stable methylation cores. When the goal is to quantify single-CpG methylation levels rather than to compare epiallele-level versus core-level discriminative power When MethCoresProfiler core annotations (Tab_Epialleles, ComposCore) are unavailable and only single-epiallele frequencies can be computed — the comparison cannot be made When the input is raw FASTQ rather than quality-filtered, converted FASTA reads produced by the upstream PEAR/PRINSEQ/ampliMethProfiler workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces the side-by-side evaluation showing that single-epiallele frequency tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) identify frequent individual epialleles but cannot separate random (R1/R2) from deterministic (Cond 4) epialleles, whereas MethCoresProfiler's methylated cores distinguish them. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Reproduces the side-by-side evaluation showing that single-epiallele frequency tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) identify frequent individual epialleles but cannot separate random (R1/R2) from deterministic (Cond 4) epialleles, whereas MethCoresProfiler's methylated cores distinguish them.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to quantify single-CpG methylation levels rather than to compare epiallele-level versus core-level discriminative power When MethCoresProfiler core annotations (Tab_Epialleles, ComposCore) are unavailable and only single-epiallele frequencies can be computed — the comparison cannot be made When the input is raw FASTQ rather than quality-filtered, converted FASTA reads produced by the upstream PEAR/PRINSEQ/ampliMethProfiler workflow

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon data (paired-end FASTQ, e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) has been reduced to binary epihaplotype tables of mCpG configurations and the goal is to detect stable phased mCpG combinations and trace epiallele families in complex DNA populations.
skills.name: methylation-core-significance-testing-chi-square
skills.search_text: methylation-core-significance-testing-chi-square Use when bisulfite amplicon data (paired-end FASTQ, e.g. ENA PRJEB28662) has been reduced to binary epihaplotype tables of mCpG configurations and the goal is to detect stable phased mCpG combinations and trace epiallele families in complex DNA populations. When the goal is only per-CpG methylation quantification or counting individual epialleles — the paper notes existing tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) handle single-CpG or single-epiallele quantification but cannot distinguish stable phased cores (e.g. MethCoresProfiler distinguishes Cond 4 from R1/R2 where they fail) When reads contain ambiguous CpG calls (gaps, A or G at the CpG dinucleotide) that have not been filtered out, or fail ampliMethProfiler quality filters (length ±50% of reference, ≥80% primer similarity, ≥98% bisulfite efficiency, ≥60% base alignment) When the input is not phased single-molecule bisulfite data (e.g. array methylation or unphased consensus methylation levels) http://edamontology.org/topic_3673 Identify significant combinations of methylated phased CpGs (methylated cores) shared by epiallele families by chi-square independence testing, as implemented in the three modules of MethCoresProfiler 2.0, and quantify them with MethCores, clonality and entanglement (E) indices. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Identify significant combinations of methylated phased CpGs (methylated cores) shared by epiallele families by chi-square independence testing, as implemented in the three modules of MethCoresProfiler 2.0, and quantify them with MethCores, clonality and entanglement (E) indices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is only per-CpG methylation quantification or counting individual epialleles — the paper notes existing tools (EBA, ampliMethProfiler, methclone) handle single-CpG or single-epiallele quantification but cannot distinguish stable phased cores (e.g. MethCoresProfiler distinguishes Cond 4 from R1/R2 where they fail) When reads contain ambiguous CpG calls (gaps, A or G at the CpG dinucleotide) that have not been filtered out, or fail ampliMethProfiler quality filters (length ±50% of reference, ≥80% primer similarity, ≥98% bisulfite efficiency, ≥60% base alignment) When the input is not phased single-molecule bisulfite data (e.g. array methylation or unphased consensus methylation levels)

skills.description: Use when amplicon bisulfite reads have been converted to binary epihaplotype matrices of phased CpG methylation states and the goal is to extract significant mCpG combinations, cores, clonality/entanglement indices, or track epiallele families across cell types or time points.
skills.name: methylation-core-statistical-annotation
skills.search_text: methylation-core-statistical-annotation Use when amplicon bisulfite reads have been converted to binary epihaplotype matrices of phased CpG methylation states and the goal is to extract significant mCpG combinations, cores, clonality/entanglement indices, or track epiallele families across cell types or time points. The analysis target is quantitative methylation of individual CpGs or abundance of single epialleles — MethCoresProfiler was designed specifically for stable combinations of phased mCpGs shared by epiallele families Input reads have not been reduced to binary epihaplotype matrices and contain ambiguous CpG calls, low bisulfite efficiency (<98%), or insufficient overlap after merging (<40 nt) Only a handful of CpGs are in the locus, so a minimum core of two significantly co-occurring mCpGs cannot be established http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Statistically annotate stable combinations of methylated phased CpGs ('methylated cores') that mark epiallele families in complex bisulfite-sequencing populations, using the three MethCoresProfiler R modules (MethCores_Extractor, MethCores_Combinator, MethCores_Analyst) with chi-square significance testing at P ≤ 10−9. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Statistically annotate stable combinations of methylated phased CpGs ('methylated cores') that mark epiallele families in complex bisulfite-sequencing populations, using the three MethCoresProfiler R modules (MethCores_Extractor, MethCores_Combinator, MethCores_Analyst) with chi-square significance testing at P ≤ 10−9.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis target is quantitative methylation of individual CpGs or abundance of single epialleles — MethCoresProfiler was designed specifically for stable combinations of phased mCpGs shared by epiallele families Input reads have not been reduced to binary epihaplotype matrices and contain ambiguous CpG calls, low bisulfite efficiency (<98%), or insufficient overlap after merging (<40 nt) Only a handful of CpGs are in the locus, so a minimum core of two significantly co-occurring mCpGs cannot be established

skills.description: Use when reconstructing or testing the methylation-count extraction step of a MethylC-seq pipeline and confirming that output tables match a reference implementation, including CpG sites absent from the reference genome.
skills.name: methylation-count-table-validation
skills.search_text: methylation-count-table-validation Use when reconstructing or testing the methylation-count extraction step of a MethylC-seq pipeline and confirming that output tables match a reference implementation, including CpG sites absent from the reference genome. Input alignments were not produced by Bismark (the 'XM'/'XG' tags and in silico bisulfite SAM format are required) The goal is downstream DMR testing or region clustering (combine_CpG_sites.py / findDMRs.r), not per-site count extraction You only need methylation counts at reference-genome CpG sites and want to exclude variant-created novel CpG sites (that is Bismark's own behavior, not DMRfinder's) http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Validates a reimplementation of DMRfinder's extract_CpG_data.py step, which converts Bismark SAM alignments into a merged, sorted table of methylated/unmethylated counts at each CpG site, explicitly including novel CpG sites created by variants (e.g. rs11348696) that Bismark omits. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1909-0
skills.summary: Validates a reimplementation of DMRfinder's extract_CpG_data.py step, which converts Bismark SAM alignments into a merged, sorted table of methylated/unmethylated counts at each CpG site, explicitly including novel CpG sites created by variants (e.g. rs11348696) that Bismark omits.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input alignments were not produced by Bismark (the 'XM'/'XG' tags and in silico bisulfite SAM format are required) The goal is downstream DMR testing or region clustering (combine_CpG_sites.py / findDMRs.r), not per-site count extraction You only need methylation counts at reference-genome CpG sites and want to exclude variant-created novel CpG sites (that is Bismark's own behavior, not DMRfinder's)

skills.description: Use when you have Msuite methylation-call outputs (CpG/CpH meth.call files) from simulated benchmark reads with known preset methylation densities and need to quantify call accuracy per cytosine context.
skills.name: methylation-density-comparison-analysis
skills.search_text: methylation-density-comparison-analysis Use when you have Msuite methylation-call outputs (CpG/CpH meth.call files) from simulated benchmark reads with known preset methylation densities and need to quantify call accuracy per cytosine context. Data is BS-seq generated — must use 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode only supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data with very low non-CpG methylation Real-data samples with unknown ground-truth methylation densities — there is no preset density to compare against; use cross-mode agreement (e.g., 4- vs 3-letter Pearson R) instead You only need alignment output — use '--align-only' rather than running the full methylation call pipeline http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Validate Msuite methylation-call accuracy by parsing Msuite.CpG.meth.call and Msuite.CpH.meth.call outputs, computing deduced methylation densities per context, and comparing them against preset densities (e.g., simulated 20% CpG and 0.5% CpH conversion rates) with R visualization. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Validate Msuite methylation-call accuracy by parsing Msuite.CpG.meth.call and Msuite.CpH.meth.call outputs, computing deduced methylation densities per context, and comparing them against preset densities (e.g., simulated 20% CpG and 0.5% CpH conversion rates) with R visualization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is BS-seq generated — must use 3-letter mode with '-m BS'; 4-letter mode only supports TAPS/5hmC-CATCH data with very low non-CpG methylation Real-data samples with unknown ground-truth methylation densities — there is no preset density to compare against; use cross-mode agreement (e.g., 4- vs 3-letter Pearson R) instead You only need alignment output — use '--align-only' rather than running the full methylation call pipeline

skills.description: Use when ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR reads have already been individually analyzed for CpG methylation and you need to compare methylation percentages between sample groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA controls) with plots and significance tests.
skills.name: methylation-group-comparison-statistics
skills.search_text: methylation-group-comparison-statistics Use when ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR reads have already been individually analyzed for CpG methylation and you need to compare methylation percentages between sample groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA controls) with plots and significance tests. Samples have not yet been individually analyzed by ABSP — run the 'Individual analysis' tab first, since grouped analysis gathers already-computed per-CpG methylation levels You need genome-wide methylation quantification rather than region-specific CpG methylation from BSP experiments — ABSP is designed for region-specific analysis from .ab1 trace files You only have sequencing data without raw trace files (e.g. already-called FASTQ alignments) — ABSP's workflow starts from .ab1 chromatogram traces Grouped methylation comparison as implemented in ABSP: after individual direct-BSP/cloning-BSP sample analysis, gather samples into groups, generate lollipop and methylation profile plots, and run comparative statistics on CpG methylation percentages between groups. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: Grouped methylation comparison as implemented in ABSP: after individual direct-BSP/cloning-BSP sample analysis, gather samples into groups, generate lollipop and methylation profile plots, and run comparative statistics on CpG methylation percentages between groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples have not yet been individually analyzed by ABSP — run the 'Individual analysis' tab first, since grouped analysis gathers already-computed per-CpG methylation levels You need genome-wide methylation quantification rather than region-specific CpG methylation from BSP experiments — ABSP is designed for region-specific analysis from .ab1 trace files You only have sequencing data without raw trace files (e.g. already-called FASTQ alignments) — ABSP's workflow starts from .ab1 chromatogram traces

skills.description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample must be deconvolved into major allelic subpopulation methylation profiles over user-defined regions, without prior knowledge of subpopulation count.
skills.name: methylation-hidden-markov-state-modeling
skills.search_text: methylation-hidden-markov-state-modeling Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample must be deconvolved into major allelic subpopulation methylation profiles over user-defined regions, without prior knowledge of subpopulation count. Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (5hmC) such as neuronal cell types — DXM does not consider 5hmC and interpretation may be impacted Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where subpopulation profiles may reflect allelic or dosage effects rather than distinct cell subpopulations Samples with extreme methylation changes such as DNMT3A mutation or demethylating agent treatment, unless transition probability parameters are retuned for the dataset http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Model binary methylation states across CpGs within a genomic region as a hidden Markov process, using distance-binned 2x2 transition matrices and beta-binomial emissions to reconstruct per-subpopulation methylation profiles via Viterbi decoding (DXM approach). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Model binary methylation states across CpGs within a genomic region as a hidden Markov process, using distance-binned 2x2 transition matrices and beta-binomial emissions to reconstruct per-subpopulation methylation profiles via Viterbi decoding (DXM approach).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (5hmC) such as neuronal cell types — DXM does not consider 5hmC and interpretation may be impacted Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where subpopulation profiles may reflect allelic or dosage effects rather than distinct cell subpopulations Samples with extreme methylation changes such as DNMT3A mutation or demethylating agent treatment, unless transition probability parameters are retuned for the dataset

skills.description: Use when observed bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing methylation percentages in case and control samples need PCR-bias correction, and the stability or concordance of the resulting hyper/hypomethylation classifications must be assessed.
skills.name: methylation-level-correction-evaluation
skills.search_text: methylation-level-correction-evaluation Use when observed bisulfite amplicon/pyrosequencing methylation percentages in case and control samples need PCR-bias correction, and the stability or concordance of the resulting hyper/hypomethylation classifications must be assessed. Input data are already PCR-bias-corrected or produced by controlled mixtures spanning the CpG range — recalibration would double-correct The goal is calibration-curve fitting alone on standard controls without case/control samples, where no differential methylation test is needed (use MethylCalCalibrationPlot directly) Methylation data come from a platform other than bisulfite amplicon sequencing/pyrosequencing whose PCR behaviour the calibration curves were not derived for http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Apply MethylCal's Bayesian calibration (R/INLA) to correct PCR-bias-distorted pyrosequenced methylation levels in case/control cohorts, then evaluate whether downstream loss/gain-of-methylation calls (e.g. ±3SD vs 1% thresholds) are stable under the corrected levels. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Apply MethylCal's Bayesian calibration (R/INLA) to correct PCR-bias-distorted pyrosequenced methylation levels in case/control cohorts, then evaluate whether downstream loss/gain-of-methylation calls (e.g. ±3SD vs 1% thresholds) are stable under the corrected levels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are already PCR-bias-corrected or produced by controlled mixtures spanning the CpG range — recalibration would double-correct The goal is calibration-curve fitting alone on standard controls without case/control samples, where no differential methylation test is needed (use MethylCalCalibrationPlot directly) Methylation data come from a platform other than bisulfite amplicon sequencing/pyrosequencing whose PCR behaviour the calibration curves were not derived for

skills.description: Use when fitted MethylCal INLA calibration models and formatted BWS-style methylation data are available and the apparent methylation level of case/control samples must be converted back to a corrected methylation degree per CpG-AMP combination.
skills.name: methylation-level-numerical-inversion
skills.search_text: methylation-level-numerical-inversion Use when fitted MethylCal INLA calibration models and formatted BWS-style methylation data are available and the apparent methylation level of case/control samples must be converted back to a corrected methylation degree per CpG-AMP combination. Only the calibration curves themselves need to be visualised or goodness-of-fit checked — use MethylCalCalibrationPlot rather than the correction step Apparent methylation levels come from a platform without AMP calibration controls (no 0%/25%/50%/75%/100% standards), so no spline-based inversion can be anchored The analysis goal is outlier detection or exploratory plotting of standard control samples (ExploratoryPlot, MethylCalCalibrationOutlierPlot), not correction of case/control levels http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Recovers the PCR-bias corrected methylation degree from fitted MethylCal calibration curves by numerically inverting equation (10): a cubic-spline interpolant of the posterior means of the AMP random effects (ηi) is built over the five standard control percentages (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and R's optimize() minimizes the discrepancy between observed and spline-predicted apparent methylation, with Moskalev's CPR inversion (equation 9) as the baseline corrector. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Recovers the PCR-bias corrected methylation degree from fitted MethylCal calibration curves by numerically inverting equation (10): a cubic-spline interpolant of the posterior means of the AMP random effects (ηi) is built over the five standard control percentages (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and R's optimize() minimizes the discrepancy between observed and spline-predicted apparent methylation, with Moskalev's CPR inversion (equation 9) as the baseline corrector.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only the calibration curves themselves need to be visualised or goodness-of-fit checked — use MethylCalCalibrationPlot rather than the correction step Apparent methylation levels come from a platform without AMP calibration controls (no 0%/25%/50%/75%/100% standards), so no spline-based inversion can be anchored The analysis goal is outlier detection or exploratory plotting of standard control samples (ExploratoryPlot, MethylCalCalibrationOutlierPlot), not correction of case/control levels

skills.description: Use when a completed per-sample (cf)MeDIP-seq methylation quantification run must be combined across many samples, groups, or batches into genome-bin x sample matrices with standardized region filtering and region-queryable output.
skills.name: methylation-matrix-aggregation-across-samples
skills.search_text: methylation-matrix-aggregation-across-samples Use when a completed per-sample (cf)MeDIP-seq methylation quantification run must be combined across many samples, groups, or batches into genome-bin x sample matrices with standardized region filtering and region-queryable output. Only a single sample is being analyzed and no cross-sample aggregation is required Input is raw FASTQ data needing QC, alignment, and methylation quantification first — this skill is the final downstream stage Data are not (cf)MeDIP-seq methylation quantifications, e.g. WGBS or array methylation data http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregates per-sample cfMeDIP-seq methylation quantifications (from MEDIPS, QSEA, MEDStrand) into TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, applies uniform region filtering (sex chromosomes, chrM, ENCODE blacklist), and Tabix-indexes the results alongside a MultiQC HTML report. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample cfMeDIP-seq methylation quantifications (from MEDIPS, QSEA, MEDStrand) into TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, applies uniform region filtering (sex chromosomes, chrM, ENCODE blacklist), and Tabix-indexes the results alongside a MultiQC HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single sample is being analyzed and no cross-sample aggregation is required Input is raw FASTQ data needing QC, alignment, and methylation quantification first — this skill is the final downstream stage Data are not (cf)MeDIP-seq methylation quantifications, e.g. WGBS or array methylation data

skills.description: Use when individually analyzed bisulfite sequencing PCR (.ab1 trace) samples must be gathered into groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA) and compared with t-tests plus per-CpG significance-annotated profile plots.
skills.name: methylation-profile-significance-plotting
skills.search_text: methylation-profile-significance-plotting Use when individually analyzed bisulfite sequencing PCR (.ab1 trace) samples must be gathered into groups (e.g. high- vs low-methylated DNA) and compared with t-tests plus per-CpG significance-annotated profile plots. Input is raw .ab1 trace files that have not yet been processed by an ABSP individual analysis — use the 'Individual analysis' tab first, since grouped analysis consumes individual methylation tables You only need per-sample CpG methylation percentages without group comparison or significance annotation — the individual analysis report suffices Multiple samples or multiple groupings must be launched in one click — the 'Multiple analyses' tab with input tables is the intended path instead In ABSP's Shiny 'Grouped analysis' tab, gathered per-sample CpG methylation tables from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP individual analyses are compared between collections with two-by-two Student's t-tests and rendered as publication-ready lollipop plots and methylation profile plots annotated with per-CpG significance ('_psign' outputs). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: In ABSP's Shiny 'Grouped analysis' tab, gathered per-sample CpG methylation tables from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP individual analyses are compared between collections with two-by-two Student's t-tests and rendered as publication-ready lollipop plots and methylation profile plots annotated with per-CpG significance ('_psign' outputs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw .ab1 trace files that have not yet been processed by an ABSP individual analysis — use the 'Individual analysis' tab first, since grouped analysis consumes individual methylation tables You only need per-sample CpG methylation percentages without group comparison or significance annotation — the individual analysis report suffices Multiple samples or multiple groupings must be launched in one click — the 'Multiple analyses' tab with input tables is the intended path instead

skills.description: Use when you have cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) aligned enrichment data from raw FASTQs and need per-sample methylation quantification plus aggregated, filtered bin-by-sample methylation matrices across a cohort.
skills.name: methylation-quantification-from-enrichment-data
skills.search_text: methylation-quantification-from-enrichment-data Use when you have cfMeDIP-seq (or MeDIP-seq) aligned enrichment data from raw FASTQs and need per-sample methylation quantification plus aggregated, filtered bin-by-sample methylation matrices across a cohort. Input is already a methylation matrix or beta-value table — quantification from enrichment data assumes raw FASTQ/aligned reads as the starting point Data type is not MeDIP-seq/cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing or methylation arrays), since MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand models assume immunoprecipitation-based enrichment Analysis goal is only per-read QC without methylation quantification or cohort-level aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantify methylation from cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data and aggregate it across samples, using three complementary models — MEDIPS (linear regression), QSEA (sigmoidal model), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model) — then produce Tabix-indexed bin-sample matrices with blacklist and sex-chromosome filtering as implemented in MEDIPIPE. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Quantify methylation from cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data and aggregate it across samples, using three complementary models — MEDIPS (linear regression), QSEA (sigmoidal model), and MEDStrand (stranded sigmoid model) — then produce Tabix-indexed bin-sample matrices with blacklist and sex-chromosome filtering as implemented in MEDIPIPE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a methylation matrix or beta-value table — quantification from enrichment data assumes raw FASTQ/aligned reads as the starting point Data type is not MeDIP-seq/cfMeDIP-seq enrichment data (e.g. whole-genome bisulfite sequencing or methylation arrays), since MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand models assume immunoprecipitation-based enrichment Analysis goal is only per-read QC without methylation quantification or cohort-level aggregation

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0/25/50/75/100% BWS or 0/12.5/25/37.5/50/62.5/87.5/100% Celiac) are available and you must pick the MethylCal model specification per assay.
skills.name: methylation-standard-control-calibration
skills.search_text: methylation-standard-control-calibration Use when bisulfite amplicon sequencing standard controls with known methylation percentages (e.g. 0/25/50/75/100% BWS or 0/12.5/25/37.5/50/62.5/87.5/100% Celiac) are available and you must pick the MethylCal model specification per assay. When the goal is to correct apparent methylation levels in case/control samples using an already-chosen calibration curve — use MethycalCorrection or MoskalevCorrection instead of re-running model selection. When standard controls with known methylation percentages are not available for the assay; the calibration curves are derived from these controls and cannot be estimated without them. When a one-at-a-time CpG calibration (e.g. Moskalev's CPR) is required; MethylCal deliberately analyses all CpGs within a CGI/DMR jointly rather than calibrating individual CpGs. http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 A Bayesian calibration skill that fits MethylCal's four random-effects regression model specifications (M1-M4) jointly across all CpGs of a CGI/DMR assay using standard controls at known methylation percentages, and selects the best-fitting model per assay via the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: A Bayesian calibration skill that fits MethylCal's four random-effects regression model specifications (M1-M4) jointly across all CpGs of a CGI/DMR assay using standard controls at known methylation percentages, and selects the best-fitting model per assay via the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC).
