You need to identify motifs from raw ChIP-seq peaks — use DESSO's train.py/predict.py motif prediction workflow first; this skill only summarizes and classifies already-predicted representative motifs. Your motifs are DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than sequence motifs; the known/undocumented JASPAR/TRANSFAC labeling described here targets sequence motifs. You want to compare motif prediction performance against DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP, KMAC or gkm-SVM rather than summarize motif class frequencies. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Clusters DESSO-predicted representative sequence motifs by TOMTOM similarity using hierarchical clustering, then labels each cluster as documented (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) or undocumented and tabulates motif frequencies and class counts. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Clusters DESSO-predicted representative sequence motifs by TOMTOM similarity using hierarchical clustering, then labels each cluster as documented (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) or undocumented and tabulates motif frequencies and class counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to identify motifs from raw ChIP-seq peaks — use DESSO's train.py/predict.py motif prediction workflow first; this skill only summarizes and classifies already-predicted representative motifs. Your motifs are DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) rather than sequence motifs; the known/undocumented JASPAR/TRANSFAC labeling described here targets sequence motifs. You want to compare motif prediction performance against DeepBind, Basset, MEME-ChIP, KMAC or gkm-SVM rather than summarize motif class frequencies.

skills.description: Use when identifying motif instances (TFBSs) from CNN motif detector outputs and you need an objective, statistically grounded cutoff instead of a fixed/subjective signal threshold.
skills.name: motif-instance-enumeration-across-cutoffs
skills.search_text: motif-instance-enumeration-across-cutoffs Use when identifying motif instances (TFBSs) from CNN motif detector outputs and you need an objective, statistically grounded cutoff instead of a fixed/subjective signal threshold. You only need raw CNN motif detector scores without statistically selected TFBS instances — the predict.py step alone suffices. Your motif detector is not from DESSO's CNN framework and lacks per-instance signal scores across a cutoff grid, so Omega(M, lambda) sets cannot be enumerated. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Reconstructs DESSO's binomial-distribution statistical model that replaces subjective motif signal cutoffs: for each motif detector, TFBS candidate sets are enumerated at varying signal cutoffs, binomial P-values are computed against a GC-matched background, and the cutoff with the minimum P-value selects the optimal motif instances. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Reconstructs DESSO's binomial-distribution statistical model that replaces subjective motif signal cutoffs: for each motif detector, TFBS candidate sets are enumerated at varying signal cutoffs, binomial P-values are computed against a GC-matched background, and the cutoff with the minimum P-value selects the optimal motif instances.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need raw CNN motif detector scores without statistically selected TFBS instances — the predict.py step alone suffices. Your motif detector is not from DESSO's CNN framework and lacks per-instance signal scores across a cutoff grid, so Omega(M, lambda) sets cannot be enumerated.

skills.description: Use when a positional motif-enrichment pipeline needs, per JASPAR PWM, a statistically calibrated log-odds cutoff (via MOODS) before scanning scored DNA sequences for motif matches.
skills.name: motif-log-odds-threshold-calculation
skills.search_text: motif-log-odds-threshold-calculation Use when a positional motif-enrichment pipeline needs, per JASPAR PWM, a statistically calibrated log-odds cutoff (via MOODS) before scanning scored DNA sequences for motif matches. The motif library is not in JASPAR PWM matrix format or the background nucleotide composition of the sequences is unknown, since both are required to calibrate the log-odds distribution The goal is de novo motif discovery or motif assembly — MEPP currently functions with a fixed motif library only A presence/absence (ZOOPs-style) enrichment call per sequence is needed rather than position-resolved excess scores, e.g. when using methods like HOMER or MEIRLOP http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Computes a JASPAR PWM-specific MOODS log-odds score threshold so that MEPP can record motif match excess scores max(0, score - threshold) when scanning one-hot encoded scored FASTA sequences, with the threshold governed by a pseudocount, p-value, and background nucleotide composition. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Computes a JASPAR PWM-specific MOODS log-odds score threshold so that MEPP can record motif match excess scores max(0, score - threshold) when scanning one-hot encoded scored FASTA sequences, with the threshold governed by a pseudocount, p-value, and background nucleotide composition.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The motif library is not in JASPAR PWM matrix format or the background nucleotide composition of the sequences is unknown, since both are required to calibrate the log-odds distribution The goal is de novo motif discovery or motif assembly — MEPP currently functions with a fixed motif library only A presence/absence (ZOOPs-style) enrichment call per sequence is needed rather than position-resolved excess scores, e.g. when using methods like HOMER or MEIRLOP

skills.description: Use when you have a strand-annotated BED file of motif occurrences (e.g. JASPAR MA0139.1 CTCF sites in hg19) and need to test whether nearby consecutive pairs within a distance window show same-strand versus opposite-strand orientation bias.
skills.name: motif-orientation-pairwise-classification
skills.search_text: motif-orientation-pairwise-classification Use when you have a strand-annotated BED file of motif occurrences (e.g. JASPAR MA0139.1 CTCF sites in hg19) and need to test whether nearby consecutive pairs within a distance window show same-strand versus opposite-strand orientation bias. The motif or feature is palindromic — sequences that are non palindromic can be oriented relative to one another, so palindromic motifs carry no orientation information and same/opposite classification is meaningless Input features lack strand annotation — use Asymmetron's separate 'orientation' function (strand assignment of an unassigned feature based on another overlapping feature) instead of consecutive orientation classification The biological question concerns motifs within strand-assigned regions or between two different motifs — use Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries functions rather than consecutive_patterns http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 A skill for classifying the relative strand orientation of consecutive occurrences of a single strand-annotated DNA motif (e.g. CTCF MA0139.1) into same-strand (m) versus opposite-strand (o) pairs, computing the strand asymmetry ratio r = m/(m+o), and testing its significance with Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns function. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: A skill for classifying the relative strand orientation of consecutive occurrences of a single strand-annotated DNA motif (e.g. CTCF MA0139.1) into same-strand (m) versus opposite-strand (o) pairs, computing the strand asymmetry ratio r = m/(m+o), and testing its significance with Asymmetron's consecutive_patterns function.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The motif or feature is palindromic — sequences that are non palindromic can be oriented relative to one another, so palindromic motifs carry no orientation information and same/opposite classification is meaningless Input features lack strand annotation — use Asymmetron's separate 'orientation' function (strand assignment of an unassigned feature based on another overlapping feature) instead of consecutive orientation classification The biological question concerns motifs within strand-assigned regions or between two different motifs — use Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries functions rather than consecutive_patterns

skills.description: Use when you have centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around TSSs) with a continuous per-sequence score (e.g. log-transformed csRNA-seq coverage) and need to determine the positional dependence of known motifs relative to the anchor point.
skills.name: motif-peak-position-identification
skills.search_text: motif-peak-position-identification Use when you have centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around TSSs) with a continuous per-sequence score (e.g. log-transformed csRNA-seq coverage) and need to determine the positional dependence of known motifs relative to the anchor point. You need de novo motif discovery/assembly — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or a motif), since positional profiles are only interpretable relative to such anchors You only need presence/absence motif enrichment without positional information — standard MEA tools like HOMER or MEIRLOP may suffice http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Uses MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) to compute position-dependent motif enrichment profiles across scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor point (e.g. a TSS), then extracts each motif's peak offset to identify where motif presence functionally correlates with a score such as csRNA-seq coverage. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Uses MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) to compute position-dependent motif enrichment profiles across scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor point (e.g. a TSS), then extracts each motif's peak offset to identify where motif presence functionally correlates with a score such as csRNA-seq coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo motif discovery/assembly — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or a motif), since positional profiles are only interpretable relative to such anchors You only need presence/absence motif enrichment without positional information — standard MEA tools like HOMER or MEIRLOP may suffice

skills.description: Use when you have a set of genomic sequences centered on a biological anchor (TSS, ChIP/ATAC/MNase peak summit, or a known motif site) plus a continuous score per sequence, and you need to know WHERE a motif enriches relative to that anchor rather than merely whether it is enriched.
skills.name: motif-positional-enrichment-profiling
skills.search_text: motif-positional-enrichment-profiling Use when you have a set of genomic sequences centered on a biological anchor (TSS, ChIP/ATAC/MNase peak summit, or a known motif site) plus a continuous score per sequence, and you need to know WHERE a motif enriches relative to that anchor rather than merely whether it is enriched. De novo motif discovery/assembly is required: MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library (though 'python -m mepp.learn_motifs' offers initial motif learning) The question is merely whether a motif is enriched, not where it enriches relative to an anchor — bin- or quartile-based MEA tools like CentriMo or TFEA, or ZOOPs-model tools like HOMER, suffice and give no positional profile Input sequences lack a meaningful continuous score per sequence (e.g. raw, unranked motif hits), since MEPP's design requires a score-based continuum of biological interest http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) computes a position-dependent enrichment profile for transcription factor binding motifs across scored, anchor-centered genomic sequences (e.g. TSSs, peak summits, or other motif sites), revealing where motif presence correlates with a continuous biological activity score while controlling for lower-order nucleotide bias. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: MEPP (Motif Enrichment Positional Profiling) computes a position-dependent enrichment profile for transcription factor binding motifs across scored, anchor-centered genomic sequences (e.g. TSSs, peak summits, or other motif sites), revealing where motif presence correlates with a continuous biological activity score while controlling for lower-order nucleotide bias.
skills.when_to_use_negative: De novo motif discovery/assembly is required: MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library (though 'python -m mepp.learn_motifs' offers initial motif learning) The question is merely whether a motif is enriched, not where it enriches relative to an anchor — bin- or quartile-based MEA tools like CentriMo or TFEA, or ZOOPs-model tools like HOMER, suffice and give no positional profile Input sequences lack a meaningful continuous score per sequence (e.g. raw, unranked motif hits), since MEPP's design requires a score-based continuum of biological interest

skills.description: Use when enhancer or promoter FASTA sequences must be converted into TFBS motif-frequency features (via PWM scanning) as input to a multi-input deep learning predictor such as Enhancer-MDLF.
skills.name: motif-pwm-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: motif-pwm-feature-extraction Use when enhancer or promoter FASTA sequences must be converted into TFBS motif-frequency features (via PWM scanning) as input to a multi-input deep learning predictor such as Enhancer-MDLF. Input is already a numerical feature table — re-scanning FASTA against PWMs would duplicate the feature step The goal is k-mer embedding features rather than TFBS motif frequencies — use dna2vec_code.py with the pre-trained dna2vec vectors instead The organism/context is not covered by the HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWM collection (e.g. non-human, non-mouse species) http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Extracts motif-based features for cell-specific enhancer prediction by scanning enhancer FASTA sequences against position weight matrices (PWMs) and p-value threshold scores from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database, producing frequency-feature files that serve as the motif-module input to Enhancer-MDLF. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Extracts motif-based features for cell-specific enhancer prediction by scanning enhancer FASTA sequences against position weight matrices (PWMs) and p-value threshold scores from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database, producing frequency-feature files that serve as the motif-module input to Enhancer-MDLF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a numerical feature table — re-scanning FASTA against PWMs would duplicate the feature step The goal is k-mer embedding features rather than TFBS motif frequencies — use dna2vec_code.py with the pre-trained dna2vec vectors instead The organism/context is not covered by the HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWM collection (e.g. non-human, non-mouse species)

skills.description: Use when you have genomic FASTA sequences (e.g., ATAC-derived distal elements) plus a PWM file such as gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme and need per-sequence motif instances/counts for downstream modeling or SRE construction.
skills.name: motif-pwm-instance-scanning
skills.search_text: motif-pwm-instance-scanning Use when you have genomic FASTA sequences (e.g., ATAC-derived distal elements) plus a PWM file such as gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme and need per-sequence motif instances/counts for downstream modeling or SRE construction. Your regulatory model must capture motif order, spacing, or grammar — BOM's representation is explicitly unordered and motif-grammar integration is an unfinished future direction The TF motifs of interest are absent from the current motif annotations, since the reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif annotations You need to account for open chromatin, histone marks, or trans-acting context — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Scans genomic or designed sequences against a curated position weight matrix (PWM) library (e.g., gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) with FIMO to enumerate concrete TF motif instances per sequence. In the BOM workflow this supplies both the motif-count features for XGBoost training and the concrete motif sequences implanted into synthetic regulatory elements (SREs). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Scans genomic or designed sequences against a curated position weight matrix (PWM) library (e.g., gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) with FIMO to enumerate concrete TF motif instances per sequence. In the BOM workflow this supplies both the motif-count features for XGBoost training and the concrete motif sequences implanted into synthetic regulatory elements (SREs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your regulatory model must capture motif order, spacing, or grammar — BOM's representation is explicitly unordered and motif-grammar integration is an unfinished future direction The TF motifs of interest are absent from the current motif annotations, since the reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif annotations You need to account for open chromatin, histone marks, or trans-acting context — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence

skills.description: Use when raw DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA enhancer sequences per cell line) must be converted into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for downstream machine learning, and a curated PWM library with p-value thresholds is available.
skills.name: motif-pwm-sliding-window-scoring
skills.search_text: motif-pwm-sliding-window-scoring Use when raw DNA sequences (e.g. FASTA enhancer sequences per cell line) must be converted into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for downstream machine learning, and a curated PWM library with p-value thresholds is available. The input is already a numeric feature table (e.g. precomputed motif frequencies) — re-running extraction would be redundant. The task is k-mer/embedding-based sequence encoding — use dna2vec_code.py for dna2vec-based features instead. Non-human or non-mouse sequences where HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWMs and their p-value thresholds are not appropriate. http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Encodes DNA enhancer sequences into fixed-length motif frequency vectors by sliding HOCOMOCO Human v11 position weight matrices (PWMs) along each sequence, counting TFBS windows that pass each motif's p-value threshold, and normalizing counts by sequence length. This yields 401-dimensional motif features for cell-specific enhancer prediction with Enhancer-MDLF. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Encodes DNA enhancer sequences into fixed-length motif frequency vectors by sliding HOCOMOCO Human v11 position weight matrices (PWMs) along each sequence, counting TFBS windows that pass each motif's p-value threshold, and normalizing counts by sequence length. This yields 401-dimensional motif features for cell-specific enhancer prediction with Enhancer-MDLF.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a numeric feature table (e.g. precomputed motif frequencies) — re-running extraction would be redundant. The task is k-mer/embedding-based sequence encoding — use dna2vec_code.py for dna2vec-based features instead. Non-human or non-mouse sequences where HOCOMOCO Human v11 PWMs and their p-value thresholds are not appropriate.

skills.description: Use when constructing a TF-target gene prior from motif scans of open-chromatin peaks and same-family TFs yield overlapping motif-to-peak sets that would create redundant, correlated rows in the decoder's TF-gene matrix.
skills.name: motif-redundancy-deduplication
skills.search_text: motif-redundancy-deduplication Use when constructing a TF-target gene prior from motif scans of open-chromatin peaks and same-family TFs yield overlapping motif-to-peak sets that would create redundant, correlated rows in the decoder's TF-gene matrix. The analysis requires resolving which specific TF within a shared-motif family is active — deduplication merges same-family motifs and cannot disambiguate them, so motif-level activities may encompass multiple TFs. The downstream model needs activation-vs-repression directionality or co-binding patterns (e.g. AP-1–IRF complexes) — the deduplicated binary prior represents neither. Input motif-to-peak assignments are already deduplicated or derived from ChIP-seq evidence rather than motif scanning, so pairwise Jaccard collapsing is unnecessary. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Deduplicates TF motifs by removing near-identical motif pairs (Jaccard similarity > 0.5) after a FIMO/cis-BP scan of the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC-seq peak atlas, collapsing to a non-redundant set of 320 TF motifs used to constrain CITRUS's TF-to-gene decoder layer. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881
skills.summary: Deduplicates TF motifs by removing near-identical motif pairs (Jaccard similarity > 0.5) after a FIMO/cis-BP scan of the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC-seq peak atlas, collapsing to a non-redundant set of 320 TF motifs used to constrain CITRUS's TF-to-gene decoder layer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires resolving which specific TF within a shared-motif family is active — deduplication merges same-family motifs and cannot disambiguate them, so motif-level activities may encompass multiple TFs. The downstream model needs activation-vs-repression directionality or co-binding patterns (e.g. AP-1–IRF complexes) — the deduplicated binary prior represents neither. Input motif-to-peak assignments are already deduplicated or derived from ChIP-seq evidence rather than motif scanning, so pairwise Jaccard collapsing is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when you have genomic intervals (chromosome, start, stop, condition BED-style input) or extracted FASTA of candidate enhancers and need per-sequence TF motif occurrences as features for cell-type-specific CRE classification or cross-species transfer.
skills.name: motif-scanning-of-regulatory-sequences
skills.search_text: motif-scanning-of-regulatory-sequences Use when you have genomic intervals (chromosome, start, stop, condition BED-style input) or extracted FASTA of candidate enhancers and need per-sequence TF motif occurrences as features for cell-type-specific CRE classification or cross-species transfer. When you need motif order, orientation, or spacing information — BOM's representation is explicitly unordered motif counts, so grammar-aware questions are out of scope (integration with motif grammar remains a stated future direction) When regulatory logic depends on sequences beyond the scanned interval — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence length When the TF motifs of interest are absent from current motif annotations — reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by PWM libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Scan distal cis-regulatory element sequences for TF motif occurrences with FIMO using the gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme PWM library, producing per-sequence motif counts that feed BOM's gradient-boosted classifiers and enable cross-species CRE prediction independent of sequence alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Scan distal cis-regulatory element sequences for TF motif occurrences with FIMO using the gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme PWM library, producing per-sequence motif counts that feed BOM's gradient-boosted classifiers and enable cross-species CRE prediction independent of sequence alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need motif order, orientation, or spacing information — BOM's representation is explicitly unordered motif counts, so grammar-aware questions are out of scope (integration with motif grammar remains a stated future direction) When regulatory logic depends on sequences beyond the scanned interval — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence length When the TF motifs of interest are absent from current motif annotations — reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by PWM libraries

skills.description: Use when comparing called-site outputs from CLIP-seq peak callers (Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) on eCLIP data and an independent motif-, sequence-, or feature-derived positive truth set is available for the assayed RBP.
skills.name: motif-sequence-truth-matching
skills.search_text: motif-sequence-truth-matching Use when comparing called-site outputs from CLIP-seq peak callers (Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) on eCLIP data and an independent motif-, sequence-, or feature-derived positive truth set is available for the assayed RBP. No orthogonally derived truth set (motif, splice site, chrM, structural RNA, or affinity-score data) exists for the RBP being evaluated — overlap-based TP/FP/FN assignment cannot be performed The goal is peak calling itself rather than benchmarking caller performance; use Skipper's pipeline (GFF partitioning, enriched window identification, fine-mapping) instead CLIP datasets lack matched input samples required for Skipper's beta-binomial statistical model, so Skipper output — one side of the comparison — cannot be generated Benchmarking CLIP-seq called binding sites (from Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) against orthogonally ascertained truth sets — such as GURUG motif sites for TARDBP, 5' splice sites for PRPF8, chrM for FASTKD2, or histone stem-loop motifs for SLBP — by overlap-based TP/FP/FN assignment and precision/recall/F1 computation. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Benchmarking CLIP-seq called binding sites (from Skipper, CLIPper, Piranha) against orthogonally ascertained truth sets — such as GURUG motif sites for TARDBP, 5' splice sites for PRPF8, chrM for FASTKD2, or histone stem-loop motifs for SLBP — by overlap-based TP/FP/FN assignment and precision/recall/F1 computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No orthogonally derived truth set (motif, splice site, chrM, structural RNA, or affinity-score data) exists for the RBP being evaluated — overlap-based TP/FP/FN assignment cannot be performed The goal is peak calling itself rather than benchmarking caller performance; use Skipper's pipeline (GFF partitioning, enriched window identification, fine-mapping) instead CLIP datasets lack matched input samples required for Skipper's beta-binomial statistical model, so Skipper output — one side of the comparison — cannot be generated

skills.description: Use when MEME has discovered candidate motifs from positive vs. negative sequence sets and you must retain only statistically significant motifs (E-value < 0.05) to build per-sample motif score features for a classifier.
skills.name: motif-significance-evalue-filtering
skills.search_text: motif-significance-evalue-filtering Use when MEME has discovered candidate motifs from positive vs. negative sequence sets and you must retain only statistically significant motifs (E-value < 0.05) to build per-sample motif score features for a classifier. Input is already an encoded feature matrix or motif score table — no motif filtering or rescoring is needed. The analysis goal is de novo motif discovery itself rather than filtering discovered motifs into classifier features. Sequences are not the fixed 41-nt 6mA-centered windows csDMA expects; the motif scoring scheme assumes 41-nt samples. http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Select statistically significant DNA motifs from MEME differential enrichment output by an E-value < 0.05 cutoff and convert the retained motifs' position-specific probability matrices into per-sample motif score matrices for downstream machine-learning feature encoding in csDMA. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4
skills.summary: Select statistically significant DNA motifs from MEME differential enrichment output by an E-value < 0.05 cutoff and convert the retained motifs' position-specific probability matrices into per-sample motif score matrices for downstream machine-learning feature encoding in csDMA.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an encoded feature matrix or motif score table — no motif filtering or rescoring is needed. The analysis goal is de novo motif discovery itself rather than filtering discovered motifs into classifier features. Sequences are not the fixed 41-nt 6mA-centered windows csDMA expects; the motif scoring scheme assumes 41-nt samples.

skills.description: Use when a large pool of predicted motifs (e.g. from DESSO predict.py across many ChIP-seq datasets) must be reduced to representative motifs and classified as known versus undocumented.
skills.name: motif-similarity-clustering
skills.search_text: motif-similarity-clustering Use when a large pool of predicted motifs (e.g. from DESSO predict.py across many ChIP-seq datasets) must be reduced to representative motifs and classified as known versus undocumented. Input motifs are already collapsed and database-annotated, so clustering would only duplicate prior labels Shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) from DESSO's --feature_format DNAShape mode are the target, since JASPAR/TRANSFAC matching of sequence motifs does not directly apply to shape motif profiles http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Clusters DNA sequence motifs by TOMTOM all-against-all similarity scores using hierarchical clustering, then labels each cluster as documented (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) or undocumented, as applied to DESSO's motifs from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Clusters DNA sequence motifs by TOMTOM all-against-all similarity scores using hierarchical clustering, then labels each cluster as documented (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) or undocumented, as applied to DESSO's motifs from 690 ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input motifs are already collapsed and database-annotated, so clustering would only duplicate prior labels Shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) from DESSO's --feature_format DNAShape mode are the target, since JASPAR/TRANSFAC matching of sequence motifs does not directly apply to shape motif profiles

skills.description: Use when predicted motifs from a motif-discovery or deep-learning pipeline must be validated or benchmarked against curated motif databases (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) via TOMTOM similarity statistics.
skills.name: motif-similarity-evaluation-against-jaspar-transfac
skills.search_text: motif-similarity-evaluation-against-jaspar-transfac Use when predicted motifs from a motif-discovery or deep-learning pipeline must be validated or benchmarked against curated motif databases (JASPAR/TRANSFAC) via TOMTOM similarity statistics. The input is raw ChIP-seq peaks or sequences rather than already-predicted motif matrices — use the motif prediction skill (train.py/predict.py) first Evaluating DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll), which are not directly comparable to JASPAR/TRANSFAC sequence motifs via TOMTOM http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Evaluates predicted sequence motifs (e.g. from DESSO CNN models) by TOMTOM similarity search against documented JASPAR and TRANSFAC motifs, using E-value, P-value and q-value significance measures to benchmark motif prediction quality across the 690 human ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Evaluates predicted sequence motifs (e.g. from DESSO CNN models) by TOMTOM similarity search against documented JASPAR and TRANSFAC motifs, using E-value, P-value and q-value significance measures to benchmark motif prediction quality across the 690 human ENCODE ChIP-seq datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw ChIP-seq peaks or sequences rather than already-predicted motif matrices — use the motif prediction skill (train.py/predict.py) first Evaluating DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll), which are not directly comparable to JASPAR/TRANSFAC sequence motifs via TOMTOM

skills.description: Use when you have a sparse scATAC-seq fragment-count matrix over peaks and want to rank motifs/annotations by cell-to-cell accessibility variability with bias correction, or to test whether motif deviations or variability differ between cell-type groups.
skills.name: motif-variability-quantification
skills.search_text: motif-variability-quantification Use when you have a sparse scATAC-seq fragment-count matrix over peaks and want to rank motifs/annotations by cell-to-cell accessibility variability with bias correction, or to test whether motif deviations or variability differ between cell-type groups. skills.search_text: multi-resolution-hic-contact-map-visualization Use when hic contact matrix files from the Microcket pipeline are available and region-specific contact-map heatmaps must be extracted and rendered at multiple resolutions for side-by-side condition comparison. Input is raw Hi-C FASTQ or unaligned pairs — the .hic files must already exist from the upstream Microcket run; this skill does no alignment or filtering (e.g., no minimum mapping quality filter at default 10). The analysis requires genome-wide quantitative scoring (e.g., compartment eigenvectors or loop calling) rather than visual region-level contact maps. Data are stored in .cool/.cooler format without a .hic conversion path — straw/dump operate on .hic. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extracts KR-normalized contact matrices from Microcket-generated .hic files with JuicerTools (straw/dump) and renders square cis-contact heatmaps at multiple bin sizes (e.g., 100-kb, 25-kb, 5-kb) so that chromatin architecture differences between conditions such as QSC and FISC are directly comparable. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2025.103962
skills.summary: Extracts KR-normalized contact matrices from Microcket-generated .hic files with JuicerTools (straw/dump) and renders square cis-contact heatmaps at multiple bin sizes (e.g., 100-kb, 25-kb, 5-kb) so that chromatin architecture differences between conditions such as QSC and FISC are directly comparable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw Hi-C FASTQ or unaligned pairs — the .hic files must already exist from the upstream Microcket run; this skill does no alignment or filtering (e.g., no minimum mapping quality filter at default 10). The analysis requires genome-wide quantitative scoring (e.g., compartment eigenvectors or loop calling) rather than visual region-level contact maps. Data are stored in .cool/.cooler format without a .hic conversion path — straw/dump operate on .hic.

skills.description: Use when per-sample QC and methylation outputs (FastQC, SAMtools, Picard, MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand quantifications) must be pooled across many samples, groups, or batches into a summarized report and region-queryable aggregated matrices.
skills.name: multi-sample-qc-report-aggregation
skills.search_text: multi-sample-qc-report-aggregation Use when per-sample QC and methylation outputs (FastQC, SAMtools, Picard, MEDIPS/QSEA/MEDStrand quantifications) must be pooled across many samples, groups, or batches into a summarized report and region-queryable aggregated matrices. Input is still raw FASTQ or unaligned BAMs — upstream QC (Trim Galore, FastQC), alignment (BWA-MEM), and per-sample methylation quantification must be complete before aggregation Only a single sample is being processed without cohort-level comparison, so aggregated bin-sample matrices and group/batch QC views provide no added value Quantifications come from a non-(cf)MeDIP-seq assay whose bin coordinates or QC report formats are incompatible with the MEDIPIPE aggregation rules http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregate per-sample QC metrics and methylation quantifications from a (cf)MeDIP-seq pipeline (e.g. MEDIPIPE) into MultiQC-derived interactive HTML QC reports and TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, filtered and Tabix-indexed so large sample cohorts spanning multiple groups or batches can be inspected jointly. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: Aggregate per-sample QC metrics and methylation quantifications from a (cf)MeDIP-seq pipeline (e.g. MEDIPIPE) into MultiQC-derived interactive HTML QC reports and TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, filtered and Tabix-indexed so large sample cohorts spanning multiple groups or batches can be inspected jointly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw FASTQ or unaligned BAMs — upstream QC (Trim Galore, FastQC), alignment (BWA-MEM), and per-sample methylation quantification must be complete before aggregation Only a single sample is being processed without cohort-level comparison, so aggregated bin-sample matrices and group/batch QC views provide no added value Quantifications come from a non-(cf)MeDIP-seq assay whose bin coordinates or QC report formats are incompatible with the MEDIPIPE aggregation rules

skills.description: Use when asked to reproduce or extend classification of cell-type-specific enhancers across species, cell types, or disease states using BED coordinates plus condition labels and the BOM pipeline.
skills.name: multi-species-enhancer-benchmarking
skills.search_text: multi-species-enhancer-benchmarking Use when asked to reproduce or extend classification of cell-type-specific enhancers across species, cell types, or disease states using BED coordinates plus condition labels and the BOM pipeline. The task requires modeling motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and grammar integration is noted as future work The regulatory activity may depend on sequence beyond the input regions or on open chromatin/histone marks — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence The target sequences contain TF binding patterns absent from known motif annotations (e.g. gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) — reliance on known motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reproduce BOM's cross-context benchmarking of motif-count-based cis-regulatory element classification across human, zebrafish, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, and AML datasets, verifying that unordered TF motif counts plus gradient-boosted trees generalize beyond the mouse benchmark. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Reproduce BOM's cross-context benchmarking of motif-count-based cis-regulatory element classification across human, zebrafish, Drosophila, Arabidopsis, and AML datasets, verifying that unordered TF motif counts plus gradient-boosted trees generalize beyond the mouse benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task requires modeling motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) — BOM represents sequences as unordered motif counts and grammar integration is noted as future work The regulatory activity may depend on sequence beyond the input regions or on open chromatin/histone marks — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence The target sequences contain TF binding patterns absent from known motif annotations (e.g. gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) — reliance on known motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current annotations

skills.description: Use when a cisTopic object (initialized binary accessibility matrix) is available and multiple LDA models over a grid of topic numbers must be trained to later choose the optimal number of cis-regulatory topics.
skills.name: multi-topic-grid-model-training
skills.search_text: multi-topic-grid-model-training Use when a cisTopic object (initialized binary accessibility matrix) is available and multiple LDA models over a grid of topic numbers must be trained to later choose the optimal number of cis-regulatory topics. Input is not a cisTopic object with a binarized accessibility matrix (e.g. raw count matrix not yet initialized via createcisTopicObject*) The optimal model has already been selected and downstream steps (getRegionsScores, binarizecisTopics, runtSNE/runUmap) are the goal Working in Python with the deprecated R cisTopic replaced by pycisTopic, where runModels() is not the applicable API http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Fits a series of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic models over a range of topic numbers on a cisTopic object built from single-cell epigenomics data, so that the best topic number can later be selected by log likelihood. In this workflow, runModels() is applied to the binary accessibility matrix of the 5,335-cell PBMC dataset (~97k regulatory regions) across a 2–40 topic grid. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-019-0367-1
skills.summary: Fits a series of Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic models over a range of topic numbers on a cisTopic object built from single-cell epigenomics data, so that the best topic number can later be selected by log likelihood. In this workflow, runModels() is applied to the binary accessibility matrix of the 5,335-cell PBMC dataset (~97k regulatory regions) across a 2–40 topic grid.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a cisTopic object with a binarized accessibility matrix (e.g. raw count matrix not yet initialized via createcisTopicObject*) The optimal model has already been selected and downstream steps (getRegionsScores, binarizecisTopics, runtSNE/runUmap) are the goal Working in Python with the deprecated R cisTopic replaced by pycisTopic, where runModels() is not the applicable API

skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq peak/CRE data must be assigned to cell types from sequence alone — e.g., multiclass classification of cell-type-specific distal elements or cross-species cell-type assignment using motif counts.
skills.name: multiclass-cell-type-classification-from-scatac-distal-elements
skills.search_text: multiclass-cell-type-classification-from-scatac-distal-elements Use when scATAC-seq peak/CRE data must be assigned to cell types from sequence alone — e.g., multiclass classification of cell-type-specific distal elements or cross-species cell-type assignment using motif counts. Input is already a feature/counts matrix rather than genomic coordinates of CREs — BOM requires a BED file of genomic intervals to extract sequences The regulatory activity is expected to depend on motif grammar (order, orientation, spacing) — BOM's representation is unordered motif counts independent of motif order, orientation, or spacing Informative sequences not captured by known TF motif annotations drive the classification — reliance on known motifs neglects unannotated informative sequences http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Train multiclass Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) models on seven shared adult heart cell types using unordered TF motif counts from distal cis-regulatory elements, then use SHAP-aggregated attributions to assign single cells to cell types, including cross-species transfer between human and mouse heart. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Train multiclass Bag-of-Motifs (BOM) models on seven shared adult heart cell types using unordered TF motif counts from distal cis-regulatory elements, then use SHAP-aggregated attributions to assign single cells to cell types, including cross-species transfer between human and mouse heart.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature/counts matrix rather than genomic coordinates of CREs — BOM requires a BED file of genomic intervals to extract sequences The regulatory activity is expected to depend on motif grammar (order, orientation, spacing) — BOM's representation is unordered motif counts independent of motif order, orientation, or spacing Informative sequences not captured by known TF motif annotations drive the classification — reliance on known motifs neglects unannotated informative sequences

skills.description: Use when clustering outputs must be scored against known ground-truth class labels (e.g. 5 simulated peak seed patterns of ~100 members each) across a parameter grid, and a single balanced score per condition is needed.
skills.name: multiclass-mcc-evaluation
skills.search_text: multiclass-mcc-evaluation Use when clustering outputs must be scored against known ground-truth class labels (e.g. 5 simulated peak seed patterns of ~100 members each) across a parameter grid, and a single balanced score per condition is needed. Clustering real data with no ground-truth class membership (e.g. the real ENCODE H3K4me3/H3K9ac K562 peaks) — MCC requires known seed-of-origin labels Binary classification tasks where standard binary MCC or balanced accuracy suffices — this skill targets multi-class cluster recovery Evaluating alignment quality directly (e.g. TSS/FSS entropy reduction after warping) rather than recovery of cluster structure http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Scores cluster recovery by computing the multi-class Matthews Correlation Coefficient of dendrogram-cut cluster assignments against known seed-of-origin labels. In the DGW paper this is the metric that quantifies how much DTW-based alignment improves recovery of simulated epigenomic peak classes over standard hierarchical clustering. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Scores cluster recovery by computing the multi-class Matthews Correlation Coefficient of dendrogram-cut cluster assignments against known seed-of-origin labels. In the DGW paper this is the metric that quantifies how much DTW-based alignment improves recovery of simulated epigenomic peak classes over standard hierarchical clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Clustering real data with no ground-truth class membership (e.g. the real ENCODE H3K4me3/H3K9ac K562 peaks) — MCC requires known seed-of-origin labels Binary classification tasks where standard binary MCC or balanced accuracy suffices — this skill targets multi-class cluster recovery Evaluating alignment quality directly (e.g. TSS/FSS entropy reduction after warping) rather than recovery of cluster structure

skills.description: Use when multiple epigenomic tracks (e.g. ChIP-Seq coverage binned into 50 bp windows per peak) must be aligned by shape across peaks without gene annotation or TSS information, as a precursor to hierarchical clustering.
skills.name: multidimensional-epigenomic-track-warping
skills.search_text: multidimensional-epigenomic-track-warping Use when multiple epigenomic tracks (e.g. ChIP-Seq coverage binned into 50 bp windows per peak) must be aligned by shape across peaks without gene annotation or TSS information, as a precursor to hierarchical clustering. When peaks are shorter than 5 or longer than 1000 bins, or have fewer than 10 counts — the paper's filtering excludes these before alignment When gene annotation or TSS positions are available and a supervised/annotation-based alignment is preferred — DGW deliberately solves alignment without such information When the input is already an aligned feature table rather than raw binned coverage sequences — warping would be redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Implements DGW's constrained multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping to align sequences of binned epigenomic coverage vectors by shape, then derives a cluster prototype via the scaled prioritised shape averaging algorithm. The Sakoe-Chiba band (width 12) and strand-symmetric distance computation make alignment tractable and orientation-invariant. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Implements DGW's constrained multidimensional Dynamic Time Warping to align sequences of binned epigenomic coverage vectors by shape, then derives a cluster prototype via the scaled prioritised shape averaging algorithm. The Sakoe-Chiba band (width 12) and strand-symmetric distance computation make alignment tractable and orientation-invariant.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When peaks are shorter than 5 or longer than 1000 bins, or have fewer than 10 counts — the paper's filtering excludes these before alignment When gene annotation or TSS positions are available and a supervised/annotation-based alignment is preferred — DGW deliberately solves alignment without such information When the input is already an aligned feature table rather than raw binned coverage sequences — warping would be redundant

skills.description: Use when you have AdaLiftOver candidate target regions for query peaks and need to separate uniquely mapped regions from multi-mappers, or to test whether epigenomic signal overrides sequence-conservation-based mapping support.
skills.name: multimapper-partitioning
skills.search_text: multimapper-partitioning Use when you have AdaLiftOver candidate target regions for query peaks and need to separate uniquely mapped regions from multi-mappers, or to test whether epigenomic signal overrides sequence-conservation-based mapping support. When the goal is orthologous region identification itself rather than post-hoc quality stratification — use the full AdaLiftOver pipeline with gr_candidate_filter() instead of the partitioning analysis. When query regions are coding or already unambiguously annotated orthologs, where multi-mapping assessment of non-coding regulatory elements is not the question. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Partition AdaLiftOver-mapped query regions by mapping multiplicity into Group I (unique sequence-based mappings) and Group II (multi-mappers), then quantify how often epigenomic mapping scores (<0.5) contradict sequence-based mappability in the uniquely mapped group. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149
skills.summary: Partition AdaLiftOver-mapped query regions by mapping multiplicity into Group I (unique sequence-based mappings) and Group II (multi-mappers), then quantify how often epigenomic mapping scores (<0.5) contradict sequence-based mappability in the uniquely mapped group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is orthologous region identification itself rather than post-hoc quality stratification — use the full AdaLiftOver pipeline with gr_candidate_filter() instead of the partitioning analysis. When query regions are coding or already unambiguously annotated orthologs, where multi-mapping assessment of non-coding regulatory elements is not the question.
