skills.search_text: multipanel-figure-composition Use when many per-sample QC summaries (e.g., FASTQ per-cycle quality and read-quality distributions) must be arranged into one combined multi-panel plot/report for visual inspection of large sample sets. Input is a single sample with no need for a combined multi-file layout — a single-panel QC plot suffices The data are not short reads in FASTQ format and no per-file QC summaries (per-cycle qualities, read-quality distributions) exist to arrange into panels The goal is interactive exploration rather than a reproducible, report-embedded figure artifact http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Compose per-sample quality results (e.g., FASTQ QC statistics) into a single combined multi-panel figure, as systemPipeR's seeFastq/seeFastqPlot do for FASTQ quality reports, so large numbers of files can be visually inspected in one report. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1241-0
skills.summary: Compose per-sample quality results (e.g., FASTQ QC statistics) into a single combined multi-panel figure, as systemPipeR's seeFastq/seeFastqPlot do for FASTQ quality reports, so large numbers of files can be visually inspected in one report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single sample with no need for a combined multi-file layout — a single-panel QC plot suffices The data are not short reads in FASTQ format and no per-file QC summaries (per-cycle qualities, read-quality distributions) exist to arrange into panels The goal is interactive exploration rather than a reproducible, report-embedded figure artifact

skills.description: Use when you have a delila-generated book of unaligned input sequences and need to find the multiple alignment that maximizes information content before calculating per-sequence information or building a sequence logo.
skills.name: multiple-alignment-information-maximization
skills.search_text: multiple-alignment-information-maximization Use when you have a delila-generated book of unaligned input sequences and need to find the multiple alignment that maximizes information content before calculating per-sequence information or building a sequence logo. You do not yet have a delila-generated book of sequences — the pipeline must first run dbbk, catal, and delila on the GenBank file and sites file You only need a final motif/logo and already possess an independently verified alignment of binding sites — cycle 1 re-alignment is unnecessary and cycle 3 tools (dalvec, makelogo) suffice You want de novo motif discovery from raw reads with expectation maximization or Gibbs sampling — tools like MEME or BioProspector are the article's cited alternatives http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Cycle 1 of the Delila-PY pipeline: the malign and malin programs search among all input sequences for the multiple alignment with the highest information content, and malin's results are fed back to delila to generate an updated book of sequences for downstream motif construction. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: Cycle 1 of the Delila-PY pipeline: the malign and malin programs search among all input sequences for the multiple alignment with the highest information content, and malin's results are fed back to delila to generate an updated book of sequences for downstream motif construction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You do not yet have a delila-generated book of sequences — the pipeline must first run dbbk, catal, and delila on the GenBank file and sites file You only need a final motif/logo and already possess an independently verified alignment of binding sites — cycle 1 re-alignment is unnecessary and cycle 3 tools (dalvec, makelogo) suffice You want de novo motif discovery from raw reads with expectation maximization or Gibbs sampling — tools like MEME or BioProspector are the article's cited alternatives

skills.description: Use when a large family of one-sided Fisher's exact tests (e.g., clusterProfiler::enrichGO GO term enrichment of BIT top-ranked TRs) must be corrected for multiple testing, with terms ranked by BH-adjusted p values at a q-value cutoff of 0.05.
skills.name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction Use when a large family of one-sided Fisher's exact tests (e.g., clusterProfiler::enrichGO GO term enrichment of BIT top-ranked TRs) must be corrected for multiple testing, with terms ranked by BH-adjusted p values at a q-value cutoff of 0.05. The quantity of interest is a BIT score with a Bayesian 95% credible interval from posterior sampling — uncertainty is already quantified by MCMC posterior draws, so frequentist BH adjustment is not the appropriate mechanism for TR ranking itself Only a single pre-specified hypothesis test is performed (no multiple-testing family), where an unadjusted p value suffices Input is raw ATAC-seq data or peak calls (e.g., MACS2 -q 0.01 peaks) rather than ranked TR lists requiring post-hoc GO enrichment correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment to control the false discovery rate when ranking statistically significant results from many simultaneous one-sided Fisher's exact tests, as done in the BIT paper's GO enrichment analysis of top-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) adjustment to control the false discovery rate when ranking statistically significant results from many simultaneous one-sided Fisher's exact tests, as done in the BIT paper's GO enrichment analysis of top-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The quantity of interest is a BIT score with a Bayesian 95% credible interval from posterior sampling — uncertainty is already quantified by MCMC posterior draws, so frequentist BH adjustment is not the appropriate mechanism for TR ranking itself Only a single pre-specified hypothesis test is performed (no multiple-testing family), where an unadjusted p value suffices Input is raw ATAC-seq data or peak calls (e.g., MACS2 -q 0.01 peaks) rather than ranked TR lists requiring post-hoc GO enrichment correction

skills.description: Use when calling or powering differential expression / eQTL tests across many genes in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, where a per-gene threshold must be corrected for the number of expressed genes tested.
skills.name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction Use when calling or powering differential expression / eQTL tests across many genes in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, where a per-gene threshold must be corrected for the number of expressed genes tested. The article's own DE power workflow uses MTmethod='FDR' for the pseudobulk negative binomial power model — do not force Bonferroni when the analysis design specifies FDR control Single-hypothesis testing with no family of gene-level tests — no correction basis applies http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Bonferroni-style multiple-testing correction to gene-level significance testing in single cell pseudobulk DE and eQTL power analysis, using the estimated number of expressed genes as the effective number of tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Apply Bonferroni-style multiple-testing correction to gene-level significance testing in single cell pseudobulk DE and eQTL power analysis, using the estimated number of expressed genes as the effective number of tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The article's own DE power workflow uses MTmethod='FDR' for the pseudobulk negative binomial power model — do not force Bonferroni when the analysis design specifies FDR control Single-hypothesis testing with no family of gene-level tests — no correction basis applies

skills.description: Use when a differential-expression or regression analysis produces thousands of raw p-values (one per gene or TR) and hits must be called with a controlled false-discovery rate, e.g. adjusted p-value < 0.05.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction Use when a differential-expression or regression analysis produces thousands of raw p-values (one per gene or TR) and hits must be called with a controlled false-discovery rate, e.g. adjusted p-value < 0.05. Only one or a small pre-specified number of hypotheses is tested, where the BH adjustment provides little benefit and raw p-values are interpretable Adjusted p-values are being computed per gene on subsets of features after filtering on effect size, which can distort the FDR calculation relative to the full test set http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to raw per-gene p-values from differential-expression analyses so that significance calls (e.g. EZH2/PRC2 down-regulation in BRAF inhibitor-resistant cells) control the expected proportion of false positives across thousands of simultaneous tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction to raw per-gene p-values from differential-expression analyses so that significance calls (e.g. EZH2/PRC2 down-regulation in BRAF inhibitor-resistant cells) control the expected proportion of false positives across thousands of simultaneous tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one or a small pre-specified number of hypotheses is tested, where the BH adjustment provides little benefit and raw p-values are interpretable Adjusted p-values are being computed per gene on subsets of features after filtering on effect size, which can distort the FDR calculation relative to the full test set

skills.description: Use when testing many motifs or functional terms simultaneously — e.g. PASTAA on REM sequences ranked by Cell type score, or g:Profiler on ~1,721 ARID3A-associated genes — to control the false discovery rate at BH FDR ≤ 0.05.
skills.name: multiple-testing-correction-fdr
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-correction-fdr Use when testing many motifs or functional terms simultaneously — e.g. PASTAA on REM sequences ranked by Cell type score, or g:Profiler on ~1,721 ARID3A-associated genes — to control the false discovery rate at BH FDR ≤ 0.05. When the analysis is not a multiple-testing setting — e.g. inspecting a single REM's activity or Cell type score in EpiRegio rather than testing many motifs or terms at once When a raw p-value threshold is explicitly required by the downstream protocol instead of a BH-adjusted one http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction to declare significance in enrichment analyses performed with EpiRegio-based workflows, using an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05 for both PASTAA TF motif enrichment over ranked REM sequences and g:Profiler GO/KEGG enrichment of TF target genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Apply Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction to declare significance in enrichment analyses performed with EpiRegio-based workflows, using an adjusted p-value cutoff of 0.05 for both PASTAA TF motif enrichment over ranked REM sequences and g:Profiler GO/KEGG enrichment of TF target genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis is not a multiple-testing setting — e.g. inspecting a single REM's activity or Cell type score in EpiRegio rather than testing many motifs or terms at once When a raw p-value threshold is explicitly required by the downstream protocol instead of a BH-adjusted one

skills.description: Use when you have per-RBP constraint regressions (mean delta score vs. gnomAD allele-frequency bin) over Skipper enriched windows and must aggregate to RBP-transcript pairs and control the false discovery rate to nominate constrained transcripts.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-correction Use when you have per-RBP constraint regressions (mean delta score vs. gnomAD allele-frequency bin) over Skipper enriched windows and must aggregate to RBP-transcript pairs and control the false discovery rate to nominate constrained transcripts. Your dataset lacks a matched input control sample, so Skipper cannot build the beta-binomial model and no reproducible enriched windows exist to aggregate for constraint testing You need window-level or site-level constraint calls; the paper's framework nominates only RBP-transcript pairs after transcript-level aggregation, not individual constrained binding windows You are testing within a single pre-specified RBP-transcript hypothesis, where a single statistical test needs no FDR correction http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Aggregates selective-constraint signal (gnomAD allele-frequency-bin regression of LS-GKM delta scores) from Skipper-defined translation factor binding windows up to the transcript level, then applies multiple-testing correction at a 10% FDR threshold to nominate constrained RBP-transcript pairs. Used because per-window constraint tests are underpowered individually, while transcript-level aggregation is a well-powered hypothesis-generating intermediate. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Aggregates selective-constraint signal (gnomAD allele-frequency-bin regression of LS-GKM delta scores) from Skipper-defined translation factor binding windows up to the transcript level, then applies multiple-testing correction at a 10% FDR threshold to nominate constrained RBP-transcript pairs. Used because per-window constraint tests are underpowered individually, while transcript-level aggregation is a well-powered hypothesis-generating intermediate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your dataset lacks a matched input control sample, so Skipper cannot build the beta-binomial model and no reproducible enriched windows exist to aggregate for constraint testing You need window-level or site-level constraint calls; the paper's framework nominates only RBP-transcript pairs after transcript-level aggregation, not individual constrained binding windows You are testing within a single pre-specified RBP-transcript hypothesis, where a single statistical test needs no FDR correction

skills.description: Use when a CITRUS in silico knock out or association analysis yields one raw p-value per TF (hundreds of TFs tested simultaneously) and significant TF–alteration or TF-overlap associations must be controlled for multiple testing.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-correction Use when a CITRUS in silico knock out or association analysis yields one raw p-value per TF (hundreds of TFs tested simultaneously) and significant TF–alteration or TF-overlap associations must be controlled for multiple testing. When only a single hypothesis is tested (e.g., one TF against one alteration) — no correction is needed and BH adjustment would be conservative. When the goal is ranking or effect-size estimation of TF activities rather than calling significance; FDR q-values alter ranking and should not replace effect sizes. When p-values are not independent or positively correlated in a BH-compatible manner without verification — e.g., heavily correlated TF families sharing motifs. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to p-value vectors arising from per-TF association testing (e.g., two-sample t-tests of CITRUS-inferred TF activities against somatic alteration status), so that significant TF–alteration associations are reported at FDR-adjusted P-value < 0.05. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to p-value vectors arising from per-TF association testing (e.g., two-sample t-tests of CITRUS-inferred TF activities against somatic alteration status), so that significant TF–alteration associations are reported at FDR-adjusted P-value < 0.05.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only a single hypothesis is tested (e.g., one TF against one alteration) — no correction is needed and BH adjustment would be conservative. When the goal is ranking or effect-size estimation of TF activities rather than calling significance; FDR q-values alter ranking and should not replace effect sizes. When p-values are not independent or positively correlated in a BH-compatible manner without verification — e.g., heavily correlated TF families sharing motifs.

skills.description: Use when dcHiC has produced one raw chi-square p-value per genomic bin (from Mahalanobis distance on quantile-normalized compartment scores) or per candidate interaction, and you must call significant differential compartments or interactions at a controlled adjusted-p threshold such as FDR 10%.
skills.name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-fdr-correction Use when dcHiC has produced one raw chi-square p-value per genomic bin (from Mahalanobis distance on quantile-normalized compartment scores) or per candidate interaction, and you must call significant differential compartments or interactions at a controlled adjusted-p threshold such as FDR 10%. You have a single hypothesis test or per-test alpha control is required (e.g., permutation-derived empirical p-values already calibrated) — family-wise or empirical calibration is a different problem than FDR control over genome-wide bin sets Input is a single Hi-C map with no replicates or comparison, since there is no multivariate Mahalanobis p-value distribution to correct The p-values come from a different compartment tool (e.g., HOMER differential scores) whose null distribution assumptions differ from dcHiC's chi-square-on-Mahalanobis-distance scheme http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Adjusts per-bin chi-square p-values from dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance differential compartment test (and p-values from its differential interaction module) for multiple testing using IHW with per-replicate variance as covariate, or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, so that significant compartment differences are called at a controlled false discovery rate (e.g., FDR 10%). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Adjusts per-bin chi-square p-values from dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance differential compartment test (and p-values from its differential interaction module) for multiple testing using IHW with per-replicate variance as covariate, or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, so that significant compartment differences are called at a controlled false discovery rate (e.g., FDR 10%).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have a single hypothesis test or per-test alpha control is required (e.g., permutation-derived empirical p-values already calibrated) — family-wise or empirical calibration is a different problem than FDR control over genome-wide bin sets Input is a single Hi-C map with no replicates or comparison, since there is no multivariate Mahalanobis p-value distribution to correct The p-values come from a different compartment tool (e.g., HOMER differential scores) whose null distribution assumptions differ from dcHiC's chi-square-on-Mahalanobis-distance scheme

skills.description: Use when a genome-wide scan (e.g., driverpower infer over eight test element sets: CDS, splice site, 5'-UTR, 3'-UTR, promoter, enhancer, lncRNA, lncRNA promoter) has produced raw p-values that must be converted to q-values before calling driver candidates.
skills.name: multiple-testing-qvalue-correction
skills.search_text: multiple-testing-qvalue-correction Use when a genome-wide scan (e.g., driverpower infer over eight test element sets: CDS, splice site, 5'-UTR, 3'-UTR, promoter, enhancer, lncRNA, lncRNA promoter) has produced raw p-values that must be converted to q-values before calling driver candidates. Input is a single pre-specified genomic element tested without a genome-wide multiplicity burden (no FDR correction needed) The background mutation rate (BMR) model has not yet been trained — run 'driverpower model' on train_feature.hdf5 and the training response table first Variants lack CADD PHRED scores and burden-test-only calling without functional adjustment is the intended mode http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to per-element p-values from DriverPower's burden/functional-impact tests and retains driver candidates with q < 0.1, controlling the false discovery rate when testing thousands of coding and non-coding elements across 2583 PCAWG cancer genomes. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Applies Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction to per-element p-values from DriverPower's burden/functional-impact tests and retains driver candidates with q < 0.1, controlling the false discovery rate when testing thousands of coding and non-coding elements across 2583 PCAWG cancer genomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single pre-specified genomic element tested without a genome-wide multiplicity burden (no FDR correction needed) The background mutation rate (BMR) model has not yet been trained — run 'driverpower model' on train_feature.hdf5 and the training response table first Variants lack CADD PHRED scores and burden-test-only calling without functional adjustment is the intended mode

skills.description: Use when planning or costing a 10X droplet scRNA-seq experiment with scPower and you must account for usable cells per lane given multiplet loss as a function of cells loaded per lane.
skills.name: multiplet-rate-modeling-10x-genomics
skills.search_text: multiplet-rate-modeling-10x-genomics Use when planning or costing a 10X droplet scRNA-seq experiment with scPower and you must account for usable cells per lane given multiplet loss as a function of cells loaded per lane. Data were generated with plate-based (non-droplet) or non-10X single cell protocols, for which the 10X user-guide-V3-derived multiplet model does not apply You already have an empirical doublet rate measured for your own experiment (e.g. from hashtag multiplexing or Scrublet), which should take precedence over the generic linear model http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Models the 10X Genomics multiplet (doublet) rate as a linear function of the number of cells loaded per lane, calibrated on the 10X Genomics user guide V3, so that experimental design and budget calculations account for cells lost to multiplets. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Models the 10X Genomics multiplet (doublet) rate as a linear function of the number of cells loaded per lane, calibrated on the 10X Genomics user guide V3, so that experimental design and budget calculations account for cells lost to multiplets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data were generated with plate-based (non-droplet) or non-10X single cell protocols, for which the 10X user-guide-V3-derived multiplet model does not apply You already have an empirical doublet rate measured for your own experiment (e.g. from hashtag multiplexing or Scrublet), which should take precedence over the generic linear model

skills.description: Use when analyzing 3D chromatin tracing coordinates (per-cell x/y/z per locus) to call chromatin loops with SnapFISH, or to test how detection-efficiency stratification affects loop-calling sensitivity and false positives.
skills.name: multiplexed-dna-fish-loop-calling
skills.search_text: multiplexed-dna-fish-loop-calling Use when analyzing 3D chromatin tracing coordinates (per-cell x/y/z per locus) to call chromatin loops with SnapFISH, or to test how detection-efficiency stratification affects loop-calling sensitivity and false positives. Input is proximity-ligation assay data (Hi-C/Micro-C contact counts) rather than per-cell 3D imaging coordinates — existing count-based loop callers, not SnapFISH, apply The goal is detecting multi-way (higher-order) chromatin interactions — SnapFISH only considers pair-wise interactions The data are DNA seqFISH+ mESC datasets where the authors note sensitivity can be further improved, if high-sensitivity de novo calling is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reproduce SnapFISH-based chromatin loop calling on multiplexed DNA FISH (chromatin tracing) data, stratified by allele and targeted segment detection efficiency, to quantify how low detection efficiency inflates false-positive loop calls (e.g., 3 false positives for the weak-loop CAST allele at ~57%/55% detection). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-40658-3
skills.summary: Reproduce SnapFISH-based chromatin loop calling on multiplexed DNA FISH (chromatin tracing) data, stratified by allele and targeted segment detection efficiency, to quantify how low detection efficiency inflates false-positive loop calls (e.g., 3 false positives for the weak-loop CAST allele at ~57%/55% detection).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is proximity-ligation assay data (Hi-C/Micro-C contact counts) rather than per-cell 3D imaging coordinates — existing count-based loop callers, not SnapFISH, apply The goal is detecting multi-way (higher-order) chromatin interactions — SnapFISH only considers pair-wise interactions The data are DNA seqFISH+ mESC datasets where the authors note sensitivity can be further improved, if high-sensitivity de novo calling is required

skills.description: Reference for combining multiple per-sample NGS quality-control outputs (FastQC, trimming/mapping stats) from a Nextflow/CIPHER run into one aggregated MultiQC report instead of inspecting each QC file individually.
skills.name: multiqc-report-aggregation
skills.search_text: multiqc-report-aggregation Reference for combining multiple per-sample NGS quality-control outputs (FastQC, trimming/mapping stats) from a Nextflow/CIPHER run into one aggregated MultiQC report instead of inspecting each QC file individually. The config mixes single-ended and pair-ended data in one file — the README states 'CIPHER DOES NOT HANDLE THIS USE-CASE YET', so the aggregated QC step cannot be reached reliably You only need a subset of pipeline steps (e.g. MultiQC alone) — the article notes 'CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, but we are aware that individuals may prefer to use only a subset of tools' Input data are not NGS datasets supported by CIPHER (ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, MNase-seq, DNase-seq, GRO-seq, ATAC-seq); e.g. GWAS or de novo transcriptome assembly have no pipeline Aggregate the per-sample quality-control outputs generated by CIPHER's five-step NGS pre-processing stage (FastQC, trimming, mapping, visualization, QC) into a single consolidated report via MultiQC, giving one at-a-glance QC view across all datasets in the run. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1
skills.summary: Aggregate the per-sample quality-control outputs generated by CIPHER's five-step NGS pre-processing stage (FastQC, trimming, mapping, visualization, QC) into a single consolidated report via MultiQC, giving one at-a-glance QC view across all datasets in the run.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The config mixes single-ended and pair-ended data in one file — the README states 'CIPHER DOES NOT HANDLE THIS USE-CASE YET', so the aggregated QC step cannot be reached reliably You only need a subset of pipeline steps (e.g. MultiQC alone) — the article notes 'CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, but we are aware that individuals may prefer to use only a subset of tools' Input data are not NGS datasets supported by CIPHER (ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, MNase-seq, DNase-seq, GRO-seq, ATAC-seq); e.g. GWAS or de novo transcriptome assembly have no pipeline

skills.description: Use when a ChIP-seq signal (e.g. H3K27me3 in human CD4+ T cells, chromosome 1) must be analyzed across multiple length scales to measure how its spatial auto-correlation length evolves under recursive coarse-graining.
skills.name: multiscale-genomic-signal-analysis
skills.search_text: multiscale-genomic-signal-analysis Use when a ChIP-seq signal (e.g. H3K27me3 in human CD4+ T cells, chromosome 1) must be analyzed across multiple length scales to measure how its spatial auto-correlation length evolves under recursive coarse-graining. The goal is standard sharp-peak calling with a local statistical model rather than multi-scale broad-domain or scale-dependence analysis The input is already a called peak/domain list or feature table rather than raw mapped reads in BED format Only a single-scale enrichment profile is needed and the recursive coarse-graining/auto-correlation machinery would add no information http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Characterize genomic ChIP-seq signal across length scales by applying RECOGNICER's recursive block transformation with phase optimization and fitting the auto-correlation function C(r) ~ C0 * exp(-r/lambda) at each coarse-graining round, to reveal scale-dependent structure (e.g. growing auto-correlation length in real H3K27me3 data vs ~100 kb in synthetic data). epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Characterize genomic ChIP-seq signal across length scales by applying RECOGNICER's recursive block transformation with phase optimization and fitting the auto-correlation function C(r) ~ C0 * exp(-r/lambda) at each coarse-graining round, to reveal scale-dependent structure (e.g. growing auto-correlation length in real H3K27me3 data vs ~100 kb in synthetic data).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is standard sharp-peak calling with a local statistical model rather than multi-scale broad-domain or scale-dependence analysis The input is already a called peak/domain list or feature table rather than raw mapped reads in BED format Only a single-scale enrichment profile is needed and the recursive coarse-graining/auto-correlation machinery would add no information

skills.description: Use when paired-end MNase-seq (or ATAC-seq) reads and a reference genome sequence are available and the goal is a probabilistic occupancy landscape of nucleosomes and transcription factors across the genome.
skills.name: multivariate-hmm-chromatin-inference
skills.search_text: multivariate-hmm-chromatin-inference Use when paired-end MNase-seq (or ATAC-seq) reads and a reference genome sequence are available and the goal is a probabilistic occupancy landscape of nucleosomes and transcription factors across the genome. The goal is peak calling of a single factor rather than joint probabilistic occupancy of hundreds of DBFs and nucleosomes — the paper shows MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling is the alternative (lower-performing) approach Only ATAC-seq data are available and MNase-seq could be used instead — the article reports markedly better performance with MNase-seq for two primary reasons (genome-wide fragment distribution and MNase exonuclease activity reflecting DBF sizes) No nucleotide sequence input can be supplied — RoboCOP integrates accessibility data with nucleotide sequence as joint input http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Infers genome-wide probabilistic occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors by running RoboCOP's multivariate HMM, which integrates chromatin accessibility data (paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence at single-nucleotide resolution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Infers genome-wide probabilistic occupancy profiles of nucleosomes and DNA-binding factors by running RoboCOP's multivariate HMM, which integrates chromatin accessibility data (paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq) with nucleotide sequence at single-nucleotide resolution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peak calling of a single factor rather than joint probabilistic occupancy of hundreds of DBFs and nucleosomes — the paper shows MACS2 peak/footprint identification followed by FIMO TF-labeling is the alternative (lower-performing) approach Only ATAC-seq data are available and MNase-seq could be used instead — the article reports markedly better performance with MNase-seq for two primary reasons (genome-wide fragment distribution and MNase exonuclease activity reflecting DBF sizes) No nucleotide sequence input can be supplied — RoboCOP integrates accessibility data with nucleotide sequence as joint input

skills.description: Use when you have BHi-Cect's named list of loci per cluster (bottom enclaves) plus ChIP-seq peaks for a set of TFs and need to check whether a low-dimensional CA projection summarizes regulatory regimes across enclaves.
skills.name: multivariate-variance-explained-interpretation
skills.search_text: multivariate-variance-explained-interpretation Use when you have BHi-Cect's named list of loci per cluster (bottom enclaves) plus ChIP-seq peaks for a set of TFs and need to check whether a low-dimensional CA projection summarizes regulatory regimes across enclaves. Input is still raw 3-column sparse Hi-C contact data that has not been clustered by BHi-Cect — the CA operates on per-enclave TF counts, not on the contact matrix (build clusters first with Rao_matrix, pow_trans, spec_bipart). You have no TF binding data (e.g., only RNAP2/H3K4me3 tracks) and instead need GSEA-style prevalence enrichment in bottom enclaves — that is a different analysis in the article. The table is already a low-dimensional coordinate/embedding rather than raw counts per enclave — computing CA would double-transform the data. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Summarize and compare the regulatory contexts of BHi-Cect bottom (leaf) enclaves by running correspondence analysis (CA) on a TF-by-bottom-enclave contingency table of ChIP-seq binding counts, then interpret the leading CA axes via their explained variance (the first two dimensions capture ~63.3% of total inertia in the IMR90 analysis). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa004
skills.summary: Summarize and compare the regulatory contexts of BHi-Cect bottom (leaf) enclaves by running correspondence analysis (CA) on a TF-by-bottom-enclave contingency table of ChIP-seq binding counts, then interpret the leading CA axes via their explained variance (the first two dimensions capture ~63.3% of total inertia in the IMR90 analysis).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is still raw 3-column sparse Hi-C contact data that has not been clustered by BHi-Cect — the CA operates on per-enclave TF counts, not on the contact matrix (build clusters first with Rao_matrix, pow_trans, spec_bipart). You have no TF binding data (e.g., only RNAP2/H3K4me3 tracks) and instead need GSEA-style prevalence enrichment in bottom enclaves — that is a different analysis in the article. The table is already a low-dimensional coordinate/embedding rather than raw counts per enclave — computing CA would double-transform the data.

skills.description: Use when eCLIP data exist for both wild-type and missense-mutant versions of an RBP (e.g., RPS19 R62W/R101H) and the goal is to detect altered binding — region-proportion shifts or novel target classes like tRNA loci.
skills.name: mutant-vs-wildtype-binding-comparison
skills.search_text: mutant-vs-wildtype-binding-comparison Use when eCLIP data exist for both wild-type and missense-mutant versions of an RBP (e.g., RPS19 R62W/R101H) and the goal is to detect altered binding — region-proportion shifts or novel target classes like tRNA loci. CLIP datasets lacking matched input samples — Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model, so mutant-vs-WT enrichment cannot be tested Questions about the mechanism of binding changes (complex formation, localization, vs. binding preference) — eCLIP data alone cannot distinguish these Single-replicate data without matched WT/mutant pairs — paired t-tests across matched replicates are required for the differential enrichment step http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 Compare eCLIP RNA-binding profiles of mutant versus wild-type RBP constructs using Skipper's reproducible_enriched_windows: quantify shifts in transcript-region binding proportions and test differential enrichment (e.g., tRNA loci) with paired statistics across matched replicates. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Compare eCLIP RNA-binding profiles of mutant versus wild-type RBP constructs using Skipper's reproducible_enriched_windows: quantify shifts in transcript-region binding proportions and test differential enrichment (e.g., tRNA loci) with paired statistics across matched replicates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking matched input samples — Skipper cannot construct the beta-binomial model, so mutant-vs-WT enrichment cannot be tested Questions about the mechanism of binding changes (complex formation, localization, vs. binding preference) — eCLIP data alone cannot distinguish these Single-replicate data without matched WT/mutant pairs — paired t-tests across matched replicates are required for the differential enrichment step

skills.description: Use when validating DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates (e.g. SGK1 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) by asking whether mutated samples show differential gene expression after correcting for copy number and tissue.
skills.name: mutation-expression-association-testing
skills.search_text: mutation-expression-association-testing Use when validating DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates (e.g. SGK1 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) by asking whether mutated samples show differential gene expression after correcting for copy number and tissue. Input is already a DriverPower background-model feature table (train_feature.hdf5 / test_feature.hdf5) rather than per-sample expression — this skill is for downstream expression validation, not driver discovery The goal is to call driver elements from somatic mutations alone (use the driverpower model/infer sub-commands instead) Samples lack copy-number state (SCNA) or tissue labels, since the GLM requires both covariates for the copy-number-corrected test http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Tests whether samples carrying mutations in DriverPower-exclusive candidate elements show copy-number-corrected differential expression, by fitting quasi-Poisson GLMs on PCAWG per-sample FPKM-UQ gene expression with MUT and SCNA covariates and comparing full vs. null models via a likelihood ratio test. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Tests whether samples carrying mutations in DriverPower-exclusive candidate elements show copy-number-corrected differential expression, by fitting quasi-Poisson GLMs on PCAWG per-sample FPKM-UQ gene expression with MUT and SCNA covariates and comparing full vs. null models via a likelihood ratio test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a DriverPower background-model feature table (train_feature.hdf5 / test_feature.hdf5) rather than per-sample expression — this skill is for downstream expression validation, not driver discovery The goal is to call driver elements from somatic mutations alone (use the driverpower model/infer sub-commands instead) Samples lack copy-number state (SCNA) or tissue labels, since the GLM requires both covariates for the copy-number-corrected test

skills.description: Use when CCLE mutation annotation and drug-sensitivity (e.g. PLX4720) tables are available and the goal is to test whether a co-mutation class (BRAF + PRC2/H3K27me3 loss) shifts pharmacological response versus a single-mutant baseline.
skills.name: mutation-status-cell-line-partitioning
skills.search_text: mutation-status-cell-line-partitioning Use when CCLE mutation annotation and drug-sensitivity (e.g. PLX4720) tables are available and the goal is to test whether a co-mutation class (BRAF + PRC2/H3K27me3 loss) shifts pharmacological response versus a single-mutant baseline. No post-treatment data are available: RePhine's CCLE analysis lacks post-treatment data, so acquired-resistance mechanisms (e.g. acquired STAT3 activation driving erlotinib resistance) cannot be detected from pre-treatment mutation/drug-response associations The cell lines being partitioned do not carry BRAF mutations, since the comparison is anchored on BRAF-mutant lines Only mRNA levels are available without mutation/pharmacology profiles — mRNA-only TR–drug prediction is described as not sufficiently robust due to inherent experimental noises Stratifies CCLE cancer cell lines by mutation status — BRAF-mutant lines split into double-mutants (BRAF plus loss-of-function alterations in H3K27me3/PRC2 genes such as EZH2) versus BRAF-only — and tests whether the two groups differ in PLX4720 drug-sensitivity response using a two-sample t-test. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Stratifies CCLE cancer cell lines by mutation status — BRAF-mutant lines split into double-mutants (BRAF plus loss-of-function alterations in H3K27me3/PRC2 genes such as EZH2) versus BRAF-only — and tests whether the two groups differ in PLX4720 drug-sensitivity response using a two-sample t-test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No post-treatment data are available: RePhine's CCLE analysis lacks post-treatment data, so acquired-resistance mechanisms (e.g. acquired STAT3 activation driving erlotinib resistance) cannot be detected from pre-treatment mutation/drug-response associations The cell lines being partitioned do not carry BRAF mutations, since the comparison is anchored on BRAF-mutant lines Only mRNA levels are available without mutation/pharmacology profiles — mRNA-only TR–drug prediction is described as not sufficiently robust due to inherent experimental noises

skills.description: Use when ranking over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs from a positive/control FASTA pair where occurrence-count-biased statistics would favor long or highly degenerate motifs; each candidate motif has a contingency table of counts (a, b, c, d).
skills.name: mutual-information-scoring-from-contingency-tables
skills.search_text: mutual-information-scoring-from-contingency-tables Use when ranking over-represented degenerate IUPAC motifs from a positive/control FASTA pair where occurrence-count-biased statistics would favor long or highly degenerate motifs; each candidate motif has a contingency table of counts (a, b, c, d). When a count-normalized enrichment statistic tied to occurrence frequency is explicitly required, e.g. comparing motif significance via Fisher's exact test P-value alone, since MI is deliberately independent of occurrence count When motifs cannot be represented in the IUPAC degenerate alphabet or when the analysis requires position-specific frequency matrices rather than discrete degenerate consensus motifs When only one dataset (no positive/control pair) is available, as MI here is defined over the contingency between motif presence and the positive-vs-negative condition http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Scores and ranks degenerate IUPAC motifs by mutual information (MI) computed from 2x2 contingency tables (motif presence/absence vs positive/negative dataset), so motif quality is captured independently of occurrence count — unlike Fisher's exact test P-value, which is biased by occurrence number. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Scores and ranks degenerate IUPAC motifs by mutual information (MI) computed from 2x2 contingency tables (motif presence/absence vs positive/negative dataset), so motif quality is captured independently of occurrence count — unlike Fisher's exact test P-value, which is biased by occurrence number.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a count-normalized enrichment statistic tied to occurrence frequency is explicitly required, e.g. comparing motif significance via Fisher's exact test P-value alone, since MI is deliberately independent of occurrence count When motifs cannot be represented in the IUPAC degenerate alphabet or when the analysis requires position-specific frequency matrices rather than discrete degenerate consensus motifs When only one dataset (no positive/control pair) is available, as MI here is defined over the contingency between motif presence and the positive-vs-negative condition

skills.description: Use when comparing de novo assembly quality (N50, mismatch rate, and related Quast metrics) between a chemically treated read set (e.g. RIMS-seq alkaline-treated) and a standard DNA-seq control to show the treatment preserves assembly metrics.
skills.name: n50-mismatch-rate-benchmarking
skills.search_text: n50-mismatch-rate-benchmarking Use when comparing de novo assembly quality (N50, mismatch rate, and related Quast metrics) between a chemically treated read set (e.g. RIMS-seq alkaline-treated) and a standard DNA-seq control to show the treatment preserves assembly metrics. The library preparation is based on tagmentation rather than adapter ligation — the article states RIMS-seq does not work with tagmentation-based protocols An exact reference genome is available and only methylase specificity (not assembly quality) is needed — the RIMS-seq option 2 analysis path skips SPAdes assembly entirely http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks de novo bacterial genome assembly quality by comparing N50 and mismatch rate between alkaline-treated RIMS-seq reads and a DNA-seq(+3H) control, using SPAdes for assembly and Quast for metric extraction, to verify that the RIMS-seq NaOH treatment does not degrade assembly quality. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Benchmarks de novo bacterial genome assembly quality by comparing N50 and mismatch rate between alkaline-treated RIMS-seq reads and a DNA-seq(+3H) control, using SPAdes for assembly and Quast for metric extraction, to verify that the RIMS-seq NaOH treatment does not degrade assembly quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library preparation is based on tagmentation rather than adapter ligation — the article states RIMS-seq does not work with tagmentation-based protocols An exact reference genome is available and only methylase specificity (not assembly quality) is needed — the RIMS-seq option 2 analysis path skips SPAdes assembly entirely

skills.description: Use when you have ONT FAST5 data basecalled with Albacore and need base-level translocation times in seconds — e.g. to build per-window TT quantiles for non-B DNA versus B-DNA comparisons.
skills.name: nanopore-event-table-to-translocation-time-conversion
skills.search_text: nanopore-event-table-to-translocation-time-conversion Use when you have ONT FAST5 data basecalled with Albacore and need base-level translocation times in seconds — e.g. to build per-window TT quantiles for non-B DNA versus B-DNA comparisons. The input is already a per-base translocation-time table produced by Tombo re-squiggling — go directly to window preparation and TT quantile computation. You only have Albacore event tables without Tombo re-squiggling: Albacore assumes the block stride attribute remains fixed, so it cannot yield the base-level measurement counts needed for TT conversion. Your goal is motif detection (GoFAE-DND novelty detection) rather than constructing the underlying TT signal. Converts Oxford Nanopore raw-signal events into per-base translocation times (seconds), computed as the number of current measurements per base divided by the ONT sampling rate. This translocation-time (TT) signal is the measurement basis for detecting non-B DNA structure effects in the ONT-nonb-GoFAE-DND workflow. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Converts Oxford Nanopore raw-signal events into per-base translocation times (seconds), computed as the number of current measurements per base divided by the ONT sampling rate. This translocation-time (TT) signal is the measurement basis for detecting non-B DNA structure effects in the ONT-nonb-GoFAE-DND workflow.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-base translocation-time table produced by Tombo re-squiggling — go directly to window preparation and TT quantile computation. You only have Albacore event tables without Tombo re-squiggling: Albacore assumes the block stride attribute remains fixed, so it cannot yield the base-level measurement counts needed for TT conversion. Your goal is motif detection (GoFAE-DND novelty detection) rather than constructing the underlying TT signal.

skills.description: Use when you have raw nanopore FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences without prior signal segmentation.
skills.name: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling
skills.search_text: nanopore-raw-signal-basecalling Use when you have raw nanopore FAST5 electrolytic-current signal files and need to decode them into per-read nucleotide sequences without prior signal segmentation. Your genome is large: Chiron runs at only ~2000 bp/s, making it unsuitable for large genomes Your input is already base-called (FASTQ/BAM) rather than raw FAST5 signal — re-base-calling is unnecessary You need a production ONT-supported caller with modified-base support rather than an end-to-end research/benchmarking tool http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Base-call Oxford Nanopore raw ion-current signal (FAST5) directly into nucleotide sequences using an end-to-end deep-learning model such as Chiron, which was the first deep-learning model to translate raw signal to sequence without an error-prone segmentation step. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xinn.2021.100153
skills.summary: Base-call Oxford Nanopore raw ion-current signal (FAST5) directly into nucleotide sequences using an end-to-end deep-learning model such as Chiron, which was the first deep-learning model to translate raw signal to sequence without an error-prone segmentation step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your genome is large: Chiron runs at only ~2000 bp/s, making it unsuitable for large genomes Your input is already base-called (FASTQ/BAM) rather than raw FAST5 signal — re-base-calling is unnecessary You need a production ONT-supported caller with modified-base support rather than an end-to-end research/benchmarking tool

skills.description: Use when assembling genomes from noisy Oxford Nanopore long reads and you must choose between correct-then-assemble vs assemble-then-correct correction strategies, or when polishing a draft long-read assembly to final accuracy with Illumina short reads.

skills.description: Use when ONT nanopore FAST5 reads (e.g. NA12878 / SRR15058166) must be converted to per-base translocation times and scored for non-B DNA novelty against motif-free B-DNA controls at an FDR-controlled level.
skills.name: nanopore-translocation-time-novelty-detection
skills.search_text: nanopore-translocation-time-novelty-detection Use when ONT nanopore FAST5 reads (e.g. NA12878 / SRR15058166) must be converted to per-base translocation times and scored for non-B DNA novelty against motif-free B-DNA controls at an FDR-controlled level. Input is not nanopore current signal (e.g. Illumina reads or SMRT data, where sequencing speed is determined by polymerization rather than pore translocation) The goal is supervised classification with abundant labeled non-B examples at balanced ratios; the paper shows novelty detectors are most valuable at extreme non-B:B ratios (e.g. 0.05) and classifiers underperform there Only motif sequence information is available without signal-level data — motifs are necessary but not sufficient indicators of non-B structures http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Detects non-B DNA structures (G-quadruplexes, short tandem repeats, A-phased repeats, Z-DNA, mirror/direct repeats) from Oxford Nanopore translocation times by formalizing detection as a novelty detection problem, using GoFAE-DND (a goodness-of-fit-regularized autoencoder) against Isolation Forest, LOF, and one-class SVM baselines. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Detects non-B DNA structures (G-quadruplexes, short tandem repeats, A-phased repeats, Z-DNA, mirror/direct repeats) from Oxford Nanopore translocation times by formalizing detection as a novelty detection problem, using GoFAE-DND (a goodness-of-fit-regularized autoencoder) against Isolation Forest, LOF, and one-class SVM baselines.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not nanopore current signal (e.g. Illumina reads or SMRT data, where sequencing speed is determined by polymerization rather than pore translocation) The goal is supervised classification with abundant labeled non-B examples at balanced ratios; the paper shows novelty detectors are most valuable at extreme non-B:B ratios (e.g. 0.05) and classifiers underperform there Only motif sequence information is available without signal-level data — motifs are necessary but not sufficient indicators of non-B structures

skills.description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into non-redundant, fixed-width 1000 bp input intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN training set.
skills.name: narrowpeak-coordinate-preprocessing
skills.search_text: narrowpeak-coordinate-preprocessing Use when raw narrow-peak BED files (chrom, start, end) from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into non-redundant, fixed-width 1000 bp input intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN training set. Input is already a compendium of fixed-width, non-overlapping intervals (e.g. a prepared Basset training compendium) rather than raw narrow-peak calls Quantitative signal tracks (fold-enrichment, pileup) are the modeling target — this workflow binarizes peaks and discards quantitative epigenomic signal information Peak sets from different profiles that must not be collapsed within a profile — merging is applied within the same profile only http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED files into fixed 1000 bp genomic training intervals for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by extending each peak symmetrically around its midpoint and greedily merging overlaps until no two intervals overlap by more than 200 bp. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED files into fixed 1000 bp genomic training intervals for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by extending each peak symmetrically around its midpoint and greedily merging overlaps until no two intervals overlap by more than 200 bp.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a compendium of fixed-width, non-overlapping intervals (e.g. a prepared Basset training compendium) rather than raw narrow-peak calls Quantitative signal tracks (fold-enrichment, pileup) are the modeling target — this workflow binarizes peaks and discards quantitative epigenomic signal information Peak sets from different profiles that must not be collapsed within a profile — merging is applied within the same profile only

skills.description: Use when the input consists of narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files and you need peak summit coordinates to build a genome-wide TF-occupancy track or define HOT regions.
skills.name: narrowpeak-format-parsing
skills.search_text: narrowpeak-format-parsing Use when the input consists of narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files and you need peak summit coordinates to build a genome-wide TF-occupancy track or define HOT regions. Input peaks are in a different format (e.g. broadPeak or bedGraph signal tracks) that lacks the narrowPeak 'peak' summit-offset column — the summit extraction formula chromStart + peak offset would be invalid. The analysis goal is something other than TF-occupancy/HOT-region definition, e.g. calling individual TF binding peaks de novo from FASTQ/BAM data — this skill assumes peaks have already been called. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Parses ENCODE/modENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files (hg19, mm9, dm3, ce10) and extracts per-TF peak summit coordinates (chromStart + peak offset column) so that TF-occupancy counts per genomic window can be tallied and HOT regions called. This is the data-ingestion step of the Wreczycka et al. 2019 HOT-region pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Parses ENCODE/modENCODE narrowPeak ChIP-seq peak files (hg19, mm9, dm3, ce10) and extracts per-TF peak summit coordinates (chromStart + peak offset column) so that TF-occupancy counts per genomic window can be tallied and HOT regions called. This is the data-ingestion step of the Wreczycka et al. 2019 HOT-region pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input peaks are in a different format (e.g. broadPeak or bedGraph signal tracks) that lacks the narrowPeak 'peak' summit-offset column — the summit extraction formula chromStart + peak offset would be invalid. skills.search_text: nearest-gene-peak-annotation Use when you have called Brd4/TF binding peaks (e.g., ~902 peaks from the mouse cortex scCC dataset) and need to assign nearest genes so peaks can later be paired with gene expression via cc.tl.pair_peak_gene_sc. Input is raw qbed/ccf insertion data that has not yet been through peak calling with cc.pp.call_peaks You need binding-expression statistics but have no annotated peaks — annotation alone does not produce peak-gene correlations Analysis targets ChIP-seq or other peak types outside the Pycallingcards qbed/CC data model http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Annotates called Calling Cards (qbed-derived) peaks with their nearest genes using Pycallingcards' preprocessing.annotation step, which is backed by bedtools/pybedtools. skills.description: Use when Copy-scAT per-cell CNV assignments are noisy (e.g., sparse scATAC coverage) and you want to smooth them into one consensus chromosome value per cell cluster using Louvain (or k-means) clustering of the accessibility matrix.
skills.name: nearest-neighbor-cell-clustering
skills.search_text: nearest-neighbor-cell-clustering Use when Copy-scAT per-cell CNV assignments are noisy (e.g., sparse scATAC coverage) and you want to smooth them into one consensus chromosome value per cell cluster using Louvain (or k-means) clustering of the accessibility matrix. The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs, so cluster-consensus CNV smoothing has nothing to stabilize (a stated Copy-scAT limitation). You lack the required upstream artifacts (CNV list and identifyCNVClusters output), so smoothClusters cannot be called. A cluster-level consensus genotype table already exists and per-cell re-smoothing is unnecessary. Generates nearest-neighbor (Louvain) cell clusters from scATAC accessibility data and uses them within Copy-scAT's smoothClusters module to convert noisy per-cell CNV calls into consensus CNV genotypes per cluster of cells, improving accuracy for cells with sparse coverage. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Generates nearest-neighbor (Louvain) cell clusters from scATAC accessibility data and uses them within Copy-scAT's smoothClusters module to convert noisy per-cell CNV calls into consensus CNV genotypes per cluster of cells, improving accuracy for cells with sparse coverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs, so cluster-consensus CNV smoothing has nothing to stabilize (a stated Copy-scAT limitation). You lack the required upstream artifacts (CNV list and identifyCNVClusters output), so smoothClusters cannot be called. A cluster-level consensus genotype table already exists and per-cell re-smoothing is unnecessary.

skills.description: Use when computing genome-wide chromatin occupancy profiles from paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment data together with nucleotide sequence, and per-factor accessibility counts must be modeled as emission distributions inside an HMM.
skills.name: negative-binomial-count-emission-modeling
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-count-emission-modeling Use when computing genome-wide chromatin occupancy profiles from paired-end MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment data together with nucleotide sequence, and per-factor accessibility counts must be modeled as emission distributions inside an HMM. The analysis goal is peak/footprint identification followed by TF labeling — the paper compares against MACS2 + FIMO, which is a different (lower-performing) paradigm Only single-end or unpaired accessibility data are available without fragment midpoint information No nucleotide sequence or PWM/dinucleotide motif models are available for the factors of interest, since RoboCOP integrates sequence and accessibility jointly http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Model chromatin accessibility fragment counts (MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment midpoints) as negative-binomial distributions within RoboCOP's multivariate HMM, so that accessibility and sequence evidence (PWM/dinucleotide emissions) jointly drive genome-wide DBF occupancy calls. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab553
skills.summary: Model chromatin accessibility fragment counts (MNase-seq or ATAC-seq fragment midpoints) as negative-binomial distributions within RoboCOP's multivariate HMM, so that accessibility and sequence evidence (PWM/dinucleotide emissions) jointly drive genome-wide DBF occupancy calls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is peak/footprint identification followed by TF labeling — the paper compares against MACS2 + FIMO, which is a different (lower-performing) paradigm Only single-end or unpaired accessibility data are available without fragment midpoint information No nucleotide sequence or PWM/dinucleotide motif models are available for the factors of interest, since RoboCOP integrates sequence and accessibility jointly

skills.description: Use when modeling base-resolution ChIP-Seq read counts as smooth functions of genomic position with a penalized NB GAM, especially genome-wide where per-tile sparsity must be exploited for tractable fitting.
skills.name: negative-binomial-count-model-regression
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-count-model-regression Use when modeling base-resolution ChIP-Seq read counts as smooth functions of genomic position with a penalized NB GAM, especially genome-wide where per-tile sparsity must be exploited for tractable fitting. The data are not base-level count data suitable for a negative-binomial link (e.g. continuous intensities or already-normalized feature tables) A dense, small-scale regression is needed where the overhead of sparse Matrix storage, tiling, and HDF5 out-of-core processing is unnecessary Ad-hoc smoothing over binned/windowed data is acceptable and data-driven cross-validated smoothing or tile-joining is not required http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Fits penalized negative-binomial generalized additive model coefficients per genomic tile by Newton-Raphson iteration in GenoGAM 2.0, exploiting sparsity of the design and Hessian matrices: the Hessian inverse is never formed, and the sparse linear systems are solved with the SuperLU direct solver. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Fits penalized negative-binomial generalized additive model coefficients per genomic tile by Newton-Raphson iteration in GenoGAM 2.0, exploiting sparsity of the design and Hessian matrices: the Hessian inverse is never formed, and the sparse linear systems are solved with the SuperLU direct solver.

skills.description: Use when raw Hi-C/pcHi-C interaction tables (frag1, frag2, coverage values, freq, dist) show coverage-driven bias and you need implicit bias correction before distance normalization or significant interaction calling.
skills.name: negative-binomial-coverage-bias-correction
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-coverage-bias-correction Use when raw Hi-C/pcHi-C interaction tables (frag1, frag2, coverage values, freq, dist) show coverage-driven bias and you need implicit bias correction before distance normalization or significant interaction calling. Input is already normalized contact maps or .hic files — covNorm expects raw fragment-level interaction tables with coverage columns You only need matrix balancing (ICE/SCN) of 40 kb contact maps — the article benchmarks those with iced/HiC-spector as alternative baselines, not the coverage model Interactions beyond 2 Mb or inter-chromosomal contacts in pcHi-C mode — the PO-normalization workflow restricts to promoter-centered interactions over 15 kb and within 2 Mb http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 covNorm's implicit normalization step that models experimental and intrinsic 'C'-technology biases as DNA fragment coverage and removes them by fitting expected ligation frequencies with a negative binomial GLM, implemented in the covNormRpkg R package. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: covNorm's implicit normalization step that models experimental and intrinsic 'C'-technology biases as DNA fragment coverage and removes them by fitting expected ligation frequencies with a negative binomial GLM, implemented in the covNormRpkg R package.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already normalized contact maps or .hic files — covNorm expects raw fragment-level interaction tables with coverage columns You only need matrix balancing (ICE/SCN) of 40 kb contact maps — the article benchmarks those with iced/HiC-spector as alternative baselines, not the coverage model Interactions beyond 2 Mb or inter-chromosomal contacts in pcHi-C mode — the PO-normalization workflow restricts to promoter-centered interactions over 15 kb and within 2 Mb

skills.description: Use when Hi-C or pcHi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) contain coverage-driven ligation bias that must be estimated and removed before distance normalization or replicate comparison.
skills.name: negative-binomial-glm-fitting
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-glm-fitting Use when Hi-C or pcHi-C fragment-pair tables (frag1, frag2, cov_frag1, cov_frag2, freq, dist) contain coverage-driven ligation bias that must be estimated and removed before distance normalization or replicate comparison. The data are already coverage-normalized and only distance-dependent background removal (normDistance with max_dist=2000000) is needed Working with pcHi-C PO-interactions without lowering the 'other'-side coverage threshold (cov2_thresh=50) and disabling shuffling — the default Hi-C parameters would mis-filter promoter-side bins http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit a negative binomial generalized linear model, log(uij) = β0 + β1*Ci + β2*Cj, to Hi-C/capture Hi-C fragment-pair data to estimate coverage bias coefficients, which are then used to compute coverage-bias-removed residuals via covNormRpkg::normCoverage. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Fit a negative binomial generalized linear model, log(uij) = β0 + β1*Ci + β2*Cj, to Hi-C/capture Hi-C fragment-pair data to estimate coverage bias coefficients, which are then used to compute coverage-bias-removed residuals via covNormRpkg::normCoverage.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are already coverage-normalized and only distance-dependent background removal (normDistance with max_dist=2000000) is needed Working with pcHi-C PO-interactions without lowering the 'other'-side coverage threshold (cov2_thresh=50) and disabling shuffling — the default Hi-C parameters would mis-filter promoter-side bins

skills.name: negative-binomial-pseudobulk-count-simulation
skills.search_text: negative-binomial-pseudobulk-count-simulation Use when analytic power estimates (e.g. from scPower) must be validated against simulated count data, when cross-checking scPower against powsimR/muscat, or when a gene's pseudobulk mean is too small (< 5) for the analytic linear-model eQTL approximation. skills.search_text: nested-feature-set-performance-comparison Use when evaluating whether adding sequence-derived epigenomic features (reference and/or alternative alleles) to generic functional annotations improves a tissue-specific variant classifier, using AUROC/AUPRC medians across tissues. Input is already a scored variant set or precomputed tissue-specific functional scores (R/TIVAN-indel.R retrieval path), not a training feature matrix requiring ablation The task is cross-tissue or external validation (e.g., DICE immune cell types), rather than with-tissue 5-fold CV across the 44 GTEx tissues Variants are not small indels in non-coding regions; the CADD.indel.rda and DanQ indel feature pipeline is specific to nc-sindels http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A nested feature-set ablation for TIVAN-indel that trains the xgboost model on three cumulative feature sets (45 CADD annotations only, CADD + 919 reference-sequence multi-omics features, CADD + reference + alternative-sequence features) across 44 GTEx tissues to quantify the contribution of sequence-derived epigenomic profiles to nc-sindel prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad060
skills.summary: A nested feature-set ablation for TIVAN-indel that trains the xgboost model on three cumulative feature sets (45 CADD annotations only, CADD + 919 reference-sequence multi-omics features, CADD + reference + alternative-sequence features) across 44 GTEx tissues to quantify the contribution of sequence-derived epigenomic profiles to nc-sindel prediction.

skills.search_text: nested-tld-boundary-specificity-detection Use when single-cell TLD predictions from multiple cell types (e.g., Lee PFC scHi-C cells) are available and the goal is to identify which nested TLD boundaries distinguish specific cell types. Input is bulk Hi-C data with a single contact matrix per condition — boundary-frequency statistics across single cells cannot be computed Cells lack sufficient TLDs (e.g., '2n DNA' stage), where deDoc2 fails to identify a sufficient number of TLDs and data must be excluded The goal is TLD prediction itself rather than comparing boundary occurrence across cell types http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Detects cell-type-specific nested TAD-like domain (TLD) boundaries by computing per-cell-type occurrence frequencies of TLD boundaries predicted by deDoc2, flagging high-frequency boundaries (mean + 3 SD) and designating boundaries as cell-type-specific only when absent from neighboring positions in other cell types. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366

skills.search_text: nested-tld-hierarchy-assessment Use when single-cell or sparse Hi-C contact matrices must be decomposed into hierarchical TLDs and the hierarchy compared across conditions (e.g., cell-cycle stages G1, early/mid/late S, G2) via modularity and similarity metrics. The data are bulk Hi-C with deep coverage — deDoc (structural-information-minimisation) or hierarchical bulk TAD callers are the appropriate predecessors, not the single-cell TLD workflow The analysis goal is cell-type clustering or 2D embedding from TLDs (e.g., TF-IDF + TruncatedSVD + t-SNE on Lee's PFC dataset) rather than quantifying hierarchy strength via modularity/WS Cells yield an insufficient number of TLDs (as with the '2n DNA' stage, which the authors excluded from subsequent analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_3957 Quantifies the nested (hierarchical) TAD-like domain (TLD) structure in single-cell Hi-C by running deDoc2 (deDoc2.w for higher-level, deDoc2.s for lower-level TLDs) on raw single-cell contact matrices and scoring each cell with TLD modularity Q and weighted TLD similarity WS(T,K). epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366

skills.description: Use when single-cell Hi-C contact matrices have been partitioned into nested TLDs (e.g., by deDoc2.w/deDoc2.s) and you need a per-cell scalar (modularity Q) to track how TLD hierarchy changes across cell-cycle stages (G1, early/mid/late S, G2) or other groupings.
skills.name: network-modularity-calculation
skills.search_text: network-modularity-calculation Use when single-cell Hi-C contact matrices have been partitioned into nested TLDs (e.g., by deDoc2.w/deDoc2.s) and you need a per-cell scalar (modularity Q) to track how TLD hierarchy changes across cell-cycle stages (G1, early/mid/late S, G2) or other groupings. Insufficient TLDs can be identified for the sample (as with the '2n DNA' stage, which the article excluded from subsequent analysis) — modularity over too few/empty partitions is not meaningful. The goal is TLD boundary detection itself — use deDoc2 prediction rather than the downstream modularity scoring step. Data require imputation or normalization before TLD calling — deDoc2 'needs no normalization process, raw Hi-C data is suitable', and this scoring workflow runs on raw contact matrices with no imputation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies the organization strength of deDoc2-predicted nested TAD-like domains (TLDs) in single-cell Hi-C by computing modularity Q = (1/2m)Σ(M_ij − k_i k_j/2m)δ(σ_i,σ_j) on each nested TLD sub-matrix, then averaging over all nested TLDs per cell. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Quantifies the organization strength of deDoc2-predicted nested TAD-like domains (TLDs) in single-cell Hi-C by computing modularity Q = (1/2m)Σ(M_ij − k_i k_j/2m)δ(σ_i,σ_j) on each nested TLD sub-matrix, then averaging over all nested TLDs per cell.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Insufficient TLDs can be identified for the sample (as with the '2n DNA' stage, which the article excluded from subsequent analysis) — modularity over too few/empty partitions is not meaningful. The goal is TLD boundary detection itself — use deDoc2 prediction rather than the downstream modularity scoring step. Data require imputation or normalization before TLD calling — deDoc2 'needs no normalization process, raw Hi-C data is suitable', and this scoring workflow runs on raw contact matrices with no imputation.
