skills.search_text: pca-embedding-of-deviation-scores Use when you need a low-dimensional cell embedding from scATAC-seq accessibility counts for clustering and want to compare it against alternatives such as SnapATAC. The goal is the best-possible clustering or embedding of scATAC-seq cells — SnapATAC outperformed all chromVAR variants, including k-mer + PCA, on the evaluated clustering tasks. Input is already a dimensionality-reduced feature matrix or deviation-scores table rather than raw per-cell peak counts requiring filterSamples/filterPeaks preprocessing. skills.summary: Embed single cells from sparse chromatin accessibility data by running PCA on the k-mer deviation-scores matrix produced by chromVAR's matchKmers(6)/computeDeviations pipeline; this k-mer + PCA variant is reported as the best chromVAR variant for clustering.

Input is already a dimensionality-reduced feature matrix or deviation-scores table rather than raw per-cell peak counts requiring filterSamples/filterPeaks preprocessing. You need TF motif usage annotation per cell or cluster rather than a clustering embedding — chromVAR motif deviations (matchMotifs) may be complementary for that purpose.

skills.description: Use when normalizing pcHi-C replicates into promoter-centered long-range P-O cis-interaction calls, or when benchmarking covNorm's significant interaction calls against a CHiCAGO baseline via ROC AUC and hypergeometric overlap.
skills.name: pchi-c-promoter-other-interaction-normalization
skills.search_text: pchi-c-promoter-other-interaction-normalization Use when normalizing pcHi-C replicates into promoter-centered long-range P-O cis-interaction calls, or when benchmarking covNorm's significant interaction calls against a CHiCAGO baseline via ROC AUC and hypergeometric overlap. Input is regular in situ Hi-C (not promoter-capture) — use the standard covNorm cis-interaction workflow without the P-O promoter/other threshold split (cov1_thresh=200, cov2_thresh=50) Interactions of interest are inter-chromosomal — the workflow explicitly filters inter-chromosomal interactions and focuses on cis-interactions only The goal is contact-map reproducibility scoring (HiC-spector) or compartment A/B correlation rather than significant P-O interaction calling http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Applies covNorm's PO-interaction normalization to promoter-capture Hi-C (pcHi-C) data — negative binomial coverage normalization with asymmetric promoter/other coverage thresholds, distance-dependent background removal, and Weibull-based significant interaction calling — to detect reproducible promoter-other (P-O) cis-interactions comparable to CHiCAGO. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Applies covNorm's PO-interaction normalization to promoter-capture Hi-C (pcHi-C) data — negative binomial coverage normalization with asymmetric promoter/other coverage thresholds, distance-dependent background removal, and Weibull-based significant interaction calling — to detect reproducible promoter-other (P-O) cis-interactions comparable to CHiCAGO.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is regular in situ Hi-C (not promoter-capture) — use the standard covNorm cis-interaction workflow without the P-O promoter/other threshold split (cov1_thresh=200, cov2_thresh=50) Interactions of interest are inter-chromosomal — the workflow explicitly filters inter-chromosomal interactions and focuses on cis-interactions only The goal is contact-map reproducibility scoring (HiC-spector) or compartment A/B correlation rather than significant P-O interaction calling

skills.name: pcr-duplicate-removal
skills.search_text: pcr-duplicate-removal Use when processing methylation-seq alignments (e.g., Msuite SAM output) where PCR over-amplification may inflate read counts; reads sharing identical start/end coordinates and strand must be collapsed before methylation calling. Data is single-molecule or UMIdeduplicated already, so identical start/end/strand reads are not PCR artifacts Running BS-seq (bisulfite) data — Msuite requires the 3-letter mode with '-m BS' rather than the 4-letter TAPS/CATCH workflow this dedup step was validated in Reads differ in start or end position or strand — they are not PCR duplicates under Msuite's rule and must not be collapsed http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Post-alignment duplicate removal step from the Msuite pipeline: aligned reads with identical start position, end position, and strand are flagged as PCR duplicates and only the copy with the best sequencing read quality is retained, ensuring downstream methylation calls are not biased by PCR-amplified fragments. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100127
skills.summary: Post-alignment duplicate removal step from the Msuite pipeline: aligned reads with identical start position, end position, and strand are flagged as PCR duplicates and only the copy with the best sequencing read quality is retained, ensuring downstream methylation calls are not biased by PCR-amplified fragments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data is single-molecule or UMIdeduplicated already, so identical start/end/strand reads are not PCR artifacts Running BS-seq (bisulfite) data — Msuite requires the 3-letter mode with '-m BS' rather than the 4-letter TAPS/CATCH workflow this dedup step was validated in Reads differ in start or end position or strand — they are not PCR duplicates under Msuite's rule and must not be collapsed

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq bins (e.g. 1000-bp from spikChIP/SeqCode binning) must be partitioned into peaks vs background regions to quantify how a normalization strategy (spikChIP, ChIP-Rx, Tag removal) affects enriched vs non-occupied loci.
skills.name: peak-background-region-classification
skills.search_text: peak-background-region-classification Use when ChIP-seq bins (e.g. 1000-bp from spikChIP/SeqCode binning) must be partitioned into peaks vs background regions to quantify how a normalization strategy (spikChIP, ChIP-Rx, Tag removal) affects enriched vs non-occupied loci. When no externally called peak BED files are available for the sample or spike-in genome — the classification is driven by user-provided peaks, so it cannot proceed from bins alone. When the analysis goal is a single global normalization factor without needing to distinguish enriched from non-enriched regions (e.g. a simple total-read-count normalization). When peak sets were not called as broad peaks with a compatible caller — the paper's workflow specifically used MACS2 broad peaks, and narrow/differently formatted peak lists may mislabel bins. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Classify genome-wide 1000-bp bins of both sample and spike-in genomes into peaks versus background regions by overlapping bins with user-provided peak BED files (MACS2 broad peaks) using SeqCode, enabling the paper's key metric: normalization-induced signal differences measured separately over enriched versus non-enriched regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Classify genome-wide 1000-bp bins of both sample and spike-in genomes into peaks versus background regions by overlapping bins with user-provided peak BED files (MACS2 broad peaks) using SeqCode, enabling the paper's key metric: normalization-induced signal differences measured separately over enriched versus non-enriched regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no externally called peak BED files are available for the sample or spike-in genome — the classification is driven by user-provided peaks, so it cannot proceed from bins alone. When the analysis goal is a single global normalization factor without needing to distinguish enriched from non-enriched regions (e.g. a simple total-read-count normalization). When peak sets were not called as broad peaks with a compatible caller — the paper's workflow specifically used MACS2 broad peaks, and narrow/differently formatted peak lists may mislabel bins.

skills.name: peak-caller-scaling-visualization
skills.search_text: peak-caller-scaling-visualization Use when comparing computational cost (wall-clock runtime, peak RSS memory) of calling-cards peak callers across a dilution series of qbed datasets with increasing insertion counts (e.g., >5M insertions). The goal is peak-calling accuracy or binding-site discovery rather than computational performance scaling. The input is single-cell CC data requiring annotation, Anndata construction, differential peak analysis, or motif calling rather than bulk runtime benchmarking. The dataset has far fewer than five million insertions, where the reported speed differences (CCcaller 7-10x faster than MACCs/ccf_tools, 2-3x faster than Blockify) do not manifest. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Benchmarks how runtime and memory of CC peak calling methods (CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, Blockify_original, ccf_tools) scale with total transposon insertions, visualizing scaling curves analogous to the Pycallingcards Fig. 2f-g runtime/memory comparison. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Benchmarks how runtime and memory of CC peak calling methods (CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, Blockify_original, ccf_tools) scale with total transposon insertions, visualizing scaling curves analogous to the Pycallingcards Fig. 2f-g runtime/memory comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is peak-calling accuracy or binding-site discovery rather than computational performance scaling. The input is single-cell CC data requiring annotation, Anndata construction, differential peak analysis, or motif calling rather than bulk runtime benchmarking. The dataset has far fewer than five million insertions, where the reported speed differences (CCcaller 7-10x faster than MACCs/ccf_tools, 2-3x faster than Blockify) do not manifest.

skills.description: Use when building or editing a NEAT project's Targets.txt for ChIPseq data (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIPseq from mouse embryonic stem cells) and you must choose between MACS and SPP as the peak caller.
skills.name: peak-calling-algorithm-selection
skills.search_text: peak-calling-algorithm-selection Use when building or editing a NEAT project's Targets.txt for ChIPseq data (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIPseq from mouse embryonic stem cells) and you must choose between MACS and SPP as the peak caller. The project is RNAseq (differential gene expression) rather than ChIPseq — peak calling modules do not apply The pipeline is not managed by NEAT's Targets.txt file (e.g. a Galaxy or systemPipeR workflow where peak callers are configured differently) Reads have not yet been mapped and filtered (map and filter modules must precede peakcalling) http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Select and configure the peak-calling algorithm (MACS or SPP) for a NEAT ChIPseq pipeline by declaring the 'peakcalling' module in the centralized Targets.txt project file, alongside the alignment (bwa/bowtie) and filtering parameters it depends on. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Select and configure the peak-calling algorithm (MACS or SPP) for a NEAT ChIPseq pipeline by declaring the 'peakcalling' module in the centralized Targets.txt project file, alongside the alignment (bwa/bowtie) and filtering parameters it depends on.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The project is RNAseq (differential gene expression) rather than ChIPseq — peak calling modules do not apply The pipeline is not managed by NEAT's Targets.txt file (e.g. a Galaxy or systemPipeR workflow where peak callers are configured differently) Reads have not yet been mapped and filtered (map and filter modules must precede peakcalling)

skills.description: Use when processing raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ files (treatment and control) and you need per-sample quality metrics to judge whether peak calls are reliable before downstream analysis.
skills.name: peak-calling-quality-assessment
skills.search_text: peak-calling-quality-assessment Use when processing raw ChIP-seq or DNase-seq FASTQ files (treatment and control) and you need per-sample quality metrics to judge whether peak calls are reliable before downstream analysis. Input is not raw FASTQ/BAM ChIP-seq or DNase-seq data (e.g., already-called peak sets without reads) — the pipeline's mapping and fragment-size steps cannot run Peak number is less than 200, where ChiLin automatically skips the MDSeqPos motif step and motif-related QC interpretation is not available You need only motif or conservation analysis without QC — the skipped/optional steps (PhastCons, regulatory potential, MDSeqPos) are not the core of this skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Assess the quality of ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peak calling using ChiLin's 13-step QC workflow, covering FastQC read quality, bwa mapping, MACS2 fragment-size estimation, PBC, replicate peak overlap/correlation, merged peak calling, FRiP scores, and meta-region annotation across 17 QC metrics in three layers. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Assess the quality of ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peak calling using ChiLin's 13-step QC workflow, covering FastQC read quality, bwa mapping, MACS2 fragment-size estimation, PBC, replicate peak overlap/correlation, merged peak calling, FRiP scores, and meta-region annotation across 17 QC metrics in three layers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not raw FASTQ/BAM ChIP-seq or DNase-seq data (e.g., already-called peak sets without reads) — the pipeline's mapping and fragment-size steps cannot run Peak number is less than 200, where ChiLin automatically skips the MDSeqPos motif step and motif-related QC interpretation is not available You need only motif or conservation analysis without QC — the skipped/optional steps (PhastCons, regulatory potential, MDSeqPos) are not the core of this skill

skills.description: Use when you need a standardized, reproducible averaged profile of sequencing signal (BAM/SAM ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads) aggregated around a set of peak centers to compare conditions, such as WT vs KO ChIP levels.
skills.name: peak-centered-metaplot-generation
skills.search_text: peak-centered-metaplot-generation Use when you need a standardized, reproducible averaged profile of sequencing signal (BAM/SAM ChIP-seq or CUT&RUN reads) aggregated around a set of peak centers to compare conditions, such as WT vs KO ChIP levels. The goal is genome-browser track files: generation of genome-wide profiles in bigwig format is not supported and deferred to future versions of SeqCode The aggregation unit should be genes rather than peaks (use produceTSSplots/produceGENEplots instead of peak-centered plots) The web tool is intended as a teaching resource with no limits locally; very large input sets should be processed with the standalone command line, not the SeqCode website http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Generate high-quality averaged meta-plots centered on a reference peak list (e.g. MACS-called ChIP-seq peaks) with SeqCode's producePEAKplots/producePEAKmaps, quantifying ChIP signal (e.g. MLL2, H3K4me3) in WT vs perturbation conditions and rendering the plots via internal R scripts. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Generate high-quality averaged meta-plots centered on a reference peak list (e.g. MACS-called ChIP-seq peaks) with SeqCode's producePEAKplots/producePEAKmaps, quantifying ChIP signal (e.g. MLL2, H3K4me3) in WT vs perturbation conditions and rendering the plots via internal R scripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is genome-browser track files: generation of genome-wide profiles in bigwig format is not supported and deferred to future versions of SeqCode The aggregation unit should be genes rather than peaks (use produceTSSplots/produceGENEplots instead of peak-centered plots) The web tool is intended as a teaching resource with no limits locally; very large input sets should be processed with the standalone command line, not the SeqCode website

skills.description: Use when input consists of peak BED files (e.g. *_peaks.stringent.bed from CUT&Tag/CUT&Run/ChIP-seq) that must be loaded as GRanges for QC/comparison, or when harmonized/lifted intervals must be written back out to a BED file.
skills.name: peak-file-bed-import-export
skills.search_text: peak-file-bed-import-export Use when input consists of peak BED files (e.g. *_peaks.stringent.bed from CUT&Tag/CUT&Run/ChIP-seq) that must be loaded as GRanges for QC/comparison, or when harmonized/lifted intervals must be written back out to a BED file. Input is already a GRanges object or in-memory peak table — no BED import/export step is needed The goal is raw read alignment or peak calling; this skill only handles called peak intervals in BED format Files are Picard metrics or other non-interval tabular outputs — use the picard-type import path, not peak BED import http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Import BED-format epigenomic peak files (e.g. CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq peaks) into R as GRanges objects and export harmonized peak files back to BED, using EpiCompare's peak-import utilities backed by rtracklayer/BiocGenerics so the intervals can feed downstream QC checks. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Import BED-format epigenomic peak files (e.g. CUT&Tag, CUT&Run, ChIP-seq peaks) into R as GRanges objects and export harmonized peak files back to BED, using EpiCompare's peak-import utilities backed by rtracklayer/BiocGenerics so the intervals can feed downstream QC checks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a GRanges object or in-memory peak table — no BED import/export step is needed The goal is raw read alignment or peak calling; this skill only handles called peak intervals in BED format Files are Picard metrics or other non-interval tabular outputs — use the picard-type import path, not peak BED import

skills.description: Use when you have qbed insertion data from two biological conditions (e.g. male vs female GBM Brd4 single-cell calling cards) plus matched single-cell RNA expression, and need to test concordance of differential binding with nearby gene expression.
skills.name: peak-gene-expression-concordance-analysis
skills.search_text: peak-gene-expression-concordance-analysis Use when you have qbed insertion data from two biological conditions (e.g. male vs female GBM Brd4 single-cell calling cards) plus matched single-cell RNA expression, and need to test concordance of differential binding with nearby gene expression. Input is already a processed peak-to-gene assignment table or feature matrix — the skill's value is in going from raw qbed insertions to concordant pairs. Data is bulk ChIP-seq or other non-calling-cards binding assay where the qbed/CCcaller/Mudata pipeline does not apply. No matched RNA expression data exist for the same cells, since pair_peak_gene_sc requires both binding and expression layers. http://edamontology.org/topic_3179 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Pairs differentially called Calling Cards peaks (TF binding) with differential expression of nearby genes to test whether sex-biased or condition-biased binding is concordant with gene expression, using Pycallingcards' tools.DE_pvalue and tools.pair_peak_gene_sc on Mudata objects. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Pairs differentially called Calling Cards peaks (TF binding) with differential expression of nearby genes to test whether sex-biased or condition-biased binding is concordant with gene expression, using Pycallingcards' tools.DE_pvalue and tools.pair_peak_gene_sc on Mudata objects.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a processed peak-to-gene assignment table or feature matrix — the skill's value is in going from raw qbed insertions to concordant pairs. Data is bulk ChIP-seq or other non-calling-cards binding assay where the qbed/CCcaller/Mudata pipeline does not apply. No matched RNA expression data exist for the same cells, since pair_peak_gene_sc requires both binding and expression layers.

skills.description: Use when you have single-cell calling cards insertions (qbed) plus matched scRNA-seq for the same cells and need to identify TF binding peaks whose cell-type-specific binding correlates with expression of nearby genes.
skills.name: peak-gene-expression-pairing
skills.search_text: peak-gene-expression-pairing Use when you have single-cell calling cards insertions (qbed) plus matched scRNA-seq for the same cells and need to identify TF binding peaks whose cell-type-specific binding correlates with expression of nearby genes. Input is already a peak-gene association table or a feature matrix without per-cell calling cards insertions The task is bulk calling cards peak-gene pairing rather than the single-cell (scCC) pairing workflow No matched gene-expression data exist for the calling cards cells, so expression correlation cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Pairs cell-type-specific calling cards TF binding peaks with nearby gene expression using Pycallingcards' cc.tl.pair_peak_gene_sc, after building a cell-by-peak AnnData and combining it with scRNA-seq data into a MuData object. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Pairs cell-type-specific calling cards TF binding peaks with nearby gene expression using Pycallingcards' cc.tl.pair_peak_gene_sc, after building a cell-by-peak AnnData and combining it with scRNA-seq data into a MuData object.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-gene association table or a feature matrix without per-cell calling cards insertions The task is bulk calling cards peak-gene pairing rather than the single-cell (scCC) pairing workflow No matched gene-expression data exist for the calling cards cells, so expression correlation cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when comparing peak sets from multiple ChIP-seq peak-calling algorithms on histone mark datasets (H3K4me3, H3K27me3) and you need overlap percentages and average peak-length summaries.
skills.name: peak-length-summary-statistics
skills.search_text: peak-length-summary-statistics Use when comparing peak sets from multiple ChIP-seq peak-calling algorithms on histone mark datasets (H3K4me3, H3K27me3) and you need overlap percentages and average peak-length summaries. The analysis targets transcription-factor ChIP-seq requiring motif-enrichment validation rather than histone-mark peak-set comparison Only one peak caller's output is available, so no pairwise inter-algorithm overlap statistics can be computed Input is raw reads needing alignment/quality filtering rather than already-called peak interval sets to summarize http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Reproduce the HPeak paper's histone-mark benchmark statistics: pairwise inter-algorithm ChIP-seq peak overlap percentages and average peak lengths (e.g., 738 bp for H3K4me3, 183 bp for H3K27me3) to test consistency of peak callers. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Reproduce the HPeak paper's histone-mark benchmark statistics: pairwise inter-algorithm ChIP-seq peak overlap percentages and average peak lengths (e.g., 738 bp for H3K4me3, 183 bp for H3K27me3) to test consistency of peak callers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis targets transcription-factor ChIP-seq requiring motif-enrichment validation rather than histone-mark peak-set comparison Only one peak caller's output is available, so no pairwise inter-algorithm overlap statistics can be computed Input is raw reads needing alignment/quality filtering rather than already-called peak interval sets to summarize

skills.description: Use when you need to evaluate agreement between different ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms on the same dataset, e.g. comparing called peak regions for histone marks like H3K4me3 or H3K27me3 by pairwise overlap percentages.
skills.name: peak-overlap-analysis-across-algorithms
skills.search_text: peak-overlap-analysis-across-algorithms Use when you need to evaluate agreement between different ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms on the same dataset, e.g. comparing called peak regions for histone marks like H3K4me3 or H3K27me3 by pairwise overlap percentages. The question is about a single algorithm's accuracy against known true positives (motif enrichment or TP rate on data like NRSF), not cross-algorithm consistency. Input is already peak-level data with no common raw BED input, so callers cannot be re-run on identical reads for a fair comparison. Data are transcription-factor ChIP-Seq with sharp punctate peaks where orientation/summit information matters; the HPeak workflow here does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A comparative analysis skill that runs multiple ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms (HPeak plus alternatives) on the same input BED files and quantifies pairwise inter-algorithm peak overlap percentages and average peak lengths, to assess whether peak callers yield consistent peak sets. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: A comparative analysis skill that runs multiple ChIP-Seq peak-calling algorithms (HPeak plus alternatives) on the same input BED files and quantifies pairwise inter-algorithm peak overlap percentages and average peak lengths, to assess whether peak callers yield consistent peak sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is about a single algorithm's accuracy against known true positives (motif enrichment or TP rate on data like NRSF), not cross-algorithm consistency. Input is already peak-level data with no common raw BED input, so callers cannot be re-run on identical reads for a fair comparison. Data are transcription-factor ChIP-Seq with sharp punctate peaks where orientation/summit information matters; the HPeak workflow here does not distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak.

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq/CUT&Run/CUT&Tag peak files (e.g. BED narrowPeaks) need QC before cross-sample comparison, specifically quantifying the fraction of peaks falling in ENCODE blacklisted regions.
skills.name: peak-qc-metrics-computation
skills.search_text: peak-qc-metrics-computation Use when ChIP-seq/CUT&Run/CUT&Tag peak files (e.g. BED narrowPeaks) need QC before cross-sample comparison, specifically quantifying the fraction of peaks falling in ENCODE blacklisted regions. Input is already a blacklist-free/feature count matrix (e.g. peak x sample matrix) rather than raw genomic interval peak files The goal is peak overlap statistics or functional annotation (ChromHMM/ChIPseeker/TSS enrichment) rather than blacklist-region QC filtering and metric computation Peaks are not genomic intervals from epigenomic experiments (e.g. ATAC fragment files or Picard duplication summaries, which are separate EpiCompare inputs) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Compute peak-level quality-control metrics for epigenomic peak files by removing blacklisted regions (and non-standard chromosomes) with EpiCompare's tidy_peakfile()/peak_info() workflow and reporting the percentage of peaks overlapping ENCODE blacklist regions in the General Metrics section of the HTML report. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Compute peak-level quality-control metrics for epigenomic peak files by removing blacklisted regions (and non-standard chromosomes) with EpiCompare's tidy_peakfile()/peak_info() workflow and reporting the percentage of peaks overlapping ENCODE blacklist regions in the General Metrics section of the HTML report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a blacklist-free/feature count matrix (e.g. peak x sample matrix) rather than raw genomic interval peak files The goal is peak overlap statistics or functional annotation (ChromHMM/ChIPseeker/TSS enrichment) rather than blacklist-region QC filtering and metric computation Peaks are not genomic intervals from epigenomic experiments (e.g. ATAC fragment files or Picard duplication summaries, which are separate EpiCompare inputs)

skills.description: Use when comparing peak-calling outputs from ChIP-Seq and ChIP-chip (or across peak callers) and you need rank-resolved evidence that higher-ranked peaks are progressively enriched for the expected TF motif family.
skills.name: peak-rank-enrichment-stratification
skills.search_text: peak-rank-enrichment-stratification Use when comparing peak-calling outputs from ChIP-Seq and ChIP-chip (or across peak callers) and you need rank-resolved evidence that higher-ranked peaks are progressively enriched for the expected TF motif family. Input is already a per-peak motif-enrichment table — recomputing family-level chi-square counts would be redundant The transcription factor has no known motif in MatBase or comparable motif databases, making family-level enrichment meaningless Peak sets lack confidence ranks or scores, so rank-bin stratification cannot be performed http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 A comparison strategy that stratifies called peaks (or ChIP-enriched regions) by rank and recomputes transcription factor motif-family enrichment within each rank bin, to quantify how motif enrichment decays with peak confidence and to contrast platforms such as ChIP-Seq (HPeak) versus ChIP-chip. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: A comparison strategy that stratifies called peaks (or ChIP-enriched regions) by rank and recomputes transcription factor motif-family enrichment within each rank bin, to quantify how motif enrichment decays with peak confidence and to contrast platforms such as ChIP-Seq (HPeak) versus ChIP-chip.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-peak motif-enrichment table — recomputing family-level chi-square counts would be redundant The transcription factor has no known motif in MatBase or comparable motif databases, making family-level enrichment meaningless Peak sets lack confidence ranks or scores, so rank-bin stratification cannot be performed

skills.description: Use when MACS2-called merged peak regions from ChIP-seq marks (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 + H3K9ac BAMs) must be filtered by region length in bins and minimum counts/pileup prior to DGW DTW clustering.
skills.name: peak-region-filtering-by-length-and-count
skills.search_text: peak-region-filtering-by-length-and-count Use when MACS2-called merged peak regions from ChIP-seq marks (e.g. ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 + H3K9ac BAMs) must be filtered by region length in bins and minimum counts/pileup prior to DGW DTW clustering. Input is already a filtered peak set with length and count constraints applied (re-filtering could bias the region set) Regions are anchored to genomic features such as transcription start sites or gene annotation rather than peak-finder output — DGW's unsupervised setting expects peak regions from a peak finder such as MACS Peak lengths are naturally shorter than 5 bins or the marks have very low pileup everywhere, since the filters would remove nearly all regions http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Filter MACS2-called merged ChIP-seq peak regions by length (larger than 5 and smaller than 1000 bins) and by count (at least 10 counts), plus a --min-pileup constraint requiring at least one bin with more than 10 reads, before DTW-based alignment and clustering with DGW. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Filter MACS2-called merged ChIP-seq peak regions by length (larger than 5 and smaller than 1000 bins) and by count (at least 10 counts), plus a --min-pileup constraint requiring at least one bin with more than 10 reads, before DTW-based alignment and clustering with DGW.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a filtered peak set with length and count constraints applied (re-filtering could bias the region set) Regions are anchored to genomic features such as transcription start sites or gene annotation rather than peak-finder output — DGW's unsupervised setting expects peak regions from a peak finder such as MACS Peak lengths are naturally shorter than 5 bins or the marks have very low pileup everywhere, since the filters would remove nearly all regions

skills.description: Use when you have multiple peak files (e.g. CUT&Tag/CUT&Run H3K27ac BED files as GRanges) that should be collapsed into a single consensus peak set, and you must choose between fast overlap-based and distribution-model-based consensus calling.
skills.name: peak-score-distribution-modelling
skills.search_text: peak-score-distribution-modelling Use when you have multiple peak files (e.g. CUT&Tag/CUT&Run H3K27ac BED files as GRanges) that should be collapsed into a single consensus peak set, and you must choose between fast overlap-based and distribution-model-based consensus calling. The peak files are already a single merged consensus set and only QC/comparison against a reference (e.g. ENCODE_H3K27ac) is needed rather than consensus calling Only a fast descriptive overlap summary is needed and the runtime cost of distribution modelling (consensusseeker) cannot be tolerated Input is raw alignment data (e.g. BAM fragments) rather than called peak files; EpiCompare operates on peak files such as BED imports http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Calling consensus peaks from a group of epigenomic peak files using EpiCompare's compute_consensus_peaks, which offers a fast interval-overlap strategy (method='granges') and a slower, more accurate strategy that models peak score distributions (method='consensusseeker'). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioadv/vbad049
skills.summary: Calling consensus peaks from a group of epigenomic peak files using EpiCompare's compute_consensus_peaks, which offers a fast interval-overlap strategy (method='granges') and a slower, more accurate strategy that models peak score distributions (method='consensusseeker').
skills.when_to_use_negative: The peak files are already a single merged consensus set and only QC/comparison against a reference (e.g. ENCODE_H3K27ac) is needed rather than consensus calling Only a fast descriptive overlap summary is needed and the runtime cost of distribution modelling (consensusseeker) cannot be tolerated Input is raw alignment data (e.g. BAM fragments) rather than called peak files; EpiCompare operates on peak files such as BED imports

skills.description: Use when a RangedSummarizedExperiment of ATAC-seq/DNase-seq fragment counts has already been sample-filtered and the peak set still contains peaks with no fragments across samples or overlapping peak intervals that would bias motif accessibility estimates.
skills.name: peak-set-non-overlapping-filtering
skills.search_text: peak-set-non-overlapping-filtering Use when a RangedSummarizedExperiment of ATAC-seq/DNase-seq fragment counts has already been sample-filtered and the peak set still contains peaks with no fragments across samples or overlapping peak intervals that would bias motif accessibility estimates. Input is raw, unfiltered counts with low-quality samples not yet removed via filterSamples — peak filtering assumes the sample set is already curated The peak set is already non-overlapping and every peak has sufficient fragment support (filterPeaks would be a no-op) Downstream analysis uses an external fixed peak set (e.g. a reference cCRE catalog) that must not be collapsed or subset http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Reduces a chromVAR fragment-count peak set to high-quality, non-overlapping peaks after sample filtering, so that downstream motif deviation computations are not biased by redundant or poorly-supported peaks. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/nmeth.4401
skills.summary: Reduces a chromVAR fragment-count peak set to high-quality, non-overlapping peaks after sample filtering, so that downstream motif deviation computations are not biased by redundant or poorly-supported peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unfiltered counts with low-quality samples not yet removed via filterSamples — peak filtering assumes the sample set is already curated The peak set is already non-overlapping and every peak has sufficient fragment support (filterPeaks would be a no-op) Downstream analysis uses an external fixed peak set (e.g. a reference cCRE catalog) that must not be collapsed or subset

skills.description: Use when calling broad histone-mark peaks (H3K27me3) and needing a data-driven, cell-type-specific peak-size cutoff to decide which merged peaks count as Polycomb domains over genes.
skills.name: peak-size-inflection-cutoff-estimation
skills.search_text: peak-size-inflection-cutoff-estimation Use when calling broad histone-mark peaks (H3K27me3) and needing a data-driven, cell-type-specific peak-size cutoff to decide which merged peaks count as Polycomb domains over genes. Input is narrow-mark ChIP-seq (e.g. TF or H3K4me1/H3K27ac peaks) where a domain-size inflection cutoff is not meaningful. The cell type of interest lacks public H3K27me3 ChIP-seq with a matched input control, so a dataset-specific cutoff cannot be derived. Only fixed promoter-window statistics are needed; this skill binarizes gene bodies from large Polycomb domains, not promoter coverage per se. http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Derives a per-dataset size cutoff for broad H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks using the findiplist() inflection-point analysis from the R inflection package, so that only peaks as large as Polycomb domains (e.g. ~6689 bp in ESC, ~6719 bp in NCC, ~8020 bp in cardiomyocytes) define the binary polycombScore metric in POSTRE. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Derives a per-dataset size cutoff for broad H3K27me3 ChIP-seq peaks using the findiplist() inflection-point analysis from the R inflection package, so that only peaks as large as Polycomb domains (e.g. ~6689 bp in ESC, ~6719 bp in NCC, ~8020 bp in cardiomyocytes) define the binary polycombScore metric in POSTRE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is narrow-mark ChIP-seq (e.g. TF or H3K4me1/H3K27ac peaks) where a domain-size inflection cutoff is not meaningful. The cell type of interest lacks public H3K27me3 ChIP-seq with a matched input control, so a dataset-specific cutoff cannot be derived. Only fixed promoter-window statistics are needed; this skill binarizes gene bodies from large Polycomb domains, not promoter coverage per se.

skills.description: Use when calling chromatin contact domains (CCDs) from CTCF ChIA-PET loops and you need to restrict the loop set to high-confidence, peak-supported interactions before merging into domain intervals.
skills.name: peak-supported-anchor-filtering
skills.search_text: peak-supported-anchor-filtering Use when calling chromatin contact domains (CCDs) from CTCF ChIA-PET loops and you need to restrict the loop set to high-confidence, peak-supported interactions before merging into domain intervals. Calling peaks or loops themselves — this filter operates downstream on already-called ChIA-PIPE loops and peaks Annotating individual enhancer-promoter loops, which uses a different criterion (PET count ≥3 and peak support) and a custom Python classification script Data types where anchor peak support is not expected (e.g., non-ChIA-PET contact data without corresponding binding peaks) http://edamontology.org/topic_0607 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 A filter step within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling workflow that retains only chromatin loops whose both anchors are supported by called binding peaks, as the basis for defining CCDs from CTCF ChIA-PET data. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: A filter step within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling workflow that retains only chromatin loops whose both anchors are supported by called binding peaks, as the basis for defining CCDs from CTCF ChIA-PET data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling peaks or loops themselves — this filter operates downstream on already-called ChIA-PIPE loops and peaks Annotating individual enhancer-promoter loops, which uses a different criterion (PET count ≥3 and peak support) and a custom Python classification script Data types where anchor peak support is not expected (e.g., non-ChIA-PET contact data without corresponding binding peaks)

skills.description: Use when ENCODE ChIP-seq peak BED files for TRs must be converted into gene-level regulatory potential scores via peak-to-TSS distances plus peak signal strength weighting.
skills.name: peak-to-gene-distance-assignment
skills.search_text: peak-to-gene-distance-assignment Use when ENCODE ChIP-seq peak BED files for TRs must be converted into gene-level regulatory potential scores via peak-to-TSS distances plus peak signal strength weighting. ChIP-seq data for a TR are missing or contain too few targets — the paper warns lack of ChIP-seq data or ChIP-seq data with too few targets would mislead TR identification. skills.description: Use when two differential analysis results (e.g., young-vs-old log2 fold-change per ATAC-seq peak in men vs women) must be compared on a common feature set to measure how much of the response is shared versus sex- or condition-specific.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-of-fold-change-signatures
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-fold-change-signatures Use when two differential analysis results (e.g., young-vs-old log2 fold-change per ATAC-seq peak in men vs women) must be compared on a common feature set to measure how much of the response is shared versus sex- or condition-specific. The two signatures are not computed over a common, matched feature set (no shared peak/gene identifiers to inner-join on), since correlating unmatched feature vectors is invalid. The goal is single-cell or sorted-cell sex-specific aging analysis, which the paper explicitly flags as future work ('Future studies are needed to describe these sex differences at single-cell resolution and in sorted cells'). You need cell-type-resolved rather than bulk PBMC signatures — the paper notes the bulk annotation approach 'is prone to biases in references'. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies how similar two condition-wise differential accessibility/expression signatures are by Pearson-correlating their log2 fold-change vectors over a shared peak or gene set, as done to compare aging chromatin signatures (young-vs-old ATAC-seq) between male and female PBMC donors (r = 0.445, p < 0.001). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Quantifies how similar two condition-wise differential accessibility/expression signatures are by Pearson-correlating their log2 fold-change vectors over a shared peak or gene set, as done to compare aging chromatin signatures (young-vs-old ATAC-seq) between male and female PBMC donors (r = 0.445, p < 0.001).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The two signatures are not computed over a common, matched feature set (no shared peak/gene identifiers to inner-join on), since correlating unmatched feature vectors is invalid. You need cell-type-resolved rather than bulk PBMC signatures — the paper notes the bulk annotation approach 'is prone to biases in references'.

skills.description: Use when you have CscoreTool-M cscore.txt or cscore.bedgraph sub-compartment probabilities and an independent track (NAD-seq, Lamin-B1 DamID) that can be aggregated over the same 100 kb windows, and you want to quantify agreement.
skills.name: pearson-correlation-of-genomic-tracks
skills.search_text: pearson-correlation-of-genomic-tracks Use when you have CscoreTool-M cscore.txt or cscore.bedgraph sub-compartment probabilities and an independent track (NAD-seq, Lamin-B1 DamID) that can be aggregated over the same 100 kb windows, and you want to quantify agreement. The tracks are not aggregated over the same equal-length Rabl windows used by CscoreTool-M, so per-window correlation would be misaligned. The input is a binary sub-compartment annotation rather than continuous probability scores — the CscoreTool-M scores are probabilities (bedgraph c-scores sum to 1 per region), which is what makes Pearson correlation interpretable. Regions with no Hi-C reads: the bedgraph omits regions with no reads, so treating missing windows as zeros instead of dropping them will distort the correlation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes Pearson correlations between CscoreTool-M per-window sub-compartment probability scores and independent genomic tracks (NAD-seq, Lamin-B1 DamID) aggregated over the same 100 kb Rabl windows, to validate that a sub-compartment (e.g., C6_6) corresponds to a nuclear-body domain such as NADs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Computes Pearson correlations between CscoreTool-M per-window sub-compartment probability scores and independent genomic tracks (NAD-seq, Lamin-B1 DamID) aggregated over the same 100 kb Rabl windows, to validate that a sub-compartment (e.g., C6_6) corresponds to a nuclear-body domain such as NADs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The tracks are not aggregated over the same equal-length Rabl windows used by CscoreTool-M, so per-window correlation would be misaligned. The input is a binary sub-compartment annotation rather than continuous probability scores — the CscoreTool-M scores are probabilities (bedgraph c-scores sum to 1 per region), which is what makes Pearson correlation interpretable. Regions with no Hi-C reads: the bedgraph omits regions with no reads, so treating missing windows as zeros instead of dropping them will distort the correlation.

skills.search_text: per-base-pair-sensitivity-specificity-analysis Use when benchmarking a peak caller for broad histone marks (e.g. H3K27me3) against a qPCR-validated truth set and needing threshold-free ROC comparison of sensitivity and specificity per base pair. Peak-like (narrow) histone marks or transcription factors, since methods searching for peak-like features were shown to generate false positive or false negative calls on broad diffuse modifications like H3K27me3 Differential (two-sample) comparison analysis rather than single-sample detection of modified versus unmodified regions No qPCR-validated or otherwise curated ground-truth regions exist, since per-base-pair sensitivity and specificity cannot be computed http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark workflow for evaluating histoneHMM and competing peak callers (MACS2 broad, Zinba, SICER, BroadPeak, Rseg) on a qPCR-validated H3K27me3 ChIP-seq dataset by sweeping score thresholds and building ROC curves from per-base-pair sensitivity and specificity against 197 validated regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Benchmark workflow for evaluating histoneHMM and competing peak callers (MACS2 broad, Zinba, SICER, BroadPeak, Rseg) on a qPCR-validated H3K27me3 ChIP-seq dataset by sweeping score thresholds and building ROC curves from per-base-pair sensitivity and specificity against 197 validated regions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Peak-like (narrow) histone marks or transcription factors, since methods searching for peak-like features were shown to generate false positive or false negative calls on broad diffuse modifications like H3K27me3 Differential (two-sample) comparison analysis rather than single-sample detection of modified versus unmodified regions No qPCR-validated or otherwise curated ground-truth regions exist, since per-base-pair sensitivity and specificity cannot be computed

skills.summary: Generates and plots per-file FASTQ quality reports using systemPipeR's seeFastq/seeFastqPlot functions, summarizing per-cycle quality scores and read-quality distributions so many FASTQ files can be visually inspected in a single multi-panel report.

skills.description: Use when a pipeline needs to persist or reload per-chromosome, binned genomic annotation arrays (e.g. deepC skeleton tags in 1–10 range) from Hi-C contact maps at 5 kb resolution.
skills.name: per-chromosome-genomic-array-io
skills.search_text: per-chromosome-genomic-array-io Use when a pipeline needs to persist or reload per-chromosome, binned genomic annotation arrays (e.g. deepC skeleton tags in 1–10 range) from Hi-C contact maps at 5 kb resolution. Input is raw, unnormalized Hi-C contact matrices that have not yet been distance-stratified and percentile-normalized into skeleton tags The analysis requires base-pair-resolution or continuous-valued interaction scores rather than 5 kb-binned categorical skeleton annotations Predicting or training with deepC models directly from DNA sequence, which takes sequence windows rather than skeleton tag arrays as input http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Handles loading and writing of per-chromosome genomic signal arrays — specifically deepC's percentile-normalized Hi-C 'skeleton' tag arrays — as .npy/.h5 files, converting continuous KR-normalized contact frequencies into discrete 1–10 percentile class annotations stored per chromosome. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Handles loading and writing of per-chromosome genomic signal arrays — specifically deepC's percentile-normalized Hi-C 'skeleton' tag arrays — as .npy/.h5 files, converting continuous KR-normalized contact frequencies into discrete 1–10 percentile class annotations stored per chromosome.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unnormalized Hi-C contact matrices that have not yet been distance-stratified and percentile-normalized into skeleton tags The analysis requires base-pair-resolution or continuous-valued interaction scores rather than 5 kb-binned categorical skeleton annotations Predicting or training with deepC models directly from DNA sequence, which takes sequence windows rather than skeleton tag arrays as input

skills.description: Use when per-cell CNV calls from scATAC-seq data are noisy or sparse and cluster-level consensus genotypes are needed — e.g. after identifyCNVClusters has produced a CNV cluster file and Louvain cell clusters exist.
skills.name: per-cluster-consensus-cnv-imputation
skills.search_text: per-cluster-consensus-cnv-imputation Use when per-cell CNV calls from scATAC-seq data are noisy or sparse and cluster-level consensus genotypes are needed — e.g. after identifyCNVClusters has produced a CNV cluster file and Louvain cell clusters exist. Malignancies driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot infer CNVs in this setting When per-cell CNV calls are already high-confidence and cluster-level imputation would erase genuine intra-cluster heterogeneity When no upstream CNV cluster file from identifyCNVClusters is available, since smoothClusters requires it as input http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Copy-scAT's optional smoothing step that imputes a consensus per-chromosome CNV genotype for each cluster of scATAC-seq cells, improving CNV calls for cells with sparse coverage by leveraging alternative clustering (Louvain by default) rather than raw per-cell bin values. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Copy-scAT's optional smoothing step that imputes a consensus per-chromosome CNV genotype for each cluster of scATAC-seq cells, improving CNV calls for cells with sparse coverage by leveraging alternative clustering (Louvain by default) rather than raw per-cell bin values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Malignancies driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot infer CNVs in this setting When per-cell CNV calls are already high-confidence and cluster-level imputation would erase genuine intra-cluster heterogeneity When no upstream CNV cluster file from identifyCNVClusters is available, since smoothClusters requires it as input

skills.search_text: per-experiment-mean-centering Use when combining gene expression values from multiple GEO series into a single matrix and you need to remove per-experiment offset differences, e.g., building COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt (mean-centered variant). When you need the raw joined values — COnTORT also produces a second output file with no mean centering; use that instead When the input is not normalized/processed GEO expression data imported into NCBI GEO — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Per-experiment mean centering of COnTORT-organized GEO transcriptomic data: each expression column (GSM experiment) is column-mean subtracted to control for inter-experiment differences, producing COnTORT's mean-centered output file alongside the non-mean-centered file. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Per-experiment mean centering of COnTORT-organized GEO transcriptomic data: each expression column (GSM experiment) is column-mean subtracted to control for inter-experiment differences, producing COnTORT's mean-centered output file alongside the non-mean-centered file.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When you need the raw joined values — COnTORT also produces a second output file with no mean centering; use that instead When the input is not normalized/processed GEO expression data imported into NCBI GEO — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data

skills.description: Use when a cell type-specific binary annotation of polycomb-repressed genes is needed from H3K27me3 ChIP-seq, e.g. as an epigenetic-state input feature for SV pathogenicity prediction in POSTRE-style analyses.
skills.name: per-gene-polycomb-repression-binarization
skills.search_text: per-gene-polycomb-repression-binarization Use when a cell type-specific binary annotation of polycomb-repressed genes is needed from H3K27me3 ChIP-seq, e.g. as an epigenetic-state input feature for SV pathogenicity prediction in POSTRE-style analyses. Input is already a per-gene repression or epigenetic-state feature table — re-deriving the score from ChIP-seq would be redundant The histone mark produces narrow punctate peaks rather than broad polycomb domains, so a broad-mode peak-size cutoff is not the right model A continuous quantitative H3K27me3 occupancy measure is required — the binarization to 0/1 discards signal magnitude http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A POSTRE-derived skill that converts H3K27me3 ChIP-seq broad peaks into a binary per-gene polycombScore, quantifying the breadth of polycomb domains in gene promoters per cell type. It derives a dataset-specific peak-size cutoff via findiplist() inflection-point analysis instead of using a fixed threshold. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: A POSTRE-derived skill that converts H3K27me3 ChIP-seq broad peaks into a binary per-gene polycombScore, quantifying the breadth of polycomb domains in gene promoters per cell type. It derives a dataset-specific peak-size cutoff via findiplist() inflection-point analysis instead of using a fixed threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a per-gene repression or epigenetic-state feature table — re-deriving the score from ChIP-seq would be redundant The histone mark produces narrow punctate peaks rather than broad polycomb domains, so a broad-mode peak-size cutoff is not the right model A continuous quantitative H3K27me3 occupancy measure is required — the binarization to 0/1 discards signal magnitude

skills.description: Use when interval-level ClinGen HI/TS dosage-sensitivity annotations (GRCh37/hg19 BED) must be mapped onto individual genes and reduced to binary per-gene dosage-sensitivity calls for LOF/GOF contexts, or when POSTRE per-SV results need a per-gene aggregated view.
skills.name: per-gene-score-table-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-gene-score-table-aggregation Use when interval-level ClinGen HI/TS dosage-sensitivity annotations (GRCh37/hg19 BED) must be mapped onto individual genes and reduced to binary per-gene dosage-sensitivity calls for LOF/GOF contexts, or when POSTRE per-SV results need a per-gene aggregated view. Interpreting SVs implicated in recessive phenotypes — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated Genes or intervals lacking ClinGen HI/TS dosage-sensitivity annotation — the 0.85 threshold and HI-as-TS proxy cannot be applied without scores Analysis requires only per-SV pathogenicity calls — the first POSTRE output table ('Results per SV and phenotype') already provides this without gene-level aggregation Collapses POSTRE's per-SV and per-interval predictions into per-gene score tables: it maps ClinGen haploinsufficiency (HI) interval annotations (ClinGen_haploinsufficiency_gene_GRCh37.bed, GRCh37/hg19) onto genes, derives final_HI_score/final_TS_score, applies a 0.85 dosage-sensitivity threshold, and writes a gene-level TSV (dosage_sensitivity_scores.tsv) used by POSTRE_multiSV()'s 'Results per gene and phenotype' aggregation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Collapses POSTRE's per-SV and per-interval predictions into per-gene score tables: it maps ClinGen haploinsufficiency (HI) interval annotations (ClinGen_haploinsufficiency_gene_GRCh37.bed, GRCh37/hg19) onto genes, derives final_HI_score/final_TS_score, applies a 0.85 dosage-sensitivity threshold, and writes a gene-level TSV (dosage_sensitivity_scores.tsv) used by POSTRE_multiSV()'s 'Results per gene and phenotype' aggregation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Interpreting SVs implicated in recessive phenotypes — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated Genes or intervals lacking ClinGen HI/TS dosage-sensitivity annotation — the 0.85 threshold and HI-as-TS proxy cannot be applied without scores Analysis requires only per-SV pathogenicity calls — the first POSTRE output table ('Results per SV and phenotype') already provides this without gene-level aggregation

skills.description: Use when you have per-cancer-type BIT rank tables and DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos gene effect data and need per-lineage counts of functionally essential TRs.
skills.name: per-lineage-count-summarization
skills.search_text: per-lineage-count-summarization Use when you have per-cancer-type BIT rank tables and DepMap CRISPR/Cas9 Chronos gene effect data and need per-lineage counts of functionally essential TRs. When the goal is to rank or identify TRs from an epigenomic query region set itself — that is BIT's job; this skill only post-processes BIT ranks against dependency data. When the input is per-cell-line rather than per-lineage Chronos data and lineage-level scores cannot be computed for the nine cancer types. When validating TR essentiality by a criterion other than knockout viability (e.g., survival correlation via Kaplan-Meier plotter), since the -0.4 Chronos cutoff applies specifically to CRISPR/Cas9 gene effect scores. Summarizes how many BIT-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) are functionally essential in each cancer lineage by intersecting BIT rank tables with lineage-level DepMap Chronos gene-effect scores under a strict < -0.4 threshold, and writing one row per cancer type to a summary CSV. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Summarizes how many BIT-ranked transcriptional regulators (TRs) are functionally essential in each cancer lineage by intersecting BIT rank tables with lineage-level DepMap Chronos gene-effect scores under a strict < -0.4 threshold, and writing one row per cancer type to a summary CSV.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to rank or identify TRs from an epigenomic query region set itself — that is BIT's job; this skill only post-processes BIT ranks against dependency data. When the input is per-cell-line rather than per-lineage Chronos data and lineage-level scores cannot be computed for the nine cancer types. When validating TR essentiality by a criterion other than knockout viability (e.g., survival correlation via Kaplan-Meier plotter), since the -0.4 Chronos cutoff applies specifically to CRISPR/Cas9 gene effect scores.

skills.search_text: per-read-methylation-calling Use when bisulfite-treated reads have been aligned with the 'three-letter' approach and you need per-read/per-site methylation states recovered by comparing alignments back to the original (un-converted) reference genome. Alignments have not yet passed Phase 3 filtering — ambiguous multi-best hits and over-cutoff mismatches must be removed before methylation estimation Only a converted ('three-letter') reference is available — methylation profiling requires comparison against the original un-converted genome sequence http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Phase 4 of the BiSpark workflow: estimate per-site methylation by merging filtered alignments with original read sequences and comparing them against the un-converted reference genome, broadcast via Spark shared variables, to produce the methylRDD methylation profile. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2498-2
skills.summary: Phase 4 of the BiSpark workflow: estimate per-site methylation by merging filtered alignments with original read sequences and comparing them against the un-converted reference genome, broadcast via Spark shared variables, to produce the methylRDD methylation profile.

skills.description: Use when a cycle-2 Delila-PY run has produced per-sequence information content values (bits) and you must decide which sequences are poor matches to keep or drop before regenerating the book with delila.
skills.name: per-sequence-information-content-interpretation
skills.search_text: per-sequence-information-content-interpretation Use when a cycle-2 Delila-PY run has produced per-sequence information content values (bits) and you must decide which sequences are poor matches to keep or drop before regenerating the book with delila. The input is the raw book from cycle 1 — per-sequence information content has not yet been computed by alist/encode/cmp/rseq, so the ≤0-bit cutoff cannot be applied. The goal is motif/logo rendering (cycle 3: alist, encode, cmp, rseq, dalvec, makelogo) rather than filtering sequences out of the book. You need soft or probabilistic down-weighting of poor matches; the ri rule is strictly binary at the ≤0-bit boundary and offers no graded removal. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 In Delila-PY's second cycle, per-sequence information content (in bits) is computed by the alist/encode/cmp/rseq chain, and the ri program applies a deterministic ≤0-bit cutoff to discard poorly matching sequences before delila regenerates the book. This interprets each sequence's individual information contribution as a quality score for motif refinement. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: In Delila-PY's second cycle, per-sequence information content (in bits) is computed by the alist/encode/cmp/rseq chain, and the ri program applies a deterministic ≤0-bit cutoff to discard poorly matching sequences before delila regenerates the book. This interprets each sequence's individual information contribution as a quality score for motif refinement.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is the raw book from cycle 1 — per-sequence information content has not yet been computed by alist/encode/cmp/rseq, so the ≤0-bit cutoff cannot be applied. The goal is motif/logo rendering (cycle 3: alist, encode, cmp, rseq, dalvec, makelogo) rather than filtering sequences out of the book. You need soft or probabilistic down-weighting of poor matches; the ri rule is strictly binary at the ≤0-bit boundary and offers no graded removal.

skills.description: Use when comparing two or more celltyping methods evaluated on the same set of matched tasks (e.g., 50 Cellcano benchmark tasks) and you need a statistical test of whether one method's accuracy advantage is significant.
skills.name: per-task-benchmark-accuracy-aggregation
skills.search_text: per-task-benchmark-accuracy-aggregation Use when comparing two or more celltyping methods evaluated on the same set of matched tasks (e.g., 50 Cellcano benchmark tasks) and you need a statistical test of whether one method's accuracy advantage is significant. Accuracies are not task-paired (methods evaluated on different task sets) — an unpaired or rank-based comparison is required instead Input is already aggregated summary statistics (e.g., mean accuracy only) without per-task values — paired t-tests cannot be recomputed http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aggregate per-task celltyping accuracy values across matched benchmark tasks and test significance of method differences with two-sided paired t-tests, as done for Cellcano vs ACTINN, scJoint, and Signac over 50 celltyping tasks. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Aggregate per-task celltyping accuracy values across matched benchmark tasks and test significance of method differences with two-sided paired t-tests, as done for Cellcano vs ACTINN, scJoint, and Signac over 50 celltyping tasks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Accuracies are not task-paired (methods evaluated on different task sets) — an unpaired or rank-based comparison is required instead Input is already aggregated summary statistics (e.g., mean accuracy only) without per-task values — paired t-tests cannot be recomputed

Input is a raw variant list without labels or tissue assignment — the skill requires cis-eQTL-labeled positive/negative nc-sindels per GTEx tissue Evaluation goal is cross-tissue prediction (training on one tissue, testing on another) rather than within-tissue 5-fold CV Variant type is SNVs or large structural variants — the framework targets non-coding small indels (sindels) with CADD-indel annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A benchmarking skill for evaluating TIVAN-indel against CADD/FATHMM-indel (SVM) and DanQ/DeepSEA (Boosted LR) baselines using 5-fold cross-validation within each of 44 GTEx tissues, reporting per-tissue and median AUROC/AUPRC for non-coding regulatory small indel (nc-sindel) prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad060
skills.summary: A benchmarking skill for evaluating TIVAN-indel against CADD/FATHMM-indel (SVM) and DanQ/DeepSEA (Boosted LR) baselines using 5-fold cross-validation within each of 44 GTEx tissues, reporting per-tissue and median AUROC/AUPRC for non-coding regulatory small indel (nc-sindel) prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a raw variant list without labels or tissue assignment — the skill requires cis-eQTL-labeled positive/negative nc-sindels per GTEx tissue Evaluation goal is cross-tissue prediction (training on one tissue, testing on another) rather than within-tissue 5-fold CV Variant type is SNVs or large structural variants — the framework targets non-coding small indels (sindels) with CADD-indel annotations

skills.name: percentile-based-outlier-winsorization
skills.search_text: percentile-based-outlier-winsorization Use when a numeric genomic data matrix (e.g. gene expression rows x samples) contains extreme outlier values that could distort row-wise statistics or downstream partitioning, as part of cola's adjust_matrix() cleaning pipeline. The input has already passed through adjust_matrix() or is otherwise outlier-adjusted and low-variance rows have been removed Downstream analysis legitimately requires untruncated extreme values (e.g. detecting genuine outlier samples rather than stabilizing feature statistics) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A matrix-cleaning step from cola's adjust_matrix() preprocessing in which row values above the 95th percentile or below the 5th percentile are replaced by the corresponding percentile values, dampening extreme outliers before consensus partitioning. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: A matrix-cleaning step from cola's adjust_matrix() preprocessing in which row values above the 95th percentile or below the 5th percentile are replaced by the corresponding percentile values, dampening extreme outliers before consensus partitioning.

skills.description: Use when you have deepC-predicted effect sizes for one or more candidate SNPs and need a population-level comparison (percentile) against sampled background SNPs to decide which variant most plausibly perturbs genome folding.
skills.name: percentile-ranking-of-predicted-variant-effects
skills.search_text: percentile-ranking-of-predicted-variant-effects Use when you have deepC-predicted effect sizes for one or more candidate SNPs and need a population-level comparison (percentile) against sampled background SNPs to decide which variant most plausibly perturbs genome folding. You have only one or a handful of variants with no sampled background SNP distribution — a percentile ranking is meaningless without the ~1000-SNP comparison set The variants are large structural variants (deletions of promoters/enhancers/CTCF sites) rather than single base pair SNPs — the deletion-screen workflow, not SNP percentile ranking, applies Predictions are being made on genomes other than the hg19 reference with matched deepC model coordinates without adjusting sequence extraction and model window coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Ranks sequence-based deepC predicted variant effect sizes (mean absolute difference between reference and variant predicted chromatin interaction maps) across a sampled SNP background to convert raw effect magnitudes into percentile scores, enabling prioritization of likely causal variants such as the 17q21 asthma SNPs rs12936231 and rs4065275. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Ranks sequence-based deepC predicted variant effect sizes (mean absolute difference between reference and variant predicted chromatin interaction maps) across a sampled SNP background to convert raw effect magnitudes into percentile scores, enabling prioritization of likely causal variants such as the 17q21 asthma SNPs rs12936231 and rs4065275.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only one or a handful of variants with no sampled background SNP distribution — a percentile ranking is meaningless without the ~1000-SNP comparison set The variants are large structural variants (deletions of promoters/enhancers/CTCF sites) rather than single base pair SNPs — the deletion-screen workflow, not SNP percentile ranking, applies Predictions are being made on genomes other than the hg19 reference with matched deepC model coordinates without adjusting sequence extraction and model window coordinates

skills.description: Use when you have ChIP-seq-scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor motif (e.g. Nanog motif sites scored by mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal) and want to test whether a second TF's motif (e.g. Sox2) occurs at periodic, helical-phase offsets rather than at a single fixed spacing.
skills.name: periodicity-detection-in-enrichment-profiles
skills.search_text: periodicity-detection-in-enrichment-profiles Use when you have ChIP-seq-scored DNA sequences centered on an anchor motif (e.g. Nanog motif sites scored by mESC Nanog ChIP-seq signal) and want to test whether a second TF's motif (e.g. Sox2) occurs at periodic, helical-phase offsets rather than at a single fixed spacing. You only need motif presence/absence enrichment across a set of sequences without positional information — zero-or-one-occurrence-per-sequence MEA tools (HOMER, MEIRLOP) are the wrong granularity, and MEPP's positional profile is unnecessary. You need de novo motif discovery/assembly — the article notes 'MEPP currently functions with a fixed motif library'; de novo recognition is left to future work. Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or a motif), since the profile is defined relative to such anchor points. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Detects helical (~10 bp) spacing periodicity in positional motif enrichment by running MEPP on sequences centered on an anchor motif and inspecting the resulting positional enrichment profile for regularly spaced peaks flanking the anchor, as demonstrated for Sox2 motif enrichment around Nanog motif sites in mESCs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Detects helical (~10 bp) spacing periodicity in positional motif enrichment by running MEPP on sequences centered on an anchor motif and inspecting the resulting positional enrichment profile for regularly spaced peaks flanking the anchor, as demonstrated for Sox2 motif enrichment around Nanog motif sites in mESCs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need motif presence/absence enrichment across a set of sequences without positional information — zero-or-one-occurrence-per-sequence MEA tools (HOMER, MEIRLOP) are the wrong granularity, and MEPP's positional profile is unnecessary. You need de novo motif discovery/assembly — the article notes 'MEPP currently functions with a fixed motif library'; de novo recognition is left to future work. Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or a motif), since the profile is defined relative to such anchor points.

skills.description: Use when reproducing the LuxR/H-NS ChIP-seq analyses in V. harveyi — counting overlapping peaks, detecting H-NS doublet peaks, or assigning peaks to ORFs — using the Perl scripts from the LuxR_H-NS GitHub repository.

skills.search_text: perl-scripting-for-genomics Use when reproducing the LuxR/H-NS ChIP-seq analyses in V. harveyi — counting overlapping peaks, detecting H-NS doublet peaks, or assigning peaks to ORFs — using the Perl scripts from the LuxR_H-NS GitHub repository. Input is already a gene expression matrix or promoter table rather than MACS2 peak interval coordinates — use differential-expression tooling instead Peak data are not from V. harveyi / not in the MACS2 interval format expected by FileUtil.pm and getPeakAnno.pl You need general-purpose genome interval arithmetic (e.g. large human datasets or bedtools-scale throughput); these scripts were written for this specific small bacterial genome analysis A method for processing bacterial ChIP-seq peak intervals with the Perl scripts deposited in the Juliacvk/LuxR_H-NS repository: intersecting LuxR and H-NS MACS2 peaks, annotating peaks to V. harveyi ORFs, and relating LuxR peaks to H-NS doublet peaks to quantify co-occupied and co-regulated quorum-sensing loci. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a gene expression matrix or promoter table rather than MACS2 peak interval coordinates — use differential-expression tooling instead Peak data are not from V. harveyi / not in the MACS2 interval format expected by FileUtil.pm and getPeakAnno.pl You need general-purpose genome interval arithmetic (e.g. large human datasets or bedtools-scale throughput); these scripts were written for this specific small bacterial genome analysis
