skills.name: permutation-based-alignment-score-normalization
skills.search_text: permutation-based-alignment-score-normalization Use when computing EpiAlign horizontal alignment scores within an epigenome (e.g. 500 kb regions of a Roadmap sample) and raw Smith-Waterman-style scores must be calibrated against a random background before ranking or clustering. Input regions are short or dominated entirely by the quiescent state 'o', whose long uniform stretches make compressed sequences uninformative for alignment (see Supplementary Figure S1 motivation) The analysis compares chromatin state sequences across two fixed epigenomes vertically (e.g. per-gene comparisons of 19,935 protein-coding genes between sample pairs) rather than horizontal within-epigenome scoring that needs a null background http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Normalizes EpiAlign local alignment scores by re-aligning each query chromatin state sequence to randomized chromatin state sequences as a negative control, so horizontal-alignment scores reflect enrichment over chance and are comparable across regions and epigenomes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Normalizes EpiAlign local alignment scores by re-aligning each query chromatin state sequence to randomized chromatin state sequences as a negative control, so horizontal-alignment scores reflect enrichment over chance and are comparable across regions and epigenomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input regions are short or dominated entirely by the quiescent state 'o', whose long uniform stretches make compressed sequences uninformative for alignment (see Supplementary Figure S1 motivation) The analysis compares chromatin state sequences across two fixed epigenomes vertically (e.g. per-gene comparisons of 19,935 protein-coding genes between sample pairs) rather than horizontal within-epigenome scoring that needs a null background

skills.description: Use when you need to establish whether a tuning parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) significantly influences AUC performance, by comparing a full linear model against a nested model without that term via ANOVA and a permutation test.
skills.name: permutation-based-anova-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-anova-significance-testing Use when you need to establish whether a tuning parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) significantly influences AUC performance, by comparing a full linear model against a nested model without that term via ANOVA and a permutation test. You have no AUC/performance table and only raw triplex prediction output (e.g. 3plex *_tpx.stability.gz files) — compute ROC curves first with pROC before modelling The question is comparing whole prediction tools (e.g. 3plex vs TriplexFPP agreement) rather than testing significance of a single parameter within one tool's scoring model http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Statistical framework from the 3plex paper to test whether a scoring parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) significantly affects prediction accuracy (AUC), combining an R lm-based ANOVA comparison of a full vs nested model with a 10000-permutation randomisation test to estimate parameter relevance probability. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Statistical framework from the 3plex paper to test whether a scoring parameter (e.g. minimal TPX length 8/10/12/16) significantly affects prediction accuracy (AUC), combining an R lm-based ANOVA comparison of a full vs nested model with a 10000-permutation randomisation test to estimate parameter relevance probability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no AUC/performance table and only raw triplex prediction output (e.g. 3plex *_tpx.stability.gz files) — compute ROC curves first with pROC before modelling The question is comparing whole prediction tools (e.g. 3plex vs TriplexFPP agreement) rather than testing significance of a single parameter within one tool's scoring model

skills.description: Use when validating that single-cell chromatin structures (e.g., TLD-cliques from deDoc2 TLD predictions) show genuine inter-TLD contact enrichment beyond what is expected from genomic layout alone.
skills.name: permutation-based-contact-enrichment
skills.search_text: permutation-based-contact-enrichment Use when validating that single-cell chromatin structures (e.g., TLD-cliques from deDoc2 TLD predictions) show genuine inter-TLD contact enrichment beyond what is expected from genomic layout alone. Input TLD structures contain 4 or fewer TLDs — the pipeline retains only cliques with more than 4 TLDs The analysis goal is de novo TLD detection from raw Hi-C data rather than enrichment testing of already-predicted structures Per-cell contact matrices are unavailable or lack sufficient contacts to support a chromosome-matched permutation control Quantifies whether predicted single-cell TLD-cliques have enriched inter-TLD Hi-C contacts by comparing observed per-cell inter-TLD contacts to expected contacts from 250 permuted control cliques, computing an observed/expected ratio per clique. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Quantifies whether predicted single-cell TLD-cliques have enriched inter-TLD Hi-C contacts by comparing observed per-cell inter-TLD contacts to expected contacts from 250 permuted control cliques, computing an observed/expected ratio per clique.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input TLD structures contain 4 or fewer TLDs — the pipeline retains only cliques with more than 4 TLDs The analysis goal is de novo TLD detection from raw Hi-C data rather than enrichment testing of already-predicted structures Per-cell contact matrices are unavailable or lack sufficient contacts to support a chromosome-matched permutation control

skills.description: Use when regressing CCLE pharmacogenomic drug response (e.g. PLX4720 sensitivity) against regulation-potential (RP) scores of TR targets and you need empirical significance beyond parametric uniP/multiP likelihood-ratio tests.
skills.name: permutation-based-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-significance-testing Use when regressing CCLE pharmacogenomic drug response (e.g. PLX4720 sensitivity) against regulation-potential (RP) scores of TR targets and you need empirical significance beyond parametric uniP/multiP likelihood-ratio tests. Lack of ChIP-seq data or ChIP-seq data with too few targets, which would mislead the identification of TRs Detection of acquired (secondary) resistance from CCLE, since lack of post-treatment data prevents integrating drug-perturbation effects on genes Cases where reliable TR target information is unavailable, since RePhine identifies drug response-related TRs through the targets http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assess the statistical significance of transcriptional regulator (TR) associations with drug response in the RePhine framework, where each TR's regression yields a RePhine coefficient with uniP and multiP likelihood-ratio statistics that are further checked against a null distribution via permutation testing (permuP). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Assess the statistical significance of transcriptional regulator (TR) associations with drug response in the RePhine framework, where each TR's regression yields a RePhine coefficient with uniP and multiP likelihood-ratio statistics that are further checked against a null distribution via permutation testing (permuP).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Lack of ChIP-seq data or ChIP-seq data with too few targets, which would mislead the identification of TRs Detection of acquired (secondary) resistance from CCLE, since lack of post-treatment data prevents integrating drug-perturbation effects on genes Cases where reliable TR target information is unavailable, since RePhine identifies drug response-related TRs through the targets

skills.description: Use when a positional enrichment profile (one correlation per heatmap column relative to an anchor point such as a TSS or motif) must carry statistical significance and confidence bands robust to GC bias and spatial autocorrelation.
skills.name: permutation-based-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-based-significance-testing Use when a positional enrichment profile (one correlation per heatmap column relative to an anchor point such as a TSS or motif) must carry statistical significance and confidence bands robust to GC bias and spatial autocorrelation. The question is genome-wide motif presence/absence enrichment without positional information (a ZOOPs-style MEA such as HOMER or MEIRLOP suffices) No continuous sequence score is available to permute — MEPP's design requires scored sequences across a continuum reflecting biological extremes De novo motif discovery is required: MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library http://edamontology.org/topic_3361 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Generates null distributions by permuting the sequence score vector to assign per-position confidence intervals and P-values to MEPP's GC-controlled partial Pearson correlations, then corrects position-wise P-values with Benjamini-Yekutieli FDR to handle dependence between neighboring positions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Generates null distributions by permuting the sequence score vector to assign per-position confidence intervals and P-values to MEPP's GC-controlled partial Pearson correlations, then corrects position-wise P-values with Benjamini-Yekutieli FDR to handle dependence between neighboring positions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is genome-wide motif presence/absence enrichment without positional information (a ZOOPs-style MEA such as HOMER or MEIRLOP suffices) No continuous sequence score is available to permute — MEPP's design requires scored sequences across a continuum reflecting biological extremes De novo motif discovery is required: MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library

skills.description: Use when benchmarking null-range generation for genomic overlap testing: you need a shuffling/permutation baseline null distribution of overlap rates to compare against block bootstrapping (bootRanges) for FPR calibration.
skills.name: permutation-shuffling-null-generation
skills.search_text: permutation-shuffling-null-generation Use when benchmarking null-range generation for genomic overlap testing: you need a shuffling/permutation baseline null distribution of overlap rates to compare against block bootstrapping (bootRanges) for FPR calibration. When the goal is a calibrated null that preserves local genomic correlation structure — use the block bootstrap (bootRanges) instead, since shuffling produces overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance When the analysis target is not genomic range overlap testing (e.g. differential expression or correlation analyses handled by macrophage.R or multiomicsCor.R scripts) http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Generates null sets of genomic ranges by conventional shuffling/permutation (bootstrap.R-style) to serve as a baseline null hypothesis generator in genomic overlap enrichment analysis, and to contrast against block-bootstrap nulls whose overly narrow test statistic null distributions inflate significance. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Generates null sets of genomic ranges by conventional shuffling/permutation (bootstrap.R-style) to serve as a baseline null hypothesis generator in genomic overlap enrichment analysis, and to contrast against block-bootstrap nulls whose overly narrow test statistic null distributions inflate significance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is a calibrated null that preserves local genomic correlation structure — use the block bootstrap (bootRanges) instead, since shuffling produces overly narrow null distributions and over-estimated significance When the analysis target is not genomic range overlap testing (e.g. differential expression or correlation analyses handled by macrophage.R or multiomicsCor.R scripts)

skills.description: Use when a TF–pathway interaction score from time-series expression data needs an empirical significance call: TSMiner derives each block's probability via permutation testing and accepts interactions with score >= 50 and probability >= 50%.
skills.name: permutation-significance-testing
skills.search_text: permutation-significance-testing Use when a TF–pathway interaction score from time-series expression data needs an empirical significance call: TSMiner derives each block's probability via permutation testing and accepts interactions with score >= 50 and probability >= 50%. Input is a static (non-time-series) expression matrix — TSMiner requires time-series profiles to evaluate temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways. Dense repressor-pathway calls are needed: known negatively correlated TF–TG interactions are limited, so results from negative interactions will be sparse. Direct TF-to-pathway-gene regulation is required: a significant block certifies the TG as directly regulated and the PG only indirectly correlated with the TF through the TG. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Permutation-based empirical significance testing of TF–pathway interactions in TSMiner: TF–TG–PG triple-gene blocks are scored with the mutual interaction measure (MIM) and compared against a permutation-derived null, so only TF–pathway pairs exceeding chance (score >= 50, probability >= 50%) are accepted. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Permutation-based empirical significance testing of TF–pathway interactions in TSMiner: TF–TG–PG triple-gene blocks are scored with the mutual interaction measure (MIM) and compared against a permutation-derived null, so only TF–pathway pairs exceeding chance (score >= 50, probability >= 50%) are accepted.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a static (non-time-series) expression matrix — TSMiner requires time-series profiles to evaluate temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways. Dense repressor-pathway calls are needed: known negatively correlated TF–TG interactions are limited, so results from negative interactions will be sparse. Direct TF-to-pathway-gene regulation is required: a significant block certifies the TG as directly regulated and the PG only indirectly correlated with the TF through the TG.

skills.description: Use when visualizing cell-to-cell similarity of single-cell ATAC-seq profiles via chromVAR deviationsTsne and a perplexity must be set for the number of filtered cells (e.g., perplexity = 10 on small filtered sets).
skills.name: perplexity-parameter-tuning-for-tsne
skills.search_text: perplexity-parameter-tuning-for-tsne Use when visualizing cell-to-cell similarity of single-cell ATAC-seq profiles via chromVAR deviationsTsne and a perplexity must be set for the number of filtered cells (e.g., perplexity = 10 on small filtered sets). The goal is cluster identification or a global embedding of a large scATAC-seq dataset: the paper notes newer methods such as SnapATAC outperform chromVAR for the clustering tasks evaluated, and chromVAR is better used to annotate TF motif usage in cells and clusters. The input is raw fragment counts rather than a chromVARDeviations object of bias-corrected deviation scores — computeDeviations must run first, since deviationsTsne operates on the deviation object. The number of cells after filtering is large enough that the small-set perplexity value (10) is inappropriate; the perplexity=10 setting is tailored to the filtered example_counts set and should be revisited for bigger datasets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Embeds chromVAR's per-cell, bias-corrected motif deviation scores in 2D with the deviationsTsne function, choosing a perplexity appropriate to the number of cells surviving sample filtering (perplexity = 10, threshold = 1.5 in the chromVAR example_counts workflow). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/nmeth.4401
skills.summary: Embeds chromVAR's per-cell, bias-corrected motif deviation scores in 2D with the deviationsTsne function, choosing a perplexity appropriate to the number of cells surviving sample filtering (perplexity = 10, threshold = 1.5 in the chromVAR example_counts workflow).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is cluster identification or a global embedding of a large scATAC-seq dataset: the paper notes newer methods such as SnapATAC outperform chromVAR for the clustering tasks evaluated, and chromVAR is better used to annotate TF motif usage in cells and clusters. The input is raw fragment counts rather than a chromVARDeviations object of bias-corrected deviation scores — computeDeviations must run first, since deviationsTsne operates on the deviation object. The number of cells after filtering is large enough that the small-set perplexity value (10) is inappropriate; the perplexity=10 setting is tailored to the filtered example_counts set and should be revisited for bigger datasets.

skills.description: Use when calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loop-calling output and you need to reduce noisy, low-support loops before merging intervals of continuous loop coverage.
skills.name: pet-count-percentile-filtering
skills.search_text: pet-count-percentile-filtering Use when calling chromatin contact domains from CTCF ChIA-PET loop-calling output and you need to reduce noisy, low-support loops before merging intervals of continuous loop coverage. Input is raw PET reads or pre-loop-calling data — peak calling and loop calling must be completed first The goal is enhancer-promoter loop annotation, which uses a different filter (PET count ≥3 and peak support per loop) rather than the 67th-percentile domain filter Loops lack peak-support annotations for both anchors (e.g., non-CTCF factor data without matched peak calls), since the filter requires both-anchor peak support http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 A filtering strategy within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling that retains only CTCF ChIA-PET loops with both anchors supported by called peaks and only the top one-third of loops by PET count (67th-percentile cutoff), then merges surviving loops into ≥25 kb domains. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: A filtering strategy within ChIA-PIPE's chromatin contact domain (CCD) calling that retains only CTCF ChIA-PET loops with both anchors supported by called peaks and only the top one-third of loops by PET count (67th-percentile cutoff), then merges surviving loops into ≥25 kb domains.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw PET reads or pre-loop-calling data — peak calling and loop calling must be completed first The goal is enhancer-promoter loop annotation, which uses a different filter (PET count ≥3 and peak support per loop) rather than the 67th-percentile domain filter Loops lack peak-support annotations for both anchors (e.g., non-CTCF factor data without matched peak calls), since the filter requires both-anchor peak support

skills.description: Use when linker-filtered ChIA-PET FASTQ tags must be mapped to a reference genome and deduplicated so that downstream peak calling and loop calling receive only uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs.
skills.name: pet-deduplication
skills.search_text: pet-deduplication Use when linker-filtered ChIA-PET FASTQ tags must be mapped to a reference genome and deduplicated so that downstream peak calling and loop calling receive only uniquely aligned, nonredundant PETs. Input is raw, unfiltered FASTQ reads that have not undergone ChIA-PIPE linker filtering — run the linker-filtering category step first. The task is calling peaks, loops, CCDs, or E-P annotations — this skill stops at analysis-ready PET BAMs and does not perform those downstream steps. The data are not PET-style chromatin interaction reads (e.g., ordinary ChIP-seq fragments) — the hybrid BWA-ALN/BWA-MEM and CPU dedup workflow is specific to paired-end tag junction reads. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Aligns linker-trimmed ChIA-PET tags to a reference genome with a hybrid BWA-ALN/BWA-MEM strategy and retains only unique (MAPQ ≥ 30), nonredundant PETs via the CPU "dedup" module, producing analysis-ready PET BAM alignments for downstream peak and loop calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.aay2078
skills.summary: Aligns linker-trimmed ChIA-PET tags to a reference genome with a hybrid BWA-ALN/BWA-MEM strategy and retains only unique (MAPQ ≥ 30), nonredundant PETs via the CPU "dedup" module, producing analysis-ready PET BAM alignments for downstream peak and loop calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw, unfiltered FASTQ reads that have not undergone ChIA-PIPE linker filtering — run the linker-filtering category step first. The task is calling peaks, loops, CCDs, or E-P annotations — this skill stops at analysis-ready PET BAMs and does not perform those downstream steps. The data are not PET-style chromatin interaction reads (e.g., ordinary ChIP-seq fragments) — the hybrid BWA-ALN/BWA-MEM and CPU dedup workflow is specific to paired-end tag junction reads.

skills.description: Use when processing raw ChIA-PET FASTQ (bridge-linker or half-linker) data and you need PCR duplicate removal and per-step QC before PET construction, MACS2 peak calling, and MICC loop calling.
skills.name: pet-duplicate-removal-and-alignment-qc
skills.search_text: pet-duplicate-removal-and-alignment-qc Use when processing raw ChIA-PET FASTQ (bridge-linker or half-linker) data and you need PCR duplicate removal and per-step QC before PET construction, MACS2 peak calling, and MICC loop calling. Input data are not ChIA-PET paired-end reads (e.g. plain ChIP-Seq or Hi-C libraries) — linker trimming, PET construction and PET duplicate removal do not apply. You only need statistically significant loop calls from an existing bedpe file and already have deduplicated PETs — use bedpe2Interaction/MICC2.R directly instead. Data come from a long-read ChIA-PET protocol requiring long-read alignment mode rather than short-read bwa alignment handled here. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Remove PCR-duplicate paired-end tags (PETs) and run quality-control plots after linker trimming and bwa alignment in the ChIA-PET2 pipeline, so that downstream peak calling and chromatin loop calling operate on deduplicated, quality-filtered PETs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Remove PCR-duplicate paired-end tags (PETs) and run quality-control plots after linker trimming and bwa alignment in the ChIA-PET2 pipeline, so that downstream peak calling and chromatin loop calling operate on deduplicated, quality-filtered PETs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not ChIA-PET paired-end reads (e.g. plain ChIP-Seq or Hi-C libraries) — linker trimming, PET construction and PET duplicate removal do not apply. You only need statistically significant loop calls from an existing bedpe file and already have deduplicated PETs — use bedpe2Interaction/MICC2.R directly instead. Data come from a long-read ChIA-PET protocol requiring long-read alignment mode rather than short-read bwa alignment handled here.

skills.description: Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET raw reads and you need to measure the sensitivity gain of linker-searching at 1 allowed mismatch (-e 1) versus the strict 0-mismatch setting (-e 0), expressed as rescued PET counts and valid PET ratio from the trim.stat summaries.
skills.name: pet-rescue-count-comparison
skills.search_text: pet-rescue-count-comparison Use when processing bridge-linker ChIA-PET raw reads and you need to measure the sensitivity gain of linker-searching at 1 allowed mismatch (-e 1) versus the strict 0-mismatch setting (-e 0), expressed as rescued PET counts and valid PET ratio from the trim.stat summaries. Input is half-linker ChIA-PET data rather than the bridge-linker protocol — use a half-linker trimming strategy instead of the -m 1 bridge-linker mode The goal is significant chromatin loop calling or allele-specific analysis rather than quantifying linker-trimming sensitivity Linker sequences differ from the bridge linker ACGCGATATCTTATCTGACT used in this protocol; the rescue benchmark does not transfer Quantifies how many paired-end tags (PETs) are rescued and how much the valid PET ratio improves when ChIA-PET2's trimLinker step allows one mismatch in the bridge-linker sequence versus zero mismatches, using the GM12878 CTCF ChIA-PET dataset as a benchmark (>16 million rescued PETs, 12.85% improvement). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Quantifies how many paired-end tags (PETs) are rescued and how much the valid PET ratio improves when ChIA-PET2's trimLinker step allows one mismatch in the bridge-linker sequence versus zero mismatches, using the GM12878 CTCF ChIA-PET dataset as a benchmark (>16 million rescued PETs, 12.85% improvement).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is half-linker ChIA-PET data rather than the bridge-linker protocol — use a half-linker trimming strategy instead of the -m 1 bridge-linker mode The goal is significant chromatin loop calling or allele-specific analysis rather than quantifying linker-trimming sensitivity Linker sequences differ from the bridge linker ACGCGATATCTTATCTGACT used in this protocol; the rescue benchmark does not transfer

skills.description: Use when aligned, PCR-deduplicated ChIA-PET PETs in bedpe format must be assigned to MACS2-called anchor peak pairs to generate candidate intra-/inter-chromosomal loops.
skills.name: pet-to-peak-interaction-mapping
skills.search_text: pet-to-peak-interaction-mapping Use when aligned, PCR-deduplicated ChIA-PET PETs in bedpe format must be assigned to MACS2-called anchor peak pairs to generate candidate intra-/inter-chromosomal loops. PETs have not yet been linker-trimmed, aligned (bwa) and PCR-duplicate-removed — bedpe2Interaction expects bedpe output from buildBedpe/removeDup No ChIP-seq-like peak list is available for the factor, since ChIA-PET2 loop calling depends on peak-calling sensitivity Input is not ChIA-PET PET data (e.g., Hi-C contact matrices or already-called loops) http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Assigns ChIA-PET paired-end tags from a deduplicated bedpe file to ChIP-seq-like anchor peaks (called by MACS2 on buildTagAlign output) to form candidate peak-pair chromatin interactions for MICC significance testing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Assigns ChIA-PET paired-end tags from a deduplicated bedpe file to ChIP-seq-like anchor peaks (called by MACS2 on buildTagAlign output) to form candidate peak-pair chromatin interactions for MICC significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: PETs have not yet been linker-trimmed, aligned (bwa) and PCR-duplicate-removed — bedpe2Interaction expects bedpe output from buildBedpe/removeDup No ChIP-seq-like peak list is available for the factor, since ChIA-PET2 loop calling depends on peak-calling sensitivity Input is not ChIA-PET PET data (e.g., Hi-C contact matrices or already-called loops)

skills.description: Use when a research question asks whether a set of transcription factors (e.g. TFs occupying HOT regions) can bind single-stranded DNA directly or through their direct interaction partners, requiring domain-level annotation via PFAM HMMs plus PPI evidence.
skills.name: pfam-hmm-domain-scan
skills.search_text: pfam-hmm-domain-scan Use when a research question asks whether a set of transcription factors (e.g. TFs occupying HOT regions) can bind single-stranded DNA directly or through their direct interaction partners, requiring domain-level annotation via PFAM HMMs plus PPI evidence. When the question is about motif occupancy or ChIP-seq peak enrichment on HOT regions rather than protein domain content and PPI-mediated ssDNA binding capability When only non-reviewed (TrEMBL) or non-human proteomes are available, since the workflow is calibrated to Swiss-Prot human sequences and iRefWeb human interactions http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Scan reviewed human protein sequences with HMMER3 (hmmsearch) against PFAM HMM profiles of ssDNA-binding domains (OB, KH, RRM, and sPC4-like clans) to determine which proteins carry ssDNA-binding domains, then join the hit list with iRefWeb physical protein-protein interactions to ask whether transcription factors bind ssDNA directly or via direct partners. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz460
skills.summary: Scan reviewed human protein sequences with HMMER3 (hmmsearch) against PFAM HMM profiles of ssDNA-binding domains (OB, KH, RRM, and sPC4-like clans) to determine which proteins carry ssDNA-binding domains, then join the hit list with iRefWeb physical protein-protein interactions to ask whether transcription factors bind ssDNA directly or via direct partners.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is about motif occupancy or ChIP-seq peak enrichment on HOT regions rather than protein domain content and PPI-mediated ssDNA binding capability When only non-reviewed (TrEMBL) or non-human proteomes are available, since the workflow is calibrated to Swiss-Prot human sequences and iRefWeb human interactions

skills.description: Use when paired-end RIMS-seq fastq data (e.g. Xp12 phage DNA across 0-14 h / 0.1-0.5 M NaOH treatments) must be converted into a C-to-T deamination rate table or R1/R2 fold-imbalance curve to choose optimal alkaline-treatment conditions.
skills.name: phage-deamination-treatment-optimization-analysis
skills.search_text: phage-deamination-treatment-optimization-analysis Use when paired-end RIMS-seq fastq data (e.g. Xp12 phage DNA across 0-14 h / 0.1-0.5 M NaOH treatments) must be converted into a C-to-T deamination rate table or R1/R2 fold-imbalance curve to choose optimal alkaline-treatment conditions. The sequencing library was prepared by tagmentation or a non-adapter-ligation protocol — RIMS-seq deamination analysis does not work with such libraries The goal is precise genomic localization of methylated cytosines rather than global treatment-optimization — use EM-seq or bisulfite-seq instead Input is already an assembled genome or methylation motif call set rather than paired-end reads aligned to a matching reference http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Quantifies how heat-alkaline (NaOH) treatment time and concentration drive C-to-T read-variant deamination in m5C-only phage DNA (Xp12), computing Read1/Read2 fold imbalance and deamination rates to calibrate RIMS-seq treatment conditions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Quantifies how heat-alkaline (NaOH) treatment time and concentration drive C-to-T read-variant deamination in m5C-only phage DNA (Xp12), computing Read1/Read2 fold imbalance and deamination rates to calibrate RIMS-seq treatment conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequencing library was prepared by tagmentation or a non-adapter-ligation protocol — RIMS-seq deamination analysis does not work with such libraries The goal is precise genomic localization of methylated cytosines rather than global treatment-optimization — use EM-seq or bisulfite-seq instead Input is already an assembled genome or methylation motif call set rather than paired-end reads aligned to a matching reference

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a TR–drug response identification method on synthetic pharmacogenomic/ChIP-seq data, or when evaluating robustness of such methods to added noise or spurious confounder-induced correlations.
skills.name: pharmacogenomic-chipseq-simulation
skills.search_text: pharmacogenomic-chipseq-simulation Use when benchmarking a TR–drug response identification method on synthetic pharmacogenomic/ChIP-seq data, or when evaluating robustness of such methods to added noise or spurious confounder-induced correlations. The goal is identifying TR–drug associations in real CCLE or liver cancer pharmacogenomic data rather than benchmarking method performance on synthetic data No reliable ChIP-seq target/RP score information is available — RePhine identification would be misled and the simulation benchmark does not address this regime http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 http://edamontology.org/topic_0204 Reproduce the RePhine simulation benchmark that generates synthetic pharmacogenomic (gene expression + drug response) and ChIP-seq regulatory-potential data with added noises or confounders, then compares RePhine against Pearson correlation, logistic regression, and GSEA for identifying drug response-related transcriptional regulators. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Reproduce the RePhine simulation benchmark that generates synthetic pharmacogenomic (gene expression + drug response) and ChIP-seq regulatory-potential data with added noises or confounders, then compares RePhine against Pearson correlation, logistic regression, and GSEA for identifying drug response-related transcriptional regulators.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is identifying TR–drug associations in real CCLE or liver cancer pharmacogenomic data rather than benchmarking method performance on synthetic data No reliable ChIP-seq target/RP score information is available — RePhine identification would be misled and the simulation benchmark does not address this regime

skills.description: Use when you have cell-line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, drug sensitivity such as CCLE PLX4720 profiles) plus ChIP-seq or RP-score target maps and need to find drug-response TRs while adjusting confounders.
skills.name: pharmacogenomic-data-integration
skills.search_text: pharmacogenomic-data-integration Use when you have cell-line pharmacogenomic data (expression, CNV, mutation, drug sensitivity such as CCLE PLX4720 profiles) plus ChIP-seq or RP-score target maps and need to find drug-response TRs while adjusting confounders. When no ChIP-seq data or only ChIP-seq data with too few targets are available for the TRs of interest, which would mislead TR identification When reliable target information is unavailable, since RePhine identifies TRs through their targets When studying acquired/secondary resistance requiring post-treatment data, which CCLE lacks (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation could not be detected) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 Integrate CCLE pharmacogenomic data (gene expression, copy number, mutation status, pharmacological profiles) with ENCODE ChIP-seq–derived regulatory potential (RP) scores via the RePhine regression framework to identify transcriptional regulators (TRs) associated with drug response. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Integrate CCLE pharmacogenomic data (gene expression, copy number, mutation status, pharmacological profiles) with ENCODE ChIP-seq–derived regulatory potential (RP) scores via the RePhine regression framework to identify transcriptional regulators (TRs) associated with drug response.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When no ChIP-seq data or only ChIP-seq data with too few targets are available for the TRs of interest, which would mislead TR identification When reliable target information is unavailable, since RePhine identifies TRs through their targets When studying acquired/secondary resistance requiring post-treatment data, which CCLE lacks (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation could not be detected)

skills.description: Use when bisulfite amplicon reads have been converted to a binary epihaplotype matrix and the goal is to identify statistically significant phased mCpG combinations (cores) and track epiallele families across populations.
skills.name: phased-methylation-core-identification
skills.search_text: phased-methylation-core-identification Use when bisulfite amplicon reads have been converted to a binary epihaplotype matrix and the goal is to identify statistically significant phased mCpG combinations (cores) and track epiallele families across populations. The analysis goal is quantitative methylation of single CpGs or abundance of individual epialleles without phased-CpG structure — tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler or methclone address this and cannot distinguish cores (e.g. they fail to separate Cond 4 from R1/R2 epialleles). The input is raw FASTQ/FASTA rather than a processed binary epihaplotype matrix — preprocessing (PEAR merge, PRINSEQ conversion, ampliMethProfiler mCpG extraction) must be completed first. The DNA segment contains fewer than two CpGs, since the minimum core requires at least two methylated cytosines with statistically significant frequency. http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Extracts stable combinations of phased methylated CpGs (methylated cores) shared by epiallele families from bisulfite-sequencing epihaplotypes using MethCoresProfiler, and quantifies each core with clonality and stability/entanglement indices in each population. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Extracts stable combinations of phased methylated CpGs (methylated cores) shared by epiallele families from bisulfite-sequencing epihaplotypes using MethCoresProfiler, and quantifies each core with clonality and stability/entanglement indices in each population.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is quantitative methylation of single CpGs or abundance of individual epialleles without phased-CpG structure — tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler or methclone address this and cannot distinguish cores (e.g. they fail to separate Cond 4 from R1/R2 epialleles). The input is raw FASTQ/FASTA rather than a processed binary epihaplotype matrix — preprocessing (PEAR merge, PRINSEQ conversion, ampliMethProfiler mCpG extraction) must be completed first. The DNA segment contains fewer than two CpGs, since the minimum core requires at least two methylated cytosines with statistically significant frequency.

skills.description: Use when comparing diploid single-individual haplotyping tools on simulated or real reads (Illumina, 10X, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and you need runtime, memory, and phasing-accuracy tables.
skills.name: phasing-accuracy-and-runtime-evaluation
skills.search_text: phasing-accuracy-and-runtime-evaluation Use when comparing diploid single-individual haplotyping tools on simulated or real reads (Illumina, 10X, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and you need runtime, memory, and phasing-accuracy tables. Organism or data are not diploid — HapCUT2 and SpecHap's graph bisection model assume two haplotypes; higher ploidy is not supported Goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — current SIH tools including SpecHap support only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Input is already a phased VCF from a population/trio phaser rather than fragment files — this skill evaluates fragment-based haplotype assembly http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarking protocol for haplotype-phasing tools (SpecHap vs HapCUT2, ReFHap, FastHare, DCHap) that measures CPU time and peak memory per run and scores phased haplotypes against 1000 Genomes trio-phased ground truth on simulated HG00403 data. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Benchmarking protocol for haplotype-phasing tools (SpecHap vs HapCUT2, ReFHap, FastHare, DCHap) that measures CPU time and peak memory per run and scores phased haplotypes against 1000 Genomes trio-phased ground truth on simulated HG00403 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Organism or data are not diploid — HapCUT2 and SpecHap's graph bisection model assume two haplotypes; higher ploidy is not supported Goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation — current SIH tools including SpecHap support only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Input is already a phased VCF from a population/trio phaser rather than fragment files — this skill evaluates fragment-based haplotype assembly

skills.description: Use when a large or error-prone long-read dataset (e.g. ~32x PacBio SMRT for a gigantic diploid genome) must be phased and tool scalability in CPU hours and memory must be empirically compared.
skills.name: phasing-tool-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: phasing-tool-benchmark-comparison Use when a large or error-prone long-read dataset (e.g. ~32x PacBio SMRT for a gigantic diploid genome) must be phased and tool scalability in CPU hours and memory must be empirically compared. Input ploidy is higher than diploid — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation phasing — current SIH software including SpecHap supports only SNPs and short indels The input is already a phased VCF and no tool comparison or resource measurement is needed http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmarks diploid haplotype-phasing tools (SpecHap, HapCUT2, DCHap, ReFHap) on the same fragment/VCF inputs, using resource monitoring to compare CPU time, peak memory, and completion under fixed usage boundaries. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Benchmarks diploid haplotype-phasing tools (SpecHap, HapCUT2, DCHap, ReFHap) on the same fragment/VCF inputs, using resource monitoring to compare CPU time, peak memory, and completion under fixed usage boundaries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input ploidy is higher than diploid — SpecHap's graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation phasing — current SIH software including SpecHap supports only SNPs and short indels The input is already a phased VCF and no tool comparison or resource measurement is needed

skills.description: Use when you need to score evolutionary conservation of genomic regions (e.g. rank candidate regulatory blocks) using a PhastCons multiple-alignment track plus RefSeq annotation, and compare score distributions across feature classes.
skills.name: phastcons-conservation-scoring
skills.search_text: phastcons-conservation-scoring Use when you need to score evolutionary conservation of genomic regions (e.g. rank candidate regulatory blocks) using a PhastCons multiple-alignment track plus RefSeq annotation, and compare score distributions across feature classes. Your input is already a per-region conservation score table or conservation profile in bigWig format — SeqCode defers bigWig genome-wide profile generation to future versions You need conservation scoring for an organism/assembly lacking a UCSC PhastCons track or RefSeq annotation, since both files are mandatory inputs You are working through the SeqCode web portal, which is intended as a teaching resource with restrictions on input set/size rather than large local conservation scans http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Compute PhastCons evolutionary conservation scores over sets of genomic intervals (CDS, UTRs, promoters, introns, intergenic) using SeqCode's scorePhastCons application, then aggregate per feature class to build a comparative conservation landscape that can rank intervals by their potential to contain conserved regulatory blocks. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Compute PhastCons evolutionary conservation scores over sets of genomic intervals (CDS, UTRs, promoters, introns, intergenic) using SeqCode's scorePhastCons application, then aggregate per feature class to build a comparative conservation landscape that can rank intervals by their potential to contain conserved regulatory blocks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is already a per-region conservation score table or conservation profile in bigWig format — SeqCode defers bigWig genome-wide profile generation to future versions You need conservation scoring for an organism/assembly lacking a UCSC PhastCons track or RefSeq annotation, since both files are mandatory inputs You are working through the SeqCode web portal, which is intended as a teaching resource with restrictions on input set/size rather than large local conservation scans

skills.name: phenotype-category-annotation
skills.search_text: phenotype-category-annotation Use when preparing SV input for POSTRE and each variant must be tagged with one or more disease-relevant phenotype categories from the seven supported options to drive tissue-specific enhancer/TAD analysis. The patient's phenotype does not map to any of the seven supported categories (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) The SV is implicated in a recessive phenotype, since POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The input is already a POSTRE results table (e.g. geneStats_recurrencyAndPathomech) rather than raw SV breakpoints needing annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Annotates each structural variant (SV) with a comma-separated list of POSTRE-supported phenotype categories (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) in column 6 of a tab-separated SV manifest, so POSTRE can run cell type/tissue-specific pathogenicity predictions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Annotates each structural variant (SV) with a comma-separated list of POSTRE-supported phenotype categories (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) in column 6 of a tab-separated SV manifest, so POSTRE can run cell type/tissue-specific pathogenicity predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The patient's phenotype does not map to any of the seven supported categories (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) The SV is implicated in a recessive phenotype, since POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The input is already a POSTRE results table (e.g. geneStats_recurrencyAndPathomech) rather than raw SV breakpoints needing annotation

skills.description: Use when a candidate gene must be scored for association with an SV-associated phenotype group using HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) annotations, as in POSTRE's genePhenoScore module.
skills.name: phenotype-group-term-propagation
skills.search_text: phenotype-group-term-propagation Use when a candidate gene must be scored for association with an SV-associated phenotype group using HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) annotations, as in POSTRE's genePhenoScore module. A precomputed genePhenoScore.tsv already ships with the POSTRE installation and no updated HPO/MPO releases need to be incorporated The phenotypes of interest fall outside the POSTRE reference phenotype groups (e.g. vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary added via cell-type data, not via this HPO/MPO module) The goal is SV pathogenicity prediction itself (use POSTRE_multiSV()) rather than building the gene-phenotype scoring layer that feeds it http://edamontology.org/topic_0218 Reconstructs POSTRE's genePhenoScore module by propagating HPO/MPO ontology terms from four reference phenotype-group roots (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) to build gene-phenotype links, assigning each gene 1 (human HPO), 0.5 (mouse MPO via ortholog) or 0 per group. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Reconstructs POSTRE's genePhenoScore module by propagating HPO/MPO ontology terms from four reference phenotype-group roots (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular) to build gene-phenotype links, assigning each gene 1 (human HPO), 0.5 (mouse MPO via ortholog) or 0 per group.
skills.when_to_use_negative: A precomputed genePhenoScore.tsv already ships with the POSTRE installation and no updated HPO/MPO releases need to be incorporated The phenotypes of interest fall outside the POSTRE reference phenotype groups (e.g. vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary added via cell-type data, not via this HPO/MPO module) The goal is SV pathogenicity prediction itself (use POSTRE_multiSV()) rather than building the gene-phenotype scoring layer that feeds it

skills.description: Use when POSTRE has been run in batch (POSTRE_multiSV or Multiple SV Submission) over an SV set with attached phenotype lists and you must tally pathogenic vs non-pathogenic calls per phenotype association and compute non-pathogenic percentages per mode.
skills.name: phenotype-stratified-results-tabulation
skills.search_text: phenotype-stratified-results-tabulation Use when POSTRE has been run in batch (POSTRE_multiSV or Multiple SV Submission) over an SV set with attached phenotype lists and you must tally pathogenic vs non-pathogenic calls per phenotype association and compute non-pathogenic percentages per mode. The SV coordinates are not in hg19 — POSTRE requires hg19 breakpoints, so tabulated calls would be invalid until lifted over The goal is evaluating recessive phenotypes — the article states POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The input involves phenotype classes outside the supported list (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary) http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 Tabulates POSTRE pathogenicity predictions per SV–phenotype association from the 'Results per SV and phenotype' output tables and computes the non-pathogenic percentage per phenotype group, SV set, and running mode (Standard vs High Specificity), enabling Type-1 error (false-positive) control assessment against healthy-individual SV benchmarks. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Tabulates POSTRE pathogenicity predictions per SV–phenotype association from the 'Results per SV and phenotype' output tables and computes the non-pathogenic percentage per phenotype group, SV set, and running mode (Standard vs High Specificity), enabling Type-1 error (false-positive) control assessment against healthy-individual SV benchmarks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The SV coordinates are not in hg19 — POSTRE requires hg19 breakpoints, so tabulated calls would be invalid until lifted over The goal is evaluating recessive phenotypes — the article states POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated The input involves phenotype classes outside the supported list (head_neck, limbs, neurodevelopmental, cardiovascular, vision_eye, liver_biliary_system, pituitary)

skills.description: Use when CITRUS ensemble TF activities (hid_tmr) must be validated against independent TF lists, e.g. MCF10A isogenic PIK3CA knock-in phosphoproteomics or AKT1 kinase assay substrate TFs.
skills.name: phosphoproteomic-tf-list-integration
skills.search_text: phosphoproteomic-tf-list-integration Use when CITRUS ensemble TF activities (hid_tmr) must be validated against independent TF lists, e.g. MCF10A isogenic PIK3CA knock-in phosphoproteomics or AKT1 kinase assay substrate TFs. Input is raw CITRUS per-run output rather than the ensembled TF activities — first run the model 10 times and aggregate with ensemble_TF.py --runs 10 The external reference set is not a TF list (e.g., gene-level or phosphosite-level data), since overlap is defined at the transcription factor level The somatic alteration of interest is not represented in the SGA matrix used to train the model, so no inferred TF activities can be associated with it http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Externally validates model-inferred transcription factor activities by testing their association with a somatic alteration (e.g., PIK3CA mutation) across TCGA samples and quantifying overlap with independent TF lists from phosphoproteomic and kinase-assay experiments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881
skills.summary: Externally validates model-inferred transcription factor activities by testing their association with a somatic alteration (e.g., PIK3CA mutation) across TCGA samples and quantifying overlap with independent TF lists from phosphoproteomic and kinase-assay experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw CITRUS per-run output rather than the ensembled TF activities — first run the model 10 times and aggregate with ensemble_TF.py --runs 10 The external reference set is not a TF list (e.g., gene-level or phosphosite-level data), since overlap is defined at the transcription factor level The somatic alteration of interest is not represented in the SGA matrix used to train the model, so no inferred TF activities can be associated with it

skills.description: Use when raw Sanger .ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) trace files must be quality-trimmed before computing CpG methylation percentages, especially when sequences end up too short or low-quality after trimming.
skills.name: phred-quality-score-sequence-trimming
skills.search_text: phred-quality-score-sequence-trimming Use when raw Sanger .ab1 bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) trace files must be quality-trimmed before computing CpG methylation percentages, especially when sequences end up too short or low-quality after trimming. Input data are not raw Sanger chromatogram traces (e.g. already-trimmed sequences or high-throughput short reads) — this trimming operates on .ab1 files within the ABSP BSP pipeline The goal is only methylation percentage computation without sequencing trimming QC — trimming boundaries are a prerequisite step, not an end in itself Reference genome is unavailable — the reference genome is only needed for genomic visualization, not for this trimming or for computing methylation percentages http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A sequence-trimming step from the ABSP tool that removes low-quality ends of raw .ab1 Sanger chromatogram reads by flagging positions whose base-calling error probability exceeds a Phred-score threshold, then combining the result with primary-peak-ratio trimming to define the final trimmed sequence used for CpG methylation computation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: A sequence-trimming step from the ABSP tool that removes low-quality ends of raw .ab1 Sanger chromatogram reads by flagging positions whose base-calling error probability exceeds a Phred-score threshold, then combining the result with primary-peak-ratio trimming to define the final trimmed sequence used for CpG methylation computation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are not raw Sanger chromatogram traces (e.g. already-trimmed sequences or high-throughput short reads) — this trimming operates on .ab1 files within the ABSP BSP pipeline The goal is only methylation percentage computation without sequencing trimming QC — trimming boundaries are a prerequisite step, not an end in itself Reference genome is unavailable — the reference genome is only needed for genomic visualization, not for this trimming or for computing methylation percentages

skills.description: Use when you have BED-format peak lists or genomic coordinate sets (e.g. bivalent vs single-mark ChIP-seq peaks) and need to quantify which genomic features they occupy and plot the distribution as pie charts.
skills.name: pie-chart-distribution-visualization
skills.search_text: pie-chart-distribution-visualization Use when you have BED-format peak lists or genomic coordinate sets (e.g. bivalent vs single-mark ChIP-seq peaks) and need to quantify which genomic features they occupy and plot the distribution as pie charts. Input is raw sequencing reads (BAM/SAM) rather than already-called peak/interval coordinates — use read mapping and peak calling first You need genome-wide signal profiles in bigWig format — SeqCode does not support bigWig generation and defers it to future versions You need a plot type other than feature-distribution charts (e.g. TSS meta-plots or heatmaps) — use produceTSSplots/produceTSSmaps instead Annotate a set of genomic intervals (e.g. MACS-called ChIP-seq peaks) to genomic features (promoter, intragenic, intergenic) using the SeqCode genomeDistribution command and visualize the resulting counts as pie-chart feature distributions via the R scripts emitted in the output folder. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Annotate a set of genomic intervals (e.g. MACS-called ChIP-seq peaks) to genomic features (promoter, intragenic, intergenic) using the SeqCode genomeDistribution command and visualize the resulting counts as pie-chart feature distributions via the R scripts emitted in the output folder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads (BAM/SAM) rather than already-called peak/interval coordinates — use read mapping and peak calling first You need genome-wide signal profiles in bigWig format — SeqCode does not support bigWig generation and defers it to future versions You need a plot type other than feature-distribution charts (e.g. TSS meta-plots or heatmaps) — use produceTSSplots/produceTSSmaps instead

skills.description: Use when quantifying end-to-end runtime and output file sizes of a NEAT NGS analysis on the truncated ChIPseq/RNAseq test datasets, or when validating speed claims for a sequenced run assessment within 24 h.
skills.name: pipeline-runtime-measurement
skills.search_text: pipeline-runtime-measurement Use when quantifying end-to-end runtime and output file sizes of a NEAT NGS analysis on the truncated ChIPseq/RNAseq test datasets, or when validating speed claims for a sequenced run assessment within 24 h. Input is full-scale (non-truncated) sequencing data where wall-time and storage expectations differ; use cluster-submission limits and customized storage settings instead of the truncated-dataset benchmark The goal is exploratory data analysis (metagenomic or differentially expressed gene analysis) rather than pipeline runtime and file-size characterization The operating environment is not Mac OSx or a qsub/bsub cluster, since NEAT support is documented only for these http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Benchmarks NEAT's NGS pipeline execution time and output file-size footprint on the bundled truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq and RNAseq test datasets (mouse embryonic stem cells), validating that the framework completes analyses well within the paper's <24-hour claim. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Benchmarks NEAT's NGS pipeline execution time and output file-size footprint on the bundled truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq and RNAseq test datasets (mouse embryonic stem cells), validating that the framework completes analyses well within the paper's <24-hour claim.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is full-scale (non-truncated) sequencing data where wall-time and storage expectations differ; use cluster-submission limits and customized storage settings instead of the truncated-dataset benchmark The goal is exploratory data analysis (metagenomic or differentially expressed gene analysis) rather than pipeline runtime and file-size characterization The operating environment is not Mac OSx or a qsub/bsub cluster, since NEAT support is documented only for these

skills.description: Use when choosing between read-trimming or read-mapping tools for an NGS pipeline and a reproducible comparison of wall-clock runtime plus retained-read yield/mapping accuracy is needed to justify the selection.
skills.name: pipeline-runtime-profiling
skills.search_text: pipeline-runtime-profiling Use when choosing between read-trimming or read-mapping tools for an NGS pipeline and a reproducible comparison of wall-clock runtime plus retained-read yield/mapping accuracy is needed to justify the selection. The goal is to execute a production pipeline rather than benchmark tool performance — CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, not subsets of tools, so timing individual tools must be done outside CIPHER The input is already trimmed, aligned, or otherwise pre-processed — runtime profiling requires a common raw FASTQ starting point for a fair comparison A tool has already been selected and no comparative runtime/accuracy justification is required http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3172 Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of NGS pre-processing tools — read trimmers (Trimmomatic, cutadapt, BBDuk) and aligners (BWA, Bowtie2, BBMap, STAR, HISAT2) — on identical public FASTQ input, recording runtime alongside accuracy metrics to justify tool selection as CIPHER did. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1
skills.summary: Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of NGS pre-processing tools — read trimmers (Trimmomatic, cutadapt, BBDuk) and aligners (BWA, Bowtie2, BBMap, STAR, HISAT2) — on identical public FASTQ input, recording runtime alongside accuracy metrics to justify tool selection as CIPHER did.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to execute a production pipeline rather than benchmark tool performance — CIPHER currently only runs entire workflows, not subsets of tools, so timing individual tools must be done outside CIPHER The input is already trimmed, aligned, or otherwise pre-processed — runtime profiling requires a common raw FASTQ starting point for a fair comparison A tool has already been selected and no comparative runtime/accuracy justification is required

skills.description: Use when you have DGW clustering outputs (config, warping paths, cluster BEDs) plus POI coordinate files and need a quantitative, per-cluster measure of whether warping tightened TSS/FSS alignment.
skills.name: poi-position-histogram-quantification
skills.search_text: poi-position-histogram-quantification Use when you have DGW clustering outputs (config, warping paths, cluster BEDs) plus POI coordinate files and need a quantitative, per-cluster measure of whether warping tightened TSS/FSS alignment. When the clustering/alignment step has not yet been run — there are no warped positions or warping paths to compare against raw ones When the analysed regions contain no points of interest; regions with no entry in the fss.poi file must be ignored (--ignore-no-poi-regions) rather than scored When assessing alignment quality for features other than genomic landmarks (TSS/FSS) — the histogram entropy metric is defined over POI position distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies the quality of DGW alignment of genomic landmarks by building binned histograms of point-of-interest (TSS and first splicing site, FSS) positions before and after warping and computing the Shannon entropy decrease. Percent entropy reduction (e.g. 12.91% TSS, 7.72% FSS in the selected cluster) provides a numeric confirmation that DGW tightens landmark alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Quantifies the quality of DGW alignment of genomic landmarks by building binned histograms of point-of-interest (TSS and first splicing site, FSS) positions before and after warping and computing the Shannon entropy decrease. Percent entropy reduction (e.g. 12.91% TSS, 7.72% FSS in the selected cluster) provides a numeric confirmation that DGW tightens landmark alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the clustering/alignment step has not yet been run — there are no warped positions or warping paths to compare against raw ones When the analysed regions contain no points of interest; regions with no entry in the fss.poi file must be ignored (--ignore-no-poi-regions) rather than scored When assessing alignment quality for features other than genomic landmarks (TSS/FSS) — the histogram entropy metric is defined over POI position distributions

skills.description: Use when Calling Cards qbed/ccf insertions must be tested for significant TF binding enrichment — e.g. after greedy candidate-peak extension, to decide which candidates become CC peaks.
skills.name: poisson-enrichment-peak-testing
skills.search_text: poisson-enrichment-peak-testing Use when Calling Cards qbed/ccf insertions must be tested for significant TF binding enrichment — e.g. after greedy candidate-peak extension, to decide which candidates become CC peaks. Input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — GILoop is explicitly not capable of dealing with extremely sparse single-cell Hi-C The target cell line's sequencing depth matches none of the repository's pre-trained models, making transfer evaluation unreliable without retraining No independent ground-truth loop set (e.g., HICCUPS/FitHiC intersection) is available, since precision and recall cannot be defined without it http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Builds and compares precision-recall curves (and PR-AUC) for chromatin loop callers such as GILoop and Peakachu by sweeping score thresholds against a ground-truth loop set, enabling both model benchmarking and transfer-learning evaluation across cell lines. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535

skills.description: Use when running Cellcano's two-round celltyping on scATAC-seq data and you need to derive anchor cells from first-round MLP prediction probabilities via an entropy quantile cutoff before training the KD model.
skills.name: prediction-entropy-computation
skills.search_text: prediction-entropy-computation Use when running Cellcano's two-round celltyping on scATAC-seq data and you need to derive anchor cells from first-round MLP prediction probabilities via an entropy quantile cutoff before training the KD model. Reference data are scRNA-seq rather than scATAC-seq: Cellcano is designed for scATAC-seq-as-reference celltyping, and cross-modality prediction using scRNA-seq as reference is planned but not implemented. The analysis goal requires jointly operating on reference and target datasets, as Seurat, Signac, and scJoint do — Cellcano's entropy-based anchor scheme works without joint embedding. You need multi-modal (jointly scRNA- and scATAC-seq) references — this is an open future direction not yet supported. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_2229 Computes per-cell prediction entropy from first-round Cellcano MLP prediction probabilities and selects the lowest-entropy target cells as anchors for the second-round Knowledge Distiller model, controlled by an entropy quantile cutoff (software default 0.4). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Computes per-cell prediction entropy from first-round Cellcano MLP prediction probabilities and selects the lowest-entropy target cells as anchors for the second-round Knowledge Distiller model, controlled by an entropy quantile cutoff (software default 0.4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Reference data are scRNA-seq rather than scATAC-seq: Cellcano is designed for scATAC-seq-as-reference celltyping, and cross-modality prediction using scRNA-seq as reference is planned but not implemented. The analysis goal requires jointly operating on reference and target datasets, as Seurat, Signac, and scJoint do — Cellcano's entropy-based anchor scheme works without joint embedding. You need multi-modal (jointly scRNA- and scATAC-seq) references — this is an open future direction not yet supported.

skills.description: Use when a leave-one-out or jackknife evaluation has emitted per-sample prediction scores and you need to aggregate them into a headline metric (e.g., ACC) for comparison against a published baseline.
skills.name: prediction-score-aggregation
skills.search_text: prediction-score-aggregation Use when a leave-one-out or jackknife evaluation has emitted per-sample prediction scores and you need to aggregate them into a headline metric (e.g., ACC) for comparison against a published baseline. The evaluation design is 5-fold cross-validation or an independent test set — use the classifier_selection.py or csDMA_indepedent_testing.py workflows instead of jackknife score aggregation. The input is already an aggregated metric (e.g., an AUC or ACC value) rather than per-sample prediction scores.
