Input is already a peak set or Anndata object rather than a raw qbed of insertions The goal is peak-accuracy (binding-site sensitivity/specificity) comparison rather than runtime/memory scaling, since downsampling changes effective depth http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Generates dilution series of calling cards qbed datasets with pycallingcards.preprocessing.down_sample so that caller runtime and memory scaling versus total transposon insertion number can be benchmarked across CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, Blockify_original, and ccf_tools. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Generates dilution series of calling cards qbed datasets with pycallingcards.preprocessing.down_sample so that caller runtime and memory scaling versus total transposon insertion number can be benchmarked across CCcaller, MACCs, Blockify, Blockify_original, and ccf_tools.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak set or Anndata object rather than a raw qbed of insertions The goal is peak-accuracy (binding-site sensitivity/specificity) comparison rather than runtime/memory scaling, since downsampling changes effective depth

skills.description: Use when the input is qbed/ccf calling cards insertion data (e.g., Brd4 scCC insertions from GEO) and TF binding sites must be called as peaks for annotation, AnnData construction, or peak-gene pairing.
skills.name: qbed-peak-calling-with-cccaller
skills.search_text: qbed-peak-calling-with-cccaller Use when the input is qbed/ccf calling cards insertion data (e.g., Brd4 scCC insertions from GEO) and TF binding sites must be called as peaks for annotation, AnnData construction, or peak-gene pairing. Input is already a peak file or feature-count matrix — use downstream tools (rank_peak_groups, pair_peak_gene_sc) instead of re-calling peaks Data are standard scRNA-seq or ChIP-seq reads rather than calling cards qbed/ccf insertions — use Scanpy or ChIP-seq peak callers instead Only motif or visualization analysis is needed and peaks already exist http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Calls transcription factor binding peaks from single-cell or bulk calling cards qbed/ccf insertion data using the CCcaller peak caller within Pycallingcards, then annotates and formats peaks for downstream binding-expression analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: Calls transcription factor binding peaks from single-cell or bulk calling cards qbed/ccf insertion data using the CCcaller peak caller within Pycallingcards, then annotates and formats peaks for downstream binding-expression analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak file or feature-count matrix — use downstream tools (rank_peak_groups, pair_peak_gene_sc) instead of re-calling peaks Data are standard scRNA-seq or ChIP-seq reads rather than calling cards qbed/ccf insertions — use Scanpy or ChIP-seq peak callers instead Only motif or visualization analysis is needed and peaks already exist

skills.description: Use when per-sample peak calls (narrowPeak) and replicate-level QC intermediates must be rolled up into a ChiLin QC JSON and per-mark distributions (e.g., DHS overlap ratios grouped by histone mark type) for atlas-scale comparison.
skills.name: qc-aggregation
skills.search_text: qc-aggregation Use when per-sample peak calls (narrowPeak) and replicate-level QC intermediates must be rolled up into a ChiLin QC JSON and per-mark distributions (e.g., DHS overlap ratios grouped by histone mark type) for atlas-scale comparison. Input samples are not ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peak sets (e.g., RNA-seq counts or ATAC-seq without an appropriate union accessibility reference), since the DHS overlap ratio is calibrated against ENCODE union DHS regions You only need an upstream QC metric already produced by ChiLin (FastQC, PBC, FRiP); use the specific metric step instead of the DHS-overlap aggregation workflow Peak calls are merged across replicates before QC, so no per-replicate *.enrich.dhs intermediates can be produced and replicate-level aggregation is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Aggregates per-sample and per-replicate ChiLin QC statistics — most notably the union DHS overlap ratio computed by intersecting id_sort_peaks.narrowPeak against the ENCODE union DHS BED — into a QC JSON (id_dhs) and per-histone-mark distribution summaries, enabling comparison against the ChiLin quality atlas. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Aggregates per-sample and per-replicate ChiLin QC statistics — most notably the union DHS overlap ratio computed by intersecting id_sort_peaks.narrowPeak against the ENCODE union DHS BED — into a QC JSON (id_dhs) and per-histone-mark distribution summaries, enabling comparison against the ChiLin quality atlas.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are not ChIP-seq/DNase-seq peak sets (e.g., RNA-seq counts or ATAC-seq without an appropriate union accessibility reference), since the DHS overlap ratio is calibrated against ENCODE union DHS regions You only need an upstream QC metric already produced by ChiLin (FastQC, PBC, FRiP); use the specific metric step instead of the DHS-overlap aggregation workflow Peak calls are merged across replicates before QC, so no per-replicate *.enrich.dhs intermediates can be produced and replicate-level aggregation is meaningless

skills.description: Use when a batch of ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples has per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs and you need to determine which QC metrics covary within each literature-based assay category.
skills.name: qc-metric-pairwise-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: qc-metric-pairwise-correlation-analysis Use when a batch of ChIP-seq/DNase-seq samples has per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs and you need to determine which QC metrics covary within each literature-based assay category. Input is raw sequencing data with no per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs yet — run the ChiLin pipeline (mapping, macs2 fragment size estimation, PBC, FRiP) first. The question is about absolute QC quality thresholds for a single sample rather than covariation structure of QC metrics across a sample collection. Samples cannot be assigned to a literature-based assay category, since correlations are computed and interpreted per category. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3574 Compile per-sample ChiLin QC statistics (FRiP, PBC, fragment size, mapping, replicate metrics) into a flat metrics table, split samples into assay categories, and compute 13x13 pairwise correlation matrices with R to reproduce the paper's QC-metric correlation structure (e.g., FRiP vs peak number). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Compile per-sample ChiLin QC statistics (FRiP, PBC, fragment size, mapping, replicate metrics) into a flat metrics table, split samples into assay categories, and compute 13x13 pairwise correlation matrices with R to reproduce the paper's QC-metric correlation structure (e.g., FRiP vs peak number).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data with no per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs yet — run the ChiLin pipeline (mapping, macs2 fragment size estimation, PBC, FRiP) first. The question is about absolute QC quality thresholds for a single sample rather than covariation structure of QC metrics across a sample collection. Samples cannot be assigned to a literature-based assay category, since correlations are computed and interpreted per category.

skills.description: Use when per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs (id_fastqc., id_map., id_frag., id_pbc., id_frip., id_macs2., id_rep.) must be aggregated into a dataset-level summary table covering the 17 QC metrics across three QC layers for benchmarking or atlas building.
skills.name: qc-metrics-compilation-across-datasets
skills.search_text: qc-metrics-compilation-across-datasets Use when per-sample ChiLin QC JSON outputs (id_fastqc., id_map., id_frag., id_pbc., id_frip., id_macs2., id_rep.) must be aggregated into a dataset-level summary table covering the 17 QC metrics across three QC layers for benchmarking or atlas building. Input is raw sequencing data needing only a single-sample QC run rather than cross-dataset compilation — use the per-sample ChiLin QC steps directly without the aggregation modules Data are not ChIP-seq or DNase-seq (e.g., RNA-seq or ATAC-seq) — ChiLin's QC metric set is designed specifically for ChIP-seq and DNase-seq experiments Only the final merged peak calls are needed and no quality assessment or historical comparison is intended http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Aggregate per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq quality-control statistics produced by the ChiLin pipeline (FastQC, mapping, fragment-size, PBC, replicate overlap, FRiP, MACS2, meta-region metrics) into a unified plain-text and tabular quality atlas across many samples and datasets, enabling comparison against historical reference metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Aggregate per-sample ChIP-seq/DNase-seq quality-control statistics produced by the ChiLin pipeline (FastQC, mapping, fragment-size, PBC, replicate overlap, FRiP, MACS2, meta-region metrics) into a unified plain-text and tabular quality atlas across many samples and datasets, enabling comparison against historical reference metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing data needing only a single-sample QC run rather than cross-dataset compilation — use the per-sample ChiLin QC steps directly without the aggregation modules Data are not ChIP-seq or DNase-seq (e.g., RNA-seq or ATAC-seq) — ChiLin's QC metric set is designed specifically for ChIP-seq and DNase-seq experiments Only the final merged peak calls are needed and no quality assessment or historical comparison is intended

skills.description: Use when evaluating whether a ChIP-seq QC metric such as FRiP is an artifact of sequencing depth: you have down-sampled BAMs (e.g., 1M, 2M, 4M reads) and want stability curves under two peak-calling settings.
skills.name: qc-stability-curve-visualization
skills.search_text: qc-stability-curve-visualization Use when evaluating whether a ChIP-seq QC metric such as FRiP is an artifact of sequencing depth: you have down-sampled BAMs (e.g., 1M, 2M, 4M reads) and want stability curves under two peak-calling settings. You only need a single FRiP value per sample at full sequencing depth (ChiLin step 7) rather than a depth-stability comparison Your QC metric is depth-independent by construction (e.g., PBC, FRiT-like ratios over fixed regions) so a stability curve adds no information You need QC reporting for batched samples rather than a methodological stability analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Constructs FRiP-versus-sequencing-depth stability curves by holding peak regions fixed across down-sampled BAM depths, distinguishing QC metrics that remain stable (peaks from all reads, Fig. 2e style) from metrics that degrade at shallow depth (peaks re-called per depth, Fig. 2d style). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Constructs FRiP-versus-sequencing-depth stability curves by holding peak regions fixed across down-sampled BAM depths, distinguishing QC metrics that remain stable (peaks from all reads, Fig. 2e style) from metrics that degrade at shallow depth (peaks re-called per depth, Fig. 2d style).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single FRiP value per sample at full sequencing depth (ChiLin step 7) rather than a depth-stability comparison Your QC metric is depth-independent by construction (e.g., PBC, FRiT-like ratios over fixed regions) so a stability curve adds no information You need QC reporting for batched samples rather than a methodological stability analysis

skills.description: Use when benchmarking differential ChIP-seq region callers against a small qPCR-validated ground truth set: you have genomic coordinates of qPCR-tested regions and called-region sets (e.g. BED/GRanges) from histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff and Rseg to classify as Y/FP/FN.
skills.name: qpcr-region-coordinate-lookup
skills.search_text: qpcr-region-coordinate-lookup Use when benchmarking differential ChIP-seq region callers against a small qPCR-validated ground truth set: you have genomic coordinates of qPCR-tested regions and called-region sets (e.g. BED/GRanges) from histoneHMM, Diffreps, Chipdiff and Rseg to classify as Y/FP/FN. The histone mark under study is a narrow peak-like feature rather than a broad diffuse modification like H3K27me3 — peak-calling-style methods are the article's stated failure mode There is no qPCR-validated region set or comparable published ground-truth table, so Y/FP/FN labels cannot be judged Calls are for a single-sample modified-region task rather than a two-sample differential comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Validates differential histone-modification region calls (e.g. histoneHMM H3K27me3 SHR vs BN) by intersecting the chromosomal coordinates of qPCR-surveyed regions with each caller's output on the rn4 rat genome, labeling each method-region pair as Y, FP or FN to reproduce the published Table 3 benchmark. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Validates differential histone-modification region calls (e.g. histoneHMM H3K27me3 SHR vs BN) by intersecting the chromosomal coordinates of qPCR-surveyed regions with each caller's output on the rn4 rat genome, labeling each method-region pair as Y, FP or FN to reproduce the published Table 3 benchmark.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The histone mark under study is a narrow peak-like feature rather than a broad diffuse modification like H3K27me3 — peak-calling-style methods are the article's stated failure mode There is no qPCR-validated region set or comparable published ground-truth table, so Y/FP/FN labels cannot be judged Calls are for a single-sample modified-region task rather than a two-sample differential comparison

skills.description: Use when expression estimates from an RNA-Seq method (uncorrected or bias-corrected) must be benchmarked against independently performed qRT-PCR measurements to quantify whether bias correction improved accuracy.
skills.name: qrt-pcr-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: qrt-pcr-correlation-analysis Use when expression estimates from an RNA-Seq method (uncorrected or bias-corrected) must be benchmarked against independently performed qRT-PCR measurements to quantify whether bias correction improved accuracy. No independent qRT-PCR (or equivalent) reference measurements exist for the sample, so correlation with a gold standard cannot be computed The goal is internal assessment of expression estimates without bias correction applied — a single uncorrected run leaves no corrected/uncorrected contrast to evaluate TaqMan probes do not map uniquely to transcripts, since the benchmark restricts to uniquely probed transcripts (907 on MAQC HBR) http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Validates RNA-Seq expression estimates (raw and bias-corrected) by computing squared Pearson correlation (R2) against independently measured qRT-PCR reference values, as done on the MAQC Human Brain Reference benchmark where Cufflinks improved from R2 = 0.753 to 0.807 and mseq/Genominator baselines reached 0.730/0.755 and 0.711/0.715. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Validates RNA-Seq expression estimates (raw and bias-corrected) by computing squared Pearson correlation (R2) against independently measured qRT-PCR reference values, as done on the MAQC Human Brain Reference benchmark where Cufflinks improved from R2 = 0.753 to 0.807 and mseq/Genominator baselines reached 0.730/0.755 and 0.711/0.715.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No independent qRT-PCR (or equivalent) reference measurements exist for the sample, so correlation with a gold standard cannot be computed The goal is internal assessment of expression estimates without bias correction applied — a single uncorrected run leaves no corrected/uncorrected contrast to evaluate TaqMan probes do not map uniquely to transcripts, since the benchmark restricts to uniquely probed transcripts (907 on MAQC HBR)

skills.description: Use when clustering a gene-by-sample transcriptomic matrix (e.g., FPKM RNA-seq) to discover stable tumor subgroups without predefining the number of clusters K, and when consensus/bootstrap clustering stability is in question.
skills.name: qt-clustering-of-transcriptomic-data
skills.search_text: qt-clustering-of-transcriptomic-data Use when clustering a gene-by-sample transcriptomic matrix (e.g., FPKM RNA-seq) to discover stable tumor subgroups without predefining the number of clusters K, and when consensus/bootstrap clustering stability is in question. The number of clusters K is fixed in advance and the task is only to assign samples — consensus clustering with predefined K is the comparison method here, not SRIQ's purpose The dataset is small and the goal is detecting small or underrepresented biological subgroups — the authors state SRIQ cannot circumvent this limitation A distance metric other than Pearson correlation or Euclidean distance is required — additional metrics are not yet implemented http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Apply SRIQ, a systematic random forest integration to quality threshold (QT) clustering that fuses Random Forest, QT clustering, and KNN concepts, to discover stable unsupervised cluster solutions in tumor gene expression data without predefining K, as demonstrated on 434 TCGA-LUAD cases with 25,785 transcripts. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: Apply SRIQ, a systematic random forest integration to quality threshold (QT) clustering that fuses Random Forest, QT clustering, and KNN concepts, to discover stable unsupervised cluster solutions in tumor gene expression data without predefining K, as demonstrated on 434 TCGA-LUAD cases with 25,785 transcripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The number of clusters K is fixed in advance and the task is only to assign samples — consensus clustering with predefined K is the comparison method here, not SRIQ's purpose The dataset is small and the goal is detecting small or underrepresented biological subgroups — the authors state SRIQ cannot circumvent this limitation A distance metric other than Pearson correlation or Euclidean distance is required — additional metrics are not yet implemented

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq narrowPeak samples (e.g. from a histone mark atlas) need a QC metric scored against ENCODE union DHS regions, or when reproducing Fig. 5 per-mark DHS overlap distributions.
skills.name: quality-atlas-benchmark-comparison
skills.search_text: quality-atlas-benchmark-comparison Use when ChIP-seq narrowPeak samples (e.g. from a histone mark atlas) need a QC metric scored against ENCODE union DHS regions, or when reproducing Fig. 5 per-mark DHS overlap distributions. Input peaks are from a non-ChIP-seq/DNase-seq assay (e.g. RNA-seq) or are unsorted/un-called reads rather than narrowPeak files, since the ratio is defined over called peaks. No genome-matched union DHS BED reference is available for the sample's assembly (hg19/hg38/mm9/mm10 dependent data), so the overlap ratio would be meaningless. The goal is general ChIP-seq QC (FRiP, PBC, NSC/RSC) rather than the DHS-overlap atlas benchmark specifically; ChiLin's other QC steps cover those metrics. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Computes per-sample union DNase hypersensitive site (DHS) overlap ratios from ChiLin peak calls and benchmarks them against the ChiLin quality atlas distributions across histone mark categories, verifying that acetylation marks show the expected high overlap pattern. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Computes per-sample union DNase hypersensitive site (DHS) overlap ratios from ChiLin peak calls and benchmarks them against the ChiLin quality atlas distributions across histone mark categories, verifying that acetylation marks show the expected high overlap pattern.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input peaks are from a non-ChIP-seq/DNase-seq assay (e.g. RNA-seq) or are unsorted/un-called reads rather than narrowPeak files, since the ratio is defined over called peaks. No genome-matched union DHS BED reference is available for the sample's assembly (hg19/hg38/mm9/mm10 dependent data), so the overlap ratio would be meaningless. The goal is general ChIP-seq QC (FRiP, PBC, NSC/RSC) rather than the DHS-overlap atlas benchmark specifically; ChiLin's other QC steps cover those metrics.

skills.description: Use when processing raw .ab1 BSP trace files where reads must be trimmed of low-quality ends and reads failing bisulfite conversion (non-CpG C-to-T conversion rate below 0.9) must be flagged before CpG methylation computation.
skills.name: quality-threshold-filtering-of-sequencing-reads
skills.search_text: quality-threshold-filtering-of-sequencing-reads Use when processing raw .ab1 BSP trace files where reads must be trimmed of low-quality ends and reads failing bisulfite conversion (non-CpG C-to-T conversion rate below 0.9) must be flagged before CpG methylation computation. Input is already trimmed, methylation-called data (e.g. a methylation percentage table) — filtering on .ab1 peak heights is unnecessary Data are bulk sequencing reads in FASTQ/BAM rather than Sanger-style .ab1 chromatogram traces from BSP experiments Only visualization or group-comparison of already-computed methylation percentages is needed — use the Grouped analysis tab instead of re-running per-read QC http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Applies ABSP's automated quality control to bisulfite sequencing PCR (.ab1) chromatogram reads: trimming reads by Phred quality scores and primary peak ratios, then accepting only reads whose bisulfite conversion rate over non-CpG cytosines exceeds a 0.9 threshold. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: Applies ABSP's automated quality control to bisulfite sequencing PCR (.ab1) chromatogram reads: trimming reads by Phred quality scores and primary peak ratios, then accepting only reads whose bisulfite conversion rate over non-CpG cytosines exceeds a 0.9 threshold.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already trimmed, methylation-called data (e.g. a methylation percentage table) — filtering on .ab1 peak heights is unnecessary Data are bulk sequencing reads in FASTQ/BAM rather than Sanger-style .ab1 chromatogram traces from BSP experiments Only visualization or group-comparison of already-computed methylation percentages is needed — use the Grouped analysis tab instead of re-running per-read QC

skills.description: Use when a supervised celltyping pipeline has produced first-round per-cell prediction probabilities for scATAC-seq target cells and a confident anchor subset is needed to train a second-round model.
skills.name: quantile-based-cell-filtering
skills.search_text: quantile-based-cell-filtering Use when a supervised celltyping pipeline has produced first-round per-cell prediction probabilities for scATAC-seq target cells and a confident anchor subset is needed to train a second-round model. When a scRNA-seq reference must be used for cross-modality label transfer — Cellcano's two-round entropy-anchored scheme is designed for scATAC-seq reference data; cross-modality adaptation is planned but not implemented. When the goal is joint dimensionality reduction or integration of reference and target datasets (as in Seurat, Signac, scJoint) — Cellcano explicitly avoids jointly operating on both datasets. When prediction probabilities from a first round are unavailable; the filter requires per-cell class-probability vectors to compute entropy. Selects anchor cells by ranking target cells on per-cell prediction entropy from a first-round classifier and keeping only those below an entropy quantile cutoff (Cellcano default 0.4), so that second-round training uses the most confidently labeled cells. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3
skills.summary: Selects anchor cells by ranking target cells on per-cell prediction entropy from a first-round classifier and keeping only those below an entropy quantile cutoff (Cellcano default 0.4), so that second-round training uses the most confidently labeled cells.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When a scRNA-seq reference must be used for cross-modality label transfer — Cellcano's two-round entropy-anchored scheme is designed for scATAC-seq reference data; cross-modality adaptation is planned but not implemented. When the goal is joint dimensionality reduction or integration of reference and target datasets (as in Seurat, Signac, scJoint) — Cellcano explicitly avoids jointly operating on both datasets. When prediction probabilities from a first round are unavailable; the filter requires per-cell class-probability vectors to compute entropy.

skills.description: Use when you have per-base translocation times from Tombo re-squiggled ONT reads and motif coordinates (e.g. non-B DNA DB hg38 annotations), and need to test which non-B structure classes show significant TT quantile deviations from B-DNA.
skills.name: quantile-deviation-visualization-across-structure-types
skills.search_text: quantile-deviation-visualization-across-structure-types Use when you have per-base translocation times from Tombo re-squiggled ONT reads and motif coordinates (e.g. non-B DNA DB hg38 annotations), and need to test which non-B structure classes show significant TT quantile deviations from B-DNA. Input is simulated translocation-time data at window_size = 50 rather than the experimental dataset at window_size = 100 — the window-fixing and control-selection steps differ The goal is non-B structure classification/prediction with GoFAE-DND rather than descriptive quantile-deviation comparison against B-DNA controls Motif coordinates come from a genome assembly other than hg38 or from motifs not in the non-B DNA DB, so windows cannot be matched to the Tombo-mapped reads http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reproduces the Fig. 4 analysis by computing per-window TT (translocation time) quantiles (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95) for 100 bp windows centred on non-B DNA motifs versus motif-free B-DNA controls, then quantifying and plotting the deviation of each non-B type from the B-DNA distribution. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Reproduces the Fig. 4 analysis by computing per-window TT (translocation time) quantiles (0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.95) for 100 bp windows centred on non-B DNA motifs versus motif-free B-DNA controls, then quantifying and plotting the deviation of each non-B type from the B-DNA distribution.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is simulated translocation-time data at window_size = 50 rather than the experimental dataset at window_size = 100 — the window-fixing and control-selection steps differ The goal is non-B structure classification/prediction with GoFAE-DND rather than descriptive quantile-deviation comparison against B-DNA controls Motif coordinates come from a genome assembly other than hg38 or from motifs not in the non-B DNA DB, so windows cannot be matched to the Tombo-mapped reads

skills.description: Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2 vectors) have been computed for multiple Hi-C datasets or replicates and must be made comparable across conditions prior to differential compartment analysis.
skills.name: quantile-normalization-of-compartment-scores
skills.search_text: quantile-normalization-of-compartment-scores Use when compartment scores (PC1/PC2 vectors) have been computed for multiple Hi-C datasets or replicates and must be made comparable across conditions prior to differential compartment analysis. Only a single Hi-C contact map is being analyzed and no cross-condition comparison of compartment scores is needed Compartment scores already come from a common normalized pipeline and distribution alignment would remove genuine between-condition score differences The goal is differential interaction (loop) calling (e.g., Fit-Hi-C-based analysis) rather than compartment score comparison http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 dcHiC applies quantile normalization to compartment scores (PC1/PC2 from a partial SVD) across two or more Hi-C contact maps/replicates so that scores are directly comparable before multivariate differential testing. This normalization is the bridge between per-map PCA and downstream Mahalanobis-distance significance calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: dcHiC applies quantile normalization to compartment scores (PC1/PC2 from a partial SVD) across two or more Hi-C contact maps/replicates so that scores are directly comparable before multivariate differential testing. This normalization is the bridge between per-map PCA and downstream Mahalanobis-distance significance calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only a single Hi-C contact map is being analyzed and no cross-condition comparison of compartment scores is needed Compartment scores already come from a common normalized pipeline and distribution alignment would remove genuine between-condition score differences The goal is differential interaction (loop) calling (e.g., Fit-Hi-C-based analysis) rather than compartment score comparison

skills.description: Use when combined significance scores from integrating multiple genomic/epigenomic p-value tracks show a spurious increasing trend with the number of component p-values per genomic interval, and the trend must be removed before scoring modules.
skills.name: quantile-permutation-pvalue-adjustment
skills.search_text: quantile-permutation-pvalue-adjustment Use when combined significance scores from integrating multiple genomic/epigenomic p-value tracks show a spurious increasing trend with the number of component p-values per genomic interval, and the trend must be removed before scoring modules. Component p-values are not yet annotated and combined into a PvalueAnnotation (run makePvalueAnnotation/annotateExpression/annotateModification/makePvalueObject first) The goal is module discovery or network scoring (scorePval/spinglass), not diagnosing or removing the number-of-p-values bias in combined significance http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 SMITE's normalizePval(method="rescale") adjustment removes the bias by which combined significance increases with the number of p-values combined per interval, by logit-transforming and rescaling each score against randomly sampled scores from the same quantile bin (illustrated in Fig. 3 of the SMITE paper). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: SMITE's normalizePval(method="rescale") adjustment removes the bias by which combined significance increases with the number of p-values combined per interval, by logit-transforming and rescaling each score against randomly sampled scores from the same quantile bin (illustrated in Fig. 3 of the SMITE paper).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Component p-values are not yet annotated and combined into a PvalueAnnotation (run makePvalueAnnotation/annotateExpression/annotateModification/makePvalueObject first) The goal is module discovery or network scoring (scorePval/spinglass), not diagnosing or removing the number-of-p-values bias in combined significance

skills.description: Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's mutation status (MUT) is associated with gene expression while correcting for copy number (SCNA) and tumour-type covariates, from per-sample quantification tables.
skills.name: quasi-poisson-glm-regression
skills.search_text: quasi-poisson-glm-regression Use when testing whether a candidate driver element's mutation status (MUT) is associated with gene expression while correcting for copy number (SCNA) and tumour-type covariates, from per-sample quantification tables. The task is driver-element identification itself — use DriverPower's model/infer subcommands on the burden/functional-feature tables instead; this skill only validates driver candidates at the expression level Expression data are raw counts appropriate to an exact Poisson model without overdispersion, or already normalized for a method requiring a different error family http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 Fit quasi-Poisson generalized linear models to overdispersed per-sample gene-expression counts (PCAWG FPKM-UQ) and compare full vs. null models via likelihood ratio testing, as used to test whether DriverPower-exclusive driver candidates (SGK1 in Lymph-BNHL, GPR126 in Bladder-TCC enhancer) are differentially expressed after copy-number correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1

Every query region maps directly with standard UCSC liftOver and only a 1:1 coordinate conversion is needed — plain liftOver/rtracklayer suffices without extension or scoring You need whole-genome synteny block mapping rather than high-resolution orthologous non-coding regulatory elements No UCSC chain file or matched orthologous functional genomic datasets are available for the species pair, so candidates cannot be generated or scored http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 AdaLiftOver's adaptive mapping strategy: when UCSC liftOver fails to map a query region directly between species (e.g. mm10 to hg38 via mm10.hg38.rbest.chain), the query region is extended with a local window on both sides and liftOver is re-applied to recover candidate target regions, which are then prioritized by epigenomic and sequence grammar similarity. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad149

skills.search_text: r-bioconductor-runtime-profiling Use when you must compare runtime of two genomic-range null-generation methods (bootRanges vs GSC) on identical GRanges inputs, e.g. ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks, to quantify a speedup factor on genome-scale statistics. The goal is the statistical validity of null distributions rather than speed — the paper shows permutation/shuffling schemes can produce overly narrow test statistic null distributions and over-estimate significance, which timing alone does not address. The input is not GRanges-style genomic ranges (e.g. an expression matrix or feature table) — bootRanges and GSC operate on genomic range sets. Only one method is of interest and no cross-method comparison or speedup factor is needed. Benchmark the wall-clock runtime of the R/Bioconductor bootRanges block bootstrapper against the GSC permutation-based shuffler on the same GRanges peak sets and hardware, quantifying the speedup of genome-scale null-range generation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190

Data are already normalized contact matrices (e.g. .hic format) rather than fragment-pair feature tables with coverage values — covNorm's input format is the fragment-pair data.frame, not matrices Inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions need analysis — the method focuses on cis-interactions only and inter-chromosomal interactions are filtered Very short-range contacts (under ~15 kb, putative self-ligations) are the target — these are removed by filtering http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 End-to-end Hi-C/capture Hi-C data processing with the covNorm R package, which performs negative binomial model-based coverage normalization, genomic distance-dependent background normalization, and significant interaction calling from fragment-pair feature tables. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: End-to-end Hi-C/capture Hi-C data processing with the covNorm R package, which performs negative binomial model-based coverage normalization, genomic distance-dependent background normalization, and significant interaction calling from fragment-pair feature tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are already normalized contact matrices (e.g. .hic format) rather than fragment-pair feature tables with coverage values — covNorm's input format is the fragment-pair data.frame, not matrices Inter-chromosomal (trans) interactions need analysis — the method focuses on cis-interactions only and inter-chromosomal interactions are filtered Very short-range contacts (under ~15 kb, putative self-ligations) are the target — these are removed by filtering

skills.description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend cola's -k selection logic in R code: you have per-k consensus matrices, individual partitions, and consensus partitions and must compute PAC/silhouette/concordance/Jaccard metrics to choose k.
skills.name: r-package-function-implementation
skills.search_text: r-package-function-implementation Use when you need to reproduce or extend cola's -k selection logic in R code: you have per-k consensus matrices, individual partitions, and consensus partitions and must compute PAC/silhouette/concordance/Jaccard metrics to choose k. You need to run the full consensus partitioning pipeline itself (matrix adjustment with adjust_matrix(), top-value feature selection, scaling) rather than score already-produced per-k consensus results The dataset is scRNA-Seq with several thousands of cells, where the article warns cola's runtime and memory usage 'might not be acceptable' There is no consensus matrix or multiple individual partitions per k, so PAC and concordance cannot be defined http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Implement R functions that recompute cola's per-k consensus-partitioning evaluation metrics — 1-PAC (after excluding the 5% most unstable samples), mean silhouette, partition-concordance, and Jaccard index between consecutive k — and apply cola's three-rule best-k selection procedure. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1146
skills.summary: Implement R functions that recompute cola's per-k consensus-partitioning evaluation metrics — 1-PAC (after excluding the 5% most unstable samples), mean silhouette, partition-concordance, and Jaccard index between consecutive k — and apply cola's three-rule best-k selection procedure.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to run the full consensus partitioning pipeline itself (matrix adjustment with adjust_matrix(), top-value feature selection, scaling) rather than score already-produced per-k consensus results The dataset is scRNA-Seq with several thousands of cells, where the article warns cola's runtime and memory usage 'might not be acceptable' There is no consensus matrix or multiple individual partitions per k, so PAC and concordance cannot be defined

skills.description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster assignments needs automated cell type annotation via an R package pipeline (e.g., scCATCH with CellMatch), following the article's documented function sequence.

skills.search_text: r-package-pipeline-execution Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster assignments needs automated cell type annotation via an R package pipeline (e.g., scCATCH with CellMatch), following the article's documented function sequence. Input is not clustered scRNA-seq data (e.g., already-annotated cells or bulk RNA-seq) — the pipeline requires cluster-level input via createscCATCH Species markers outside human/mouse are needed without adapting the cellmatch reference — the standard database covers 2,096 human and mouse references Marker-gene identification rather than cell type annotation is the goal — Seurat's one-against-all approach or other marker tools may be more appropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Executes an R package's documented two-function pipeline (here scCATCH's findmarkergene() then findcelltype()) end-to-end on a single-cell RNA-seq dataset to produce automatic cell type annotations per cluster, reproducing the article's reported workflow and consistency metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Executes an R package's documented two-function pipeline (here scCATCH's findmarkergene() then findcelltype()) end-to-end on a single-cell RNA-seq dataset to produce automatic cell type annotations per cluster, reproducing the article's reported workflow and consistency metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not clustered scRNA-seq data (e.g., already-annotated cells or bulk RNA-seq) — the pipeline requires cluster-level input via createscCATCH Species markers outside human/mouse are needed without adapting the cellmatch reference — the standard database covers 2,096 human and mouse references Marker-gene identification rather than cell type annotation is the goal — Seurat's one-against-all approach or other marker tools may be more appropriate

skills.description: Use when you need to analyze multiple structural variants (e.g. a patient cohort or benchmark set) with POSTRE beyond the online single-SV interface, by scripting POSTRE_multiSV() in R (>=3.5.0).
skills.name: r-scripted-batch-sv-analysis
skills.search_text: r-scripted-batch-sv-analysis Use when you need to analyze multiple structural variants (e.g. a patient cohort or benchmark set) with POSTRE beyond the online single-SV interface, by scripting POSTRE_multiSV() in R (>=3.5.0). You only need a single-SV analysis without scripting — the online version at postre-tool.csic.es supports Single SV submissions and avoids local installation The SVs are implicated in recessive phenotypes — POSTRE is oriented towards prediction of SVs causing dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated SV coordinates are not in hg19 and cannot be lifted — the POSTRE_multiSV() mandatory argument requires hg19 coordinates http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Runs POSTRE programmatically in R for sequential analysis of multiple structural variants, using the POSTRE_multiSV() function instead of the Shiny GUI. This enables batch pathogenicity prediction of coding and long-range (enhancer-driven) SV pathomechanisms in a cell type/tissue-specific manner. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Runs POSTRE programmatically in R for sequential analysis of multiple structural variants, using the POSTRE_multiSV() function instead of the Shiny GUI. skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a single-SV analysis without scripting — the online version at postre-tool.csic.es supports Single SV submissions and avoids local installation The SVs are implicated in recessive phenotypes — POSTRE is oriented towards prediction of SVs causing dominant disorders and its capacity for recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated SV coordinates are not in hg19 and cannot be lifted — the POSTRE_multiSV() mandatory argument requires hg19 coordinates

skills.search_text: r-squared-goodness-of-fit-assessment Use when a parametric model (e.g. scPower expression probability model) yields numeric predictions that must be validated against observed values across controlled conditions such as sequencing-depth subsampling of count matrices. When the goal is experimental design optimization (budget-constrained parameter search with scPower) rather than validating model predictions against observed data When predicted and observed values are not paired across comparable conditions (e.g. a single sample with no read-depth series), making r2 over conditions meaningless When input data are not scRNA-seq count matrices with matching cell-type annotations (e.g. feature tables or bulk RNA-seq without a pseudobulk aggregation step) http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Quantifies agreement between model-predicted and observed quantities by computing the r-squared across paired conditions — here, scPower-estimated expressed gene numbers versus observed expressed gene counts from subsampled 10X PBMC UMI count matrices at different read depths. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Quantifies agreement between model-predicted and observed quantities by computing the r-squared across paired conditions — here, scPower-estimated expressed gene numbers versus observed expressed gene counts from subsampled 10X PBMC UMI count matrices at different read depths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is experimental design optimization (budget-constrained parameter search with scPower) rather than validating model predictions against observed data When predicted and observed values are not paired across comparable conditions (e.g. a single sample with no read-depth series), making r2 over conditions meaningless When input data are not scRNA-seq count matrices with matching cell-type annotations (e.g. feature tables or bulk RNA-seq without a pseudobulk aggregation step)

skills.description: Use when running or reconstructing the QC step of the NEAT NGS pipeline on truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq FASTQ test data, and per-cycle quality and read-distribution reports are required.
skills.name: r-systempiper-workflow-execution
skills.search_text: r-systempiper-workflow-execution Use when running or reconstructing the QC step of the NEAT NGS pipeline on truncated H3K4me3 ChIPseq or RNAseq FASTQ test data, and per-cycle quality and read-distribution reports are required. Input is already aligned or post-QC (e.g. BAM files) — the QC module operates on decompressed FASTQ reads in the 'fatsq' folder. The pipeline has not yet run the 'unzip' module, so FASTQ files are still compressed and unrenamed in the project folder. A numeric quality threshold must be enforced as an acceptance criterion — the NEAT paper explicitly reports no numeric QC threshold, only output existence/completeness. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3577 Execute the quality-control step of the NEAT ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline, which is implemented with the R/Bioconductor systemPipeR package and exposed to users as a double-clickable, automated module that produces human-readable PDF QC reports. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Execute the quality-control step of the NEAT ChIPseq/RNAseq pipeline, which is implemented with the R/Bioconductor systemPipeR package and exposed to users as a double-clickable, automated module that produces human-readable PDF QC reports.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already aligned or post-QC (e.g. BAM files) — the QC module operates on decompressed FASTQ reads in the 'fatsq' folder. The pipeline has not yet run the 'unzip' module, so FASTQ files are still compressed and unrenamed in the project folder. A numeric quality threshold must be enforced as an acceptance criterion — the NEAT paper explicitly reports no numeric QC threshold, only output existence/completeness.

skills.description: Decision support for choosing among MethylCal's four random-effects model specifications (equations 2-5) for a methylation calibration assay when standard-control data at known methylation percentages are available and goodness-of-fit comparison via DIC is required.
skills.name: random-effects-model-specification-methylation
skills.search_text: random-effects-model-specification-methylation Decision support for choosing among MethylCal's four random-effects model specifications (equations 2-5) for a methylation calibration assay when standard-control data at known methylation percentages are available and goodness-of-fit comparison via DIC is required. The goal is calibration of case/control methylation levels using an already-selected model — use MethylCalCorrection/MethycalCorrection rather than re-running model selection The data are single-CpG or average-methylation calibration problems, which MethylCal explicitly avoids ('one-at-a-time' CpG calibration); this skill requires joint analysis across all CpGs of a CGI/DMR Comparison against alternative calibration methods (Warnecke 1997, Moskalev 2011) is the goal — those use WarneckeCalibrationPlot or MoskalevCalibrationPlot, not the M1-M4 random-effects specifications http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Selects the best-fitting MethylCal random-effects regression specification (AMP effects, crossed CpG effects, RW1 latent Gaussian field, or random CpG intercepts/slopes) for each bisulfite amplicon-sequencing assay by comparing Deviance Information Criterion values across the four candidate models fitted jointly to all CpGs of a CGI/DMR. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz325
skills.summary: Selects the best-fitting MethylCal random-effects regression specification (AMP effects, crossed CpG effects, RW1 latent Gaussian field, or random CpG intercepts/slopes) for each bisulfite amplicon-sequencing assay by comparing Deviance Information Criterion values across the four candidate models fitted jointly to all CpGs of a CGI/DMR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is calibration of case/control methylation levels using an already-selected model — use MethylCalCorrection/MethycalCorrection rather than re-running model selection The data are single-CpG or average-methylation calibration problems, which MethylCal explicitly avoids ('one-at-a-time' CpG calibration); this skill requires joint analysis across all CpGs of a CGI/DMR Comparison against alternative calibration methods (Warnecke 1997, Moskalev 2011) is the goal — those use WarneckeCalibrationPlot or MoskalevCalibrationPlot, not the M1-M4 random-effects specifications

skills.description: Use when the goal is to predict or reproduce TF-DNA binding affinities from experimental intensity/enrichment data (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) using structural/mechanical DNA features rather than sequence-only models.

skills.search_text: random-forest-binding-prediction Use when the goal is to predict or reproduce TF-DNA binding affinities from experimental intensity/enrichment data (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX) using structural/mechanical DNA features rather than sequence-only models. The input is already a trained model output or feature table rather than raw experimental affinity/intensity data requiring regression The task is in vivo binding site identification without accompanying chromatin structure data — DNAffinity alone predicts many potential sites with no experimental in vivo binding evidence and needs nucleosome positioning maps for in vivo TFBS localization Sequence-only deep learning is preferred and structural/mechanical DNA features from MD simulations are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Train a random forest regressor on DNA equilibrium-geometry and flexibility features derived from atomistic MD simulations to reproduce in vitro transcription factor binding affinities (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX), yielding R2-scored per-protein affinity predictions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Train a random forest regressor on DNA equilibrium-geometry and flexibility features derived from atomistic MD simulations to reproduce in vitro transcription factor binding affinities (gcPBM, uPBM, HT-SELEX), yielding R2-scored per-protein affinity predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a trained model output or feature table rather than raw experimental affinity/intensity data requiring regression The task is in vivo binding site identification without accompanying chromatin structure data — DNAffinity alone predicts many potential sites with no experimental in vivo binding evidence and needs nucleosome positioning maps for in vivo TFBS localization Sequence-only deep learning is preferred and structural/mechanical DNA features from MD simulations are unavailable

Input data lacks the required ChIP-seq marks (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) or DNase-seq — the model cannot score bins without these signals Analysis goal is general peak calling or motif identification rather than enhancer element prediction (use CIPHER's standard ChIP-seq or DNase-seq pipelines instead) Non-model organism genomes without suitable ENCODE-derived enhancer training data for the random-forest model http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Applies CIPHER's trained random-forest enhancer prediction model (R randomForest package) to classify 200-bp genomic bins as enhancer or non-enhancer, using ChIP-seq (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) and DNase-seq signals, achieving ~93% accuracy against ENCODE enhancer training data. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1770-1

skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data lacks the required ChIP-seq marks (H3K4me1, H3K4me3, H3K27ac) or DNase-seq — the model cannot score bins without these signals Analysis goal is general peak calling or motif identification rather than enhancer element prediction (use CIPHER's standard ChIP-seq or DNase-seq pipelines instead) Non-model organism genomes without suitable ENCODE-derived enhancer training data for the random-forest model

skills.search_text: random-forest-cross-validation-evaluation Use when comparing feature subsets or classifiers for DNA 6mA sequence prediction on 41nt sequences and you need cross-validated AUC estimates (e.g. Binary vs Motif+Kmer+Binary) before freezing a feature matrix. skills.description: Use when predicting TF binding affinities from uPBM (35-mer oligos), gcPBM, or HT-SELEX datasets with a random forest over MD-derived DNA shape/flexibility features rather than sequence-only CNNs like DeepBind.
skills.name: random-forest-dna-affinity-regression
skills.search_text: random-forest-dna-affinity-regression Use when predicting TF binding affinities from uPBM (35-mer oligos), gcPBM, or HT-SELEX datasets with a random forest over MD-derived DNA shape/flexibility features rather than sequence-only CNNs like DeepBind. Input is raw sequences without experimental affinity labels — the regressor requires a `*_training.txt` file pairing k-mers with measured affinities. HT-SELEX data displays inconsistency between enrichments at different cycles — apply the SVM filtering step first instead of training on suspicious cases. Goal is in vivo TFBS prediction without chromatin context — the paper warns that factors beyond intrinsic TF affinity operate in vivo, so predictions must be complemented with nucleosome positioning maps. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 Train a random forest regressor on MD-derived DNA equilibrium geometry and flexibility parameters (base-pair step resolution) to reproduce in vitro transcription factor binding affinities from uPBM, gcPBM, or HT-SELEX data, evaluating the determination coefficient (R2) on a held-out 20% of each dataset. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Train a random forest regressor on MD-derived DNA equilibrium geometry and flexibility parameters (base-pair step resolution) to reproduce in vitro transcription factor binding affinities from uPBM, gcPBM, or HT-SELEX data, evaluating the determination coefficient (R2) on a held-out 20% of each dataset.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequences without experimental affinity labels — the regressor requires a `*_training.txt` file pairing k-mers with measured affinities. HT-SELEX data displays inconsistency between enrichments at different cycles — apply the SVM filtering step first instead of training on suspicious cases. Goal is in vivo TFBS prediction without chromatin context — the paper warns that factors beyond intrinsic TF affinity operate in vivo, so predictions must be complemented with nucleosome positioning maps.

skills.name: random-forest-model-training-hic
skills.search_text: random-forest-model-training-hic Use when a 10 kb-binned contact map (.cool or .hic) and a positive interaction list (bedpe from ChIA-PET, HiChIP, or annotated loops) are available and supervised chromatin loop detection is needed. The input is a contact map from a platform with no binned 10 kb matrix or no orthogonal positive interaction set available for training The goal is de novo statistical peak calling rather than supervised loop classification — enrichment-based tools (HiCCUPS, Fit-Hi-C, MAPS, CHiCAGO) are the comparison baselines here, not the method being trained The contact map resolution differs substantially from 10 kb and rescaling/rebinning cannot be performed, since models are fit at 10 kb binning (default -r 10000) http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train chromosome-wise Peakachu Random Forest classifiers that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loops in 10 kb-binned genome-wide contact maps (.cool/.hic), using positive interaction sets (e.g. CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe) and negative randomly sampled contacts, to enable platform-agnostic loop prediction across Hi-C, Micro-C, and DNA SPRITE. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Train chromosome-wise Peakachu Random Forest classifiers that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loops in 10 kb-binned genome-wide contact maps (.cool/.hic), using positive interaction sets (e.g. CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe) and negative randomly sampled contacts, to enable platform-agnostic loop prediction across Hi-C, Micro-C, and DNA SPRITE.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a contact map from a platform with no binned 10 kb matrix or no orthogonal positive interaction set available for training The goal is de novo statistical peak calling rather than supervised loop classification — enrichment-based tools (HiCCUPS, Fit-Hi-C, MAPS, CHiCAGO) are the comparison baselines here, not the method being trained The contact map resolution differs substantially from 10 kb and rescaling/rebinning cannot be performed, since models are fit at 10 kb binning (default -r 10000)

skills.description: Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool or .hic Hi-C matrix and a bedpe list of positive interactions (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need chromosome-wise random forest models for loop prediction.
skills.name: random-forest-model-training-on-3c-derived-interactions
skills.search_text: random-forest-model-training-on-3c-derived-interactions Use when you have a 10 kb-binned .cool or .hic Hi-C matrix and a bedpe list of positive interactions (ChIA-PET, HiChIP, Capture Hi-C) and need chromosome-wise random forest models for loop prediction. You only need per-pixel loop probabilities or pooled loop calls and already possess trained models — use peakachu score_genome plus pool instead of retraining. The input contact matrix is raw without a balancing weight column and you cannot compute ICE weights — specify '--clr-weight-name raw' consciously or fix balancing first, since the workflow assumes 'weight' normalization. The positive interaction set is not from an orthogonal genome-wide assay mapped to the same genome build/resolution as the contact map (e.g., a small hand-curated list unrelated to the organism or assembly). http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Train per-chromosome Peakachu random forest models that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loop contacts in a Hi-C contact map, using orthogonal 3C-derived interactions (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe files) as the positive training set. This is the supervised-learning core of Peakachu's loop-detection framework. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Train per-chromosome Peakachu random forest models that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loop contacts in a Hi-C contact map, using orthogonal 3C-derived interactions (e.g., CTCF ChIA-PET or H3K27ac HiChIP bedpe files) as the positive training set. This is the supervised-learning core of Peakachu's loop-detection framework.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need per-pixel loop probabilities or pooled loop calls and already possess trained models — use peakachu score_genome plus pool instead of retraining. The input contact matrix is raw without a balancing weight column and you cannot compute ICE weights — specify '--clr-weight-name raw' consciously or fix balancing first, since the workflow assumes 'weight' normalization. The positive interaction set is not from an orthogonal genome-wide assay mapped to the same genome build/resolution as the contact map (e.g., a small hand-curated list unrelated to the organism or assembly).

skills.description: Use when you have a .cool or .hic genome-wide contact map and an orthogonal positive interaction set (e.g. HiChIP/ChIA-PET bedpe) and need supervised loop classifiers for genome-wide prediction.
skills.name: random-forest-model-training-per-chromosome
skills.search_text: random-forest-model-training-per-chromosome Use when you have a .cool or .hic genome-wide contact map and an orthogonal positive interaction set (e.g. HiChIP/ChIA-PET bedpe) and need supervised loop classifiers for genome-wide prediction. You have no orthogonal positive interaction set (HiChIP, ChIA-PET, or manually annotated loops) — training requires a positive training list in bedpe format The contact map is not binned (resolution is unknown or far from 10 kb) — the framework requires a Hi-C matrix binned to 10 kb You only need generic statistical peak enrichment rather than supervised loop classification — enrichment-based tools like Fit-Hi-C or HiCCUPS do not require training data http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train chromosome-labeled random forest classifiers (Peakachu) that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loop pixels using a 10 kb-binned Hi-C contact matrix and a positive interaction list in bedpe format, with a chromosome-wise train/hold-out split to avoid overfitting. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Train chromosome-labeled random forest classifiers (Peakachu) that distinguish chromatin loops from non-loop pixels using a 10 kb-binned Hi-C contact matrix and a positive interaction list in bedpe format, with a chromosome-wise train/hold-out split to avoid overfitting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have no orthogonal positive interaction set (HiChIP, ChIA-PET, or manually annotated loops) — training requires a positive training list in bedpe format The contact map is not binned (resolution is unknown or far from 10 kb) — the framework requires a Hi-C matrix binned to 10 kb You only need generic statistical peak enrichment rather than supervised loop classification — enrichment-based tools like Fit-Hi-C or HiCCUPS do not require training data

skills.description: Use when clustering high-dimensional tumor gene expression data (e.g., RNA-seq FPKM matrices) into stable, reproducible subgroups without predefining K, and when consensus clustering overfits due to the curse of dimensionality.
skills.name: random-forest-proximity-based-clustering
skills.search_text: random-forest-proximity-based-clustering Use when clustering high-dimensional tumor gene expression data (e.g., RNA-seq FPKM matrices) into stable, reproducible subgroups without predefining K, and when consensus clustering overfits due to the curse of dimensionality. Input is single-cell sequencing or epigenomic data — the pipeline is not yet applied to these data types The dataset is small and the goal is detecting small or underrepresented biological subgroups — SRIQ cannot circumvent this limitation The analysis requires distance metrics beyond Pearson correlation or Euclidean distance, which are the only implemented options http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 SRIQ clustering fuses Random Forest, quality threshold (QT) clustering, and KNN concepts to find core clusters of highly correlated observations and spirals out to build larger clusters, self-evaluating solution stability without a predefined K. Applied to 434 TCGA-LUAD cases with 25,785 transcripts, it identifies stable transcriptional subgroups with recurrence, QSS, and silhouette metrics. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: SRIQ clustering fuses Random Forest, quality threshold (QT) clustering, and KNN concepts to find core clusters of highly correlated observations and spirals out to build larger clusters, self-evaluating solution stability without a predefined K. Applied to 434 TCGA-LUAD cases with 25,785 transcripts, it identifies stable transcriptional subgroups with recurrence, QSS, and silhouette metrics.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell sequencing or epigenomic data — the pipeline is not yet applied to these data types The dataset is small and the goal is detecting small or underrepresented biological subgroups — SRIQ cannot circumvent this limitation The analysis requires distance metrics beyond Pearson correlation or Euclidean distance, which are the only implemented options

skills.description: Use when k-mer binding data (e.g. HT-SELEX penultimate-cycle affinities, uPBM/gcPBM intensities) must be converted into per-protein affinity predictions via regression on MD-derived DNA shape features, with R2/Pearson/MSE evaluation.
skills.name: random-forest-regressor-training
skills.search_text: random-forest-regressor-training Use when k-mer binding data (e.g. HT-SELEX penultimate-cycle affinities, uPBM/gcPBM intensities) must be converted into per-protein affinity predictions via regression on MD-derived DNA shape features, with R2/Pearson/MSE evaluation. Input is raw sequencing reads or unprocessed peak data — the regressor requires preprocessed, template-formatted affinity/k-mer training files The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than affinity regression on already-quantified binding data http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train a random forest regressor on DNA physical-property features (equilibrium geometry and flexibility from MD simulations) to predict transcription factor binding affinities from in vitro datasets such as HT-SELEX, uPBM, and gcPBM, as implemented in DNAffinity. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Train a random forest regressor on DNA physical-property features (equilibrium geometry and flexibility from MD simulations) to predict transcription factor binding affinities from in vitro datasets such as HT-SELEX, uPBM, and gcPBM, as implemented in DNAffinity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sequencing reads or unprocessed peak data — the regressor requires preprocessed, template-formatted affinity/k-mer training files The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than affinity regression on already-quantified binding data

skills.description: Use when building the RF component of an iPro-WAEL-style promoter classifier and you need to empirically select the number of trees via cross-validated grid search over promoter training sequences.
skills.name: random-forest-tree-number-tuning
skills.search_text: random-forest-tree-number-tuning Use when building the RF component of an iPro-WAEL-style promoter classifier and you need to empirically select the number of trees via cross-validated grid search over promoter training sequences. Input is already a set of trained iPro-WAEL component models with fixed hyperparameters (the 'model' folder provides trained models for validation, not re-tuning) The goal is tuning the CNN component (learning rate, kernel number, kernel size) rather than the RF tree number Working with the enhancer-vs-promoter discrimination task or cross-cell-line evaluation where the goal is applying, not optimizing, the RF component http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Grid-search optimization of the random forest tree count (n_estimators) for the iPro-WAEL promoter-prediction RF component, as demonstrated on the GM12878 cell line where 300 trees was identified as the best configuration. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac824
skills.summary: Grid-search optimization of the random forest tree count (n_estimators) for the iPro-WAEL promoter-prediction RF component, as demonstrated on the GM12878 cell line where 300 trees was identified as the best configuration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a set of trained iPro-WAEL component models with fixed hyperparameters (the 'model' folder provides trained models for validation, not re-tuning) The goal is tuning the CNN component (learning rate, kernel number, kernel size) rather than the RF tree number Working with the enhancer-vs-promoter discrimination task or cross-cell-line evaluation where the goal is applying, not optimizing, the RF component

skills.search_text: random-sample-subsetting-of-expression-cohorts Use when assessing how stable an unsupervised clustering solution (e.g., SRIQ K3/K5/K6 on 434 TCGA LUAD samples) is to cohort-size reduction, alongside BagSize reduction tests. When the goal is to test parameter sensitivity rather than cohort-size sensitivity — use the BagSize stepwise reduction (1100 down to 300) test instead When the biological question is differential expression or pathway analysis of established clusters (SAM one-versus-rest, EnrichR), not reproducibility testing When the dataset is too small to begin with — the article notes SRIQ cannot circumvent small datasets limiting detection of small or underrepresented subgroups http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 A technical reproducibility test for SRIQ clustering in which the cohort size is perturbed by randomly removing an increasing fraction of the original samples while keeping all other parameters intact, then comparing perturbed cluster solutions to the original run. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
