skills.description: Use when individual single-cell Hi-C contact files are too sparse for direct loop detection and normalized per-cell contact probabilities at 10-kb resolution must be imputed before statistical testing.
skills.name: random-walk-restart-contact-imputation
skills.search_text: random-walk-restart-contact-imputation Use when individual single-cell Hi-C contact files are too sparse for direct loop detection and normalized per-cell contact probabilities at 10-kb resolution must be imputed before statistical testing. Input data is bulk Hi-C or pooled contacts where per-cell imputation is unnecessary and standard loop callers like Juicer HiCCUPS suffice Bins or regions fall in the excluded filter file (mappability <=0.8 or ENCODE blacklist overlaps), where imputed values should not drive loop calling Memory-constrained environments cannot host the chromosome-sized matrix inversion and the sliding_window approximation is unacceptable for the analysis http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Imputes per-cell contact probabilities in single-cell Hi-C by solving the random walk with restart (RWR) equation over a 10-kb binned contact matrix per chromosome, densifying extremely sparse single-cell data so loop calling becomes statistically tractable. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Imputes per-cell contact probabilities in single-cell Hi-C by solving the random walk with restart (RWR) equation over a 10-kb binned contact matrix per chromosome, densifying extremely sparse single-cell data so loop calling becomes statistically tractable.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is bulk Hi-C or pooled contacts where per-cell imputation is unnecessary and standard loop callers like Juicer HiCCUPS suffice Bins or regions fall in the excluded filter file (mappability <=0.8 or ENCODE blacklist overlaps), where imputed values should not drive loop calling Memory-constrained environments cannot host the chromosome-sized matrix inversion and the sliding_window approximation is unacceptable for the analysis

skills.description: Use when a Hi-C contact matrix is extremely sparse (e.g., 0.025% downsampled or single-cell data) and needs imputation prior to structural-entropy TLD detection.
skills.name: random-walk-with-restart-imputation
skills.search_text: random-walk-with-restart-imputation Use when a Hi-C contact matrix is extremely sparse (e.g., 0.025% downsampled or single-cell data) and needs imputation prior to structural-entropy TLD detection. When running deDoc2 on bulk or reasonably dense Hi-C data — deDoc2 'decodes TLD from single-cell Hi-C data with no need of data imputation', and the paper reports it is robust to various imputation algorithms When the goal is TLD detection itself rather than matrix preprocessing — RWR here is only an optional imputation step, not the domain caller http://edamontology.org/topic_3922 Optional preprocessing module of deDoc2 that imputes sparse single-cell or downsampled Hi-C contact matrices via random walk with restart (RWR) before TLD prediction, controlled by the -rwr flag and the -rp restart probability (default 0.5). epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Optional preprocessing module of deDoc2 that imputes sparse single-cell or downsampled Hi-C contact matrices via random walk with restart (RWR) before TLD prediction, controlled by the -rwr flag and the -rp restart probability (default 0.5).
skills.when_to_use_negative: When running deDoc2 on bulk or reasonably dense Hi-C data — deDoc2 'decodes TLD from single-cell Hi-C data with no need of data imputation', and the paper reports it is robust to various imputation algorithms When the goal is TLD detection itself rather than matrix preprocessing — RWR here is only an optional imputation step, not the domain caller

skills.description: Use when training a GLM BMR model in DriverPower from high-dimensional genomic feature tables (e.g. train_feature.hdf5 with 1373 features) and a mutation-count response table, to discard uninformative features before fitting.
skills.name: randomized-lasso-feature-selection
skills.search_text: randomized-lasso-feature-selection Use when training a GLM BMR model in DriverPower from high-dimensional genomic feature tables (e.g. train_feature.hdf5 with 1373 features) and a mutation-count response table, to discard uninformative features before fitting. The goal is to fit the GBM background model — GBM training uses 5-fold cross-validated XGBoost models with poisson deviance objective and does not use randomized lasso feature selection You are at the 'driverpower infer' stage with an already-trained model; feature selection applies only to the 'model' sub-command The input is raw somatic mutations rather than a processed training feature table; run prepare.py and build the feature/response tables first http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Feature-selection step within DriverPower's GLM background mutation rate (BMR) modelling, where randomized lasso ranks genomic features and only those with importance score >= the --featImpCut cutoff (default 0.5) are retained in the generalized linear model. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Feature-selection step within DriverPower's GLM background mutation rate (BMR) modelling, where randomized lasso ranks genomic features and only those with importance score >= the --featImpCut cutoff (default 0.5) are retained in the generalized linear model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to fit the GBM background model — GBM training uses 5-fold cross-validated XGBoost models with poisson deviance objective and does not use randomized lasso feature selection You are at the 'driverpower infer' stage with an already-trained model; feature selection applies only to the 'model' sub-command The input is raw somatic mutations rather than a processed training feature table; run prepare.py and build the feature/response tables first

skills.description: Use when computing horizontal or vertical alignment scores over chromatin state sequences (e.g. EpiAlign on Roadmap 500 kb regions) and raw scores need a null baseline to separate real from randomized signal.
skills.name: randomized-sequence-negative-control
skills.search_text: randomized-sequence-negative-control Use when computing horizontal or vertical alignment scores over chromatin state sequences (e.g. EpiAlign on Roadmap 500 kb regions) and raw scores need a null baseline to separate real from randomized signal. Input data are raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than discrete chromatin state sequences — ChromHMM annotation (e.g. 15-state model on Roadmap data) must precede this control. The comparison targets cross-sample biology (e.g. cell-type grouping or gene-level vertical alignment between male/female samples with Wilcoxon tests) where a randomized null is not the stated normalization design in the article. Sequences are uncompressed — long quiescent stretches dominate alignment and, per the paper's benchmark, uncompressed alignment fails to distinguish real chromosomes from randomized controls. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 A normalization/negative-control procedure from EpiAlign in which each query chromatin state sequence is aligned to randomized chromatin state sequences, so that raw horizontal alignment scores can be interpreted relative to a null distribution and real epigenomes distinguished from random ones. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: A normalization/negative-control procedure from EpiAlign in which each query chromatin state sequence is aligned to randomized chromatin state sequences, so that raw horizontal alignment scores can be interpreted relative to a null distribution and real epigenomes distinguished from random ones.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data are raw multi-track epigenomic signal matrices rather than discrete chromatin state sequences — ChromHMM annotation (e.g. 15-state model on Roadmap data) must precede this control. The comparison targets cross-sample biology (e.g. cell-type grouping or gene-level vertical alignment between male/female samples with Wilcoxon tests) where a randomized null is not the stated normalization design in the article. Sequences are uncompressed — long quiescent stretches dominate alignment and, per the paper's benchmark, uncompressed alignment fails to distinguish real chromosomes from randomized controls.

skills.description: Use when computing or consuming EpiRegio Cell type scores from GeneQuery REM tables and you must verify normalization: every score in [-1, 1] and absolute scores per gene per cell type summing to 1.
skills.name: range-validation-of-computed-scores
skills.search_text: range-validation-of-computed-scores Use when computing or consuming EpiRegio Cell type scores from GeneQuery REM tables and you must verify normalization: every score in [-1, 1] and absolute scores per gene per cell type summing to 1. Input REM annotations are already pre-normalized Cell type scores (e.g. downloaded directly as scored output) rather than raw regression coefficients and DNase1 signals The goal is motif enrichment or TF target-gene identification (PASTAA, ChIP-seq peak overlap), not verifying score normalization REMs have no associated cell-type-resolved DNase1 signal, so the linear-model normalization cannot be computed Validates that EpiRegio Cell type scores, computed as normalized per-REM contributions (regressionCoefficient beta_r * standardized DNase1 signal) to a target gene's expression, fall within [-1, 1] and that absolute scores of all REMs of a gene sum to 1 per cell type. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Validates that EpiRegio Cell type scores, computed as normalized per-REM contributions (regressionCoefficient beta_r * standardized DNase1 signal) to a target gene's expression, fall within [-1, 1] and that absolute scores of all REMs of a gene sum to 1 per cell type.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input REM annotations are already pre-normalized Cell type scores (e.g. downloaded directly as scored output) rather than raw regression coefficients and DNase1 signals The goal is motif enrichment or TF target-gene identification (PASTAA, ChIP-seq peak overlap), not verifying score normalization REMs have no associated cell-type-resolved DNase1 signal, so the linear-model normalization cannot be computed

skills.description: Use when candidate cis genes from SCNA/gene-expression integrative analysis must be prioritized by their trans mediation signal, and the pruned Rank-1 lists need in silico validation against known driver databases.
skills.name: rank1-driver-pruning-fdr-thresholding
skills.search_text: rank1-driver-pruning-fdr-thresholding Use when candidate cis genes from SCNA/gene-expression integrative analysis must be prioritized by their trans mediation signal, and the pruned Rank-1 lists need in silico validation against known driver databases. Transgenes are not defined or downstream trans effects cannot be measured — mediation ranking of cis genes requires trans gene-expression signatures Sample size is small or copy-number/gene-expression correlations are weak — the Sobel test only achieved high AUC under adequate sample size and strong correlation effects The goal is cataloguing all cis genes within an alteration rather than prioritizing drivers (tools like GISTIC2.0 that only consider genes within the alterations) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Ranks iEDGE cis candidate drivers by Sobel statistical mediation of trans gene-expression effects and retains only the Rank-1 (top FDR, e.g. prune.thres=0.05) driver per cancer type, then validates the pruned list by hypergeometric enrichment against known cancer driver compendia. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Ranks iEDGE cis candidate drivers by Sobel statistical mediation of trans gene-expression effects and retains only the Rank-1 (top FDR, e.g. prune.thres=0.05) driver per cancer type, then validates the pruned list by hypergeometric enrichment against known cancer driver compendia.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Transgenes are not defined or downstream trans effects cannot be measured — mediation ranking of cis genes requires trans gene-expression signatures Sample size is small or copy-number/gene-expression correlations are weak — the Sobel test only achieved high AUC under adequate sample size and strong correlation effects The goal is cataloguing all cis genes within an alteration rather than prioritizing drivers (tools like GISTIC2.0 that only consider genes within the alterations)

skills.description: Use when two or more tools output ranked TR lists for the same query region sets (e.g., TR perturbation-derived DARs or cancer-type-specific accessible regions) and you need pairwise top-k list agreement via Jaccard indices.
skills.name: ranked-transcription-factor-list-overlap-analysis
skills.search_text: ranked-transcription-factor-list-overlap-analysis Use when two or more tools output ranked TR lists for the same query region sets (e.g., TR perturbation-derived DARs or cancer-type-specific accessible regions) and you need pairwise top-k list agreement via Jaccard indices. Only one method's ranked TR list is available — pairwise Jaccard requires at least two ranked lists for the same region set The goal is to measure accuracy rather than inter-method agreement — use mean reciprocal rank (MRR) against known perturbed TRs, as the article did for five perturbed TRs in bulk datasets The objects to compare are genomic region sets (BED peaks) rather than ranked TR name lists — Jaccard here is computed over top-k TR sets, not over genomic intervals http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Quantifies pairwise concordance of top-ranked transcriptional regulator (TR) lists produced by different TR-identification methods (BIT, BART, ChIP-Atlas, i-cisTarget, HOMER, WhichTF) by computing Jaccard indices at top-k cutoffs, revealing how much the methods agree on the same epigenomic query region sets. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Quantifies pairwise concordance of top-ranked transcriptional regulator (TR) lists produced by different TR-identification methods (BIT, BART, ChIP-Atlas, i-cisTarget, HOMER, WhichTF) by computing Jaccard indices at top-k cutoffs, revealing how much the methods agree on the same epigenomic query region sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one method's ranked TR list is available — pairwise Jaccard requires at least two ranked lists for the same region set The goal is to measure accuracy rather than inter-method agreement — use mean reciprocal rank (MRR) against known perturbed TRs, as the article did for five perturbed TRs in bulk datasets The objects to compare are genomic region sets (BED peaks) rather than ranked TR name lists — Jaccard here is computed over top-k TR sets, not over genomic intervals

skills.description: Use when comparing the number of enriched candidate binding sites called by Skipper against Piranha and CLIPper on matched eCLIP replicates, or when benchmarking a new CLIP-seq caller's sensitivity on ENCODE data.
skills.name: rbp-binding-site-count-aggregation
skills.search_text: rbp-binding-site-count-aggregation Use when comparing the number of enriched candidate binding sites called by Skipper against Piranha and CLIPper on matched eCLIP replicates, or when benchmarking a new CLIP-seq caller's sensitivity on ENCODE data. CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper requires one to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing Datasets where the goal is motif discovery or binding-affinity estimation rather than caller sensitivity benchmarking Analyses targeting repetitive-element or multi-mapping-sequence binding, which this peak-count comparison framework does not address http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Benchmark-style aggregation of enriched binding-site counts across CLIP-seq callers: run Skipper (window-tiling, peak-free) side-by-side with Piranha and CLIPper on matched ENCODE eCLIP IP/input replicates, then intersect and summarize per-RBP site counts to quantify how many more transcriptomic binding sites Skipper recovers. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Benchmark-style aggregation of enriched binding-site counts across CLIP-seq callers: run Skipper (window-tiling, peak-free) side-by-side with Piranha and CLIPper on matched ENCODE eCLIP IP/input replicates, then intersect and summarize per-RBP site counts to quantify how many more transcriptomic binding sites Skipper recovers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper requires one to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing Datasets where the goal is motif discovery or binding-affinity estimation rather than caller sensitivity benchmarking Analyses targeting repetitive-element or multi-mapping-sequence binding, which this peak-count comparison framework does not address

skills.description: Use when eCLIP replicates (e.g., WT vs point-mutant RBP) have Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows output and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding windows assigned to transcript regions such as CDS, deep introns, or tRNA loci.
skills.name: rbp-transcript-region-distribution-analysis
skills.search_text: rbp-transcript-region-distribution-analysis Use when eCLIP replicates (e.g., WT vs point-mutant RBP) have Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows output and the goal is to compare the fraction of binding windows assigned to transcript regions such as CDS, deep introns, or tRNA loci. CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper requires matched input controls to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing Analyses where raw peak-caller output (e.g., CLIPper BED peaks), not Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows, is the only available binding-site representation Questions about the mechanism of binding change (complex formation vs localization vs binding preference), which eCLIP data alone cannot resolve http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Quantifies how an RBP's reproducible enriched CLIP-seq windows distribute across annotated transcript regions (CDS, UTRs, introns, repeats) using Skipper's fixed-window annotation framework, enabling detection of WT-vs-mutant binding profile shifts such as the RPS19 R62W/R101H CDS-increase and deep-intron-decrease signature. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Quantifies how an RBP's reproducible enriched CLIP-seq windows distribute across annotated transcript regions (CDS, UTRs, introns, repeats) using Skipper's fixed-window annotation framework, enabling detection of WT-vs-mutant binding profile shifts such as the RPS19 R62W/R101H CDS-increase and deep-intron-decrease signature.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper requires matched input controls to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing Analyses where raw peak-caller output (e.g., CLIPper BED peaks), not Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows, is the only available binding-site representation Questions about the mechanism of binding change (complex formation vs localization vs binding preference), which eCLIP data alone cannot resolve

skills.description: Use when you have cell-line gene expression, copy number, mutation, and pharmacological sensitivity data plus ChIP-seq (or precomputed RP) targets, and want to infer which transcriptional regulators drive resistance or sensitivity to a specific drug.
skills.name: regression-based-tr-activity-inference
skills.search_text: regression-based-tr-activity-inference Use when you have cell-line gene expression, copy number, mutation, and pharmacological sensitivity data plus ChIP-seq (or precomputed RP) targets, and want to infer which transcriptional regulators drive resistance or sensitivity to a specific drug. No ChIP-seq data exist for the TR of interest, or available ChIP-seq has too few targets — RePhine identifies TRs through targets and such data would mislead identification The question is detecting acquired/secondary resistance (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation) — CCLE lacks post-treatment data, so pre-treatment-based RePhine cannot capture these mechanisms The goal is establishing causality rather than association — correlations detected through targets may not be causal and require TR knockout/activation experiments with drug response testing http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Applies RePhine, a regression-based integration of CCLE pharmacogenomic data and ENCODE ChIP-seq regulatory potential (RP) scores, to identify transcriptional regulators independently associated with response to a given drug (e.g., BRAF inhibitor PLX4720). It models concordant partial correlations of TR target sets while adjusting confounders such as CNVs and kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Applies RePhine, a regression-based integration of CCLE pharmacogenomic data and ENCODE ChIP-seq regulatory potential (RP) scores, to identify transcriptional regulators independently associated with response to a given drug (e.g., BRAF inhibitor PLX4720). It models concordant partial correlations of TR target sets while adjusting confounders such as CNVs and kinase/tumor-suppressor mutations.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ChIP-seq data exist for the TR of interest, or available ChIP-seq has too few targets — RePhine identifies TRs through targets and such data would mislead identification The question is detecting acquired/secondary resistance (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation) — CCLE lacks post-treatment data, so pre-treatment-based RePhine cannot capture these mechanisms The goal is establishing causality rather than association — correlations detected through targets may not be causal and require TR knockout/activation experiments with drug response testing

skills.description: Use when you need to quantify or rank how strongly individual REMs associated to a gene contribute to that gene's expression in a specific cell type, e.g. after a GeneQuery retrieval of regressionCoefficient and DNase1 signal data.
skills.name: regression-coefficient-normalization
skills.search_text: regression-coefficient-normalization Use when you need to quantify or rank how strongly individual REMs associated to a gene contribute to that gene's expression in a specific cell type, e.g. after a GeneQuery retrieval of regressionCoefficient and DNase1 signal data. You want to identify enriched TF motifs in REM sequences — use PASTAA or similar motif enrichment tools instead of the Cell type score normalization. You need the actual regulatory regions linked to a gene from scratch — first run EpiRegio's GeneQuery; this skill only normalizes coefficients for REMs already associated to a gene. The input is a single REM without its full set R of associated REMs, since the denominator requires summing over all REMs of the gene. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Computes EpiRegio's Cell type score, which normalizes each REM's regression coefficient times its per-cell-type DNase1 signal over all REMs of a gene, yielding a cell type-specific contribution to the target gene's expression bounded in [-1, 1]. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Computes EpiRegio's Cell type score, which normalizes each REM's regression coefficient times its per-cell-type DNase1 signal over all REMs of a gene, yielding a cell type-specific contribution to the target gene's expression bounded in [-1, 1].
skills.when_to_use_negative: You want to identify enriched TF motifs in REM sequences — use PASTAA or similar motif enrichment tools instead of the Cell type score normalization. You need the actual regulatory regions linked to a gene from scratch — first run EpiRegio's GeneQuery; this skill only normalizes coefficients for REMs already associated to a gene. The input is a single REM without its full set R of associated REMs, since the denominator requires summing over all REMs of the gene.

skills.description: Use when you have smoothed time-course expression data for a target gene and candidate regulators and need to estimate ODE synthesis/decay/weight parameters while forcing them into biologically interpretable ranges.
skills.name: regularized-maximum-a-posteriori-estimation
skills.search_text: regularized-maximum-a-posteriori-estimation Use when you have smoothed time-course expression data for a target gene and candidate regulators and need to estimate ODE synthesis/decay/weight parameters while forcing them into biologically interpretable ranges. skills.summary: Query EpiRegio to retrieve regulatory elements (REMs) linked to genes of interest, either by submitting ChIP-seq peak BED files (Region Query) or differential-expression gene lists (Gene Query), returning REM–gene association tables with genomic coordinates and cell-type-specific scores.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need REMs identified de novo from raw chromatin accessibility data rather than retrieval of pre-computed REM–gene associations from EpiRegio's database Your regions are not in a supported genomic coordinate format (BED) or your gene identifiers cannot be matched by EpiRegio's Gene Query, which causes substantial shortfalls in returned REMs You want TF motif discovery directly — that requires a follow-up PASTAA run on extracted REM sequences, not the query itself

skills.description: Use when an EpiRegio Gene Query result table (CSV of REMs linked to genes of interest, filtered for a cell type/tissue such as 'heart') must be turned into DNA sequences in FASTA format to feed a motif enrichment tool.
skills.name: regulatory-element-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: regulatory-element-sequence-extraction Use when an EpiRegio Gene Query result table (CSV of REMs linked to genes of interest, filtered for a cell type/tissue such as 'heart') must be turned into DNA sequences in FASTA format to feed a motif enrichment tool. The sequences are already available in FASTA form and only motif enrichment is needed — skip extraction and feed the FASTA directly to PASTAA The task is to identify a TF's target genes from ChIP-seq peaks (Region Query of ChIP-seq peaks against REMs with 50% overlap), which does not require sequence extraction http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Extract the DNA sequences of REMs identified by EpiRegio's Gene Query by converting the downloaded result CSV to a BED file (chromosome, start, end) and running bedtools getfasta against a current human genome FASTA, producing REMs.fa for downstream motif enrichment (e.g. PASTAA). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Extract the DNA sequences of REMs identified by EpiRegio's Gene Query by converting the downloaded result CSV to a BED file (chromosome, start, end) and running bedtools getfasta against a current human genome FASTA, producing REMs.fa for downstream motif enrichment (e.g. PASTAA).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The sequences are already available in FASTA form and only motif enrichment is needed — skip extraction and feed the FASTA directly to PASTAA The task is to identify a TF's target genes from ChIP-seq peaks (Region Query of ChIP-seq peaks against REMs with 50% overlap), which does not require sequence extraction

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq peak BED files with signal enrichment values and gene/TSS annotations must be converted into quantitative TR-target regulatory potential scores for target inference.
skills.name: regulatory-potential-score-calculation
skills.search_text: regulatory-potential-score-calculation Use when ChIP-seq peak BED files with signal enrichment values and gene/TSS annotations must be converted into quantitative TR-target regulatory potential scores for target inference. No ChIP-seq data are available, or the ChIP-seq data have too few targets, which would mislead TR identification Reliable target information for the TR of interest is unavailable, since RePhine identifies drug-response TRs through their targets The goal is direct TR-drug association from mRNA levels only, without ChIP-seq-based target inference http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Calculates regulatory-potential (RP) scores that quantify how strongly a transcriptional regulator binds each target gene, using a modified model that weights ChIP-seq peaks by both peak-to-TSS distance and peak signal strength (enrichment m). These gene x TR RP scores are the target-inference input RePhine needs for drug-response TR identification. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Calculates regulatory-potential (RP) scores that quantify how strongly a transcriptional regulator binds each target gene, using a modified model that weights ChIP-seq peaks by both peak-to-TSS distance and peak signal strength (enrichment m). These gene x TR RP scores are the target-inference input RePhine needs for drug-response TR identification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ChIP-seq data are available, or the ChIP-seq data have too few targets, which would mislead TR identification Reliable target information for the TR of interest is unavailable, since RePhine identifies drug-response TRs through their targets The goal is direct TR-drug association from mRNA levels only, without ChIP-seq-based target inference

skills.description: Use when a candidate regulon definition (ChIP-derived, knockout-derived, or literature/database-mined) must be paired with a time-course expression series and preprocessed before network inference.
skills.name: regulon-dataset-preparation
skills.search_text: regulon-dataset-preparation Use when a candidate regulon definition (ChIP-derived, knockout-derived, or literature/database-mined) must be paired with a time-course expression series and preprocessed before network inference. The data are not time-course measurements — Cytoscape does not natively support time series, and the Genexpi ODE model requires expression over time The candidate regulon has no source (no ChIP, knockout, or database/literature-mined candidates) to combine with the expression data The target organism's regulons are eukaryotic and no caution is applied — the article states Genexpi was designed for bacterial regulons and eukaryotic use requires validation http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Prepares paired inputs for Genexpi-style regulon inference: a network of putative regulatory relationships (from databases like Subtiwiki, YEASTRACT, or ChIP-chip/knockout experiments) combined with time-course gene expression data, smoothed via B-spline linear regression and cleaned of non-informative genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: Prepares paired inputs for Genexpi-style regulon inference: a network of putative regulatory relationships (from databases like Subtiwiki, YEASTRACT, or ChIP-chip/knockout experiments) combined with time-course gene expression data, smoothed via B-spline linear regression and cleaned of non-informative genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are not time-course measurements — Cytoscape does not natively support time series, and the Genexpi ODE model requires expression over time The candidate regulon has no source (no ChIP, knockout, or database/literature-mined candidates) to combine with the expression data The target organism's regulons are eukaryotic and no caution is applied — the article states Genexpi was designed for bacterial regulons and eukaryotic use requires validation

skills.description: Use when a candidate regulon (ChIP, knockout, or database-derived) plus a matching expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GSE44415, GDS38) is available and you need to quantify recovery rate versus a random-profile baseline.
skills.name: regulon-recovery-benchmarking
skills.search_text: regulon-recovery-benchmarking Use when a candidate regulon (ChIP, knockout, or database-derived) plus a matching expression time series (e.g. GSE6865, GSE44415, GDS38) is available and you need to quantify recovery rate versus a random-profile baseline. Regulators known to act in complexes (e.g. MBP1, SWI4, SWI6 in yeast): Genexpi gave its worst, random-indistinguishable results there because complex regulation breaks its single-regulator model The regulon gene list is unrelated to any time-course expression data, so smoothing and ODE fitting cannot be performed A complete regulatory network is required: time-series expression data cannot in principle provide complete interaction information, so Genexpi is best used as one of multiple sources of insight http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Benchmark a time-course gene-network inference method (Genexpi vs TD-Aracne) by measuring how much of a literature-derived regulon (e.g. SigB from Subtiwiki, SigR from ChIP-chip/knockout studies, yeast TFs from YEASTRACT) it recovers, and how often it falsely accepts random regulator profiles. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2138-x
skills.summary: Benchmark a time-course gene-network inference method (Genexpi vs TD-Aracne) by measuring how much of a literature-derived regulon (e.g. SigB from Subtiwiki, SigR from ChIP-chip/knockout studies, yeast TFs from YEASTRACT) it recovers, and how often it falsely accepts random regulator profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Regulators known to act in complexes (e.g. MBP1, SWI4, SWI6 in yeast): Genexpi gave its worst, random-indistinguishable results there because complex regulation breaks its single-regulator model The regulon gene list is unrelated to any time-course expression data, so smoothing and ODE fitting cannot be performed A complete regulatory network is required: time-series expression data cannot in principle provide complete interaction information, so Genexpi is best used as one of multiple sources of insight

skills.description: Use when you have interval-formatted REM/genomic region coordinates (chr, start, end) and need to merge overlapping or adjacent regions into clusters and report aggregate span/size statistics.
skills.name: rem-clustering-into-crems
skills.search_text: rem-clustering-into-crems Use when you have interval-formatted REM/genomic region coordinates (chr, start, end) and need to merge overlapping or adjacent regions into clusters and report aggregate span/size statistics. You only need individual REMs and their associated genes (e.g. a Gene Query), not the merged CREM-level grouping of overlapping/adjacent REMs Your intervals require a different merging criterion, e.g. the EpiRegio Region Query 50% REM-overlap threshold for ChIP-seq peaks rather than >= 1 bp overlap or 0 bp gap adjacency http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduces EpiRegio's definition of Clusters of Regulatory EleMents (CREMs): per chromosome, REMs overlapping by at least 1 bp or directly adjacent (0 bp gap) are merged, and only clusters containing a minimum of two REMs are retained as CREMs, enabling quantitative characterization of the 2,404,861 REM set. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Reproduces EpiRegio's definition of Clusters of Regulatory EleMents (CREMs): per chromosome, REMs overlapping by at least 1 bp or directly adjacent (0 bp gap) are merged, and only clusters containing a minimum of two REMs are retained as CREMs, enabling quantitative characterization of the 2,404,861 REM set.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need individual REMs and their associated genes (e.g. a Gene Query), not the merged CREM-level grouping of overlapping/adjacent REMs Your intervals require a different merging criterion, e.g. the EpiRegio Region Query 50% REM-overlap threshold for ChIP-seq peaks rather than >= 1 bp overlap or 0 bp gap adjacency

skills.description: Use when comparing phased mCpG/epiallele frequencies across bisulfite-sequenced amplicon samples with unequal read depths, where raw frequency comparisons are biased by library size.
skills.name: repeated-random-sampling-of-methylation-reads
skills.search_text: repeated-random-sampling-of-methylation-reads Use when comparing phased mCpG/epiallele frequencies across bisulfite-sequenced amplicon samples with unequal read depths, where raw frequency comparisons are biased by library size. All samples already share the same sequencing depth, so size-comparison bias is absent and rarefaction only discards molecules The goal is quantitative methylation of individual CpGs or abundance of single epialleles (the scope of tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler and methclone), not phased mCpG core/epiallele-family structure Input reads have ambiguous CpG calls (gaps or A/G at CpG dinucleotides) that have not yet been removed by the ampliMethProfiler quality filters http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reduces read-depth (size-comparison) bias in bisulfite epiallele analysis by iteratively subsampling each experimental sample y=1000 times at the average sample depth b4, as implemented in MethCoresProfiler's MethCores_Extractor before mCpG-combination significance testing. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqaa096
skills.summary: Reduces read-depth (size-comparison) bias in bisulfite epiallele analysis by iteratively subsampling each experimental sample y=1000 times at the average sample depth b4, as implemented in MethCoresProfiler's MethCores_Extractor before mCpG-combination significance testing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: All samples already share the same sequencing depth, so size-comparison bias is absent and rarefaction only discards molecules The goal is quantitative methylation of individual CpGs or abundance of single epialleles (the scope of tools like EBA, ampliMethProfiler and methclone), not phased mCpG core/epiallele-family structure Input reads have ambiguous CpG calls (gaps or A/G at CpG dinucleotides) that have not yet been removed by the ampliMethProfiler quality filters

skills.description: Use when an analysis requires strand-annotated genomic coordinates of transposable elements (LINE, SINE, LTR subclasses) from UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker as motif input for interval-overlap or asymmetry tooling.
skills.name: repeatmasker-repeat-coordinate-extraction
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-repeat-coordinate-extraction Use when an analysis requires strand-annotated genomic coordinates of transposable elements (LINE, SINE, LTR subclasses) from UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker as motif input for interval-overlap or asymmetry tooling. The analysis needs nucleotide-level repeat sequences or consensus motifs rather than genomic interval coordinates The target genome build is not hg38 — the extracted coordinates are genome-build-specific and would require liftOver A feature table with strand annotation already exists (e.g. pre-formatted BED files), making re-extraction from rmsk redundant http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3175 Extracts chromosome, start, end and strand coordinates for selected repeat classes (e.g. Alu SINEs, MIRs, L1/L2 LINEs) from the UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker table (rmsk.txt.gz, 11 March 2019 version) into strand-annotated BED files suitable for strand asymmetry analysis with Asymmetron. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Extracts chromosome, start, end and strand coordinates for selected repeat classes (e.g. Alu SINEs, MIRs, L1/L2 LINEs) from the UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker table (rmsk.txt.gz, 11 March 2019 version) into strand-annotated BED files suitable for strand asymmetry analysis with Asymmetron.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis needs nucleotide-level repeat sequences or consensus motifs rather than genomic interval coordinates The target genome build is not hg38 — the extracted coordinates are genome-build-specific and would require liftOver A feature table with strand annotation already exists (e.g. pre-formatted BED files), making re-extraction from rmsk redundant

skills.description: Use when preparing centered, score-carrying motif-site sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around Nanog ChIP-seq motif sites) for positional motif enrichment, and repeats must be removed to avoid confounding motif-matching with low-complexity DNA.
skills.name: repeatmasker-repetitive-element-filtering
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-repetitive-element-filtering Use when preparing centered, score-carrying motif-site sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around Nanog ChIP-seq motif sites) for positional motif enrichment, and repeats must be removed to avoid confounding motif-matching with low-complexity DNA. The goal is de novo motif discovery — MEPP only functions with a fixed motif library, so repeat filtering in its pipeline cannot assemble new motifs. Sequences are already filtered (e.g. an existing deduplicated, RepeatMasker-masked site set) — re-filtering adds no information and risks discarding valid sites. Input is not centered, scored sequences (e.g. raw FASTQ or an unsorted BAM) — this skill presumes motif sites already called, deduplicated, and score-ordered for MEPP. http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Filters repetitive/low-complexity sequence out of ChIP-seq-derived motif site sets (e.g. deduplicated, RepeatMasker-filtered Nanog motif sites in mm10) so that downstream MEPP positional enrichment profiles reflect specific TF binding rather than repeat-driven spurious motif matches. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Filters repetitive/low-complexity sequence out of ChIP-seq-derived motif site sets (e.g. deduplicated, RepeatMasker-filtered Nanog motif sites in mm10) so that downstream MEPP positional enrichment profiles reflect specific TF binding rather than repeat-driven spurious motif matches.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo motif discovery — MEPP only functions with a fixed motif library, so repeat filtering in its pipeline cannot assemble new motifs. Sequences are already filtered (e.g. an existing deduplicated, RepeatMasker-masked site set) — re-filtering adds no information and risks discarding valid sites. Input is not centered, scored sequences (e.g. raw FASTQ or an unsorted BAM) — this skill presumes motif sites already called, deduplicated, and score-ordered for MEPP.

skills.description: Use when a strand-asymmetry or breakpoint-enrichment analysis needs class-filtered, strand-annotated transposable element coordinates from UCSC hg38 rmsk (e.g. LINE/SINE/LTR) to orient mutations or assign background orientation probabilities.
skills.name: repeatmasker-transposable-element-annotation-processing
skills.search_text: repeatmasker-transposable-element-annotation-processing Use when a strand-asymmetry or breakpoint-enrichment analysis needs class-filtered, strand-annotated transposable element coordinates from UCSC hg38 rmsk (e.g. LINE/SINE/LTR) to orient mutations or assign background orientation probabilities. The query features already carry strand annotations — the orientation step against repeats is unnecessary; feed them directly into Asymmetron's asymmetry estimation functions. The analysis targets a non-hg38 genome or a non-mammalian species for which the 11 March 2019 UCSC rmsk table is not the correct coordinate system. The question concerns palindromic sequence content or nucleotide compositional skews rather than orienting features relative to strand-annotated transposable elements. http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Processes UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker (rmsk) repeat annotations into strand-annotated, class-filtered transposable element intervals (LINE, SINE, LTR) that serve as the reference elements for orienting unassigned genomic features such as gnomAD germline structural variant breakpoints in strand-asymmetry analyses with Asymmetron. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Processes UCSC hg38 RepeatMasker (rmsk) repeat annotations into strand-annotated, class-filtered transposable element intervals (LINE, SINE, LTR) that serve as the reference elements for orienting unassigned genomic features such as gnomAD germline structural variant breakpoints in strand-asymmetry analyses with Asymmetron.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The query features already carry strand annotations — the orientation step against repeats is unnecessary; feed them directly into Asymmetron's asymmetry estimation functions. The analysis targets a non-hg38 genome or a non-mammalian species for which the 11 March 2019 UCSC rmsk table is not the correct coordinate system. The question concerns palindromic sequence content or nucleotide compositional skews rather than orienting features relative to strand-annotated transposable elements.

skills.description: Use when the goal is to organize anti-cancer drugs (e.g., CCLE compounds) into mechanism-of-action groups from TR-drug response associations, or to reproduce the RePhine drug-cluster dendrogram of Figure 3A.
skills.name: rephine-response-signature-computation
skills.search_text: rephine-response-signature-computation Use when the goal is to organize anti-cancer drugs (e.g., CCLE compounds) into mechanism-of-action groups from TR-drug response associations, or to reproduce the RePhine drug-cluster dendrogram of Figure 3A. ChIP-seq data for a TR is missing or contains too few targets — the article warns this would mislead TR identification, so the signature values are unreliable The goal is inferring acquired/secondary resistance from post-treatment dynamics — CCLE lacks post-treatment data (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation cannot be detected) Input is already a curated drug-feature table not derived from TR response associations — clustering would not reflect RePhine's mechanism-of-action signature http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Compute RePhine transcriptional-regulator response signatures (-Log10 uniP values) for each drug in the CCLE pharmacogenomic data and use them to hierarchically cluster drugs by mechanism of action, reproducing the Figure 3A organization. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.gpb.2019.09.008
skills.summary: Compute RePhine transcriptional-regulator response signatures (-Log10 uniP values) for each drug in the CCLE pharmacogenomic data and use them to hierarchically cluster drugs by mechanism of action, reproducing the Figure 3A organization.
skills.when_to_use_negative: ChIP-seq data for a TR is missing or contains too few targets — the article warns this would mislead TR identification, so the signature values are unreliable The goal is inferring acquired/secondary resistance from post-treatment dynamics — CCLE lacks post-treatment data (e.g., erlotinib resistance via acquired STAT3 activation cannot be detected) Input is already a curated drug-feature table not derived from TR response associations — clustering would not reflect RePhine's mechanism-of-action signature

skills.description: Use when QC-ing a ChIP-seq experiment with ≥2 biological replicates and you need to measure agreement before merging BAMs or trusting merged peak calls.
skills.name: replicate-consistency-assessment-via-peak-overlap-and-correlation
skills.search_text: replicate-consistency-assessment-via-peak-overlap-and-correlation Use when QC-ing a ChIP-seq experiment with ≥2 biological replicates and you need to measure agreement before merging BAMs or trusting merged peak calls. Single-replicate ChIP-seq experiments — there is no second replicate to correlate or overlap against QC layers that only need library-level metrics (PBC, FastQC GC content, FRiP per sample) without inter-replicate agreement DNase-seq-only pipelines where MACS2 peak-based replicate overlap semantics do not apply as configured http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 ChiLin's ChIP-layer QC step (step 5) that quantifies ChIP-seq replicate consistency using two complementary metrics: Pearson correlation of genome-wide normalized signal via UCSC wigCorrelate, and the inter-replicate percentage of overlapping MACS2-called peaks. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: ChiLin's ChIP-layer QC step (step 5) that quantifies ChIP-seq replicate consistency using two complementary metrics: Pearson correlation of genome-wide normalized signal via UCSC wigCorrelate, and the inter-replicate percentage of overlapping MACS2-called peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Single-replicate ChIP-seq experiments — there is no second replicate to correlate or overlap against QC layers that only need library-level metrics (PBC, FastQC GC content, FRiP per sample) without inter-replicate agreement DNase-seq-only pipelines where MACS2 peak-based replicate overlap semantics do not apply as configured

skills.description: Use when two or more ChIP-seq treatment replicates (plus controls) are supplied as FASTQ and the QC goal is to quantify replicate agreement via wiggle correlation and peak overlap before interpreting the experiment.
skills.name: replicate-consistency-correlation-analysis
skills.search_text: replicate-consistency-correlation-analysis Use when two or more ChIP-seq treatment replicates (plus controls) are supplied as FASTQ and the QC goal is to quantify replicate agreement via wiggle correlation and peak overlap before interpreting the experiment. Only one replicate is available — pairwise wiggle correlation and peak overlap cannot be computed. The goal is annotation or motif analysis of a single merged peak set rather than replicate QC — use ChiLin steps 6 and 8 instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Assesses ChIP-seq biological replicate consistency within the ChiLin QC pipeline by calling peaks per replicate with MACS2 and computing wiggle correlations and replicate peak-overlap counts (pipeline step 5), reported against historical reference metrics (e.g. TRRAP wiggle correlation 0.14 / 20-peak overlap). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Assesses ChIP-seq biological replicate consistency within the ChiLin QC pipeline by calling peaks per replicate with MACS2 and computing wiggle correlations and replicate peak-overlap counts (pipeline step 5), reported against historical reference metrics (e.g. TRRAP wiggle correlation 0.14 / 20-peak overlap).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one replicate is available — pairwise wiggle correlation and peak overlap cannot be computed. The goal is annotation or motif analysis of a single merged peak set rather than replicate QC — use ChiLin steps 6 and 8 instead.

skills.description: Use when multiple Hi-C replicates (e.g., QSC and FISC MuSC replicates) exist as Microcket-produced .hic files and a per-condition contact matrix/heatmap is needed for specific regions and bin sizes.
skills.name: replicate-merging-of-hic-contact-matrices
skills.search_text: replicate-merging-of-hic-contact-matrices Use when multiple Hi-C replicates (e.g., QSC and FISC MuSC replicates) exist as Microcket-produced .hic files and a per-condition contact matrix/heatmap is needed for specific regions and bin sizes. Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned pairs — this skill operates on Microcket-generated .hic files produced by the upstream Microcket run Only one replicate per condition exists and no merging is required — extracting and plotting a single matrix is sufficient The goal is calling TADs/loops or other quantitative analysis rather than visual contact-map rendering for expert review http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Merges per-replicate Microcket-generated .hic contact matrices into a single KR-normalized contact matrix per condition (QSC, FISC) and renders them as side-by-side chr16 contact-map heatmaps at 100-kb, 25-kb, and 5-kb resolutions for comparative chromatin architecture analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xpro.2025.103962
skills.summary: Merges per-replicate Microcket-generated .hic contact matrices into a single KR-normalized contact matrix per condition (QSC, FISC) and renders them as side-by-side chr16 contact-map heatmaps at 100-kb, 25-kb, and 5-kb resolutions for comparative chromatin architecture analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ or unaligned pairs — this skill operates on Microcket-generated .hic files produced by the upstream Microcket run Only one replicate per condition exists and no merging is required — extracting and plotting a single matrix is sufficient The goal is calling TADs/loops or other quantitative analysis rather than visual contact-map rendering for expert review

skills.description: Use when a set of candidate CRE or OCR coordinates must be functionally benchmarked against previously tested enhancers, e.g. intersecting scATAC-seq-derived OCRs with VISTA e11.5 transgenic reporter regions and recovering per-region positive/negative outcomes.
skills.name: reporter-assay-outcome-annotation
skills.search_text: reporter-assay-outcome-annotation Use when a set of candidate CRE or OCR coordinates must be functionally benchmarked against previously tested enhancers, e.g. intersecting scATAC-seq-derived OCRs with VISTA e11.5 transgenic reporter regions and recovering per-region positive/negative outcomes. The candidate regions already carry functional validation or the analysis goal is de novo motif/state inference rather than benchmarking against tested enhancers The reporter-assay reference lacks outcome annotations (regions tested but unclassified), making outcome annotation impossible without external information The candidate and reference coordinates cannot be brought to a common genome build (e.g. liftover fails for a large fraction of regions), so overlaps would be spurious http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Annotates candidate cis-regulatory elements (e.g. the ~370,000 candidate CREs from the SnapATAC mouse secondary motor cortex atlas) with transgenic reporter-assay outcomes from a reference database such as the VISTA Enhancer Browser, converting coordinate overlaps into empirical functional validation rates (65% reproducible vs 9.7% background). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Annotates candidate cis-regulatory elements (e.g. the ~370,000 candidate CREs from the SnapATAC mouse secondary motor cortex atlas) with transgenic reporter-assay outcomes from a reference database such as the VISTA Enhancer Browser, converting coordinate overlaps into empirical functional validation rates (65% reproducible vs 9.7% background).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The candidate regions already carry functional validation or the analysis goal is de novo motif/state inference rather than benchmarking against tested enhancers The reporter-assay reference lacks outcome annotations (regions tested but unclassified), making outcome annotation impossible without external information The candidate and reference coordinates cannot be brought to a common genome build (e.g. liftover fails for a large fraction of regions), so overlaps would be spurious

skills.description: Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq replicates to detect RBP binding transcriptome-wide as reproducible enriched windows (with annotation metadata) rather than peaks, especially when repetitive elements or diverse binding modes break peak callers.
skills.name: reproducible-enriched-window-calling
skills.search_text: reproducible-enriched-window-calling Use when analyzing eCLIP/CLIP-seq replicates to detect RBP binding transcriptome-wide as reproducible enriched windows (with annotation metadata) rather than peaks, especially when repetitive elements or diverse binding modes break peak callers. The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, which Skipper needs to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing The goal is not window-level binding detection but a downstream task already covered, e.g., feature tables for benchmarking precision/recall/F1 against truth sets The annotation GFF has not been filtered to one best transcript per gene, which Skipper requires for interpretable window selection http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Run Skipper, an end-to-end Snakemake workflow, to convert raw eCLIP FASTQ reads into reproducible enriched windows over annotated transcripts, replacing conventional peak calling with a beta-binomial test of read-start signal in tiled fixed windows. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Run Skipper, an end-to-end Snakemake workflow, to convert raw eCLIP FASTQ reads into reproducible enriched windows over annotated transcripts, replacing conventional peak calling with a beta-binomial test of read-start signal in tiled fixed windows.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The CLIP dataset lacks a matched input sample, which Skipper needs to construct the beta-binomial model for statistical testing The goal is not window-level binding detection but a downstream task already covered, e.g., feature tables for benchmarking precision/recall/F1 against truth sets The annotation GFF has not been filtered to one best transcript per gene, which Skipper requires for interpretable window selection

skills.description: Use when the analysis goal is to rapidly run or test a complete NGS workflow in R/Bioconductor — e.g. reproducing a template RNA-Seq analysis from FASTQ inputs through reporting — with logged, reproducible execution.
skills.name: reproducible-ngs-analysis-execution-in-r
skills.search_text: reproducible-ngs-analysis-execution-in-r Use when the analysis goal is to rapidly run or test a complete NGS workflow in R/Bioconductor — e.g. reproducing a template RNA-Seq analysis from FASTQ inputs through reporting — with logged, reproducible execution. When reads are already summarized into a feature/count table with no alignment-level fragment information — the likelihood framework operates on fragment alignments (SAM) When the library preparation is known to produce uniformly distributed fragments and only a raw count baseline is needed, since bias estimation adds complexity without expected gain When no reference transcriptome/annotation is available, as simultaneous bias and expression estimation is transcriptome-guided http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Likelihood-based simultaneous estimation of fragment-bias parameters and RNA-Seq expression levels (eXpress-D / mseq), which corrects non-uniform cDNA fragment distribution within transcripts and improves the correlation of estimates with independently performed qRT-PCR. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Likelihood-based simultaneous estimation of fragment-bias parameters and RNA-Seq expression levels (eXpress-D / mseq), which corrects non-uniform cDNA fragment distribution within transcripts and improves the correlation of estimates with independently performed qRT-PCR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are already summarized into a feature/count table with no alignment-level fragment information — the likelihood framework operates on fragment alignments (SAM) When the library preparation is known to produce uniformly distributed fragments and only a raw count baseline is needed, since bias estimation adds complexity without expected gain When no reference transcriptome/annotation is available, as simultaneous bias and expression estimation is transcriptome-guided

skills.description: Use when two or more differentially expressed gene sets (e.g. H-NS and LuxR regulons from RNA-seq comparisons) must be intersected to count shared regulators/genes, with identifiers harmonized first.
skills.name: rna-seq-regulon-gene-list-processing
skills.search_text: rna-seq-regulon-gene-list-processing Use when two or more differentially expressed gene sets (e.g. H-NS and LuxR regulons from RNA-seq comparisons) must be intersected to count shared regulators/genes, with identifiers harmonized first. Input is raw RNA-seq reads or count matrices — the skill operates on already-called regulon/differential-expression gene lists, not on read processing or DE calling itself. The task is ChIP-seq peak overlap (e.g. the 88 overlapping LuxR/H-NS peaks proximal to an ORF ≤500 bp) rather than gene-list regulon overlap; that requires a separate peak-based workflow. The gene sets are not from V. harveyi or identifiers cannot be harmonized to a common namespace — the reported 178-gene validation target would not apply. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Harmonize and intersect RNA-seq-derived regulon gene lists — here, the H-NS regulons from wild-type and ΔluxR V. harveyi RNA-seq against the previously identified 308-gene LuxR regulon — using Perl set-operation scripts to quantify regulatory overlap (178 shared genes). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Harmonize and intersect RNA-seq-derived regulon gene lists — here, the H-NS regulons from wild-type and ΔluxR V. harveyi RNA-seq against the previously identified 308-gene LuxR regulon — using Perl set-operation scripts to quantify regulatory overlap (178 shared genes).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw RNA-seq reads or count matrices — the skill operates on already-called regulon/differential-expression gene lists, not on read processing or DE calling itself. The task is ChIP-seq peak overlap (e.g. the 88 overlapping LuxR/H-NS peaks proximal to an ORF ≤500 bp) rather than gene-list regulon overlap; that requires a separate peak-based workflow. The gene sets are not from V. harveyi or identifiers cannot be harmonized to a common namespace — the reported 178-gene validation target would not apply.

skills.description: Use when aligning RNA-Seq FASTQ files inside a systemPipeR workflow and you need to choose or benchmark an aligner (Bowtie2/TopHat2 vs HISAT2/Rsubread) or verify near-linear parallel speedup via clusterRun.
skills.name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment

The workflow is not runnable via systemPipeR (e.g. no R/Bioconductor >=3.2 environment, per the paper's stated R >=3.2, Bioconductor >=3.2 requirement). http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Run short-read alignment for RNA-Seq within systemPipeR workflows, swapping the alignment step between Bowtie2/TopHat2 and faster aligners such as HISAT2 or Rsubread, and benchmarking runtime scaling across CPU-core counts on FASTQ sample sets. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1241-0
skills.summary: Run short-read alignment for RNA-Seq within systemPipeR workflows, swapping the alignment step between Bowtie2/TopHat2 and faster aligners such as HISAT2 or Rsubread, and benchmarking runtime scaling across CPU-core counts on FASTQ sample sets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis goal is a downstream step (variant calling, peak calling, or differential expression analysis) rather than the alignment stage itself. skills.description: Use when FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single- or paired-end Illumina) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome before expression estimation, and novel junction discovery should be suppressed in favor of known annotated junctions.
skills.name: rna-seq-short-read-alignment
skills.search_text: rna-seq-short-read-alignment Use when FASTQ RNA-Seq reads (single- or paired-end Illumina) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome before expression estimation, and novel junction discovery should be suppressed in favor of known annotated junctions. The alignment target requires novel splice-junction discovery — --no-novel-juncs restricts TopHat to annotated refGene junctions only Reads are already aligned (an accepted_hits.bam or other BAM of mapped reads exists); proceed directly to eXpress-D expression estimation and bias correction The reference genome/annotation combination is not hg18 with RefSeq refGene and the transcript models needed downstream differ http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Maps Illumina RNA-Seq reads (e.g., MAQC Human Brain Reference reads from SRA012427) to the NCBI36/hg18 genome with TopHat 1.1.0, using the UCSC RefSeq refGene annotation and --no-novel-juncs so only annotated junctions are considered. skills.summary: Maps Illumina RNA-Seq reads (e.g., MAQC Human Brain Reference reads from SRA012427) to the NCBI36/hg18 genome with TopHat 1.1.0, using the UCSC RefSeq refGene annotation and --no-novel-juncs so only annotated junctions are considered. skills.description: Use when you have compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from multiple Hi-C or pseudo-bulk scHi-C maps and need to test which genomic bins have statistically significant compartmentalization differences without relying on an A/B compartment flip.
skills.name: robust-covariance-estimation-with-mcd
skills.search_text: robust-covariance-estimation-with-mcd Use when you have compartment scores (PC1/PC2) from multiple Hi-C or pseudo-bulk scHi-C maps and need to test which genomic bins have statistically significant compartmentalization differences without relying on an A/B compartment flip. You have only a single Hi-C contact map and no comparative compartment scores — MCD/Mahalanobis significance requires two or more maps/replicates to define a multivariate null distribution. Your goal is calling differential interactions/loops rather than differential compartments — use dcHiC's Fit-Hi-C-linked differential interaction module instead. Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized across maps/replicates — raw PC scores from independent PCAs are not comparable and would distort the covariance estimate. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 dcHiC's step-2 differential compartment module uses a Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) robust covariance estimate, stabilized by two passes of chi-square-based outlier removal, to compute weighted-center Mahalanobis distances from quantile-normalized compartment scores across two or more Hi-C maps. This turns per-bin PC1/PC2 score vectors into chi-square p-values for compartment differences. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: dcHiC's step-2 differential compartment module uses a Minimum Covariance Determinant (MCD) robust covariance estimate, stabilized by two passes of chi-square-based outlier removal, to compute weighted-center Mahalanobis distances from quantile-normalized compartment scores across two or more Hi-C maps. This turns per-bin PC1/PC2 score vectors into chi-square p-values for compartment differences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You have only a single Hi-C contact map and no comparative compartment scores — MCD/Mahalanobis significance requires two or more maps/replicates to define a multivariate null distribution. Your goal is calling differential interactions/loops rather than differential compartments — use dcHiC's Fit-Hi-C-linked differential interaction module instead. Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized across maps/replicates — raw PC scores from independent PCAs are not comparable and would distort the covariance estimate.

skills.description: Use when detecting non-B DNA windows in nanopore translocation-time matrices as a novelty detection problem, or when scoring windows against an empirical null built from B-DNA controls.
skills.name: robust-mahalanobis-anomaly-scoring
skills.search_text: robust-mahalanobis-anomaly-scoring Use when detecting non-B DNA windows in nanopore translocation-time matrices as a novelty detection problem, or when scoring windows against an empirical null built from B-DNA controls. skills.summary: Computes robust Mahalanobis-distance (and reconstruction-error) novelty statistics from the GoFAE-DND autoencoder's latent encoding of ONT translocation-time windows, calibrates empirical-null P-values from held-out B-DNA windows, and calls non-B DNA via Benjamini-Hochberg FDR.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw ONT current or FAST5 signal that has not yet been converted to base-level translocation times via Albacore basecalling and Tombo re-squiggling The goal is supervised classification with labeled non-B training data (the repo instead offers SVC, random forest, nearest neighbors, logistic regression, and gaussian process classifiers) Windows have not been prepared around non-B DB motifs with fixed-length windows, opposite-strand extension, and motif-free control regions
