You need de novo motif discovery from raw sequencing reads without genomic coordinates — Delila-PY requires a sites file of genomic positions and a GenBank file Your genome of interest has no GenBank record available, since dbbk and catal require it to build the Delila libraries http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Generate a DNA binding-site sequence logo and PWM from a set of genomic coordinates using the Delila-PY pipeline, which wraps the classic Delila suite in a Python3/Docker workflow with a three-cycle information-maximization loop. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00160-21
skills.summary: Generate a DNA binding-site sequence logo and PWM from a set of genomic coordinates using the Delila-PY pipeline, which wraps the classic Delila suite in a Python3/Docker workflow with a three-cycle information-maximization loop.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo motif discovery from raw sequencing reads without genomic coordinates — Delila-PY requires a sites file of genomic positions and a GenBank file Your genome of interest has no GenBank record available, since dbbk and catal require it to build the Delila libraries

skills.description: Use when a single non-coding SNP needs motif-level interpretation: predicting how every base substitution within ~200 bp of the variant alters a specific chromatin profile (e.g. NFE2 binding) and visualizing informative motifs.
skills.name: sequence-motif-visualization
skills.search_text: sequence-motif-visualization Use when a single non-coding SNP needs motif-level interpretation: predicting how every base substitution within ~200 bp of the variant alters a specific chromatin profile (e.g. NFE2 binding) and visualizing informative motifs. The question is variant-level prioritization across many SNPs rather than motif dissection of one locus — use DeepFun's SNP Activity Difference (sad.ipynb) workflow instead of saturated mutagenesis The effect of interest involves long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact, which the DeepFun model does not consider Quantitative (non-binarized) epigenomic signal magnitude matters, since DeepFun treats peaks as binary during training http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Visualizes the sequence features (motifs) a deep learning chromatin model learned around a query variant by running in silico saturated mutagenesis with DeepFun/Basset and rendering SAD heat maps for reference and alternative alleles. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Visualizes the sequence features (motifs) a deep learning chromatin model learned around a query variant by running in silico saturated mutagenesis with DeepFun/Basset and rendering SAD heat maps for reference and alternative alleles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question is variant-level prioritization across many SNPs rather than motif dissection of one locus — use DeepFun's SNP Activity Difference (sad.ipynb) workflow instead of saturated mutagenesis The effect of interest involves long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact, which the DeepFun model does not consider Quantitative (non-binarized) epigenomic signal magnitude matters, since DeepFun treats peaks as binary during training

skills.description: Use when planning a multi-sample single cell DE or eQTL study under a fixed budget and you must decide the trade-off between cells per individual, sequencing depth (reads/cell), and number of samples on a droplet (10X) platform.
skills.name: sequencing-cost-modeling-droplet-platforms
skills.search_text: sequencing-cost-modeling-droplet-platforms Use when planning a multi-sample single cell DE or eQTL study under a fixed budget and you must decide the trade-off between cells per individual, sequencing depth (reads/cell), and number of samples on a droplet (10X) platform. The input is already collected single cell count data requiring pseudobulk construction (create.pseudobulk, nbinom.estimation) rather than prospective experimental design The study uses a non-droplet or non-10X platform whose kit/flowcell cost model and read.umi.fit differ from the 10X parameters used here Power analysis for variance QTLs or continuous annotations such as pseudo time is needed — the paper did not address variance QTL power due to lack of effect size priors, and continuous annotations must be discretized first http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Model 10X droplet scRNA-seq experimental costs (library prep plus sequencing) and, for a restricted budget, sweep cells-per-individual and read-depth combinations with scPower's optimize.constant.budget to select the design maximizing overall detection power, with sample size inferred from the remaining budget. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Model 10X droplet scRNA-seq experimental costs (library prep plus sequencing) and, for a restricted budget, sweep cells-per-individual and read-depth combinations with scPower's optimize.constant.budget to select the design maximizing overall detection power, with sample size inferred from the remaining budget.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already collected single cell count data requiring pseudobulk construction (create.pseudobulk, nbinom.estimation) rather than prospective experimental design The study uses a non-droplet or non-10X platform whose kit/flowcell cost model and read.umi.fit differ from the 10X parameters used here Power analysis for variance QTLs or continuous annotations such as pseudo time is needed — the paper did not address variance QTL power due to lack of effect size priors, and continuous annotations must be discretized first

skills.description: Use when validating that a Hi-C compartment/sub-compartment inference method recovers stable scores at shallow sequencing depths, by simulating trans-interaction summary files at multiple downsampled depths (e.g. 1x, 0.1x, 0.01x).
skills.name: sequencing-depth-downsampling
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-downsampling Use when validating that a Hi-C compartment/sub-compartment inference method recovers stable scores at shallow sequencing depths, by simulating trans-interaction summary files at multiple downsampled depths (e.g. 1x, 0.1x, 0.01x). Input is already a low-depth experimental Hi-C dataset rather than a high-resolution reference from which downsampled simulations are derived The analysis goal is compartment inference on a single full-depth dataset rather than robustness/validation testing across depths Downsampling would be applied directly to the interaction summary without preserving the HOMER HiCsummary format required by CscoreTool-M Simulate reduced-depth Hi-C datasets by downsampling reads (e.g. 0.5%-selected reads from the Rao 2014 GM12878 high-resolution dataset) to test whether CscoreTool-M sub-compartment inference is robust to sequencing depth. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Simulate reduced-depth Hi-C datasets by downsampling reads (e.g. 0.5%-selected reads from the Rao 2014 GM12878 high-resolution dataset) to test whether CscoreTool-M sub-compartment inference is robust to sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a low-depth experimental Hi-C dataset rather than a high-resolution reference from which downsampled simulations are derived The analysis goal is compartment inference on a single full-depth dataset rather than robustness/validation testing across depths Downsampling would be applied directly to the interaction summary without preserving the HOMER HiCsummary format required by CscoreTool-M

skills.description: Use when validating that a broad-domain caller (e.g., RECOGNICER on H3K27me3/H3K9me3 ChIP-seq) is robust to sequencing depth by downsampling mapped reads and comparing aggregate domain length and FRIP across depths.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-downsampling
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-downsampling Use when validating that a broad-domain caller (e.g., RECOGNICER on H3K27me3/H3K9me3 ChIP-seq) is robust to sequencing depth by downsampling mapped reads and comparing aggregate domain length and FRIP across depths. Calling peaks on the downsampled data for discovery purposes — downsampling here is strictly a robustness/replication test, not a depth-normalization or peak-calling strategy The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) — the method operates on already-mapped reads (BED); remapping each downsampled subset is a different question not covered here Peak-caller robustness to narrow, punctate marks — the article frames RECOGNICER and this test around broad domains from kb to Mb such as H3K27me3 and H3K9me3 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Robustness assessment in which a mapped ChIP-seq dataset is randomly downsampled (e.g., human CD4+ T cell H3K27me3 from 17.23M to 4M reads) and a broad-domain caller is re-run at each depth to test invariance of total aggregate domain length and FRIP score. epigenomics/v2 10.1007/s40484-020-0225-2
skills.summary: Robustness assessment in which a mapped ChIP-seq dataset is randomly downsampled (e.g., human CD4+ T cell H3K27me3 from 17.23M to 4M reads) and a broad-domain caller is re-run at each depth to test invariance of total aggregate domain length and FRIP score.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Calling peaks on the downsampled data for discovery purposes — downsampling here is strictly a robustness/replication test, not a depth-normalization or peak-calling strategy The input is raw sequencing data (FASTQ) — the method operates on already-mapped reads (BED); remapping each downsampled subset is a different question not covered here Peak-caller robustness to narrow, punctate marks — the article frames RECOGNICER and this test around broad domains from kb to Mb such as H3K27me3 and H3K9me3

skills.description: Decision support for whether a ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metric like FRiP is a genuine quality readout or merely an artifact of sequencing depth, especially when benchmarking shallow libraries or choosing downsampling conventions.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-downsampling-simulation
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-downsampling-simulation Decision support for whether a ChIP-seq/DNase-seq QC metric like FRiP is a genuine quality readout or merely an artifact of sequencing depth, especially when benchmarking shallow libraries or choosing downsampling conventions. Input data is not ChIP-seq/DNase-seq with callable peaks — FRiP is undefined without a peak set The goal is to measure absolute library quality rather than depth-dependence of a QC metric; ChiLin's standard one-shot FRiP step suffices Peak regions are not comparable across samples (e.g. mixing broad and narrow peak types, when MACS2 narrow is the ChiLin TF default) http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Simulates sequencing-depth variation by sub-sampling BAM (or FASTQ) files at stepwise depths and comparing QC metrics — such as FRiP scores — computed against peaks called per-depth versus peaks called once from the full-depth BAM, exposing how metric stability depends on peak-calling strategy. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1274-4
skills.summary: Simulates sequencing-depth variation by sub-sampling BAM (or FASTQ) files at stepwise depths and comparing QC metrics — such as FRiP scores — computed against peaks called per-depth versus peaks called once from the full-depth BAM, exposing how metric stability depends on peak-calling strategy.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is not ChIP-seq/DNase-seq with callable peaks — FRiP is undefined without a peak set The goal is to measure absolute library quality rather than depth-dependence of a QC metric; ChiLin's standard one-shot FRiP step suffices Peak regions are not comparable across samples (e.g. mixing broad and narrow peak types, when MACS2 narrow is the ChiLin TF default)

skills.description: Use when scoring/predicting chromatin loops on a new Hi-C, Micro-C, or DNA SPRITE contact map (.cool/.hic) in a cell type or species different from the training set, and a depth-matched pre-trained model must be chosen.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-matched-model-selection
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-matched-model-selection Use when scoring/predicting chromatin loops on a new Hi-C, Micro-C, or DNA SPRITE contact map (.cool/.hic) in a cell type or species different from the training set, and a depth-matched pre-trained model must be chosen. The contact map has fewer than ~30 million intrachromosomal reads, where loop detection at high resolution is unreliable even with the depth-robust models You are training a new model from scratch rather than applying an existing pre-trained model — use the train workflow instead Selects the appropriate pre-trained Peakachu Random Forest loop-prediction model by first measuring the total number of intra-chromosomal contacts in a Hi-C contact map, since Peakachu models are robust to sequencing depth only when matched to it (usable down to ~30 million intrachromosomal reads). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-17239-9
skills.summary: Selects the appropriate pre-trained Peakachu Random Forest loop-prediction model by first measuring the total number of intra-chromosomal contacts in a Hi-C contact map, since Peakachu models are robust to sequencing depth only when matched to it (usable down to ~30 million intrachromosomal reads).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The contact map has fewer than ~30 million intrachromosomal reads, where loop detection at high resolution is unreliable even with the depth-robust models You are training a new model from scratch rather than applying an existing pre-trained model — use the train workflow instead

skills.description: Use when computing normalized ChIP-seq signal (buildChIPprofile, recoverChIPlevels, meta-plots, boxplots) from BAM files of samples sequenced at different depths, or when down-sampling to test depth requirements.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-normalization
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-normalization Use when computing normalized ChIP-seq signal (buildChIPprofile, recoverChIPlevels, meta-plots, boxplots) from BAM files of samples sequenced at different depths, or when down-sampling to test depth requirements. The experiment includes spike-in material (e.g. MTF2 samples) — use the spike-in genome read counts as the normalization factor instead of total BAM depth Input data is already a normalized profile (e.g. bigWig/BedGraph) rather than a raw mapped BAM, so depth normalization would double-normalize the signal http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Normalizes ChIP-seq/NGS signal values by sequencing depth (total mapped reads in the BAM) before generating SeqCode profiles, region-level counts, and plots, ensuring comparability across samples sequenced at different depths; spike-in read counts over an exogenous genome can substitute as the normalization factor. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Normalizes ChIP-seq/NGS signal values by sequencing depth (total mapped reads in the BAM) before generating SeqCode profiles, region-level counts, and plots, ensuring comparability across samples sequenced at different depths; spike-in read counts over an exogenous genome can substitute as the normalization factor.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The experiment includes spike-in material (e.g. MTF2 samples) — use the spike-in genome read counts as the normalization factor instead of total BAM depth Input data is already a normalized profile (e.g. bigWig/BedGraph) rather than a raw mapped BAM, so depth normalization would double-normalize the signal

skills.description: Use when a SnapATAC cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel must be normalized for per-cell sequencing-depth bias before spectral dimensionality reduction of scATAC-seq data.
skills.name: sequencing-depth-regression-normalization
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-regression-normalization Use when a SnapATAC cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel must be normalized for per-cell sequencing-depth bias before spectral dimensionality reduction of scATAC-seq data. Input is already a normalized feature matrix or embedding rather than a raw cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel — re-normalizing would double-correct depth effects Peak-by-cell count matrices from predefined population-level peaks — this skill is designed for the peak-free, genome-wide bin Jaccard framework of SnapATAC When using SnapATAC2, which replaces the Jaccard kernel with a matrix-free spectral embedding algorithm and does not expose runNormJaccard http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Regression-based sequencing-depth normalization of the cell-by-cell Jaccard similarity kernel in SnapATAC, followed by row centering and scaling (runNormJaccard), so that eigendecomposition is not dominated by per-cell differences in sequencing depth. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: Regression-based sequencing-depth normalization of the cell-by-cell Jaccard similarity kernel in SnapATAC, followed by row centering and scaling (runNormJaccard), so that eigendecomposition is not dominated by per-cell differences in sequencing depth.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a normalized feature matrix or embedding rather than a raw cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel — re-normalizing would double-correct depth effects Peak-by-cell count matrices from predefined population-level peaks — this skill is designed for the peak-free, genome-wide bin Jaccard framework of SnapATAC When using SnapATAC2, which replaces the Jaccard kernel with a matrix-free spectral embedding algorithm and does not expose runNormJaccard

skills.description: Use when evaluating loop-calling model robustness on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch performance across sequencing depths (e.g., 1.5% / 39M reads up to 520M reads).
skills.name: sequencing-depth-robustness-analysis
skills.search_text: sequencing-depth-robustness-analysis Use when evaluating loop-calling model robustness on downsampled Hi-C contact maps, or when comparing graph-view vs image-view branch performance across sequencing depths (e.g., 1.5% / 39M reads up to 520M reads). Input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — the paper states GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and cannot handle extremely sparse scHi-C The targeted cell line's sequencing depth does not match any pre-trained model in the repository and retraining is out of scope — the paper flags weak usability in this case Only full-depth loop calling without any depth-variation or robustness question — a standard loop caller benchmark suffices http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 A skill for assessing how CTCF-mediated chromatin loop calling performance degrades or shifts across downsampled Hi-C sequencing depths, using GILoop's dual-branch (GCN graph view + U-Net image view) model and its matrix downsampling function. It reproduces the paper's depth-preference findings by tracking PR-AUC and MAD smoothness as depth decreases. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2022.105535
skills.summary: A skill for assessing how CTCF-mediated chromatin loop calling performance degrades or shifts across downsampled Hi-C sequencing depths, using GILoop's dual-branch (GCN graph view + U-Net image view) model and its matrix downsampling function. It reproduces the paper's depth-preference findings by tracking PR-AUC and MAD smoothness as depth decreases.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) data — the paper states GILoop only focuses on bulk Hi-C and cannot handle extremely sparse scHi-C The targeted cell line's sequencing depth does not match any pre-trained model in the repository and retraining is out of scope — the paper flags weak usability in this case Only full-depth loop calling without any depth-variation or robustness question — a standard loop caller benchmark suffices

skills.description: Use when you have genomic coordinates of systematic sequencing errors (e.g. the 3272 monocyte SSE positions on Hg18) and need paired signal/control FASTA inputs for fixed-position IUPAC motif discovery.
skills.name: sequencing-error-region-sequence-extraction
skills.search_text: sequencing-error-region-sequence-extraction Use when you have genomic coordinates of systematic sequencing errors (e.g. the 3272 monocyte SSE positions on Hg18) and need paired signal/control FASTA inputs for fixed-position IUPAC motif discovery. The goal is de novo scanning-mode motif discovery in ChIP-seq peaks rather than motifs at a specific position relative to sequencing errors (DiNAMO's default scanning mode, not fixed-position mode, is appropriate there) The error coordinates and genome build do not match (e.g. Hg18 coordinates lifted onto another assembly), which would corrupt the extracted sequences No control dataset can be assembled — DiNAMO is a discriminative method requiring both a positive and a negative FASTA input http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Builds a positive FASTA dataset by extracting genomic sequences at systematic sequencing error (SSE) positions and a matched control FASTA from non-error regions, so DiNAMO can discover degenerate IUPAC motifs that induce systematic sequencing errors. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Builds a positive FASTA dataset by extracting genomic sequences at systematic sequencing error (SSE) positions and a matched control FASTA from non-error regions, so DiNAMO can discover degenerate IUPAC motifs that induce systematic sequencing errors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo scanning-mode motif discovery in ChIP-seq peaks rather than motifs at a specific position relative to sequencing errors (DiNAMO's default scanning mode, not fixed-position mode, is appropriate there) The error coordinates and genome build do not match (e.g. Hg18 coordinates lifted onto another assembly), which would corrupt the extracted sequences No control dataset can be assembled — DiNAMO is a discriminative method requiring both a positive and a negative FASTA input

skills.description: Use when preparing fragment files for haplotype assembly tools (SpecHap, HapCUT2, FastHare, DCHap, ReFHap) from BAM/CRAM alignments and bgzipped VCF variant calls across diverse sequencing platforms.
skills.name: sequencing-fragment-extraction
skills.search_text: sequencing-fragment-extraction Use when preparing fragment files for haplotype assembly tools (SpecHap, HapCUT2, FastHare, DCHap, ReFHap) from BAM/CRAM alignments and bgzipped VCF variant calls across diverse sequencing platforms. The task is haplotype phasing of polyploid organisms — SpecHap's graph bisection model and ExtractHair's diploid fragment assumptions do not fit increased ploidy The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation detection — the fragment/linkage graph supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Variants and genotypes span multiple individuals — HapCUT2/ExtractHair-based processing expects VCF input for a single diploid individual http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Extract per-fragment allele observations (read-backed haplotype fragments) from aligned reads and variant calls using the modified ExtractHair utility from SpecHap, with technology-specific flags for NGS, Hi-C, 10x linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and ONT data, then sort fragments for downstream haplotype assembly. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Extract per-fragment allele observations (read-backed haplotype fragments) from aligned reads and variant calls using the modified ExtractHair utility from SpecHap, with technology-specific flags for NGS, Hi-C, 10x linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and ONT data, then sort fragments for downstream haplotype assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is haplotype phasing of polyploid organisms — SpecHap's graph bisection model and ExtractHair's diploid fragment assumptions do not fit increased ploidy The goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation detection — the fragment/linkage graph supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Variants and genotypes span multiple individuals — HapCUT2/ExtractHair-based processing expects VCF input for a single diploid individual

skills.description: Use when simulated (wgsim/LRSIM, PBSIM/DeepSimulator) or real sequencing reads must be mapped to a reference genome and produced as sorted, indexed BAM files as a prerequisite for fragment extraction (extractHAIRS) and haplotype assembly.
skills.name: sequencing-read-alignment
skills.search_text: sequencing-read-alignment Use when simulated (wgsim/LRSIM, PBSIM/DeepSimulator) or real sequencing reads must be mapped to a reference genome and produced as sorted, indexed BAM files as a prerequisite for fragment extraction (extractHAIRS) and haplotype assembly. Input is already a sorted, indexed BAM ready for extractHAIRS fragment extraction — skip alignment and proceed to fragment extraction The goal is direct phasing from pre-computed fragment files — this skill covers the upstream read-to-reference mapping step, not phasing itself Data are Hi-C or 10X barcode fragments already in extractHAIRS fragment format; alignment with these tools is not the relevant transformation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Aligns simulated or real sequencing reads to the human reference genome — BWA-MEM for paired-end Illumina short reads and minimap2 for PacBio SMRT and ONT long reads — then coordinate-sorts and indexes the BAMs with samtools/htslib so variant-supporting fragments can be extracted for haplotype phasing with SpecHap. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Aligns simulated or real sequencing reads to the human reference genome — BWA-MEM for paired-end Illumina short reads and minimap2 for PacBio SMRT and ONT long reads — then coordinate-sorts and indexes the BAMs with samtools/htslib so variant-supporting fragments can be extracted for haplotype phasing with SpecHap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a sorted, indexed BAM ready for extractHAIRS fragment extraction — skip alignment and proceed to fragment extraction The goal is direct phasing from pre-computed fragment files — this skill covers the upstream read-to-reference mapping step, not phasing itself Data are Hi-C or 10X barcode fragments already in extractHAIRS fragment format; alignment with these tools is not the relevant transformation

skills.description: Use when you have BAM/SAM reads mapped to a genome with a RefSeq refGene annotation and want standardized TSS-centered heatmaps or aggregated meta-plots of ChIP-seq or RNA-seq signal.
skills.name: sequencing-signal-heatmap-visualization
skills.search_text: sequencing-signal-heatmap-visualization Use when you have BAM/SAM reads mapped to a genome with a RefSeq refGene annotation and want standardized TSS-centered heatmaps or aggregated meta-plots of ChIP-seq or RNA-seq signal. You need genome-wide continuous profiles in bigWig format — the article states this is not yet supported and deferred to future versions Your reads are not yet mapped — quality control, read mapping (e.g. Bowtie) and exclusion of unaligned reads must be completed first You rely on annotations outside the RefSeq catalog — SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generate TSS-centered sequencing signal heatmaps and meta-plots (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIP-seq in mESC) with SeqCode's produceTSSmaps and produceTSSplots, rendering the final graphics via the R scripts emitted into the output folder. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-021-98889-7
skills.summary: Generate TSS-centered sequencing signal heatmaps and meta-plots (e.g. H3K4me3 ChIP-seq in mESC) with SeqCode's produceTSSmaps and produceTSSplots, rendering the final graphics via the R scripts emitted into the output folder.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need genome-wide continuous profiles in bigWig format — the article states this is not yet supported and deferred to future versions Your reads are not yet mapped — quality control, read mapping (e.g. Bowtie) and exclusion of unaligned reads must be completed first You rely on annotations outside the RefSeq catalog — SeqCode relies on RefSeq reference annotations

skills.description: Use when you have male and female ATAC-seq peak-level log2 fold-change tables (young vs old) for the same peak identifiers and need a between-sex correlation of aging signatures plus per-sex DA peak counts.
skills.name: sex-comparative-epigenomic-aging-analysis
skills.search_text: sex-comparative-epigenomic-aging-analysis Use when you have male and female ATAC-seq peak-level log2 fold-change tables (young vs old) for the same peak identifiers and need a between-sex correlation of aging signatures plus per-sex DA peak counts. Input is single-cell or sorted-cell ATAC-seq data — the paper explicitly notes sex differences have not been described at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells, so this bulk-PBMC peak-level correlation does not transfer You need sex-specific biomarker validation (e.g., IL7R, LEF1, TCF7, IL8, IL18) — the paper flags these as unvalidated, requiring future work beyond this correlation skill http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 A method for quantifying how much of the chromatin accessibility aging signature (ATAC-seq on PBMCs) is shared between men and women by correlating young-vs-old log2 fold-changes per sex at the same peak coordinates, and tallying per-sex opening/closing DA peaks. It reproduces the shared-vs-sex-specific structure of immune system aging reported by Márquez et al. 2020. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: A method for quantifying how much of the chromatin accessibility aging signature (ATAC-seq on PBMCs) is shared between men and women by correlating young-vs-old log2 fold-changes per sex at the same peak coordinates, and tallying per-sex opening/closing DA peaks. It reproduces the shared-vs-sex-specific structure of immune system aging reported by Márquez et al. 2020.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell or sorted-cell ATAC-seq data — the paper explicitly notes sex differences have not been described at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells, so this bulk-PBMC peak-level correlation does not transfer You need sex-specific biomarker validation (e.g., IL7R, LEF1, TCF7, IL8, IL18) — the paper flags these as unvalidated, requiring future work beyond this correlation skill

skills.description: Use when flow-cytometry or compositional immune-cell data must be split by sex and age groups (e.g., 65-year cutoff) and non-parametric group differences tested against reported statistics.
skills.name: sex-dimorphism-aging-group-comparison
skills.search_text: sex-dimorphism-aging-group-comparison Use when flow-cytometry or compositional immune-cell data must be split by sex and age groups (e.g., 65-year cutoff) and non-parametric group differences tested against reported statistics. The input is single-cell or sorted-cell data — the paper notes future work is needed to describe these sex differences at single-cell resolution and in sorted cells, so this bulk PBMC-composition skill does not apply The goal is testing monocyte (CD14+/CD16+) differences between older men and women — the article reports no significant differences were detected, so verification of such comparisons will not reproduce a reported finding The analysis requires parametric modeling or covariate adjustment rather than non-parametric two-group rank-sum testing http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduce sex-stratified aging group comparisons on flow-cytometry PBMC cell-type proportions (67 women, 62 men) using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, verifying reported p-values such as the male-specific CD19+ B cell decline after age 65 (p=1.6e-05). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Reproduce sex-stratified aging group comparisons on flow-cytometry PBMC cell-type proportions (67 women, 62 men) using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, verifying reported p-values such as the male-specific CD19+ B cell decline after age 65 (p=1.6e-05).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is single-cell or sorted-cell data — the paper notes future work is needed to describe these sex differences at single-cell resolution and in sorted cells, so this bulk PBMC-composition skill does not apply The goal is testing monocyte (CD14+/CD16+) differences between older men and women — the article reports no significant differences were detected, so verification of such comparisons will not reproduce a reported finding The analysis requires parametric modeling or covariate adjustment rather than non-parametric two-group rank-sum testing

skills.description: Use when PCA has been computed on age-stratified PBMC ATAC-seq or RNA-seq samples and you must verify that PC1 scores correlate with donor age, match reported variance-explained, and differ between older men and older women.
skills.name: sex-dimorphism-pca-interpretation
skills.search_text: sex-dimorphism-pca-interpretation Use when PCA has been computed on age-stratified PBMC ATAC-seq or RNA-seq samples and you must verify that PC1 scores correlate with donor age, match reported variance-explained, and differ between older men and older women. The question concerns cell-type-specific or single-cell resolution sex differences, which the authors explicitly defer to future studies Data are from a single sex or lack donor age/sex metadata, making the older-men-vs-older-women comparison impossible You need mechanistic explanation of inflammaging differences (sex hormones, DAMPs/PAMPs), which the paper leaves unexplored http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 Interpret PC1 of PCA on paired PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq data as an aging gradient and test for a sex difference within older donors, as in Márquez et al. 2020 (Nature Communications). The skill reproduces and validates the claim that age drives shared epigenomic/transcriptomic variation and that men and women diverge after age 65. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Interpret PC1 of PCA on paired PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq data as an aging gradient and test for a sex difference within older donors, as in Márquez et al. 2020 (Nature Communications). The skill reproduces and validates the claim that age drives shared epigenomic/transcriptomic variation and that men and women diverge after age 65.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns cell-type-specific or single-cell resolution sex differences, which the authors explicitly defer to future studies Data are from a single sex or lack donor age/sex metadata, making the older-men-vs-older-women comparison impossible You need mechanistic explanation of inflammaging differences (sex hormones, DAMPs/PAMPs), which the paper leaves unexplored

skills.description: Use when you have two sex-stratified sets of differentially bound calling cards peaks (e.g. female vs male GBM CC Brd4 peaks) and need to identify TF motif families enriched in one sex but not the other.
skills.name: sex-linked-motif-family-comparison
skills.search_text: sex-linked-motif-family-comparison Use when you have two sex-stratified sets of differentially bound calling cards peaks (e.g. female vs male GBM CC Brd4 peaks) and need to identify TF motif families enriched in one sex but not the other. The input is bulk qbed/ccf insertion data that has not yet been peak-called and differentially analyzed — run cc preprocessing (clean_qbed, call_peaks, make_Anndata, filter_peaks, differential peak analysis) first. Only one sex/condition is available — a between-sex comparison via cc.tools.compare_motif cannot be performed. The goal is single-cell clustering or peak-to-gene expression pairing rather than motif family enrichment comparison between peak sets. http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 A motif-comparison skill that calls enriched TF motifs separately on differentially bound Brd4 peaks from female and male glioblastoma calling cards samples (using pycallingcards' HOMER-backed motif calling) and contrasts them to identify sex-specific motif families such as IRF, ETS, TEA, and MADS. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: A motif-comparison skill that calls enriched TF motifs separately on differentially bound Brd4 peaks from female and male glioblastoma calling cards samples (using pycallingcards' HOMER-backed motif calling) and contrasts them to identify sex-specific motif families such as IRF, ETS, TEA, and MADS.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk qbed/ccf insertion data that has not yet been peak-called and differentially analyzed — run cc preprocessing (clean_qbed, call_peaks, make_Anndata, filter_peaks, differential peak analysis) first. Only one sex/condition is available — a between-sex comparison via cc.tools.compare_motif cannot be performed. The goal is single-cell clustering or peak-to-gene expression pairing rather than motif family enrichment comparison between peak sets.

skills.description: Use when comparing chromatin state sequences of protein-coding genes across male and female Roadmap epigenomic samples to test whether same-sex pairs align better than different-sex pairs and identify sex-linked differentially aligned genes.
skills.name: sex-specific-epigenomic-differential-analysis
skills.search_text: sex-specific-epigenomic-differential-analysis Use when comparing chromatin state sequences of protein-coding genes across male and female Roadmap epigenomic samples to test whether same-sex pairs align better than different-sex pairs and identify sex-linked differentially aligned genes. Input includes genes on chromosome Y — the analysis explicitly excludes Y-chromosome genes from the male/female comparison. The question only needs global epigenome similarity (e.g., mark-overlap or correlation summaries) rather than sequential local alignment of compressed chromatin state sequences. Epigenomic signals have not been reduced to chromatin state sequences (e.g., raw ChIP-seq tracks with no ChromHMM segmentation), since EpiAlign operates on discrete state label sequences. http://edamontology.org/topic_3301 Detect differentially aligned chromatin state sequences between male and female Roadmap epigenomes by running EpiAlign local alignments per gene across male-vs-male, female-vs-female, and male-vs-female sample pairs, then testing score groups with a two-sample one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test to surface sex-linked (X-chromosome) differentially aligned genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz287
skills.summary: Detect differentially aligned chromatin state sequences between male and female Roadmap epigenomes by running EpiAlign local alignments per gene across male-vs-male, female-vs-female, and male-vs-female sample pairs, then testing score groups with a two-sample one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test to surface sex-linked (X-chromosome) differentially aligned genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input includes genes on chromosome Y — the analysis explicitly excludes Y-chromosome genes from the male/female comparison. The question only needs global epigenome similarity (e.g., mark-overlap or correlation summaries) rather than sequential local alignment of compressed chromatin state sequences. Epigenomic signals have not been reduced to chromatin state sequences (e.g., raw ChIP-seq tracks with no ChromHMM segmentation), since EpiAlign operates on discrete state label sequences.

skills.description: Use when comparing age-related chromatin accessibility or gene-expression changes between male and female donors to determine whether cell-type-specific loci (e.g., B cell loci) close in one sex and open in the other.
skills.name: sex-stratified-aging-signature-interpretation
skills.search_text: sex-stratified-aging-signature-interpretation Use when comparing age-related chromatin accessibility or gene-expression changes between male and female donors to determine whether cell-type-specific loci (e.g., B cell loci) close in one sex and open in the other. When the goal is shared (non-sex-stratified) aging signatures, such as the common decline in naive T cell loci — that is a single-cohort trend, not a male-vs-female contrast When input is single-cell or sorted-cell data — the article notes its conclusions come from bulk PBMC annotation and that sex differences 'at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells' remain unestablished When comparing cell-composition shifts rather than chromatin accessibility at annotated cell-type-specific loci — use flow cytometry deconvolution instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Method for verifying sex-specific (male vs female) aging signatures in PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq data by testing whether chromHMM cell-type-specific loci (e.g., B cell loci BCL7A, PAX5, CD79A) are enriched among closing DA peaks in men versus opening DA peaks in women, using Fisher's exact tests on the article's Source Data sheets. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Method for verifying sex-specific (male vs female) aging signatures in PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq data by testing whether chromHMM cell-type-specific loci (e.g., B cell loci BCL7A, PAX5, CD79A) are enriched among closing DA peaks in men versus opening DA peaks in women, using Fisher's exact tests on the article's Source Data sheets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is shared (non-sex-stratified) aging signatures, such as the common decline in naive T cell loci — that is a single-cohort trend, not a male-vs-female contrast When input is single-cell or sorted-cell data — the article notes its conclusions come from bulk PBMC annotation and that sex differences 'at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells' remain unestablished When comparing cell-composition shifts rather than chromatin accessibility at annotated cell-type-specific loci — use flow cytometry deconvolution instead

skills.description: Use when a CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa sgRNA screening dataset provides continuous phenotype or activity scores per sgRNA and a classification task (e.g., ROC-AUC evaluation) requires dichotomized activity labels.
skills.name: sgrna-activity-label-binarization
skills.search_text: sgrna-activity-label-binarization Use when a CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa sgRNA screening dataset provides continuous phenotype or activity scores per sgRNA and a classification task (e.g., ROC-AUC evaluation) requires dichotomized activity labels. The downstream task is regression of continuous sgRNA activity/efficiency (e.g., Spearman correlation evaluation) rather than binary classification The dataset already provides binary activity calls or the analysis specifies a different, dataset-specific activity score definition Applying a CRISPRoff-derived cutoff to CRISPRa/CRISPRi data without checking that the phenotype score scale and screen type are comparable http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Converts continuous sgRNA screening phenotype scores (e.g., from CRISPRoff tiling screens) into binary 'highly active' vs. inactive labels using the published cutoff (phenotype score < -0.1 -> class '1'), enabling downstream classification models such as EpiCas-DL's ROC-AUC benchmark against DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Converts continuous sgRNA screening phenotype scores (e.g., from CRISPRoff tiling screens) into binary 'highly active' vs. inactive labels using the published cutoff (phenotype score < -0.1 -> class '1'), enabling downstream classification models such as EpiCas-DL's ROC-AUC benchmark against DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The downstream task is regression of continuous sgRNA activity/efficiency (e.g., Spearman correlation evaluation) rather than binary classification The dataset already provides binary activity calls or the analysis specifies a different, dataset-specific activity score definition Applying a CRISPRoff-derived cutoff to CRISPRa/CRISPRi data without checking that the phenotype score scale and screen type are comparable

skills.description: Use when you must predict sgRNA gene-silencing or activation activity scores (e.g. CRISPRoff_tiling, 111,682 sgRNAs within ±2.5 kb of TSS of 520 genes) from sequence plus cell-type epigenetic tracks, and benchmark regressors by Spearman correlation.
skills.name: sgrna-activity-score-regression-prediction
skills.search_text: sgrna-activity-score-regression-prediction Use when you must predict sgRNA gene-silencing or activation activity scores (e.g. CRISPRoff_tiling, 111,682 sgRNAs within ±2.5 kb of TSS of 520 genes) from sequence plus cell-type epigenetic tracks, and benchmark regressors by Spearman correlation. The prediction target is Cas9 nuclease cutting/indel editing efficiency rather than dCas-mediated gene repression or activation (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa) activity scores The task is binary on-target efficiency classification (AUC evaluation) rather than regression of gene-level normalized activity scores The sgRNAs fall outside ±2.5 kb of a TSS or lack the four epigenetic tracks and cell-line context, so epigenetic channels cannot be populated (use the CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq sequence-only models instead) http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 A deep learning regression skill (EpiCas-DL) that predicts gene-repression/activation sgRNA activity from 11x40 encoded sequence-and-epigenetic feature matrices (one-hot sequence plus nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and gene expression channels), benchmarked against Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, DeepHF, and C-RNNcrispr by Spearman correlation, MSE, and cosine similarity. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: A deep learning regression skill (EpiCas-DL) that predicts gene-repression/activation sgRNA activity from 11x40 encoded sequence-and-epigenetic feature matrices (one-hot sequence plus nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, and gene expression channels), benchmarked against Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, DeepHF, and C-RNNcrispr by Spearman correlation, MSE, and cosine similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The prediction target is Cas9 nuclease cutting/indel editing efficiency rather than dCas-mediated gene repression or activation (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa) activity scores The task is binary on-target efficiency classification (AUC evaluation) rather than regression of gene-level normalized activity scores The sgRNAs fall outside ±2.5 kb of a TSS or lack the four epigenetic tracks and cell-line context, so epigenetic channels cannot be populated (use the CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq sequence-only models instead)

skills.description: Use when sgRNA loci from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens must be assigned cell-type epigenetic values (accessibility, TSS distance, methylation, expression) by genomic interval overlap before model training or prediction.
skills.name: sgrna-genomic-interval-assignment
skills.search_text: sgrna-genomic-interval-assignment Use when sgRNA loci from CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa screens must be assigned cell-type epigenetic values (accessibility, TSS distance, methylation, expression) by genomic interval overlap before model training or prediction. The input is already a normalized sgRNA-by-feature matrix ready for EpiCas-DL — re-running interval assignment would be redundant. Only sequence-based prediction is needed: EpiCas-DL's seq-only models (CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq) require just the one-hot encoded sgRNA sequence, no epigenetic annotation. Cell-type-specific ATACdb/GEO tracks for the sgRNA's cell line are unavailable — assigned epigenetic values would be unreliable for that context. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Annotates each sgRNA target site with seven continuous epigenetic feature channels (4 nucleosome-positioning distances to primary/secondary CAGE TSS, ATACdb chromatin accessibility, WGBS DNA methylation, RNA-seq expression) using pybedtools-based chromosome-position overlap, followed by min-max normalization to [0, 1] for EpiCas-DL input. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Annotates each sgRNA target site with seven continuous epigenetic feature channels (4 nucleosome-positioning distances to primary/secondary CAGE TSS, ATACdb chromatin accessibility, WGBS DNA methylation, RNA-seq expression) using pybedtools-based chromosome-position overlap, followed by min-max normalization to [0, 1] for EpiCas-DL input.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a normalized sgRNA-by-feature matrix ready for EpiCas-DL — re-running interval assignment would be redundant. Only sequence-based prediction is needed: EpiCas-DL's seq-only models (CRISPRoff_seq/CRISPRa_seq) require just the one-hot encoded sgRNA sequence, no epigenetic annotation. Cell-type-specific ATACdb/GEO tracks for the sgRNA's cell line are unavailable — assigned epigenetic values would be unreliable for that context.

skills.description: Use when building or interpreting sgRNA activity prediction models for CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa) and you need epigenetic feature matrices or SHAP-based feature importance for sgRNA design.
skills.name: sgrna-sequence-epigenetic-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: sgrna-sequence-epigenetic-feature-extraction Use when building or interpreting sgRNA activity prediction models for CRISPR-mediated epigenome editing (CRISPRoff/CRISPRi/CRISPRa) and you need epigenetic feature matrices or SHAP-based feature importance for sgRNA design. When the analysis goal is pure sequence-only sgRNA efficiency prediction without epigenetic context (e.g., DeepHF-style sequence models) — this skill requires cell-type-specific epigenetic tracks (ATAC-seq, methylation, expression). When the input is already a ranked feature-importance table and no new sgRNA/epigenetic feature extraction is needed. When working with epigenome editing systems whose key determinants lie outside the four feature types considered (nucleosome occupancy, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA expression), since incomplete epigenetic feature information limited EpiCas-DL performance. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assemble sgRNA sequence encodings together with four epigenetic feature types (nucleosome positioning/distance to TSS, DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, RNA expression) for CRISPR off/i/a datasets, then rank feature contributions to sgRNA activity via Tree SHAP mean |SHAP| values from an XGBoost model. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Assemble sgRNA sequence encodings together with four epigenetic feature types (nucleosome positioning/distance to TSS, DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, RNA expression) for CRISPR off/i/a datasets, then rank feature contributions to sgRNA activity via Tree SHAP mean |SHAP| values from an XGBoost model.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the analysis goal is pure sequence-only sgRNA efficiency prediction without epigenetic context (e.g., DeepHF-style sequence models) — this skill requires cell-type-specific epigenetic tracks (ATAC-seq, methylation, expression). When the input is already a ranked feature-importance table and no new sgRNA/epigenetic feature extraction is needed. When working with epigenome editing systems whose key determinants lie outside the four feature types considered (nucleosome occupancy, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, RNA expression), since incomplete epigenetic feature information limited EpiCas-DL performance.

skills.description: Use when RRBS-derived epiallele proportions phi_s exist per locus per sample (e.g. tumour regions R1-R7 plus normal N) and the goal is to quantify how disordered or heterogeneous each locus/sample is via entropy.
skills.name: shannon-entropy-computation-from-probability-distributions
skills.search_text: shannon-entropy-computation-from-probability-distributions Use when RRBS-derived epiallele proportions phi_s exist per locus per sample (e.g. tumour regions R1-R7 plus normal N) and the goal is to quantify how disordered or heterogeneous each locus/sample is via entropy. The locus has fewer than six CpGs, median read depth below 100, more than 25% missing data, or lies on chromosomes X/Y — these loci are excluded before entropy computation Epiallele proportions are unavailable (e.g. reads were not pooled across tissue samples and modelled with bed_fit/bed_marginal); raw read counts alone cannot be used directly The goal is inter-sample differential comparison of epiallele composition at specific loci rather than a per-sample global disorder measure http://edamontology.org/topic_0625 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Quantifies global epigenetic disorder in multi-region tumour samples by computing the normalised Shannon entropy of epiallele distributions phi_s at each locus, after Bayesian epiallele inference with the bed R package (bed_fit / bed_marginal). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1753-2
skills.summary: Quantifies global epigenetic disorder in multi-region tumour samples by computing the normalised Shannon entropy of epiallele distributions phi_s at each locus, after Bayesian epiallele inference with the bed R package (bed_fit / bed_marginal).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The locus has fewer than six CpGs, median read depth below 100, more than 25% missing data, or lies on chromosomes X/Y — these loci are excluded before entropy computation Epiallele proportions are unavailable (e.g. reads were not pooled across tissue samples and modelled with bed_fit/bed_marginal); raw read counts alone cannot be used directly The goal is inter-sample differential comparison of epiallele composition at specific loci rather than a per-sample global disorder measure

skills.description: Use when a fitted gradient-boosted tree model needs post-hoc interpretation into ranked feature contributions, e.g. identifying which epigenetic features (nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, RNA expression) favor sgRNA silencing efficiency.
skills.name: shap-feature-importance-interpretation
skills.search_text: shap-feature-importance-interpretation Use when a fitted gradient-boosted tree model needs post-hoc interpretation into ranked feature contributions, e.g. identifying which epigenetic features (nucleosome positioning, chromatin accessibility, RNA expression) favor sgRNA silencing efficiency. The model is a deep neural network rather than a tree ensemble — the paper uses DeepSHAP for the deep learning framework instead of Tree SHAP The input is raw sgRNA screening data without a fitted model; SHAP interpretation requires a trained model first Goal is predictive performance benchmarking (e.g. AUC/Spearman comparison against DeepHF or C-RNNcrispr) rather than feature attribution http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Interpret a trained tree-based model (e.g. XGBoost on CRISPRoff sgRNA epigenetic features) by computing Tree SHAP values and ranking features by mean |SHAP| to reveal which epigenetic and sequence features drive sgRNA activity predictions. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Interpret a trained tree-based model (e.g. XGBoost on CRISPRoff sgRNA epigenetic features) by computing Tree SHAP values and ranking features by mean |SHAP| to reveal which epigenetic and sequence features drive sgRNA activity predictions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The model is a deep neural network rather than a tree ensemble — the paper uses DeepSHAP for the deep learning framework instead of Tree SHAP The input is raw sgRNA screening data without a fitted model; SHAP interpretation requires a trained model first Goal is predictive performance benchmarking (e.g. AUC/Spearman comparison against DeepHF or C-RNNcrispr) rather than feature attribution

skills.description: Use when you have a trained EpiCas-DL model (TensorFlow 2.4.1 backend) plus one-hot encoded 40-bp sgRNA sequences (9 bp upstream, 23 bp target, 8 bp downstream) and want position-specific nucleotide contributions explaining sgRNA efficiency predictions.
skills.name: shap-sequence-attribution-analysis
skills.search_text: shap-sequence-attribution-analysis Use when you have a trained EpiCas-DL model (TensorFlow 2.4.1 backend) plus one-hot encoded 40-bp sgRNA sequences (9 bp upstream, 23 bp target, 8 bp downstream) and want position-specific nucleotide contributions explaining sgRNA efficiency predictions. Input is raw sgRNA sequences or activity scores rather than a trained EpiCas-DL model with one-hot encoded inputs — SHAP attribution requires an existing fitted model Interpreting the machine-learning (Gradient Boosting/Random Forest) models — use Tree SHAP via TreeExplainer instead of DeepExplainer Screening datasets other than the CRISPRoff/CRISPRa epigenome-editing contexts, where the reported nucleotide-preference findings may not transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Interprets the trained EpiCas-DL CNN models by computing DeepSHAP per-base, per-position attribution values over one-hot encoded 40-bp sgRNA sequence matrices, to reveal position-specific nucleotide preferences (e.g. PAM-proximal guanine favoring) that drive predicted sgRNA efficiency in CRISPRoff/CRISPRa epigenome editing. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Interprets the trained EpiCas-DL CNN models by computing DeepSHAP per-base, per-position attribution values over one-hot encoded 40-bp sgRNA sequence matrices, to reveal position-specific nucleotide preferences (e.g. PAM-proximal guanine favoring) that drive predicted sgRNA efficiency in CRISPRoff/CRISPRa epigenome editing.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw sgRNA sequences or activity scores rather than a trained EpiCas-DL model with one-hot encoded inputs — SHAP attribution requires an existing fitted model Interpreting the machine-learning (Gradient Boosting/Random Forest) models — use Tree SHAP via TreeExplainer instead of DeepExplainer Screening datasets other than the CRISPRoff/CRISPRa epigenome-editing contexts, where the reported nucleotide-preference findings may not transfer

skills.description: Use when individually analyzed BSP samples (per-sample methylation tables from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP .ab1 trace files) must be gathered into groups, compared statistically, and visualized with publication-ready boxplots, lollipop plots, and methylation profile plots.
skills.name: shiny-app-grouped-analysis-configuration
skills.search_text: shiny-app-grouped-analysis-configuration Use when individually analyzed BSP samples (per-sample methylation tables from direct-BSP or cloning-BSP .ab1 trace files) must be gathered into groups, compared statistically, and visualized with publication-ready boxplots, lollipop plots, and methylation profile plots. Individual samples have not yet been processed by the ABSP 'Individual analysis' tab — grouped analysis gathers pre-computed individual methylation tables, not raw .ab1 trace files The goal is a single sample's CpG methylation table or trimming diagnostics (use the 'Individual analysis' tab with its Sequencing trimming and Methylation tabs instead) Only an arbitrary reference genome is available and per-CpG genomic coordinates matter — use 'CpG numbers' or 'None' labels and disregard coordinates in tables/plots, or handle coordinates separately http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Configure and run the 'Grouped analysis' tab of ABSP's R Shiny app to gather individually analyzed bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) samples into collections, generate lollipop and methylation-profile plots, and run two-by-two Student's t-tests comparing CpG methylation between groups. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad008
skills.summary: Configure and run the 'Grouped analysis' tab of ABSP's R Shiny app to gather individually analyzed bisulfite sequencing PCR (BSP) samples into collections, generate lollipop and methylation-profile plots, and run two-by-two Student's t-tests comparing CpG methylation between groups.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Individual samples have not yet been processed by the ABSP 'Individual analysis' tab — grouped analysis gathers pre-computed individual methylation tables, not raw .ab1 trace files The goal is a single sample's CpG methylation table or trimming diagnostics (use the 'Individual analysis' tab with its Sequencing trimming and Methylation tabs instead) Only an arbitrary reference genome is available and per-CpG genomic coordinates matter — use 'CpG numbers' or 'None' labels and disregard coordinates in tables/plots, or handle coordinates separately

skills.description: Use when a ChIA-PET dataset (e.g. GM12878 CTCF paired-end FASTQ) must be analyzed for very short-range (<8 kb) chromatin loops that standard pipelines miss due to self-ligation span cutoffs.
skills.name: short-range-chromatin-loop-verification
skills.search_text: short-range-chromatin-loop-verification Use when a ChIA-PET dataset (e.g. GM12878 CTCF paired-end FASTQ) must be analyzed for very short-range (<8 kb) chromatin loops that standard pipelines miss due to self-ligation span cutoffs. Input data was generated by a half-linker ChIA-PET protocol and you intend to use Mango-specific assumptions; ChIA-PET2 supports both, but Mango was reported too conservative at significant loop calling The analysis goal is allele-specific chromatin interaction calling rather than short-range loop detection Only long-range (>8 kb) loops are of interest and the default self-ligation cutoff is acceptable — removing the span filter will admit many short-range self-ligation events you would then discard http://edamontology.org/topic_0607 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Detects and validates short-range (<8 kb) CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from ChIA-PET data using the ChIA-PET2 pipeline with the empirical 8 kb self-ligation span filter removed, including MICC2.R statistical significance calling and anchor-level ChIP-seq validation (e.g. the ~1.6 kb MYC loop). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Detects and validates short-range (<8 kb) CTCF-mediated chromatin loops from ChIA-PET data using the ChIA-PET2 pipeline with the empirical 8 kb self-ligation span filter removed, including MICC2.R statistical significance calling and anchor-level ChIP-seq validation (e.g. the ~1.6 kb MYC loop).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data was generated by a half-linker ChIA-PET protocol and you intend to use Mango-specific assumptions; ChIA-PET2 supports both, but Mango was reported too conservative at significant loop calling The analysis goal is allele-specific chromatin interaction calling rather than short-range loop detection Only long-range (>8 kb) loops are of interest and the default self-ligation cutoff is acceptable — removing the span filter will admit many short-range self-ligation events you would then discard

skills.description: Use when ChIP-Seq short-read alignments (BED/ELAND) must be converted into a per-bin coverage profile that reflects fragment-length uncertainty, e.g. before HMM-based peak calling.
skills.name: short-read-directional-extension-to-hdf
skills.search_text: short-read-directional-extension-to-hdf Use when ChIP-Seq short-read alignments (BED/ELAND) must be converted into a per-bin coverage profile that reflects fragment-length uncertainty, e.g. before HMM-based peak calling. When reads are pair-ended with known insert size — HPeak treats the two ends together as ONE fragment, so directional extension/weighting of single reads is unnecessary When the input is already a binned coverage track or peak calls — re-extending reads would double-count coverage When strand orientation within a peak must be distinguished to pinpoint the peak summit — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reconstructs a genome-wide HDF (hypothetical DNA fragment) coverage profile from mapped ChIP-Seq short reads by extending each read directionally from its start position and applying HPeak's unbalanced end-weighting scheme to account for uncertainty in actual DNA fragment lengths. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Reconstructs a genome-wide HDF (hypothetical DNA fragment) coverage profile from mapped ChIP-Seq short reads by extending each read directionally from its start position and applying HPeak's unbalanced end-weighting scheme to account for uncertainty in actual DNA fragment lengths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When reads are pair-ended with known insert size — HPeak treats the two ends together as ONE fragment, so directional extension/weighting of single reads is unnecessary When the input is already a binned coverage track or peak calls — re-extending reads would double-count coverage When strand orientation within a peak must be distinguished to pinpoint the peak summit — the current HPeak algorithm does not distinguish reads of different orientation

skills.description: Use when raw or adapter-trimmed FASTQ reads from ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, DNase-seq, MNase-seq, ATAC-seq, or GRO-seq datasets must be aligned to a reference genome to produce sorted BAMs with alignment statistics.
skills.name: short-read-reference-alignment
skills.search_text: short-read-reference-alignment Use when raw or adapter-trimmed FASTQ reads from ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, DNase-seq, MNase-seq, ATAC-seq, or GRO-seq datasets must be aligned to a reference genome to produce sorted BAMs with alignment statistics. Input is already a sorted BAM or otherwise aligned — the mapping step would be redundant; proceed to mode-specific downstream analysis instead. When real TCGA-like data are being analyzed for discovery — simulation is a validation step, not a driver-discovery method When sample sizes are small or correlation effects are weak — the Sobel test's high AUC was established under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions, so recovery metrics would be unreliable http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Validates an iEDGE-style mediation pipeline by simulating input gene expression data with cis and trans genes having known mediation effects, then checking that the Sobel-test-based recovery reproduces those planted connections and matches the pruning step's significant results. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Validates an iEDGE-style mediation pipeline by simulating input gene expression data with cis and trans genes having known mediation effects, then checking that the Sobel-test-based recovery reproduces those planted connections and matches the pruning step's significant results.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When real TCGA-like data are being analyzed for discovery — simulation is a validation step, not a driver-discovery method When sample sizes are small or correlation effects are weak — the Sobel test's high AUC was established under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions, so recovery metrics would be unreliable

skills.search_text: simulation-based-method-benchmarking Use when a paper claims a deconvolution or inference method outperforms a competitor and you must reproduce the comparison on simulated mixtures with known ground-truth subpopulation profiles, such as 40x GCB-monocyte bisulfite data. The data are real patient samples with unknown ground-truth subpopulations, so reconstruction accuracy cannot be computed against a gold standard The competitor method cannot be run on the input (e.g. methylPurify cannot handle reads longer than 100 bp without the documented code edits, so the comparison would be invalid) http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 Benchmark a deconvolution method (DXM) against a competing method (methylPurify) on simulated bisulfite sequencing mixtures with known ground-truth subpopulation methylation states, quantifying minor-subpopulation reconstruction accuracy to support claims of improved performance. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Benchmark a deconvolution method (DXM) against a competing method (methylPurify) on simulated bisulfite sequencing mixtures with known ground-truth subpopulation methylation states, quantifying minor-subpopulation reconstruction accuracy to support claims of improved performance.

skills.description: Use when you need to validate an analytic power-analysis method for multi-sample scRNA-seq DE studies against ground-truth simulations, or when you must quantify the runtime/memory cost of simulation-based power tools.
skills.name: simulation-based-single-cell-power-analysis
skills.search_text: simulation-based-single-cell-power-analysis Use when you need to validate an analytic power-analysis method for multi-sample scRNA-seq DE studies against ground-truth simulations, or when you must quantify the runtime/memory cost of simulation-based power tools. The goal is rapid power evaluation across many design options — simulation-based tools have long runtimes and are unsuitable for optimizing parameter combinations; use the analytic method instead The target design involves hundreds of samples (e.g. eQTL-scale studies) — such data sets will be very difficult to simulate with simulation-based tools Sample sizes far exceed the pilot data underlying the priors — data driven priors only allow reliable power assessment for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot study http://edamontology.org/topic_3517 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Benchmark simulation-based power estimation for multi-sample single cell differential expression by simulating count data with powsimR and muscat over a sample-size/cell-number grid and comparing expected expressed genes, DE power, and overall detection power against scPower's analytic estimates, while recording runtime and memory cost. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Benchmark simulation-based power estimation for multi-sample single cell differential expression by simulating count data with powsimR and muscat over a sample-size/cell-number grid and comparing expected expressed genes, DE power, and overall detection power against scPower's analytic estimates, while recording runtime and memory cost.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is rapid power evaluation across many design options — simulation-based tools have long runtimes and are unsuitable for optimizing parameter combinations; use the analytic method instead The target design involves hundreds of samples (e.g. eQTL-scale studies) — such data sets will be very difficult to simulate with simulation-based tools Sample sizes far exceed the pilot data underlying the priors — data driven priors only allow reliable power assessment for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot study

skills.description: Use when validating a statistical test (e.g., Sobel mediation) whose performance depends on sample size and effect strength, by simulating positive/negative controls over a parameter grid and computing per-cell performance metrics.
skills.name: simulation-parameter-grid-sweep
skills.search_text: simulation-parameter-grid-sweep Use when validating a statistical test (e.g., Sobel mediation) whose performance depends on sample size and effect strength, by simulating positive/negative controls over a parameter grid and computing per-cell performance metrics. The input is real experimental data with no known mediation ground truth — simulation-based validation requires known positive/negative pairs The statistical test's performance does not plausibly depend on sample size or effect correlation, so a parameter sweep adds no information The goal is driver discovery on real multi-omics data (use the full iEDGE run_iEDGE pipeline instead of a simulation grid) http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Simulates synthetic mediation ground truth (true-positive and true-negative pairs) across a two-dimensional grid of effect correlation and sample size, then evaluates the Sobel test of mediation (via iEDGE's calc_sobel) per grid cell to characterize sensitivity, specificity, and AUC as a function of those parameters. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Simulates synthetic mediation ground truth (true-positive and true-negative pairs) across a two-dimensional grid of effect correlation and sample size, then evaluates the Sobel test of mediation (via iEDGE's calc_sobel) per grid cell to characterize sensitivity, specificity, and AUC as a function of those parameters.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is real experimental data with no known mediation ground truth — simulation-based validation requires known positive/negative pairs The statistical test's performance does not plausibly depend on sample size or effect correlation, so a parameter sweep adds no information The goal is driver discovery on real multi-omics data (use the full iEDGE run_iEDGE pipeline instead of a simulation grid)

The goal is novel biological annotation of a new dataset rather than benchmarking method accuracy against a curated reference No manually curated reference cell types are available for the dataset, so consistent rates cannot be computed The evaluation target is marker-gene identification quality (where Seurat is the comparator) rather than cluster-level annotation accuracy http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Reproduce the cluster-level consistent-rate comparison of scCATCH against cell-based annotation methods (CellAssign, Garnett, SingleR, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn benchmark datasets, following the scCATCH_performance_comparison workflow and Table 1 conventions. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Reproduce the cluster-level consistent-rate comparison of scCATCH against cell-based annotation methods (CellAssign, Garnett, SingleR, scMap, CHETAH) on the Chen, Xin, and Gierahn benchmark datasets, following the scCATCH_performance_comparison workflow and Table 1 conventions.

skills.search_text: single-cell-atac-cell-type-signature-enrichment Use when a selected cisTopic LDA model exists for a scATAC-seq dataset and you must quantify per-cell enrichment of external epigenomic signatures (marker gene sets or bulk ATAC profiles) to assign or visualize cell-type identity. skills.description: Use when you have a normalized binned single-cell ATAC-seq matrix and need to call CNVs per cell to identify malignant subclones, focal amplifications, or arm-level chromosome gains/losses without a matched control file.
skills.name: single-cell-atac-copy-number-calling
skills.search_text: single-cell-atac-copy-number-calling Use when you have a normalized binned single-cell ATAC-seq matrix and need to call CNVs per cell to identify malignant subclones, focal amplifications, or arm-level chromosome gains/losses without a matched control file. The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot be used in this case per the article's discussion. The goal is copy number calling from scRNA-seq rather than scATAC data (other dedicated tools exist for that modality). The input is already a curated CNV profile or feature table rather than raw/binned scATAC accessibility data. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Infers copy number variants (CNVs) — including focal amplifications and chromosome arm-level gains/losses — from single-cell ATAC-seq data using the Copy-scAT R package, enabling discrimination of malignant from nonmalignant cells and subclone deconvolution in cancer. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Infers copy number variants (CNVs) — including focal amplifications and chromosome arm-level gains/losses — from single-cell ATAC-seq data using the Copy-scAT R package, enabling discrimination of malignant from nonmalignant cells and subclone deconvolution in cancer.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot be used in this case per the article's discussion. The goal is copy number calling from scRNA-seq rather than scATAC data (other dedicated tools exist for that modality). The input is already a curated CNV profile or feature table rather than raw/binned scATAC accessibility data.

skills.summary: Preprocess raw single-cell ATAC-seq data into a normalized, filtered binned accessibility matrix suitable for Copy-scAT copy number inference, including cell filtering, matrix normalization, and collapsing of binned signal to chromosome-arm level.

skills.description: Use when single-cell ATAC peak sets need to be separated into cell-type-specific CREs and you need an interpretable, motif-based model that names the TF motifs (e.g. MEF2C, NKX2-5, GATA, FLI1) driving the classification.
skills.name: single-cell-atac-enhancer-classification
skills.search_text: single-cell-atac-enhancer-classification Use when single-cell ATAC peak sets need to be separated into cell-type-specific CREs and you need an interpretable, motif-based model that names the TF motifs (e.g. MEF2C, NKX2-5, GATA, FLI1) driving the classification. When the question requires regulatory information beyond the input sequence (e.g. open chromatin status, histone marks, or distal influences outside the CRE) — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence. When discovering novel sequence patterns unrepresented in current motif annotations is the goal — the reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif libraries. When motif order, orientation, or spacing (motif grammar) matters — BOM represents each sequence as an unordered set of motif counts and integration with motif grammar remains a future direction. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Classify cell-type-specific distal cis-regulatory elements from single-cell ATAC data by representing each CRE as unordered transcription factor motif counts (via FIMO scanning against gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) and training gradient-boosted tree (XGBoost) models with the BOM R package, then interpreting motif importance with SHAP. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Classify cell-type-specific distal cis-regulatory elements from single-cell ATAC data by representing each CRE as unordered transcription factor motif counts (via FIMO scanning against gimme.vertebrate.v5.0.meme) and training gradient-boosted tree (XGBoost) models with the BOM R package, then interpreting motif importance with SHAP.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question requires regulatory information beyond the input sequence (e.g. open chromatin status, histone marks, or distal influences outside the CRE) — BOM is constrained to cis-regulatory information within the input sequence. When discovering novel sequence patterns unrepresented in current motif annotations is the goal — the reliance on known TF motifs neglects informative sequences not captured by current motif libraries. When motif order, orientation, or spacing (motif grammar) matters — BOM represents each sequence as an unordered set of motif counts and integration with motif grammar remains a future direction.
