skills.description: Use when the input is a sparse, near-binary scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder) and the goal is denoising/imputation of missing accessibility values for downstream correlation or clustering evaluation.

skills.search_text: single-cell-atac-seq-imputation Use when the input is a sparse, near-binary scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder) and the goal is denoising/imputation of missing accessibility values for downstream correlation or clustering evaluation. skills.description: Use when single-cell histone-modification datasets (e.g. scCUT&Tag GSE124680 vs GSE124690 replicates) contain distinct technical batches that must be merged before UMAP projection or clustering without losing true K562-vs-H1 biological separation.
skills.name: single-cell-batch-correction-fastmnn
skills.search_text: single-cell-batch-correction-fastmnn Use when single-cell histone-modification datasets (e.g. scCUT&Tag GSE124680 vs GSE124690 replicates) contain distinct technical batches that must be merged before UMAP projection or clustering without losing true K562-vs-H1 biological separation. The dataset contains only a single batch/replicate — mutual nearest neighbor correction has nothing to merge and can distort the embedding. Batch is fully confounded with biology (each batch contains a distinct cell type), so correction would remove the very population differences (e.g. K562 vs H1) you want to recover. Input is raw unfiltered reads or an unnormalized count matrix — normalization and centered PCA (50 PCs) must precede FastMNN in the ChromSCape workflow. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Merge single-cell epigenomic batches (e.g. two K562 scCUT&Tag replicates) by applying FastMNN mutual-nearest-neighbors batch correction, as implemented in ChromSCape via the batchelor R package, on a centered PCA embedding of normalized H3K27me3/H3K4me3 count matrices. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Merge single-cell epigenomic batches (e.g. two K562 scCUT&Tag replicates) by applying FastMNN mutual-nearest-neighbors batch correction, as implemented in ChromSCape via the batchelor R package, on a centered PCA embedding of normalized H3K27me3/H3K4me3 count matrices.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The dataset contains only a single batch/replicate — mutual nearest neighbor correction has nothing to merge and can distort the embedding. Batch is fully confounded with biology (each batch contains a distinct cell type), so correction would remove the very population differences (e.g. K562 vs H1) you want to recover. Input is raw unfiltered reads or an unnormalized count matrix — normalization and centered PCA (50 PCs) must precede FastMNN in the ChromSCape workflow.

skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-analysis Use when scATAC clustering may be driven by CNVs rather than genuine accessibility states, and you need to test cluster stability by removing CNV-bearing chromosome peaks and comparing pre/post-reclustering assignments via AMI. Malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot infer CNVs there, so CNV-peak removal is undefined Clustering is based on motif activity scores (e.g., ChromVAR), where CNV effects are less pronounced and peak removal is not the relevant control The input is already a CNV-free feature matrix with no need to test CNV confounding http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Recluster single-cell ATAC-seq data after removing CNV-harboring chromosome peaks to test whether copy number variants confound clustering, quantifying cluster stability with adjusted mutual information (AMI) against a reference value (0.634 in Copy-scAT Fig. 4I). epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Recluster single-cell ATAC-seq data after removing CNV-harboring chromosome peaks to test whether copy number variants confound clustering, quantifying cluster stability with adjusted mutual information (AMI) against a reference value (0.634 in Copy-scAT Fig. 4I).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT cannot infer CNVs there, so CNV-peak removal is undefined Clustering is based on motif activity scores (e.g., ChromVAR), where CNV effects are less pronounced and peak removal is not the relevant control The input is already a CNV-free feature matrix with no need to test CNV confounding

skills.description: Use when clustering scATAC-seq data (e.g. the Forebrain.h5ad dataset, 2088 cells, k=8) and you need to compare SCALE against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, or SC3 using ARI/NMI/F1 metrics against reference labels.
skills.name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
skills.search_text: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking Use when clustering scATAC-seq data (e.g. the Forebrain.h5ad dataset, 2088 cells, k=8) and you need to compare SCALE against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, or SC3 using ARI/NMI/F1 metrics against reference labels. The input is scRNA-seq data requiring online multi-dataset integration — use SCALEX instead, which is designed for projecting heterogeneous datasets into a common cell-embedding space. You need explicit identification and removal of batch effects from the input data — SCALE is not specifically designed to identify and remove these artifacts. chromVAR-style motif-level analysis of peak groups rather than whole-dataset cell clustering is the goal. http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Benchmarks SCALE — a VAE+Gaussian Mixture Model method for single-cell ATAC-seq latent feature extraction — against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, and SC3 clustering tools, scoring cluster assignments against reference cell-type labels with ARI, NMI, and micro-F1. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12630-7
skills.summary: Benchmarks SCALE — a VAE+Gaussian Mixture Model method for single-cell ATAC-seq latent feature extraction — against scABC, scVI, cisTopic, and SC3 clustering tools, scoring cluster assignments against reference cell-type labels with ARI, NMI, and micro-F1.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is scRNA-seq data requiring online multi-dataset integration — use SCALEX instead, which is designed for projecting heterogeneous datasets into a common cell-embedding space. You need explicit identification and removal of batch effects from the input data — SCALE is not specifically designed to identify and remove these artifacts. chromVAR-style motif-level analysis of peak groups rather than whole-dataset cell clustering is the goal.

skills.summary: Clusters cells from single-cell Calling Cards (scCC) experiments using Scanpy on matched scRNA-seq data, so that Brd4 (or other TF) insertion counts can be grouped by cortical cell type and paired with cell-type-specific peaks via Pycallingcards.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Calling Cards data rather than single-cell qbed/insertions with matched scRNA-seq — cell-type clustering is not applicable. Input is bulk RNA-seq or already-aggregated expression data rather than cell-level single-cell counts — Seurat's FindAllMarkers per-cell Wilcoxon framework does not apply The goal is to rank REMs or identify enriched TF motifs from pre-existing REM sequences (use EpiRegio Region Query plus PASTAA instead of DE analysis) Gene identifiers or Seurat identity (condition) assignments have not been established, since incorrect identifiers are a stated failure mode of the downstream Gene Query http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Identifies genes differentially expressed between cell conditions in single-cell RNA-seq data using Seurat's FindAllMarkers with the Wilcoxon Rank Sum test, producing a filtered gene list (e.g. 304 genes at P ≤ 0.01 for TGF-β-treated vs untreated HUVECs) suitable for downstream REM retrieval via EpiRegio's Gene Query. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382

skills.name: single-cell-epigenomic-data-ingestion
skills.search_text: single-cell-epigenomic-data-ingestion Use when raw single-cell epigenomic data (paired-end FASTQ or per-cell BED files from GEO accessions like GSE124680, GSE124690, GSE105012) must be converted into count matrices for ChromSCape-based subpopulation analysis. Input is already a count matrix or feature table — skip ingestion and load directly into ChromSCape Data are single-cell RNA-seq or other non-chromatin modalities; existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are also not fit for the low coverage and sparsity of single-cell histone modification datasets Peak calling is required but only BED files (no BAM) are available — the ChromSCape peak calling module requires user-supplied BAM files with barcode-labeled reads http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Ingest public single-cell histone modification datasets (scCUT&Tag, scChIC-seq, scChIP-seq) as gzipped single-cell BED files from GEO into ChromSCape, building count matrices by aggregating signal around gene TSS (±2500bp) or into successive 50kbp genomic bins before downstream clustering. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x
skills.summary: Ingest public single-cell histone modification datasets (scCUT&Tag, scChIC-seq, scChIP-seq) as gzipped single-cell BED files from GEO into ChromSCape, building count matrices by aggregating signal around gene TSS (±2500bp) or into successive 50kbp genomic bins before downstream clustering.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a count matrix or feature table — skip ingestion and load directly into ChromSCape Data are single-cell RNA-seq or other non-chromatin modalities; existing bulk ChIP-seq tools are also not fit for the low coverage and sparsity of single-cell histone modification datasets Peak calling is required but only BED files (no BAM) are available — the ChromSCape peak calling module requires user-supplied BAM files with barcode-labeled reads

skills.description: Use when fitting/validating scPower's expression probability priors on a new atlas count matrix (e.g., Drop-seq, Smart-seq2, 10X) to verify predicted expressed gene numbers match observed counts before power analysis.
skills.name: single-cell-expression-probability-model-fitting
skills.search_text: single-cell-expression-probability-model-fitting Use when fitting/validating scPower's expression probability priors on a new atlas count matrix (e.g., Drop-seq, Smart-seq2, 10X) to verify predicted expressed gene numbers match observed counts before power analysis. The goal is simulation-based power analysis rather than analytic expression probability fitting (simulation tools like muscat and powsimR have long runtimes and high memory requirements, e.g., 35-48 GB for 20 samples x 3000 cells) The input is effect size priors for DEG/eQTL power (use scPower's de.ref.study reference studies such as Pancreas_alphabeta or 10X_PBMC_1 instead of fitting expression priors) The data are not single-cell count matrices (scPower priors require cell-level counts with donor and cell-type annotations; continuous annotations like pseudo time would need to be discretized first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Fit scPower's expression probability model to single-cell RNA-seq count matrices from droplet-based (UMI) or read-count (Smart-seq2) technologies, then validate predicted expressed gene numbers against observed counts (r2 ~0.995 for Drop-seq lung, ~0.991 for Smart-seq2 pancreas). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Fit scPower's expression probability model to single-cell RNA-seq count matrices from droplet-based (UMI) or read-count (Smart-seq2) technologies, then validate predicted expressed gene numbers against observed counts (r2 ~0.995 for Drop-seq lung, ~0.991 for Smart-seq2 pancreas).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is simulation-based power analysis rather than analytic expression probability fitting (simulation tools like muscat and powsimR have long runtimes and high memory requirements, e.g., 35-48 GB for 20 samples x 3000 cells) The input is effect size priors for DEG/eQTL power (use scPower's de.ref.study reference studies such as Pancreas_alphabeta or 10X_PBMC_1 instead of fitting expression priors) The data are not single-cell count matrices (scPower priors require cell-level counts with donor and cell-type annotations; continuous annotations like pseudo time would need to be discretized first)

skills.description: Use when starting from per-cell tab-separated single-cell Hi-C contact files (chromosome and mapped-position columns) that must be converted to binned contact matrices at 10-kb resolution prior to imputation or loop calling.
skills.name: single-cell-hic-contact-binning
skills.search_text: single-cell-hic-contact-binning Use when starting from per-cell tab-separated single-cell Hi-C contact files (chromosome and mapped-position columns) that must be converted to binned contact matrices at 10-kb resolution prior to imputation or loop calling. Input is bulk Hi-C or already-binned .hic/.cool contact matrices rather than per-single-cell raw contact lists The goal is diploid/haplotype-resolved 3D genome reconstruction (use Dip-C or hickit instead of SnapHiC binning) A resolution other than 10 kb is required without regenerated mappability/filter files — the provided filter files cover mm10, hg19 and hg38 only at 10-kb resolution with MboI http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 Bins per-single-cell mapped read-pair contacts into fixed 10-kb genomic bins as the first step of the SnapHiC pipeline, excluding unreliable bins (mappability <=0.8 and ENCODE blacklist overlaps) before downstream RWR imputation and loop calling. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-021-01231-2
skills.summary: Bins per-single-cell mapped read-pair contacts into fixed 10-kb genomic bins as the first step of the SnapHiC pipeline, excluding unreliable bins (mappability <=0.8 and ENCODE blacklist overlaps) before downstream RWR imputation and loop calling.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Hi-C or already-binned .hic/.cool contact matrices rather than per-single-cell raw contact lists The goal is diploid/haplotype-resolved 3D genome reconstruction (use Dip-C or hickit instead of SnapHiC binning) A resolution other than 10 kb is required without regenerated mappability/filter files — the provided filter files cover mm10, hg19 and hg38 only at 10-kb resolution with MboI

skills.description: Use when raw (non-imputed) single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Tan GM12878, Nagano mouse ES, Flyamer, Lee PFC datasets) need hierarchical TAD-like domain calls, and when benchmarking TLD predictors on sparse per-cell data.
skills.name: single-cell-hic-tld-detection
skills.search_text: single-cell-hic-tld-detection Use when raw (non-imputed) single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Tan GM12878, Nagano mouse ES, Flyamer, Lee PFC datasets) need hierarchical TAD-like domain calls, and when benchmarking TLD predictors on sparse per-cell data. Input is bulk Hi-C with deep coverage where hierarchical TAD callers such as deDoc or SuperTAD suffice — deDoc2's sparsity robustness is the reason for choosing it The task requires imputation-dependent embedding pipelines as the primary method (e.g., Higashi embeddings for cell clustering) rather than direct entropy-based TLD calls Stages with too few detectable TLDs (e.g., the '2n DNA' stage excluded in the article) — insufficient TLDs make downstream hierarchy analysis invalid http://edamontology.org/topic_3420 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Detect TAD-like domains (TLDs) in single-cell Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2, a structural-information-theory tool that treats the contact map as a weighted graph and globally minimizes 2D structural entropy via dynamic programming, without data imputation. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Detect TAD-like domains (TLDs) in single-cell Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2, a structural-information-theory tool that treats the contact map as a weighted graph and globally minimizes 2D structural entropy via dynamic programming, without data imputation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is bulk Hi-C with deep coverage where hierarchical TAD callers such as deDoc or SuperTAD suffice — deDoc2's sparsity robustness is the reason for choosing it The task requires imputation-dependent embedding pipelines as the primary method (e.g., Higashi embeddings for cell clustering) rather than direct entropy-based TLD calls Stages with too few detectable TLDs (e.g., the '2n DNA' stage excluded in the article) — insufficient TLDs make downstream hierarchy analysis invalid

Peak calling is intended with external callers (e.g., MACS-style ChIP-seq callers) rather than the CC-specific CCcaller/MACCs callers designed for CC insertion distributions. http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A Pycallingcards-based workflow that takes raw single-cell calling cards qbed insertion records (e.g., Brd4 GBM data from GEO GSE148448, Moudgil et al., Cell 2020), cleans them, calls and annotates peaks, and builds cell-by-peak AnnData objects for downstream differential binding and peak-gene pairing analysis. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: A Pycallingcards-based workflow that takes raw single-cell calling cards qbed insertion records (e.g., Brd4 GBM data from GEO GSE148448, Moudgil et al., Cell 2020), cleans them, calls and annotates peaks, and builds cell-by-peak AnnData objects for downstream differential binding and peak-gene pairing analysis.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a called/annotated peak table or cell-by-peak feature matrix — skip preprocessing and go directly to tools (tl) differential peak analysis. Analysis targets bulk calling cards data with a different pipeline rather than single-cell qbed preprocessing. Peak calling is intended with external callers (e.g., MACS-style ChIP-seq callers) rather than the CC-specific CCcaller/MACCs callers designed for CC insertion distributions.

skills.search_text: single-cell-quality-control-filtering Use when raw single-cell count matrices (50kbp/5kbp bins or TSS regions) from scChIP-seq/scCUT&Tag/scChIC-seq must be cleaned of low-coverage and outlier cells before dimensionality reduction. Input is already a QC-filtered count matrix from a prior ChromSCape run — reapplying coverage filters could remove valid cells Data is bulk ChIP-seq or scRNA-seq where per-cell read coverage sparsity thresholds (1600 unique reads) do not apply The analysis goal is upstream raw-read processing (FASTQ-to-count-matrix), which requires the scChIPseq_DataEngineering pipeline instead of this QC module ChromSCape's cell- and region-level quality-control filtering for sparse single-cell histone modification data (scChIP-seq, scCUT&Tag, scChIC-seq): enforcing minimum per-cell read coverage, removing top-percentile coverage outliers, and filtering unsupported regions before normalization and PCA. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-19542-x

No matched scRNA-seq data are available for the scATAC-seq sample, so imputed gene expression cannot be fitted The goal is cell-type clustering or dimensionality reduction rather than linking distal elements to putative target genes http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Integrates matched scRNA-seq expression data with scATAC-seq chromatin accessibility in SnapATAC by imputing gene expression from accessibility and binarizing distal enhancer accessibility, then fitting logistic-regression associations between imputed gene expression and linked distal peaks to identify enhancer–gene pairs. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9

skills.search_text: single-cell-rnaseq-power-analysis Use when planning an interindividual single cell RNA-seq differential expression or eQTL study and you need to choose sample size, cells per sample, and sequencing depth to maximize detection power under a fixed budget. The goal is a single-cell-level (not pseudobulk) DE method evaluation — scPower's model is specifically developed for the pseudobulk approach Sample sizes far exceed the pilot/reference study used for priors — data-driven priors only reliably assess power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data The study targets variance QTL detection or continuous annotations like pseudo time — the article did not address variance QTLs (no effect size priors) and pseudo time would need discretization http://edamontology.org/topic_3512 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Analytical power analysis and experimental design optimization for multi-sample single cell RNA-seq DE and eQTL studies using scPower, which multiplies per-gene expression probability by pseudobulk DE/eQTL power and selects the parameter combination (sample size, cells per individual, read depth) maximizing power for a restricted budget. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Analytical power analysis and experimental design optimization for multi-sample single cell RNA-seq DE and eQTL studies using scPower, which multiplies per-gene expression probability by pseudobulk DE/eQTL power and selects the parameter combination (sample size, cells per individual, read depth) maximizing power for a restricted budget.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is a single-cell-level (not pseudobulk) DE method evaluation — scPower's model is specifically developed for the pseudobulk approach Sample sizes far exceed the pilot/reference study used for priors — data-driven priors only reliably assess power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data The study targets variance QTL detection or continuous annotations like pseudo time — the article did not address variance QTLs (no effect size priors) and pseudo time would need discretization

skills.description: Use when input is sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Lee human prefrontal cortex cells) and the goal is to detect hierarchical TAD-like domains per cell and test whether nested TLD features distinguish cell types.
skills.name: single-cell-tld-hierarchical-decoding
skills.search_text: single-cell-tld-hierarchical-decoding Use when input is sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (e.g., Lee human prefrontal cortex cells) and the goal is to detect hierarchical TAD-like domains per cell and test whether nested TLD features distinguish cell types. Input is bulk Hi-C or dense population contact data where standard TAD callers suffice — deDoc2's single-cell hierarchy decoding targets sparse per-cell matrices The goal is allele-specific or haplotype-resolved domain calling, which this structural-entropy workflow does not address The cell yields too few contacts to identify a sufficient number of TLDs (as with '2n DNA' stage cells, which the article excluded from subsequent analysis) http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Decode the hierarchy of TAD-like domains (TLDs) in individual single-cell Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2 (deDoc2.w global partition and deDoc2.s sliding-window partition), then convert each cell's TLD set into a feature vector for cell-type clustering. This skill exists because single-cell Hi-C is too sparse for standard TAD callers and because TLD hierarchy carries cell identity information. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Decode the hierarchy of TAD-like domains (TLDs) in individual single-cell Hi-C contact matrices using deDoc2 (deDoc2.w global partition and deDoc2.s sliding-window partition), then convert each cell's TLD set into a feature vector for cell-type clustering. skills.description: Use when calling candidate driver elements (coding or non-coding) from tumour somatic mutation callsets (WGS or WES, e.g. PCAWG or TCGA) by testing whether per-element mutational burden exceeds a modelled background mutation rate.
skills.name: somatic-mutation-burden-testing
skills.search_text: somatic-mutation-burden-testing Use when calling candidate driver elements (coding or non-coding) from tumour somatic mutation callsets (WGS or WES, e.g. PCAWG or TCGA) by testing whether per-element mutational burden exceeds a modelled background mutation rate. Input is already a driver result table or a precomputed feature table — this skill only covers building BMR models and inferring drivers from raw somatic mutation calls plus element/feature tables Analysis targets negatively selected sites or requires explicit modelling of negative selection — the BMR is trained on predominantly neutral regions and does not model this effect Tumour type has very few samples (<30), where statistical power for burden testing is limited per the paper's discussion http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Combined burden and functional impact testing for cancer driver discovery using DriverPower, which models regional background mutation rates with genomic features (GBM/XGBoost poisson models from 1373 features) and calls coding or non-coding driver elements by testing excess mutational burden adjusted for functional impact scores such as CADD. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-13929-1
skills.summary: Combined burden and functional impact testing for cancer driver discovery using DriverPower, which models regional background mutation rates with genomic features (GBM/XGBoost poisson models from 1373 features) and calls coding or non-coding driver elements by testing excess mutational burden adjusted for functional impact scores such as CADD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a driver result table or a precomputed feature table — this skill only covers building BMR models and inferring drivers from raw somatic mutation calls plus element/feature tables Analysis targets negatively selected sites or requires explicit modelling of negative selection — the BMR is trained on predominantly neutral regions and does not model this effect Tumour type has very few samples (<30), where statistical power for burden testing is limited per the paper's discussion

skills.description: Use when a target finding is tied to a specific figure of a paper with a downloadable Source Data file, and you must verify a directional claim (e.g. male-specific B cell decline) from the published numbers.
skills.name: source-data-reproduction-check
skills.search_text: source-data-reproduction-check Use when a target finding is tied to a specific figure of a paper with a downloadable Source Data file, and you must verify a directional claim (e.g. male-specific B cell decline) from the published numbers. The paper provides no Source Data workbook or figure-level sheets — raw data re-analysis (e.g. re-running differential accessibility from FASTQs) is required instead. The claim depends on cell-type-composition or flow cytometry results not contained in the figure sheets (e.g. monocyte activation differences discussed in the paper's discussion). You need single-cell or sorted-cell resolution; the article's discussion explicitly notes sex differences have not yet been described at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reproduces a published figure's key statistical claims by downloading the article's Source Data workbook (e.g. Fig. 2 from the Nature Communications paper 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9), re-running enrichment and fold-change checks (Fisher's exact test, log2FC sign/significance) in pandas/scipy, and writing a structured pass/fail verification report. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: Reproduces a published figure's key statistical claims by downloading the article's Source Data workbook (e.g. Fig. 2 from the Nature Communications paper 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9), re-running enrichment and fold-change checks (Fisher's exact test, log2FC sign/significance) in pandas/scipy, and writing a structured pass/fail verification report.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The paper provides no Source Data workbook or figure-level sheets — raw data re-analysis (e.g. re-running differential accessibility from FASTQs) is required instead. The claim depends on cell-type-composition or flow cytometry results not contained in the figure sheets (e.g. monocyte activation differences discussed in the paper's discussion). You need single-cell or sorted-cell resolution; the article's discussion explicitly notes sex differences have not yet been described at single-cell resolution or in sorted cells.

skills.description: Use when running bisulfite (WGBS/FASTQ) read alignment on a Spark cluster where uneven partitions — e.g. from HDFS chunk boundaries or post-filtering imbalances — cause some executors to lag and dominate wall-clock time.
skills.name: spark-distributed-data-load-balancing
skills.search_text: spark-distributed-data-load-balancing Use when running bisulfite (WGBS/FASTQ) read alignment on a Spark cluster where uneven partitions — e.g. from HDFS chunk boundaries or post-filtering imbalances — cause some executors to lag and dominate wall-clock time. Input data is already evenly distributed across partitions — re-shuffling only adds overhead since load balancing and shuffling are a trade-off in terms of speed. Small datasets or single-node runs where BiSpark-plain suffices; the paper attributes BiSpark-balance's advantage to large clusters where more nodes wait for the slowest node. The task is alignment accuracy or methylation profiling rather than distributed-execution balancing — this skill alters partition placement, not mapping results. http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Reproduces BiSpark-balance's hash-partitioning load-balancing step, which applies Spark's portable_hash function to re-distribute bisulfite read RDDs almost evenly across cluster executors to minimize straggler delays during 'three-letter' alignment. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2498-2
skills.summary: Reproduces BiSpark-balance's hash-partitioning load-balancing step, which applies Spark's portable_hash function to re-distribute bisulfite read RDDs almost evenly across cluster executors to minimize straggler delays during 'three-letter' alignment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input data is already evenly distributed across partitions — re-shuffling only adds overhead since load balancing and shuffling are a trade-off in terms of speed. Small datasets or single-node runs where BiSpark-plain suffices; the paper attributes BiSpark-balance's advantage to large clusters where more nodes wait for the slowest node. The task is alignment accuracy or methylation profiling rather than distributed-execution balancing — this skill alters partition placement, not mapping results.

skills.search_text: spark-rdd-distributed-processing Use when aligning bisulfite-sequencing (WGBS) reads with the 'three-letter' approach where data volume (up to 4× genome expansion) makes single-node aligners like Bismark or CloudAligner too slow, and a Spark cluster with HDFS is available. skills.search_text: sparse-cholesky-factorization Use when standard errors are needed for a fitted GenoGAM tile (e.g. genogam() output with lambda = 4601, theta = 4.51) but the sparse penalized Hessian is too large for a dense inverse. The model matrix is small enough that a dense matrix inverse is feasible — the sparse inverse subset machinery adds complexity without benefit The task requires off-diagonal covariances of H^-1 outside NZ(H), which the sparse inverse subset algorithm does not evaluate The input is raw count data not yet fitted — use GenoGAMDataSet(), computeSizeFactors(), and genogam() first http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes pointwise standard errors of GenoGAM smooth estimates by sparse Cholesky factorization of the penalized Hessian and evaluating only the inverse elements within the Hessian's sparsity pattern, avoiding explicit full-matrix inversion. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7

skills.when_to_use_negative: The model matrix is small enough that a dense matrix inverse is feasible — the sparse inverse subset machinery adds complexity without benefit The task requires off-diagonal covariances of H^-1 outside NZ(H), which the sparse inverse subset algorithm does not evaluate The input is raw count data not yet fitted — use GenoGAMDataSet(), computeSizeFactors(), and genogam() first

skills.description: Use when fitting penalized GAMs (e.g., negative-binomial ChIP-Seq count models) whose Hessian is sparse, and you need direct sparse solves of the Newton-Raphson system rather than dense matrix inversion.
skills.name: sparse-hessian-linear-system-solving
skills.search_text: sparse-hessian-linear-system-solving Use when fitting penalized GAMs (e.g., negative-binomial ChIP-Seq count models) whose Hessian is sparse, and you need direct sparse solves of the Newton-Raphson system rather than dense matrix inversion. The Hessian or design matrix is dense — sparse storage and SuperLU would add overhead without benefit You need the inverse Hessian itself (e.g., for full covariance estimation) rather than only solving the Newton step Smooth hyperparameters must be estimated from data by cross-validation rather than fixed — this skill covers the fitting step with fixed lambda/theta http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Solves the penalized Newton-Raphson fitting equations of GenoGAM 2.0 by exploiting the sparsity of the model Hessian: instead of forming the inverse Hessian, the sparse linear system is solved directly with SuperLU and all matrices are stored in sparse format to avoid redundant storage of zeros. This is the key trick that makes GenoGAM 2.0 2 to 3 orders of magnitude faster than the previous version. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Solves the penalized Newton-Raphson fitting equations of GenoGAM 2.0 by exploiting the sparsity of the model Hessian: instead of forming the inverse Hessian, the sparse linear system is solved directly with SuperLU and all matrices are stored in sparse format to avoid redundant storage of zeros. This is the key trick that makes GenoGAM 2.0 2 to 3 orders of magnitude faster than the previous version.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The Hessian or design matrix is dense — sparse storage and SuperLU would add overhead without benefit You need the inverse Hessian itself (e.g., for full covariance estimation) rather than only solving the Newton step Smooth hyperparameters must be estimated from data by cross-validation rather than fixed — this skill covers the fitting step with fixed lambda/theta

skills.description: Use when standard errors or variances of fitted smooths are needed from a sparse penalized GAM fit (e.g., GenoGAM tiles with lambda = 4601, theta = 4.51) and explicitly inverting the Hessian would be too slow or memory-intensive.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-inverse-subset-computation
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-inverse-subset-computation Use when standard errors or variances of fitted smooths are needed from a sparse penalized GAM fit (e.g., GenoGAM tiles with lambda = 4601, theta = 4.51) and explicitly inverting the Hessian would be too slow or memory-intensive. When only the model fit or p-values are needed and no standard errors/variances of smooths are required (e.g., just calling computeSignificance(result)) When the Hessian is small or dense enough that a direct inverse or mgcv's indirect method is affordable without the sparse inverse subset machinery http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Computes the diagonal of the inverse of a sparse penalized Hessian (i.e., pointwise variances/standard errors of GAM smooth estimates) using the sparse inverse subset algorithm implemented in the R package sparseinv, a wrapper of SuiteSparse code, instead of explicitly forming the full matrix inverse. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2238-7
skills.summary: Computes the diagonal of the inverse of a sparse penalized Hessian (i.e., pointwise variances/standard errors of GAM smooth estimates) using the sparse inverse subset algorithm implemented in the R package sparseinv, a wrapper of SuiteSparse code, instead of explicitly forming the full matrix inverse.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only the model fit or p-values are needed and no standard errors/variances of smooths are required (e.g., just calling computeSignificance(result)) When the Hessian is small or dense enough that a direct inverse or mgcv's indirect method is affordable without the sparse inverse subset machinery

skills.description: Use when a very sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., single-cell or downsampled to 0.025% sampling rate) needs imputation via RWR diffusion before downstream analysis, with symmetric sqrtVC normalization for convergence.
skills.name: sparse-matrix-iterative-convergence
skills.search_text: sparse-matrix-iterative-convergence Use when a very sparse Hi-C contact matrix (e.g., single-cell or downsampled to 0.025% sampling rate) needs imputation via RWR diffusion before downstream analysis, with symmetric sqrtVC normalization for convergence. The input is bulk or already dense Hi-C data — deDoc2 'needs no normalization process, raw Hi-C data is suitable' and decodes TLDs 'with no need of data imputation'. You only need the TLD partition itself and do not require imputation, since deDoc2 is robust to various data imputation algorithms. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Optional random-walk-with-restart (RWR) imputation preprocessing in deDoc2 that densifies sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices by iterative diffusion until a squared 2-norm convergence criterion (‖Qt − Qt−1‖2 ≤ 10−2) is met. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Optional random-walk-with-restart (RWR) imputation preprocessing in deDoc2 that densifies sparse single-cell Hi-C contact matrices by iterative diffusion until a squared 2-norm convergence criterion (‖Qt − Qt−1‖2 ≤ 10−2) is met.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is bulk or already dense Hi-C data — deDoc2 'needs no normalization process, raw Hi-C data is suitable' and decodes TLDs 'with no need of data imputation'. skills.name: sparse-triplet-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: sparse-triplet-matrix-generation Use when you have a duplicate-removed ChIA-PET bedpe file (e.g. prefixname.rmdup.bedpe) plus a tab-delimited chromosome sizes file and need a 2D genome-wide contact map rather than peak-anchored loop calls. You need statistically significant peak-anchored chromatin loops rather than a raw binned contact map — use bedpe2Interaction / MICC-based loop calling instead The interactions are already anchored to ChIP-seq-like peaks (bedpe2Interaction output) rather than raw genomic bins, so bin-level PET counting would discard peak resolution A dense full matrix or a non-HiC-Pro consumer format is required and the triplet sparse tuple format cannot be converted downstream http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Generates a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix from ChIA-PET paired-end tag (PET) data by binning PET ends from a PCR-duplicate-removed bedpe file into fixed-size genome bins and aggregating counts per bin pair, stored in the triplet sparse (HiC-Pro-style) tuple format for rendering with HiCPlotter. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkw809
skills.summary: Generates a Hi-C style 2D contact matrix from ChIA-PET paired-end tag (PET) data by binning PET ends from a PCR-duplicate-removed bedpe file into fixed-size genome bins and aggregating counts per bin pair, stored in the triplet sparse (HiC-Pro-style) tuple format for rendering with HiCPlotter.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need statistically significant peak-anchored chromatin loops rather than a raw binned contact map — use bedpe2Interaction / MICC-based loop calling instead The interactions are already anchored to ChIP-seq-like peaks (bedpe2Interaction output) rather than raw genomic bins, so bin-level PET counting would discard peak resolution A dense full matrix or a non-HiC-Pro consumer format is required and the triplet sparse tuple format cannot be converted downstream

Task output is binary classification (enhancer-target gene or eQTL tasks), which the benchmark scores with AUROC rather than SCC Input is not a 2D contact map / structure-related prediction — SCC contact-map agreement is specific to the 3D genome organization task You need a training-time loss rather than an evaluation metric; SCC here is a post-inference test-split evaluation Computes the Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC) between predicted and ground-truth contact maps on the DNALONGBENCH contact map prediction (HFF subset) test split, the benchmark's reported metric for evaluating how well DNA foundation models capture long-range 3D genomic dependencies. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4

skills.description: Use when a model outputs continuous sgRNA activity/efficiency predictions and you must quantify rank agreement with measured phenotype or activity scores, e.g. validating EpiCas-DL on independent genome-wide screening datasets.

skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-regression-scoring Use when a model outputs continuous sgRNA activity/efficiency predictions and you must quantify rank agreement with measured phenotype or activity scores, e.g. validating EpiCas-DL on independent genome-wide screening datasets. The prediction task is purely binary classification with no continuous predicted scores — ROC-AUC alone suffices and rank correlation is not the target metric Input sgRNAs are from the training distribution rather than independent cell-line/dataset validation, so the generalization claim being tested does not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Evaluates regression predictions of sgRNA editing efficiency by computing Spearman rank correlation (alongside classification ROC-AUC) with scikit-learn, as used to score EpiCas-DL CNN models on independent CRISPRi/CRISPRoff/CRISPRa screening datasets. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Evaluates regression predictions of sgRNA editing efficiency by computing Spearman rank correlation (alongside classification ROC-AUC) with scikit-learn, as used to score EpiCas-DL CNN models on independent CRISPRi/CRISPRoff/CRISPRa screening datasets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The prediction task is purely binary classification with no continuous predicted scores — ROC-AUC alone suffices and rank correlation is not the target metric Input sgRNAs are from the training distribution rather than independent cell-line/dataset validation, so the generalization claim being tested does not apply

skills.description: Use when comparing regression or classification models for sgRNA activity prediction on datasets like CRISPRoff_tiling (111,682 sgRNAs, 520 genes) and you need rank-based correlation plus significance testing across CV folds.
skills.name: spearman-correlation-statistical-testing
skills.search_text: spearman-correlation-statistical-testing Use when comparing regression or classification models for sgRNA activity prediction on datasets like CRISPRoff_tiling (111,682 sgRNAs, 520 genes) and you need rank-based correlation plus significance testing across CV folds. Your goal is feature attribution or mechanistic interpretation (use Tree SHAP / DeepSHAP with XGBoost instead, as in the paper's feature-identification workflow) You need binary editing-call classification metrics on data with no continuous activity scores — use AUC-based evaluation rather than Spearman correlation Predictions and observations come from different sgRNAs or unmatched samples, so a rank correlation is meaningless http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Evaluate sgRNA activity prediction models by computing Spearman rank correlations between predicted and observed sgRNA gene-repression/activation efficiencies across cross-validation folds, and test performance differences (e.g., EpiCas-DL vs. Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr) with Student's t-test, supported by MSE and cosine similarity. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.11.034
skills.summary: Evaluate sgRNA activity prediction models by computing Spearman rank correlations between predicted and observed sgRNA gene-repression/activation efficiencies across cross-validation folds, and test performance differences (e.g., EpiCas-DL vs. Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, DeepHF, C-RNNcrispr) with Student's t-test, supported by MSE and cosine similarity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is feature attribution or mechanistic interpretation (use Tree SHAP / DeepSHAP with XGBoost instead, as in the paper's feature-identification workflow) You need binary editing-call classification metrics on data with no continuous activity scores — use AUC-based evaluation rather than Spearman correlation Predictions and observations come from different sgRNAs or unmatched samples, so a rank correlation is meaningless

skills.search_text: species-specific-marker-mapping-human-mouse Use when a single-cell cluster annotation or marker-lookup task requires a curated, tissue-specific marker reference restricted to human or mouse, or when rebuilding/extending a CellMatch-style cellmatch table. The analysis uses species other than human or mouse without first building a custom cellmatch (default reference covers only human and mouse) The input is raw scRNA-seq data requiring clustering — this skill covers the reference database, not marker gene identification (findmarkergene handles that) A limited or tissue-mismatched reference would be the only available option, since a limited reference database can lead to incorrect annotation http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0605 Reconstruct and apply a species-annotated (human/mouse) tissue-specific cell marker reference database, following CellMatch for scCATCH: aggregate literature-reported markers into a unified table linking each gene to cell type, subtype, tissue, species, and reference. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.isci.2020.100882
skills.summary: Reconstruct and apply a species-annotated (human/mouse) tissue-specific cell marker reference database, following CellMatch for scCATCH: aggregate literature-reported markers into a unified table linking each gene to cell type, subtype, tissue, species, and reference.

skills.description: Use when you have a binarized cell-by-bin accessibility matrix (e.g., 5-kb bins in a snap file) and need a peak-free low-dimensional embedding of single-cell chromatin profiles for clustering rare populations.
skills.name: spectral-eigenvector-embedding
skills.search_text: spectral-eigenvector-embedding Use when you have a binarized cell-by-bin accessibility matrix (e.g., 5-kb bins in a snap file) and need a peak-free low-dimensional embedding of single-cell chromatin profiles for clustering rare populations. Input is already a peak-by-cell matrix derived from population-level peak calls — SnapATAC's Jaccard/spectral approach is designed to avoid predefined peak annotation, which biases toward abundant cell types Data are extremely sparse raw fragment counts without binarization — the Jaccard kernel requires binary per-cell accessible-genome profiles Python/R environment constraints are violated: SnapTools requires Python >= 2.7 & < 3.0 and SnapATAC requires R >= 3.4.0 & < 3.6.0 (rhdf5 fails on R 3.6); use SnapATAC2 instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3366 SnapATAC's spectral embedding: eigenvector decomposition of the depth-normalized cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel (jmat) to produce a low-dimensional representation of scATAC-seq cells without predefined population-level peaks. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-21583-9
skills.summary: SnapATAC's spectral embedding: eigenvector decomposition of the depth-normalized cell-by-cell Jaccard kernel (jmat) to produce a low-dimensional representation of scATAC-seq cells without predefined population-level peaks.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a peak-by-cell matrix derived from population-level peak calls — SnapATAC's Jaccard/spectral approach is designed to avoid predefined peak annotation, which biases toward abundant cell types Data are extremely sparse raw fragment counts without binarization — the Jaccard kernel requires binary per-cell accessible-genome profiles Python/R environment constraints are violated: SnapTools requires Python >= 2.7 & < 3.0 and SnapATAC requires R >= 3.4.0 & < 3.6.0 (rhdf5 fails on R 3.6); use SnapATAC2 instead

skills.description: Use when assembling haplotypes for a single diploid individual from long reads (PacBio SMRT, ONT), Hi-C, or 10X linked-reads, especially very large genomes or high coverage where max-cut/MEC tools exceed memory or time limits.
skills.name: spectral-graph-haplotype-phasing
skills.search_text: spectral-graph-haplotype-phasing Use when assembling haplotypes for a single diploid individual from long reads (PacBio SMRT, ONT), Hi-C, or 10X linked-reads, especially very large genomes or high coverage where max-cut/MEC tools exceed memory or time limits. Organism is polyploid or ploidy > 2: the current graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy and high-ploidy generalization is not implemented Goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation / genome rearrangements: SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions and deletions Input is already a fragment file from an incompatible protocol — note 10X linked-reads require filtering to keep only white-listed barcode fragments before phasing http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Phases diploid single-individual haplotypes by transforming the SIH problem into a linear-algebra problem: build a linkage graph from read fragments, then partition alleles using spectral graph theory (Fiedler-vector bisection) with divide-and-conquer over chromosome intervals. Enables phasing of gigantic genomes (e.g. 32 Gbp axolotl) where MEC/max-cut tools fail. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Phases diploid single-individual haplotypes by transforming the SIH problem into a linear-algebra problem: build a linkage graph from read fragments, then partition alleles using spectral graph theory (Fiedler-vector bisection) with divide-and-conquer over chromosome intervals. Enables phasing of gigantic genomes (e.g. 32 Gbp axolotl) where MEC/max-cut tools fail.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Organism is polyploid or ploidy > 2: the current graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy and high-ploidy generalization is not implemented Goal is haplotype-resolved structural variation / genome rearrangements: SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions and deletions Input is already a fragment file from an incompatible protocol — note 10X linked-reads require filtering to keep only white-listed barcode fragments before phasing

skills.description: Use when preparing to run spikChIP on multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in (e.g. human hg19 + fruit fly dm3) and BAM/peak files must be wired into a configuration file before normalization.
skills.name: spike-in-chipseq-configuration-handling
skills.search_text: spike-in-chipseq-configuration-handling Use when preparing to run spikChIP on multiple ChIP-seq experiments with exogenous spike-in (e.g. human hg19 + fruit fly dm3) and BAM/peak files must be wired into a configuration file before normalization. BAM files or BED peak files do not yet exist — spikChIP requires them as pre-generated user inputs and its Step 0 check will fail The ChIP-seq experiment has no spike-in control, so there is no sample/spike BAM pair or exogenous genome identifier to declare in the configuration The exogenous genome is not among the supported identifiers (FLY, HUMAN, MOUSE, EXO) handled by the -e option http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Assemble and validate the spikChIP inputs for comparative ChIP-seq with spike-in chromatin: a plain-text configuration file mapping each condition to its sample/spike BAM files and BED peak files, plus a ChromInfo file listing sample (hg19) and spike-in (dm3, 'FLY'-suffixed) chromosome names and lengths. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Assemble and validate the spikChIP inputs for comparative ChIP-seq with spike-in chromatin: a plain-text configuration file mapping each condition to its sample/spike BAM files and BED peak files, plus a ChromInfo file listing sample (hg19) and spike-in (dm3, 'FLY'-suffixed) chromosome names and lengths.
skills.when_to_use_negative: BAM files or BED peak files do not yet exist — spikChIP requires them as pre-generated user inputs and its Step 0 check will fail The ChIP-seq experiment has no spike-in control, so there is no sample/spike BAM pair or exogenous genome identifier to declare in the configuration The exogenous genome is not among the supported identifiers (FLY, HUMAN, MOUSE, EXO) handled by the -e option

skills.summary: Within MEDIPIPE's methylation quantification module, when spike-in controls are declared in the YAML configuration, MEDIPS (v1.46.0) with its linear regression CpG-density correction is run separately on the extracted spike-in read alignments to quantify methylation levels for the controls.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The configuration declares no spike-in controls — the spike-in MEDIPS run and its output table should be skipped You need absolute or strand-aware methylation estimates for the main samples rather than spike-in control quantification — use the QSEA sigmoidal or MEDStrand stranded sigmoid runs instead

skills.description: Use when you have human+fly spike-in BAM files (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 mixtures, GEO GSM1465005/GSM1465007) and need to quantify how a spike-in normalization strategy alters background vs peak-region ChIP signal.
skills.name: spikein-normalization-strategy-comparison
skills.search_text: spikein-normalization-strategy-comparison Use when you have human+fly spike-in BAM files (e.g. Jurkat H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 mixtures, GEO GSM1465005/GSM1465007) and need to quantify how a spike-in normalization strategy alters background vs peak-region ChIP signal. The goal is to avoid overcorrection of non-occupied/background regions — use the spikChIP local regression normalization instead of Tag removal or ChIP-Rx The BAM files contain no fly spike-in alignments (no FLY-suffix chromosomes), so the spike-in scaling factor R = M/N cannot be computed Only one experimental condition needs normalization (no cross-condition comparison), so spike-in strategy comparison has no contrast to quantify http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Reproduce and compare spike-in ChIP-seq normalization strategies (RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAG REMOVAL, SPIKCHIP) as calculated by the spikChIP pipeline, quantifying how each strategy corrects signal at non-enriched background regions versus peaks — e.g. the ~20–25% Tag removal background difference between 25:75 and 75:25 H3K79me2 conditions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Reproduce and compare spike-in ChIP-seq normalization strategies (RAW, TRADITIONAL, CHIPRX, TAG REMOVAL, SPIKCHIP) as calculated by the spikChIP pipeline, quantifying how each strategy corrects signal at non-enriched background regions versus peaks — e.g. the ~20–25% Tag removal background difference between 25:75 and 75:25 H3K79me2 conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to avoid overcorrection of non-occupied/background regions — use the spikChIP local regression normalization instead of Tag removal or ChIP-Rx The BAM files contain no fly spike-in alignments (no FLY-suffix chromosomes), so the spike-in scaling factor R = M/N cannot be computed Only one experimental condition needs normalization (no cross-condition comparison), so spike-in strategy comparison has no contrast to quantify

skills.description: Use when comparing two spike-in ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 with fly chromatin) and you need a ratio-based scaling factor to equalize spike-in read depth before bin-level signal counting.
skills.name: spikein-read-ratio-scaling-factor-calculation
skills.search_text: spikein-read-ratio-scaling-factor-calculation Use when comparing two spike-in ChIP-seq conditions (e.g. H3K79me2 25:75 vs 75:25 with fly chromatin) and you need a ratio-based scaling factor to equalize spike-in read depth before bin-level signal counting. When the goal is to avoid overcorrection of non-occupied/background regions — the article shows tag removal (like ChIP-Rx) applies the correction uniformly and yields a ~20-25% background signal difference; use spikChIP's local regression instead When sample and spike-in BAM files have not yet been generated with a mapping tool (Bowtie with multi-locus reads discarded) and peaks not yet called with MACS2 When spike-in reads are far below the recommended minimum of ~1 million reads (2%-5% of the experimental genome), making M/N unstable http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Computes a spike-in-based scaling factor R = M/N from fly spike-in read totals of two ChIP-seq conditions and down-samples the high-spike-in sample with Samtools (the 'tag removal' normalization strategy also implemented inside spikChIP), producing comparable BAM inputs for genome-wide signal comparison. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Computes a spike-in-based scaling factor R = M/N from fly spike-in read totals of two ChIP-seq conditions and down-samples the high-spike-in sample with Samtools (the 'tag removal' normalization strategy also implemented inside spikChIP), producing comparable BAM inputs for genome-wide signal comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is to avoid overcorrection of non-occupied/background regions — the article shows tag removal (like ChIP-Rx) applies the correction uniformly and yields a ~20-25% background signal difference; use spikChIP's local regression instead When sample and spike-in BAM files have not yet been generated with a mapping tool (Bowtie with multi-locus reads discarded) and peaks not yet called with MACS2 When spike-in reads are far below the recommended minimum of ~1 million reads (2%-5% of the experimental genome), making M/N unstable

skills.description: Use when gene-level p-values from transcriptomic and epigenomic data must be projected onto an interaction network to find dysregulated modules, or when two module-detection runs (e.g., FEM vs SMITE) need quantitative comparison of overlap and enrichment.
skills.name: spin-glass-network-scoring
skills.search_text: spin-glass-network-scoring Use when gene-level p-values from transcriptomic and epigenomic data must be projected onto an interaction network to find dysregulated modules, or when two module-detection runs (e.g., FEM vs SMITE) need quantitative comparison of overlap and enrichment. When only individual loci with the most significant effects are needed rather than network-level module discovery — pruning-based approaches introduce the bias SMITE was designed to avoid. When no interactome (e.g., REACTOME) is available for the organism, since spinglass module detection requires a gene network. When p-value columns still contain NA or zero values, since these must be filtered/replaced before scoring or the score distribution and downstream KS tests are invalid. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 Score genes from integrated expression/methylation p-values and detect network modules with igraph's spin-glass algorithm on the REACTOME interactome, then benchmark modules (e.g., FEM vs SMITE-R/SMITE-F) by gene overlap and two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests of high-scoring gene enrichment. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Score genes from integrated expression/methylation p-values and detect network modules with igraph's spin-glass algorithm on the REACTOME interactome, then benchmark modules (e.g., FEM vs SMITE-R/SMITE-F) by gene overlap and two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests of high-scoring gene enrichment.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When only individual loci with the most significant effects are needed rather than network-level module discovery — pruning-based approaches introduce the bias SMITE was designed to avoid. When no interactome (e.g., REACTOME) is available for the organism, since spinglass module detection requires a gene network. When p-value columns still contain NA or zero values, since these must be filtered/replaced before scoring or the score distribution and downstream KS tests are invalid.

skills.description: Use when RNAseq fastq files in a NEAT project's 'fatsq' folder need alignment and Targets.txt marks samples as RNAseq, requiring splice-aware mapping with Tophat.
skills.name: splice-aware-rnaseq-alignment
skills.search_text: splice-aware-rnaseq-alignment Use when RNAseq fastq files in a NEAT project's 'fatsq' folder need alignment and Targets.txt marks samples as RNAseq, requiring splice-aware mapping with Tophat. Input samples are ChIPseq (e.g. H3K4me3), which NEAT routes to bwa or bowtie rather than splice-aware Tophat Input is already aligned data (.bam), where the 'filter', 'peakcalling', 'GRanges' or 'cleanfiles' modules are appropriate instead The experiment requires a user-scripted, terminal-driven workflow rather than NEAT's double-clickable, GUI-based pipeline approach http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Performs automated read alignment for RNAseq samples by dispatching NEAT's 'map' module to the bowtie-based Tophat aligner, which handles splice junctions across the transcriptome, while ChIPseq samples are routed to bwa or bowtie instead. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-0902-3
skills.summary: Performs automated read alignment for RNAseq samples by dispatching NEAT's 'map' module to the bowtie-based Tophat aligner, which handles splice junctions across the transcriptome, while ChIPseq samples are routed to bwa or bowtie instead.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input samples are ChIPseq (e.g. H3K4me3), which NEAT routes to bwa or bowtie rather than splice-aware Tophat Input is already aligned data (.bam), where the 'filter', 'peakcalling', 'GRanges' or 'cleanfiles' modules are appropriate instead The experiment requires a user-scripted, terminal-driven workflow rather than NEAT's double-clickable, GUI-based pipeline approach

skills.description: Use when RNA-Seq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a genome for downstream expression estimation or fragment-bias correction, and known gene annotations are available to constrain splice junctions.
skills.name: splice-junction-aware-mapping
skills.search_text: splice-junction-aware-mapping Use when RNA-Seq FASTQ reads must be aligned to a genome for downstream expression estimation or fragment-bias correction, and known gene annotations are available to constrain splice junctions. When the goal is discovery of novel splice junctions not present in the supplied annotation — the --no-novel-juncs setting explicitly restricts alignments to annotated junctions only. When reads can be aligned directly to a transcriptome without a spliced genome alignment step, since this skill's purpose is splice-aware genome mapping. http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Map Illumina RNA-Seq reads to a reference genome with a splice-aware aligner (TopHat 1.1.0), supplying known transcript annotations and disallowing novel junction discovery so only annotated splice junctions are considered, producing the BAM alignments consumed by downstream expression-estimation and bias-correction tools such as Cufflinks/eXpress-D. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Map Illumina RNA-Seq reads to a reference genome with a splice-aware aligner (TopHat 1.1.0), supplying known transcript annotations and disallowing novel junction discovery so only annotated splice junctions are considered, producing the BAM alignments consumed by downstream expression-estimation and bias-correction tools such as Cufflinks/eXpress-D.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is discovery of novel splice junctions not present in the supplied annotation — the --no-novel-juncs setting explicitly restricts alignments to annotated junctions only. When reads can be aligned directly to a transcriptome without a spliced genome alignment step, since this skill's purpose is splice-aware genome mapping.

skills.description: Use when bootRanges overlap counts between differential expression genes (logFC) and differential accessibility peaks must be converted into an optimized, data-driven logFC or SNP -log10(P) significance threshold rather than an arbitrary cutoff.
skills.name: spline-glm-fitting-overlap-counts
skills.search_text: spline-glm-fitting-overlap-counts Use when bootRanges overlap counts between differential expression genes (logFC) and differential accessibility peaks must be converted into an optimized, data-driven logFC or SNP -log10(P) significance threshold rather than an arbitrary cutoff. skills.search_text: svm-baseline-reimplementation Use when a study claims a new 6mA-site predictor outperforms iDNA6mA-PseKNC and the comparison must be reproduced under identical 5-fold cross-validation on cross-species, rice, or M. musculus datasets. The input is already a per-fold cross-validation score file or a finished comparison table — no reimplementation is needed. The question concerns independent-test-set performance or LeaveOneOut evaluation rather than the 5-fold cross-validation comparison against iDNA6mA-PseKNC. A direct i6mA-Pred comparison is requested — the article notes i6mA-Pred was still in corrected proof phase and its method could not be reached, so no faithful reimplementation exists in this repo. http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reimplements the iDNA6mA-PseKNC predictor as an SVM baseline (C=0.336, gamma=0.02) evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation on the same Motif+Kmer+Binary feature matrices used by csDMA, enabling a head-to-head AUC/ACC/Sn/Sp/MCC comparison (Table 4). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4
skills.summary: Reimplements the iDNA6mA-PseKNC predictor as an SVM baseline (C=0.336, gamma=0.02) evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation on the same Motif+Kmer+Binary feature matrices used by csDMA, enabling a head-to-head AUC/ACC/Sn/Sp/MCC comparison (Table 4).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is already a per-fold cross-validation score file or a finished comparison table — no reimplementation is needed.
