skills.description: Use when you have phased VCF outputs from haplotype assembly tools on NA12878/NA19240 WGS data (NGS, 10x, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and need to quantify phasing accuracy against trio-phased truth.
skills.name: switch-error-rate-evaluation
skills.search_text: switch-error-rate-evaluation Use when you have phased VCF outputs from haplotype assembly tools on NA12878/NA19240 WGS data (NGS, 10x, Hi-C, PacBio SMRT, ONT) and need to quantify phasing accuracy against trio-phased truth. No trio-phased ground truth is available for the sample (e.g. non-human or non-1000 Genomes individuals), so switch/mismatch error rates cannot be computed The output is haplotype-resolved structural variation calling rather than SNV/short-indel phasing — SpecHap and this SIH evaluation framework support only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Polyploid organisms — the graph bisection model underlying SpecHap and this diploid evaluation does not fit increased ploidy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Evaluates haplotype assembly outputs by comparing each tool's phased VCF against the 1000 Genomes Project trio-phased 'ground truth', computing switch error rate, mismatch error rate, AN50, and number of phased variants for methods such as SpecHap, FastHare, HapCUT, HapCUT2, DCHap and ReFHap. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Evaluates haplotype assembly outputs by comparing each tool's phased VCF against the 1000 Genomes Project trio-phased 'ground truth', computing switch error rate, mismatch error rate, AN50, and number of phased variants for methods such as SpecHap, FastHare, HapCUT, HapCUT2, DCHap and ReFHap.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trio-phased ground truth is available for the sample (e.g. non-human or non-1000 Genomes individuals), so switch/mismatch error rates cannot be computed The output is haplotype-resolved structural variation calling rather than SNV/short-indel phasing — SpecHap and this SIH evaluation framework support only SNPs and short insertions/deletions Polyploid organisms — the graph bisection model underlying SpecHap and this diploid evaluation does not fit increased ploidy

skills.description: Use when you need a ground-truth-labelled benchmark to test whether a clustering or alignment method (e.g. DGW vs hierarchical clustering) can recover known seed patterns from epigenomic peak-profile data.
skills.name: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-generation Use when you need a ground-truth-labelled benchmark to test whether a clustering or alignment method (e.g. DGW vs hierarchical clustering) can recover known seed patterns from epigenomic peak-profile data. The goal is to measure clustering performance on real, unlabelled epigenomic data where no seed-of-origin ground truth exists (use the ENCODE evaluation instead). The input is already a curated labelled benchmark or feature table, not raw seed profiles from which synthetic variants must be seeded. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates a labelled synthetic benchmark of ~500 ChIP-Seq peak profiles by perturbing five real seed patterns (ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 read-count profiles from UCSC knownGenes 2 kb regions) with parameterised multiplicative noise, bin duplication/deletion, and orientation switching, so that clustering performance can be scored against known seed-of-origin labels. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-016-1306-0
skills.summary: Generates a labelled synthetic benchmark of ~500 ChIP-Seq peak profiles by perturbing five real seed patterns (ENCODE K562 H3K4me3 read-count profiles from UCSC knownGenes 2 kb regions) with parameterised multiplicative noise, bin duplication/deletion, and orientation switching, so that clustering performance can be scored against known seed-of-origin labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to measure clustering performance on real, unlabelled epigenomic data where no seed-of-origin ground truth exists (use the ENCODE evaluation instead). The input is already a curated labelled benchmark or feature table, not raw seed profiles from which synthetic variants must be seeded.

skills.description: Use when comparing sequencing methods (RIMS-seq vs DNA-seq vs bisulfite-seq) for species-level relative abundance estimation in mixed or synthetic bacterial communities with a reference genome per species.
skills.name: synthetic-community-abundance-estimation
skills.search_text: synthetic-community-abundance-estimation Use when comparing sequencing methods (RIMS-seq vs DNA-seq vs bisulfite-seq) for species-level relative abundance estimation in mixed or synthetic bacterial communities with a reference genome per species. The library preparation is based on tagmentation rather than adapter ligation — RIMS-seq (and thus its abundance profile) is not valid in that setting The goal is precise genomic localization of methylation sites rather than community composition — EM-seq or bisulfite-seq are more appropriate for positional methylation No reference genome is available and species cannot be distinguished by mapping — abundance estimation by per-species read counts requires exact references http://edamontology.org/topic_3697 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Estimates normalized per-species relative abundances in ATCC synthetic microbiome communities (MSA-1005/1006) by mapping RIMS-seq, DNA-seq(+3H), and bisulfite-seq reads with BWA-mem and dividing each species' mapped read count by total mapped reads per library, enabling cross-method abundance comparison. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab705
skills.summary: Estimates normalized per-species relative abundances in ATCC synthetic microbiome communities (MSA-1005/1006) by mapping RIMS-seq, DNA-seq(+3H), and bisulfite-seq reads with BWA-mem and dividing each species' mapped read count by total mapped reads per library, enabling cross-method abundance comparison.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The library preparation is based on tagmentation rather than adapter ligation — RIMS-seq (and thus its abundance profile) is not valid in that setting The goal is precise genomic localization of methylation sites rather than community composition — EM-seq or bisulfite-seq are more appropriate for positional methylation No reference genome is available and species cannot be distinguished by mapping — abundance estimation by per-species read counts requires exact references

skills.description: Use when benchmarking DNA motif-discovery tools on ground-truth data: you need FASTA pairs with known implanted IUPAC motifs at controlled frequencies and an nCC-based recovery score.
skills.name: synthetic-dna-sequence-motif-implantation
skills.search_text: synthetic-dna-sequence-motif-implantation Use when benchmarking DNA motif-discovery tools on ground-truth data: you need FASTA pairs with known implanted IUPAC motifs at controlled frequencies and an nCC-based recovery score. The goal is de novo motif discovery on real biological data (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks) rather than controlled benchmarking against known implanted motifs Motifs of interest are not representable as IUPAC strings of the fixed length used in the implantation (here L=6) You need position-level occupancy metrics rather than nucleotide-level recovery (nCC) of implanted motifs http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Generate synthetic positive/control FASTA benchmark pairs with length-6 IUPAC (degenerate or exact) motifs implanted at controlled frequencies (5% down to 0.5% of initial sequences), then score motif-discovery recovery with the nucleotide level correlation coefficient (nCC). epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2215-1
skills.summary: Generate synthetic positive/control FASTA benchmark pairs with length-6 IUPAC (degenerate or exact) motifs implanted at controlled frequencies (5% down to 0.5% of initial sequences), then score motif-discovery recovery with the nucleotide level correlation coefficient (nCC).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is de novo motif discovery on real biological data (e.g. ChIP-seq peaks) rather than controlled benchmarking against known implanted motifs Motifs of interest are not representable as IUPAC strings of the fixed length used in the implantation (here L=6) You need position-level occupancy metrics rather than nucleotide-level recovery (nCC) of implanted motifs

skills.description: Use when BOM's save_shap_multi() SHAP scores identify the most predictive motifs for two conditions and you need concrete synthetic enhancer DNA sequences for reporter/MPRA validation of cell-type-specific activity.
skills.name: synthetic-enhancer-sequence-design
skills.search_text: synthetic-enhancer-sequence-design Use when BOM's save_shap_multi() SHAP scores identify the most predictive motifs for two conditions and you need concrete synthetic enhancer DNA sequences for reporter/MPRA validation of cell-type-specific activity. When motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) is expected to matter — BOM's representation and the random implantation procedure are explicitly unordered When the analysis goal is predicting activity of native regulatory elements rather than experimentally validating BOM's motif predictions with synthetic constructs When informative sequences are not captured by current TF motif annotations, since the design is limited to known PWMs from the provided motif set http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Design synthetic regulatory elements (SREs) by implanting concrete motif sequences for the top-5 SHAP-ranked BOM motifs per cell condition into a common enhancer template, to experimentally test whether the predicted motif sets confer cell-type-specific enhancer activity. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Design synthetic regulatory elements (SREs) by implanting concrete motif sequences for the top-5 SHAP-ranked BOM motifs per cell condition into a common enhancer template, to experimentally test whether the predicted motif sets confer cell-type-specific enhancer activity.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When motif grammar (order, orientation, or spacing) is expected to matter — BOM's representation and the random implantation procedure are explicitly unordered When the analysis goal is predicting activity of native regulatory elements rather than experimentally validating BOM's motif predictions with synthetic constructs When informative sequences are not captured by current TF motif annotations, since the design is limited to known PWMs from the provided motif set

skills.description: Use when benchmarking non-B DNA detectors or classifiers on ONT nanopore translocation times and labelled synthetic windows with controlled non-B-to-B ratios are needed as ground truth.
skills.name: synthetic-labeled-dataset-generation
skills.search_text: synthetic-labeled-dataset-generation Use when benchmarking non-B DNA detectors or classifiers on ONT nanopore translocation times and labelled synthetic windows with controlled non-B-to-B ratios are needed as ground truth. The goal is to evaluate on real sequencing signal rather than controlled synthetic benchmarks — use the experimental NA12878/SRR15058166 windows instead Input is already a labelled window dataset with the desired non-B-to-B ratio; regenerating with the simulator would duplicate it The downstream method requires other non-B structure types (e.g. Z-DNA, hairpins) not modeled by the quadratic/sinusoidal generators http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Reconstructs the translocation-time (TT) simulator that generates labelled synthetic benchmark datasets combining G-quadruplex and short-tandem-repeat non-B windows with B-DNA windows, so GoFAE-DND, classifiers, and novelty detectors can be evaluated on data with known labels. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Reconstructs the translocation-time (TT) simulator that generates labelled synthetic benchmark datasets combining G-quadruplex and short-tandem-repeat non-B windows with B-DNA windows, so GoFAE-DND, classifiers, and novelty detectors can be evaluated on data with known labels.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to evaluate on real sequencing signal rather than controlled synthetic benchmarks — use the experimental NA12878/SRR15058166 windows instead Input is already a labelled window dataset with the desired non-B-to-B ratio; regenerating with the simulator would duplicate it The downstream method requires other non-B structure types (e.g. Z-DNA, hairpins) not modeled by the quadratic/sinusoidal generators

skills.description: Use when preprocessing spike-in ChIP-seq FASTQ reads that must align to both the experimental genome (hg19) and the exogenous spike-in genome (dm3) before spikChIP bin-level normalization.
skills.name: synthetic-reference-genome-concatenation
skills.search_text: synthetic-reference-genome-concatenation Use when preprocessing spike-in ChIP-seq FASTQ reads that must align to both the experimental genome (hg19) and the exogenous spike-in genome (dm3) before spikChIP bin-level normalization. Input BAM files of each sample/spike genome are already generated and split — spikChIP expects these pre-mapped inputs and the concatenation/mapping step is redundant The spike-in genome is not a known xenogenic reference (FLY/HUMAN/MOUSE/EXO identifiers), so no standard concatenated genome can be constructed Reads have already been binned or normalized (e.g. a feature table of per-bin counts exists) — genome construction and mapping would not apply http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Constructs a combined sample+spike-in reference genome (e.g. human hg19 plus fruit fly dm3 chromosomes renamed with a mandatory 'FLY' suffix), builds Bowtie indexes over the concatenation, maps raw ChIP-seq FASTQ reads against it, and filters unmapped reads with SAMtools so sample and spike-in reads can later be separated and counted in 1-kbp bins. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqab064
skills.summary: Constructs a combined sample+spike-in reference genome (e.g. human hg19 plus fruit fly dm3 chromosomes renamed with a mandatory 'FLY' suffix), builds Bowtie indexes over the concatenation, maps raw ChIP-seq FASTQ reads against it, and filters unmapped reads with SAMtools so sample and spike-in reads can later be separated and counted in 1-kbp bins.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input BAM files of each sample/spike genome are already generated and split — spikChIP expects these pre-mapped inputs and the concatenation/mapping step is redundant The spike-in genome is not a known xenogenic reference (FLY/HUMAN/MOUSE/EXO identifiers), so no standard concatenated genome can be constructed Reads have already been binned or normalized (e.g. a feature table of per-bin counts exists) — genome construction and mapping would not apply

skills.description: Use when a completed COnTORT run (GenBank .gbff plus a GEO search term) has produced per-series matched expression files and they must be joined into the final annotated, tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix.
skills.name: tab-delimited-output-assembly
skills.search_text: tab-delimited-output-assembly Use when a completed COnTORT run (GenBank .gbff plus a GEO search term) has produced per-series matched expression files and they must be joined into the final annotated, tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix. The data of interest are raw reads or unprocessed GEO submissions — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO The input expression files have not yet been filtered against the GenBank annotation via gffMatch Only a single series needs reformatting with no cross-experiment joining or mean-centering http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Assembles COnTORT's final tab-delimited text files by joining mean-centered (and non-mean-centered) log2 normalized GEO expression data to GenBank gene annotations, using the gene annotation as the join key. Produces COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt and a parallel non-centered file for downstream analysis in Excel or R. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Assembles COnTORT's final tab-delimited text files by joining mean-centered (and non-mean-centered) log2 normalized GEO expression data to GenBank gene annotations, using the gene annotation as the join key. Produces COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt and a parallel non-centered file for downstream analysis in Excel or R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data of interest are raw reads or unprocessed GEO submissions — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO The input expression files have not yet been filtered against the GenBank annotation via gffMatch Only a single series needs reformatting with no cross-experiment joining or mean-centering

skills.description: Use when a task requires anchoring GEO gene expression data to gene annotations from a user-provided GenBank .gbff file and producing a joined, Excel/R-ready tab-delimited table.
skills.name: tab-delimited-transcriptome-table-generation
skills.search_text: tab-delimited-transcriptome-table-generation Use when a task requires anchoring GEO gene expression data to gene annotations from a user-provided GenBank .gbff file and producing a joined, Excel/R-ready tab-delimited table. The expression data are raw reads or not normalized/processed data imported into NCBI GEO — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed GEO data. The organism's gene annotations are not available as a GenBank .gbff file, since the user must provide it and gffMatch retains only matches to annotations in that file. A single GEO series' raw metadata alone is needed — GEOannotate/GEOparse organization, not annotation-keyed table generation, is the appropriate step. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3174 Generate a single tab-delimited transcriptomic output file in which the first five columns carry GenBank-derived gene annotations (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product) followed by GEO expression values, produced by COnTORT's gffMatch/GEOannotate pipeline. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Generate a single tab-delimited transcriptomic output file in which the first five columns carry GenBank-derived gene annotations (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product) followed by GEO expression values, produced by COnTORT's gffMatch/GEOannotate pipeline.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are raw reads or not normalized/processed data imported into NCBI GEO — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed GEO data. The organism's gene annotations are not available as a GenBank .gbff file, since the user must provide it and gffMatch retains only matches to annotations in that file. A single GEO series' raw metadata alone is needed — GEOannotate/GEOparse organization, not annotation-keyed table generation, is the appropriate step.

skills.description: Use when per-sample cfMeDIP-seq methylation quantification files (e.g. MEDIPS, QSEA, or MEDStrand outputs) must be aggregated into bin-by-sample matrices and made region-queryable across many samples or batches.
skills.name: tabix-indexed-genomic-matrix-generation
skills.search_text: tabix-indexed-genomic-matrix-generation Use when per-sample cfMeDIP-seq methylation quantification files (e.g. MEDIPS, QSEA, or MEDStrand outputs) must be aggregated into bin-by-sample matrices and made region-queryable across many samples or batches. Input is raw FASTQ data that has not yet undergone MEDIPIPE's QC, alignment, and per-sample methylation quantification steps Only a single sample is being analyzed and no cross-sample aggregation or region-queryable matrix is needed Analysis requires read-level or peak-level cfMeDIP-seq data rather than binned, aggregated methylation summaries http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 MEDIPIPE's aggregation module: per-sample methylation quantifications (MEDIPS, QSEA, MEDStrand) are combined into TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, uniformly filtered to remove sex chromosomes, the mitochondrial chromosome, and ENCODE blacklist regions, then sorted, bgzip-compressed, and indexed with Tabix (v1.17) for rapid region queries. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad423
skills.summary: MEDIPIPE's aggregation module: per-sample methylation quantifications (MEDIPS, QSEA, MEDStrand) are combined into TAB-delimited bin-sample TXT matrices, uniformly filtered to remove sex chromosomes, the mitochondrial chromosome, and ENCODE blacklist regions, then sorted, bgzip-compressed, and indexed with Tabix (v1.17) for rapid region queries.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw FASTQ data that has not yet undergone MEDIPIPE's QC, alignment, and per-sample methylation quantification steps Only a single sample is being analyzed and no cross-sample aggregation or region-queryable matrix is needed Analysis requires read-level or peak-level cfMeDIP-seq data rather than binned, aggregated methylation summaries

skills.description: Use when an XML Watchdog workflow task definition contains <processblocks> entries and the concrete set of subtasks (one per sequence element, matching path, or table row) must be enumerated before execution.
skills.name: table-row-subtask-generation
skills.search_text: table-row-subtask-generation Use when an XML Watchdog workflow task definition contains <processblocks> entries and the concrete set of subtasks (one per sequence element, matching path, or table row) must be enumerated before execution. The workflow task definition contains no process blocks (e.g. example_basic_sleep.xml with a single fixed task) — no instantiation is needed Subtask inputs are already concrete file paths written directly in the XML task rather than placeholders to be expanded You are authoring module definitions rather than instantiating workflow subtasks — use the moduleMaker workflow instead http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Generates the set of Watchdog subtasks from process blocks defined in an XML workflow: each process block (process sequences, folders/paths, or tables) enumerates instances holding one or more variables, and one subtask is created per instance with placeholders replaced by the instance's variable values. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2107-4
skills.summary: Generates the set of Watchdog subtasks from process blocks defined in an XML workflow: each process block (process sequences, folders/paths, or tables) enumerates instances holding one or more variables, and one subtask is created per instance with placeholders replaced by the instance's variable values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The workflow task definition contains no process blocks (e.g. example_basic_sleep.xml with a single fixed task) — no instantiation is needed Subtask inputs are already concrete file paths written directly in the XML task rather than placeholders to be expanded You are authoring module definitions rather than instantiating workflow subtasks — use the moduleMaker workflow instead

skills.description: Use when you hold a COnTORT mean-centered tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product + GSM-labeled columns) and need ranked co-expressed gene pairs across many GEO experiments.
skills.name: tabular-genomic-data-manipulation
skills.search_text: tabular-genomic-data-manipulation Use when you hold a COnTORT mean-centered tab-delimited transcriptomic matrix (locus tag, old locus tag, gene name, gene synonyms, product + GSM-labeled columns) and need ranked co-expressed gene pairs across many GEO experiments. The input is the non-mean-centered COnTORT output file — experiment-to-experiment offsets are not controlled for, so cross-experiment correlations are not comparable. The data are raw or unnormalized reads not imported into NCBI GEO; COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO. The goal is retrieving/organizing GEO data rather than downstream analysis of an already-organized COnTORT matrix (use the COnTORT download pipeline instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0085 Manipulates the COnTORT-organized, mean-centered transcriptomic matrix (COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt) — a tab-delimited file with five GenBank annotation columns followed by per-experiment expression columns — to compute and rank pairwise gene-gene Pearson correlations for identifying candidate transcription factor targets. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Manipulates the COnTORT-organized, mean-centered transcriptomic matrix (COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt) — a tab-delimited file with five GenBank annotation columns followed by per-experiment expression columns — to compute and rank pairwise gene-gene Pearson correlations for identifying candidate transcription factor targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is the non-mean-centered COnTORT output file — experiment-to-experiment offsets are not controlled for, so cross-experiment correlations are not comparable. The data are raw or unnormalized reads not imported into NCBI GEO; COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO. The goal is retrieving/organizing GEO data rather than downstream analysis of an already-organized COnTORT matrix (use the COnTORT download pipeline instead).

skills.description: Use when a variant-by-feature score matrix (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM columns from ANNOVAR annotation) contains missing entries that must be filled before feeding the features into the ncDeepBrain/iMEGES deep learning model.
skills.name: tabular-imputation-quality-control
skills.search_text: tabular-imputation-quality-control Use when a variant-by-feature score matrix (e.g. EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM columns from ANNOVAR annotation) contains missing entries that must be filled before feeding the features into the ncDeepBrain/iMEGES deep learning model. The feature table is already complete (zero missing values) — imputation is unnecessary and could distort true scores. The goal is variant calling or annotation rather than preparing numeric feature scores for deep-learning gene/variant prioritization. The missingness structure involves features outside the five score types (EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM) for which the genome-wide non-missing-score bPCA strategy was validated. Imputes missing feature scores (DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) in ANNOVAR-annotated variant feature matrices using Bayesian Principal Component Analysis (bPCA), and audits the imputation with per-feature missingness counts before downstream deep-learning prioritization in iMEGES. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7
skills.summary: Imputes missing feature scores (DANN, CADD, EIGEN, GWAVA, FATHMM) in ANNOVAR-annotated variant feature matrices using Bayesian Principal Component Analysis (bPCA), and audits the imputation with per-feature missingness counts before downstream deep-learning prioritization in iMEGES.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature table is already complete (zero missing values) — imputation is unnecessary and could distort true scores. The goal is variant calling or annotation rather than preparing numeric feature scores for deep-learning gene/variant prioritization. The missingness structure involves features outside the five score types (EIGEN, CADD, DANN, GWAVA, FATHMM) for which the genome-wide non-missing-score bPCA strategy was validated.

skills.description: Use when building a gene-to-phenotype scoring lookup from HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) resources, where each gene needs a tiered score per phenotype group.
skills.name: tabular-scoring-table-construction
skills.search_text: tabular-scoring-table-construction Use when building a gene-to-phenotype scoring lookup from HPO (hp.obo, genes_to_phenotype.txt) and MPO (mp.obo, HMD_HumanPhenotype.rpt) resources, where each gene needs a tiered score per phenotype group. The SV already has a pathogenicity prediction per gene/phenotype/mechanism from POSTRE_multiSV() — this skill builds the gene-phenotype scoring resource, not the per-SV or per-gene results tables. The analysis concerns recessive phenotypes — POSTRE is oriented towards dominant disorders and 'its capacity to identify SVs implicated in recessive phenotypes has not been specifically evaluated'. Only mouse phenotype data exists and the human-only (0 score for mouse-only genes) mode is desired — the 0.5 tier applies in Standard Running Mode only. http://edamontology.org/topic_0166 Constructs per-gene numeric scoring tables (e.g. POSTRE's genePhenoScore) by aggregating ontology-based gene-phenotype associations into tiered scores (1 human, 0.5 mouse-only, 0 none) and emitting them as tab-separated plain text files. It mirrors POSTRE's convention of one row per gene and phenotype group so candidate genes can be scored against SV-associated phenotypes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkad225
skills.summary: Constructs per-gene numeric scoring tables (e.g. POSTRE's genePhenoScore) by aggregating ontology-based gene-phenotype associations into tiered scores (1 human, 0.5 mouse-only, 0 none) and emitting them as tab-separated plain text files. The task graph has no dependencies and a simple single-task workflow (example_basic_sleep.xml) suffices without scheduling logic You only need to validate workflow or module integrity without executing — use workflowValidator.jar or moduleValidator.jar instead of the execution loop Workflows must be defined by rule-based filename inference (as in Snakemake) rather than explicitly declared XML dependencies http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_3365 Reconstructs Watchdog's core control loop: parsing an XML workflow into an in-memory task/dependency representation, generating the initial set of dependency-free tasks, scheduling tasks as dependencies resolve, invoking per-task success checkers, and blocking downstream tasks on failure with manual intervention options. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2107-4
skills.summary: Reconstructs Watchdog's core control loop: parsing an XML workflow into an in-memory task/dependency representation, generating the initial set of dependency-free tasks, scheduling tasks as dependencies resolve, invoking per-task success checkers, and blocking downstream tasks on failure with manual intervention options.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task graph has no dependencies and a simple single-task workflow (example_basic_sleep.xml) suffices without scheduling logic You only need to validate workflow or module integrity without executing — use workflowValidator.jar or moduleValidator.jar instead of the execution loop Workflows must be defined by rule-based filename inference (as in Snakemake) rather than explicitly declared XML dependencies

skills.description: Use when a candidate eccDNA region from whole-genome sequencing (e.g. an AmpliconArchitect-called amplicon) needs chromatin accessibility validation using the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks.
skills.name: tcga-atacseq-bigwig-retrieval
skills.search_text: tcga-atacseq-bigwig-retrieval Use when a candidate eccDNA region from whole-genome sequencing (e.g. an AmpliconArchitect-called amplicon) needs chromatin accessibility validation using the TCGA pan-cancer ATAC-seq BigWig signal tracks. No TCGA ATAC-seq data are available for the cancer type of the eccDNA call (ATAC-seq coverage in TCGA is cancer-type dependent) The goal is eccDNA detection/amplicon reconstruction from WGS data itself — use the AmpliconArchitect pipeline instead; this skill only validates accessibility of already-called regions The candidate region is tiny (e.g. short amplicon) where per-base ATAC-seq signal is too sparse/noisy to interpret as accessibility http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Retrieves and renders TCGA ATAC-seq BigWig coverage tracks over candidate eccDNA genomic regions to test whether eccDNA-containing loci (e.g. EGFR at chr7:54370001-55996000 in GBM) show elevated chromatin accessibility, as done in eccDNAdb's chromatin accessibility integration. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Retrieves and renders TCGA ATAC-seq BigWig coverage tracks over candidate eccDNA genomic regions to test whether eccDNA-containing loci (e.g. EGFR at chr7:54370001-55996000 in GBM) show elevated chromatin accessibility, as done in eccDNAdb's chromatin accessibility integration.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No TCGA ATAC-seq data are available for the cancer type of the eccDNA call (ATAC-seq coverage in TCGA is cancer-type dependent) The goal is eccDNA detection/amplicon reconstruction from WGS data itself — use the AmpliconArchitect pipeline instead; this skill only validates accessibility of already-called regions The candidate region is tiny (e.g. short amplicon) where per-base ATAC-seq signal is too sparse/noisy to interpret as accessibility

skills.description: Use when TCGA gene expression (e.g., EGFR in TCGA-LGG) must be merged with overall-survival clinical metadata and compared between expression-defined patient groups to assess prognosis.
skills.name: tcga-clinical-expression-data-integration
skills.search_text: tcga-clinical-expression-data-integration Use when TCGA gene expression (e.g., EGFR in TCGA-LGG) must be merged with overall-survival clinical metadata and compared between expression-defined patient groups to assess prognosis. No clinical survival time or vital-status metadata is available for the cohort, so no survival comparison can be performed The question concerns eccDNA discovery/identification itself (AmpliconArchitect on WGS data) rather than downstream prognosis testing — the article notes all eccDNAs in eccDNAdb were identified by the AmpliconArchitect pipeline only, which is a separate workflow The outcome is not overall survival (e.g., disease-free survival or response data), since this workflow is defined specifically around OS time and vital status http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 Links TCGA gene expression values with clinical survival metadata to test whether eccDNA-derived gene expression (e.g., EGFR from eccDNA hsa_Chr7_3S_1 in TCGA-LGG) predicts patient prognosis. This mirrors how eccDNAdb integrates expression and clinical data to determine clinical relevance of eccDNAs in cancers. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Links TCGA gene expression values with clinical survival metadata to test whether eccDNA-derived gene expression (e.g., EGFR from eccDNA hsa_Chr7_3S_1 in TCGA-LGG) predicts patient prognosis. This mirrors how eccDNAdb integrates expression and clinical data to determine clinical relevance of eccDNAs in cancers.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No clinical survival time or vital-status metadata is available for the cohort, so no survival comparison can be performed The question concerns eccDNA discovery/identification itself (AmpliconArchitect on WGS data) rather than downstream prognosis testing — the article notes all eccDNAs in eccDNAdb were identified by the AmpliconArchitect pipeline only, which is a separate workflow The outcome is not overall survival (e.g., disease-free survival or response data), since this workflow is defined specifically around OS time and vital status

skills.description: Use when an analysis needs tumor/normal gene expression values for specific genes (e.g., genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) in a cancer cohort such as TCGA-GBM or CCLE cell lines, to compute expression differences and per-gene p-values.
skills.name: tcga-gdc-expression-data-retrieval
skills.search_text: tcga-gdc-expression-data-retrieval Use when an analysis needs tumor/normal gene expression values for specific genes (e.g., genes on an eccDNA like hsa_Chr7_3S_1) in a cancer cohort such as TCGA-GBM or CCLE cell lines, to compute expression differences and per-gene p-values. The eccDNAs or genes of interest lie outside the cohorts covered by eccDNAdb (e.g., non-human species or non-cancer diseases, which the database does not yet include) The goal is eccDNA identification from WGS data rather than expression analysis of already-annotated eccDNA genes — that requires the AmpliconArchitect pipeline, not expression matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Retrieves gene expression matrices for cancer cohorts from TCGA (GDC portal) and CCLE so that eccDNA gene expression can be compared between tumor and normal samples, as done in eccDNAdb where per-gene expression is presented as Tumor vs. Normal box plots with Student's t-test p-values. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41388-022-02286-x
skills.summary: Retrieves gene expression matrices for cancer cohorts from TCGA (GDC portal) and CCLE so that eccDNA gene expression can be compared between tumor and normal samples, as done in eccDNAdb where per-gene expression is presented as Tumor vs. Normal box plots with Student's t-test p-values.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The eccDNAs or genes of interest lie outside the cohorts covered by eccDNAdb (e.g., non-human species or non-cancer diseases, which the database does not yet include) The goal is eccDNA identification from WGS data rather than expression analysis of already-annotated eccDNA genes — that requires the AmpliconArchitect pipeline, not expression matrices

skills.description: Use when raw TCGA-LUAD FPKM expression data (samples as columns, genes as rows) must be converted into SRIQ's required log2/median-centered format, or when per-sample TRU/PI/PP subtype labels must be derived from Wilkerson centroid genes.
skills.name: tcga-luad-expression-matrix-handling
skills.search_text: tcga-luad-expression-matrix-handling Use when raw TCGA-LUAD FPKM expression data (samples as columns, genes as rows) must be converted into SRIQ's required log2/median-centered format, or when per-sample TRU/PI/PP subtype labels must be derived from Wilkerson centroid genes. Input is single-cell sequencing or epigenomic data — the paper states the pipeline is not yet applied to such data types The expression matrix is already off-set, log2-transformed, and median-centered '_mc_log2_nz' output — re-running SRIQPreprocess.jar would double-transform the data The dataset is small, since SRIQ cannot circumvent limited detection of small or underrepresented biological subgroups in smaller datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Handles TCGA-LUAD gene expression matrices for SRIQ clustering and downstream Wilkerson TRU/PI/PP centroid subtyping: preprocessing 434 RNA-seq samples into a log2-transformed, median-centered '_mc_log2_nz' tab-separated matrix and restricting it to subtype centroid genes for Pearson-correlation classification. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: Handles TCGA-LUAD gene expression matrices for SRIQ clustering and downstream Wilkerson TRU/PI/PP centroid subtyping: preprocessing 434 RNA-seq samples into a log2-transformed, median-centered '_mc_log2_nz' tab-separated matrix and restricting it to subtype centroid genes for Pearson-correlation classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is single-cell sequencing or epigenomic data — the paper states the pipeline is not yet applied to such data types The expression matrix is already off-set, log2-transformed, and median-centered '_mc_log2_nz' output — re-running SRIQPreprocess.jar would double-transform the data The dataset is small, since SRIQ cannot circumvent limited detection of small or underrepresented biological subgroups in smaller datasets

skills.name: tcga-pancancer-dataset-loading
skills.search_text: tcga-pancancer-dataset-loading Use when a task requires training or re-tuning CITRUS, reproducing the paper's TCGA experiments, or inspecting the pre-packaged pan-cancer SGA/GEP/TF-target matrices delivered as a pickle file. Your input is a raw, unprocessed TCGA download (Firehose/GDC files) rather than the pre-processed pickle — preprocessing/filtering steps (top-variant gene selection, whitelisting) must be applied first You need patient-level clinical or imaging data; the pickle contains only SGA, GEP, TF-target matrix, cancer types, and tumor barcodes http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 Load the CITRUS-packaged TCGA pan-cancer dataset (dataset_CITRUS.pkl, 5803 samples across 17 tumor types) from the ./data directory and inspect its contents (SGA index lists, GEP of 5541 filtered genes, TF-target matrix, cancer types, tumor barcodes) before model training or hyperparameter sweeps. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881
skills.summary: Load the CITRUS-packaged TCGA pan-cancer dataset (dataset_CITRUS.pkl, 5803 samples across 17 tumor types) from the ./data directory and inspect its contents (SGA index lists, GEP of 5541 filtered genes, TF-target matrix, cancer types, tumor barcodes) before model training or hyperparameter sweeps.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your input is a raw, unprocessed TCGA download (Firehose/GDC files) rather than the pre-processed pickle — preprocessing/filtering steps (top-variant gene selection, whitelisting) must be applied first You need patient-level clinical or imaging data; the pickle contains only SGA, GEP, TF-target matrix, cancer types, and tumor barcodes

skills.description: Use when raw Firehose GISTIC2.0 lesion output (arm-level or focal, with q-values) plus paired TCGA RNASeq expression per cancer type must be transformed into iEDGE objects (cn, gep, cisgenes) as RDS for cis driver analysis.
skills.name: tcga-pancancer-omics-preprocessing
skills.search_text: tcga-pancancer-omics-preprocessing Use when raw Firehose GISTIC2.0 lesion output (arm-level or focal, with q-values) plus paired TCGA RNASeq expression per cancer type must be transformed into iEDGE objects (cn, gep, cisgenes) as RDS for cis driver analysis. Input is already an iEDGE object or RDS file produced by this preprocessing step — proceed directly to run_iEDGE. The epi-DNA data is not GISTIC2.0-formatted copy-number output (e.g., mutation or methylation matrices); other iEDGE converters would be required. The goal is a single-cohort analysis rather than uniform preprocessing across the 19 TCGA cancer types. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Converts Firehose GISTIC2.0 copy-number lesion files and TCGA RNASeq expression matrices, per cancer type, into iEDGE-ready objects (cn, gep, cisgenes) suitable for the iEDGE cis/trans driver pipeline, using the make_GISTIC2/make_GISTIC2_focal converters and the preprocessing logic of scripts_TCGA_pancancer/1.preprocess_all_TCGA.R. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Converts Firehose GISTIC2.0 copy-number lesion files and TCGA RNASeq expression matrices, per cancer type, into iEDGE-ready objects (cn, gep, cisgenes) suitable for the iEDGE cis/trans driver pipeline, using the make_GISTIC2/make_GISTIC2_focal converters and the preprocessing logic of scripts_TCGA_pancancer/1.preprocess_all_TCGA.R.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an iEDGE object or RDS file produced by this preprocessing step — proceed directly to run_iEDGE. The epi-DNA data is not GISTIC2.0-formatted copy-number output (e.g., mutation or methylation matrices); other iEDGE converters would be required. The goal is a single-cohort analysis rather than uniform preprocessing across the 19 TCGA cancer types.

skills.description: Use when preparing SpecHap input: an aligned BAM plus a variant VCF must be converted into per-read allele observations (a fragment file) for haplotype phasing.
skills.name: technology-specific-extracthairs-parameterization
skills.search_text: technology-specific-extracthairs-parameterization Use when preparing SpecHap input: an aligned BAM plus a variant VCF must be converted into per-read allele observations (a fragment file) for haplotype phasing. The goal is haplotype assembly itself — SpecHap (the downstream spectral graph phasing step) handles that; this skill only produces its fragment input Variants include large structural rearrangements — SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions, so fragment extraction for haplotype-resolved structural variation is out of scope Ploidy is higher than diploid — the downstream SpecHap graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Generates the haplotype fragment file that SpecHap consumes by running the modified ExtractHAIRs utility from HapCUT2 with technology-specific flags for WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and Oxford Nanopore data, then sorting the fragment file to match the variant VCF order. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: Generates the haplotype fragment file that SpecHap consumes by running the modified ExtractHAIRs utility from HapCUT2 with technology-specific flags for WGS, Hi-C, 10X linked-reads, PacBio SMRT and Oxford Nanopore data, then sorting the fragment file to match the variant VCF order.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is haplotype assembly itself — SpecHap (the downstream spectral graph phasing step) handles that; this skill only produces its fragment input Variants include large structural rearrangements — SpecHap supports only SNPs and short insertions/deletions, so fragment extraction for haplotype-resolved structural variation is out of scope Ploidy is higher than diploid — the downstream SpecHap graph bisection model does not fit increased ploidy

The target cells have not been through the first-round MLP reference-based prediction — no prediction probabilities exist to compute anchor-selection entropies Input is raw scATAC-seq data (fragment/bam files) rather than processed gene score features — the ArchR preprocessing step must run first A joint reference/target integration method (Seurat, Signac, scJoint) is required because Cellcano does not jointly operate on reference and target datasets http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Train a self-Knowledge Distiller (KD) model on high-confidence anchor cells with pseudo labels to classify remaining non-anchor target cells in Cellcano's second-round scATAC-seq celltyping, using temperature-scaled soft teacher probabilities plus hard pseudo-label cross-entropy. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-023-37439-3

skills.description: Use when you have compartment scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered conditions/time points (e.g. dcHiC quantile-normalized PCA scores at 100 kb for days 1/7/28/56/309/347) and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare pairs of transitions.
skills.name: temporal-cluster-profile-summarization
skills.search_text: temporal-cluster-profile-summarization Use when you have compartment scores for the same genomic bins across ≥3 ordered conditions/time points (e.g. dcHiC quantile-normalized PCA scores at 100 kb for days 1/7/28/56/309/347) and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape rather than compare pairs of transitions. Only two time points/conditions are available — pairwise differential compartment testing with dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance significance is the appropriate analysis, not trajectory clustering The scores are not comparable across conditions (no quantile normalization has been applied), so clusters would reflect scale differences rather than dynamics Input is raw Hi-C contact maps rather than per-bin compartment scores — compartment identification/PCA must be run first http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Groups genomic bins with similar compartment-score trajectories across a multi-point time course by z-transforming dcHiC's quantile-normalized PCA scores and running time-series clustering with the TCseq workflow, then summarizing each cluster's mean Early-to-Late profile. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6
skills.summary: Groups genomic bins with similar compartment-score trajectories across a multi-point time course by z-transforming dcHiC's quantile-normalized PCA scores and running time-series clustering with the TCseq workflow, then summarizing each cluster's mean Early-to-Late profile.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only two time points/conditions are available — pairwise differential compartment testing with dcHiC's Mahalanobis-distance significance is the appropriate analysis, not trajectory clustering The scores are not comparable across conditions (no quantile normalization has been applied), so clusters would reflect scale differences rather than dynamics Input is raw Hi-C contact maps rather than per-bin compartment scores — compartment identification/PCA must be run first

skills.search_text: ten-fold-cross-validation-evaluation Use when evaluating a deep-learning variant-prioritization score (e.g. ncDeepBrain) against labeled disease/non-disease variant sets, where ROC curves and AUC on cross-validated testing data are the required performance metrics. The goal is gene-level prioritization (iMEGES step 2 score with GTEx, RVIS, haploinsufficiency, Phenolyzer features) rather than non-coding variant classification The input is already a trained model output or rank list, with no labeled positive/negative testing set to compute ROC/AUC Class balance and feature imputation (ROSE, bPCA) cannot be applied because the raw variant-score annotations are unavailable http://edamontology.org/topic_0196 Benchmark the ncDeepBrain non-coding variant score in iMEGES by training its Keras/TensorFlow multilayer neural network on four feature matrices and running ten-fold cross-validation on held-out testing datasets, generating ROC curves and AUC values to verify classification performance against the published figures. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-018-2469-7

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is gene-level prioritization (iMEGES step 2 score with GTEx, RVIS, haploinsufficiency, Phenolyzer features) rather than non-coding variant classification The input is already a trained model output or rank list, with no labeled positive/negative testing set to compute ROC/AUC Class balance and feature imputation (ROSE, bPCA) cannot be applied because the raw variant-score annotations are unavailable

skills.search_text: ten-fold-cross-validation-of-sequence-classifiers Use when reproducing or extending promoter-prediction benchmarking that requires ten-fold cross-validation of ensemble sequence classifiers (RF + CNN + weighted average) on labeled promoter/non-promoter FASTA-style training sets. skills.name: tensorflow-model-shape-verification
skills.search_text: tensorflow-model-shape-verification Use when reimplementing, auditing, or extending the DESSO motif-prediction CNN and you must verify that filter kernels, fully connected weights, and output-layer weights match the published layer dimensions. The goal is to train the Gated-CNN (GCNN) on long 1001 bp sequences rather than verify the base CNN — use the GCNN workflow with --peak_flank 500 instead Input is already a trained model checkpoint and the task is motif prediction (predict.py) rather than architecture verification The framework or TensorFlow version differs substantially (DESSO was built against TensorFlow 1.1.0 and Python 2.7), so shape conventions may not transfer directly http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Reconstructs the one-layer DESSO CNN architecture in TensorFlow (16 convolutional filters, ReLU, max pooling, a 32-neuron fully connected layer, and a single sigmoid output unit) and asserts that every parameter shape matches the published specification for sequence and DNA shape inputs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672

skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is to train the Gated-CNN (GCNN) on long 1001 bp sequences rather than verify the base CNN — use the GCNN workflow with --peak_flank 500 instead Input is already a trained model checkpoint and the task is motif prediction (predict.py) rather than architecture verification The framework or TensorFlow version differs substantially (DESSO was built against TensorFlow 1.1.0 and Python 2.7), so shape conventions may not transfer directly

skills.description: Use when you have per-RBP enriched-window/peak counts from two or more CLIP-seq callers (e.g., Skipper, Piranha, CLIPper) on the same ENCODE eCLIP datasets and must visualize and quantify how caller sensitivity compares.
skills.name: ternary-and-scatter-method-comparison-visualization
skills.search_text: ternary-and-scatter-method-comparison-visualization Use when you have per-RBP enriched-window/peak counts from two or more CLIP-seq callers (e.g., Skipper, Piranha, CLIPper) on the same ENCODE eCLIP datasets and must visualize and quantify how caller sensitivity compares. CLIP datasets lacking matched input controls — Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model, so the Skipper arm of the comparison cannot be computed Datasets where callers were run on different window tiling or genome builds — genomic interval overlap comparisons would be confounded and counts non-comparable Analyses not benchmarking caller sensitivity, e.g., motif discovery or fine-mapping of individual binding sites http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_0769 Benchmarking visualization skill for comparing called binding-site counts across eCLIP peak/window callers: Skipper vs Piranha vs ENCODE CLIPper, rendered as Figure 2A ternary and Figure 2B scatter summaries with an aggregate method_comparison_counts.csv table. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Benchmarking visualization skill for comparing called binding-site counts across eCLIP peak/window callers: Skipper vs Piranha vs ENCODE CLIPper, rendered as Figure 2A ternary and Figure 2B scatter summaries with an aggregate method_comparison_counts.csv table.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking matched input controls — Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model, so the Skipper arm of the comparison cannot be computed Datasets where callers were run on different window tiling or genome builds — genomic interval overlap comparisons would be confounded and counts non-comparable Analyses not benchmarking caller sensitivity, e.g., motif discovery or fine-mapping of individual binding sites

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq peak files and DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs are available for a panel of TFs in one cell type, and you need to identify co-factor-mediated (tethering) binding by finding peaks lacking a TF's own motif that co-occur with another TF's motif-bearing peaks.
skills.name: tethering-interaction-inference-from-chip-seq
skills.search_text: tethering-interaction-inference-from-chip-seq Use when ChIP-seq peak files and DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs are available for a panel of TFs in one cell type, and you need to identify co-factor-mediated (tethering) binding by finding peaks lacking a TF's own motif that co-occur with another TF's motif-bearing peaks. You only have peak files without DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs, since D/I/K peak classification depends on matching peaks against predicted motif instances The goal is direct motif discovery or DNA-shape motif prediction from ChIP-seq peaks rather than inferring co-factor-mediated tethering between TFs Only a single TF's ChIP-seq data is available, since the method requires cross-matching I peaks of one TF against D peaks of other TFs Infers putative protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions by cross-matching DESSO-classified indirect-binding (I) peaks of one TF against direct-binding (D) peaks of another TF, applied here to the 100 TFs expressed in the K562 cell line. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Infers putative protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions by cross-matching DESSO-classified indirect-binding (I) peaks of one TF against direct-binding (D) peaks of another TF, applied here to the 100 TFs expressed in the K562 cell line.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only have peak files without DESSO-predicted motifs/TFBSs, since D/I/K peak classification depends on matching peaks against predicted motif instances The goal is direct motif discovery or DNA-shape motif prediction from ChIP-seq peaks rather than inferring co-factor-mediated tethering between TFs Only a single TF's ChIP-seq data is available, since the method requires cross-matching I peaks of one TF against D peaks of other TFs
