skills.name: trans-homolog-interference-removal
skills.search_text: trans-homolog-interference-removal Use when preparing Hi-C fragment files for SpecHap phasing: read pairs with inferred insertion spanning >40 Mbp signal trans-homolog interactions and higher trans interaction error rates that should be dropped before assembly. Input fragments come from WGS, PacBio SMRT or Oxford Nanopore data where long spans reflect true read length rather than trans-homolog ligation artifacts The analysis goal is to model or study trans-homolog interactions rather than exclude them from diploid phasing The fragment file is not Hi-C mode output (not generated with extractHAIRS --hic 1), since the insertion-size criterion is Hi-C specific http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 A Hi-C fragment filtering step from the SpecHap pipeline that removes read pairs whose inferred insertion size exceeds 40 Mbp, so that trans-homolog interactions—which SpecHap treats as general errors rather than modeling them—are excluded from haplotype assembly. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab709
skills.summary: A Hi-C fragment filtering step from the SpecHap pipeline that removes read pairs whose inferred insertion size exceeds 40 Mbp, so that trans-homolog interactions—which SpecHap treats as general errors rather than modeling them—are excluded from haplotype assembly.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input fragments come from WGS, PacBio SMRT or Oxford Nanopore data where long spans reflect true read length rather than trans-homolog ligation artifacts The analysis goal is to model or study trans-homolog interactions rather than exclude them from diploid phasing The fragment file is not Hi-C mode output (not generated with extractHAIRS --hic 1), since the insertion-size criterion is Hi-C specific

skills.description: Use when RNA-Seq alignments (BAM/SAM, e.g. from SRA012427 or MAQC HBR libraries) must be converted into per-transcript expression estimates whose non-uniform fragment bias has been corrected before correlation or differential-expression analysis.
skills.name: transcript-expression-quantification
skills.search_text: transcript-expression-quantification Use when RNA-Seq alignments (BAM/SAM, e.g. from SRA012427 or MAQC HBR libraries) must be converted into per-transcript expression estimates whose non-uniform fragment bias has been corrected before correlation or differential-expression analysis. When expression estimates have already been bias-corrected upstream (re-correcting the same alignments risks double-modeling fragment bias) When no reference genome FASTA is available for the alignments, since the -b fragment-bias correction cannot be applied When the input is not fragment-level alignment data (e.g. already-aggregated count or FPKM tables), since the likelihood approach operates on fragment alignments http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 http://edamontology.org/topic_3520 Estimate transcript-level expression from RNA-Seq alignments with a likelihood-based approach that simultaneously models fragment bias (non-uniform cDNA fragment distribution) and abundance, yielding corrected expression estimates and improved cross-library replicability. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Estimate transcript-level expression from RNA-Seq alignments with a likelihood-based approach that simultaneously models fragment bias (non-uniform cDNA fragment distribution) and abundance, yielding corrected expression estimates and improved cross-library replicability.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When expression estimates have already been bias-corrected upstream (re-correcting the same alignments risks double-modeling fragment bias) When no reference genome FASTA is available for the alignments, since the -b fragment-bias correction cannot be applied When the input is not fragment-level alignment data (e.g. already-aggregated count or FPKM tables), since the likelihood approach operates on fragment alignments

skills.description: Use when per-window variant-depletion delta scores exist for RBP binding windows and you need transcript-level nomination of constrained RBP-transcript pairs with FDR control.
skills.name: transcript-level-constraint-aggregation
skills.search_text: transcript-level-constraint-aggregation Use when per-window variant-depletion delta scores exist for RBP binding windows and you need transcript-level nomination of constrained RBP-transcript pairs with FDR control. CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and no fine-mapped windows exist to aggregate You need binding-site-level (window-level) constraint calls rather than transcript-level hypotheses; per-window constraint signal is noisier and the transcript-level step is explicitly an aggregation http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Aggregates per-window selective-constraint evidence (mean LS-GKM delta score regressed against gnomAD allele-frequency bins) up to the RBP-transcript level and applies multiple-testing correction at 10% FDR to nominate constrained translation factor binding targets. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Aggregates per-window selective-constraint evidence (mean LS-GKM delta score regressed against gnomAD allele-frequency bins) up to the RBP-transcript level and applies multiple-testing correction at 10% FDR to nominate constrained translation factor binding targets.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lacking a matched input sample, since Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and no fine-mapped windows exist to aggregate You need binding-site-level (window-level) constraint calls rather than transcript-level hypotheses; per-window constraint signal is noisier and the transcript-level step is explicitly an aggregation

skills.description: Use when two RNA-Seq libraries from different sequencing platforms (e.g. SOLiD MAQC WT-protocol and Illumina SRA012427) need expression estimates compared, and you must quantify how fragment-bias correction improves cross-platform agreement.
skills.name: transcript-level-estimate-reconciliation-across-sequencing-technologies
skills.search_text: transcript-level-estimate-reconciliation-across-sequencing-technologies Use when two RNA-Seq libraries from different sequencing platforms (e.g. SOLiD MAQC WT-protocol and Illumina SRA012427) need expression estimates compared, and you must quantify how fragment-bias correction improves cross-platform agreement. Libraries are generated on the same sequencing platform with the same sample preparation — bias correction regimes are designed to explain cross-technology discordance, not within-platform variation. Input is raw reads without alignments: eXpress-D requires fragment alignments plus reference transcript sequences, not FASTQ alone. You only need within-library differential expression ranking; this skill targets cross-platform correlation of absolute expression estimates. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Reconciles transcript-level RNA-Seq expression estimates generated on different sequencing technologies (Illumina vs SOLiD) by running likelihood-based estimation in eXpress-D under four fragment-bias-correction regimes and joining estimates by transcript identifier to compute cross-platform Pearson R-squared. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/gb-2011-12-3-r22
skills.summary: Reconciles transcript-level RNA-Seq expression estimates generated on different sequencing technologies (Illumina vs SOLiD) by running likelihood-based estimation in eXpress-D under four fragment-bias-correction regimes and joining estimates by transcript identifier to compute cross-platform Pearson R-squared.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Libraries are generated on the same sequencing platform with the same sample preparation — bias correction regimes are designed to explain cross-technology discordance, not within-platform variation. Input is raw reads without alignments: eXpress-D requires fragment alignments plus reference transcript sequences, not FASTQ alone. You only need within-library differential expression ranking; this skill targets cross-platform correlation of absolute expression estimates.

skills.description: Use when benchmarking TPX prediction tools on peak regions and you need shuffled-transcript negative controls that preserve nucleotide composition while destroying genuine triplex-forming signal.
skills.name: transcript-sequence-scrambling
skills.search_text: transcript-sequence-scrambling Use when benchmarking TPX prediction tools on peak regions and you need shuffled-transcript negative controls that preserve nucleotide composition while destroying genuine triplex-forming signal. When the negative-control strategy of interest is randomised genomic regions (bedtools shuffle excluding positives, genome gaps and ENCODE blacklist regions) rather than scrambled transcripts — that is a separate strategy in the paper's benchmark. When sequence order information must be preserved (e.g. k-mer frequency analyses sensitive to local context), since -kmer 1 shuffling destroys all di- and higher-order structure. http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 Generates negative-control sequences by shuffling transcript nucleotides with fasta-shuffle-letters (MEME suite, -kmer 1) so that TPX prediction tools can be benchmarked against matched-composition but non-functional transcript sequences. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Generates negative-control sequences by shuffling transcript nucleotides with fasta-shuffle-letters (MEME suite, -kmer 1) so that TPX prediction tools can be benchmarked against matched-composition but non-functional transcript sequences.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the negative-control strategy of interest is randomised genomic regions (bedtools shuffle excluding positives, genome gaps and ENCODE blacklist regions) rather than scrambled transcripts — that is a separate strategy in the paper's benchmark. When sequence order information must be preserved (e.g. k-mer frequency analyses sensitive to local context), since -kmer 1 shuffling destroys all di- and higher-order structure.

skills.description: Use when you have a time-series expression matrix plus TF–TG interaction data and need to identify which TFs significantly regulate each subpath of a tree-structure model and when they are activated or repressed.
skills.name: transcription-factor-activity-inference
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-activity-inference Use when you have a time-series expression matrix plus TF–TG interaction data and need to identify which TFs significantly regulate each subpath of a tree-structure model and when they are activated or repressed. Input is a single-condition or static (non-time-series) expression profile — TSMiner is built specifically for time-series expression data No TF–gene interaction data are available for the organism, since the hypergeometric/permutation scoring depends on TF-TG interaction information The goal is clustering expression profiles rather than inferring time-specific regulator activity — clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 TSMiner's TF prediction module assigns transcription factors to time-specific subpaths of a tree-structure model using a hypergeometric test followed by a permutation test (Benjamini–Hochberg corrected), then classifies each TF as activated or repressed at specific time points based on the average fold change of its target genes. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: TSMiner's TF prediction module assigns transcription factors to time-specific subpaths of a tree-structure model using a hypergeometric test followed by a permutation test (Benjamini–Hochberg corrected), then classifies each TF as activated or repressed at specific time points based on the average fold change of its target genes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single-condition or static (non-time-series) expression profile — TSMiner is built specifically for time-series expression data No TF–gene interaction data are available for the organism, since the hypergeometric/permutation scoring depends on TF-TG interaction information The goal is clustering expression profiles rather than inferring time-specific regulator activity — clustering methods cannot evaluate the temporal dynamics of regulators or pathways

skills.description: Use when raw DNA binding sequences from uPBM, HT-SELEX or gcPBM must be converted into structural/mechanical feature matrices to train or apply a transcription-factor affinity regressor.
skills.name: transcription-factor-affinity-feature-engineering
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-affinity-feature-engineering Use when raw DNA binding sequences from uPBM, HT-SELEX or gcPBM must be converted into structural/mechanical feature matrices to train or apply a transcription-factor affinity regressor. Input is already a feature table or preprocessed data file (e.g. Gata4_training.txt from the test_data folder) ready for the regressor — skip to {method}_regressor.py The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than affinity prediction — use MEME suite, BEESEM, or BindSpace instead Sequences contain non-standard nucleobases or epigenetic variants beyond the tetramer parameter database, where lookups will fail http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Engineer DNA sequence features for the DNAffinity random-forest affinity predictor: overlapping tetramer counts plus indirect-readout (MD-derived equilibrium geometry and flexibility) and direct-readout (electrostatic) base-pair-step parameters, feeding {method}_regressor.py. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Engineer DNA sequence features for the DNAffinity random-forest affinity predictor: overlapping tetramer counts plus indirect-readout (MD-derived equilibrium geometry and flexibility) and direct-readout (electrostatic) base-pair-step parameters, feeding {method}_regressor.py.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already a feature table or preprocessed data file (e.g. Gata4_training.txt from the test_data folder) ready for the regressor — skip to {method}_regressor.py The goal is de novo motif discovery rather than affinity prediction — use MEME suite, BEESEM, or BindSpace instead Sequences contain non-standard nucleobases or epigenetic variants beyond the tetramer parameter database, where lookups will fail

skills.description: Use when experimental TF-DNA binding data (uPBM training files, gcPBM concentration files, HT-SELEX per-cycle count files) must be converted into per-sequence affinity predictions with an R2-validated random-forest regressor.
skills.name: transcription-factor-affinity-regression
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-affinity-regression Use when experimental TF-DNA binding data (uPBM training files, gcPBM concentration files, HT-SELEX per-cycle count files) must be converted into per-sequence affinity predictions with an R2-validated random-forest regressor. When extrapolating in vitro predictions to in vivo TFBS identification: this regressor alone does not model chromatin — combine it with yeast G1 nucleosome positioning maps instead When the input is already a trained model or affinity prediction table rather than raw per-cycle/per-concentration sequence count files For experimental techniques other than uPBM, gcPBM and HT-SELEX, which the provided regressors are not configured to parse http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Train the DNAffinity random-forest regressor on uPBM, gcPBM or HT-SELEX in vitro binding data using DNA structural/mechanical features derived from atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, to produce per-sequence transcription factor binding affinity predictions evaluated by R2 on a held-out 20% split. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac708
skills.summary: Train the DNAffinity random-forest regressor on uPBM, gcPBM or HT-SELEX in vitro binding data using DNA structural/mechanical features derived from atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, to produce per-sequence transcription factor binding affinity predictions evaluated by R2 on a held-out 20% split.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When extrapolating in vitro predictions to in vivo TFBS identification: this regressor alone does not model chromatin — combine it with yeast G1 nucleosome positioning maps instead When the input is already a trained model or affinity prediction table rather than raw per-cycle/per-concentration sequence count files For experimental techniques other than uPBM, gcPBM and HT-SELEX, which the provided regressors are not configured to parse

skills.description: Use when you have anchor-centered sequences (FASTA with per-sequence scores in headers) and a motif PWM, and need motif match positions/scores relative to the anchor for positional enrichment profiling.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-scoring
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-motif-scoring Use when you have anchor-centered sequences (FASTA with per-sequence scores in headers) and a motif PWM, and need motif match positions/scores relative to the anchor for positional enrichment profiling. You need de novo motif discovery — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library and does not recognize or assemble new motifs You need a single aggregate motif enrichment score independent of position — MEPP outputs a positional profile rather than a position-independent enrichment statistic Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or peak summit) — the positional profile requires a common anchor to be interpretable http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Score centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around MACS2 ChIP-seq peak summits) for TF binding motif occurrences using a position weight matrix (e.g. the GATA1 PWM from JASPAR/HOMER-format motif files), producing motif match positions and scores that MEPP uses to build a position-dependent enrichment profile around the anchor point. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Score centered genomic sequences (e.g. ±200 bp around MACS2 ChIP-seq peak summits) for TF binding motif occurrences using a position weight matrix (e.g. the GATA1 PWM from JASPAR/HOMER-format motif files), producing motif match positions and scores that MEPP uses to build a position-dependent enrichment profile around the anchor point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need de novo motif discovery — MEPP currently only functions with a fixed motif library and does not recognize or assemble new motifs You need a single aggregate motif enrichment score independent of position — MEPP outputs a positional profile rather than a position-independent enrichment statistic Your sequences are not centered on a biologically meaningful anchor point (e.g. TSS or peak summit) — the positional profile requires a common anchor to be interpretable

skills.description: Use when a non-coding SNP needs functional interpretation against a transcription factor binding profile, and you want saturated mutagenesis SAD heat maps that reveal which motif and which allele-specific substitutions drive predicted binding activity.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-profile-interpretation
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-profile-interpretation Use when a non-coding SNP needs functional interpretation against a transcription factor binding profile, and you want saturated mutagenesis SAD heat maps that reveal which motif and which allele-specific substitutions drive predicted binding activity. The question concerns DNA accessibility, histone marks, or CTCF binding rather than transcription factor binding profiles — model A (dnacnn_best_A.zip / DeepFun_best_A.th.gz) is the appropriate pre-trained model instead You need to assess long-range regulatory effects such as 3D DNA contact, which the DeepFun model does not consider You only need a variant's predicted effect without motif dissection — the SNP Activity Difference (SAD) workflow is simpler than saturated mutagenesis http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Runs DeepFun's in silico saturated mutagenesis (via Basset's sat-mut workflow) to predict the effect of every single-nucleotide substitution within ~200 bp of a query SNP on transcription factor binding profiles, and reads out the motif (e.g. NFE2 TGACTCAGCA) that explains the predicted binding change. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Runs DeepFun's in silico saturated mutagenesis (via Basset's sat-mut workflow) to predict the effect of every single-nucleotide substitution within ~200 bp of a query SNP on transcription factor binding profiles, and reads out the motif (e.g. NFE2 TGACTCAGCA) that explains the predicted binding change.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The question concerns DNA accessibility, histone marks, or CTCF binding rather than transcription factor binding profiles — model A (dnacnn_best_A.zip / DeepFun_best_A.th.gz) is the appropriate pre-trained model instead You need to assess long-range regulatory effects such as 3D DNA contact, which the DeepFun model does not consider You only need a variant's predicted effect without motif dissection — the SNP Activity Difference (SAD) workflow is simpler than saturated mutagenesis

skills.description: Use when converting enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for a deep learning enhancer predictor, using HOCOMOCO v11 PWMs with p-value thresholds.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-site-detection
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-site-detection Use when converting enhancer FASTA sequences (e.g. data/train/NHLF.fasta) into per-motif TFBS count/frequency features for a deep learning enhancer predictor, using HOCOMOCO v11 PWMs with p-value thresholds. Input is already an extracted feature table (motif frequency vectors); re-running motif extraction would duplicate Step 2 The goal is dna2vec k-mer word vector features rather than PWM-based TFBS motif features; use dna2vec_code.py instead Sequences are non-human enhancers: the PWMs and p-value thresholds come from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database, so TFBS counts for other species are not supported by the provided motif files http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Encodes cell-line enhancer DNA sequences into fixed-length motif frequency feature vectors by matching sequences against transcription factor binding motif PWMs from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database. This motif feature input is one of the two feature streams consumed by the Enhancer-MDLF multi-input deep learning framework for cell-specific enhancer prediction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Encodes cell-line enhancer DNA sequences into fixed-length motif frequency feature vectors by matching sequences against transcription factor binding motif PWMs from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database. This motif feature input is one of the two feature streams consumed by the Enhancer-MDLF multi-input deep learning framework for cell-specific enhancer prediction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already an extracted feature table (motif frequency vectors); re-running motif extraction would duplicate Step 2 The goal is dna2vec k-mer word vector features rather than PWM-based TFBS motif features; use dna2vec_code.py instead Sequences are non-human enhancers: the PWMs and p-value thresholds come from the HOCOMOCO Human v11 database, so TFBS counts for other species are not supported by the provided motif files

skills.description: Use when you have a promoter nucleotide sequence (FASTA) and a known TF consensus/position-specific motif, and need to enumerate motif matches and test positional overlap with other factors' binding sites.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-site-mapping
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-site-mapping Use when you have a promoter nucleotide sequence (FASTA) and a known TF consensus/position-specific motif, and need to enumerate motif matches and test positional overlap with other factors' binding sites. Input is ChIP-seq peak data rather than a promoter nucleotide sequence — use peak-overlap tooling (e.g., the deposited findOverlaps.pl/getPeakAnno.pl scripts) instead No credible motif for the factor of interest is available; FIMO scanning of an arbitrary/unsupported motif would not reproduce the article's H-NS nucleation-site logic The goal is genome-wide binding discovery from ChIP-seq (e.g., the 506 LuxR / 302 H-NS peaks via MACS2), not targeted motif scanning of a single promoter http://edamontology.org/topic_0160 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Maps transcription factor binding sites on a promoter sequence by scanning a known, high-affinity motif (e.g., the E. coli H-NS nucleation motif TCGATAAATT) with FIMO, then intersecting predicted sites with independently established binding sites (here, the seven established LuxR binding sites in the PluxCDABE promoter). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Maps transcription factor binding sites on a promoter sequence by scanning a known, high-affinity motif (e.g., the E. coli H-NS nucleation motif TCGATAAATT) with FIMO, then intersecting predicted sites with independently established binding sites (here, the seven established LuxR binding sites in the PluxCDABE promoter).
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is ChIP-seq peak data rather than a promoter nucleotide sequence — use peak-overlap tooling (e.g., the deposited findOverlaps.pl/getPeakAnno.pl scripts) instead No credible motif for the factor of interest is available; FIMO scanning of an arbitrary/unsupported motif would not reproduce the article's H-NS nucleation-site logic The goal is genome-wide binding discovery from ChIP-seq (e.g., the 506 LuxR / 302 H-NS peaks via MACS2), not targeted motif scanning of a single promoter

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq peak coordinate files (e.g., MACS2 peak lists from GSE136050 H-NS and GSE136191 LuxR datasets) must be related by interval distance — e.g., counting how many of a structural peak class (H-NS doublets) lie within 1 kb of a TF peak.
skills.name: transcription-factor-binding-site-proximity-annotation
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-binding-site-proximity-annotation Use when ChIP-seq peak coordinate files (e.g., MACS2 peak lists from GSE136050 H-NS and GSE136191 LuxR datasets) must be related by interval distance — e.g., counting how many of a structural peak class (H-NS doublets) lie within 1 kb of a TF peak. When the goal is simple peak-overlap Venn counting of two peak sets (≤500 bp ORF-proximal overlap of 88 peaks) rather than doublet-structure-plus-proximity annotation — use findOverlaps.pl-style set overlap instead. When peaks lack height/trough information, since doublet detection requires the trough (≤80% of the lower peak height) criterion and cannot be computed from coordinates alone. When annotating peaks to gene ORFs rather than to another TF's binding sites — getPeakAnno.pl/getGenePeakAnno2.pl gene annotation is the wrong proxy for TF-to-TF proximity. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A method for annotating transcription factor (LuxR) ChIP-seq peaks by their genomic proximity to architecturally distinctive features of a second ChIP-seq dataset (H-NS doublet peaks), computed with interval-distance logic in Perl over MACS2-derived peak coordinate tables. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: A method for annotating transcription factor (LuxR) ChIP-seq peaks by their genomic proximity to architecturally distinctive features of a second ChIP-seq dataset (H-NS doublet peaks), computed with interval-distance logic in Perl over MACS2-derived peak coordinate tables.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is simple peak-overlap Venn counting of two peak sets (≤500 bp ORF-proximal overlap of 88 peaks) rather than doublet-structure-plus-proximity annotation — use findOverlaps.pl-style set overlap instead. When peaks lack height/trough information, since doublet detection requires the trough (≤80% of the lower peak height) criterion and cannot be computed from coordinates alone. When annotating peaks to gene ORFs rather than to another TF's binding sites — getPeakAnno.pl/getGenePeakAnno2.pl gene annotation is the wrong proxy for TF-to-TF proximity.

skills.description: Use when two transcription factors have ChIP-seq peak sets and transcriptomic differential-expression data, and the goal is promoters and downstream genes co-occupied and co-regulated by both factors.
skills.name: transcription-factor-co-occupancy-intersection
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-co-occupancy-intersection Use when two transcription factors have ChIP-seq peak sets and transcriptomic differential-expression data, and the goal is promoters and downstream genes co-occupied and co-regulated by both factors. Input is a single transcription factor's ChIP-seq data with no second factor to intersect — co-occupancy logic does not apply. The question is about ChIP-seq peak calling quality or normalization rather than promoter-level overlap with transcriptomic co-regulation. Peaks are not anchored to annotated ORFs/promoters (no gene annotation available), so the 500-bp-upstream promoter assignment cannot be made. http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Method for identifying promoters co-occupied and co-regulated by two transcription factors (here V. harveyi LuxR and H-NS) by intersecting ChIP-seq peak overlaps with RNA-seq co-regulation data using deposited Perl annotation scripts. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: Method for identifying promoters co-occupied and co-regulated by two transcription factors (here V. harveyi LuxR and H-NS) by intersecting ChIP-seq peak overlaps with RNA-seq co-regulation data using deposited Perl annotation scripts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a single transcription factor's ChIP-seq data with no second factor to intersect — co-occupancy logic does not apply. The question is about ChIP-seq peak calling quality or normalization rather than promoter-level overlap with transcriptomic co-regulation. Peaks are not anchored to annotated ORFs/promoters (no gene annotation available), so the 500-bp-upstream promoter assignment cannot be made.

skills.description: Use when you have DESSO motifs/TFBSs and ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs in one cell line and need to classify indirect binding and infer TF-cofactor tethering from motif co-occurrence.
skills.name: transcription-factor-cofactor-motif-annotation
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-cofactor-motif-annotation Use when you have DESSO motifs/TFBSs and ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks for multiple TFs in one cell line and need to classify indirect binding and infer TF-cofactor tethering from motif co-occurrence. You only need de novo motif discovery from ChIP-seq peaks without classifying direct vs indirect binding or inferring tethering ChIP-seq data lacks the paired motif/TFBS predictions needed to distinguish D, I, and K peaks http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Annotates ChIP-seq peaks of a TF as direct-binding (D), indirect-binding (I) or indecipherable (K) using DESSO-predicted motifs, then cross-matches I peaks against D peaks of other TFs to infer putative protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions (e.g. 61 associations among 100 K562 TFs, including ATF3-USF1 and NFE2-MAX). epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Annotates ChIP-seq peaks of a TF as direct-binding (D), indirect-binding (I) or indecipherable (K) using DESSO-predicted motifs, then cross-matches I peaks against D peaks of other TFs to infer putative protein-protein-DNA tethering interactions (e.g. 61 associations among 100 K562 TFs, including ATF3-USF1 and NFE2-MAX).
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need de novo motif discovery from ChIP-seq peaks without classifying direct vs indirect binding or inferring tethering ChIP-seq data lacks the paired motif/TFBS predictions needed to distinguish D, I, and K peaks

skills.description: Use when a set of de novo TF sequence motifs (e.g., predicted by DESSO from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) needs to be labeled as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or flagged as novel/undocumented.
skills.name: transcription-factor-motif-database-matching
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-motif-database-matching Use when a set of de novo TF sequence motifs (e.g., predicted by DESSO from ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks) needs to be labeled as matching documented JASPAR/TRANSFAC motifs or flagged as novel/undocumented. Input motifs are already annotated with database IDs — matching is only needed for de novo, unannotated motifs Analyzing DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) from --feature_format DNAShape — these are not directly matchable to JASPAR/TRANSFAC sequence logos The goal is TF-DNA binding prediction accuracy (AUC) rather than motif annotation/classification http://edamontology.org/topic_0080 Classifies de novo DNA motifs discovered by DESSO's CNN framework on ENCODE ChIP-seq data into known versus undocumented classes by matching them against documented motifs in the JASPAR and TRANSFAC databases, using TOMTOM similarity scores and hierarchical clustering of representative motifs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz672
skills.summary: Classifies de novo DNA motifs discovered by DESSO's CNN framework on ENCODE ChIP-seq data into known versus undocumented classes by matching them against documented motifs in the JASPAR and TRANSFAC databases, using TOMTOM similarity scores and hierarchical clustering of representative motifs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input motifs are already annotated with database IDs — matching is only needed for de novo, unannotated motifs Analyzing DNA shape motifs (HelT, MGW, ProT, Roll) from --feature_format DNAShape — these are not directly matchable to JASPAR/TRANSFAC sequence logos The goal is TF-DNA binding prediction accuracy (AUC) rather than motif annotation/classification

skills.description: Use when you have binarized topic-enriched regions from a cisTopic model on single-cell ATAC-seq data and want to recover topic-specific TF cistromes and master regulators such as SPI1 and CEBPB.
skills.name: transcription-factor-motif-enrichment-analysis
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-motif-enrichment-analysis Use when you have binarized topic-enriched regions from a cisTopic model on single-cell ATAC-seq data and want to recover topic-specific TF cistromes and master regulators such as SPI1 and CEBPB. The input is raw fragments/peaks and no cisTopic topic model has been fit yet — run the LDA topic modeling and binarizecisTopics steps first. Your regions are from a genome assembly other than what the available RcisTarget feather databases cover (cisTopic's current version provides hg19 databases; mm10/hg38 require separate vignette workflows). You need de novo motif discovery rather than recovery of known TF motifs via enrichment over a precomputed ranking database. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Identifies master regulator transcription factors of cisTopic topics by running RcisTarget motif-enrichment analysis on the binarized, topic-enriched regions (e.g. PBMC topics), ranking TFs by normalized enrichment score (NES) against an hg19 region-based ranking database. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-019-0367-1
skills.summary: Identifies master regulator transcription factors of cisTopic topics by running RcisTarget motif-enrichment analysis on the binarized, topic-enriched regions (e.g. PBMC topics), ranking TFs by normalized enrichment score (NES) against an hg19 region-based ranking database.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is raw fragments/peaks and no cisTopic topic model has been fit yet — run the LDA topic modeling and binarizecisTopics steps first. Your regions are from a genome assembly other than what the available RcisTarget feather databases cover (cisTopic's current version provides hg19 databases; mm10/hg38 require separate vignette workflows). You need de novo motif discovery rather than recovery of known TF motifs via enrichment over a precomputed ranking database.

skills.description: Use when the input is a genome-wide TF motif occurrence track (e.g. JASPAR PWM-derived BED with strand annotations) and the goal is to quantify orientation bias — same vs opposite strand — between consecutive or paired motif occurrences.
skills.name: transcription-factor-motif-occurrence-analysis
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-motif-occurrence-analysis Use when the input is a genome-wide TF motif occurrence track (e.g. JASPAR PWM-derived BED with strand annotations) and the goal is to quantify orientation bias — same vs opposite strand — between consecutive or paired motif occurrences. The motif is palindromic — palindromic motifs cannot be oriented relative to one another, so same/opposite strand classification is meaningless (only non-palindromic motifs like CTCF are suitable). The input lacks strand annotations and no strand information can be assigned — Asymmetron requires DNA features provided with strand annotation (though the separate 'orientation' function can assign strand to a feature based on an overlapping strand-annotated feature). The question concerns strand asymmetry of features within regions or relative to transcription/replication rather than consecutive occurrences — use contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries instead. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3125 Workflow for analyzing the strand orientation of genome-wide transcription factor binding site (TFBS) motif occurrences using strand-annotated BED files and Asymmetron's consecutive strand asymmetry estimation, as demonstrated with CTCF (JASPAR MA0139.1) homotypic motif pairs. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Workflow for analyzing the strand orientation of genome-wide transcription factor binding site (TFBS) motif occurrences using strand-annotated BED files and Asymmetron's consecutive strand asymmetry estimation, as demonstrated with CTCF (JASPAR MA0139.1) homotypic motif pairs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The motif is palindromic — palindromic motifs cannot be oriented relative to one another, so same/opposite strand classification is meaningless (only non-palindromic motifs like CTCF are suitable). The input lacks strand annotations and no strand information can be assigned — Asymmetron requires DNA features provided with strand annotation (though the separate 'orientation' function can assign strand to a feature based on an overlapping strand-annotated feature). The question concerns strand asymmetry of features within regions or relative to transcription/replication rather than consecutive occurrences — use contained_asymmetries or pairwise_asymmetries instead.

skills.description: Use when you have FASTA sequences under predicted ChIP-enriched peaks (plus matched control sequences) and need to verify enrichment of an expected TF binding motif family, or compare motif enrichment across peak ranks or platforms.
skills.name: transcription-factor-motif-scanning
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-motif-scanning Use when you have FASTA sequences under predicted ChIP-enriched peaks (plus matched control sequences) and need to verify enrichment of an expected TF binding motif family, or compare motif enrichment across peak ranks or platforms. The binding motif of interest is novel or not represented in motif databases — the article notes many stored motif patterns may be inaccurate and novel motifs may not exist in databases You have peak intervals but no matched control sequences, so no test-vs-control chi-square enrichment can be computed You need de novo motif discovery rather than scanning against known curated matrices http://edamontology.org/topic_0797 Scan genomic sequences underlying ChIP-Seq peaks (e.g., HPeak-called STAT1 peaks) and matched control sequences for transcription factor binding motifs using MatInspector against Genomatix MatBase 7.0, then quantify per-family enrichment with chi-square statistics to validate peak-calling quality. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Scan genomic sequences underlying ChIP-Seq peaks (e.g., HPeak-called STAT1 peaks) and matched control sequences for transcription factor binding motifs using MatInspector against Genomatix MatBase 7.0, then quantify per-family enrichment with chi-square statistics to validate peak-calling quality.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The binding motif of interest is novel or not represented in motif databases — the article notes many stored motif patterns may be inaccurate and novel motifs may not exist in databases You have peak intervals but no matched control sequences, so no test-vs-control chi-square enrichment can be computed You need de novo motif discovery rather than scanning against known curated matrices

skills.description: Use when analyzing time-series gene expression profiles (e.g., RNA-seq across a biological process such as liver regeneration) to identify which TFs and pathways are activated or repressed at specific time points.
skills.name: transcription-factor-pathway-interaction-analysis
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-pathway-interaction-analysis Use when analyzing time-series gene expression profiles (e.g., RNA-seq across a biological process such as liver regeneration) to identify which TFs and pathways are activated or repressed at specific time points. Input is not a time-series expression profile — clustering methods or static network inference are more appropriate when temporal dynamics are not of interest TF–TG interaction data or pathway gene-set annotations for the organism of interest are unavailable, since TSMiner requires all three input file types The goal is a static gene co-expression module detection rather than time-specific TF–pathway regulatory events http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0602 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Construct time-specific TF–pathway regulatory networks from time-series expression data using TSMiner, which integrates a time-series expression matrix, TF–TG interaction information, and GO/KEGG/Reactome pathway gene sets to identify transcriptional activators and repressors at each time point. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Construct time-specific TF–pathway regulatory networks from time-series expression data using TSMiner, which integrates a time-series expression matrix, TF–TG interaction information, and GO/KEGG/Reactome pathway gene sets to identify transcriptional activators and repressors at each time point.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is not a time-series expression profile — clustering methods or static network inference are more appropriate when temporal dynamics are not of interest TF–TG interaction data or pathway gene-set annotations for the organism of interest are unavailable, since TSMiner requires all three input file types The goal is a static gene co-expression module detection rather than time-specific TF–pathway regulatory events

skills.description: Use when ChIP-seq FASTQ data for a DNA-binding factor (e.g., LuxR or H-NS in V. harveyi) needs trimming, reference alignment, and macs2 peak calling to count and compare binding peaks across conditions.
skills.name: transcription-factor-peak-calling
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-peak-calling Use when ChIP-seq FASTQ data for a DNA-binding factor (e.g., LuxR or H-NS in V. harveyi) needs trimming, reference alignment, and macs2 peak calling to count and compare binding peaks across conditions. Input is RNA-seq differential expression data rather than ChIP-seq immunoprecipitation reads (use the RNA-seq analysis path; the paper deposited RNA-seq separately under GSE136191) The question is promoter co-occupancy or overlap analysis of already-called peak sets rather than peak calling itself — use findOverlaps.pl / findClosest2.pl on existing macs2 peak files instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 End-to-end ChIP-seq transcription factor binding analysis: trim ChIP-seq FASTQ reads, align them to the V. harveyi ATCC BAA-1116 reference genome with bwa, and call transcription factor binding peaks with macs2 to quantify LuxR and H-NS occupancy under wild-type and mutant conditions. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkz1089
skills.summary: End-to-end ChIP-seq transcription factor binding analysis: trim ChIP-seq FASTQ reads, align them to the V. harveyi ATCC BAA-1116 reference genome with bwa, and call transcription factor binding peaks with macs2 to quantify LuxR and H-NS occupancy under wild-type and mutant conditions.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is RNA-seq differential expression data rather than ChIP-seq immunoprecipitation reads (use the RNA-seq analysis path; the paper deposited RNA-seq separately under GSE136191) The question is promoter co-occupancy or overlap analysis of already-called peak sets rather than peak calling itself — use findOverlaps.pl / findClosest2.pl on existing macs2 peak files instead

skills.description: Use when comparing TR-identification tools on query region sets where the true perturbed/active TR is known, and a rank-based metric (MRR) over ranked TR output is needed for fair method comparison.
skills.name: transcription-factor-rank-benchmarking
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-rank-benchmarking Use when comparing TR-identification tools on query region sets where the true perturbed/active TR is known, and a rank-based metric (MRR) over ranked TR output is needed for fair method comparison. No ground-truth perturbed TR is known for the query region set, so a reciprocal rank cannot be computed. Input is raw sequencing data rather than processed peak/region sets — peak calling (e.g., MACS2 q-value 0.01) must precede this benchmarking step. Only one method is being run; MRR is a cross-method comparison metric and is uninformative without competing ranked outputs. http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Benchmark TR-identification methods by computing mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of known perturbed TRs across methods' ranked TR output lists, as done to show BIT outperforms BART, ChIP-Atlas, i-cisTarget, WhichTF, and HOMER on five bulk perturbation DAR datasets (Fig. 3f). epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Benchmark TR-identification methods by computing mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of known perturbed TRs across methods' ranked TR output lists, as done to show BIT outperforms BART, ChIP-Atlas, i-cisTarget, WhichTF, and HOMER on five bulk perturbation DAR datasets (Fig. 3f).
skills.when_to_use_negative: No ground-truth perturbed TR is known for the query region set, so a reciprocal rank cannot be computed. Input is raw sequencing data rather than processed peak/region sets — peak calling (e.g., MACS2 q-value 0.01) must precede this benchmarking step. Only one method is being run; MRR is a cross-method comparison metric and is uninformative without competing ranked outputs.

skills.description: Use when you have a TF ChIP-seq peak file (e.g. an ENCODE BED file) and need the set of unique genes whose associated REMs overlap the TF's binding regions.
skills.name: transcription-factor-target-gene-identification
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-target-gene-identification Use when you have a TF ChIP-seq peak file (e.g. an ENCODE BED file) and need the set of unique genes whose associated REMs overlap the TF's binding regions. The input is a list of genes of interest rather than genomic regions — use EpiRegio's Gene Query instead of the Region Query The goal is de novo identification of enriched TF motifs within a set of regions — use a motif enrichment tool such as PASTAA, Clover, MotifCounter, or Homer instead The input peaks are not in a coordinate format (BED) that the Region Query can compare against REMs by overlap percentage http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_3656 Identifies the target genes of a transcription factor by querying ChIP-seq peak regions (BED) against EpiRegio's database of regulatory elements (REMs) using the Region Query, retrieving REM–gene associations filtered by an overlap-percentage criterion. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa382
skills.summary: Identifies the target genes of a transcription factor by querying ChIP-seq peak regions (BED) against EpiRegio's database of regulatory elements (REMs) using the Region Query, retrieving REM–gene associations filtered by an overlap-percentage criterion.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is a list of genes of interest rather than genomic regions — use EpiRegio's Gene Query instead of the Region Query The goal is de novo identification of enriched TF motifs within a set of regions — use a motif enrichment tool such as PASTAA, Clover, MotifCounter, or Homer instead The input peaks are not in a coordinate format (BED) that the Region Query can compare against REMs by overlap percentage

skills.description: Use when the goal is to identify candidate transcription factor targets by correlating gene expression across many diverse GEO experiments, given a mean-centered COnTORT output file with GenBank annotation columns.
skills.name: transcription-factor-target-identification
skills.search_text: transcription-factor-target-identification Use when the goal is to identify candidate transcription factor targets by correlating gene expression across many diverse GEO experiments, given a mean-centered COnTORT output file with GenBank annotation columns. The expression matrix has not been mean-centered per experiment (use the non-mean-centered COnTORT output for other purposes; raw cross-experiment correlation would be confounded by experiment-level differences) The data are not normalized, processed GEO series data — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO Genes of interest lack matches in the provided GenBank file, since COnTORT retains only matches to gene annotations present in the GenBank file (missing annotations are listed as 'N/A') http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 Rank co-expressed gene pairs by computing pairwise Pearson correlations across the experimentally mean-centered COnTORT transcriptomic matrix (COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt) to surface candidate targets of bacterial transcription factors. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Rank co-expressed gene pairs by computing pairwise Pearson correlations across the experimentally mean-centered COnTORT transcriptomic matrix (COnTORT_organized_transcriptomic_data.txt) to surface candidate targets of bacterial transcription factors.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression matrix has not been mean-centered per experiment (use the non-mean-centered COnTORT output for other purposes; raw cross-experiment correlation would be confounded by experiment-level differences) The data are not normalized, processed GEO series data — COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO Genes of interest lack matches in the provided GenBank file, since COnTORT retains only matches to gene annotations present in the GenBank file (missing annotations are listed as 'N/A')

skills.description: Use when benchmarking 100,000-bp DNA sequence models on nucleotide-wise signal-intensity regression for transcription initiation, or when verifying that DNA foundation models underperform a task-specific expert model on TISP.
skills.name: transcription-initiation-signal-regression
skills.search_text: transcription-initiation-signal-regression Use when benchmarking 100,000-bp DNA sequence models on nucleotide-wise signal-intensity regression for transcription initiation, or when verifying that DNA foundation models underperform a task-specific expert model on TISP. The task is binary or short-range classification (e.g. GenomicBenchmarks-style tasks) rather than base-pair-resolution regression of long-range signal intensities. You only need qualitative model rankings without reproducing the PCC benchmark table — the DNALONGBENCH paper's published averages (Puffin 0.733 vs. CNN 0.042) may suffice as reference values. Transformer-based DNA foundation models with quadratic self-attention (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) are the models of interest — the paper excludes them because the quadratic cost makes 100k-bp+ tasks infeasible. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Reproduce the DNALONGBENCH transcription initiation signal prediction (TISP) nucleotide-wise regression benchmark, comparing the expert Puffin model against a CNN baseline and three fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) using per-assay Pearson correlation on held-out test chromosomes. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65077-4
skills.summary: Reproduce the DNALONGBENCH transcription initiation signal prediction (TISP) nucleotide-wise regression benchmark, comparing the expert Puffin model against a CNN baseline and three fine-tuned DNA foundation models (HyenaDNA, Caduceus-Ph, Caduceus-PS) using per-assay Pearson correlation on held-out test chromosomes.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is binary or short-range classification (e.g. GenomicBenchmarks-style tasks) rather than base-pair-resolution regression of long-range signal intensities. You only need qualitative model rankings without reproducing the PCC benchmark table — the DNALONGBENCH paper's published averages (Puffin 0.733 vs. CNN 0.042) may suffice as reference values. Transformer-based DNA foundation models with quadratic self-attention (DNABERT-1, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer) are the models of interest — the paper excludes them because the quadratic cost makes 100k-bp+ tasks infeasible.

skills.description: Use when you have a processed peak/DAR region set (BED with chromosome coordinates, e.g., from DiffBind or MACS2) and need to identify and rank candidate transcriptional regulators with uncertainty estimates.
skills.name: transcriptional-regulator-ranking-from-bit-scores
skills.search_text: transcriptional-regulator-ranking-from-bit-scores Use when you have a processed peak/DAR region set (BED with chromosome coordinates, e.g., from DiffBind or MACS2) and need to identify and rank candidate transcriptional regulators with uncertainty estimates. Input is a gene set rather than an epigenomic region set — BART's geneset mode or motif-based tools like WhichTF/HOMER are alternatives, but BIT specifically requires region coordinates You need frequentist enrichment p-values (e.g., Fisher exact test rankings as in ChIP-Atlas) rather than Bayesian posterior scores with credible intervals The region set comes from a genome build not supported by the pre-compiled reference libraries (hg38 or mm10) http://edamontology.org/topic_3179 http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Runs the BIT R package on a user-provided epigenomic region set (e.g., an mm10 RUNX1 KO differentially accessible region BED file) to produce a ranked table of transcriptional regulators based on posterior-derived BIT scores from a Bayesian hierarchical model sampled via Gibbs-sampler MCMC. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-60269-4
skills.summary: Runs the BIT R package on a user-provided epigenomic region set (e.g., an mm10 RUNX1 KO differentially accessible region BED file) to produce a ranked table of transcriptional regulators based on posterior-derived BIT scores from a Bayesian hierarchical model sampled via Gibbs-sampler MCMC.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is a gene set rather than an epigenomic region set — BART's geneset mode or motif-based tools like WhichTF/HOMER are alternatives, but BIT specifically requires region coordinates You need frequentist enrichment p-values (e.g., Fisher exact test rankings as in ChIP-Atlas) rather than Bayesian posterior scores with credible intervals The region set comes from a genome build not supported by the pre-compiled reference libraries (hg38 or mm10)

skills.description: Use when strand-annotated motifs (BED files with '+'/'-' strands) must be tested for same-vs-opposite orientation bias relative to template/non-template direction of strand-annotated regions such as GENCODE protein-coding genes.
skills.name: transcriptional-strand-asymmetry-estimation
skills.search_text: transcriptional-strand-asymmetry-estimation Use when strand-annotated motifs (BED files with '+'/'-' strands) must be tested for same-vs-opposite orientation bias relative to template/non-template direction of strand-annotated regions such as GENCODE protein-coding genes. Motifs are palindromic (e.g. some restriction-site-like sequences) so a '+'/'-' strand orientation cannot be meaningfully assigned The question is replicative rather than transcriptional asymmetry, or the features are unassigned and must first be oriented relative to overlapping elements via Asymmetron's orientation function Genic region overlap counts alone cannot disentangle motif orientation from element-class background strand preference and no background correction data is available http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 Estimates transcriptional strand asymmetry of strand-annotated motifs (e.g. Alu/SINE repeats from UCSC hg38 rmsk, PolyASite PAS clusters) within strand-annotated genic regions (GENCODE v33 protein-coding genes) using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries interval-overlap function, a two-tailed binomial test against p=0.5, and Bonferroni correction. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Estimates transcriptional strand asymmetry of strand-annotated motifs (e.g. Alu/SINE repeats from UCSC hg38 rmsk, PolyASite PAS clusters) within strand-annotated genic regions (GENCODE v33 protein-coding genes) using Asymmetron's contained_asymmetries interval-overlap function, a two-tailed binomial test against p=0.5, and Bonferroni correction.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Motifs are palindromic (e.g. some restriction-site-like sequences) so a '+'/'-' strand orientation cannot be meaningfully assigned The question is replicative rather than transcriptional asymmetry, or the features are unassigned and must first be oriented relative to overlapping elements via Asymmetron's orientation function Genic region overlap counts alone cannot disentangle motif orientation from element-class background strand preference and no background correction data is available

skills.description: Use when building a cross-experiment gene expression compendium where per-experiment (per-GSM) offsets must be removed before downstream correlation or statistical analysis, following COnTORT's mean-centering-per-experiment output format.
skills.name: transcriptomic-matrix-tab-delimited-formatting
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-matrix-tab-delimited-formatting Use when building a cross-experiment gene expression compendium where per-experiment (per-GSM) offsets must be removed before downstream correlation or statistical analysis, following COnTORT's mean-centering-per-experiment output format. The analysis requires the non-mean-centered output file (COnTORT also produces a second file with no mean centering) — do not apply centering when raw organized expression values are the target. Input data are raw/unprocessed reads rather than normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO; COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed GEO data. Only a single experiment/sample is present — per-experiment mean-centering would reduce every column to zero and provide no cross-experiment normalization benefit. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Reconstruct COnTORT's mean-centered output file: organize GEO expression data annotated from a GenBank (.gbff) file, subtract each experiment's (GSM column's) mean from every value, and write a tab-delimited text file with the five annotation columns intact so experiments are comparable across a compendium. epigenomics/v2 10.1128/mra.00587-20
skills.summary: Reconstruct COnTORT's mean-centered output file: organize GEO expression data annotated from a GenBank (.gbff) file, subtract each experiment's (GSM column's) mean from every value, and write a tab-delimited text file with the five annotation columns intact so experiments are comparable across a compendium.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The analysis requires the non-mean-centered output file (COnTORT also produces a second file with no mean centering) — do not apply centering when raw organized expression values are the target. Input data are raw/unprocessed reads rather than normalized and processed data imported into NCBI GEO; COnTORT can only download and combine normalized and processed GEO data. Only a single experiment/sample is present — per-experiment mean-centering would reduce every column to zero and provide no cross-experiment normalization benefit.

skills.description: Use when a newly developed unsupervised clustering method for tumor gene expression data must be benchmarked against an established method (e.g., consensus clustering) by quantifying solution concordance per number of clusters K.
skills.name: transcriptomic-subtype-benchmarking
skills.search_text: transcriptomic-subtype-benchmarking Use when a newly developed unsupervised clustering method for tumor gene expression data must be benchmarked against an established method (e.g., consensus clustering) by quantifying solution concordance per number of clusters K. The clustering solutions being compared are not defined over the same sample set — Jaccard on pairwise co-clustering matrices requires identical sample indices across methods You need an absolute quality assessment of a single clustering solution rather than a relative comparison between two methods on the same cohort The dataset is too small to support resampling-based consensus clustering (2000 iterations at 70% item/feature resampling) http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_3518 Benchmarks a novel unsupervised transcriptomic clustering method (SRIQ) against a consensus clustering baseline on the same gene expression cohort by comparing cluster solutions with a Jaccard-based Pair Similarity score across K values (here K=3–7 on 434 TCGA-LUAD cases). epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2022.03.036
skills.summary: Benchmarks a novel unsupervised transcriptomic clustering method (SRIQ) against a consensus clustering baseline on the same gene expression cohort by comparing cluster solutions with a Jaccard-based Pair Similarity score across K values (here K=3–7 on 434 TCGA-LUAD cases).
skills.when_to_use_negative: The clustering solutions being compared are not defined over the same sample set — Jaccard on pairwise co-clustering matrices requires identical sample indices across methods You need an absolute quality assessment of a single clustering solution rather than a relative comparison between two methods on the same cohort The dataset is too small to support resampling-based consensus clustering (2000 iterations at 70% item/feature resampling)

skills.description: Use when a trained multi-input deep learning model must be adapted to a new cell line with limited or divergent enhancer data, and the goal is to quantify which transfer strategy (transfer_1/2/3) counters enhancer specificity.
skills.name: transfer-learning-fine-tuning
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-fine-tuning Use when a trained multi-input deep learning model must be adapted to a new cell line with limited or divergent enhancer data, and the goal is to quantify which transfer strategy (transfer_1/2/3) counters enhancer specificity. The target cell line already has abundant labeled training data and the standard per-cell-line Enhancer-MDLF training path ('python main.py --cell_line ...') suffices Input is raw enhancer sequences without labels or without extracted features — feature extraction (dna2vec_code.py, motif_find.py) must be run first The task is generic enhancer (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L data) or enhancer-promoter identification rather than cross-cell line transfer http://edamontology.org/topic_0092 http://edamontology.org/topic_3307 Fine-tunes the pre-trained Enhancer-MDLF models (trained on all eight cell lines) on a target cell line to mitigate cross-cell line enhancer prediction challenges caused by enhancer specificity, comparing transfer_1, transfer_2, and transfer_3 strategies against random-weight retraining. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bib/bbae083
skills.summary: Fine-tunes the pre-trained Enhancer-MDLF models (trained on all eight cell lines) on a target cell line to mitigate cross-cell line enhancer prediction challenges caused by enhancer specificity, comparing transfer_1, transfer_2, and transfer_3 strategies against random-weight retraining.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The target cell line already has abundant labeled training data and the standard per-cell-line Enhancer-MDLF training path ('python main.py --cell_line ...') suffices Input is raw enhancer sequences without labels or without extracted features — feature extraction (dna2vec_code.py, motif_find.py) must be run first The task is generic enhancer (Liu et al. iEnhancer-2L data) or enhancer-promoter identification rather than cross-cell line transfer

skills.description: Use when you have Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. HiC-Pro output from GM12878 GSE63525 or downsampled valid-contact subsets) and need a sequence-based chromatin model retrained on that depth, starting from the chromatin-feature-seeded base model.
skills.name: transfer-learning-model-retraining
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-model-retraining Use when you have Hi-C contact matrices (e.g. HiC-Pro output from GM12878 GSE63525 or downsampled valid-contact subsets) and need a sequence-based chromatin model retrained on that depth, starting from the chromatin-feature-seeded base model. You only need a Hi-C model for deeply sequenced tissue data already covered by the published pre-trained deepC models — retraining is for new depths or new tissue-specific Hi-C training sets You want a direct deepC-vs-Akita benchmark — the authors explicitly defer comparative consolidation between these models to future work and provide no such benchmark Your Hi-C data has extremely low depth (on the order of the 10M-contact subset), where the model demonstrably fails to learn chromatin structure http://edamontology.org/topic_3678 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Retrain deepC 5 kb-resolution chromatin-interaction models on user-supplied Hi-C data (e.g. downsampled GM12878 contact matrices) by initializing from the pre-trained chromatin-feature-seeded base model in the deepC repository, then evaluate predictions against holdout chromosomes with Pearson correlation. This tests how low sequencing depth can go before sequence-based structure prediction fails. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Retrain deepC 5 kb-resolution chromatin-interaction models on user-supplied Hi-C data (e.g. downsampled GM12878 contact matrices) by initializing from the pre-trained chromatin-feature-seeded base model in the deepC repository, then evaluate predictions against holdout chromosomes with Pearson correlation. This tests how low sequencing depth can go before sequence-based structure prediction fails.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need a Hi-C model for deeply sequenced tissue data already covered by the published pre-trained deepC models — retraining is for new depths or new tissue-specific Hi-C training sets You want a direct deepC-vs-Akita benchmark — the authors explicitly defer comparative consolidation between these models to future work and provide no such benchmark Your Hi-C data has extremely low depth (on the order of the 10M-contact subset), where the model demonstrably fails to learn chromatin structure

skills.description: Use when training a sequence-based deep learning model on scarce, low-depth Hi-C targets and pre-trained chromatin feature weights are available to seed hidden layers before fine-tuning on interaction prediction.
skills.name: transfer-learning-weight-seeding
skills.search_text: transfer-learning-weight-seeding Use when training a sequence-based deep learning model on scarce, low-depth Hi-C targets and pre-trained chromatin feature weights are available to seed hidden layers before fine-tuning on interaction prediction. You need to train the chromatin feature predictor itself from labels — this skill covers the second-phase interaction training, not DeepSEA-style feature pre-training You lack the pre-seeded chromatin feature weights; deepC models yield substantially better predictions when pre-seeded, and training from scratch forfeits this advantage Your TensorFlow version is outside the tested set (v1.8, 1.14, 2.1) with no matching deepC compatibility branch http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Two-phase transfer learning in which deepC's convolutional module is initialized with weights pre-trained to predict ~936 ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin features, then fine-tuned alongside from-scratch dilated gated conv layers to predict Hi-C chromatin interactions from megabase-scale DNA sequence. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Two-phase transfer learning in which deepC's convolutional module is initialized with weights pre-trained to predict ~936 ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin features, then fine-tuned alongside from-scratch dilated gated conv layers to predict Hi-C chromatin interactions from megabase-scale DNA sequence.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need to train the chromatin feature predictor itself from labels — this skill covers the second-phase interaction training, not DeepSEA-style feature pre-training You lack the pre-seeded chromatin feature weights; deepC models yield substantially better predictions when pre-seeded, and training from scratch forfeits this advantage Your TensorFlow version is outside the tested set (v1.8, 1.14, 2.1) with no matching deepC compatibility branch

skills.description: Use when benchmarking a sequence-based classifier against pretrained DNA transformers on the same CRE train/test partitions, e.g. comparing BOM or k-mer SVMs to DNABERT/Enformer on mouse mm10 E8.25 distal regulatory elements.
skills.name: transformer-fine-tuning-genomic-sequences
skills.search_text: transformer-fine-tuning-genomic-sequences Use when benchmarking a sequence-based classifier against pretrained DNA transformers on the same CRE train/test partitions, e.g. comparing BOM or k-mer SVMs to DNABERT/Enformer on mouse mm10 E8.25 distal regulatory elements. When unordered motif counts are sufficient: BOM outperformed DNABERT and Enformer by 55.1% and 10.3% auPR (211.9% and 33.4% MCC) on this task, so transformers may add cost without benefit for this data scale When training data per cell state is small — the article notes performance of sequence-based deep learning methods is likely linked to the limited amount of data available for many cell states When the input is already a motif count/feature table rather than raw DNA sequence Fine-tunes pretrained genomic transformers (DNABERT with 6-mer tokenization and Enformer with an adaptive two-layer head) as deep-learning baselines for binary cell-type-specific distal CRE classification on mouse E8.25 data. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-025-65362-2
skills.summary: Fine-tunes pretrained genomic transformers (DNABERT with 6-mer tokenization and Enformer with an adaptive two-layer head) as deep-learning baselines for binary cell-type-specific distal CRE classification on mouse E8.25 data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When unordered motif counts are sufficient: BOM outperformed DNABERT and Enformer by 55.1% and 10.3% auPR (211.9% and 33.4% MCC) on this task, so transformers may add cost without benefit for this data scale When training data per cell state is small — the article notes performance of sequence-based deep learning methods is likely linked to the limited amount of data available for many cell states When the input is already a motif count/feature table rather than raw DNA sequence

skills.description: Use when raw ONT FAST5 files (e.g. SRR15058166, R9.4.1 FLO-PRO002/SQK-LSK109) must be converted into per-position translocation-time signals for downstream non-B DNA structure modelling.
skills.name: translocation-time-computation-from-current-events
skills.search_text: translocation-time-computation-from-current-events Use when raw ONT FAST5 files (e.g. SRR15058166, R9.4.1 FLO-PRO002/SQK-LSK109) must be converted into per-position translocation-time signals for downstream non-B DNA structure modelling. Input is already basecalled FASTQ or a fixed-stride Albacore event table without per-base segmentation — Albacore alone assumes the block stride attribute remains fixed and cannot yield per-base translocation times. The goal is direct non-B motif annotation from sequence only, not translocation-time signal extraction (use the non-B DNA DB motif workflow instead). http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3168 Computes per-base DNA translocation times (seconds) from Oxford Nanopore raw FAST5 current signals by basecalling with Albacore, re-squiggling with Tombo to obtain base-level event measurements, and dividing each event's measurement count by the ONT sampling rate. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Computes per-base DNA translocation times (seconds) from Oxford Nanopore raw FAST5 current signals by basecalling with Albacore, re-squiggling with Tombo to obtain base-level event measurements, and dividing each event's measurement count by the ONT sampling rate.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is already basecalled FASTQ or a fixed-stride Albacore event table without per-base segmentation — Albacore alone assumes the block stride attribute remains fixed and cannot yield per-base translocation times. The goal is direct non-B motif annotation from sequence only, not translocation-time signal extraction (use the non-B DNA DB motif workflow instead).

skills.description: Use when nanopore (ONT) per-base translocation-time data and non-B DNA DB motif annotations (e.g. hg38) are available and the goal is to test whether 100 bp non-B motif windows deviate in TT quantiles from motif-free B-DNA controls, as in Fig. 4.
skills.name: translocation-time-quantile-analysis
skills.search_text: translocation-time-quantile-analysis Use when nanopore (ONT) per-base translocation-time data and non-B DNA DB motif annotations (e.g. hg38) are available and the goal is to test whether 100 bp non-B motif windows deviate in TT quantiles from motif-free B-DNA controls, as in Fig. 4. The data are simulated translocation times rather than the experimental dataset — the paper's separate simulated pipeline (simulator.py + GoFAE-DND) is the intended path for simulated windows. The goal is non-B structure prediction/classification via GoFAE-DND or novelty detectors (isolation forest, LOF, one-class SVM) rather than descriptive quantile-deviation analysis of windows. Only raw FAST5 current signal is available and per-base translocation times have not yet been computed via Albacore basecalling and Tombo re-squiggle. http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Reproduces the Fig. 4 analysis of the ONT non-B DNA paper by computing the 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 0.95 quantiles of per-base translocation times (Tombo re-squiggle events converted to seconds) within 100 bp windows centred on non-B DNA motifs and comparing them against B-DNA control windows to quantify and rank deviations by non-B structure class. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad220
skills.summary: Reproduces the Fig. 4 analysis of the ONT non-B DNA paper by computing the 0.05, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, and 0.95 quantiles of per-base translocation times (Tombo re-squiggle events converted to seconds) within 100 bp windows centred on non-B DNA motifs and comparing them against B-DNA control windows to quantify and rank deviations by non-B structure class.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The data are simulated translocation times rather than the experimental dataset — the paper's separate simulated pipeline (simulator.py + GoFAE-DND) is the intended path for simulated windows. The goal is non-B structure prediction/classification via GoFAE-DND or novelty detectors (isolation forest, LOF, one-class SVM) rather than descriptive quantile-deviation analysis of windows. Only raw FAST5 current signal is available and per-base translocation times have not yet been computed via Albacore basecalling and Tombo re-squiggle.

Input is already a trained model or prediction score file — use the independent testing script (csDMA_indepedent_testing.py) instead of retraining The goal is evaluation only (e.g., LeaveOneOut scoring) — use leaveoneout.py rather than re-running classifier selection The feature matrix is not yet encoded from raw sequences — run the feature encoding scheme (feature_selection.py) first http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Train and compare tree-ensemble classifiers (Random Forest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees) on encoded sequence feature matrices to select the best-performing model, as done in csDMA where ExtraTrees achieved the best AUC of 0.878 by 5-fold cross-validation and was used to train the final model. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-49430-4
skills.summary: Train and compare tree-ensemble classifiers (Random Forest, GradientBoosting, AdaBoost, ExtraTrees) on encoded sequence feature matrices to select the best-performing model, as done in csDMA where ExtraTrees achieved the best AUC of 0.878 by 5-fold cross-validation and was used to train the final model.
