skills.description: Use when calibrating or benchmarking triplex (TPX) prediction parameters: multiple RNA:DNA interaction peak sets and RNA sequences are available and you need to determine which minimal TPX length, masking cut-off or scoring option maximises AUC against shuffled genomic negatives.
skills.name: triplex-prediction-parameter-sweep
skills.search_text: triplex-prediction-parameter-sweep Use when calibrating or benchmarking triplex (TPX) prediction parameters: multiple RNA:DNA interaction peak sets and RNA sequences are available and you need to determine which minimal TPX length, masking cut-off or scoring option maximises AUC against shuffled genomic negatives. You need whole-transcript triplex potential classification without parameter tuning — TriplexFPP gives triplex lncRNA/DNA-site predictions directly from FASTA, though it failed to identify known TPX-forming lncRNAs (CDKN2B-AS1, lncSmad7, MEG3, NEAT1, TERC) in this paper's comparison Input is a single fixed run where 3plex defaults (minimal length 10, error rate 20%, guanine rate 40%) are already accepted and no AUC comparison across settings is required The binding data lack replicates or multiple peak sets, so the peak-filtering factor of the sweep cannot be varied and only the default method is testable http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 A systematic evaluation workflow that sweeps 3plex parameter combinations (minimal TPX length, error rate, guanine rate, consecutive errors, ssRNA masking, repeat filter) against experimental lncRNA binding-site positives versus matched genomic negatives, scoring each configuration by ROC/AUC and testing parameter effects with linear models, ANOVA and permutation tests. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: A systematic evaluation workflow that sweeps 3plex parameter combinations (minimal TPX length, error rate, guanine rate, consecutive errors, ssRNA masking, repeat filter) against experimental lncRNA binding-site positives versus matched genomic negatives, scoring each configuration by ROC/AUC and testing parameter effects with linear models, ANOVA and permutation tests.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You need whole-transcript triplex potential classification without parameter tuning — TriplexFPP gives triplex lncRNA/DNA-site predictions directly from FASTA, though it failed to identify known TPX-forming lncRNAs (CDKN2B-AS1, lncSmad7, MEG3, NEAT1, TERC) in this paper's comparison Input is a single fixed run where 3plex defaults (minimal length 10, error rate 20%, guanine rate 40%) are already accepted and no AUC comparison across settings is required The binding data lack replicates or multiple peak sets, so the peak-filtering factor of the sweep cannot be varied and only the default method is testable

skills.description: Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. stability-based vs match-count) on lncRNA peak sets with ROC/AUC, to decide whether biophysical scoring improves prediction over raw match counts.
skills.name: triplex-scoring-method-evaluation
skills.search_text: triplex-scoring-method-evaluation Use when comparing TPX prediction scoring functions (e.g. stability-based vs match-count) on lncRNA peak sets with ROC/AUC, to decide whether biophysical scoring improves prediction over raw match counts. When the goal is simply predicting TPXs with a single default scoring scheme rather than comparing scoring strategies head-to-head When no experimentally validated positive regions (e.g. RADICL-seq peaks) are available to construct a positive/negative benchmark http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3511 Benchmarks triplex (TPX) scoring strategies — thermal stability-derived measures such as the Normalised stability score against the match-count-based Triplexator potential — by computing per-lncRNA ROC/AUC over positive and matched negative regions. Grounded in the 3plex paper's finding that stability-derived scoring slightly outperforms simple match counts. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Benchmarks triplex (TPX) scoring strategies — thermal stability-derived measures such as the Normalised stability score against the match-count-based Triplexator potential — by computing per-lncRNA ROC/AUC over positive and matched negative regions. Grounded in the 3plex paper's finding that stability-derived scoring slightly outperforms simple match counts.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the goal is simply predicting TPXs with a single default scoring scheme rather than comparing scoring strategies head-to-head When no experimentally validated positive regions (e.g. RADICL-seq peaks) are available to construct a positive/negative benchmark

skills.description: Use when predicting ssRNA:dsDNA triple-helix interactions and you need to rank TFO:TTS matches by in vitro thermal stability instead of raw match counts, e.g. within a 3plex/Triplexator-style pipeline.
skills.name: triplex-thermal-stability-scoring
skills.search_text: triplex-thermal-stability-scoring Use when predicting ssRNA:dsDNA triple-helix interactions and you need to rank TFO:TTS matches by in vitro thermal stability instead of raw match counts, e.g. within a 3plex/Triplexator-style pipeline. You only need triplex presence/absence or lncRNA classification by deep learning — TriplexFPP (CNN on experimental TPX features) is a different approach, and the paper found no good agreement between 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions You require protein-mediated RNA:DNA interactions — this skill addresses only non-protein-mediated (NPM) triplex formation such as measured by RADICL-seq http://edamontology.org/topic_0099 http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 Scores predicted RNA:DNA triplexes (TPXs) using experimentally determined triplet thermal stability data from the LongTarget collection of triplex denaturation experiments (He et al., 2015), replacing simple match counts with a stability-derived score. The 3plex paper reports better prediction performance using stability-derived measures than match-count scoring. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2023.05.016
skills.summary: Scores predicted RNA:DNA triplexes (TPXs) using experimentally determined triplet thermal stability data from the LongTarget collection of triplex denaturation experiments (He et al., 2015), replacing simple match counts with a stability-derived score. The 3plex paper reports better prediction performance using stability-derived measures than match-count scoring.
skills.when_to_use_negative: You only need triplex presence/absence or lncRNA classification by deep learning — TriplexFPP (CNN on experimental TPX features) is a different approach, and the paper found no good agreement between 3plex and TriplexFPP predictions You require protein-mediated RNA:DNA interactions — this skill addresses only non-protein-mediated (NPM) triplex formation such as measured by RADICL-seq

skills.description: Use when Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows tables exist for matched WT and mutant eCLIP replicates and the goal is to quantify and statistically test binding shifts toward annotated tRNA (or other repeat/ncRNA) loci.
skills.name: trna-binding-enrichment-testing
skills.search_text: trna-binding-enrichment-testing Use when Skipper reproducible_enriched_windows tables exist for matched WT and mutant eCLIP replicates and the goal is to quantify and statistically test binding shifts toward annotated tRNA (or other repeat/ncRNA) loci. CLIP datasets lack matched input samples, since Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and thus no reproducible enriched windows exist to intersect with tRNA loci The question is which transcript regions (CDS vs introns vs UTRs) windows fall in rather than testing enrichment at tRNA loci specifically — use a feature-proportion aggregation (figure7e-style) instead Only single replicates per condition are available, so a paired t-test across matched replicate pairs is not statistically valid http://edamontology.org/topic_0659 http://edamontology.org/topic_3524 Tests whether an RBP eCLIP experiment shows significant enrichment of reproducible Skipper binding windows over annotated tRNA loci, and compares tRNA enrichment between matched wild-type and mutant replicate pairs with paired t-tests. Used to detect mutant-induced retargeting (e.g., RPS19 R62W/R101H) toward non-coding RNAs. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Tests whether an RBP eCLIP experiment shows significant enrichment of reproducible Skipper binding windows over annotated tRNA loci, and compares tRNA enrichment between matched wild-type and mutant replicate pairs with paired t-tests. Used to detect mutant-induced retargeting (e.g., RPS19 R62W/R101H) toward non-coding RNAs.
skills.when_to_use_negative: CLIP datasets lack matched input samples, since Skipper cannot construct its beta-binomial model and thus no reproducible enriched windows exist to intersect with tRNA loci The question is which transcript regions (CDS vs introns vs UTRs) windows fall in rather than testing enrichment at tRNA loci specifically — use a feature-proportion aggregation (figure7e-style) instead Only single replicates per condition are available, so a paired t-test across matched replicate pairs is not statistically valid

skills.search_text: tsa-seq-enrichment-quantification Use when a Hi-C-derived sub-compartment inference (A1/B1/B3) needs quantitative validation against independent nuclear-body or lamina enrichment data such as SON TSA-seq, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq, or H3K27me3 ChIP-seq. The input is not Hi-C-derived sub-compartment assignments — e.g. the goal is de novo inference of sub-compartments rather than benchmarking existing probabilities against enrichment tracks The genome assembly lacks an hg19 mapping path or the enrichment tracks are unavailable for the target genome, since correlations are computed genome-wide on hg19 Only a normalized bedgraph visualization is needed and no probability scores or benchmarking are required http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Quantifies sub-compartment assignments against independent TSA-seq/cTSA-seq protein-DNA interaction enrichment tracks (SON TSA-seq for A1, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq for B3, plus H3K27me3 ChIP-seq for B1) by computing genome-wide correlation coefficients, using CscoreTool-M compartment probabilities as the method under test. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad314
skills.summary: Quantifies sub-compartment assignments against independent TSA-seq/cTSA-seq protein-DNA interaction enrichment tracks (SON TSA-seq for A1, lamin-B1 cTSA-seq for B3, plus H3K27me3 ChIP-seq for B1) by computing genome-wide correlation coefficients, using CscoreTool-M compartment probabilities as the method under test.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The input is not Hi-C-derived sub-compartment assignments — e.g. the goal is de novo inference of sub-compartments rather than benchmarking existing probabilities against enrichment tracks The genome assembly lacks an hg19 mapping path or the enrichment tracks are unavailable for the target genome, since correlations are computed genome-wide on hg19 Only a normalized bedgraph visualization is needed and no probability scores or benchmarking are required

skills.description: Use when a motif enrichment analysis requires positional interpretation, i.e. you have assay-derived anchor coordinates (TSSs or cleavage sites) and want motif enrichment profiled at offsets around that anchor rather than presence/absence per sequence.
skills.name: tss-and-cleavage-site-coordinate-anchoring
skills.search_text: tss-and-cleavage-site-coordinate-anchoring Use when a motif enrichment analysis requires positional interpretation, i.e. you have assay-derived anchor coordinates (TSSs or cleavage sites) and want motif enrichment profiled at offsets around that anchor rather than presence/absence per sequence. Sequences are genomic windows not anchored at a TSS or cleavage site, so positional offsets would be biologically meaningless The question is simple motif presence/absence enrichment under a zero-or-one-occurrence-per-sequence (ZOOPs) model, where position is irrelevant (e.g. standard HOMER-style MEA) De novo motif discovery is needed, since MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library http://edamontology.org/topic_0749 Anchor genomic sequences to biologically meaningful 5'-end coordinates — transcription start sites from csRNA-seq or Tn5/MNase cleavage sites from ATAC-seq and MNase-seq — so that positional motif enrichment (MEPP) profiles can be interpreted relative to a common center across assays. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nargab/lqac075
skills.summary: Anchor genomic sequences to biologically meaningful 5'-end coordinates — transcription start sites from csRNA-seq or Tn5/MNase cleavage sites from ATAC-seq and MNase-seq — so that positional motif enrichment (MEPP) profiles can be interpreted relative to a common center across assays.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Sequences are genomic windows not anchored at a TSS or cleavage site, so positional offsets would be biologically meaningless The question is simple motif presence/absence enrichment under a zero-or-one-occurrence-per-sequence (ZOOPs) model, where position is irrelevant (e.g. standard HOMER-style MEA) De novo motif discovery is needed, since MEPP currently functions only with a fixed motif library

skills.description: Use when calling peaks from Calling Cards (qbed) insertion data with MACCs and computing Poisson p-values comparing experimental vs background insertions, to normalize for local TTAA-site density differences across candidate peaks.
skills.name: ttaa-density-relative-correction
skills.search_text: ttaa-density-relative-correction Use when calling peaks from Calling Cards (qbed) insertion data with MACCs and computing Poisson p-values comparing experimental vs background insertions, to normalize for local TTAA-site density differences across candidate peaks. Data are not Calling Cards transposon insertions (e.g. ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq peaks), where TTAA-site integration bias does not apply Peak calling is being done with CCcaller rather than MACCs, or the analysis goal is downstream differential peak analysis rather than significance testing of candidate peaks The insertion data have not yet been scanned and merged into candidate peak regions by MACCs (apply the window scan first) http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 A correction step in the MACCs peak-calling algorithm (Pycallingcards) that adjusts Poisson significance testing of Calling Cards insertions by the relative density of TTAA sites, accounting for the fact that the CC transposon integrates at TTAA sites and genomic regions differ in how many such target sites they contain. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btae070
skills.summary: A correction step in the MACCs peak-calling algorithm (Pycallingcards) that adjusts Poisson significance testing of Calling Cards insertions by the relative density of TTAA sites, accounting for the fact that the CC transposon integrates at TTAA sites and genomic regions differ in how many such target sites they contain.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Data are not Calling Cards transposon insertions (e.g. ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq peaks), where TTAA-site integration bias does not apply Peak calling is being done with CCcaller rather than MACCs, or the analysis goal is downstream differential peak analysis rather than significance testing of candidate peaks The insertion data have not yet been scanned and merged into candidate peak regions by MACCs (apply the window scan first)

skills.description: Use when you have a CITRUS output pickle with patient-by-TF activity matrices ('hid_tmr', 'tmr', 'can') and want to check whether inferred TF activities recover known tumor-type distinctions or identify TF–tumor-type associations.
skills.name: tumor-clustering-from-tf-activity-profiles
skills.search_text: tumor-clustering-from-tf-activity-profiles Use when you have a CITRUS output pickle with patient-by-TF activity matrices ('hid_tmr', 'tmr', 'can') and want to check whether inferred TF activities recover known tumor-type distinctions or identify TF–tumor-type associations. Your input is raw somatic alteration or gene expression matrices rather than a trained CITRUS output pickle — you must train CITRUS (python run_CITRUS.py) first to obtain 'hid_tmr'. Your goal is disambiguating individual TFs that share similar motifs — CITRUS motifs may encompass the activities of multiple TFs of the same family. You need directionality (activation vs repression) of TF–target effects — the TF–target gene priors used by CITRUS do not represent directionality. http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_3173 Clusters TCGA tumors (17 cancer types, 5803 samples) using patient-specific transcription factor activities inferred by CITRUS ('hid_tmr' layer), recovering known tumor-type groupings such as squamous-morphology and tissue-proximity clusters. Companion t-tests link each TF's activity to individual tumor types. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac881

skills.description: Use when oriented genomic features (e.g. strand-annotated TFBS BED files) must be tested for significant same/opposite strand preference relative to a null expectation of 0.5 across many feature sets.

skills.search_text: two-tailed-binomial-orientation-testing Use when oriented genomic features (e.g. strand-annotated TFBS BED files) must be tested for significant same/opposite strand preference relative to a null expectation of 0.5 across many feature sets. The null hypothesis is not a symmetric 0.5 same/opposite expectation, e.g. when testing against a background strand-composition bias rather than random orientation. http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Statistical testing of strand orientation asymmetry for DNA features: same/opposite strand counts are compared against the random-expectation ratio of 0.5 with a two-tailed binomial test (scipy), and P-values are adjusted with Bonferroni correction when multiple features are tested. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052

skills.description: Use when you have classified strand-oriented genomic events (e.g. same/opposite or convergent/divergent motif orientations) into two classes and need a significance test against a null expectation of 0.5, with multiple-testing correction.
skills.name: two-tailed-binomial-pvalue-calculation
skills.search_text: two-tailed-binomial-pvalue-calculation Use when you have classified strand-oriented genomic events (e.g. same/opposite or convergent/divergent motif orientations) into two classes and need a significance test against a null expectation of 0.5, with multiple-testing correction. The comparison involves more than two categories (e.g. replication-timing bins or multi-class orientations), where a binomial test against p = 0.5 does not apply. Feature positions or strand assignments are so spatially/structurally biased that a plain binomial null of 0.5 is inappropriate — use the permutation simulation mode instead of the plain binomial P-value. http://edamontology.org/topic_0091 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Statistical testing procedure from Asymmetron that computes two-tailed binomial P-values (expected probability 0.5) on strand-orientation counts and adjusts them with Bonferroni correction for multiple tests, optionally complemented by permutation simulations for empirical P-values. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkaa1052
skills.summary: Statistical testing procedure from Asymmetron that computes two-tailed binomial P-values (expected probability 0.5) on strand-orientation counts and adjusts them with Bonferroni correction for multiple tests, optionally complemented by permutation simulations for empirical P-values.

Feature positions or strand assignments are so spatially/structurally biased that a plain binomial null of 0.5 is inappropriate — use the permutation simulation mode instead of the plain binomial P-value.

skills.name: variant-delta-score-scoring
skills.search_text: variant-delta-score-scoring Use when you need per-variant sequence-effect scores for SNVs in RBP binding windows — e.g. to test whether disruptive variants (low gnomAD AF) show larger predicted binding changes than common variants. Your goal is de novo motif discovery or binding-site calling from raw CLIP reads — use the Skipper window/enrichment pipeline instead; the post hoc fine-mapping does not learn sequence motifs or binding affinity directly from CLIP data Variants of interest are not SNVs overlapping scored binding windows (e.g. indels or SVs without modeled allele sequences), since delta scores are defined only for reference/alternate sequence pairs the gkm-SVM can score You need state-of-the-art variant-effect estimates for functional follow-up — the paper notes the gapped k-mer SVM 'is easy to use but less sophisticated than emerging tools based on deep learning' Scores gnomAD SNVs overlapping fine-mapped Skipper binding windows with a trained LS-GKM gapped k-mer SVM, computing a per-variant delta score (reference minus alternate allele prediction) that is then binned by allele frequency and regressed to test for selective constraint on translation factor occupied sites. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100317
skills.summary: Scores gnomAD SNVs overlapping fine-mapped Skipper binding windows with a trained LS-GKM gapped k-mer SVM, computing a per-variant delta score (reference minus alternate allele prediction) that is then binned by allele frequency and regressed to test for selective constraint on translation factor occupied sites.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Your goal is de novo motif discovery or binding-site calling from raw CLIP reads — use the Skipper window/enrichment pipeline instead; the post hoc fine-mapping does not learn sequence motifs or binding affinity directly from CLIP data Variants of interest are not SNVs overlapping scored binding windows (e.g. indels or SVs without modeled allele sequences), since delta scores are defined only for reference/alternate sequence pairs the gkm-SVM can score You need state-of-the-art variant-effect estimates for functional follow-up — the paper notes the gapped k-mer SVM 'is easy to use but less sophisticated than emerging tools based on deep learning'

skills.search_text: variant-effect-prediction-from-chromatin-interaction-models Use when prioritizing non-coding SNPs (e.g., GWAS loci such as the 17q21 asthma variants rs12936231 and rs4065275) for likely causal status based on their predicted effect on chromatin interaction maps. No direct deepC-vs-Akita comparative benchmark is presented in the paper, so this skill should not be used as evidence that deepC outperforms Akita deepC predicts chromatin interactions, not gene expression, so do not use it to claim expression effects without an additional linkage analysis The installed tensorflow version is outside the tested range (v1.8, 1.14, 2.1); other versions are untested and may break predictions http://edamontology.org/topic_0654 http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Predicts the impact of single base-pair variants on 3D genome folding by running a trained deepC model on reference and variant megabase-scale sequence windows and computing effect sizes as the mean absolute difference between predicted Hi-C interaction maps, enabling fine-mapping of causal SNPs among candidates. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41592-020-0960-3
skills.summary: Predicts the impact of single base-pair variants on 3D genome folding by running a trained deepC model on reference and variant megabase-scale sequence windows and computing effect sizes as the mean absolute difference between predicted Hi-C interaction maps, enabling fine-mapping of causal SNPs among candidates.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No direct deepC-vs-Akita comparative benchmark is presented in the paper, so this skill should not be used as evidence that deepC outperforms Akita deepC predicts chromatin interactions, not gene expression, so do not use it to claim expression effects without an additional linkage analysis The installed tensorflow version is outside the tested range (v1.8, 1.14, 2.1); other versions are untested and may break predictions

skills.search_text: variant-to-gene-genomic-distance-assignment Use when you have a prioritized list of non-coding variant scores (e.g., ncDeepBrain output on a VCF/Annovar bed input) and need them attached to genes to build gene-level feature vectors for disease-gene prioritization. When you have direct regulatory evidence (eQTL or enhancer-promoter links) linking variants to target genes — the paper notes closest-gene assignment 'may be less optimal' for non-promoter regulatory elements When variants are already coding and directly gene-assigned — no distance-based mapping is needed When variants lie more than 100 kb from any annotated gene — the assignment rule will not link them to a gene http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Assigns non-coding variants to genes by nearest-genomic-distance (≤100 kb) so that variant-level scores (e.g., the ncDeepBrain brain-variant score) can be aggregated into gene-level features for iMEGES gene prioritization. skills.description: Use when scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode count data (e.g. Forebrain.h5ad, 2088 cells) are sparse and high-dimensional with severe missingness, and clustering/visualization/imputation requires learning low-dimensional latent features via a VAE with GMM prior.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-implementation
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-implementation Use when scATAC-seq peak-by-barcode count data (e.g. Forebrain.h5ad, 2088 cells) are sparse and high-dimensional with severe missingness, and clustering/visualization/imputation requires learning low-dimensional latent features via a VAE with GMM prior. The goal is explicit identification and removal of batch effects or other technical artifacts — the paper states SCALE 'is not specifically designed to identify and remove these artifacts from the input data' Integrating heterogeneous scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq datasets online — use SCALEX, the dedicated integration tool, instead Input is already a latent/feature-reduced table, so dimensionality reduction via VAE would add no value Implement SCALE's VAE+GMM neural network for sparse scATAC-seq: a PyTorch variational autoencoder with a Gaussian Mixture Model prior over 10 latent features that learns representations for clustering, visualization, and imputation of peak-by-barcode data. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12630-7
skills.summary: Implement SCALE's VAE+GMM neural network for sparse scATAC-seq: a PyTorch variational autoencoder with a Gaussian Mixture Model prior over 10 latent features that learns representations for clustering, visualization, and imputation of peak-by-barcode data.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The goal is explicit identification and removal of batch effects or other technical artifacts — the paper states SCALE 'is not specifically designed to identify and remove these artifacts from the input data' Integrating heterogeneous scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq datasets online — use SCALEX, the dedicated integration tool, instead Input is already a latent/feature-reduced table, so dimensionality reduction via VAE would add no value

skills.description: Use when input is a scATAC-seq count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder of peak/barcode files) that is sparse and close-to-binary, and the goal is cell clustering, visualization, or imputation via a learned latent feature space.
skills.name: variational-autoencoder-latent-feature-extraction
skills.search_text: variational-autoencoder-latent-feature-extraction Use when input is a scATAC-seq count matrix (h5ad, txt/tsv/csv, or mtx folder of peak/barcode files) that is sparse and close-to-binary, and the goal is cell clustering, visualization, or imputation via a learned latent feature space. Input is scRNA-seq data or multi-dataset integration/batch-removal is the primary goal — use SCALEX (github.com/jsxlei/SCALEX) instead, since SCALE is not specifically designed to identify and remove batch effects or other artifacts. The task requires single-peak motif resolution only — chromVAR-style grouped motif analysis may be preferred, since chromVAR only analyzes peaks in groups; SCALE's imputed output is meant to be combined with tools like Homer or chromVAR for downstream motif discovery. The data are high-coverage bulk ATAC-seq or already a feature/embedding table rather than a per-cell peak count matrix. http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Apply SCALE, a VAE-based deep generative model with a probabilistic Gaussian Mixture Model prior, to extract latent features from sparse, near-binary single-cell ATAC-seq count matrices and use them for clustering, UMAP visualization, and denoising/imputation of open-chromatin profiles. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-019-12630-7
skills.summary: Apply SCALE, a VAE-based deep generative model with a probabilistic Gaussian Mixture Model prior, to extract latent features from sparse, near-binary single-cell ATAC-seq count matrices and use them for clustering, UMAP visualization, and denoising/imputation of open-chromatin profiles.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is scRNA-seq data or multi-dataset integration/batch-removal is the primary goal — use SCALEX (github.com/jsxlei/SCALEX) instead, since SCALE is not specifically designed to identify and remove batch effects or other artifacts. The task requires single-peak motif resolution only — chromVAR-style grouped motif analysis may be preferred, since chromVAR only analyzes peaks in groups; SCALE's imputed output is meant to be combined with tools like Homer or chromVAR for downstream motif discovery. The data are high-coverage bulk ATAC-seq or already a feature/embedding table rather than a per-cell peak count matrix.

skills.description: Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample has been reduced to per-CpG fractional methylation and coverage over user-defined regions (e.g. CGIs), and the most likely methylation state vector of each underlying subpopulation across the region must be recovered.
skills.name: viterbi-decoding-of-binary-methylation-vectors
skills.search_text: viterbi-decoding-of-binary-methylation-vectors Use when bisulfite sequencing data from a heterogeneous sample has been reduced to per-CpG fractional methylation and coverage over user-defined regions (e.g. CGIs), and the most likely methylation state vector of each underlying subpopulation across the region must be recovered. Input regions have extreme methylation changes (e.g. DNMT3A mutation or demethylating agent treatment) without retuning transition probability parameters first Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where subpopulation deconvolution results are hard to interpret Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (e.g. neuronal cell types), since DXM does not consider 5hmC http://edamontology.org/topic_3674 http://edamontology.org/topic_3295 Reconstructs the most likely per-subpopulation methylation profiles across a genomic region by running Viterbi decoding over a hidden Markov model with 2x2 distance-binned transition matrices and beta-binomial emissions on fractional methylation and coverage, as implemented in DXM's dxm_solveMethylation. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab516
skills.summary: Reconstructs the most likely per-subpopulation methylation profiles across a genomic region by running Viterbi decoding over a hidden Markov model with 2x2 distance-binned transition matrices and beta-binomial emissions on fractional methylation and coverage, as implemented in DXM's dxm_solveMethylation.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input regions have extreme methylation changes (e.g. DNMT3A mutation or demethylating agent treatment) without retuning transition probability parameters first Regions with allele-specific methylation or copy number variants, where subpopulation deconvolution results are hard to interpret Samples with high 5-hydroxymethylation (e.g. neuronal cell types), since DXM does not consider 5hmC

skills.description: Use when a trained tree-structure model of a time-series expression matrix (e.g., mouse liver-regeneration RNA-seq) exists and each regulator must be assigned to the time point at which it influences its targets.
skills.name: viterbi-regulator-time-assignment
skills.search_text: viterbi-regulator-time-assignment Use when a trained tree-structure model of a time-series expression matrix (e.g., mouse liver-regeneration RNA-seq) exists and each regulator must be assigned to the time point at which it influences its targets. The expression data are not time-series (no ordered time points), since bifurcation times and TF action times are defined by temporal fold-change comparisons between consecutive time points. No TF-gene interaction information is available, because the tree-structure model's branches and regulator assignments depend on integrating the time-series matrix with TF-TG interactions. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 Run Viterbi decoding on TSMiner's trained tree-structure (input-output hidden Markov) model to assign each transcription factor to the specific time point at which it acts on its targets, turning a trained bifurcation model into time-specific TF-target assignments. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab629
skills.summary: Run Viterbi decoding on TSMiner's trained tree-structure (input-output hidden Markov) model to assign each transcription factor to the specific time point at which it acts on its targets, turning a trained bifurcation model into time-specific TF-target assignments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The expression data are not time-series (no ordered time points), since bifurcation times and TF action times are defined by temporal fold-change comparisons between consecutive time points. No TF-gene interaction information is available, because the tree-structure model's branches and regulator assignments depend on integrating the time-series matrix with TF-TG interactions.

skills.description: Use when significant long-range chromatin contacts must be called from distance-normalized Hi-C/capture Hi-C contact tables, requiring a fitted null distribution for p-value/FDR computation.
skills.name: weibull-distribution-fitting
skills.search_text: weibull-distribution-fitting Use when significant long-range chromatin contacts must be called from distance-normalized Hi-C/capture Hi-C contact tables, requiring a fitted null distribution for p-value/FDR computation. Input has not yet been coverage- and distance-normalized (covNormRpkg::normCoverage and normDistance must run first); fitting raw frequencies violates the background model Contacts beyond 2 Mb are the target — the covNorm Hi-C workflow uses max_dist=2000000, and pcHi-C considers only 15 kb–2 Mb interactions The goal is a reproducibility score of contact maps (HiC-spector) rather than significance calling of individual contacts http://edamontology.org/topic_0102 Fits a three-parameter Weibull distribution (location, shape, scale) to the distance-normalized Hi-C background set within 2-fold of expected values, then computes per-contact p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR for significant interaction calling, as implemented in covNorm's contactPval step. epigenomics/v2 10.1016/j.csbj.2021.05.041
skills.summary: Fits a three-parameter Weibull distribution (location, shape, scale) to the distance-normalized Hi-C background set within 2-fold of expected values, then computes per-contact p-values and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR for significant interaction calling, as implemented in covNorm's contactPval step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input has not yet been coverage- and distance-normalized (covNormRpkg::normCoverage and normDistance must run first); fitting raw frequencies violates the background model Contacts beyond 2 Mb are the target — the covNorm Hi-C workflow uses max_dist=2000000, and pcHi-C considers only 15 kb–2 Mb interactions The goal is a reproducibility score of contact maps (HiC-spector) rather than significance calling of individual contacts

skills.description: Use when two complementary base classifiers (e.g. RF and CNN) trained on the same promoter/non-promoter sequences must be combined into one ensemble prediction without retraining, following the iPro-WAEL weighted average design.
skills.name: weighted-average-ensemble-fusion
skills.search_text: weighted-average-ensemble-fusion Use when two complementary base classifiers (e.g. RF and CNN) trained on the same promoter/non-promoter sequences must be combined into one ensemble prediction without retraining, following the iPro-WAEL weighted average design. Only one base model is available (e.g. you already have a standalone RF or CNN prediction) — the weighted average requires both RF and CNN outputs to fuse Sequences are not yet featurized — run feature_code.py for word2vec features and iLearnPlus for the other features before invoking the ensemble The goal is motif/TFBS interpretation rather than promoter prediction — use feature_importance.rar instead http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 http://edamontology.org/topic_3510 Fuses the outputs of a random forest (RF.py) base model and a CNN (CNN.py) base model into a single promoter predictor via a weighted average algorithm (Weighted_average.py), as implemented in iPro-WAEL for promoter identification across seven species. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkac824
skills.summary: Fuses the outputs of a random forest (RF.py) base model and a CNN (CNN.py) base model into a single promoter predictor via a weighted average algorithm (Weighted_average.py), as implemented in iPro-WAEL for promoter identification across seven species.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Only one base model is available (e.g. you already have a standalone RF or CNN prediction) — the weighted average requires both RF and CNN outputs to fuse Sequences are not yet featurized — run feature_code.py for word2vec features and iLearnPlus for the other features before invoking the ensemble The goal is motif/TFBS interpretation rather than promoter prediction — use feature_importance.rar instead

skills.description: Use when raw narrow-peak BED files from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-overlapping (>200 bp) genomic training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input.
skills.name: weighted-midpoint-center-computation
skills.search_text: weighted-midpoint-center-computation Use when raw narrow-peak BED files from ENCODE/Roadmap chromatin profiles must be converted into fixed-length (1000 bp), non-overlapping (>200 bp) genomic training intervals for a Basset/DeepFun CNN input. Quantitative epigenomic signal information is required — this skill treats 'peaks' in binary format and ignores quantitative signal, which DeepFun's authors explicitly note as a limitation Long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact are part of the modeling goal — the DeepFun/Basset CNN model does not consider them The input peak set is already a preprocessed, non-redundant 1000 bp interval compendium (e.g. an existing Basset compendium) http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into non-redundant 1000 bp training intervals for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by extending each peak ±500 bp around its midpoint, greedily merging overlapping intervals (>200 bp overlap), and setting each merged peak center to the weighted average of constituent peak midpoints. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/nar/gkab429
skills.summary: Preprocesses raw ENCODE/Roadmap narrow-peak BED intervals into non-redundant 1000 bp training intervals for Basset/DeepFun-style CNNs by extending each peak ±500 bp around its midpoint, greedily merging overlapping intervals (>200 bp overlap), and setting each merged peak center to the weighted average of constituent peak midpoints.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Quantitative epigenomic signal information is required — this skill treats 'peaks' in binary format and ignores quantitative signal, which DeepFun's authors explicitly note as a limitation Long-range interactions such as 3D DNA contact are part of the modeling goal — the DeepFun/Basset CNN model does not consider them The input peak set is already a preprocessed, non-redundant 1000 bp interval compendium (e.g. an existing Basset compendium)

skills.description: Use when two sets of TAD/TLD boundary predictions must be compared quantitatively (e.g., noisy vs. reference Hi-C calls, or two predictors on the same matrix) and a contact-weighted domain-overlap score, excluding intermediate windows, is needed.

skills.search_text: weighted-similarity-domain-matching Use when two sets of TAD/TLD boundary predictions must be compared quantitatively (e.g., noisy vs. reference Hi-C calls, or two predictors on the same matrix) and a contact-weighted domain-overlap score, excluding intermediate windows, is needed. When the question is preserving hierarchy including intermediate/nested windows — WS explicitly excludes intermediate windows of domains; use AMI including T and K intermediate windows instead When inputs are raw contact matrices rather than already-predicted TLD boundary partitions — predictors (deDoc2, scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, etc.) must run first When inputs are bulk-depth Hi-C data where domain calls are already stable, so noise-robustness fidelity scoring is not the analysis goal http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computes the weighted similarity (WS) between two sets of predicted TAD-like domains (TLDs) — e.g., TLDs called on noisy versus original downsampled Hi-C matrices — as the fidelity metric used alongside adjusted mutual information (AMI) to benchmark TLD predictors such as deDoc2, deDoc, scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, and SpectralTAD. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Computes the weighted similarity (WS) between two sets of predicted TAD-like domains (TLDs) — e.g., TLDs called on noisy versus original downsampled Hi-C matrices — as the fidelity metric used alongside adjusted mutual information (AMI) to benchmark TLD predictors such as deDoc2, deDoc, scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, and SpectralTAD.
skills.when_to_use_negative: When the question is preserving hierarchy including intermediate/nested windows — WS explicitly excludes intermediate windows of domains; use AMI including T and K intermediate windows instead When inputs are raw contact matrices rather than already-predicted TLD boundary partitions — predictors (deDoc2, scHiCluster, deTOKI, Higashi, etc.) must run first When inputs are bulk-depth Hi-C data where domain calls are already stable, so noise-robustness fidelity scoring is not the analysis goal

skills.description: Use when comparing TLD/TAD partitions predicted from a raw bulk Hi-C matrix against partitions from downsampled (e.g. 0.1%, 0.05%, 0.025%) or otherwise degraded Hi-C data to quantify predictor robustness to sparsity.
skills.name: weighted-similarity-scoring
skills.search_text: weighted-similarity-scoring Use when comparing TLD/TAD partitions predicted from a raw bulk Hi-C matrix against partitions from downsampled (e.g. 0.1%, 0.05%, 0.025%) or otherwise degraded Hi-C data to quantify predictor robustness to sparsity. The comparison target is internal clustering quality of a single partition rather than cross-condition (raw vs. downsampled) partition agreement — use structural entropy/modularity indices or AMI alone instead Data are already single-cell scHi-C experiments rather than downsampled bulk matrices — the WS benchmark in the paper is defined for raw-vs-downsampled bulk Hi-C pairs Predicted TLDs include intermediate windows that cannot be removed — including them in T and K violates the metric's definition as described in the paper's workflow http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Benchmark metric that scores the agreement between TAD-like domain (TLD) partitions predicted from raw (reference) Hi-C data and partitions predicted from downsampled/imputed data at single-cell-level sparsity, as used to rank deDoc2.w against deDoc, IS, deTOKI, scHiCluster, SpectralTAD, GRiNCH, and Higashi in the deDoc2 paper. epigenomics/v2 10.1002/advs.202300366
skills.summary: Benchmark metric that scores the agreement between TAD-like domain (TLD) partitions predicted from raw (reference) Hi-C data and partitions predicted from downsampled/imputed data at single-cell-level sparsity, as used to rank deDoc2.w against deDoc, IS, deTOKI, scHiCluster, SpectralTAD, GRiNCH, and Higashi in the deDoc2 paper.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison target is internal clustering quality of a single partition rather than cross-condition (raw vs. downsampled) partition agreement — use structural entropy/modularity indices or AMI alone instead Data are already single-cell scHi-C experiments rather than downsampled bulk matrices — the WS benchmark in the paper is defined for raw-vs-downsampled bulk Hi-C pairs Predicted TLDs include intermediate windows that cannot be removed — including them in T and K violates the metric's definition as described in the paper's workflow

skills.description: Use when a copy-number (SCNA) or epi-DNA alteration has both a cis gene candidate set and a trans gene expression signature, and you must rank cis genes by how much of the trans effect they statistically mediate to flag the Rank-1 driver.
skills.name: weighted-trans-mediation-fraction-computation
skills.search_text: weighted-trans-mediation-fraction-computation Use when a copy-number (SCNA) or epi-DNA alteration has both a cis gene candidate set and a trans gene expression signature, and you must rank cis genes by how much of the trans effect they statistically mediate to flag the Rank-1 driver. No trans gene expression signature is associated with the alteration (mediation step requires mediated trans genes to compute WFTM) Sample size or correlation effects are insufficient for valid Sobel-test mediation inference — the article notes the Sobel test achieved high AUC only under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions The goal is driver detection considering only genes within the alteration boundaries — the article contrasts iEDGE with tools like GISTIC2.0 and expects trans mediation signal beyond the alteration http://edamontology.org/topic_2640 http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Computation of the Weighted Fraction of Trans Mediation (WFTM) score in iEDGE: for each SCNA, Sobel mediation statistics rank cis gene mediators of trans gene expression, and each cis gene's fractional weighted mediation effect across significantly mediated trans genes identifies the Rank-1 candidate driver. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41598-019-52886-z
skills.summary: Computation of the Weighted Fraction of Trans Mediation (WFTM) score in iEDGE: for each SCNA, Sobel mediation statistics rank cis gene mediators of trans gene expression, and each cis gene's fractional weighted mediation effect across significantly mediated trans genes identifies the Rank-1 candidate driver.
skills.when_to_use_negative: No trans gene expression signature is associated with the alteration (mediation step requires mediated trans genes to compute WFTM) Sample size or correlation effects are insufficient for valid Sobel-test mediation inference — the article notes the Sobel test achieved high AUC only under adequate sample size and strong correlation assumptions The goal is driver detection considering only genes within the alteration boundaries — the article contrasts iEDGE with tools like GISTIC2.0 and expects trans mediation signal beyond the alteration

skills.search_text: weighted-unweighted-score-concordance-evaluation Use when a SMITE-style p-value aggregation offers optional per-interval weights (e.g., TSS distance) and you must decide whether weighting materially changes final gene scores, modules, or annotations. The aggregation method has no optional weighting mechanism, so there is no weighted/unweighted pair to compare The goal is to optimize or select weights for performance rather than to assess sensitivity of final scores to the weighting choice Input p-values have not yet been cleaned (NAs and zero p-values), since zero p-values break the Stouffer combination and must first be replaced with the minimum non-zero p-value Quantifies how much optional weighting (e.g., distance from the transcription start site for promoter, gene body, and h3k4me1 data) alters SMITE's aggregated interval p-values and final gene scores, by regressing distance-weighted Stouffer-combined scores on unweighted scores and reporting the R-squared of concordance. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-017-1477-3
skills.summary: Quantifies how much optional weighting (e.g., distance from the transcription start site for promoter, gene body, and h3k4me1 data) alters SMITE's aggregated interval p-values and final gene scores, by regressing distance-weighted Stouffer-combined scores on unweighted scores and reporting the R-squared of concordance.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The aggregation method has no optional weighting mechanism, so there is no weighted/unweighted pair to compare The goal is to optimize or select weights for performance rather than to assess sensitivity of final scores to the weighting choice Input p-values have not yet been cleaned (NAs and zero p-values), since zero p-values break the Stouffer combination and must first be replaced with the minimum non-zero p-value

skills.search_text: wgbs-methylation-profiling Use when comparing DNA methylation levels or methylation variability between pre-defined genomic region sets (e.g., HOT regions, occupancy-binned non-HOT regions, CpG islands) across multiple cell types using WGBS methylation calls. Data are paired or repeated-measures (same donor before/after) — Wilcoxon rank-sum is for independent samples; use a signed-rank or paired test instead The comparison involves more than two groups or requires effect-size/interaction modeling (e.g. sex × age), rather than a two-sample proportion test Input is single-cell count matrices or sequencing data rather than precomputed cell-type proportion tables http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 http://edamontology.org/topic_3474 Non-parametric two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann–Whitney U) testing to verify reported cell-composition differences, e.g. the male-specific CD19+ B cell decline after age 65 and CD8+ T cell declines with age, from flow-cytometry proportions in the sexual-dimorphism immune aging study. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9

skills.search_text: z-score-amplification-thresholding Use when you have a normalized binned scATAC-seq matrix per cell and need to call focal amplifications (e.g., double minutes) at single-cell resolution without a matched control sample. The malignancy is driven primarily by single nucleotide variants with no or rare CNVs — Copy-scAT explicitly cannot be used in that setting The goal is arm-level (whole-chromosome) gain/loss annotation rather than focal amplification detection — use the annotateCNV3/annotateCNV4 branch instead A matched control/baseline file already exists and is required by the analysis design — CopyscAT is designed to work without a control file, so control-based workflows are out of scope http://edamontology.org/topic_3308 Detects focal amplifications in single-cell ATAC-seq data by scaling binned accessibility per cell/chromosome (median-IQR), segmenting with mean-variance changepoint analysis, and flagging segments whose scaled signal exceeds a z-score > 5, then pooling per-cell calls into consensus amplified regions. epigenomics/v2 10.1126/sciadv.abg6045
skills.summary: Detects focal amplifications in single-cell ATAC-seq data by scaling binned accessibility per cell/chromosome (median-IQR), segmenting with mean-variance changepoint analysis, and flagging segments whose scaled signal exceeds a z-score > 5, then pooling per-cell calls into consensus amplified regions.

skills.search_text: z-score-normalization-of-genomic-bins Use when you have dcHiC quantile-normalized compartment scores for multiple ordered time points (e.g., an ESC-NPC-CN developmental course) and want to cluster bins by trajectory shape before time-series clustering. Comparing only two Hi-C maps or a single condition — standard dcHiC differential compartment analysis (Mahalanobis distance significance) is the right choice, not trajectory clustering Compartment scores have not been quantile-normalized jointly across all input Hi-C data, so score scales are not comparable and z-transformation would fold in batch/scale artifacts Data are unordered or non-temporal samples (e.g., a panel of unrelated LCLs) where TCseq trajectory clustering is inappropriate http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Z-transform the quantile-normalized compartment scores of each 100 kb genomic bin across the six developmental time points (days 1, 7, 28, 56, 309, 347) so that downstream time-series clustering (TCseq) groups bins by relative compartmentalization dynamics rather than absolute A/B score scales. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-022-34626-6

skills.description: Use when an observed overlap between query ranges (e.g., caQTL or SNP sets) and target ranges (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks) must be tested against block-bootstrapped null ranges, and a z-score of the overlap rate is needed.
skills.name: z-score-significance-assessment
skills.search_text: z-score-significance-assessment Use when an observed overlap between query ranges (e.g., caQTL or SNP sets) and target ranges (e.g., ATAC-seq peaks) must be tested against block-bootstrapped null ranges, and a z-score of the overlap rate is needed. The comparison requires overlap counts of DEGs vs differential accessibility peaks with spline-based logFC threshold optimization (macrophage analysis uses macrophage.R/fit_splines.R instead) The query statistic is a correlation across single-cell multiome modalities rather than a range overlap rate (use multiomicsCor.R) A conventional shuffling/permutation null is intentionally desired (bootstrap.R path), though this risks overly narrow null distributions http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Quantifies significance of an observed genomic range overlap by standardizing the observed statistic (e.g., overlap rate, the proportion of SNPs with peaks within 10 kb) against the bootRanges block-bootstrap null distribution via a z-score, computed in the var.R step. epigenomics/v2 10.1093/bioinformatics/btad190
skills.summary: Quantifies significance of an observed genomic range overlap by standardizing the observed statistic (e.g., overlap rate, the proportion of SNPs with peaks within 10 kb) against the bootRanges block-bootstrap null distribution via a z-score, computed in the var.R step.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The comparison requires overlap counts of DEGs vs differential accessibility peaks with spline-based logFC threshold optimization (macrophage analysis uses macrophage.R/fit_splines.R instead) The query statistic is a correlation across single-cell multiome modalities rather than a range overlap rate (use multiomicsCor.R) A conventional shuffling/permutation null is intentionally desired (bootstrap.R path), though this risks overly narrow null distributions

skills.description: Use when a feature-by-donor abundance matrix has an ordered age/time axis and you need to normalize per-feature fitted temporal trends to comparable scale before clustering, e.g. finding shared aging trajectories of peaks/genes across adult lifespan.
skills.name: z-score-trajectory-normalization
skills.search_text: z-score-trajectory-normalization Use when a feature-by-donor abundance matrix has an ordered age/time axis and you need to normalize per-feature fitted temporal trends to comparable scale before clustering, e.g. finding shared aging trajectories of peaks/genes across adult lifespan. The feature series have no meaningful chronological/time ordering — z-scoring and k-means on unordered samples would not capture longitudinal trends. The input is raw or already-interpreted cluster labels rather than a normalized abundance matrix requiring per-feature trend fitting. Short series where ARIMA fitting is unreliable; the paper's design assumes one value per donor across a 22-93 year adult lifespan span. http://edamontology.org/topic_0203 A trajectory-normalization and clustering skill from PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq aging analysis: features passing an auto.arima longitudinal-trend filter (differencing D>0 plus at least one AR or MA term) have their fitted age-series z-scored and then grouped with k-means (k=3) to recover the major aging trajectories. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-020-14396-9
skills.summary: A trajectory-normalization and clustering skill from PBMC ATAC-seq/RNA-seq aging analysis: features passing an auto.arima longitudinal-trend filter (differencing D>0 plus at least one AR or MA term) have their fitted age-series z-scored and then grouped with k-means (k=3) to recover the major aging trajectories.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The feature series have no meaningful chronological/time ordering — z-scoring and k-means on unordered samples would not capture longitudinal trends. skills.description: Use when count-per-bin data (e.g., HDF counts per 25 bp genome bin) shows far more zeros than a Poisson predicts and you need to choose among ZIP, Poisson, and NB emissions for a background state.
skills.name: zero-inflated-count-modeling
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-count-modeling Use when count-per-bin data (e.g., HDF counts per 25 bp genome bin) shows far more zeros than a Poisson predicts and you need to choose among ZIP, Poisson, and NB emissions for a background state. For ChIP-enriched bin counts — the article shows the GP distribution fits these much better than Poisson and slightly better than NB, so GP (not ZIP) is the right emission model there For data without zero inflation (observed zero frequency close to the Poisson prediction), where plain Poisson suffices For continuous coverage values rather than discrete HDF counts per bin http://edamontology.org/topic_3053 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) distribution by maximum likelihood to low-count genomic bin data (e.g., HDF counts in background bins of ChIP-Seq data) and benchmark it against Poisson and negative binomial alternatives. In HPeak, the ZIP emission models the excess of empty 25 bp bins that Poisson underfits. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369

skills.description: Use when building scPower expression priors from a pilot UMI count matrix: you have pseudobulk-normalized gene means per cell type and need a zero-inflated gamma model over the means to later compute expression probabilities at chosen read depths.
skills.name: zero-inflated-gamma-mixture-fitting
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-gamma-mixture-fitting Use when building scPower expression priors from a pilot UMI count matrix: you have pseudobulk-normalized gene means per cell type and need a zero-inflated gamma model over the means to later compute expression probabilities at chosen read depths. The task is differential expression or power calculation with existing published priors (e.g. 10X_PBMC_1 or Pancreas_alphabeta reference studies) rather than fitting new priors from a pilot dataset Data are full-length read-count based with radically different count characteristics and no UMI matrix available for pseudobulk mean estimation The planned study sample size far exceeds the pilot dataset, since data-driven priors only reliably assess overall power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data http://edamontology.org/topic_3170 http://edamontology.org/topic_2269 Fits a mixed distribution of a zero component plus two left-censored gamma components to per-gene pseudobulk mean expression values, then re-parameterizes and serializes the gamma fits (with dispersion and read-depth curves) as an scPower expression prior for predicting cell type-specific expression probability in planned scRNA-seq experiments. epigenomics/v2 10.1038/s41467-021-26779-7
skills.summary: Fits a mixed distribution of a zero component plus two left-censored gamma components to per-gene pseudobulk mean expression values, then re-parameterizes and serializes the gamma fits (with dispersion and read-depth curves) as an scPower expression prior for predicting cell type-specific expression probability in planned scRNA-seq experiments.
skills.when_to_use_negative: The task is differential expression or power calculation with existing published priors (e.g. 10X_PBMC_1 or Pancreas_alphabeta reference studies) rather than fitting new priors from a pilot dataset Data are full-length read-count based with radically different count characteristics and no UMI matrix available for pseudobulk mean estimation The planned study sample size far exceeds the pilot dataset, since data-driven priors only reliably assess overall power for sample sizes smaller or roughly equal to the pilot data

skills.description: Use when you have preprocessed binned bivariate read-count tables (e.g. histoneHMM BN.txt/SHR.txt) and need to reconstruct or fit the emission densities of a bivariate HMM for differential histone modification analysis.
skills.name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixture-fitting
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-mixture-fitting Use when you have preprocessed binned bivariate read-count tables (e.g. histoneHMM BN.txt/SHR.txt) and need to reconstruct or fit the emission densities of a bivariate HMM for differential histone modification analysis. Input is raw BAM/bed data not yet aggregated into binned read counts — preprocess first (e.g. with preprocess.for.hmm and 1000 bp bins) before fitting marginals The data are peak-like ChIP-seq marks rather than broad diffuse histone modifications, where methods searching for peak-like features are more appropriate You need a supervised or tuning-parameter-driven classification — histoneHMM's emission fitting is explicitly unsupervised with no further tuning parameters http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 http://edamontology.org/topic_0622 Fit zero-inflated negative-binomial (ZINB) marginal distributions to binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts and couple them through a Gaussian copula, reproducing the four-component bivariate emission model that powers histoneHMM's three-state differential classification. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/s12859-015-0491-6
skills.summary: Fit zero-inflated negative-binomial (ZINB) marginal distributions to binned bivariate ChIP-seq read counts and couple them through a Gaussian copula, reproducing the four-component bivariate emission model that powers histoneHMM's three-state differential classification.
skills.when_to_use_negative: Input is raw BAM/bed data not yet aggregated into binned read counts — preprocess first (e.g. with preprocess.for.hmm and 1000 bp bins) before fitting marginals The data are peak-like ChIP-seq marks rather than broad diffuse histone modifications, where methods searching for peak-like features are more appropriate You need a supervised or tuning-parameter-driven classification — histoneHMM's emission fitting is explicitly unsupervised with no further tuning parameters

skills.description: Use when calling ChIP-enriched regions from HDF per-bin counts (e.g., 25 bp bins) and you need a discrete emission model that explicitly handles excess zeros in background coverage alongside an overdispersed enriched-state signal.
skills.name: zero-inflated-poisson-background-modeling
skills.search_text: zero-inflated-poisson-background-modeling Use when calling ChIP-enriched regions from HDF per-bin counts (e.g., 25 bp bins) and you need a discrete emission model that explicitly handles excess zeros in background coverage alongside an overdispersed enriched-state signal. Input is already a set of called peak intervals or a feature table rather than raw aligned short reads needing coverage-based classification Comparative histone modification datasets of the type handled by ChIPDiff, which is restricted to comparative histone data rather than general peak calling You need to distinguish reads of different orientation within a peak to pinpoint summits — the current HPeak algorithm does not support this http://edamontology.org/topic_3169 Model background HDF coverage in ChIP-Seq bins with a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission within HPeak's two-state HMM, since background bins are dominated by zeros that plain Poisson underfits. The ZIP is paired with a Generalized Poisson emission for the ChIP-enriched state during Viterbi-based parameter estimation. epigenomics/v2 10.1186/1471-2105-11-369
skills.summary: Model background HDF coverage in ChIP-Seq bins with a zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) emission within HPeak's two-state HMM, since background bins are dominated by zeros that plain Poisson underfits. The ZIP is paired with a Generalized Poisson emission for the ChIP-enriched state during Viterbi-based parameter estimation.
